前言和致谢

PREFATORY STATEMENTS AND ACKNOWLEDGMENTS

这本书是在我试图写作其他作品时突然冒出来的，或许至今仍留有我当初写作时极不情愿的痕迹。在完成对威廉·布莱克的研究（《恐惧的对称》，1947）之后，我决定将从布莱克那里学到的文学象征主义和圣经类型学原理应用于另一位诗人，最好是那些从当时的批评理论中汲取这些原理的诗人，而不是像布莱克那样自行摸索出来的。于是，我开始研究斯宾塞的《仙后》，却发现我的开始即是我的结束。对斯宾塞的介绍变成了对寓言理论的介绍，而这个理论又固执地依附于一个更为庞大的理论框架。论证的基础变得越来越偏重于论述，而越来越脱离历史和斯宾塞式的视角。我很快发现自己陷入了批评中那些与“神话”、“象征”、“仪式”和“原型”等词汇相关的部分，而我试图在已发表的文章中阐释这些词汇的努力也引起了足够的关注，这鼓励我继续沿着这条思路深入研究。最终，我最初着手的理论和实践工作完全分离了。本书所提供的是纯粹的批评理论，刻意省略了所有具体的批评，甚至在四篇文章中的三篇中省略了引文。就我目前的判断而言，本书似乎需要一本补充性的著作，探讨实践批评，一种文学象征主义的形态学研究。

THIS book forced itself on me while I was trying to write something else, and it probably still bears the marks of the reluctance with which a great part of it was composed. After completing a study of William Blake (Fearful Symmetry, 1947), I determined to apply the principles of literary symbolism and Biblical typology which I had learned from Blake to another poet, preferably one who had taken these principles from the critical theories of his own day, instead of working them out by himself as Blake did. I therefore began a study of Spenser’s Faerie Queene, only to discover that in my beginning was my end. The introduction to Spenser became an introduction to the theory of allegory, and that theory obstinately adhered to a much larger theoretical structure. The basis of argument became more and more discursive, and less and less historical and Spenserian. I soon found myself entangled in those parts of criticism that have to do with such words as “myth,” “symbol,” “ritual,” and “archetype,” and my efforts to make sense of these words in various published articles met with enough interest to encourage me to proceed further along these lines. Eventually the theoretical and the practical aspects of the task I had begun completely separated. What is here offered is pure critical theory, and the omission of all specific criticism, even, in three of the four essays, of quotation, is deliberate. The present book seems to me, so far as I can judge at present, to need a complementary volume concerned with practical criticism, a sort of morphology of literary symbolism.

我感谢 JS 古根海姆纪念基金会提供的奖学金（1950-1951 年），这使我有了闲暇和自由来处理我那变化莫测的主题，而当时它正最需要这两者。

I am grateful to the J. S. Guggenheim Memorial Foundation for a Fellowship (1950-1951) which gave me leisure and freedom to deal with my Protean subject at the time when it stood in the greatest need of both.

我还要感谢普林斯顿大学1932届的同学们，以及普林斯顿大学人文科学特别项目委员会，他们为我提供了一个极具启发性的学期，本书的大部分内容正是在此期间最终成型的。本书收录了我于1954年3月在普林斯顿发表的四次公开演讲的实质内容。

I am also grateful to the Class of 1932 of Princeton University, and to the Committee of the Special Program in the Humanities at Princeton, for providing me with a most stimulating term of work, in the course of which a good deal of the present book took its final shape. This book contains the substance of the four public lectures delivered in Princeton in March 1954.

《论战性导论》是《第一篇文章《当代批评的功能》，发表于1949年10月的《多伦多大学季刊》，后重印于马尔科姆·罗斯主编的《我们的身份认同感》（多伦多，1954年）。该文是《文化史理论初探》（发表于1953年7月的《多伦多大学季刊》）的修订和扩展版。第二篇文章融合了以下文章的内容：《文学中的意义层次》 （发表于1950年春季的《肯扬评论》）；《象征主义的三种含义》（发表于1952年《耶鲁法语研究》第9期）；《诗歌的语言》（发表于1955年《探索》第4期，多伦多）；以及《文学原型》 （发表于1951年冬季的《肯扬评论》） 。第三篇文章包含了以下文章的内容：《喜剧的论证》（发表于1948年英语研究所论文集，哥伦比亚大学出版社，1949年）；以及《莎士比亚喜剧中的人物刻画》（发表于《莎士比亚》）。 1953年7月《季刊》；1952年6月《加拿大皇家学会会刊（第二部分）》“莎士比亚作品中的喜剧神话” ；以及1944年10月《多伦多大学季刊》 “讽刺的本质” 。第四篇文章包含了以下文章的内容： 1942年1月《多伦多大学季刊》“诗歌中的音乐”；1951年秋季《肯扬评论》“戏剧体裁概览”；1950年冬季《哈德逊评论》“散文小说的四种形式”；以及1954年夏季《哈德逊评论》 “作为信息的神话” 。我非常感谢上述期刊的编辑、哥伦比亚大学出版社和加拿大皇家学会允许我转载这些内容。此外，我还从我发表在上述期刊上的其他文章和评论中摘录了一些句子，以使其与本文的语境相符。

The “Polemical Introduction” is a revised version of “The Function of Criticism at the Present Time,” University of Toronto Quarterly, October 1949, also reprinted in Our Sense of Identity, ed. Malcolm Ross, Toronto, 1954. The first essay is a revised and expanded version of “Towards a Theory of Cultural History,” University of Toronto Quarterly, July 1953. The second essay incorporates the material of “Levels of Meaning in Literature,” Kenyon Review, Spring 1950; of “Three Meanings of Symbolism,” Yale French Studies No. 9 (1952); of “The Language of Poetry,” Explorations 4 (Toronto, 1955); and of “The Archetypes of Literature,” Kenyon Review, Winter 1951. The third essay contains the material of “The Argument of Comedy,” English Institute Essays 1948, Columbia University Press, 1949; of “Characterization in Shakespearean Comedy,” Shakespeare Quarterly, July 1953; of “Comic Myth in Shakespeare,” Transactions of the Royal Society of Canada (Section II), June 1952; and of “The Nature of Satire,” University of Toronto Quarterly, October 1944. The fourth essay contains the material of “Music in Poetry,” University of Toronto Quarterly, January 1942; of “A Conspectus of Dramatic Genres,” Kenyon Review, Autumn 1951; of “The Four Forms of Prose Fiction,” Hudson Review, Winter 1950; and of “Myth as Information,” Hudson Review, Summer 1954. I am greatly obliged to the courtesy of the editors of the above-mentioned periodicals, the Columbia University Press, and the Royal Society of Canada, for permission to reprint this material. I have also transplanted a few sentences from other articles and reviews of mine, all from the same periodicals, when they appeared to fit the present context.

至于我接下来的义务，这里只能说，而且即便老生常谈也并非不实，那就是本书的许多优点都归功于他人：事实、品味、逻辑和比例上的错误是可悲的，但却是我的错。

For my further obligations, all that can be said here, and is not less true for being routine, is that many of the virtues of this book are due to others: the errors of fact, taste, logic, and proportion are poor things, but my own.

批评的剖析

ANATOMY OF CRITICISM

四篇论文

Four Essays

论战性引言

Polemical Introduction

本书由一系列“随笔”组成，这里的“随笔”一词保留了其原意——尝试或不完整的尝试——探讨了构建一个概括性视角来审视文学批评的范围、理论、原则和技巧的可能性。本书的主要目的是阐述我为何相信存在这样一种概括性视角；其次，本书旨在提供一个初步的版本，使其足以说服读者，我所概述的这种视角是可行的。由于本书探讨的主题存在诸多空白，因此它绝不能被视为呈现我的体系，甚至不能被视为呈现我的理论。本书更应被视为一系列相互关联的建议，希望它们能对文学批评家和学生有所助益。任何对任何人都没有实际用处的内容都是可以舍弃的。我的方法基于马修·阿诺德的格言：让思维自由地围绕一个已被广泛研究却鲜有深入探讨的主题展开。所有文章都涉及批评，但我所说的批评指的是与文学相关的全部学术研究和鉴赏活动，它是人们通常所说的博雅教育、文化或人文学科研究的一部分。我的出发点是，批评不仅是这一更广泛活动的一部分，而且是其不可或缺的一部分。

THIS BOOK consists of “essays,” in the word’s original sense of a trial or incomplete attempt, on the possibility of a synoptic view of the scope, theory, principles, and techniques of literary criticism. The primary aim of the book is to give my reasons for believing in such a synoptic view; its secondary aim is to provide a tentative version of it which will make enough sense to convince my readers that a view, of the kind that I outline, is attainable. The gaps in the subject as treated here are too enormous for the book ever to be regarded as presenting my system, or even my theory. It is to be regarded rather as an interconnected group of suggestions which it is hoped will be of some practical use to critics and students of literature. Whatever is of no practical use to anybody is expendable. My approach is based on Matthew Arnold’s precept of letting the mind play freely around a subject in which there has been much endeavor and little attempt at perspective. All the essays deal with criticism, but by criticism I mean the whole work of scholarship and taste concerned with literature which is a part of what is variously called liberal education, culture, or the study of the humanities. I start from the principle that criticism is not simply a part of this larger activity, but an essential part of it.

文学批评的主题是一门艺术，而批评本身显然也是一种艺术。这听起来好像批评是一种寄生性的文学表达形式，一种建立在既有艺术基础上的艺术，一种对创造力的二手模仿。按照这种理论，批评家是知识分子，他们既缺乏创作能力，也缺乏赞助艺术的资金，因此构成了一个文化中间人阶层，他们以自身利益为代价向社会分发文化，同时剥削艺术家，加重公众的负担。批评家是寄生虫或“失败艺术家”的观念至今仍然非常流行，尤其是在艺术家群体中。这种观念有时会被一种可疑的类比所强化，这种类比将创造力和生育功能联系起来，以至于我们经常听到批评家的“无能”和“枯燥”，以及他们对真正有创造力的人的憎恨等等。反批评的黄金时代是十九世纪后期，但当时的一些偏见至今仍然存在。

The subject-matter of literary criticism is an art, and criticism is evidently something of an art too. This sounds as though criticism were a parasitic form of literary expression, an art based on pre-existing art, a second-hand imitation of creative power. On this theory critics are intellectuals who have a taste for art but lack both the power to produce it and the money to patronize it, and thus form a class of cultural middlemen, distributing culture to society at a profit to themselves while exploiting the artist and increasing the strain on his public. The conception of the critic as a parasite or artist manqué is still very popular, especially among artists. It is sometimes reinforced by a dubious analogy between the creative and the procreative functions, so that we hear about the “impotence” and “dryness” of the critic, of his hatred for genuinely creative people, and so on. The golden age of anticritical criticism was the latter part of the nineteenth century, but some of its prejudices are still around.

然而，试图摆脱批评的艺术的命运是……颇具启发性。试图通过“大众”艺术直接接触公众的做法，假定批评是人为的，而公众品味是自然而然的。其背后还隐藏着一个关于自然品味的假设，这个假设可以追溯到托尔斯泰，再到浪漫主义关于自发创造的“大众”理论。这些理论已经过充分的检验；它们经不起文学史和经验的检验，或许是时候超越它们了。一种对原始观点的极端反动，曾一度与“为艺术而艺术”的口号联系在一起，它以截然相反的视角看待艺术，将其视为一种神秘，一种进入神秘文明社群的入门仪式。在这种视角下，批评被限制在仪式化的共济会手势、扬起的眉毛、晦涩的评论以及其他一些过于深奥而无法用语法表达的理解的迹象。这两种态度的共同谬误在于，它们都认为艺术的价值与公众的反应程度之间存在粗略的相关性，尽管这种相关性在一种情况下是正相关，而在另一种情况下则是负相关。

However, the fate of art that tries to do without criticism is instructive. The attempt to reach the public directly through “popular” art assumes that criticism is artificial and public taste natural. Behind this is a further assumption about natural taste which goes back through Tolstoy to Romantic theories of a spontaneously creative “folk.” These theories have had a fair trial; they have not stood up very well to the facts of literary history and experience, and it is perhaps time to move beyond them. An extreme reaction against the primitive view, at one time associated with the “art for art’s sake” catchword, thinks of art in precisely the opposite terms, as a mystery, an initiation into an esoterically civilized community. Here criticism is restricted to ritual masonic gestures, to raised eyebrows and cryptic comments and other signs of an understanding too occult for syntax. The fallacy common to both attitudes is that of a rough correlation between the merit of art and the degree of public response to it, though the correlation assumed is direct in one case and inverse in the other.

人们或许能找到一些看似支持​​这两种观点的例子；但显而易见的真相是，艺术的价值与其公众接受度之间并无真正的关联。莎士比亚比韦伯斯特更受欢迎，但这并非因为他是一位更伟大的剧作家；济慈不如蒙哥马利受欢迎，但这也并非因为他是一位更优秀的诗人。因此，无论好坏，批评家都不可避免地会成为教育的先驱和文化传统的塑造者。莎士比亚和济慈如今的受欢迎程度，同样也是批评宣传的结果。如果公众试图摒弃批评，并声称自己知道想要什么或喜欢什么，那么艺术就会遭到摧残，文化记忆也会随之消逝。为艺术而艺术是对批评的逃避，最终只会导致文明生活本身的贫瘠。阻止批评的唯一途径是审查制度，而审查制度与批评的关系，正如私刑与正义的关系一样。

One can find examples which appear to support both these views; but it is clearly the simple truth that there is no real correlation either way between the merits of art and its public reception. Shakespeare was more popular than Webster, but not because he was a greater dramatist; Keats was less popular than Montgomery, but not because he was a better poet. Consequently there is no way of preventing the critic from being, for better or worse, the pioneer of education and the shaper of cultural tradition. Whatever popularity Shakespeare and Keats have now is equally the result of the publicity of criticism. A public that tries to do without criticism, and asserts that it knows what it wants or likes, brutalizes the arts and loses its cultural memory. Art for art’s sake is a retreat from criticism which ends in an impoverishment of civilized life itself. The only way to forestall the work of criticism is through censorship, which has the same relation to criticism that lynching has to justice.

批评存在还有另一个原因。批评可以言说，而所有艺术都是哑的。在绘画、雕塑或音乐中，我们很容易看出艺术本身是展现出来的，但却无法表达任何内容。而且，无论称诗人为不善言辞或哑口无言听起来如何，诗歌在某种至关重要的意义上确实像雕像一样沉默。诗歌是对文字的客观运用：它并不直接与读者对话。当诗歌直接与读者对话时，我们通常会感到诗人对读者和评论家的能力抱有某种不信任。他无需他人协助便能解读其含义，因此已沦落到任何人都能学会创作的格律诗（“诗”或“打油诗”）的低级境地。并非只有传统才驱使诗人祈求缪斯，并声称其言语并非出于本能。麦克利什先生在其名著《诗艺》中将“哑的”、“无声的”和“无言的”等词语用于形容诗歌，也并非出于故弄玄虚。正如约翰·斯图亚特·密尔在一次精彩的批判性洞察中所见，艺术家并非被聆听，而是被窃听。批评的公理必然是：诗人并非不知其所言，而是无法言说其所知。因此，捍卫批评存在的权利，就意味着假定批评是一种独立存在的思想和知识体系，它在某种程度上独立于其所评论的艺术之外。

There is another reason why criticism has to exist. Criticism can talk, and all the arts are dumb. In painting, sculpture, or music it is easy enough to see that the art shows forth, but cannot say anything. And, whatever it sounds like to call the poet inarticulate or speechless, there is a most important sense in which poems are as silent as statues. Poetry is a disinterested use of words: it does not address a reader directly. When it does so, we usually feel that the poet has some distrust in the capacity of readers and critics to interpret his meaning without assistance, and has therefore dropped into the sub-poetic level of metrical talk (“verse” or “doggerel”) which anybody can learn to produce. It is not only tradition that impels a poet to invoke a Muse and protest that his utterance is involuntary. Nor is it strained wit that causes Mr. MacLeish, in his famous Ars Poetica, to apply the words “mute,” “dumb,” and “wordless” to a poem. The artist, as John Stuart Mill saw in a wonderful flash of critical insight, is not heard but overheard. The axiom of criticism must be, not that the poet does not know what he is talking about, but that he cannot talk about what he knows. To defend the right of criticism to exist at all, therefore, is to assume that criticism is a structure of thought and knowledge existing in its own right, with some measure of independence from the art it deals with.

诗人当然可能具备一定的批判能力，因此能够谈论自己的作品。但为《天堂篇》第一歌撰写评注的但丁，只不过是众多批评但丁作品的批评者之一。他的评论固然有其独特之处，但并不具有权威性。人们普遍认为，批评家比诗歌的创作者更能评判其价值，但仍然有人认为，将批评家视为诗歌意义的最终评判者是荒谬的，尽管在实践中，批评家显然必须如此。造成这种误解的原因在于，人们无法将文学与源于主动意志和意识的描述性或陈述性写作区分开来，后者主要目的是“表达”某些内容。

The poet may of course have some critical ability of his own, and so be able to talk about his own work. But the Dante who writes a commentary on the first canto of the Paradiso is merely one more of Dante’s critics. What he says has a peculiar interest, but not a peculiar authority. It is generally accepted that a critic is a better judge of the value of a poem than its creator, but there is still a lingering notion that it is somehow ridiculous to regard the critic as the final judge of its meaning, even though in practice it is clear that he must be. The reason for this is an inability to distinguish literature from the descriptive or assertive writing which derives from the active will and the conscious mind, and which is primarily concerned to “say” something.

评论家认为诗人只有在死后才能得到恰当的评价，部分原因在于诗人死后便无法再凭借其诗歌才华，以所谓的内幕消息来挑衅评论家。当易卜生坚称《皇帝与加利利人》是他最伟大的剧作，并声称《培尔·金特》中的某些情节并非寓言时，我们只能说易卜生对自己的评论也显得漫不经心。华兹华斯的《抒情歌谣集》序言是一份杰出的文献，但作为一篇华兹华斯式的评论，恐怕无人会给它打出B+的水平。人们常常用“如果莎士比亚死而复生，他根本无法欣赏甚至理解他们的评论”来嘲讽莎士比亚的评论家。这种说法本身就很有可能：我们几乎没有证据表明莎士比亚对评论感兴趣，无论是对他自己的评论还是对其他人的评论。即便他真的感兴趣，也未必能理解评论家们的批评。这样的证据，就如同他自己对《哈姆雷特》创作意图的阐述一样，并不能构成对该剧的最终评论，彻底解开所有谜团；正如他执导的演出也并非最终版本一样。诗人对待自身作品的这种态度，更适用于他对其他诗人的评价。批评家诗人几乎不可能避免将自身与创作实践紧密相连的品味，扩展成一条普遍的文学法则。但批评必须建立在文学整体的实际运作之上：在文学的光照下，任何一位备受尊敬的作家对文学整体应有的理解，都将呈现出其应有的面貌。诗人以批评家的身份发表作品，并非直接提出批评，而是提供供批评家审视的文献。这些文献或许很有价值：只有当它们被奉为批评的指导原则时，才有可能产生误导。

Part of the critic’s reason for feeling that poets can be properly assessed only after their death is that they are then unable to presume on their merits as poets to tease him with hints of inside knowledge. When Ibsen maintains that Emperor and Galilean is his greatest play and that certain episodes in Peer Gynt are not allegorical, one can only say that Ibsen is an indifferent critic of Ibsen. Wordsworth’s Preface to the Lyrical Ballads is a remarkable document, but as a piece of Wordsworthian criticism nobody would give it more than about a B plus. Critics of Shakespeare are often supposed to be ridiculed by the assertion that if Shakespeare were to come back from the dead he would not be able to appreciate or even understand their criticism. This in itself is likely enough: we have little evidence of Shakespeare’s interest in criticism, either of himself or of anyone else. Even if there were such evidence, his own account of what he was trying to do in Hamlet would no more be a definitive criticism of that play, clearing all its puzzles up for good, than a performance of it under his direction would be a definitive performance. And what is true of the poet in relation to his own work is still more true of his opinion of other poets. It is hardly possible for the critical poet to avoid expanding his own tastes, which are intimately linked to his own practice, into a general law of literature. But criticism has to be based on what the whole of literature actually does: in its light, whatever any highly respected writer thinks literature in general ought to do will show up in its proper perspective. The poet speaking as critic produces, not criticism, but documents to be examined by critics. They may well be valuable documents: it is only when they are accepted as directives for criticism that they are in any danger of becoming misleading.

认为诗人必然是或能够成为自身或文学理论的最终诠释者，这种观念源于将批评家视为寄生虫或豺狼的设想。一旦我们承认批评家拥有自身的活动领域，并且在该领域内拥有自主性，我们就必须承认批评是在一个特定的概念框架下处理文学问题的。这个框架并非文学本身，因为这又是寄生虫理论；但它也不是文学之外的某种东西，因为那样一来，批评的自主性就会再次消失，整个批评学科也会被同化。

The notion that the poet necessarily is or could be the definitive interpreter of himself or of the theory of literature belongs to the conception of the critic as a parasite or jackal. Once we admit that the critic has his own field of activity, and that he has autonomy within that field, we have to concede that criticism deals with literature in terms of a specific conceptual framework. The framework is not that of literature itself, for this is the parasite theory again, but neither is it something outside literature, for in that case the autonomy of criticism would again disappear, and the whole subject would be assimilated to something else.

后者在批评领域给我们带来了一种谬误，即历史上所谓的决定论。在这种谬误中，一位对地理或经济学特别感兴趣的学者，会运用一种修辞手法，将自己钟爱的研究领域与他不太感兴趣的领域建立因果关系。这种方法给人一种错觉，仿佛在研究的同时就能解释研究对象，从而节省时间。在批评领域，我们很容易列举出一长串这样的决定论，无论是马克思主义的、托马斯主义的、自由人文主义的、新古典主义的、弗洛伊德主义的、荣格主义的，还是存在主义的，它们都用一种批判的态度取代了批评本身，它们都试图在文学内部寻找批评的概念框架，而是将批评依附于文学之外的各种框架。然而，批评的公理和假设必须源于它所研究的艺术。文学批评家首先要做的是阅读文学作品，对其研究领域进行归纳式的考察，并让其批评能力发挥作用。原则的形成完全源于他对该领域的了解。批判性原则不能直接从神学、哲学、政治学、科学或这些领域的任何组合中照搬而来。

This latter gives us, in criticism, the fallacy of what in history is called determinism, where a scholar with a special interest in geography or economics expresses that interest by the rhetorical device of putting his favorite study into a causal relationship with whatever interests him less. Such a method gives one the illusion of explaining one’s subject while studying it, thus wasting no time. It would be easy to compile a long list of such determinisms in criticism, all of them, whether Marxist, Thomist, liberal-humanist, neo-Classical, Freudian, Jungian, or existentialist, substituting a critical attitude for criticism, all proposing, not to find a conceptual framework for criticism within literature, but to attach criticism to one of a miscellany of frameworks outside it. The axioms and postulates of criticism, however, have to grow out of the art it deals with. The first thing the literary critic has to do is to read literature, to make an inductive survey of his own field and let his critical principles shape themselves solely out of his knowledge of that field. Critical principles cannot be taken over ready-made from theology, philosophy, politics, science, or any combination of these.

将批评置于外在的批评态度之下，就等于夸大了文学中与外部来源（无论其为何）相关的价值。我们很容易将一种文学之外的模式，一种宗教政治色彩滤镜，强加于文学之上，这使得一些诗人一举成名，而另一些诗人则显得黯淡无光、缺陷重重。客观的批评家面对这种色彩滤镜所能做的，不过是礼貌地低声说，它以全新的视角展现了事物，的确对批评做出了极具启发性的贡献。当然，这类带有滤镜色彩的批评家通常暗示，并且常常相信，他们是在让自己的文学体验说话，而将其他态度保留在心底；他们的批评价值与宗教或政治观点之间的契合，令他们暗自感到满足，但并未明确地强加于读者。然而，即便在那些最了解批评的人当中，这种不受偏见影响的批评也并非总是能够实现。至于那些不如他们的人，还是少说为妙。

To subordinate criticism to an externally derived critical attitude is to exaggerate the values in literature that can be related to the external source, whatever it is. It is all too easy to impose on literature an extra-literary schematism, a sort of religio-political color-filter, which makes some poets leap into prominence and others show up as dark and faulty. All that the disinterested critic can do with such a color-filter is to murmur politely that it shows things in a new light and is indeed a most stimulating contribution to criticism. Of course such filtering critics usually imply, and often believe, that they are letting their literary experience speak for itself and are holding their other attitudes in reserve, the coincidence between their critical valuations and their religious or political views being silently gratifying to them but not explicitly forced on the reader. Such independence of criticism from prejudice, however, does not invariably occur even with those who best understand criticism. Of their inferiors the less said the better.

如果坚持认为，在我们获得一套以其他事物为重心的连贯人生哲学之前，我们无法批评文学，那么批评作为一门独立学科的存在仍然是被否定的。但还有另一种可能性。如果批评存在，它必然是对文学的一种考察，而这种考察必须基于一个概念框架，该框架可以通过对文学领域的归纳式考察而得出。“归纳”一词暗示着某种科学程序。如果批评既是一门科学又是一门艺术呢？当然，它并非一门“纯粹的”或“精确的”科学，因为这些词汇属于十九世纪的宇宙观，而我们早已不再拥有这种宇宙观。历史写作是一门艺术，但没有人怀疑历史学家在处理证据时运用了科学原理，而正是这种科学因素的存在将历史与传说区分开来。或许，批评中也存在着某种科学因素，正是这种因素使其既区别于文学寄生，又区别于强加的批评态度。科学的介入会改变任何学科的性质，使其从随意转向因果，从随机和直觉转向系统，同时也能保护该学科的完整性免受外部侵害。然而，如果有些读者对“科学”一词感到困惑，那么……如果“系统性”或“进步性”等词语带有缺乏想象力的野蛮情绪，他们可能会用这些词语来代替。

If it is insisted that we cannot criticize literature until we have acquired a coherent philosophy of life with its center of gravity in something else, the existence of criticism as a separate subject is still being denied. But there is another possibility. If criticism exists, it must be an examination of literature in terms of a conceptual framework derivable from an inductive survey of the literary field. The word “inductive” suggests some sort of scientific procedure. What if criticism is a science as well as an art? Not a “pure” or “exact” science, of course, but these phrases belong to a nineteenth-century cosmology which is no longer with us. The writing of history is an art, but no one doubts that scientific principles are involved in the historian’s treatment of evidence, and that the presence of this scientific element is what distinguishes history from legend. It may also be a scientific element in criticism which distinguishes it from literary parasitism on the one hand, and the superimposed critical attitude on the other. The presence of science in any subject changes its character from the casual to the causal, from the random and intuitive to the systematic, as well as safeguarding the integrity of that subject from external invasions. However, if there are any readers for whom the word “scientific” conveys emotional overtones of unimaginative barbarism, they may substitute “systematic” or “progressive” instead.

说文学批评中可能存在科学成分，这似乎很荒谬，因为有几十种学术期刊都基于这个假设，而且有数百名学者从事与文学批评相关的科学研究。证据经过科学检验；前人的权威被科学地运用；研究领域经过科学研究；文本经过科学编辑。韵律学、语音学和语文学的结构都是科学的。要么文学批评本身就是科学的，要么所有这些训练有素、才智过人的学者都在浪费时间研究某种伪科学，比如颅相学。然而，人们不禁要问，学者们是否意识到他们的工作是科学的这一事实的意义。随着二手资料的日益复杂化，人们逐渐失去了科学所特有的那种不断巩固进步的感觉。研究始于所谓的“背景”，人们理应期待它随着研究的深入，也能开始构建前景。告诉我们应该了解哪些关于文学的知识，就应该同时告诉我们文学是什么。一旦到了这一步，学术研究似乎就受到了某种阻碍，不得不退回到进一步的研究项目中。

It seems absurd to say that there may be a scientific element in criticism when there are dozens of learned journals based on the assumption that there is, and hundreds of scholars engaged in a scientific procedure related to literary criticism. Evidence is examined scientifically; previous authorities are used scientifically; fields are investigated scientifically; texts are edited scientifically. Prosody is scientific in structure; so is phonetics; so is philology. Either literary criticism is scientific, or all these highly trained and intelligent scholars are wasting their time on some kind of pseudoscience like phrenology. Yet one is forced to wonder whether scholars realize the implications of the fact that their work is scientific. In the growing complication of secondary sources one misses that sense of consolidating progress which belongs to a science. Research begins in what is known as “background,” and one would expect it, as it goes on, to start organizing the foreground as well. Telling us what we should know about literature ought to fulfil itself in telling us something about what it is. As soon as it comes to this point, scholarship seems to be dammed by some kind of barrier, and washes back into further research projects.

因此，为了“欣赏”文学并与之建立更直接的联系，我们转向公共批评家，比如兰姆、哈兹利特、阿诺德或圣伯夫，他们代表着最专业、最明智的读者群体。公共批评家的任务是阐明一个有品位的人如何运用和评价文学，从而展现文学如何融入社会。但在这里，我们不再感受到一种客观的知识体系。公共批评家倾向于采用讲座和通俗散文等片段式的形式，他们的工作并非科学，而是另一种文学艺术。他们的思想源于对文学的实用研究，并不试图构建或融入某种理论框架。在莎士比亚批评领域，我们看到了约翰逊对奥古斯都时代品味的精彩诠释，柯勒律治对浪漫主义品味的体现，以及布拉德利对维多利亚时代品味的展现。我们认为，理想的莎士比亚批评家应该避免约翰逊、柯勒律治和布拉德利分别受到的奥古斯都时代、浪漫主义时期和维多利亚时代的局限和偏见。但是，我们对莎士比亚批评的发展历程并没有清晰的认识，也不清楚一位阅读过所有前人著作的批评家该如何才能……其结果，充其量不过是当代品味的丰碑，充满了局限性和偏见。

So to “appreciate” literature and get more direct contact with it, we turn to the public critic, the Lamb or Hazlitt or Arnold or Sainte-Beuve who represents the reading public at its most expert and judicious. It is the task of the public critic to exemplify how a man of taste uses and evaluates literature, and thus show how literature is to be absorbed into society. But here we no longer have the sense of an impersonal body of consolidating knowledge. The public critic tends to episodic forms like the lecture and the familiar essay, and his work is not a science, but another kind of literary art. He has picked up his ideas from a pragmatic study of literature, and does not try to create or enter into a theoretical structure. In Shakespearean criticism we have a fine monument of Augustan taste in Johnson, of Romantic taste in Coleridge, of Victorian taste in Bradley. The ideal critic of Shakespeare, we feel, would avoid the Augustan, Romantic, and Victorian limitations and prejudices respectively of Johnson, Coleridge, and Bradley. But we have no clear notion of progress in the criticism of Shakespeare, or of how a critic who read all his predecessors could, as a result, become anything better than a monument of contemporary taste, with all its limitations and prejudices.

换句话说，目前还没有办法区分真正的批评（因此有助于理解整个文学）和仅仅属于趣味史范畴的批评（因此只是追逐时髦偏见的摇摆不定）。我举一个例子来说明两者之间的区别，这简直是正面碰撞。约翰·罗斯金在他为《Munera Pulveris》所写的一条奇特、精彩却又杂乱无章的脚注中写道：

In other words, there is as yet no way of distinguishing what is genuine criticism, and therefore progresses toward making the whole of literature intelligible, from what belongs only to the history of taste, and therefore follows the vacillations of fashionable prejudice. I give an example of the difference between the two which amounts to a head-on collision. In one of his curious, brilliant, scatter-brained footnotes to Munera Pulveris, John Ruskin says:

关于莎士比亚笔下人物的名字，我稍后会详细论述；它们奇特地——有时甚至是粗野地——融合了各种传统和语言。其中三个含义最为清晰的名字，我们已经提及。苔丝狄蒙娜——“δυσδαιμουία”，意为“不幸的命运”——也十分直白。奥赛罗，我认为，意为“谨慎”；整部悲剧的灾难都源于他那看似强大却又脆弱的性格缺陷。奥菲莉娅，意为“贤良淑德”，是哈姆雷特真正失去的妻子，她的名字源于希腊语，因为她的哥哥莱尔特斯也叫奥菲莉娅；莱尔特斯临终前对她的遗言，巧妙地暗示了奥菲莉娅名字的含义，她温柔的珍贵与粗鄙无礼的教士形成了鲜明的对比：“当你哀嚎时，我的妹妹将成为你的守护天使。”

Of Shakspeare’s names I will afterwards speak at more length; they are curiously—often barbarously—mixed out of various traditions and languages. Three of the clearest in meaning have been already noticed. Desdemona—“δυσδαιμουία,”miserable fortune—is also plain enough. Othello is, I believe, “the careful”; all the calamity of the tragedy arising from the single flaw and error in his magnificently collected strength. Ophelia, “serviceableness,” the true, lost wife of Hamlet, is marked as having a Greek name by that of her brother Laertes; and its signification is once exquisitely alluded to in that brother’s last word of her, where her gentle preciousness is opposed to the uselessness of the churlish clergy:—“A ministering angel shall my sister be, when thou liest howling.”

马修·阿诺德对这段文字评论如下：

On this passage Matthew Arnold comments as follows:

哎，这真是太过分了！我并非说莎士比亚笔下人物名字的含义（暂且不论罗斯金先生的词源学解释是否正确）完全无关紧要，可以完全忽略；但如此强调名字的含义，无异于放任自流，忘却一切节制与平衡，彻底丧失理智。这无异于在评论中极尽夸张地展现狭隘的地域性。

Now, really, what a piece of extravagance all that is! I will not say that the meaning of Shakspeare’s names (I put aside the question as to the correctness of Mr. Ruskin’s etymologies) has no effect at all, may be entirely lost sight of; but to give it that degree of prominence is to throw the reins to one’s whim, to forget all moderation and proportion, to lose the balance of one’s mind altogether. It is to show in one’s criticism, to the highest excess, the note of provinciality.

无论罗斯金的观点是对是错，他都在尝试进行真正的批评。他试图用一套仅属于批评家的概念框架来解读莎士比亚，而这套框架又只与莎士比亚的剧作相关。阿诺德认为这种素材并非公众批评家可以直接使用的，他的看法完全正确。但他似乎甚至没有意识到这种批评的存在。这是一种系统性的批评，与趣味史截然不同。在这里，阿诺德显得目光短浅。罗斯金的技艺源于伟大的图像学传统，这一传统经由古典和圣经研究传承至但丁和斯宾塞——罗斯金曾仔细研读过这两位作家——并融入了他曾细致研究过的中世纪大教堂之中。阿诺德假定某些“显而易见”的批评公理是普遍的自然法则，这些公理在德莱顿时代之前几乎闻所未闻，而且肯定无法在弗洛伊德、荣格、弗雷泽和卡西尔的时代幸存下来。

Now whether Ruskin is right or wrong, he is attempting genuine criticism. He is trying to interpret Shakespeare in terms of a conceptual framework which belongs to the critic alone, and yet relates itself to the plays alone. Arnold is perfectly right in feeling that this is not the sort of material that the public critic can directly use. But he does not seem even to suspect the existence of a systematic criticism as distinct from the history of taste. Here it is Arnold who is the provincial. Ruskin has learned his trade from the great iconological tradition which comes down through Classical and Biblical scholarship into Dante and Spenser, both of whom he had studied carefully, and which is incorporated in the medieval cathedrals he had pored over in such detail. Arnold is assuming, as a universal law of nature, certain “plain sense” critical axioms which were hardly heard of before Dryden’s time and which can assuredly not survive the age of Freud and Jung and Frazer and Cassirer.

目前我们所看到的，一方面是学者为使“文学研究”成为可能而进行的工作，另一方面是假定其存在的公共批评家的工作。两者之间是“文学”本身，一个学生仅凭自身天赋智慧漫游其中的猎场。这种假设似乎认为，学者和公共批评家之间的联系仅仅在于对文学的共同兴趣。学者将他们的研究材料置于文学的门外：如同其他献给素未谋面的读者的供品一样，许多此类学术成果似乎源于一种颇为感人的信念，有时仅仅是希望未来某个综合性的批评救世主会发现它们有用。公共批评家，或者说这种强加的批评态度的代言人，往往只是随意地、漫不经心地使用这些材料，实际上常常像哈姆雷特对待掘墓人那样对待学者，对学者丢弃的一切视而不见，只捡起一个奇特的头骨，然后大加道德说教。

What we have so far is, on one side of the “study of literature,” the work of the scholar who tries to make it possible, and on the other side the work of the public critic who assumes that it exists. In between is “literature” itself, a game preserve where the student wanders with his native intelligence his only guide. The assumption seems to be that the scholar and the public critic are connected by a common interest in literature alone. The scholar lays down his materials outside the portals of literature: like other offerings brought to unseen consumers, a good deal of such scholarship seems to be the product of a rather touching faith, sometimes only a hope that some synthetizing critical Messiah of the future will find it useful. The public critic, or the spokesman of the imposed critical attitude, is apt to make only a random and haphazard use of this material, often in fact to treat the scholar as Hamlet did the grave-digger, ignoring everything he throws out except an odd skull which he can pick up and moralize about.

那些关注艺术的人常常会被问到一些问题，这些问题并非总是出于善意，比如他们所做的事情有何用途或价值。或许根本无法直接回答这些问题，或者至少无法回答提问者的问题。大多数答案，例如纽曼的“博雅知识本身就是目的”，仅仅诉诸于那些拥有正确经验的人的体验。同样，大多数“诗歌辩护”也只有那些身处辩护阵营的人才能理解。因此，批判性辩护的基础必须是对艺术的实际体验，而对于那些关注文学的人来说，首先要回答的问题不是“研究文学有什么用？”，而是“研究文学的可能性带来了什么？”

Those who are concerned with the arts are often asked questions, not always sympathetic ones, about the use or value of what they are doing. It is probably impossible to answer such questions directly, or at any rate to answer the people who ask them. Most of the answers, such as Newman’s “liberal knowledge is its own end,” merely appeal to the experience of those who have had the right experience. Similarly, most “defenses of poetry” are intelligible only to those well within the defenses. The basis of critical apologetics, therefore, has to be the actual experience of art, and for those concerned with literature, the first question to answer is not “What use is the study of literature?” but, “What follows from the fact that it is possible?”

凡是认真研究过文学的人都知道，其中涉及的思维过程与研究本身一样，都是连贯且循序渐进的。科学也是如此。思维训练与科学训练完全相同，对学科整体性的理解也类似。如果这种整体性源于文学本身，那么文学本身就必须像科学一样构建，这与我们对它的体验相矛盾；或者，它必须从存在的核心某种难以言喻的奥秘中汲取某种启示力量，而这种奥秘似乎很模糊；又或者，人们声称从文学中获得的那些精神益处是虚构的，实际上来源于与文学相关的其他学科的附带学习。

Everyone who has seriously studied literature knows that the mental process involved is as coherent and progressive as the study of science. A precisely similar training of the mind takes place, and a similar sense of the unity of the subject is built up. If this unity comes from literature itself, then literature itself must be shaped like a science, which contradicts our experience of it; or it must derive some informing power from an ineffable mystery at the heart of being, which seems vague; or the mental benefits alleged to be derived from it are imaginary, and are really derived from other subjects studied incidentally in connection with it.

我们只能假设学者和有品位的人之间仅仅因为对文学的共同兴趣而有所联系，并以此为前提得出这样的结论。如果这个假设成立，那么所有批评中普遍存在的大量无效性就必须正视，因为随着批评数量的增加，无效性只会越来越高，最终，批评，尤其对于大学教师而言，会变成一种机械式的获取功绩的方式，如同转动经轮一般。但这仅仅是一种无意识的假设——至少我从未见过它被当作教条提出——如果最终证明它是无稽之谈，那当然是件好事。另一种假设是，学者和公众批评家之间存在着一种中间形式的批评，一种逻辑严密、科学严谨的、连贯全面的文学理论，学生在学习过程中会不知不觉地习得其中的一些内容，但其主要原则我们目前尚不了解。这种批评的发展将满足研究中系统性和进步性的要素，因为它能像其他学科一样，将研究成果整合到一个统一的知识体系中。同时，这将为公众评论家和有品位的人在评论界树立权威。

This is as far as we can get on the assumption that the scholar and the man of taste are connected by nothing more than a common interest in literature. If this assumption is true, the high percentage of sheer futility in all criticism should be honestly faced, for the percentage can only increase with its bulk, until criticizing becomes, especially for university teachers, merely an automatic method of acquiring merit, like turning a prayer-wheel. But it is only an unconscious assumption—at least, I have never seen it stated as a doctrine—and it would certainly be convenient if it turned out to be nonsense. The alternative assumption is that scholars and public critics are directly related by an intermediate form of criticism, a coherent and comprehensive theory of literature, logically and scientifically organized, some of which the student unconsciously learns as he goes on, but the main principles of which are as yet unknown to us. The development of such a criticism would fulfil the systematic and progressive element in research by assimilating its work into a unified structure of knowledge, as other sciences do. It would at the same time establish an authority within criticism for the public critic and the man of taste.

我们应该谨慎地认识到这种中间批评的可能性意味着什么。它意味着文学本身永远无法被直接学习。物理学是一门关于自然的系统知识体系，学习物理学的学生会说他学习的是物理学，而不是自然。艺术，如同自然一样，必须与对它的系统研究（即批评）区分开来。因此，不可能“学习文学”：人们以某种​​方式了解文学，但间接地，他们所学到的是对文学的批评。同样，“教授文学”常常遇到的困难也源于它无法被教授这一事实：唯一可以直接教授的只有对文学的批评。文学不是研究对象，而是研究对象：它由文字构成，正如我们……我们所见所闻，使我们容易将其与语言学科混淆。图书馆将批评列为文学的一个分支，也反映了我们的这种困惑。然而，批评之于艺术，正如历史之于行动，哲学之于智慧：它是对人类创造力的一种语言模仿，而这种创造力本身并不言说。正如哲学家可以对任何事物进行哲学思考，历史学家可以对任何事物进行历史思考一样，批评家也应该能够构建并栖居于他自己的概念宇宙之中。这个批评宇宙似乎正是阿诺德文化概念中所蕴含的内容之一。

We should be careful to realize what the possibility of such an intermediate criticism implies. It implies that at no point is there any direct learning of literature itself. Physics is an organized body of knowledge about nature, and a student of it says that he is learning physics, not nature. Art, like nature, has to be distinguished from the systematic study of it, which is criticism. It is therefore impossible to “learn literature”: one learns about it in a certain way, but what one learns, transitively, is the criticism of literature. Similarly, the difficulty often felt in “teaching literature” arises from the fact that it cannot be done: the criticism of literature is all that can be directly taught. Literature is not a subject of study, but an object of study: the fact that it consists of words, as we have seen, makes us confuse it with the talking verbal disciplines. The libraries reflect our confusion by cataloguing criticism as one of the subdivisions of literature. Criticism, rather, is to art what history is to action and philosophy to wisdom: a verbal imitation of a human productive power which in itself does not speak. And just as there is nothing which the philosopher cannot consider philosophically, and nothing which the historian cannot consider historically, so the critic should be able to construct and dwell in a conceptual universe of his own. This critical universe seems to be one of the things implied in Arnold’s conception of culture.

因此，我并非认为当下的文学批评必然是错误的，或者应该另辟蹊径。我的意思是，我们应该能够全面了解它实际发挥的作用。学者和公众批评家必须继续为批评事业做出贡献。他们所贡献的成果不必像珊瑚虫看不到珊瑚岛那样隐形。在文学研究的过程中，学生会意识到一股暗流正将他们从文学本身带走。他们发现，文学是人文学科的核心分支，一边是历史，另一边是哲学。由于文学本身并非一个系统的知识体系，批评家不得不求助于历史学家的概念框架来理解事件，求助于哲学家的概念框架来理解思想。当被问及研究方向时，批评家们总是会说他们在研究约翰·邓恩、雪莱的思想、1640-1660年间的作品，或者给出其他一些暗示历史、哲学或文学本身才是其批评理论基础的答案。即便他真的关注批评理论，他也会说自己在研究一个“一般性”议题。显然，系统性批评的缺失造成了权力真空，所有邻近学科都纷纷涌入。因此，上文提到的阿基米德谬误才会如此盛行：这种谬误认为，只要我们足够坚定地立足于基督教、民主或马克思主义价值观，就能用辩证法撬起整个批评体系。然而，如果批评家们形形色色的兴趣能够与一个不断扩展的系统性理解模式联系起来，这种暗流就会消失，他们就会被视为正在向批评靠拢，而不是背离批评。

I am not, therefore, saying that literary criticism at present must be doing the wrong thing and ought to be doing something else. I am saying that it should be possible to get a comprehensive view of what it actually is doing. It is necessary that scholars and public critics should continue to make their contributions to criticism. It is not necessary that the thing they contribute to should be invisible, as the coral island is invisible to the polyp. In the study of literary scholarship the student becomes aware of an undertow carrying him away from literature. He finds that literature is the central division of the humanities, flanked on one side by history and on the other by philosophy. As literature is not itself an organized structure of knowledge, the critic has to turn to the conceptual framework of the historian for events, and to that of the philosopher for ideas. Asked what he is working on, the critic will invariably say that he is working on Donne, or Shelley’s thought, or the 1640-1660 period, or give some other answer implying that history, philosophy, or literature itself is the conceptual basis of his criticism. In the unlikely event that he was concerned with the theory of criticism, he would say that he was working on a “general” topic. It is clear that the absence of systematic criticism has created a power vacuum, and all the neighboring disciplines have moved in. Hence the prominence of the Archimedes fallacy mentioned above: the notion that if we plant our feet solidly enough in Christian or democratic or Marxist values we shall be able to lift the whole of criticism at once with a dialectic crowbar. But if the varied interests of critics could be related to a central expanding pattern of systematic comprehension, this undertow would disappear, and they would be seen as converging on criticism instead of running away from it.

系统性地理解某一学科实际上我们有能力编写一本阐述其基本原理的入门教科书。如果真有这样一本批评著作，内容会是怎样的，着实令人好奇。它不会从对第一个问题的明确回答开始：“什么是文学？”我们没有真正的标准来区分文学的语言结构和非文学的，也不知道该如何处理那些因为“文笔优美”、可以作为“背景知识”或仅仅因为被列入大学“经典著作”课程而被冠以“文学”之名的书籍。然后我们发现，我们找不到一个词，像诗歌中的“诗”或戏剧中的“剧”那样，用来描述文学作品。布莱克说概括是愚蠢的，这固然没错，但当我们身处原始社会，他们有词来指代白蜡树和柳树，却没有词来指代树时，我们不禁会想，是不是真的存在概括能力严重不足的情况。

One proof that a systematic comprehension of a subject actually exists is the ability to write an elementary textbook expounding its fundamental principles. It would be interesting to see what such a book on criticism would contain. It would not start with a clear answer to the first question of all: “What is literature?” We have no real standards to distinguish a verbal structure that is literary from one that is not, and no idea what to do with the vast penumbra of books that may be claimed for literature because they are written with “style,” or are useful as “background,” or have simply got into a university course of “great books.” We then discover that we have no word, corresponding to “poem” in poetry or “play” in drama, to describe a work of literary art. It is all very well for Blake to say that to generalize is to be an idiot, but when we find ourselves in the cultural situation of savages who have words for ash and willow and no word for tree, we wonder if there is not such a thing as being too deficient in the capacity to generalize.

手册第一页就到此为止。第二页本应解释文学中最具深远意义的事实——诗歌和散文在节奏上的区别。但似乎任何人都能在实践中做出的区分，在理论上却无法被任何批评家所理解。我们继续翻阅空白页。接下来要做的是概述文学的主要类别，例如戏剧、史诗、散文小说等等。至少亚里士多德认为这是批评的显而易见的第一步。我们发现，关于体裁的批评理论仍然停留在亚里士多德的阶段。“体裁”（genre）这个词本身在英语句子中就显得格格不入，因为它发音生硬，难以理解。大多数对“史诗”和“小说”这类体裁术语的批评尝试，主要趣味在于它们作为谣言心理学的例证。多亏了古希腊人，我们才能区分戏剧中的悲剧和喜剧，因此我们仍然倾向于认为，它们各自构成戏剧中不可分割的一部分。当我们谈到假面剧、歌剧、电影、芭蕾舞、木偶戏、神秘剧、道德剧、即兴喜剧和魔幻剧等艺术形式时，我们发现自己处境就像文艺复兴时期的医生一样，他们因为盖伦没有提及梅毒而拒绝治疗。

So much for page one of our handbook. Page two would be the place to explain what seems the most far-reaching of literary facts, the distinction in rhythm between verse and prose. But it appears that a distinction which anyone can make in practice cannot be made as yet by any critic in theory. We continue to riffle through the blank pages. The next thing to do is to outline the primary categories of literature, such as drama, epic, prose fiction, and the like. This at any rate is what Aristotle assumed to be the obvious first step in criticism. We discover that the critical theory of genres is stuck precisely where Aristotle left it. The very word “genre” sticks out in an English sentence as the unpronounceable and alien thing it is. Most critical efforts to handle such generic terms as “epic” and “novel” are chiefly interesting as examples of the psychology of rumor. Thanks to the Greeks, we can distinguish tragedy from comedy in drama, and so we still tend to assume that each is the half of drama that is not the other half. When we come to deal with such forms as the masque, opera, movie, ballet, puppet-play, mystery-play, morality, commedia dell’ arte, and Zauberspiel, we find ourselves in the position of the Renaissance doctors who refused to treat syphilis because Galen said nothing about it.

古希腊人几乎不需要对散文形式进行分类。我们虽然需要，却从未这样做过。和往常一样，我们没有一个词来指代散文小说，所以“小说”一词就包罗万象，从而失去了它作为文体名称的唯一真正意义。流通图书馆对虚构类和非虚构类作品的区分，介于讲述公认虚构故事的书籍和讲述其他一切事物的书籍之间，这种分类似乎已经足以让评论家们感到厌倦。如果被问及《格列佛游记》属于哪种散文小说形式，即使评论家们能给出“梅尼普式讽刺”的答案，也很少有人会认为这是理解这本书的必要知识，尽管对小说的本质有所了解无疑是理解严肃小说家的先决条件。其他散文形式的处境则更加糟糕。西方文学受《圣经》的影响远超其他任何书籍，但尽管评论家们对“来源”抱有敬意，他们对这种影响的了解也仅限于它的存在。圣经类型学如今已是死气沉沉的语言，以至于大多数读者，包括学者在内，都无法理解任何运用这种语言的诗歌的表面含义。诸如此类，不胜枚举。如果批评能够被理解为一门连贯而系统的学科，其基本原理能够向任何一个有智力的十九岁青年解释清楚，那么，从这种理解的角度来看，如今的批评家们对批评一无所知。如今的批评家们所拥有的，不过是一种没有教义的神秘宗教，而他们只是一群只能彼此交流或争论的入门者。

The Greeks hardly needed to develop a classification of prose forms. We do, but have never done so. We have, as usual, no word for a work of prose fiction, so the word “novel” does duty for everything, and thereby loses its only real meaning as the name of a genre. The circulating-library distinction between fiction and non-fiction, between books which are about things admitted not to be true and books which are about everything else, is apparently exhaustive enough for critics. Asked what form of prose fiction Gulliver’s Travels belongs to, there are few critics who, if they could give the answer “Menippean satire,” would regard it as knowledge essential for dealing with the book, although some notion of what a novel is is surely a prerequisite for dealing with a serious novelist. Other prose forms are even worse off. Western literature has been more influenced by the Bible than by any other book, but with all his respect for “sources,” the critic knows little more about that influence than the fact that it exists. Biblical typology is so dead a language now that most readers, including scholars, cannot construe the superficial meaning of any poem which employs it. And so on. If criticism could ever be conceived as a coherent and systematic study, the elementary principles of which could be explained to any intelligent nineteen-year-old, then, from the point of view of such a conception, no critic now knows the first thing about criticism. What critics now have is a mystery-religion without a gospel, and they are initiates who can communicate, or quarrel, only with one another.

我认为亚里士多德所说的诗学，指的是一种批评理论，其原则适用于整个文学领域，并能解释所有有效的批评方法。在我看来，亚里士多德研究诗歌的方式，就像生物学家研究生物系统一样，他辨别出诗歌的属和种，阐述文学经验的普遍规律，简而言之，他似乎相信存在一种关于诗歌的完全可理解的知识结构，这种知识结构并非诗歌本身，也不是对诗歌的体验，而是诗学。人们或许会认为，在亚里士多德之后的两千年文学活动之后，他关于诗学的观点，就像他对动物繁殖的观点一样，可以根据新的证据重新审视。与此同时，拜沃特译本《诗学》的开篇之语，依然是理解这一主题的绝佳入门，它描述了我一直努力遵循的研究方法：

A theory of criticism whose principles apply to the whole of literature and account for every valid type of critical procedure is what I think Aristotle meant by poetics. Aristotle seems to me to approach poetry as a biologist would approach a system of organisms, picking out its genera and species, formulating the broad laws of literary experience, and in short writing as though he believed that there is a totally intelligible structure of knowledge attainable about poetry which is not poetry itself, or the experience of it, but poetics. One would imagine that, after two thousand years of post-Aristotelian literary activity, his views on poetics, like his views on the generation of animals, could be re-examined in the light of fresh evidence. Meanwhile, the opening words of the Poetics, in the Bywater translation, remain as good an introduction to the subject as ever, and describe the kind of approach that I have tried to keep in mind for myself:

鉴于我们的主题是诗歌，我打算不仅谈论诗歌这门艺术的总体情况，还要谈论诗歌的各种类型及其各自的特点；谈论一首好诗所需的情节结构；谈论诗歌的组成部分的数量和性质；等等。还有其他与此相关的问题。让我们遵循自然顺序，从基本事实开始。

Our subject being poetry, I propose to speak not only of the art in general but also of its species and their respective capacities; of the structure of plot required for a good poem; of the number and nature of the constituent parts of a poem; and likewise of any other matters in the same line of inquiry. Let us follow the natural order and begin with the primary facts.

当然，文学只是众多艺术形式之一，但本书必须避免探讨诗学之外的美学问题。然而，每一种艺术都需要其自身的批评体系，而一旦美学成为对所有艺术的统一批评，而非如今这种现状，诗学自然会成为美学的一部分。

Of course literature is only one of many arts, but this book is compelled to avoid the treatment of aesthetic problems outside of poetics. Every art, however, needs its own critical organization, and poetics will form a part of aesthetics as soon as aesthetics becomes the unified criticism of all the arts instead of whatever it is now.

科学通常始于朴素归纳：它们首先倾向于将需要解释的现象视为数据。例如，物理学最初将直接的经验感觉（如冷、湿、干）视为基本原理。最终，物理学彻底转变，发现其真正的功能在于解释热和湿的本质。历史学起源于编年史；但古代编年史家与现代历史学家的区别在于，对编年史家而言，他所记录的事件本身就是历史的结构，而历史学家则将这些事件视为历史现象，并将其置于一个不仅更广阔而且形态迥异的概念框架中加以联系。同样，每一门现代科学都必须经历培根所说的（尽管是在另一个语境中）归纳飞跃，占据一个新的视角，从而能够将先前的数据视为需要解释的新事物。只要天文学家将天体的运动视为天文学的结构，他们自然就会认为自己的观点是固定不变的。一旦人们认为运动本身是可以解释的，运动的数学理论就成为了概念框架，从而为日心说和万有引力定律的提出扫清了障碍。只要生物学将动植物生命形式视为其研究对象，生物学的各个分支在很大程度上就只是对生命形式的分类罗列。而一旦需要解释的是生命形式本身的存在，进化论以及原生质和细胞的概念便涌入生物学，并使其焕然一新。

Sciences normally begin in a state of naive induction: they tend first of all to take the phenomena they are supposed to interpret as data. Thus physics began by taking the immediate sensations of experience, classified as hot, cold, moist, and dry, as fundamental principles. Eventually physics turned inside out, and discovered that its real function was rather to explain what heat and moisture were. History began as chronicle; but the difference between the old chronicler and the modern historian is that to the chronicler the events he recorded were also the structure of his history, whereas the historian sees these events as historical phenomena, to be connected within a conceptual framework not only broader but different in shape from them. Similarly each modern science has had to take what Bacon calls (though in another context) an inductive leap, occupying a new vantage ground from which it can see its former data as new things to be explained. As long as astronomers regarded the movements of heavenly bodies as the structure of astronomy, they naturally regarded their own point of view as fixed. Once they thought of movement as itself explicable, a mathematical theory of movement became the conceptual framework, and so the way was cleared for the heliocentric solar system and the law of gravitation. As long as biology thought of animal and vegetable forms of life as constituting its subject, the different branches of biology were largely efforts of cataloguing. As soon as it was the existence of forms of life themselves that had to be explained, the theory of evolution and the conceptions of protoplasm and the cell poured into biology and completely revitalized it.

我突然意识到，文学批评如今正处于一种如同原始科学般幼稚的归纳状态。它的研究对象——文学杰作——尚未被视为需要用概念框架来解释的现象。仅凭自身就足以构成批评的框架或结构。我认为，批评是时候跃升到一个新的高度，从中探寻其概念框架的组织形式或包含形式了。批评似乎迫切需要一个协调原则，一个核心假设，如同生物学中的进化论一样，将它所处理的现象视为整体的一部分。

It occurs to me that literary criticism is now in such a state of naive induction as we find in a primitive science. Its materials, the masterpieces of literature, are not yet regarded as phenomena to be explained in terms of a conceptual framework which criticism alone possesses. They are still regarded as somehow constituting the framework or structure of criticism as well. I suggest that it is time for criticism to leap to a new ground from which it can discover what the organizing or containing forms of its conceptual framework are. Criticism seems to be badly in need of a coordinating principle, a central hypothesis which, like the theory of evolution in biology, will see the phenomena it deals with as parts of a whole.

这种归纳飞跃的首要假设与任何科学的假设相同：即完全连贯性的假设。尽管这个假设看似简单，但一门科学需要很长时间才能发现它实际上是一个完全可理解的知识体系。在发现这一点之前，它并非作为一门独立的科学诞生，而只是其他学科内部的一个胚胎。物理学从“自然哲学”中诞生，社会学从“伦理哲学”中诞生，便可说明这一过程。现代科学的发展大致与其与数学的接近程度成正比。因此，物理学和天文学在文艺复兴时期开始形成现代形态，化学在十八世纪，生物学在十九世纪，社会科学在二十世纪。如果批评是一门科学，那么它显然是一门社会科学；即使它只是在今天才发展起来，至少也并非时代错置。与此同时，专业化的短视仍然是朴素归纳法不可分割的一部分。从这个角度来看，“一般性”问题是人类根本无法处理的，因为它们涉及一个极其庞大的领域。批评家就好比一位数学家，他必须处理如此庞大的数字，即使只是用传统的整数形式写出来，也得写到下一个冰河时代才能完成。批评家和数学家都必须设法发明一种不那么繁琐的符号系统。

The first postulate of this inductive leap is the same as that of any science: the assumption of total coherence. Simple as this assumption appears, it takes a long time for a science to discover that it is in fact a totally intelligible body of knowledge. Until it makes this discovery, it has not been born as an individual science but remains an embryo within the body of some other subject. The birth of physics from “natural philosophy” and of sociology from “moral philosophy” will illustrate the process. It is also approximately true that the modern sciences have developed in the order of their closeness to mathematics. Thus physics and astronomy began to assume their modern form in the Renaissance, chemistry in the eighteenth century, biology in the nineteenth, and the social sciences in the twentieth. If criticism is a science, it is clearly a social science, and if it is developing only in our day, the fact is at least not an anachronism. Meanwhile, the myopia of specialization remains an inseparable part of naive induction. From such a perspective, “general” questions are humanly impossible to deal with, because they involve “covering” a frighteningly large field. The critic is in the position of a mathematician who has to deal with numbers so large that it would keep him scribbling digits until the next ice age even to write them out in their conventional form as integers. Critic and mathematician alike will have somehow to invent a less cumbersome notation.

朴素归纳法完全从文学作品的列举式书目角度来理解文学：也就是说，它将文学视为大量零散的“作品”集合体或杂乱堆砌而成。显然，如果文学仅仅是这样，那么任何基于文学的系统性思维训练都将变得不可能。迄今为止，在文学中只发现了一个组织原则，即时间顺序原则。这便引出了“传统”这个神奇的词汇，这意味着，当我们看到这些杂乱的作品沿着时间线排列时，仅仅凭借顺序本身就赋予了它们某种连贯性。但即使是传统也无法解答我们所有的问题。历史让我们得以窥见这样一种可能性：文学可以被视为原始文化中相对有限且简单的公式体系的复杂化。我们随后意识到，后世文学与这些原始公式的关系绝非纯粹的复杂化，因为我们会在最伟大的经典作品中发现这些原始公式的重现——事实上，伟大的经典作品似乎普遍倾向于回归这些公式。这与我们所有人都有的感受不谋而合：对平庸艺术作品的研究仍然是一种随机且边缘化的批评体验，而深刻的杰作则引领我们到达一个临界点，在那里我们似乎能看到无数意义模式的汇聚。我们开始思考，我们是否可以将文学不仅视为在时间长河中不断复杂化的产物，而且视为从某种批评可以定位的中心向外扩展的概念空间。

Naive induction thinks of literature entirely in terms of the enumerative bibliography of literature: that is, it sees literature as a huge aggregate or miscellaneous pile of discrete “works.” Clearly, if literature is nothing more than this, any systematic mental training based on it becomes impossible. Only one organizing principle has so far been discovered in literature, the principle of chronology. This supplies the magic word “tradition,” which means that when we see the miscellaneous pile strung out along a chronological line, some coherence is given it by sheer sequence. But even tradition does not answer all our questions. Total literary history gives us a glimpse of the possibility of seeing literature as a complication of a relatively restricted and simple group of formulas that can be studied in primitive culture. We next realize that the relation of later literature to these primitive formulas is by no means purely one of complication, as we find the primitive formulas reappearing in the greatest classics—in fact there seems to be a general tendency on the part of great classics to revert to them. This coincides with a feeling we have all had: that the study of mediocre works of art remains a random and peripheral form of critical experience, whereas the profound masterpiece draws us to a point at which we seem to see an enormous number of converging patterns of significance. We begin to wonder if we cannot see literature, not only as complicating itself in time, but as spread out in conceptual space from some kind of center that criticism could locate.

显然，除非文学本身具备某种特质，否则批评就无法成为一门系统性的研究。因此，我们必须接受这样的假设：正如自然科学背后存在着某种自然秩序，文学也并非“作品”的简单堆砌，而是一种文字秩序。然而，对自然秩序的信念源于自然科学的可理解性；如果自然科学能够完全揭示自然秩序，那么它们的研究也就无从谈起。同样，批评若要成为一门科学，就必须完全可理解，但文学作为使这门科学成为可能的文字秩序，就我们所知，是新批评发现的取之不尽的源泉，即便新的文学作品不再创作，它依然如此。如此看来，试图在文学中寻找某种限制性原则来阻碍批评发展的做法是错误的。这种荒谬的量子批评公式，即批评家应该仅仅局限于从诗歌中“提取”出诗人可能模糊地意识到自己“放入”的东西，是缺乏系统批评所滋生的众多粗浅谬误之一。这种量子理论是文学中所谓的“过早目的论谬误”。在自然科学中，它对应于这样一种断言：某种现象之所以如此，是因为上帝以其不可测度的智慧创造了它。也就是说，批评家被认为没有任何概念框架：他的工作仅仅是把一首诗人精心填充了特定数量美感或效果的诗歌，然后……心满意足地将它们一个个取出，就像他的原型人物小杰克·荷马一样。

It is clear that criticism cannot be a systematic study unless there is a quality in literature which enables it to be so. We have to adopt the hypothesis, then, that just as there is an order of nature behind the natural sciences, so literature is not a piled aggregate of “works,” but an order of words. A belief in an order of nature, however, is an inference from the intelligibility of the natural sciences; and if the natural sciences ever completely demonstrated the order of nature they would presumably exhaust their subject. Similarly, criticism, if a science, must be totally intelligible, but literature, as the order of words which makes the science possible, is, so far as we know, an inexhaustible source of new critical discoveries, and would be even if new works of literature ceased to be written. If so, then the search for a limiting principle in literature in order to discourage the development of criticism is mistaken. The absurd quantum formula of criticism, the assertion that the critic should confine himself to “getting out” of a poem exactly what the poet may vaguely be assumed to have been aware of “putting in,” is one of the many slovenly illiteracies that the absence of systematic criticism has allowed to grow up. This quantum theory is the literary form of what may be called the fallacy of premature teleology. It corresponds, in the natural sciences, to the assertion that a phenomenon is as it is because Providence in its inscrutable wisdom made it so. That is, the critic is assumed to have no conceptual framework: it is simply his job to take a poem into which a poet has diligently stuffed a specific number of beauties or effects, and complacently extract them one by one, like his prototype Little Jack Homer.

发展真正诗学的第一步，是识别并摒弃毫无意义的批评，或者说，摒弃那些无助于构建系统知识体系的文学论述。这包括我们经常在评论的泛泛之谈、反思性评论、意识形态的结语以及其他对杂乱无章的主题采取宏观视角所产生的种种空洞无物的言论。它包括所有“最佳”小说、诗歌或作家的榜单，无论其优点是排他性还是包容性。它包括所有随意、感伤和带有偏见的价值判断，以及所有让诗人声誉在虚构的股票交易所中暴涨暴跌的文学闲谈。那位富有的投资者艾略特先生在抛售弥尔顿之后，现在又重新买入；邓恩的声誉可能已经达到顶峰，即将开始下滑；丁尼生的声誉或许会略有波动，但雪莱的声誉仍然低迷。这类事情不能纳入任何系统的研究范畴，因为系统的研究只能不断进步：任何犹豫不决、摇摆不定或反应迟钝的东西都不过是闲暇时代的闲谈。品味史与批评的结构无关，正如赫胥黎-威尔伯福斯之争与生物科学的结构无关一样。

The first step in developing a genuine poetics is to recognize and get rid of meaningless criticism, or talking about literature in a way that cannot help to build up a systematic structure of knowledge. This includes all the sonorous nonsense that we so often find in critical generalities, reflective comments, ideological perorations, and other consequences of taking a large view of an unorganized subject. It includes all lists of the “best” novels or poems or writers, whether their particular virtue is exclusiveness or inclusiveness. It includes all casual, sentimental, and prejudiced value-judgments, and all the literary chit-chat which makes the reputations of poets boom and crash in an imaginary stock exchange. That wealthy investor Mr. Eliot, after dumping Milton on the market, is now buying him again; Donne has probably reached his peak and will begin to taper off; Tennyson may be in for a slight flutter but the Shelley stocks are still bearish. This sort of thing cannot be part of any systematic study, for a systematic study can only progress: whatever dithers or vacillates or reacts is merely leisure-class gossip. The history of taste is no more a part of the structure of criticism than the Huxley-Wilberforce debate is a part of the structure of biological science.

我相信，如果坚持这一区分并将其应用于过去的批评家，他们关于真正批评的论述将会展现出惊人的共识，从而勾勒出一个连贯而系统的研究轮廓。在趣味史中，由于缺乏事实，所有真理都像黑格尔那样被分割成半真半假的论述以增强其锋芒，我们或许会觉得文学研究过于相对和主观，永远无法得出任何一致的结论。但由于趣味史与批评之间并无内在联系，因此很容易将其分离。艾略特先生的论文《批评的功能》开篇便提出一个原则：现存的文学丰碑本身构成了一种理想的秩序，而不仅仅是个人作品的集合。这才是批评，而且是非常根本的批评。本书的大部分内容都试图对此进行阐释。本书的严谨性体现在其与历代优秀批评家提出的其他数百条论述的一致性上。接下来是一场修辞辩论，将传统及其对立面拟人化，使其成为相互对立的力量。前者被冠以天主教和古典主义的尊贵头衔，后者则被嘲讽为“辉格党”。这种现象令人困惑，直到我们意识到将其剔除并抛弃是多么容易。这场辩论针对的是米德尔顿·默里先生，人们对他赞许道，因为“他意识到有些立场是必须采取的，而且有时必须真正地舍弃某些东西，选择其他东西”。化学或语言学中不存在必须采取的立场，即便批评中存在，批评也并非真正的学术领域。因为在任何真正的学术领域，对“立场”挑战的唯一明智回应，正如福斯塔夫所说：“我这样做，违背了我的意愿。”一个人的“明确立场”是他的弱点，是他容易犯错和产生偏见的根源，而争取那些认同某种明确立场的人，只会像传染病一样加剧他的弱点。

I believe that if this distinction is maintained and applied to the critics of the past, what they have said about real criticism will show an astonishing amount of agreement, in which the outlines of a coherent and systematic study will begin to emerge. In the history of taste, where there are no facts, and where all truths have been, in Hegelian fashion, split into half-truths in order to sharpen their cutting edges, we perhaps do feel that the study of literature is too relative and subjective ever to make any consistent sense. But as the history of taste has no organic connection with criticism, it can easily be separated. Mr. Eliot’s essay The Function of Criticism begins by laying down the principle that the existing monuments of literature form an ideal order among themselves, and are not simply collections of the writings of individuals. This is criticism, and very fundamental criticism. Much of this book attempts to annotate it. Its solidity is indicated by its consistency with a hundred other statements that could be collected from the better critics of all ages. There follows a rhetorical debate which makes tradition and its opposite into personified and contending forces, the former dignified with the titles of Catholic and Classical, the latter ridiculed by the epithet “Whiggery.” This is the sort of thing that makes for confusion until we realize how easy it is to snip it off and throw it away. The debate is maintained against Mr. Middleton Murry, who is spoken of approvingly because “he is aware that there are definite positions to be taken, and that now and then one must actually reject something and select something else.” There are no definite positions to be taken in chemistry or philology, and if there are any to be taken in criticism, criticism is not a field of genuine learning. For in any field of genuine learning, the only sensible response to the challenge “stand” is Falstaff’s “so I do, against my will.” One’s “definite position” is one’s weakness, the source of one’s liability to error and prejudice, and to gain adherents to a definite position is only to multiply one’s weakness like an infection.

下一步是要意识到批评领域涉及众多学科，批评家必须以任何能够确保自身独立性的方式与它们建立联系。他或许想了解一些自然科学，但无需浪费时间去模仿它们的方法。我听说某处有一篇博士论文，列出了哈代所有小说的阴郁程度百分比，但这种做法并不值得提倡。批评家或许想了解一些社会科学，但例如，根本不存在所谓的社会学“方法”来研究文学。社会学家完全可以专门研究文学材料，但如果他这样做，就不应该关注文学价值。在他的研究领域，霍雷肖·阿尔杰和《艾尔西》系列小说的作者可能比霍桑或梅尔维尔更重要，《女士家庭杂志》的一期内容可能胜过亨利·詹姆斯的所有作品。同样，批评家也无需受制于社会学价值观，因为有利于伟大艺术诞生的社会条件未必是社会科学的研究对象。批评家或许需要了解一些宗教知识，但按照神学标准，一首正统的宗教诗歌比一首异端的宗教诗歌更能令人满意地表达其内容：这在批评中是荒谬的，混淆这两个领域的标准毫无益处。

The next step is to realize that criticism has a great variety of neighbors, and that the critic must enter into relations with them in any way that guarantees his own independence. He may want to know something of the natural sciences, but he need waste no time in emulating their methods. I understand that there is a Ph.D. thesis somewhere which displays a list of Hardy’s novels in the order of the percentages of gloom they contain, but one does not feel that that sort of procedure should be encouraged. The critic may want to know something of the social sciences, but there can be no such thing as, for instance, a sociological “approach” to literature. There is no reason why a sociologist should not work exclusively on literary material, but if he does he should pay no attention to literary values. In his field Horatio Alger and the writer of the Elsie books may well be more important than Hawthorne or Melville, and a single issue of the Ladies’ Home Journal worth all of Henry James. The critic is similarly under no obligation to sociological values, as the social conditions favorable to the production of great art are not necessarily those at which the social sciences aim. The critic may need to know something of religion, but by theological standards an orthodox religious poem will give a more satisfactory expression of its content than a heretical one: this makes nonsense in criticism, and there is nothing to be gained by confusing the standards of the two subjects.

文学一直被认为是一种可销售的产品，其生产者是富有创造力的作家，其消费者是受过良好教育的人士。读者群体以评论家为首。从这个角度来看，评论家正如我们开篇所比喻的那样，是中间人。他享有批发商的一些特权，例如免费的评测样书，但他的功能，与书商不同，本质上是一种消费者研究。我认为文学中存在第二种分工，它与其他形式的思维建构一样，既有理论也有实践。文学实践者和文学生产者并不完全相同，尽管他们有很多重叠之处；文学理论家和文学消费者则完全不同，即使他们同时存在于同一个人身上。本书假定文学理论与文学实践一样，首先是一种人文主义和自由主义的追求。因此，尽管它假定某些文学价值是理所当然的，并认为这些价值已由批评经验充分确立，但它并不直接关注价值判断。这一点需要解释，因为价值判断通常被认为是人文主义和自由主义追求的显著特征，而且就我所知，这种看法或许是正确的。

Literature has been always recognized to be a marketable product, its producers being the creative writers and its consumers the cultivated readers, with the critics at their head. From this point of view the critic is, in the metaphor of our opening page, the middleman. He has some wholesaler’s privileges, such as free review copies, but hiş function, as distinct from the bookseller’s, is essentially a form of consumer’s research. I recognize a second division of labor in literature, which, like other forms of mental construction, has a theory and a practice. The practitioner of literature and the producer of literature are not quite the same, though they overlap a good deal; the theorist of literature and the consumer of literature are not the same at all, even when they co-exist in the same man. The present book assumes that the theory of literature is as primary a humanistic and liberal pursuit as its practice. Hence, although it takes certain literary values for granted, as fully established by critical experience, it is not directly concerned with value-judgements. This fact needs explanation, as the value-judgement is often, and perhaps rightly for all I know, regarded as the distinguishing feature of the humanistic and liberal pursuit.

价值判断的主观性体现在它们只能间接传递，而不能直接传递。当它们流行或被普遍接受时，看起来似乎是客观的，但也仅此而已。可论证的价值判断是文学批评中诱人的胡萝卜，每一种新的批评潮流，例如当前流行的繁复修辞分析，都伴随着一种信念：批评终于找到了区分优秀与平庸的终极方法。但这最终总是被证明是品味历史的幻象。价值判断建立在文学研究之上；而文学研究永远不可能建立在价值判断之上。我们说，莎士比亚是1600年前后一群英国剧作家中的一员，也是世界伟大的诗人之一。前半部分是事实陈述，后半部分是被普遍接受以至于被误认为是事实陈述的价值判断。但它并非事实陈述。这仍然是一种价值判断，任何系统性的批评都无法与之相提并论。

Value-judgements are subjective in the sense that they can be indirectly but not directly communicated. When they are fashionable or generally accepted, they look objective, but that is all. The demonstrable value-judgement is the donkey’s carrot of literary criticism, and every new critical fashion, such as the current fashion for elaborate rhetorical analysis, has been accompanied by a belief that criticism has finally devised a definitive technique for separating the excellent from the less excellent. But this always turns out to be an illusion of the history of taste. Value-judgements are founded on the study of literature; the study of literature can never be founded on value-judgements. Shakespeare, we say, was one of a group of English dramatists working around 1600, and also one of the great poets of the world. The first part of this is a statement of fact, the second a value-judgement so generally accepted as to pass for a statement of fact. But it is not a statement of fact. It remains a value-judgement, and not a shred of systematic criticism can ever be attached to it.

价值判断有两种类型：比较价值判断和实证价值判断。基于比较价值的批评根据艺术作品被视为产品还是财产，可分为两大类。前者发展出传记批评，主要将艺术作品与其创作者联系起来。后者我们可以称之为“热带批评”，它主要关注当代读者。传记批评则主要关注伟大与个人权威的比较问题。它将诗歌视为创作者的演说，并且只有在诗歌背后存在一个明确的、最好是英雄式的个性时，它才会感到最有把握。如果找不到这样的个性，它可能会试图从修辞的虚幻中构建出一个，就像卡莱尔在其关于莎士比亚是“英雄”诗人的文章中所做的那样。热带批评比较的是风格和技巧，是意义的复杂性和比喻的运用。它往往不喜欢并贬低雄辩的诗人，而且几乎无法处理英雄式的个性。两者本质上都是修辞批评的形式，因为一种关注说服性演讲的修辞，另一种关注语言装饰的修辞，但两者都对另一种修辞抱有怀疑。

There are two types of value-judgements, comparative and positive. Criticism founded on comparative values falls into two main divisions, according to whether the work of art is regarded as a product or as a possession. The former develops biographical criticism, which relates the work of art primarily to the man who wrote it. The latter we may call tropical criticism, and it is primarily concerned with the contemporary reader. Biographical criticism concerns itself largely with comparative questions of greatness and personal authority. It regards the poem as the oratory of its creator, and it feels most secure when it knows of a definite, and preferably heroic, personality behind the poetry. If it cannot find such a personality, it may try to project one out of rhetorical ectoplasm, as Carlyle does in his essay on Shakespeare as a “heroic” poet. Tropical criticism deals comparatively with style and craftsmanship, with complexity of meaning and figurative assimilation. It tends to dislike and belittle the oratorical poets, and it can hardly deal at all with heroic personality. Both are essentially rhetorical forms of criticism, as one deals with the rhetoric of persuasive speech and the other with the rhetoric of verbal ornament, but each distrusts the other’s kind of rhetoric.

修辞价值判断与社会价值观密切相关，通常要经过一套道德隐喻的检验：真诚、简洁、精妙、朴实等等。但由于诗学尚不成熟，将修辞学不合理地延伸到文学理论中便会产生谬误。这种谬误的典型特征是选择性地接受传统，阿诺德的“试金石”理论对此进行了清晰的阐释。在该理论中，我们从试金石所代表的价值直觉出发，构建了一套将诗人划分等级的体系。通过衡量诗句的重量来比较诗人的做法（这并非什么新鲜事，阿里斯托芬在《蛙》中就曾嘲讽过）被传记批评家和文学批评家广泛采用，其主要目的是为了否定那些被归入对立阵营的诗人。

Rhetorical value-judgements are closely related to social values, and are usually cleared through a customs-house of moral metaphors: sincerity, economy, subtlety, simplicity, and the like. But because poetics is undeveloped, a fallacy arises from the illegitimate extension of rhetoric into the theory of literature. The invariable mark of this fallacy is the selected tradition, illustrated with great clarity in Arnold’s “touchstone” theory, where we proceed from the intuition of value represented by the touchstone to a system of ranking poets in classes. The practice of comparing poets by weighing their lines (no new invention, as it was ridiculed by Aristophanes in The Frogs) is used by both biographical and tropical critics, mainly in order to deny first-class rating to those in favor with the opposite group.

然而，当我们审视阿诺德的试金石技巧时，他的动机便会引发一些疑问。《暴风雨》中的“在黑暗的、倒退的、时间的深渊里”这句台词作为试金石台词再合适不过了。人们总觉得“裁缝或许能挠挠她痒处”这句台词不太合适，尽管它同样具有莎士比亚风格，对同一部剧也同样至关重要。（当然，这种批评方式的极端形式会否认这一点，并坚持认为这句台词是庸俗之辈添加的。）显然，这里运用了一种比纯粹的戏剧评论更具选择性的原则。

When we examine the touchstone technique in Arnold, however, certain doubts arise about his motivation. The line from The Tempest, “In the dark backward and abysm of time,” would do very well as a touchstone line. One feels that the line “Yet a tailor might scratch her where’er she did itch” somehow would not do, though it is equally Shakespearean and equally essential to the same play. (An extreme form of the same kind of criticism would, of course, deny this and insist that the line had been interpolated by a vulgar hack.) Some principle is clearly at work here which is much more highly selective than a purely critical experience of the play would be.

阿诺德的“高度严肃”显然与此密切相关史诗和悲剧因为描写统治阶级人物，且要求高雅的礼仪，所以被认为是文学形式中的贵族。他所有一级文学的标杆都来自史诗和悲剧，或者以史诗和悲剧的标准来评判。因此，他将乔叟和伯恩斯降级到二级，似乎是出于一种观念，即喜剧和讽刺应该像它们所象征的道德标准和社会阶层一样，保持其应有的地位。我们开始怀疑，文学价值判断是社会价值判断的投射。阿诺德为什么要给诗人分级？他说，当我们使那些诗人很难留在一级文学行列时，我们会更加钦佩他们。这显然是无稽之谈，我们必须进一步探究。当我们读到“在诗歌中，区分优劣……至关重要……因为诗歌肩负着崇高的使命”时，我们开始有所领悟。我们看到，阿诺德试图用诗歌创造新的圣经经典，以此作为指导社会原则的准则，他希望文化能够取代宗教。

Arnold’s “high seriousness” evidently is closely connected with the view that epic and tragedy, because they deal with ruling-class figures and require the high style of decorum, are the aristocrats of literary forms. All his Class One touchstones are from, or judged by the standards of, epic and tragedy. Hence his demotion of Chaucer and Burns to Class Two seems to be affected by a feeling that comedy and satire should be kept in their proper place, like the moral standards and the social classes which they symbolize. We begin to suspect that the literary value-judgements are projections of social ones. Why does Arnold want to rank poets? He says that we increase our admiration for those who manage to stay in Class One after we have made it very hard for them to do so. This being clearly nonsense, we must look further. When we read “in poetry the distinction between excellent and inferior … is of paramount importance … because of the high destinies of poetry,” we begin to get a clue. We see that Arnold is trying to create a new scriptural canon out of poetry to serve as a guide for those social principles which he wants culture to take over from religion.

将批评视为一种社会态度的应用，是我们所说的批评领域权力真空的必然结果。系统性的研究应在归纳经验和演绎原则之间交替进行。在批评中，修辞分析提供了一些归纳方法，而作为批评理论的诗学则应是演绎方法的对应物。由于缺乏诗学，批​​评家只能依赖于其作为社会人所形成的偏见。因为偏见本质上是不充分的演绎，头脑中的偏见永远只能是一个被掩盖的主要前提，就像一座冰山。

The treatment of criticism as the application of a social attitude is a natural enough result of what we have called the power vacuum in criticism. A systematic study alternates between inductive experience and deductive principles. In criticism rhetorical analysis provides some of the induction, and poetics, the theory of criticism, should be the deductive counterpart. There being no poetics, the critic is thrown back on prejudice derived from his existence as a social being. For prejudice is simply inadequate deduction, as a prejudice in the mind can never be anything but a major premise which is mostly submerged, like an iceberg.

阿诺德的观点带有偏见并不难察觉，因为他的观点已经过时；但当“高度严肃性”变成“成熟”，或者其他一些更现代的批评修辞中常用的有力论据时，就更难看出其中的偏见了。更难理解的是，当“如果被困在荒岛上，你会带哪些书”这个古老的问题，从它原本所属的客厅游戏，变成了一个据称构成民主价值观圣经的昂贵图书馆。修辞价值判断通常取决于礼仪问题，而礼仪的核心概念是高雅、中庸和低俗风格之间的区别。这些风格是由社会阶级结构决定的，批评如果不想否定文学经验的一半事实，显然必须从一个理想的无阶级社会的视角来看待艺术。阿诺德本人也指出了这一点，他说“文化寻求……”“废除阶级。”据我所知，文学作品中所有刻意构建的价值等级都基于某种隐蔽的社会、道德或知识类比。无论这种类比是保守浪漫的（如阿诺德的作品），还是激进的（如萧伯纳的作品），将喜剧、讽刺以及散文和理性置于首位，都适用这一原则。那些用来贬低某些作家作品的传播力的种种借口——比如晦涩难懂、淫秽不堪、虚无主义、反动等等——通常都掩盖着一种观念：既得利益的社会或知识阶层所持有的礼仪观念要么应该得到维护，要么应该受到挑战。这些社会观念不断变化，如同风扇在灯光下转动，而这种变化又激发了人们的信念：后世终将发现艺术的全部真相。

It is not hard to see prejudice in Arnold, because his views have dated: it is a little harder when “high seriousness” becomes “maturity,” or some other powerful persuader of more recent critical rhetoric. It is harder when the old question of what books one would take to a desert island emerges from parlor games, where it belongs, into an expensive library alleged to constitute the scriptural canon of democratic values. Rhetorical value-judgements usually turn on questions of decorum, and the central conception of decorum is the difference between high, middle, and low styles. These styles are suggested by the class structure of society, and criticism, if it is not to reject half the facts of literary experience, obviously has to look at art from the standpoint of an ideally classless society. Arnold himself points this out when he says that “culture seeks to do away with classes.” Every deliberately constructed hierarchy of values in literature known to me is based on a concealed social, moral, or intellectual analogy. This applies whether the analogy is conservative and Romantic, as it is in Arnold, or radical, giving the top place to comedy, satire, and the values of prose and reason, as it is in Bernard Shaw. The various pretexts for minimizing the communicative power of certain writers, that they are obscure or obscene or nihilistic or reactionary or what not, generally turn out to be disguises for a feeling that the views of decorum held by the ascendant social or intellectual class ought to be either maintained or challenged. These social fixations keep changing, like a fan turning in front of a light, and the changing inspires the belief that posterity eventually discovers the whole truth about art.

因此，对传统的选择性解读，必然暗藏着某种极端批判的陷阱。这并非意味着要将整个文学作品都作为研究的基础，而是从中抽象出一种传统（或者，当然，是“唯一”的传统），并将其与当代社会价值观联系起来，进而用来论证这些价值观。我们邀请犹豫不决的读者尝试以下练习：随机挑选三位文学巨匠，列出八种可能的升格和降格组合（以简化的两级分类为基础），并逐一进行辩护。例如，如果挑选的三位是莎士比亚、弥尔顿和雪莱，那么讨论的议程将是：

A selective approach to tradition, then, invariably has some ultra-critical joker concealed in it. There is no question of accepting the whole of literature as the basis of study, but a tradition (or, of course, “the” tradition) is abstracted from it and attached to contemporary social values, being then used to document those values. The hesitant reader is invited to try the following exercise. Pick three big names at random, work out the eight possible combinations of promotion and demotion (on a simplified, or two-class, basis) and defend each in turn. Thus if the three names picked were Shakespeare, Milton, and Shelley, the agenda would run :

1. 将雪莱降级，理由是与其他作家相比，他的技巧和思想深度不够成熟。

1. Demoting Shelley, on the ground that he is immature in technique and profundity of thought compared to the others.

2. 将弥尔顿降级，理由是他的宗教蒙昧主义和沉重的教义内容损害了他言论的自发性。

2. Demoting Milton, on the ground that his religious obscurantism and heavy doctrinal content impair the spontaneity of his utterance.

3. 贬低莎士比亚，理由是他脱离思想，导致他的戏剧反映的是生活，而不是对生活的创造性改进。

3. Demoting Shakespeare, on the ground that his detachment from ideas makes his dramas a reflection of life rather than a creative attempt to improve it.

4. 提倡莎士比亚，理由是他保持了诗歌视野的完整性，而其他作家的诗歌视野却被说教所掩盖。

4. Promoting Shakespeare, on the ground that he preserves an integrity of poetic vision which in the others is obfuscated by didacticism.

5. 提倡弥尔顿，理由是他对信仰最高奥秘的洞察使他超越了莎士比亚一成不变的世俗和雪莱的幼稚。

5. Promoting Milton, on the ground that his penetration of the highest mysteries of faith raises him above Shakespeare’s unvarying worldliness and Shelley’s callowness.

6. 提倡雪莱，理由是他热爱自由。相比那些接受过时社会或宗教价值观的诗人，它更能直接触动现代人的心灵。

6. Promoting Shelley, on the ground that his love of freedom speaks to the heart of modern man more immediately than poets who accepted outworn social or religious values.

7. 推广这三者（为此，应该使用一种特殊的风格，我们可以称之为结尾演讲风格）。

7. Promoting all three (for this a special style, which we may call the peroration style, should be used).

8. 以法国、古典或中国的标准来衡量，英国天才的桀骜不驯为由，将这三种天才都降级。

8. Demoting all three, on the ground of the untidiness of English genius when examined by French or Classical or Chinese standards.

读者或许会对某些所谓的“立场”比其他立场更感兴趣，从而被诱导认为其中必定有一方是正确的，并且必须做出判断。然而，在完成这项任务之前，他很快就会意识到，整个过程不过是道德审查员引发的焦虑神经症，毫无实质内容可言。当然，除了道德家之外，还有一些诗人只认为那些听起来像自己作品的诗人才是真正的诗人；还有一些评论家，他们热衷于用贴着“弥尔顿”或“雪莱”标签的玩具士兵进行宗教、反宗教或政治运动，而不是真正研究诗歌；还有一些学生，他们迫切希望尽可能多地阅读有益的书籍，却发现这些阅读都是多余的。但即便所有这些因素结合在一起，也无法构成真正的批评。

The reader may sympathize with some of these “positions,” as they are called, more than with others, and so be seduced into thinking that one of them must be right, and that it is important to decide which one it is. But long before he has finished his assignment he will realize that the whole procedure involved is an anxiety neurosis prompted by a moral censor, and is totally devoid of content. Of course, in addition to the moralists, there are poets who regard only those other poets as authentic who sound like themselves; there are critics who enjoy making religious, anti-religious, or political campaigns with toy soldiers labelled “Milton” or “Shelley” more than they enjoy studying poetry; there are students who have urgent reasons for making as much edifying reading as possible superfluous. But a conspiracy even of all these still does not make criticism.

因此，外加于批评的社会辩证法，在批评内部则沦为伪辩证法或虚假修辞。接下来需要探讨的是，如何界定批评的真正辩证法。在此层面，传记批评家转变为历史批评家。他从英雄崇拜走向全面且不加区分的接纳：在他研究的领域内，没有什么是他不愿饶有兴趣阅读的。然而，从纯粹的历史视角来看，文化现象应当在其自身的语境中解读，而非应用于当代语境。我们研究它们如同研究星辰，观察它们之间的相互关系，却不去接近它们。因此，历史批评需要一种源于热带批评的相应活动来补充。

The social dialectics applied externally to criticism, then, are, within criticism, pseudo-dialectics, or false rhetoric. It remains to try to define the true dialectic of criticism. On this level the biographical critic becomes the historical critic. He develops from hero-worship towards total and indiscriminate acceptance: there is nothing “in his field” that he is not prepared to read with interest. From a purely historical point of view, however, cultural phenomena are to be read in their own context without contemporary application. We study them as we do the stars, seeing their interrelationships but not approaching them. Hence historical criticism needs to be complemented by a corresponding activity growing out of tropical criticism.

我们可以称之为伦理批判，将伦理理解为对社会存在的一种意识，而非将社会事实与预设价值进行修辞上的比较。作为一种批判范畴，这便是文化在社群中真实存在的感知。因此，伦理批判将艺术视为从过去到现在的沟通，并基于对过去文化的全面且同时拥有的观念。一种排他性的奉献如果忽视历史批评，就会天真地将所有文化现象生硬地套用我们自己的语言，而罔顾其原本的本质。作为历史批评的平衡力量，它旨在表达所有艺术的当代影响，而不偏袒任何传统。每一种新的批评风潮都会提升某些诗人的地位，同时贬低另一些诗人，正如大约二十五年前，人们对玄学派诗人的兴趣日益浓厚，导致浪漫主义诗人的地位下降一样。从伦理层面来看，每一次对艺术的欣赏都是正确的，每一次对艺术的欣赏都是不正确的：批评不应反对事物，而应稳步迈向不加区分的包容性。奥斯卡·王尔德曾说，只有拍卖师才能对所有类型的艺术都抱有同样的欣赏：他当然指的是公共批评家，但即便公共批评家的工作——将文化瑰宝送到真正需要它们的人手中——在很大程度上也是拍卖师的工作。如果这句话对王尔德适用，那么对学术批评家来说就更加适用了。

We may call this ethical criticism, interpreting ethics not as a rhetorical comparison of social facts to predetermined values, but as the consciousness of the presence of society. As a critical category this would be the sense of the real presence of culture in the community. Ethical criticism, then, deals with art as a communication from the past to the present, and is based on the conception of the total and simultaneous possession of past culture. An exclusive devotion to it, ignoring historical criticism, would lead to a naive translation of all cultural phenomena into our own terms without regard to their original character. As a counterweight to historical criticism, it is designed to express the contemporary impact of all art, without selecting a tradition. Every new critical fashion has increased the appreciation of some poets and depreciated others, as the increase of interest in the metaphysical poets tended to depreciate the Romantics about twenty-five years ago. On the ethical level we can see that every increase of appreciation has been right, and every decrease wrong: that criticism has no business to react against things, but should show a steady advance toward undiscriminating catholicity. Oscar Wilde said that only an auctioneer could be equally appreciative of all kinds of art: he had of course the public critic in mind, but even the public critic’s job of getting the treasures of culture into the hands of the people who want them is largely an auctioneer’s job. And if this is true of him, it is a fortiori true of the scholarly critic.

因此，批评的辩证轴线一端是对文学数据的全然接受，另一端是对这些数据潜在价值的全然接受。这才是文化和博雅教育的真正境界，是学问滋养生命的境界，在这个境界中，学术的系统进步转化为品味和理解的系统进步。在这个境界中，人们不会急于做出重大的评判，也不会受到过度追求判断力所带来的种种弊端的影响，而正是这些弊端使得“批评家”一词沦为受过教育的泼妇的代名词。价值的比较评估实际上是从批评实践中得出的推论，而且这些推论在不言而喻时最为有效，而非指导其实践的明确原则。批评家很快就会发现，弥尔顿比布莱克莫尔更值得研究，也更具启发性。但这一点越是显而易见，批评家就越不想浪费时间在这一点上。因为批评家所能做的也只有这一点：任何出于确立或证明这一点的动机而进行的批评，都只不过是品味史中的又一份文献而已。毫无疑问，过去的文化中有很多东西对现在而言价值微乎其微。但是，艺术的可救赎性与不可救赎性之间的区别，是基于批评的全部经验而得出的，因此永远无法用理论来表述。诗人中有太多灰姑娘，太多石头。被一栋时髦建筑拒之门外的人，如今却成了下一个街角的领头羊。
