The dialectic axis of criticism, then, has as one pole the total acceptance of the data of literature, and as the other the total acceptance of the potential values of those data. This is the real level of culture and of liberal education, the fertilizing of life by learning, in which the systematic progress of scholarship flows into a systematic progress of taste and understanding. On this level there is no itch to make weighty judgements, and none of the ill effects which follow the debauchery of judiciousness, and have made the word critic a synonym for an educated shrew. Comparative estimates of value are really inferences, most valid when silent ones, from critical practice, not expressed principles guiding its practice. The critic will find soon, and constantly, that Milton is a more rewarding and suggestive poet to work with than Blackmore. But the more obvious this becomes, the less time he will want to waste in belaboring the point. For belaboring the point is all he can do: any criticism motivated by a desire to establish or prove it will be merely one more document in the history of taste. There is doubtless much in the culture of the past which will always be of comparatively slight value to the present. But the difference between redeemable and irredeemable art, being based on the total experience of criticism, can never be theoretically formulated. There are too many Cinderellas among the poets, too many stones rejected from one fashionable building that have become heads of the next corner.

因此，或许存在着诸如批评程序规则和法则之类的东西，它们指的是观察到的现象模式，即文学实践的规律。批评家们试图发现道德准则意义上的规则或法则，以此来指导艺术家应该做什么或已经做什么才能成为一名真正的艺术家，但这些努力都失败了。“诗歌，”雪莱说，“与声称要规范和限制其力量的艺术，无法共存。”这样的艺术并不存在，也从未存在过。用从属关系和价值判断来取代协调和描述，用“所有诗人都应该”来取代“有些诗人确实如此”，这仅仅表明所有相关的事实尚未被考虑在内。谓语中包含“必须”或“应该”的批评性陈述，要么是迂腐，要么是同义反复，这取决于人们是否认真对待它们。例如，一位戏剧评论家可能想说“所有戏剧都必须具有情节统一性”。如果他是个迂腐的人，他就会试图用具体的术语来定义情节统一性。但创造力是多变的，他迟早会发现自己会断言，某些声誉卓著、舞台表现力经受过反复验证的剧作家，其作品并不符合他所定义的“动作统一性”，因此根本算不上他眼中的戏剧。试图以更开放或更谨慎的态度运用这些原则的评论家，很快就会发现自己的观念变得狭隘，甚至不得不刻意掩饰自己其实是在说：“所有具有动作统一性的戏剧都必须具有动作统一性”，或者更简单、更常见的是：“所有好剧都必须是好剧”。

There may, then, be such things as rules of critical procedure, and laws, in the sense of the patterns of observed phenomena, of literary practice. All efforts of critics to discover rules or laws in the sense of moral mandates telling the artist what he ought to do, or have done, to be an authentic artist, have failed. “Poetry,” said Shelley, “and the art which professes to regulate and limit its powers, cannot subsist together.” There is no such art, and there never has been. The substitution of subordination and value-judgement for coordination and description, the substitution of “all poets should” for “some poets do,” is only a sign that all the relevant facts have not yet been considered. Critical statements with “must” or “should” in their predicates are either pedantries or tautologies, depending on whether they are taken seriously or not. Thus a dramatic critic may wish to say “all plays must have unity of action.” If he is a pedant, he will then try to define unity of action in specific terms. But creative power is versatile, and he is sure to find himself sooner or later asserting that some perfectly reputable dramatist, whose effectiveness on the stage has been proved over and over again, does not exhibit the unity of action he has defined, and is consequently not writing what he regards as plays at all. The critic who attempts to apply such principles in a more liberal or more cautious spirit will soon have to broaden his conceptions to the point, not of course of saying, but of trying to conceal the fact that he is saying, “all plays that have unity of action must have unity of action,” or, more simply and more commonly, “all good plays must be good plays.”

简而言之，批评，乃至整个美学，都必须学会效仿伦理学的做法。曾几何时，伦理学可以简单地将人的实际行为与人应有的行为（即所谓的“善”）进行比较。而所谓的“善”，往往就是作者习以为常且被其所在社群认可的行为。如今的伦理学作家虽然依然秉持价值观，但他们看待问题的方式却大相径庭。然而，在伦理学领域早已过时的方法，在美学研究者中却依然盛行。批评家仍然可以将自己喜欢的东西定义为真正的艺术，并进而断言，自己不喜欢的东西，按照这个定义，就不是真正的艺术。这种论证方式极具说服力。循环论证的优点在于它无可辩驳，但这只是表象，而非实质。

Criticism, in short, and aesthetics generally, must learn to do what ethics has already done. There was a time when ethics could take the simple form of comparing what man does with what he ought to do, known as the good. The “good” invariably turned out to be whatever the author of the book was accustomed to and found sanctioned by his community. Ethical writers now, though they still have values, tend to look at their problems rather differently. But a procedure which is hopelessly outmoded in ethics is still in vogue among writers on aesthetic problems. It is still possible for a critic to define as authentic art whatever he happens to like, and to go on to assert that what he happens not to like is, in terms of that definition, not authentic art. The argument has the great advantage of being irrefutable, as all circular arguments are, but it is shadow and not substance.

因此，那些令人厌恶的伟大比较，就让它自行消散吧，因为即便我们不得不认同它们，它们也只不过是些毫无意义的陈词滥调。评论家真正关注的是作品的积极价值，是诗歌本身的优秀，或者说是其真诚，而非作者的伟大。这样的评论能够产生基于深思熟虑的良好品味的直接价值判断，是对艺术脉搏的检验，是高度协调的神经系统对诗歌冲击的自律反应。任何理智的评论家都不会轻视这一点的重要性；然而，即便如此，也存在一些需要注意的地方。首先，认为良好品味的快速直觉判断是绝对正确的，这是一种迷信。良好品味源于文学研究并在此基础上发展；它的精准性来自知识，但知识本身并不产生知识。因此，任何评论家良好品味的准确性，都不能保证其基于文学经验的归纳基础是充分的。即使批评家学会了基于自身文学体验而非社会、道德、宗教或个人焦虑来做出判断，这种情况或许依然存在。诚实的批评家会不断发现自身品味中的盲点：他们发现自己有可能识别出某种有效的诗歌体验形式，而自己却无法真正领悟。

The odious comparisons of greatness, then, may be left to take care of themselves, for even when we feel obliged to assent to them they are still only unproductive platitudes. The real concern of the evaluating critic is with positive value, with the goodness, or perhaps the genuineness, of the poem rather than with the greatness of its author. Such criticism produces the direct value-judgement of informed good taste, the proving of art on the pulses, the disciplined response of a highly organized nervous system to the impact of poetry. No critic in his senses would try to belittle the importance of this; nevertheless there are some caveats even here. In the first place, it is superstition to believe that the swift intuitive certainty of good taste is infallible. Good taste follows and is developed by the study of literature; its precision results from knowledge, but does not produce knowledge. Hence the accuracy of any critic’s good taste is no guarantee that its inductive basis in literary experience is adequate. This may still be true even after the critic has learned to base his judgements on his experience of literature and not on his social, moral, religious, or personal anxieties. Honest critics are continually finding blind spots in their taste: they discover the possibility of recognizing a valid form of poetic experience without being able to realize it for themselves.

其次，积极的价值判断建立在直接体验之上，这种体验是批评的核心，却又永远被批评所排除在外。批评只能用批评术语来解释它，而这些术语永远无法重现或包含最初的体验。最初的体验就像对色彩的直接视觉感知，或对冷热的直接感觉，物理学对此的“解释”，从体验本身的角度来看，却完全无关紧要。无论品味和技巧如何规范，文学体验，如同文学本身一样，都无法言说。“如果我感觉自己的头顶仿佛被掀开了，”艾米莉·狄金森说，“我就知道这是诗。” 这句话完全正确，但它只与作为体验的批评相关。阅读文学作品，应该像福音书中的祈祷一样，走出批评的言辞世界，进入文学私密而隐秘的临在之中。否则，阅读就不是真正的文学体验，而仅仅是对批评惯例、记忆和偏见的反映。无法沟通的经验的存在批评的中心将始终保持批评的艺术性，只要批评家认识到批评源于批评中心，但不能建立在批评中心之上。

In the second place, the positive value-judgement is founded on a direct experience which is central to criticism yet forever excluded from it. Criticism can account for it only in critical terminology, and that terminology can never recapture or include the original experience. The original experience is like the direct vision of color, or the direct sensation of heat or cold, that physics “explains” in what, from the point of view of the experience itself, is a quite irrelevant way. However disciplined by taste and skill, the experience of literature is, like literature itself, unable to speak. “If I feel physically as if the top of my head were taken off,” said Emily Dickinson, “I know this is poetry.” This remark is perfectly sound, but it relates only to criticism as experience. The reading of literature should, like prayer in the Gospels, step out of the talking world of criticism into the private and secret presence of literature. Otherwise the reading will not be a genuine literary experience, but a mere reflection of critical conventions, memories, and prejudices. The presence of incommunicable experience in the center of criticism will always keep criticism an art, as long as the critic recognizes that criticism comes out of it but cannot be built on it.

因此，尽管批评家品味的正常发展方向是趋向更大的宽容和包容，但作为知识的批评是一回事，而受品味影响的价值判断则是另一回事。试图将文学的直接体验融入批评的框架，会产生前文已论述过的品味史中的种种偏差。反之，试图将批评融入直接体验，则会破坏二者的完整性。直接体验，即便面对已被阅读数百遍的作品，也力求每次都带来新鲜感，而如果诗歌本身被对诗歌的批评性解读所取代，这显然是不可能的。将我关于批评作为知识应当不断进步、不排斥任何事物的观点引入直接体验，意味着后者应当趋向于对所有文字作品都感到麻木和满足，这并非我所期望的。

Thus, though the normal development of a critic’s taste is toward greater tolerance and catholicity, still criticism as knowledge is one thing, and value-judgements informed by taste are another. The attempt to bring the direct experience of literature into the structure of criticism produces the aberrations of the history of taste already dealt with. The attempt to reverse the procedure and bring criticism into direct experience will destroy the integrity of both. Direct experience, even if it is concerned with something already read hundreds of times, still tries to be a new and fresh experience each time, which is clearly impossible if the poem itself has been replaced by a critical view of the poem. To bring my own view that criticism as knowledge should constantly progress and reject nothing into direct experience would mean that the latter should progress toward a general stupor of satisfaction with everything written, which is not quite what I have in mind.

最后，通过不断直接体验文学而培养的技能是一种特殊的技能，如同弹钢琴一般，而非像在浴室唱歌那样，是对生活的一种普遍态度的表达。评论家拥有由其性情以及与文字的每一次接触所形成的、主观的经验背景，包括报纸、广告、谈话、电影，以及他九岁时读过的所有书籍。他应对文学作品的特殊技能，与这种包含所有私人记忆、联想和任意偏见的主观背景截然不同，就像读温度计与打哆嗦截然不同一样。再者，任何具有批判能力的人都曾体验过从某件事物中获得的强烈而深刻的愉悦，同时又对其本身评价不高。基于主观愉悦和对艺术的特定反应是同一事物、源于同一事物或最终成为同一事物的假设，必然存在数十种批评和美学理论。然而，任何一个没有患上严重妄想症的有教养的人都知道，它们始终是不同的。或者，理想价值可能与实际价值截然不同。批评家可能会花费一篇论文、一本书，甚至毕生精力去研究他坦率承认为三流的作品，仅仅因为它与他认为足够重要的其他作品相关。据我所知，没有任何批评理论真正考虑到了不同的体系。批评中最常见的做法之一所隐含的价值评估。

Finally, the skill developed from constant practice in the direct experience of literature is a special skill, like playing the piano, not the expression of a general attitude to life, like singing in the shower. The critic has a subjective background of experience formed by his temperament and by every contact with words he has made, including newspapers, advertisements, conversations, movies, and whatever he read at the age of nine. He has a specific skill in responding to literature which is no more like this subjective background, with all its private memories, associations, and arbitrary prejudices, than reading a thermometer is like shivering. Again, there is no one of critical ability who has not experienced intense and profound pleasure from something simultaneously with a low critical valuation of what produced it. There must be several dozen critical and aesthetic theories based on the assumption that subjective pleasure and the specific response to art are, or develop from, or ultimately become, the same thing. Yet every cultivated person who is not suffering from advanced paranoia knows that they are constantly distinct. Or, again, the ideal value may be quite different from the actual one. A critic may spend a thesis, a book, or even a life work on something that he candidly admits to be third-rate, simply because it is connected with something else that he thinks sufficiently important for his pains. No critical theory known to me takes any real account of the different systems of valuation implied by one of the most common practices of criticism.

既然我们已经本着法律的精神清扫了诠释者的客厅，拂去了尘埃，我们将再次尝试，运用我们所拥有的任何启示之膏。我的论战文章是用第一人称复数写成的，而且与其说是论战，不如说是忏悔，这一点几乎无需赘述。同样显而易见的是，只有那些对本书目标有足够的共鸣，能够忽略（并非忽视，而是超越）任何在他看来不足或错误之处的读者，才能读懂这本书。我确信，如果我们等待一位完全合格的评论家来探讨这些文章的主题，我们将等待很长时间。为了使本书的篇幅控制在能够写作和出版的范围内，我采用了演绎法，并在例证和说明方面进行了严格的筛选。本书的演绎推理仅限于战术方法，而且据我所知，书中没有任何原则被宣称为完美无缺、没有例外或反例的大前提。诸如“通常”、“一般”、“经常”或“一般”之类的表达方式在书中随处可见。读者总可以提出“那某某呢？”之类的异议，而这并不一定会推翻基于集体观察的论断；此外，还有许多“你会把某某放在哪里？”之类的问题，而笔者本人也无法回答。

Now that we have swept out our interpreter’s parlor in the spirit of the law, and raised the dust, we shall try it again with whatever unguents of revelation we may possess. It should hardly be necessary to point out that my polemic has been written in the first person plural, and is quite as much a confession as a polemic. It is clear, too, that a book of this kind can only be offered to a reader who has enough sympathy with its aims to overlook, in the sense not of ignoring but of seeing past, whatever strikes him as inadequate or simply wrong. I am convinced that if we wait for a fully qualified critic to tackle the subjects of these essays, we shall wait a long time. In order to keep the book within the bounds that would make it possible to write and publish it, I have proceeded deductively, and been rigorously selective in examples and illustrations. The deductiveness does not extend further than tactical method, and so far as I know there is no principle in the book which is claimed as a perfect major premise, without exceptions or negative instances. Such expressions as “normally,” “usually,” “regularly,” or “as a rule” are thickly strewn throughout. An objection of the- “what about so-and-so?” type may always be made by the reader without necessarily destroying statements based on collective observations, and there are many questions of the “where would you put so-and-so?” type that cannot be answered by the present writer.

然而，本书的图式化特征是刻意为之，经过长时间的思考，我对此也无法辩解。批评中存在分类，正如任何其他学科一样，分类的重要性远胜于某些精英阶层的优雅成就。许多批评家对诗学中任何形式的图式化都感到强烈的反感，这同样源于他们未能将批评作为一门知识体系与直接的文学体验区分开来——在文学体验中，每一次行为都是独一无二的，分类毫无意义。在接下来的篇章中，每当出现图式化时，我并不在意图式化的形式本身，这或许只是我缺乏创造力的结果。我预期，实际上也希望，其中许多图式化仅仅是脚手架，待建筑更加完善后便可拆除。其余部分则属于对艺术形式成因的系统研究。

Still, the schematic nature of this book is deliberate, and is a feature of it that I am unable, after long reflection, to apologize for. There is a place for classification in criticism, as in any other discipline which is more important than an elegant accomplishment of some mandarin caste. The strong emotional repugnance felt by many critics toward any form of schematization in poetics is again the result of a failure to distinguish criticism as a body of knowledge from the direct experience of literature, where every act is unique, and classification has no place. Whenever schematization appears in the following pages, no importance is attached to the schematic form itself, which may be only the result of my own lack of ingenuity. Much of it, I expect, and in fact hope, may be mere scaffolding, to be knocked away when the building is in better shape. The rest of it belongs to the systematic study of the formal causes of art.

第一篇论文

历史批评：模式理论

FIRST ESSAY

Historical Criticism: Theory of Modes

第一篇论文

First Essay

历史批评：模式理论

HISTORICAL CRITICISM: THEORY OF MODES

虚构模式：引言

FICTIONAL MODES: INTRODUCTION

在《诗学》第二段中，亚里士多德谈到小说作品之间的差异，这种差异源于作品中人物地位的不同。他指出，有些小说中的人物比我们更优秀，有些则比我们更糟糕，还有一些则与我们处于同一水平。这段文字并未引起现代批评家的太多关注，因为亚里士多德对善恶的重视似乎表明他对文学持有一种略显狭隘的道德主义观点。然而，亚里士多德用来表示“善”和“恶”的词语是希腊语的“spoudaios”和“phaulos”，它们具有象征意义上的“沉重”和“轻盈”。在文学作品中，情节由某人做某事构成。这个人，如果是一个个体，就是主人公；而他所做或未做的事情，则是他能够做到或本可以做到的事情，这取决于作者对他的设定以及由此产生的读者预期。因此，虚构作品的分类并非基于道德层面，而是基于主人公的行动能力，这种能力可能强于我们，也可能弱于我们，或者大致相同。例如：

IN THE SECOND paragraph of the Poetics Aristotle speaks of the differences in works of fiction which are caused by the different elevations of the characters in them. In some fictions, he says, the characters are better than we are, in others worse, in still others on the same level. This passage has not received much attention from modem critics, as the importance Aristotle assigns to goodness and badness seems to indicate a somewhat narrowly moralistic view of literature. Aristotle’s words for good and bad, however, are spoudaios and phaulos, which have a figurative sense of weighty and light. In literary fictions the plot consists of somebody doing something. The somebody, if an individual, is the hero, and the something he does or fails to do is what he can do, or could have done, on the level of the postulates made about him by the author and the consequent expectations of the audience. Fictions, therefore, may be classified, not morally, but by the hero’s power of action, which may be greater than ours, less, or roughly the same. Thus:

1. 如果英雄在本质上超越其他人，也超越其他人所处的环境，那么他就是神，关于他的故事就属于通常意义上的神话，即关于神的故事。这类故事在文学中占有重要地位，但通常不属于常规的文学范畴。

1. If superior in kind both to other men and to the environment of other men, the hero is a divine being, and the story about him will be a myth in the common sense of a story about a god. Such stories have an important place in literature, but are as a rule found outside the normal literary categories.

2. 如果英雄在程度上超越他人和周围环境，那么他就是典型的浪漫英雄，其行为令人惊叹，但他本身仍被视为凡人。浪漫英雄生活在一个自然法则略微失效的世界：对我们来说不自然的勇气和耐力，对他而言却是自然而然的；一旦浪漫的既定前提确立，魔法武器、会说话的动物、可怕的食人魔和女巫，以及拥有神奇力量的护身符，都不再违背任何概率法则。至此，我们从严格意义上的神话，过渡到了传说、民间故事、童话及其文学衍生品。

2. If superior in degree to other men and to his environment, the hero is the typical hero of romance, whose actions are marvellous but who is himself identified as a human being. The hero of romance moves in a world in which the ordinary laws of nature are slightly suspended: prodigies of courage and endurance, unnatural to us, are natural to him, and enchanted weapons, talking animals, terrifying ogres and witches, and talismans of miraculous power violate no rule of probability once the postulates of romance have been established. Here we have moved from myth, properly so called, into legend, folk tale, märchen, and their literary affiliates and derivatives.

3. 如果其地位高于其他人，但低于其自然环境，英雄是领袖。他拥有远超常人的权威、激情和表达能力，但他的所作所为既受社会批判的约束，也受自然秩序的制约。这是高阶模仿模式的英雄，是大多数史诗和悲剧的英雄，也是亚里士多德心目中典型的英雄类型。

3. If superior in degree to other men but not to his natural environment, the hero is a leader. He has authority, passions, and powers of expression far greater than ours, but what he does is subject both to social criticism and to the order of nature. This is the hero of the high mimetic mode, of most epic and tragedy, and is primarily the kind of hero that Aristotle had in mind.

4. 如果英雄既不凌驾于他人之上，也不凌驾于环境之上，那么他就是我们的一份子：我们能感受到他身上所体现的共同人性，并要求诗人遵循我们在自身经验中发现的同样的概率准则。这便造就了低级模仿模式中的英雄，也就是大多数喜剧和现实主义小说中的英雄。“高”与“低”并无价值比较之意，而纯粹是图解性的，正如它们指代圣经批评家或英国国教徒时那样。在这个层面上，保留“英雄”一词的难度——因为在前述模式中，“英雄”的含义更为有限——有时会令作者感到困扰。因此，萨克雷不得不称《名利场》为一部没有英雄的小说。

4. If superior neither to other men nor to his environment, the hero is one of us: we respond to a sense of his common humanity, and demand from the poet the same canons of probability that we find in our own experience. This gives us the hero of the low mimetic mode, of most comedy and of realistic fiction. “High” and “low” have no connotations of comparative value, but are purely diagrammatic, as they are when they refer to Biblical critics or Anglicans. On this level the difficulty in retaining the word “hero,” which has a more limited meaning among the preceding modes, occasionally strikes an author. Thackeray thus feels obliged to call Vanity Fair a novel without a hero.

5. 如果主人公在力量或智力上不如我们，以至于我们感到自己俯视着一个充满束缚、挫败或荒谬的场景，那么他就属于反讽模式。即使读者感觉自己身处或可能身处同样的境地，这一点仍然成立，因为这种境况是以更高自由的标准来评判的。

5. If inferior in power or intelligence to ourselves, so that we have the sense of looking down on a scene of bondage, frustration, or absurdity, the hero belongs to the ironic mode. This is still true when the reader feels that he is or might be in the same situation, as the situation is being judged by the norms of a greater freedom.

纵观这张表格，我们可以看出，在过去的十五个世纪里，欧洲小说的重心逐渐下移。在中世纪之前，文学与基督教、晚期古典主义、凯尔特或日耳曼神话紧密相连。如果基督教不是一种外来的神话，并且不吞噬其他神话，那么西方文学的这一阶段或许更容易被单独列出。就我们今天所见的形式而言，其中大部分已经归入了浪漫小说的范畴。浪漫小说主要分为两种形式：一种是世俗的，描写骑士精神和游侠故事；另一种是宗教的，讲述圣徒的传说。这两种形式都大量依赖于违反自然法则的神迹来吸引读者。浪漫小说主导了文学，直到文艺复兴时期对王子和朝臣的崇拜将高度模仿的模式推向前台。这种模式的特征在戏剧，特别是悲剧和民族史诗中体现得最为明显。随后，一种新型的中产阶级文化引入了低级模仿，这种模仿从笛福时代到十九世纪末在英国文学中占据主导地位。在法国文学中，这种模仿的兴起和结束时间则早了大约五十年。在过去的一百年里，大多数严肃小说越来越倾向于采用讽刺的手法。

Looking over this table, we can see that European fiction, during the last fifteen centuries, has steadily moved its center of gravity down the list. In the pre-medieval period literature is closely attached to Christian, late Classical, Celtic, or Teutonic myths. If Christianity had not been both an imported myth and a devourer of rival ones, this phase of Western literature would be easier to isolate. In the form in which we possess it, most of it has already moved into the category of romance. Romance divides into two main forms: a secular form dealing with chivalry and knight-errantry, and a religious form devoted to legends of saints. Both lean heavily on miraculous violations of natural law for their interest as stories. Fictions of romance dominate literature until the cult of the prince and the courtier in the Renaissance brings the high mimetic mode into the foreground. The characteristics of this mode are most clearly seen in the genres of drama, particularly tragedy, and national epic. Then a new kind of middle-class culture introduces the low mimetic, which predominates in English literature from Defoe’s time to the end of the nineteenth century. In French literature it begins and ends about fifty years earlier. During the last hundred years, most serious fiction has tended increasingly to be ironic in mode.

古典文学中也能找到类似的演变轨迹，尽管形式更为简略。在神话和多神教盛行的宗教中，存在着性关系错综复杂的化身、被神化的英雄和拥有神性血统的君王，同一个形容词“神一般的”既可以用来形容宙斯，也可以用来形容阿喀琉斯，在这种情况下，神话、浪漫和高度模仿的元素几乎无法完全分离。而在神学盛行的宗教中，则强调神性和人性之间的鲜明界限，浪漫元素则更为突出，例如基督教的骑士精神和圣洁传说、伊斯兰教的《一千零一夜》以及以色列的士师和先知的故事。同样，古典世界后期难以摆脱神性领袖的形象，很大程度上与低级模仿和反讽模式的萌芽发展不尽如人意有关，而这些模式在罗马讽刺文学中才刚刚起步。与此同时，高超的模仿模式的确立，以及一种贯穿始终、具有自然秩序意识的文学传统的形成，是希腊文明的伟大成就之一。据我所知，东方小说并没有真正摆脱神话和浪漫的模式。

Something of the same progression may be traced in Classical literature too, in a greatly foreshortened form. Where a religion is mythological and polytheistic, where there are promiscuous incarnations, deified heroes and kings of divine descent, where the same adjective “godlike” can be applied either to Zeus or to Achilles, it is hardly possible to separate the mythical, romantic, and high mimetic strands completely. Where the religion is theological, and insists on a sharp division between divine and human natures, romance becomes more clearly isolated, as it does in the legends of Christian chivalry and sanctity, in the Arabian Nights of Mohammedanism, in the stories of the judges and thaumaturgic prophets of Israel. Similarly, the inability of the Classical world to shake off the divine leader in its later period has much to do with the abortive development of low mimetic and ironic modes that got barely started with Roman satire. At the same time the establishing of the high mimetic mode, the developing of a literary tradition with a consistent sense of an order of nature in it, is one of the great feats of Greek civilization. Oriental fiction does not, so far as I know, get very far away from mythical and romantic formulas.

我们将主要探讨上文所述的西方文学五大时期，古典文学只是顺带提及。在每种时期，区分朴素文学和成熟文学都十分必要。我借用席勒关于朴素诗歌和感伤诗歌的论述中的“朴素”一词：我指的是原始的或通俗的，而席勒的原文则更接近古典风格。“感伤”一词在英语中还有其他含义，但我们目前缺乏足够的正式批评术语来取代它。因此，加引号的“感伤”指的是对早期文学模式的后世再现。例如，浪漫主义是浪漫故事的一种“感伤”形式，而童话在很大程度上是民间故事的一种“感伤”形式。此外，小说中主人公与社会隔绝和融入社会之间也存在着普遍的区别。这种区别体现在“悲剧”和“喜剧”这两个词上，它们指的是情节的一般特征，而不仅仅是戏剧形式。

We shall here deal chiefly with the five epochs of Western literature, as given above, using Classical parallels only incidentally. In each mode a distinction will be useful between naive and sophisticated literature. The word naive I take from Schiller’s essay on naive and sentimental poetry: I mean by it, however, primitive or popular, whereas in Schiller it means something more like Classical. The word sentimental also means something else in English, but we do not have enough genuine critical terms to dispense with it. In quotation marks, therefore, “sentimental” refers to a later recreation of an earlier mode. Thus Romanticism is a “sentimental” form of romance, and the fairy tale, for the most part, a “sentimental” form of folk tale. Also there is a general distinction between fictions in which the hero becomes isolated from his society, and fictions in which he is incorporated into it. This distinction is expressed by the words “tragic” and “comic” when they refer to aspects of plot in general and not simply to forms of drama.

悲剧小说模式

TRAGIC FICTIONAL MODES

当悲剧故事涉及神灵时，它们可以被称为狄俄尼索斯式的。这些故事讲述的是垂死的神祇，例如赫拉克勒斯身穿毒衣自焚，俄耳甫斯被酒神女祭司们撕成碎片，巴尔德被洛基的阴谋所害，基督死在十字架上，用“你为什么离弃我？”这句话表明，作为神圣的存在，他被排除在三位一体的群体之外。

Tragic stories, when they apply to divine beings, may be called Dionysiac. These are stories of dying gods, like Hercules with his poisoned shirt and his pyre, Orpheus tom to pieces by the Bacchantes, Balder murdered by the treachery of Loki, Christ dying on the cross and marking with the words “Why hast thou forsaken me?” a sense of his exclusion, as a divine being, from the society of the Trinity.

在文学作品中，将神祇之死与秋季或日落联系起来，并不一定意味着他是掌管植物或太阳的神，而仅仅意味着他是一位能够死亡的神，无论他掌管哪个领域。然而，由于神祇凌驾于自然和凡人之上，因此神祇之死恰如莎士比亚在《维纳斯与阿多尼斯》中所说的自然的“庄严同情”，这里的“庄严”一词与仪式有着一定的词源联系。当神祇成为故事的主角时，罗斯金的拟人谬误就很难说是谬误了，例如《十字架之梦》的诗人告诉我们，万物都为基督之死而哭泣。当然，在人与自然之间建立纯粹的想象联系本身并无谬误，但在一部更为现实主义的小说中使用“庄严同情”一词，表明作者试图赋予其主人公一些神话色彩。罗斯金举的拟人谬误的例子是金斯利那首关于溺亡少女的民谣中“残酷的、翻滚的泡沫”。但正是这种对泡沫的描述，使得金斯利笔下的玛丽隐隐带有了一丝安德洛墨达神话的色彩。

The association of a god’s death with autumn or sunset does not, in literature, necessarily mean that he is a god “of” vegetation or the sun, but only that he is a god capable of dying, whatever his department. But as a god is superior to nature as well as to other men, the death of a god appropriately involves what Shakespeare, in Venus and Adonis, calls the “solemn sympathy” of nature, the word solemn having here some of its etymological connections with ritual. Ruskin’s pathetic fallacy can hardly be a fallacy when a god is the hero of the action, as when the poet of The Dream of the Rood tells us that all creation wept at the death of Christ. Of course there is never any real fallacy in making a purely imaginative alignment between man and nature, but the use of “solemn sympathy” in a piece of more realistic fiction indicates that the author is trying to give his hero some of the overtones of the mythical mode. Ruskin’s example of a pathetic fallacy is “the cruel, crawling foam” from Kingsley’s ballad about a girl drowned in the tide. But the fact that the foam is so described gives to Kingsley’s Mary a faint coloring of the myth of Andromeda.

日落和落叶的意象在浪漫故事中依然存在，英雄依然是半神。在浪漫故事中，自然法则的失效和英雄事迹的个人化，将自然界简化为动植物世界。英雄的大部分时间都与动物相伴，或者至少与那些天生浪漫的动物——例如马、狗和猎鹰——相伴，而森林则是浪漫故事的典型背景。因此，英雄的死亡或孤寂如同灵魂脱离自然，唤起一种哀歌般的氛围。这种哀歌展现了一种不带讽刺意味的英雄主义。贝奥武夫之死的必然性、罗兰之死的背叛、殉道圣徒之死的恶意，其情感意义远胜于其中可能存在的任何傲慢和过失等讽刺意味。因此，挽歌中常常伴随着一种弥漫的、听天由命的、忧郁的时光流逝感，一种旧秩序改变并让位于新秩序的感伤。一、人们会想到贝奥武夫临终前凝望着那些在他面前消逝的历史时代的宏伟石碑。丁尼生的《亚瑟之死》以一种非常晚期的“感伤”形式，很好地捕捉到了同样的情绪。

The same associations with sunset and the fall of the leaf linger in romance, where the hero is still half a god. In romance the suspension of natural law and the individualizing of the hero’s exploits reduce nature largely to the animal and vegetable world. Much of the hero’s life is spent with animals, or at any rate the animals that are incurable romantics, such as horses, dogs, and falcons, and the typical setting of romance is the forest. The hero’s death or isolation thus has the effect of a spirit passing out of nature, and evokes a mood best described as elegiac. The elegiac presents a heroism unspoiled by irony. The inevitability in the death of Beowulf, the treachery in the death of Roland, the malignancy that compasses the death of the martyred saint, are of much greater emotional importance than any ironic complications of hybris and hamartia that may be involved. Hence the elegiac is often accompanied by a diffused, resigned, melancholy sense of the passing of time, of the old order changing and yielding to a new one: one thinks of Beowulf looking, while he is dying, at the great stone monuments of the eras of history that vanished before him. In a very late “sentimental” form the same mood is well caught in Tennyson’s Passing of Arthur.

悲剧，就其核心或高度模仿意义而言，即描写领袖陨落的虚构故事（领袖必须陨落，因为这是他与社会隔绝的唯一途径），融合了英雄主义与讽刺意味。在哀歌式的浪漫故事中，英雄的死亡主要是一种自然事实，是其人性的象征；而在高度模仿的悲剧中，它同时也是一种社会和道德事实。悲剧英雄必须具备恰当的英雄气概，但他的陨落既与他与社会的关系息息相关，也与自然法则至高无上的观念相关，而这两者都带有讽刺意味。悲剧主要属于五世纪雅典和十七世纪欧洲（从莎士比亚到拉辛）悲剧戏剧的两大本土发展脉络。这两个时期都属于贵族阶层迅速丧失实际权力但仍保留相当程度的意识形态威望的社会历史时期。

Tragedy in the central or high mimetic sense, the fiction of the fall of a leader (he has to fall because that is the only way in which a leader can be isolated from his society), mingles the heroic with the ironic. In elegiac romance the hero’s mortality is primarily a natural fact, the sign of his humanity; in high mimetic tragedy it is also a social and moral fact. The tragic hero has to be of a properly heroic size, but his fall is involved both with a sense of his relation to society and with a sense of the supremacy of natural law, both of which are ironic in reference. Tragedy belongs chiefly to the two indigenous developments of tragic drama in fifth-century Athens and seventeenth-century Europe from Shakespeare to Racine. Both belong to a period of social history in which an aristocracy is fast losing its effective power but still retains a good deal of ideological prestige.

在五种悲剧模式中，高模仿悲剧占据中心地位，它介于神一般的英雄主义和过于人性化的讽刺之间，这种平衡体现在传统的净化概念中。怜悯和恐惧这两个词可以理解为情感流动的两个大致方向：趋向某个对象或远离它。天真的浪漫故事更接近于愿望实现的梦想，它倾向于吸收情感，并将其内在传递给读者。因此，浪漫故事的特点在于接受怜悯和恐惧——在日常生活中，它们与痛苦相关——并将其视为快乐的形式。它将远距离的恐惧或惊恐转化为冒险；将接触时的恐惧或惊骇转化为奇妙；将无对象的恐惧或恐惧（焦虑）转化为沉思的忧郁。它将远距离的怜悯或关切转化为骑士拯救的主题；触碰时的怜悯或温柔，可以转化为一种慵懒而放松的魅力；而无对象的怜悯（这种怜悯没有明确的名称，但它是一种万物有灵论，或者说将自然界的一切事物都视为具有人类情感）则可以转化为富有创造性的幻想。在精致的浪漫故事中，这种形式特有的特征并不那么明显，尤其是在悲剧浪漫故事中，不可避免的死亡主题与奇幻元素相悖，常常迫使奇幻元素退居幕后。例如，在《罗密欧与朱丽叶》中，奇幻元素仅在墨丘西奥关于麦布女王的演讲中得以保留。但这部剧被认为比……更接近浪漫故事。后来的悲剧受到软化因素的影响，这些因素与宣泄作用的方向相反，可以说，它们抽走了主角们的讽刺意味。

The central position of high mimetic tragedy in the five tragic modes, balanced midway between godlike heroism and all-too-human irony, is expressed in the traditional conception of catharsis. The words pity and fear may be taken as referring to the two general directions in which emotion moves, whether towards an object or away from it. Naive romance, being closer to the wish-fulfilment dream, tends to absorb emotion and communicate it internally to the reader. Romance, therefore, is characterized by the acceptance of pity and fear, which in ordinary life relate to pain, as forms of pleasure. It turns fear at a distance, or terror, into the adventurous; fear at contact, or horror, into the marvellous, and fear without an object, or dread (Angst) into a pensive melancholy. It turns pity at a distance, or concern, into the theme of chivalrous rescue; pity at contact, or tenderness, into a languid and relaxed charm, and pity without an object (which has no name but is a kind of animism, or treating everything in nature as though it had human feelings) into creative fantasy. In sophisticated romance the characteristics peculiar to the form are less obvious, especially in tragic romance, where the theme of inevitable death works against the marvellous, and often forces it into the background. In Romeo and Juliet, for instance, the marvellous survives only in Mercutio’s speech on Queen Mab. But this play is marked as closer to romance than the later tragedies by the softening influences that work in the opposite direction from catharsis, draining off the irony, so to speak, from the main characters.

在高度模仿性的悲剧中，怜悯和恐惧分别成为有利和不利的道德判断，它们与悲剧相关，但并非悲剧的核心。我们怜悯苔丝狄蒙娜，畏惧伊阿古，但悲剧的核心人物是奥赛罗，我们对他的感情是复杂的。发生在悲剧英雄身上的所谓“悲剧”并不取决于他的道德地位。如果它与他的某种行为存在因果关系（通常如此），那么悲剧在于行为后果的必然性，而非行为本身的道德意义。因此，悲剧中出现了怜悯和恐惧被唤起又被抛弃的悖论。因此，亚里士多德所说的“缺陷”（hamartia）未必是罪行，更非道德软弱：它可能仅仅是指像科迪莉亚那样，身处险境却性格坚强。这种暴露在外的位置通常是领导者的位置，身处其中的人物既特立独行又孤立无援，从而呈现出悲剧特有的那种必然与不协调的奇特融合。这种领导者的过失性缺陷在朴素的高模仿性悲剧中体现得更为明显，例如《法官之镜》以及其他以命运之轮为主题的类似故事集。

In high mimetic tragedy pity and fear become, respectively, favorable and adverse moral judgement, which are relevant to tragedy but not central to it. We pity Desdemona and fear Iago, but the central tragic figure is Othello, and our feelings about him are mixed. The particular thing called tragedy that happens to the tragic hero does not depend on his moral status. If it is causally related to something he has done, as it generally is, the tragedy is in the inevitability of the consequences of the act, not in its moral significance as an act. Hence the paradox that in tragedy pity and fear are raised and cast out. Aristotle’s hamartia or “flaw,” therefore, is not necessarily wrongdoing, much less moral weakness: it may be simply a matter of being a strong character in an exposed position, like Cordelia. The exposed position is usually the place of leadership, in which a character is exceptional and isolated at the same time, giving us that curious blend of the inevitable and the incongruous which is peculiar to tragedy. The principle of the hamartia of leadership can be more clearly seen in naive high mimetic tragedy, as we get it in The Mirror for Magistrates and similar collections of tales based on the theme of the wheel of fortune.

在低级模仿悲剧中，怜悯和恐惧既不被净化，也不被融入享乐之中，而是以感官体验的形式外化。事实上，“耸人听闻”一词如果不仅仅是一种负面的价值判断，在批评中或许会有更有意义的含义。或许，用来形容低级模仿悲剧或家庭悲剧的最佳词汇是“悲情”（pathos），而悲情与眼泪这种感官反射密切相关。悲情将主人公描绘成因某种弱点而孤立无援，这种弱点之所以能引起我们的同情，是因为它与我们自身的经验水平相符。我所说的是主人公，但悲情的核心人物往往是女性或儿童（或者两者兼有，例如小伊娃和小内尔的死亡场景），从克拉丽莎·哈洛到哈代的苔丝，再到詹姆斯的黛西·米勒，英国低级模仿小说中充斥着大量令人心碎的女性牺牲形象。我们注意到，虽然悲剧可能会屠杀整个剧组，但悲情通常集中在一个角色身上，部分原因是低模仿社会更加个人化。

In low mimetic tragedy, pity and fear are neither purged nor absorbed into pleasures, but are communicated externally, as sensations. In fact the word “sensational” could have a more useful meaning in criticism if it were not merely an adverse value-judgement. The best word for low mimetic or domestic tragedy is, perhaps, pathos, and pathos has a close relation to the sensational reflex of tears. Pathos presents its hero as isolated by a weakness which appeals to our sympathy because it is on our own level of experience. I speak of a hero, but the central figure of pathos is often a woman or a child (or both, as in the death-scenes of Little Eva and Little Nell), and we have a whole procession of pathetic female sacrifices in English low mimetic fiction from Clarissa Harlowe to Hardy’s Tess and James’s Daisy Miller. We notice that while tragedy may massacre a whole cast, pathos is usually concentrated on a single character, partly because low mimetic society is more strongly individualized.

同样，与高度模仿性的悲剧相反，悲情情绪有所增加。受害者的无力表达往往令人悲悯。动物的死亡通常令人心碎，现代美国文学中常见的智力缺陷带来的灾难亦是如此。华兹华斯作为一位低级模仿艺术家，却是我们这个时代最伟大的悲情大师之一。他笔下的水手母亲用一种平淡、笨拙、荒谬而无力的语调讲述她如何努力抢救儿子的衣物和“其他财产”——或者说，在糟糕的批评毁了他的诗作之前，他是这样做的。悲情是一种奇特而阴森的情感，某种表达上的缺陷，无论是真实的还是人为的，似乎是它所特有的。它总是能让一首流畅哀婉的葬礼挽歌，转而去追寻像斯威夫特的《斯特拉》回忆录那样的悲情。高度表达的悲情很容易沦为一种虚假的自怜或煽情。低级模仿中对恐惧的利用也具有耸人听闻的效果，这是一种反向的悲情。这一传统中的可怕人物，以希斯克利夫、西蒙·莱格里和狄更斯笔下的反派为代表，通常是一个冷酷无情的人物，与某种细腻的美德形成鲜明对比，通常是他权力下的无助受害者。

Again, in contrast to high mimetic tragedy, pathos is increased by the inarticulateness of the victim. The death of an animal is usually pathetic, and so is the catastrophe of defective intelligence that is frequent in modern American literature. Wordsworth, who as a low mimetic artist was one of our great masters of pathos, makes his sailor’s mother speak in a flat, dumpy, absurdly inadequate style about her efforts to salvage her son’s clothes and “other property”—or did before bad criticism made him spoil his poem. Pathos is a queer ghoulish emotion, and some failure of expression, real or simulated, seems to be peculiar to it. It will always leave a fluently plangent funeral elegy to go and batten on something like Swift’s memoir of Stella. Highly articulate pathos is apt to become a factitious appeal to self-pity, or tear-jerking. The exploiting of fear in the low mimetic is also sensational, and is a kind of pathos in reverse. The terrible figure in this tradition, exemplified by Heathcliff, Simon Legree, and the villains of Dickens, is normally a ruthless figure strongly contrasted with some kind of delicate virtue, generally a helpless victim in his power.

悲情（pathos）的根本理念在于，个体试图融入某个社会群体却被排斥在外，而这种排斥感与我们自身的境遇息息相关。因此，高雅悲情的核心传统在于研究孤立的心灵，讲述一个与我们自身极为相似的个体如何因内心世界与外部世界、想象的现实与社会共识所构建的现实之间的冲突而崩溃的故事。这种悲剧可能像巴尔扎克作品中常见的那样，关注一种对向上攀升的狂热或执念，这构成了领袖陨落这一虚构主题的核心低级模仿对应物。或者，它可能探讨内心世界与外部生活的冲突，如《包法利夫人》和《吉姆爷》；也可能探讨僵化的道德观对经验的影响，如梅尔维尔的《皮埃尔》和易卜生的《布兰德》 。我们或许可以用希腊语“ alazon”来称呼这类人物，意为冒名顶替者，即假装或试图成为比自身更优秀之人。最受欢迎的alazon类型是miles gloriosus和博学的怪人或痴迷的哲学家。

The root idea of pathos is the exclusion of an individual on our own level from a social group to which he is trying to belong. Hence the central tradition of sophisticated pathos is the study of the isolated mind, the story of how someone recognizably like ourselves is. broken by a conflict between the inner and outer world, between imaginative reality and the sort of reality which is established by a social consensus. Such tragedy may be concerned, as it often is in Balzac, with a mania or obsession about rising in the world, this being the central low mimetic counterpart of the fiction of the fall of the leader. Or it may deal with the conflict of inner and outer life, as in Madame Bovary and Lord Jim, or with the impact of inflexible morality on experience, as in Melville’s Pierre and Ibsen’s Brand. The type of character involved here we may call by the Greek word alazon, which means impostor, someone who pretends or tries to be something more than he is. The most popular types of alazon are the miles gloriosus and the learned crank or obsessed philosopher.

我们最熟悉喜剧中的这类人物，在喜剧中，他们往往被置于外部视角，我们看到的只是他们的社会面具。但这种“虚荣心”也可能是悲剧英雄的一个面向：帖木儿和奥赛罗身上那种自负的气质显而易见，浮士德和哈姆雷特身上那种痴迷哲学家的气质也同样如此。研究一个痴迷的案例非常困难，甚至……从内部视角审视虚伪，尤其是在戏剧媒介中：即使是达尔杜弗，就其戏剧功能而言，也是对寄生而非虚伪的探讨。对痴迷的分析更自然地属于散文小说或类似勃朗宁独白的半戏剧媒介。尽管技巧和态度各有不同，康拉德的《吉姆爷》与那些自命不凡的人物有着血缘关系，与萧伯纳的塞尔吉乌斯或辛格的花花公子同属一脉，他们在戏剧和喜剧的背景下都是平行类型。当然，完全可以按照自己的标准来评判这种痴迷：例如，哥特式惊悚小说中那些神秘莫测、阴郁的英雄的创作者就采用了这种手法，他们眼神狂野或锐利，暗示着引人入胜的罪恶。其结果通常与其说是悲剧，不如说是某种可以被定义为没有幽默的喜剧的通俗剧。当这种现象浮现出来时，我们看到的是对痴迷的探讨，而这种痴迷的本质是恐惧而非怜悯：也就是说，痴迷表现为一种不受约束的意志，驱使受害者超越人类的正常极限。最明显的例子之一是希斯克利夫，他纵身跃入死亡，化身为吸血鬼；但这样的例子不胜枚举，从康拉德笔下的库尔茨到通俗小说中的疯狂科学家，不一而足。

We are most familiar with such characters in comedy, where they are looked at from the outside, so that we see only the social mask. But the alazon may be one aspect of the tragic hero as well: the touch of miles gloriosus in Tamburlaine, even in Othello, is unmistakable, as is the touch of the obsessed philosopher in Faustus and Hamlet. It is very difficult to study a case of obsession, or even hypocrisy, from the inside, in a dramatic medium: even Tartuffe, as far as his dramatic function is concerned, is a study of parasitism rather than hypocrisy. The analysis of obsession belongs more naturally to prose fiction or to a semi-dramatic medium like the Browning monologue. For all the differences in technique and attitude, Conrad’s Lord Jim is a lineal descendant of the miles gloriosus, of the same family as Shaw’s Sergius or Synge’s playboy, who are parallel types in a dramatic and comic setting. It is, of course, quite possible to take the alazon at his own valuation: this is done for instance by the creators of the inscrutable gloomy heroes in Gothic thrillers, with their wild or piercing eyes and their dark hints of interesting sins. The result as a rule is not tragedy so much as the kind of melodrama which may be defined as comedy without humor. When it rises out of this, we have a study of obsession presented in terms of fear instead of pity: that is, the obsession takes the form of an unconditioned will that drives its victim beyond the normal limits of humanity. One of the clearest examples is Heathcliff, who plunges through death itself into vampirism; but there are many others, ranging from Conrad’s Kurtz to the mad scientists of popular fiction.

反讽的概念最早出现在亚里士多德的《伦理学》中。在《伦理学》中， “eiron”指的是自贬之人，与“ alazon”相对。这样的人使自己刀枪不入，尽管亚里士多德并不赞同他，但毫无疑问，他是一位命中注定的艺术家，正如“ alazon”是他命中注定的受害者之一。因此，“反讽”一词指的是一种使自己看起来不如实际的技巧，在文学中最常见的是一种用最少的言辞表达最多含义的技巧，或者更广义地说，是一种避免直接陈述或回避其显而易见含义的语言模式。（我在这里使用“反讽”一词本身并没有什么不寻常的含义，尽管我正在探讨它的一些引申义。）

The conception of irony meets us in Aristotle’s Ethics, where the eiron is the man who deprecates himself, as opposed to the alazon. Such a man makes himself invulnerable, and, though Aristotle disapproves of him, there is no question that he is a predestined artist, just as the alazon is one of his predestined victims. The term irony, then, indicates a technique of appearing to be less than one is, which in literature becomes most commonly a technique of saying as little and meaning as much as possible, or, in a more general way, a pattern of words that turns away from direct statement or its own obvious meaning. (I am not using the word ironic itself in any unfamiliar sense, though I am exploring some of its implications.)

因此，反讽小说家会贬低自己，像苏格拉底一样，假装一无所知，甚至连自己是反讽者这件事也假装不知道。完全的客观性和对所有明确道德判断的压制是其方法的核心。因此，反讽艺术不会引发怜悯和恐惧：它们是由艺术本身反射给读者的。当我们试图将反讽本身分离出来时，我们会发现它似乎仅仅是诗人的一种态度，一种对文学形式的冷静建构，其中包含所有断言的元素，无论是隐含的还是明确的。反讽作为一种修辞手法，源于低级的模仿；它如实呈现生活本来的样子。但反讽者创作寓言故事时并不进行道德说教，其对象也仅限于主题本身。反讽本质上是一种高雅的修辞手法，高雅反讽与朴素反讽的主要区别在于，朴素反讽者会刻意强调自己是在使用反讽，而高雅反讽则只是陈述事实，让读者自行体会其中的反讽意味。柯勒律治在注意到笛福的一句反讽评论时指出，笛福的微妙之处可以通过过度使用斜体、破折号、感叹号以及其他表明作者有意使用反讽的符号而变得粗俗不堪。

The ironic fiction-writer, then, deprecates himself and, like Socrates, pretends to know nothing, even that he is ironic. Complete objectivity and suppression of all explicit moral judgements are essential to his method. Thus pity and fear are not raised in ironic art: they are reflected to the reader from the art. When we try to isolate the ironic as such, we find that it seems to be simply the attitude of the poet as such, a dispassionate construction of a literary form, with all assertive elements, implied or expressed, eliminated. Irony, as a mode, is born from the low mimetic; it takes life exactly as it finds it. But the ironist fables without moralizing, and has no object but his subject. Irony is naturally a sophisticated mode, and the chief difference between sophisticated and naive irony is that the naive ironist calls attention to the fact that he is being ironic, whereas sophisticated irony merely states, and lets the reader add the ironic tone himself. Coleridge, noting an ironic comment in Defoe, points out how Defoe’s subtlety could be made crude and obvious simply by over-punctuating the same words with italics, dashes, exclamation points, and other signs of being oneself aware of irony.

因此，悲剧反讽就变成了对悲剧性孤立本身的研究，从而剔除了其他所有模式中都或多或少存在的特殊案例因素。它的主人公未必具有任何悲剧性的过错或令人同情的执念：他只是一个与社会隔绝的人。因此，悲剧反讽的核心原则是，发生在主人公身上的任何特殊事件都应与其性格不符。悲剧之所以可理解，并非在于它具有某种现成的道德教条，而在于亚里士多德所说的发现或认知对于悲剧情节至关重要的意义。悲剧之所以可理解，是因为其灾难与其所处情境之间存在合理的关联。反讽从悲剧情境中剥离出任意性，剥离出受害者不幸、随机或抽签被选中、以及他并不比其他人更应承受其遭遇的意味。如果非要说选择他来应对灾难有什么理由，那也是个不充分的理由，而且它提出的反对意见比它能解答的问题还多。

Tragic irony, then, becomes simply the study of tragic isolation as such, and it thereby drops out the element of the special case, which in some degree is in all the other modes. Its hero does not necessarily have any tragic hamartia or pathetic obsession: he is only somebody who gets isolated from his society. Thus the central principle of tragic irony is that whatever exceptional happens to the hero should be causally out of line with his character. Tragedy is intelligible, not in the sense of having any pat moral to go with it, but in the sense that Aristotle had in mind when he spoke of discovery or recognition as essential to the tragic plot. Tragedy is intelligible because its catastrophe is plausibly related to its situation. Irony isolates from the tragic situation the sense of arbitrariness, of the victim’s having been unlucky, selected at random or by lot, and no more deserving of what happens to him than anyone else would be. If there is a reason for choosing him for catastrophe, it is an inadequate reason, and raises more objections than it answers.

因此，随着家庭悲剧讽刺意味的加深，一个典型的或随机的受害者形象开始在家庭悲剧中逐渐成形。我们可以称这个典型的受害者为“替罪羊” （pharmakos）。我们在霍桑的《海丝特·白兰》、梅尔维尔的《比利·巴德》、哈代的《苔丝》、达洛维夫人的《塞普蒂默斯》 、以及关于受迫害的犹太人和黑人的故事中，在那些天才使他们成为资产阶级社会中“以实玛利”的艺术家的故事中，都能遇到“替罪羊”的形象。“替罪羊”既非无辜也非有罪。说他是无辜的，是因为发生在他身上的事远远大于他所作所为所引发的后果，就像登山者的呼喊引发了雪崩一样。说他是有罪的，是因为他是罪恶社会的一员，或者生活在一个不公正现象不可避免地成为生存一部分的世界里。这两个事实无法结合起来；讽刺的是，它们始终彼此分离。简而言之，药剂师的处境与约伯类似。约伯可以为自己辩护，否认自己做了什么使他的灾难在道德上可以理解；但他辩护的成功反而使他的灾难在道德上变得不可理解。

Thus the figure of a typical or random victim begins to crystallize in domestic tragedy as it deepens in ironic tone. We may call this typical victim the pharmakos or scapegoat. We meet a pharmakos figure in Hawthorne’s Hester Prynne, in Melville’s Billy Budd, in Hardy’s Tess, in the Septimus of Mrs. Dalloway, in stories of persecuted Jews and Negroes, in stories of artists whose genius makes them Ishmaels of a bourgeois society. The pharmakos is neither innocent nor guilty. He is innocent in the sense that what happens to him is far greater than anything he has done provokes, like the mountaineer whose shout brings down an avalanche. He is guilty in the sense that he is a member of a guilty society, or living in a world where such injustices are an inescapable part of existence. The two facts do not come together; they remain ironically apart. The pharmakos, in short, is in the situation of Job. Job can defend himself against the charge of having done something that makes his catastrophe morally intelligible; but the success of his defense makes it morally unintelligible.

因此，悲剧中融合的矛盾与必然，分离成两个对立的讽刺极点。一极是人生不可避免的讽刺。例如，卡夫卡《审判》中的主人公的遭遇，并非源于他所作所为，而是他自身存在的终结——他是一个“过于人性化”的存在。必然讽刺的原型是亚当，人性被判处死刑。另一极是人生不协调的讽刺，所有试图将罪责转嫁给受害者的努力，反而赋予了受害者某种无辜的尊严。不协调讽刺的原型是基督，这位完全无辜的受害者被排除在人类社会之外。介于两者之间的是悲剧的核心人物，他既是人，又具有英雄般的伟大，常常带有神性的暗示。他的原型是普罗米修斯，这位不朽的泰坦因与人类为友而被众神所抛弃。 《约伯记》并非普罗米修斯式的悲剧，而是一部充满悲剧色彩的讽刺作品，其中神性与人性的辩证关系得以展现。约伯试图将自己塑造成普罗米修斯式的悲剧人物，但他通过将自己辩解为上帝的受害者而失败了。

Thus the incongruous and the inevitable, which are combined in tragedy, separate into opposite poles of irony. At one pole is the inevitable irony of human life. What happens to, say, the hero of Kafka’s Trial is not the result of what he has done, but the end of what he is, which is an “all too human” being. The archetype of the inevitably ironic is Adam, human nature under sentence of death. At the other pole is the incongruous irony of human life, in which all attempts to transfer guilt to a victim give that victim something of the dignity of innocence. The archetype of the incongruously ironic is Christ, the perfectly innocent victim excluded from human society. Halfway between is the central figure of tragedy, who is human and yet of a heroic size which often has in it the suggestion of divinity. His archetype is Prometheus, the immortal titan rejected by the gods for befriending men. The Book of Job is not a tragedy of the Promethean type, but a tragic irony in which the dialectic of the divine and the human nature works itself out. By justifying himself as a victim of God, Job tries to make himself into a tragic Promethean figure, but he does not succeed.

这些引证或许有助于解释现代文学中一个原本令人费解的事实。反讽源于低级模仿：它始于现实主义和冷静的观察。但随着模仿的深入，它逐渐向神话靠拢，祭祀仪式和垂死之神的模糊轮廓开始在其中重现。我们所说的五种模式显然是循环往复的。这种神话在反讽中的重现，在卡夫卡和乔伊斯的作品中尤为明显。从某种角度来看，卡夫卡的作品可以被视为一系列对《约伯记》的评注，其中囊括了当代常见的悲剧反讽类型：犹太人、艺术家、普通人，以及一种忧郁的卓别林式小丑。而乔伊斯的《闪》则将这些元素以喜剧的形式融合在一起。然而，反讽式的神话在其他作品中也十分常见，许多反讽文学的特征若脱离神话便难以理解。亨利·詹姆斯主要从十九世纪的现实主义和自然主义作家那里学习写作技巧，但如果我们仅仅以低级的模仿标准来评判他的作品，例如《死者的祭坛》 ，我们应该称其为一系列匪夷所思的巧合、缺乏充分的动机和模棱两可的结论交织而成的产物。但如果我们将其视为一种反讽式的神话，讲述一个人的神明是另一个人的灵药，那么它的结构就变得简单而合乎逻辑了。

These references may help to explain something that might otherwise be a puzzling fact about modern literature. Irony descends from the low mimetic: it begins in realism and dispassionate observation. But as it does so, it moves steadily towards myth, and dim outlines of sacrificial rituals and dying gods begin to reappear in it. Our five modes evidently go around in a circle. This reappearance of myth in the ironic is particularly clear in Kafka and in Joyce. In Kafka, whose work, from one point of view, may be said to form a series of commentaries on the Book of Job, the common contemporary types of tragic irony, the Jew, the artist, Everyman, and a kind of sombre Chaplin clown, are all found, and most of these elements are combined, in a comic form, in Joyce’s Shem. However, ironic myth is frequent enough elsewhere, and many features of ironic literature are unintelligible without it. Henry James learned his trade mainly from the realists and naturalists of the nineteenth century, but if we were to judge, for example, the story called The Altar of the Dead purely by low mimetic standards, we should have to call it a tissue of improbable coincidence, inadequate motivation, and inconclusive resolution. When we look at it as ironic myth, a story of how the god of one person is the pharmakos of another, its structure becomes simple and logical.

漫画虚构模式

COMIC FICTIONAL MODES

喜剧的主题是社会融合，通常表现为将中心人物融入社会。与狄俄尼索斯之死相对应的神话喜剧是阿波罗式的，讲述的是英雄如何被众神接纳的故事。在古典文学中，接纳的主题贯穿于赫拉克勒斯、墨丘利和其他需要经历考验的神祇的故事中；而在基督教文学中，它是救赎的主题，或者更确切地说，是接纳的主题：但丁《神曲》结尾处的喜剧便是如此。与哀歌相对应的浪漫喜剧模式最好被描述为田园式，其主要载体是田园诗。由于喜剧的社会意义，田园诗无法像哀歌那样内省，但它保留了逃离社会的主题，甚至将乡村或边疆的简朴生活理想化（现代通俗文学中的田园诗是西部故事）。我们在哀歌中注意到的与动物和植物自然的密切联系，在田园诗中的绵羊和宜人的牧场（或牛和牧场）中再次出现；同样，与神话的轻松联系也体现在，这种意象经常被用来表达救赎的主题，就像在《圣经》中那样。

The theme of the comic is the integration of society, which usually takes the form of incorporating a central character into it. The mythical comedy corresponding to the death of the Dionysiac god is Apollonian, the story of how a hero is accepted by a society of gods. In Classical literature the theme of acceptance forms part of the stories of Hercules, Mercury, and other deities who had a probation to go through, and in Christian literature it is the theme of salvation, or, in a more concentrated form, of assumption: the comedy that stands just at the end of Dante’s Commedia. The mode of romantic comedy corresponding to the elegiac is best described as idyllic, and its chief vehicle is the pastoral. Because of the social interest of comedy, the idyllic cannot equal the introversion of the elegiac, but it preserves the theme of escape from society to the extent of idealizing a simplified life in the country or on the frontier (the pastoral of popular modern literature is the Western story). The close association with animal and vegetable nature that we noted in the elegiac recurs in the sheep and pleasant pastures (or the cattle and ranches) of the idyllic, and the same easy connection with myth recurs in the fact that such imagery is often used, as it is in the Bible, for the theme of salvation.

高模仿喜剧最鲜明的例证是阿里斯托芬的古喜剧。米南德的新喜剧则更接近低模仿喜剧，其模式经由普劳图斯和泰伦提乌斯传承至文艺复兴时期，因此社会喜剧始终带有浓厚的低模仿倾向。在阿里斯托芬的作品中，通常有一个中心人物，他顶着强大的阻力建立起自己的社会，逐一驱逐所有阻挠或剥削他的人，最终获得英雄般的胜利，拥有众多情妇，有时甚至被赋予重生之神的荣耀。我们注意到，正如悲剧中存在怜悯和恐惧的净化作用一样，古喜剧中也存在着相应的喜剧情感的净化作用，即同情和嘲讽。无论喜剧英雄的行为是明智还是愚蠢，是正直还是卑鄙，他最终都会获得胜利。因此，古希腊喜剧，如同同时期的悲剧一样，融合了英雄主义和讽刺意味。在一些剧作中，阿里斯托芬急于将自己对英雄行为的看法记录下来，这在一定程度上掩盖了这一事实，但他最伟大的喜剧《鸟》却在喜剧英雄主义和喜剧讽刺之间保持了精妙的平衡。

The clearest example of high mimetic comedy is the Old Comedy of Aristophanes. The New Comedy of Menander is closer to the low mimetic, and through Plautus and Terence its formulas were handed down to the Renaissance, so that there has always been a strongly low mimetic bias to social comedy. In Aristophanes there is usually a central figure who constructs his (or her) own society in the teeth of strong opposition, driving off one after another all the people who come to prevent or exploit him, and eventually achieving a heroic triumph, complete with mistresses, in which he is sometimes assigned the honors of a reborn god. We notice that just as there is a catharsis of pity and fear in tragedy, so there is a catharsis of the corresponding comic emotions, which are sympathy and ridicule, in Old Comedy. The comic hero will get his triumph whether what he has done is sensible or silly, honest or rascally. Thus Old Comedy, like the tragedy contemporary with it, is a blend of the heroic and the ironic. In some plays this fact is partly concealed by Aristophanes’ strong desire to get his own opinion of what the hero is doing into the record, but his greatest comedy, The Birds, preserves an exquisite balance between comic heroism and comic irony.

新喜剧通常展现一对年轻男女之间一段情欲纠葛，这段情欲受到某种阻碍（通常是父权制），最终通过情节转折得以解决，这种转折是亚里士多德“发现”的喜剧形式，其手法比悲剧更为精巧。在剧作伊始，阻碍主人公的力量掌控着剧中的社会，但当主人公获得财富或女主人公获得体面后，一个新的社会便围绕着主人公及其新娘在舞台上逐渐形成。喜剧的剧情由此展开，最终将主人公融入他自然而然适应的社会。主人公本身很少是一个引人入胜的角色：为了符合低级模仿的礼仪规范，他的品德平庸，但社交魅力十足。在莎士比亚及其作品中最接近的浪漫喜剧中，这些模式朝着更为鲜明的高级模仿方向发展。在普洛斯彼罗这个人物身上，我们看到了少数几个运用阿里斯托芬式技巧，即由中心人物展现全部喜剧情节的例子。莎士比亚通常通过将压抑社会与理想社会之间的斗争描绘成两种存在层面之间的斗争来实现其高度的模仿性，前者类似于我们所处的世界，而后者则更糟，充满魔幻色彩且田园牧歌般美好。这一点将在后文中详细探讨。

New Comedy normally presents an erotic intrigue between a young man and a young woman which is blocked by some kind of opposition, usually paternal, and resolved by a twist in the plot which is the comic form of Aristotle’s “discovery,” and is more manipulated than its tragic counterpart. At the beginning of the play the forces thwarting the hero are in control of the play’s society, but after a discovery in which the hero becomes wealthy or the heroine respectable, a new society crystallizes on the stage around the hero and his bride. The action of the comedy thus moves towards the incorporation of the hero into the society that he naturally fits. The hero himself is seldom a very interesting person: in conformity with low mimetic decorum, he is ordinary in his virtues, but socially attractive. In Shakespeare and in the kind of romantic comedy that most closely resembles his there is a development of these formulas in a more distinctively high mimetic direction. In the figure of Prospero we have one of the few approaches to the Aristophanic technique of having the whole comic action projected by a central character. Usually Shakespeare achieves his high mimetic pattern by making the struggle of the repressive and the desirable societies a struggle between two levels of existence, the former like our own world or worse, the latter enchanted and idyllic. This point will be dealt with more fully later.

基于上述原因，后世小说中的家庭喜剧沿用了文艺复兴时期的大部分惯例。家庭喜剧通常以灰姑娘的原型为基础，讲述帕梅拉的美德得到回报的故事，将一个与读者极为相似的个体融入到他们共同向往的社会——一个伴随着婚纱和钞票的欢快沙沙声而开启的社会。莎士比亚的喜剧可能会让八到十个戏剧性大致相当的角色结婚，正如一部高雅的模仿悲剧可能会让同样数量的人死去一样，但在家庭喜剧中，这种性欲的扩散则更为罕见。然而，高雅模仿喜剧和低俗模仿喜剧的主要区别在于后者的结局。更常见的情况是，这涉及到社会地位的提升。一些技艺更为高超的低级模仿喜剧作家，常常会采用同样的成功故事模式，并带有我们在阿里斯托芬作品中发现的道德模糊性。在巴尔扎克或司汤达的作品中，一个聪明而冷酷的恶棍或许能够获得与塞缪尔·斯迈尔斯和霍雷肖·阿尔杰笔下那些正直的英雄相同的成功。因此，与阿莱宗（alazon）相对应的喜剧角色，似乎是流浪汉小说中那个聪明、讨人喜欢却又毫无原则的流浪汉。

For the reasons given above the domestic comedy of later fiction carries on with much the same conventions as were used in the Renaissance. Domestic comedy is usually based on the Cinderella archetype, the kind of thing that happens when Pamela’s’virtue is rewarded, the incorporation of an individual very like the reader into the society aspired to by both, a society ushered in with a happy rustle of bridal gowns and banknotes. Here again, Shakespearean comedy may marry off eight or ten people of approximately equal dramatic interest, just as a high mimetic tragedy may kill the same number, but in domestic comedy such diffusion of sexual energy is more rare. The chief difference between high and low mimetic comedy, however, is that the resolution of the latter more frequently involves a social promotion. More sophisticated writers of low mimetic comedy often present the same success-story formula with the moral ambiguities that we have found in Aristophanes. In Balzac or Stendhal a clever and ruthless scoundrel may achieve the same kind of success as the virtuous heroes of Samuel Smiles and Horatio Alger. Thus the comic counterpart of the alazon seems to be the clever, likeable, unprincipled picaro of the picaresque novel.

在研究讽刺喜剧时，我们必须从社会的角度出发，探讨“驱逐恶人”这一主题。这迎合了我们看到本·琼森笔下的福尔蓬被判处苦役、夏洛克被剥夺财产或达尔杜弗被押入监狱时所感受到的那种解脱感。然而，除非处理得非常巧妙，否则这样的主题很难令人信服，原因与讽刺悲剧中提到的类似。如果过分强调社会对个人的报复，无论他多么卑鄙无耻，都会使他显得罪责较轻，而社会则显得罪责更重。对于那些试图取悦观众（无论是实际观众还是内心观众）的角色来说，尤其如此，他们是悲剧英雄作为艺术家的喜剧对应角色。无论是傻瓜、小丑、丑角还是笨蛋，对艺人的拒绝都是艺术中最可怕的讽刺之一，正如对福斯塔夫的拒绝以及卓别林电影中的某些场景所表明的那样。

In studying ironic comedy we must start with the theme of driving out the pharmakos from the point of view of society. This appeals to the kind of relief we are expected to feel when we see Jonson’s Volpone condemned to the galleys, Shylock stripped of his wealth, or Tartuffe taken off to prison. Such a theme, unless touched very lightly, is difficult to make convincing, for the reasons suggested in connection with ironic tragedy. Insisting on the theme of social revenge on an individual, however great a rascal he may be, tends to make him look less involved in guilt and the society more so. This is particularly true of characters who have been trying to amuse either the actual or the internal audience, and who are the comic counterparts of the tragic hero as artist. The rejection of the entertainer, whether fool, clown, buffoon, or simpleton, can be one of the most terrible ironies known to art, as the rejection of Falstaff shows, and certain scenes in Chaplin.

在一些宗教诗歌中，例如《天堂篇》的结尾，我们可以看到文学存在一个上限，即对永恒世界的想象愿景转化为对它的体验。在讽刺喜剧中，我们开始看到艺术在现实生活中也存在一个下限。这就是野蛮的状态，在这个世界里，喜剧在于对无助的受害者施加痛苦，而悲剧在于忍受痛苦。讽刺喜剧将我们引向替罪羊仪式和噩梦般的梦境，这个象征着我们恐惧和仇恨的人性符号。当这个符号变得具有存在主义意义时，我们就超越了艺术的边界，就像被私刑处死的黑人、被大屠杀的犹太人、被猎巫的老妇人，或者任何被暴民随意抓走的人，比如《尤利乌斯·凯撒》中的诗人辛纳。在阿里斯托芬的戏剧中，讽刺有时几乎等同于暴民暴力，因为攻击是针对个人的：想想他在一出又一出戏里，对克里斯提尼的恋童癖或克莱奥尼莫斯的懦弱所获得的那些轻易的嘲笑。在阿里斯托芬的戏剧中，“pharmakos”一词的意思就是恶棍，毫不含糊。在《云》的结尾，诗人似乎几乎是在号召一群人去烧毁苏格拉底的房子，这与文学史上最伟大的悲剧讽刺杰作之一——柏拉图的《申辩篇》 ——形成了滑稽的对应。

In some religious poetry, for example at the end of the Paradiso, we can see that literature has an upper limit, a point at which an imaginative vision of an eternal world becomes an experience of it. In ironic comedy we begin to see that art has also a lower limit in actual life. This is the condition of savagery, the world in which comedy consists of inflicting pain on a helpless victim, and tragedy in enduring it. Ironic comedy brings us to the figure of the scapegoat ritual and the nightmare dream, the human symbol that concentrates our fears and hates. We pass the boundary of art when this symbol becomes existential, as it does in the black man of a lynching, the Jew of a pogrom, the old woman of a witch hunt, or anyone picked up at random by a mob, like Cinna the poet in Julius Caesar. In Aristophanes the irony sometimes edges very close to mob violence because the attacks are personal: one thinks of all the easy laughs he gets, in play after play, at the pederasty of Cleisthenes or the cowardice of Cleonymus. In Aristophanes the word pharmakos means simply scoundrel, with no nonsense about it. At the conclusion of The Clouds, where the poet seems almost to be summoning a lynching party to go and burn down Socrates’ house, we reach the comic counterpart of one of the greatest masterpieces of tragic irony in literature, Plato’s Apology.

但游戏元素正是艺术与野蛮之间的屏障，而扮演活人祭祀似乎是讽刺喜剧的一个重要主题。即使在笑声本身中，某种从不愉快甚至可怕的事物中解脱出来的方式似乎也至关重要。我们尤其在所有有大量观众同时在场的艺术形式中注意到这一点，例如戏剧，以及更明显的游戏。我们还注意到，扮演活人祭祀与任何源自祭祀仪式的历史渊源都无关，例如有人认为古希腊喜剧源于此。所有此类仪式的特征——国王的儿子、模仿死亡、刽子手、替代的受害者——在吉尔伯特和沙利文的《米卡多》中都比在阿里斯托芬的作品中更加明确。当然，没有任何证据表明棒球起源于活人祭祀仪式，但裁判员的形象与棒球起源于此并无二致：他是一个无赖，比巴拉巴更像个强盗。他眼神凶狠，输球一方的支持者们高喊着要他命。在戏剧中，群体情绪如同沸水般翻腾；而在私刑暴徒中，他们的情绪则如同被囚禁在布莱克所谓的道德熔炉中。角斗士般的搏斗，观众对那些娱乐他们的人拥有生杀大权，或许是所有野蛮或邪恶的戏剧模仿中最集中、最极致的。

But the element of play is the barrier that separates art from savagery, and playing at human sacrifice seems to be an important theme of ironic comedy. Even in laughter itself some kind of deliverance from the unpleasant, even the horrible, seems to be very important. We notice this particularly in all forms of art in which a large number of auditors are simultaneously present, as in drama, and, still more obviously, in games. We notice too that playing at sacrifice has nothing to do with any historical descent from sacrificial ritual, such as has been suggested for Old Comedy. All the features of such ritual, the king’s son, the mimic death, the executioner, the substituted victim, are far more explicit in Gilbert and Sullivan’s Mikado than they are in Aristophanes. There is certainly no evidence that baseball has descended from a ritual of human sacrifice, but the umpire is quite as much of a pharmakos as if it had: he is an abandoned scoundrel, a greater robber than Barabbas; he has the evil eye; the supporters of the losing team scream for his death. At play, mob emotions are boiled in an open pot, so to speak; in the lynching mob they are in a sealed furnace of what Blake would call moral virtue. The gladiatorial combat, in which the audience has the actual power of life and death over the people who are entertaining them, is perhaps the most concentrated of all the savage or demonic parodies of drama.

我们如今正处于文学的讽刺阶段，这在很大程度上解释了侦探小说的流行，以及侦探如何找到并除掉毒贩的套路。侦探小说起源于福尔摩斯时代，是对低级模仿的强化，对细节的关注日益敏锐，使得日常生活中最乏味、最容易被忽视的琐事都跃然纸上，具有神秘而重要的意义。但随着我们逐渐远离这种风格，我们转向了围绕尸体展开的仪式性戏剧，社会谴责的指头在一群“嫌疑人”之间摇摆不定，最终落在一人身上。受害者被随机选中的感觉非常强烈，因为对他的指控似乎只是人为操纵的。如果这真的不可避免，我们应该看到悲剧性的讽刺，就像《罪与罚》中那样，拉斯科尔尼科夫的罪行与他的性格如此紧密地交织在一起，以至于毋庸置疑。在任何“谁是凶手”的悬疑故事中，随着犯罪故事的残酷程度日益加深（这种残酷受到形式惯例的保护，因为按照惯例，追捕者不可能误认为嫌疑人是凶手），侦探小说开始与惊悚片融合，成为情节剧的一种形式。情节剧有两个重要的主题：道德战胜邪恶，以及由此产生的对观众所持有的道德观念的理想化。在残酷惊悚片的情节剧中，我们几乎达到了艺术所能达到的极限，接近于私刑暴徒那种纯粹的自以为是。

The fact that we are now in an ironic phase of literature largely accounts for the popularity of the detective story, the formula of how a man-hunter locates a pharmakos and gets rid of him. The detective story begins in the Sherlock Holmes period as an intensification of low mimetic, in the sharpening of attention to details that makes the dullest and most neglected trivia of daily living leap into mysterious and fateful significance. But as we move further away from this we move toward a ritual drama around a corpse in which a wavering finger of social condemnation passes over a group of “suspects” and finally settles on one. The sense of a victim chosen by lot is very strong, for the case against him is only plausibly manipulated. If it were really inevitable, we should have tragic irony, as in Crime and Punishment, where Raskolnikoff’s crime is so interwoven with his character that there can be no question of any “whodunit” mystery. In the growing brutality of the crime story (a brutality protected by the convention of the form, as it is conventionally impossible that the man-hunter can be mistaken in believing that one of his suspects is a murderer), detection begins to merge with the thriller as one of the forms of melodrama. In melodrama two themes are important: the triumph of moral virtue over villainy, and the consequent idealizing of the moral views assumed to be held by the audience. In the melodrama of the brutal thriller we come as close as it is normally possible for art to come to the pure self-righteousness of the lynching mob.

因此，我们或许应该说，所有形式的通俗剧，尤其是侦探剧，如果可以认真对待的话，都是警察国家的宣传工具，因为它们代表着暴民暴力的合法化。但这似乎是不可能的。戏剧的保护墙依然存在。严肃的通俗剧很快就会陷入自身的怜悯和恐惧之中：它越严肃，就越容易被读者以讽刺的眼光看待，其怜悯和恐惧分别被视为感伤的废话和呆板的严肃。讽刺喜剧的一个极端是对天真通俗剧荒谬性的认识，或者至少是对它试图将社会敌人定义为社会之外的人的荒谬性的认识。由此，它发展到另一个极端，即真正的喜剧讽刺或讽刺，它将社会敌人定义为社会内部的精神。让我们从这个角度来梳理讽刺喜剧的形式。

We should have to say, then, that all forms of melodrama, the detective story in particular, were advance propaganda for the police state, in so far as that represents the regularizing of mob violence, if it were possible to take them seriously. But it seems not to be possible. The protecting wall of play is still there. Serious melodrama soon gets entangled with its own pity and fear: the more serious it is, the more likely it is to be looked at ironically by the reader, its pity and fear seen as sentimental drivel and owlish solemnity, respectively. One pole of ironic comedy is the recognition of the absurdity of naive melodrama, or, at least, of the absurdity of its attempt to define the enemy of society as a person outside that society. From there it develops toward the opposite pole, which is true comic irony or satire, and which defines the enemy of society as a spirit within that society. Let us arrange the forms of ironic comedy from this point of view.

有教养的人去看情节剧，会带着居高临下的姿态对反派发出嘘声：他们意在表明自己无法认真对待反派的罪行。这种讽刺手法与讽刺时代的另外两大艺术形式——广告和宣传——的讽刺手法完全吻合。这些艺术形式假装严肃地面向一群潜在的愚昧受众，这群受众或许根本不存在，但却被假定足够愚钝，会不加思考地接受关于肥皂纯度或政府动机的种种说法。而我们其他人，意识到讽刺从不直白地表达其含义，所以会以一种讽刺的眼光看待这些艺术形式，或者至少将其视为一种讽刺游戏。同样，我们在阅读谋杀故事时，也会强烈地感受到其中罪行的不真实性。谋杀无疑是严重的罪行，但如果私人谋杀真的构成重大威胁……读到关于我们文明的种种描述，绝非轻松之事。我们可以将其与罗马喜剧中对皮条客的抨击相比较，后者同样基于妓院不道德这一无可辩驳的论断。

Cultivated people go to a melodrama to hiss the villain with an air of condescension: they are making a point of the fact that they cannot take his villainy seriously. We have here a type of irony which exactly corresponds to that of two other major arts of the ironic age, advertising and propaganda. These arts pretend to address themselves seriously to a subliminal audience of cretins, an audience that may not even exist, but which is assumed to be simple-minded enough to accept at their face value the statements made about the purity of a soap or a government’s motives. The rest of us, realizing that irony never says precisely what it means, take these arts ironically, or, at least, regard them as a kind of ironic game. Similarly, we read murder stories with a strong sense of the unreality of the villainy involved. Murder is doubtless a serious crime, but if private murder really were a major threat to our civilization it would not be relaxing to read about it. We may compare the abuse showered on the pimp in Roman comedy, which was similarly based on the indisputable ground that brothels are immoral.

下一步是讽刺喜剧，其目标受众是那些能够意识到杀戮暴力与其说是恶人对道德社会的攻击，不如说是社会自身邪恶本质的体现的人们。这种喜剧是对情节剧套路的理性化戏仿，例如格雷厄姆·格林的小说就体现了这一点。再往后是讽刺喜剧，它直接针对情节剧精神本身，这是所有带有浓厚讽刺意味的喜剧中一个令人惊讶的持久传统。人们注意到，讽刺喜剧反复出现一种倾向，即嘲讽和斥责那些被认为渴望感伤、庄严以及忠诚和既定道德标准的观众。本·琼森和康格里夫的傲慢，戈德史密斯对资产阶级感伤的嘲弄，王尔德和萧伯纳对情节剧情境的戏仿，都属于这一一脉相承的传统。莫里哀必须取悦国王，但他的性情也并无例外。除了喜剧之外，我们还应该加上小说家们对情节剧式爱情的嘲讽，从菲尔丁到乔伊斯，莫里哀的小说家们都对这种爱情进行了嘲讽。

The next step is an ironic comedy addressed to the people who can realize that murderous violence is less an attack on a virtuous society by a malignant individual than a symptom of that society’s own viciousness. Such a comedy would be the kind of intellectualized parody of melodramatic formulas represented by, for instance, the novels of Graham Greene. Next comes the ironic comedy directed at the melodramatic spirit itself, an astonishingly persistent tradition in all comedy in which there is a large ironic admixture. One notes a recurring tendency on the part of ironic comedy to ridicule and scold an audience assumed to be hankering after sentiment, solemnity, and the triumph of fidelity and approved moral standards. The arrogance of Jonson and Congreve, the mocking of bourgeois sentiment in Goldsmith, the parody of melodramatic situations in Wilde and Shaw, belong to a consistent tradition. Molière had to please his king, but was not temperamentally an exception. To comic drama one may add the ridicule of melodramatic romance in the novelists, from Fielding to Joyce.

最后是风俗喜剧，它描绘了一个喋喋不休、充满势利和诽谤的社会。在这种讽刺中，那些与虚构社会格格不入或被排斥在外的角色往往能博得观众的同情。这几乎是对悲剧性讽刺的一种戏仿，正如我们在伊夫林·沃的《一把尘土》中那个相对无害的主人公的悲惨命运中所见。或者，我们可能会看到一个角色，在作者或观众的同情下，彻底否定了这样的社会，甚至刻意地离开，从而成为一种反向的“药师”（pharmakos） 。例如，奥尔德斯·赫胥黎的《那些荒芜的叶子》的结尾就出现了这种情况。然而，更常见的情况是，艺术家会呈现一种讽刺性的僵局：主人公被虚构的社会视为傻瓜，甚至更糟，但他却给现实中的观众留下了深刻的印象，让他们觉得他拥有比他所在的社会更有价值的东西。最明显的例子，也是最伟大的例子之一，是陀思妥耶夫斯基的《白痴》，但还有很多其他作品。《好兵帅克》、《天堂是我的归宿》和《马嘴》等作品都能体现这一主题的广泛性。

Finally comes the comedy of manners, the portrayal of a chattering-monkey society devoted to snobbery and slander. In this kind of irony the characters who are opposed to or excluded from the fictional society have the sympathy of the audience. Here we are close to a parody of tragic irony, as we can see in the appalling fate of the relatively harmless hero of Evelyn Waugh’s A Handful of Dust. Or we may have a character who, with the sympathy of the author or audience, repudiates such a society to the point of deliberately walking out of it, becoming thereby a kind of pharmakos in reverse. This happens for instance at the conclusion of Aldous Huxley’s Those Barren Leaves. It is more usual, however, for the artist to present an ironic deadlock in which the hero is regarded as a fool or worse by the fictional society, and yet impresses the real audience as having something more valuable than his society has. The obvious example, and certainly one of the greatest, is Dostoievsky’s The Idiot, but there are many others. The Good Soldier Schweik, Heaven’s My Destination and The Horse’s Mouth are instances that will give some idea of the range of the theme.

我们之前谈到过，在悲剧中，讽刺意味回归神话因此，这种模式同样适用于喜剧。甚至连通俗文学似乎也在逐渐将其重心从谋杀故事转向科幻小说——或者至少，科幻小说的快速增长无疑是当代通俗文学的一个事实。科幻小说常常试图想象，在一个远高于我们自身、如同我们远高于野蛮世界一般遥远的层面上，生活会是什么样子；它的背景设定往往在我们看来是科技奇迹。因此，它是一种具有强烈神话倾向的浪漫模式。

What we have said about the return of irony to myth in tragic modes thus holds equally well for comic ones. Even popular literature appears to be slowly shifting its center of gravity from murder stories to science fiction—or at any rate a rapid growth of science fiction is certainly a fact about contemporary popular literature. Science fiction frequently tries to imagine what life would be like on a plane as far above us as we are above savagery; its setting is often of a kind that appears to us as technologically miraculous. It is thus a mode of romance with a strong inherent tendency to myth.

我们希望，对一系列虚构模式的构想能够赋予一些文学术语更灵活的含义。例如，“浪漫主义”和“现实主义”这两个词，通常用作相对或比较性的术语：它们阐明了虚构作品的倾向，而不能作为描述性的形容词进行精确的描述。如果我们考察《珀耳塞福涅的掳掠》、《律师的故事》、《无事生非》、《傲慢与偏见》和《美国悲剧》这一系列作品，就会发现，每一部作品相对于其后的作品而言都是“浪漫主义”的，而相对于其前的作品而言则是“现实主义”的。另一方面，“自然主义”一词在其恰当的视角下，作为虚构作品的一个阶段而出现。它与侦探小说颇为相似（尽管方式截然不同），都始于对低级模仿的强化，试图如实描绘生活，并最终，由于这种尝试本身的逻辑，走向了纯粹的讽刺。因此，左拉对讽刺手法的痴迷使他获得了冷漠地记录人类生活场景的声誉。

The conception of a sequence of fictional modes should do something, let us hope, to give a more flexible meaning to some of our literary terms. The words “romantic” and “realistic,” for instance, as ordinarily used, are relative or comparative terms: they illustrate tendencies in fiction, and cannot be used as simply descriptive adjectives with any sort of exactness. If we take the sequence De Raptu Proserpinae, The Man of Law’s Tale, Much Ado About Nothing, Pride and Prejudice, An American Tragedy, it is clear that each work is “romantic” compared to its successors and “realistic” compared to its predecessors. On the other hand, the term “naturalism” shows up in its proper perspective as a phase of fiction which, rather like the detective story, though in a very different way, begins as an intensification of low mimetic, an attempt to describe life exactly as it is, and ends, by the very logic of that attempt, in pure irony. Thus Zola’s obsession with ironic formulas gave him a reputation as a detached recorder of the human scene.

在实践中，我们很容易感受到低模仿或早期模式中可能出现的反讽语调与反讽模式本身的反讽结构之间的差异。例如，当狄更斯运用反讽时，读者被邀请参与其中，因为作者和读者都默认存在某些共同的常态标准。这种假设是相对通俗模式的标志：正如狄更斯的例子所示，在低模仿写作中，严肃小说和通俗小说之间的差距比在反讽写作中要小。文学作品对相对稳定的社会规范的接受与低模仿小说相比反讽小说的含蓄密切相关。在低模仿模式中，人物通常以他们呈现给别人的形象出现，衣着完整，并且会展现他们大部分的生理生活和内心独白。经过仔细删减。这种做法完全符合其他相关惯例。

The difference between the ironic tone that we may find in low mimetic or earlier modes and the ironic structure of the ironic mode itself is not hard to sense in practice. When Dickens, for instance, uses irony the reader is invited to share in the irony, because certain standards of normality common to author and reader are assumed. Such assumptions are a mark of a relatively popular mode: as the example of Dickens indicates, the gap between serious and popular fiction is narrower in low mimetic than in ironic writing. The literary acceptance of relatively stable social norms is closely connected with the reticence of low mimetic as compared to ironic fiction. In low mimetic modes characters are usually presented as they appear to others, fully dressed and with a large section of both their physical lives and their inner monologue carefully excised. Such an approach is entirely consistent with the other conventions involved.

如果我们以此区分作为比较价值判断的基础（这当然是一种伪装成批判性的道德价值判断），那么我们就不得不要么抨击低级模仿的惯例，认为它们矫揉造作、虚伪做作，忽略了生活的方方面面；要么抨击反讽的惯例，认为它们不像狄更斯的作品那样健康、有益、通俗、令人安心、合理。如果我们仅仅关注区分这些惯例，那么我们只需指出，低级模仿比反讽更具英雄气概，而且低级模仿的含蓄使得其笔下的人物平均而言比反讽小说中的人物更具英雄气概，或者至少更显尊严。

If we were to make this distinction the basis of a comparative value-judgement, which would, of course, be a moral value-judgement disguised as a critical one, we should be compelled either to attack low mimetic conventions for being prudish and hypocritical and leaving too much of life out, or to attack ironic conventions for not being wholesome, healthy, popular, reassuring, and sound, like the conventions of Dickens. As long as we are concerned simply to distinguish between the conventions, we need only remark that the low mimetic is one step more heroic than the ironic, and that low mimetic reticence has the effect of making its characters, on the average, more heroic, or at least more dignified, than the characters in ironic fiction.

我们也可以将此方案应用于小说家创作时所遵循的选择原则。让我们随机举个例子，看看小说中鬼魂的运用。在真正的神话中，鬼魂和活人之间显然不可能有明确的界限。在浪漫故事中，我们有真实的人类角色，因此鬼魂属于另一个类别，但在浪漫故事中，鬼魂通常只是众多角色之一：他并不令人感到惊奇，因为他的出现并不比许多其他事件更令人惊奇。在高阶模仿文学中，我们处于自然秩序之内，引入鬼魂相对容易，因为鬼魂的经验层面高于我们自身的层面，但当他出现时，他是一个可怕而神秘的存在，来自一个明显不同的世界。在低阶模仿文学中，自笛福以来，鬼魂几乎完全被限制在一个单独的“鬼故事”类别中。在普通的低级模仿小说中，鬼魂是不可接受的，正如菲尔丁所说，“这是为了迎合读者的怀疑态度”，而这种怀疑态度仅限于低级模仿的惯例。少数例外，例如《呼啸山庄》，恰恰证明了这条规则——也就是说，我们能从《呼啸山庄》中感受到浓厚的浪漫主义影响。在某些讽刺小说中，例如亨利·詹姆斯的后期作品，鬼魂开始以一个逐渐瓦解的人格碎片的形式出现。

We may also apply our scheme to the principles of selection on which a writer of fiction operates. Let us take, as a random example, the use of ghosts in fiction. In a true myth there can obviously be no consistent distinction between ghosts and living beings. In romance we have real human beings, and consequently ghosts are in a separate category, but in a romance a ghost as a rule is merely one more character: he causes little surprise because his appearance is no more marvellous than many other events. In high mimetic, where we are within the order of nature, a ghost is relatively easy to introduce because the plane of experience is above our own, but when he appears he is an awful and mysterious being from what is perceptibly another world. In low mimetic, ghosts have been, ever since Defoe, almost entirely confined to a separate category of “ghost stories.” In ordinary low mimetic fiction they are inadmissible, “in complaisance to the scepticism of a reader,” as Fielding puts it, a skepticism which extends only to low mimetic conventions. The few exceptions, such as Wuthering Heights, go a long way to prove the rule—that is, we recognize a strong influence of romance in Wuthering Heights. In some forms of ironic fiction, such as the later works of Henry James, the ghost begins to come back as a fragment of a disintegrating personality.

然而，一旦我们学会区分各种调式，就必须学会将它们重新组合起来。因为虽然一种调式构成了小说作品的潜在基调，但其他四种调式中的任何一种或全部都可能同时存在。我们对伟大文学作品微妙之处的感知，很大程度上源于这种调式上的对比。乔叟是一位中世纪诗人，主要创作浪漫故事，涵盖宗教和世俗题材。在他的朝圣者中，骑士和牧师清晰地展现了他作为诗人所处的社会规范，而我们今天所见的《坎特伯雷故事集》也正是由这两个人物构成，他们分别作为故事的开篇和结尾。然而，忽视乔叟对低级模仿和反讽技巧的精湛运用，就如同把他看作是一位误入中世纪的现代小说家一样大错特错。 《安东尼与克莉奥佩特拉》的基调是高级模仿，讲述的是一位伟大领袖的陨落。但我们很容易以反讽的眼光看待马克·安东尼，把他看作一个被激情奴役的人；我们很容易在他身上看到与我们自身相同的人性；我们很容易把他看作是一位拥有非凡勇气和毅力的浪漫冒险家，却被一个女巫出卖。剧中甚至暗示着一位超人的存在，他的双腿跨越海洋，而他的陨落则是命运的阴谋，只有预言家才能解释。忽略其中任何一点都会使这部剧过于简单化，从而贬低其内涵。通过这样的分析，我们或许会意识到，关于一件艺术作品的两个基本事实——它与它所处的时代相符，以及它与我们当今的时代相符——并非对立，而是相辅相成。

Once we have learned to distinguish the modes, however, we must then learn to recombine them. For while one mode constitutes the underlying tonality of a work of fiction, any or all of the other four may be simultaneously present. Much of our sense of the subtlety of great literature comes from this modal counter-point. Chaucer is a medieval poet specializing mainly in romance, whether sacred or secular. Of his pilgrims, the knight and the parson clearly present the norms of the society in which he functions as a poet, and, as we have them, the Canterbury Tales are contained by these two figures, who open and close the series. But to overlook Chaucer’s mastery of low mimetic and ironic techniques would be as wrong as to think of him as a modern novelist who got into the Middle Ages by mistake. The tonality of Antony and Cleopatra is high mimetic, the story of the fall of a great leader. But it is easy to look at Mark Antony ironically, as a man enslaved by passion; it is easy to recognize his common humanity with ourselves; it is easy to see in him a romantic adventurer of prodigious courage and endurance betrayed by a witch; there are even hints of a superhuman being whose legs bestrid the ocean and whose downfall is a conspiracy of fate, explicable only to a soothsayer. To leave out any of these would oversimplify and belittle the play. Through such an analysis we may come to realize that the two essential facts about a work of art, that it is contemporary with its own time and that it is contemporary with ours, are not opposed but complementary facts.

我们对虚构模式的考察也表明，模仿倾向本身，即追求逼真和精确描述的倾向，是文学的两大极点之一。另一极点似乎与亚里士多德的“神话”（mythos ）一词以及神话的通常含义都有关联。也就是说，它是一种讲述故事的倾向，故事的起源是讲述那些无所不能的人物，而这种倾向只是逐渐转向讲述一个合情合理或可信的故事。神祇的神话融入了英雄的传说；英雄的传说融入了悲剧和喜剧的情节；悲剧和喜剧的情节融入了或多或少写实的虚构作品的情节。但这些变化是社会语境的改变，而非文学形式的改变，叙事的基本原则始终保持不变，当然，它们也会根据语境进行调整。汤姆·琼斯和奥利弗·特威斯特作为模仿能力较弱的人物，其形象颇为典型。然而，他们所卷入的身世之谜式的故事情节，却是对米南德作品中流传已久的虚构模式的合理改编。这些模式又可追溯至欧里庇得斯的《伊翁》，以及珀尔修斯和摩西等传奇故事。我们在此顺便指出，虚构作品中对自然的模仿，其产生的并非真理或现实，而是合情合理，而合情合理本身也存在差异。从神话或民间故事中敷衍的让步，到自然主义小说中的某种审查原则，其分量不断加重。因此，纵观历史，我们可以将浪漫主义、高级模仿和低级模仿模式视为一系列错位的神话、神话体系或情节模式，它们逐渐向逼真性的另一端移动，然后，带着讽刺意味，又开始向后移动。

Our survey of fictional modes has also shown us that the mimetic tendency itself, the tendency to verisimilitude and accuracy of description, is one of two poles of literature. At the other pole is something that seems to be connected both with Aristotle’s word mythos and with the usual meaning of myth. That is, it is a tendency to tell a story which is in origin a story about characters who can do anything, and only gradually becomes attracted toward a tendency to tell a plausible or credible story. Myths of gods merge into legends of heroes; legends of heroes merge into plots of tragedies and comedies; plots of tragedies and comedies merge into plots of more or less realistic fiction. But these are change of social context rather than of literary form, and the constructive principles of story-telling remain constant through them, though of course they adapt to them. Tom Jones and Oliver Twist are typical enough as low mimetic characters, but the birth-mystery plots in which they are involved are plausible adaptations of fictional formulas that go back to Menander, and from Menander to Euripides’ Ion, and from Euripides to legends like those of Perseus and Moses. We note in passing that imitation of nature in fiction produces, not truth or reality, but plausibility, and plausibility varies in weight from a mere perfunctory concession in a myth or folk tale to a kind of censor principle in a naturalistic novel. Reading forward in history, therefore, we may think of our romantic, high mimetic and low mimetic modes as a series of displaced myths, mythoi or plot-formulas progressively moving over towards the opposite pole of verisimilitude, and then, with irony, beginning to move back.

主题模式

THEMATIC MODES

亚里士多德列举了诗歌的六个方面：其中三个——旋律、措辞和场面——自成一类，我们稍后会详细探讨。另外三个方面分别是神话（或情节）、伦理（包括人物和背景）以及思想（或“思想”）。我们目前讨论的文学作品都是虚构作品，其中情节正如亚里士多德所说，是作品的“灵魂”或塑造原则，而人物的存在主要是为了服务于情节。但是，除了英雄及其社会的内在虚构之外，还存在一种外在虚构，即作家与作家所处社会之间的关系。诗歌可以像莎士比亚或荷马的作品那样，完全沉浸于其内在人物之中。在荷马的作品中，诗人本人只是指向他的故事，然后便消失了，《奥德赛》中的第二个词“我”（moi）就是我们在这部史诗中唯一能了解到的关于他的内容。但是，一旦诗人的个性出现在视野中，诗人与读者之间就建立了一种贯穿故事的关系，这种关系可能会不断加深，直到除了诗人向读者传达的内容之外，故事本身完全消失了。

Aristotle lists six aspects of poetry: three of them, melody, diction, and spectacle, form a group by themselves, and we shall consider them in due course. The other three are mythos or plot, ethos, which includes both characters and setting, and dianoia or “thought.” The literary works we have so far been considering are works of fiction in which the plot is, as Aristotle called it, the “soul” or shaping principle, and the characters exist primarily as functions of the plot. But besides the internal fiction of the hero and his society, there is an external fiction which is a relation between the writer and the writer’s society. Poetry may be as completely absorbed in its internal characters as it is in Shakespeare, or in Homer, where the poet himself simply points to his story and disappears, the second word of the Odyssey, moi, being all we get of him in that poem. But as soon as the poet’s personality appears on the horizon, a relation with the reader is established which cuts across the story, and which may increase until there is no story at all apart from what the poet is conveying to his reader.
