在小说和戏剧等体裁中，内在的虚构通常是主要关注点；而在散文和抒情诗中，主要关注点在于“dianoia”，即读者从作者那里获得的理念或诗意思想（当然，这与其他类型的思想截然不同）。“dianoia ”的最佳译法或许是“主题”，而具有这种理想或概念意义的文学作品可以被称为主题文学。当小说读者问“这个故事会如何发展？”时，他是在询问情节，特别是情节中那个关键的方面，亚里士多德称之为“发现”或“anagnorisis ”。但他同样可能会问“这个故事的意义是什么？”这个问题与“dianoia ”相关，表明主题和情节一样，都包含着发现的要素。

In such genres as novels and plays the internal fiction is usually of primary interest; in essays and in lyrics the primary interest is in dianoia, the idea or poetic thought (something quite different, of course, from other kinds of thought) that the reader gets from the writer. The best translation of dianoia is, perhaps, “theme,” and literature with this ideal or conceptual interest may be called thematic. When a reader of a novel asks, “How is this story going to turn out?” he is asking a question about the plot, specifically about that crucial aspect of the plot which Aristotle calls discovery or anagnorisis. But he is equally likely to ask, “What’s the point of this story?” This question relates to dianoia, and indicates that themes have their elements of discovery just as plots do.

很容易说有些文学作品是虚构的，而另一些则是真实的。主题是其主要强调之处。但显然，文学作品中并不存在虚构的或主题式的作品，因为所有四个伦理要素（伦理在此指与人物相关的要素）、主人公、主人公所处的社会、诗人以及诗人的读者，至少在潜在意义上始终存在。几乎任何文学作品都不可能不存在创作者与其读者之间的某种关系，无论这种关系是隐含的还是明确的。当诗人最初设想的读者被后世所取代时，这种关系会发生改变，但它依然存在。另一方面，即使在抒情诗和散文中，作者在某种程度上也是一个虚构的主人公，拥有一个虚构的读者，因为如果虚构的投射要素完全消失，写作就会变成直接对话或直白的论述性写作，从而不再是文学。一位诗人写给爱人的情诗，抱怨她的残忍，这便将四个伦理要素简化为两个，但这四个要素仍然存在。

It is easy to say that some literary works are fictional and others thematic in their main emphasis. But clearly there is no such thing as a fictional or a thematic work of literature, for all four ethical elements (ethical in the sense of relating to character), the hero, the hero’s society, the poet and the poet’s readers, are always at least potentially present. There can hardly be a work of literature without some kind of relation, implied or expressed, between its creator and its auditors. When the audience the poet had in mind is superseded by posterity, the relation changes, but it still holds. On the other hand, even in lyrics and essays the writer is to some extent a fictional hero with a fictional audience, for if the element of fictional projection disappeared completely, the writing would become direct address, or straight discursive writing, and cease to be literature. A poet sending a love poem to his lady complaining of her cruelty has stereoscoped his four ethical elements into two, but the four are still there.

因此，每一部文学作品都兼具虚构性和主题性，而哪一方面更为重要，往往只是个人观点或解读侧重点的问题。我们曾以荷马为例，指出他是一位典型的非个人化的虚构作家，但至少在1750年之前，荷马史诗批评的重点几乎完全在于主题，关注的是两部史诗中隐含的“领袖精神”（dianoia）或领导理想。《弃儿汤姆·琼斯的故事》是一部以其情节命名的长篇小说；《理智与情感》则以其主题命名。但菲尔丁对主题的关注（主要体现在各部作品的引言章节中）与简·奥斯汀对讲述精彩故事的关注一样强烈。与《汤姆叔叔的小屋》或《愤怒的葡萄》相比，这两部小说都更侧重于虚构性，后两者的情节主要是为了分别阐释奴隶制和移民劳工的主题。与《天路历程》相比，它们更侧重于虚构；而与蒙田的一篇散文相比， 《天路历程》又更侧重于虚构。我们注意到，随着我们从虚构的侧重转向主题的侧重，神话（mythos）一词所代表的要素往往越来越倾向于“叙事”而非“情节”。

Hence every work of literature has both a fictional and a thematic aspect, and the question of which is more important is often simply a matter of opinion or emphasis in interpretation. We have cited Homer as the very type of impersonal fiction writer, but the main emphasis of Homeric criticism, down to about 1750 at least, has been overwhelmingly thematic, concerned with the dianoia or ideal of leadership implicit in the two epics. The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling, is a novel named after its plot; Sense and Sensibility is named after its theme. But Fielding has as strong a thematic interest (revealed chiefly in the introductory chapters to the different books) as Jane Austen has in telling a good story. Both novels are strongly fictional in emphasis compared to Uncle Tom’s Cabin or The Grapes of Wrath, where the plot exists primarily to illustrate the themes of slavery and migratory labor respectively. They in their turn are fictional in emphasis compared to The Pilgrim’s Progress, and The Pilgrim’s Progress is fictional in emphasis compared to an essay of Montaigne. We note that as we move from fictional to thematic emphasis, the element represented by the term mythos tends to mean increasingly “narrative” rather than “plot.”

当一部虚构作品以主题为导向进行创作或解读时，它就变成了寓言或例证寓言。所有形式上的寓言本身就具有强烈的主题意义，尽管并非如人们常说的那样，任何对虚构作品的主题批评都会将其转化为寓言（尽管它可能而且确实会起到寓言的作用，正如我们……）。拭目以待）。真正的寓言是文学作品中的一个结构性要素：它必须存在，单靠批评性的解读是无法添加的。

When a work of fiction is written or interpreted thematically, it becomes a parable or illustrative fable. All formal allegories have, ipso facto, a strong thematic interest, though it does not follow, as is often said, that any thematic criticism of a work of fiction will turn it into an allegory (though it may and does allegorize, as we shall see). Genuine allegory is a structural element in literature: it has to be there, and cannot be added by critical interpretation alone.

同样，几乎每个文明在其传统神话体系中都存在一个特殊的群体，被认为比其他神话更严肃、更权威、更有教育意义，也更接近事实和真理。对于大多数同时运用《圣经》和古典文学的基督教时代诗人而言，后者在权威性上并不与前者相提并论，尽管就文学批评而言，二者都具有神话性质。这种正典神话与伪经神话的区分，甚至在原始社会中也存在，赋予了前者一种特殊的主题重要性。

Again, nearly every civilization has, in its stock of traditional myths, a particular group which is thought of as more serious, more authoritative, more educational and closer to fact and truth than the rest. For most poets of the Christian era who have used both the Bible and Classical literature, the latter has not stood on the same plane of authority as the former, although they are equally mythological as far as literary criticism is concerned. This distinction of canonical and apocryphal myth, which can be found even in primitive societies, gives to the former group a particular thematic importance.

现在，我们需要考察这一系列模式在文学主题层面上的表现。这里，我们必须将研究范围更严格地限定在西方文学，因为我们在古典小说中观察到的透视缩短过程在主题方面更为显著。

We have now to see how our sequence of modes works out in the thematic aspect of literature. We shall have to confine ourselves here more strictly to Western literature, as the foreshortening process that we noticed in Classical fiction is even more marked on the thematic side.

在小说创作中，我们发现了两种主要倾向：一种是“喜剧”倾向，即把主人公融入社会；另一种是“悲剧”倾向，即把主人公孤立起来。在主题文学中，诗人可以以个人身份写作，强调其个性的独立性和视野的独特性。这种态度催生了大部分抒情诗和散文，以及大量的讽刺作品、警句和“田园诗”或一般的应景诗。这类作品中频繁出现的抗议、抱怨、嘲讽和孤独（无论是苦涩的还是宁静的）等情绪，或许暗示着与悲剧小说模式的某种粗略相似之处。或者，诗人可以致力于成为其所在社会的代言人，这意味着，由于他并非在向另一个社会发声，因此，他所在社会中潜藏或亟需的诗意知识和表达能力得以在他身上得以表达。

In fiction, we discovered two main tendencies, a “comic” tendency to integrate the hero with his society, and a “tragic” tendency to isolate him. In thematic literature the poet may write as an individual, emphasizing the separateness of his personality and the distinctness of his vision. This attitude produces most lyrics and essays, a good deal of satire, epigrams, and the writing of “eclogues” or occasional pieces generally. The frequency of the moods of protest, complaint, ridicule, and loneliness (whether bitter or serene) in such works may perhaps indicate a rough analogy to the tragic modes of fiction. Or the poet may devote himself to being a spokesman of his society, which means, as he is not addressing a second society, that a poetic knowledge and expressive power which is latent or needed in his society comes to articulation in him.

这种态度催生了广义上具有教育意义的诗歌：例如，较为人为或主题鲜明的史诗、说教诗和散文，以及像奥维德和斯诺里那样百科全书式的神话、民间传说和传奇故事汇编。在这些作品中，尽管故事本身是虚构的，但它们的编排方式和收集动机却具有主题性。在这种意义上的教育性诗歌中，诗人的社会功能作为一个主题占据了显著地位。如果我们把孤立个体的诗歌称为“抒情诗”，把社会代言人的诗歌称为“史诗”，那么（在通过与那些更“戏剧化”的、以内心人物为中心的虚构作品进行比较，我们或许能对它们有所初步了解。但显然，我们在此并非以任何一般意义来使用这些术语，而它们理应以一般意义来使用，因此我们立即舍弃它们，代之以“片段式”和“百科全书式”。也就是说，当诗人以个人身份进行交流时，他的形式往往是间断的；而当他以具有社会职能的专业人士身份进行交流时，他则倾向于寻求更为连贯的模式。

Such an attitude produces poetry which is educational in the broadest sense: epics of the more artificial or thematic kind, didactic poetry and prose, encyclopaedic compilations of myth, folklore, and legend like those of Ovid and Snorri, where, though the stories themselves are fictional, the arrangement of them and the motive for collecting them is thematic. In poetry which is educational in this sense, the social function of the poet figures prominently as a theme. If we call the poetry of the isolated individual a “lyric” and the poetry of the social spokesman an “epic” tendency (in comparison to the more “dramatic” fictions of internal characters) we shall perhaps gain some preliminary conception of them. But it is obvious that we are not here using these terms in any generic sense, and as they certainly should be used in a generic sense, we shall drop them at once and substitute “episodic” and “encyclopaedic” instead. That is, when the poet communicates as an individual, his forms tend to be discontinuous; when he communicates as a professional man with a social function, he tends to seek more extended patterns.

在神话层面，传说多于证据，但显而易见的是，歌颂神明的诗人往往被视为以神明的身份歌唱，或作为神明的工具。他的社会功能是灵感启示的先知；他常常处于狂喜状态，我们听闻许多关于他神力的奇闻轶事。俄耳甫斯能凭空变出树木；凯尔特世界的吟游诗人和奥拉维人能用讽刺杀死敌人；以色列的先知能预言未来。在这个层面，诗人作为诗人的愿景功能，即他作为诗人的真正职责，在于揭示他所歌颂的神明。这通常意味着，当他在“热情”或神灵附体状态下被当作先知咨询时，他会在特定场合揭示神的旨意。但随着时间的推移，他体内的神性会揭示他的本质、历史以及他的旨意，于是，一系列神谕便构建起一个更为宏大的神话和仪式体系。这一点在弥赛亚神话从希伯来先知的神谕中涌现出来时体现得非常明显。《古兰经》是西方早期神话模式运作的一个清晰的历史例证。真正的神谕诗歌大多是前文学时期或文学之外的作品，因此很难单独找出。对于更近期的例子，例如据说是平原印第安人文化重要组成部分的狂喜神谕，我们只能依赖人类学家的研究。

On the mythical plane there is more legend than evidence, but it is clear that the poet who sings about gods is often considered to be singing as one, or as an instrument of one. His social function is that of an inspired oracle; he is frequently an ecstatic, and we hear strange stories of his powers. Orpheus could draw trees after him; the bards and ollaves of the Celtic world could kill their enemies with their satire; the prophets of Israel foretold the future. The poet’s visionary function, his proper work as a poet, is on this plane to reveal the god for whom he speaks. This usually means that he reveals the god’s will in connection with a specific occasion, when he is consulted as an oracle in a state of “enthusiasm” or divine possession. But in time the god in him reveals his nature and history as well as his will, and so a larger pattern of myth and ritual is built up out of a series of oracular pronouncements. We can see this very clearly in the emergence of the Messiah myth from the oracles of the Hebrew prophets. The Koran is one clear historical instance at the beginning of the Western period of the mythical mode in action. Authentic examples of oracular poetry are so largely pre- and extra-literary that they are difficult to isolate. For more recent examples, such as the ecstatic oracles which are said to be an important aspect of the culture of the Plains Indians, we have to depend on anthropologists.

我们的论证中已经隐含了两个重要的原则。其一是诗人作为一个整体所肩负的视野整体的概念，这个整体倾向于将自身整合为一个百科全书式的形式，一个博学或灵感充沛的诗人可以尝试做到这一点，而一个诗歌流派或传统，如果文化足够同质化，也可以做到。我们注意到，传统故事、神话和历史都有很强的凝聚力，并最终形成百科全书式的形式。聚合体，尤其是当它们采用传统韵律时（通常如此），往往会经历类似的演变过程。有人推测荷马史诗的形成也经历了类似的演变过程，而散文埃达则将老埃达残篇的主题组织成连贯的散文序列。圣经历史显然也经历了类似的演变过程，而在传播过程较为宽松的印度，两部传统史诗——《摩诃婆罗多》和《罗摩衍那》 ——似乎像蟒蛇吞羊般，在数个世纪中不断膨胀。中世纪的一个例子是，第二位作者将《玫瑰传奇》扩展成一部百科全书式的讽刺作品。芬兰史诗《卡勒瓦拉》中所有统一或连贯的部分都是十九世纪的重构。但这并不意味着《卡勒瓦拉》作为一部独立的史诗是伪造的：恰恰相反，这意味着《卡勒瓦拉》的素材本身就很容易被重构。在神话模式中，百科全书式的形式就是神圣的经文；而在其他模式中，我们应该会发现百科全书式的形式，这些形式构成了一系列越来越人性化的神话或经文启示的类比。

Two principles of some importance are already implicit in our argument. One is a conception of a total body of vision that poets as a whole class are entrusted with, a total body tending to incorporate itself in a single encyclopaedic form, which can be attempted by one poet if he is sufficiently learned or inspired, or by a poetic school or tradition if the culture is sufficiently homogeneous. We note that traditional tales and myths and histories have a strong tendency to stick together and form encyclopaedic aggregates, especially when they are in a conventional metre, as they usually are. Some such process as this has been postulated for the Homeric epics, and in the Prose Edda the themes of the fragmentary lays of the Elder Edda are organized into a connected prose sequence. The Biblical histories obviously developed in a similar way, and in India, where the process of transmission was more relaxed, the two traditional epics, the Mahabharata and the Ramayana, apparently went on distending themselves for centuries, like pythons swallowing sheep. The expansion of The Romaunt of the Rose into an encyclopaedic satire by a second author is a medieval example. In the Finnish Kalevala everything that is unified or continuous about the poem is a nineteenth-century reconstruction. It does not follow that the Kalevala, considered as a single epic, is a fake: on the contrary, what follows is that the material of the Kalevala is the sort of material that lends itself readily to such reconstruction. In the mythical mode the encyclopaedic form is the sacred scripture, and in the other modes we should expect to find encyclopaedic forms which constitute a series of increasingly human analogies of mythical or scriptural revelation.

另一个原则是，虽然任何模式中都可能存在多种多样的叙事形式，但在每种模式中，我们都可以赋予某种特定的叙事形式以特殊的意义，这种形式似乎是百科全书式叙事形式的萌芽。在神话模式中，这种核心或典型的叙事形式是神谕。神谕发展出许多附属形式，特别是诫命、寓言、格言和预言。无论这些形式是像《古兰经》那样松散地串联在一起，还是像《圣经》那样经过精心编辑和编排，最终都形成了经文或圣书。例如，《以赛亚书》可以被分析成大量独立的神谕，可以说它有三个主要焦点：一个主要集中在被掳前时期，一个主要集中在被掳时期，还有一个主要集中在被掳后时期。圣经的“高级批评家”不是文学批评家，我们必须自己提出，《以赛亚书》实际上是它一直以来传统上被认为是的那种统一体，这种统一体不是作者的统一，而是主题的统一，而这个主题概括了整本圣经的主题，即以色列失落、被掳和被救赎的寓言。

The other principle is that while there may be a great variety of episodic forms in any mode, in each mode we may attach a special significance to the particular episodic form that seems to be the germ out of which the encyclopaedic forms develop. In the mythical mode this central or typical episodic product is the oracle. The oracle develops a number of subsidiary forms, notably the commandment, the parable, the aphorism, and the prophecy. Out of these, whether strung loosely together as they are in the Koran or carefully edited and arranged as they are in the Bible, the scripture or sacred book takes shape. The Book of Isaiah, for example, can be analyzed into a mass of separate oracles, with three major foci, so to speak, one mainly pre-exilic, one exilic and one post-exilic. The “higher critics” of the Bible are not literary critics, and we have to make the suggestion ourselves that the Book of Isaiah is in fact the unity it has always been traditionally taken to be, a unity not of authorship but of theme, and that theme in epitome the theme of the Bible as a whole, as the parable of Israel lost, captive, and redeemed.

在浪漫主义时期，诗人如同相应的英雄一样，化身为凡人，而神则退隐到……天空。他现在的主要功能是记忆。希腊神话在其历史时期之初就说过，记忆是缪斯女神的母亲，缪斯女神启发诗人，但这种启发已不再像神祇启发神谕那样强烈——尽管诗人尽可能地保留着这种联系。在荷马、或许更为原始的赫西俄德以及北方英雄时代的诗人中，我们可以看到诗人必须记住的东西。国王和外邦部落的名单、神话和诸神的谱系、历史传统、民间智慧的谚语、禁忌、吉凶日、护身符、部落英雄的事迹，这些都是诗人打开他文字宝库时所涌现的内容。中世纪吟游诗人背诵着大量故事，而像高尔或《世界轨迹》的作者那样，试图将自己所知的一切都融入一首鸿篇巨制或诗歌遗嘱的教士诗人，都属于同一范畴。这类诗歌中蕴含的百科全书式的知识被视为神圣的象征，是人类对神圣知识的一种类比。

In the period of romance, the poet, like the corresponding hero, has become a human being, and the god has retreated to the sky. His function now is primarily to remember. Memory, said Greek myth at the beginning of its historical period, is the mother of the Muses, who inspire the poets, but no longer in the same degree that the god inspires the oracle—though the poets clung to the connection as long as they could. In Homer, in the perhaps more primitive Hesiod, in the poets of the heroic age of the North, we can see the kind of thing the poet had to remember. Lists of kings and foreign tribes, myths and genealogies of gods, historical traditions, the proverbs of popular wisdom, taboos, lucky and unlucky days, charms, the deeds of the tribal heroes, were some of the things that came out when the poet unlocked his word-hoard. The medieval minstrel with his repertory of memorized stories and the clerical poet who, like Gower or the author of the Cursor Mundi, tries to get everything he knows into one vast poem or poetic testament, belong in the same category. The encyclopaedic knowledge in such poems is regarded sacramentally, as a human analogy of divine knowledge.

浪漫英雄的时代在很大程度上是一个游牧时代，其诗人也常常是流浪者。盲人游吟诗人是希腊和凯尔特文学中的传统形象；古英语诗歌表达了该语言中最凄凉的孤独；中世纪的游吟诗人和歌利亚讽刺诗人游历欧洲；但丁本人也是一位流亡者。或者，如果诗人留在原地，那么旅行的便是诗歌：民间故事沿着贸易路线传播；民谣和浪漫故事从盛大的集市中归来；又或者，身处英格兰的马洛里将他手中的“法国书”的内容告诉读者。在所有虚构的故事中，奇妙的旅程是​​唯一永不过时的模式，而正是这种虚构被用作寓言，出现在该模式的代表作——但丁的《神曲》中。这种模式的诗歌是普世性的载体，无论是在某个时代是希腊的，还是在另一个时代是罗马的。

The age of romantic heroes is largely a nomadic age, and its poets are frequently wanderers. The blind wandering minstrel is traditional in both Greek and Celtic literature; Old English poetry expresses some of the bleakest loneliness in the language; troubadours and Goliardic satirists roam over Europe in the Middle Ages; Dante himself was an exile. Or, if the poet stays where he is, it is poetry that travels: folk tales follow the trade routes; ballads and romances return from the great fairs; or Malory, writing in England, tells his readers what the “French book” says that has come to his hand. Of all fictions, the marvellous journey is the one formula that is never exhausted, and it is this fiction that is employed as a parable in the definitive encyclopaedic poem of the mode, Dante’s Commedia. Poetry in this mode is an agent of catholicity, whether Hellenic in one age or Roman Christian in another.

其典型的片段式主题或许最好地被描述为意识边界的主题，即诗人的心灵在两个世界之间穿梭，或同时意识到这两个世界。流放之诗，即游吟诗人或旅人（可能是流浪的吟游诗人、被抛弃的恋人或游牧的讽刺作家）的歌谣，通常对比记忆与经验的世界。幻象之诗，通常创作于五月的清晨，则对比经验与梦境的世界。这部通过女性或神圣恩典启示的诗歌，将旧秩序与新生（vita nuova）进行了对比。在《地狱篇》的开篇，这部伟大的百科全书式诗歌与流放之诗和异象之诗之间的关联就已清晰地展现出来。

Its typical episodic theme is perhaps best described as the theme of the boundary of consciousness, the sense of the poetic mind as passing from one world to another, or as simultaneously aware of both. The poem of exile, the lay of the Widsith or wayfarer who may be a wandering minstrel, a rejected lover, or a nomadic satirist, normally contrasts the worlds of memory and of experience. The poem of vision, conventionally dated on a May morning, contrasts the worlds of experience and dream. The poem of revelation through female or divine grace contrasts the old dispensation with the vita nuova. In the opening lines of the Inferno the affinity of the great encyclopaedic poem with both the poem of exile and the poem of vision is clearly marked.

高度模仿时期展现了一个以宫廷和都城为中心的更为稳固的社会，向心视角取代了浪漫主义时期的离心视角。遥远的追寻目标，如圣杯或上帝之城，转变为凝聚的象征，成为君主、国家和民族信仰的标志。这一时期的百科全书式长诗，如《仙后》、《卢济塔尼亚人传》、《耶路撒冷的解放》和《失乐园》，都是以爱国主义和宗教思想为纽带的民族史诗。政治元素在《失乐园》中扮演的特殊角色原因众所周知，因此将其视为民族史诗并不困难。与《天路历程》一样，它也构成了一种对英国低度模仿时期的介绍，因为其本质特征之一是讲述普通人的故事。这类主题史诗的重点通常与以讲述故事为主要目的的叙事作品有明显的区别，例如英雄时代的大多数史诗、大多数冰岛萨迦和凯尔特浪漫故事，以及文艺复兴时期的大部分《疯狂的奥兰多》，尽管文艺复兴时期的评论家表明，从主题的角度来解读阿里奥斯托的作品是完全可能的。

The high mimetic period brings in a society more strongly established around the court and capital city, and a centripetal perspective replaces the centrifugal one of romance. The distant goals of the quest, the Holy Grail or the City of God, modulate into symbols of convergence, the emblems of prince, nation, and national faith. The encyclopaedic poems of this period, The Faerie Queene, The Lusiad, Jerusalem Delivered, Paradise Lost, are national epics unified by patriotic and religious ideas. The reasons for the exceptional role of the political elements in Paradise Lost are familiar, and constitute no real difficulty in seeing it as a national epic. Along with The Pilgrim’s Progress, it also constitutes a kind of introduction to English low mimetic, being in one of its essential aspects the story of Everyman. Such thematic epics are as a rule recognizably different in emphasis from narratives where the primary interest is in telling the story, as in most epic poetry of the heroic age, most Icelandic sagas and Celtic romances, and, in the Renaissance period, in the greater part of Orlando Furioso, though Renaissance critics showed that it was quite possible to interpret Ariosto thematically.

高阶模仿戏剧的核心主题是“焦点”或“向心凝视”，无论这种凝视的对象是情妇、朋友还是神明，似乎都带有某种宫廷凝视君主、法庭凝视演说家或观众凝视演员的意味。因为高阶模仿戏剧的诗人首先是一位朝臣、一位顾问、一位布道者、一位公共演说家或一位礼仪大师，而高阶模仿戏剧时期正是固定剧场作为主要虚构形式媒介蓬勃发展的时期。在莎士比亚的作品中，礼仪的掌控如此之强，以至于他的个性完全被礼仪所掩盖，但这种情况不太可能发生在像本·琼森这样具有强烈主题兴趣的剧作家身上。通常，高阶模仿戏剧的诗人倾向于将自己的功能与社会或神圣的领导地位联系起来，领导主题是其常规虚构模式的核心。宫廷诗人将学识奉献给宫廷，将一生奉献给礼仪：他所受教育的目的是侍奉君主，而其最终目的则是……这是一种宫廷爱情，被视为凝视美后与之结合的圆满满足。宗教诗人或许会将这种意象移植到精神生活中，正如英国玄学派诗人常做的那样；又或许，他会在礼拜仪式中寻找这种向心意象。十七世纪的耶稣会诗歌，以及克拉肖的英国同类作品，都具有一种独特的象征性强度：赫伯特也一步步地将读者引入一座可见的“圣殿”。

The central episodic theme of the high mimetic is the theme of cynosure or centripetal gaze, which, whether addressed to mistress, friend, or deity, seems to have something about it of the court gazing upon its sovereign, the court-room gazing upon the orator, or the audience gazing upon the actor. For the high mimetic poet is pre-eminently a courtier, a counsellor, a preacher, a public orator or a master of decorum, and the high mimetic is the period in which the settled theatre comes into its own as the chief medium of fictional forms. In Shakespeare the control of decorum is so great that his personality disappears behind it altogether, but this is unlikely to happen with a dramatist who has a strong thematic interest, like Ben Jonson. As a rule the high mimetic poet tends to think of his function in relation to social or divine leadership, the theme of leadership being at the center of his normal fictional mode. The courtier-poet devotes his learning to the court and his life to courtesy: the function of his education is the service of his prince and the climax of it is courtly love, conceived as the fulfilling of the gaze upon beauty in the union with it. The religious poet may transfer this imagery to the spiritual life, as the English metaphysicals often do, or he may find his centripetal images in the liturgy. Jesuit poetry of the seventeenth century, and its English counterpart in Crashaw, have a unique quality of iconic intensity: Herbert, too, draws his reader step by step into a visible “temple.”

文艺复兴时期盛期的文学柏拉图主义与当时的模式相契合。大多数文艺复兴时期的人文主义者都强烈重视宴饮和对话，分别代表精英文化的社会和教育层面。此外，人们普遍认为诗歌的“理想”（ dianoia）体现了自然界的某种形式、模式、理想或典范。西德尼说：“自然界是金碧辉煌的，诗人只是将其描绘成金色的。”他明确指出，这个金色的世界并非与自然分离，而是“实际上是一种第二自然”：它是事实或例证与典范或准则的统一。在艺术和批评领域，通常所说的“新古典主义”，用我们的话来说，主要是指将诗歌的“理想”视为自然真实形式的体现，而这种真实形式被认为是理想的。

The literary Platonism of the high mimetic period is of a kind appropriate to the mode. Most of the Renaissance humanists show a strong sense of the importance of symposium and dialogue, the social and educational aspects respectively of an elite culture. There is also a widespread assumption that the dianoia of poetry represents a form, pattern, ideal, or model in nature. “Nature’s world is brazen,” says Sidney: “the poets only deliver a golden.” He makes it clear that this golden world is not something separated from nature but is “in effect a second nature”: a unification of fact, or example, with model, or precept. What is usually called the “neo-Classical” in art and criticism is chiefly, in our terms, a sense of poetic dianoia as a manifestation of the true form of nature, the true form being assumed to be ideal.

在低级模仿文学中，虚构形式关注的是一个高度个体化的社会，因此，神话的类比只能归结为一种个人创作行为。其典型结果是“浪漫主义”，这是一种主题发展，它在很大程度上背离了当时的虚构形式，并发展出一种与之截然不同的类型。创作《海伯利安》和创作《傲慢与偏见》所需的特质，尽管都属于当代，却显得格外对立，仿佛在低级模仿文学中，虚构与主题之间的界限比其他模式更为分明。在某种程度上，这种说法是正确的，因为主观与客观、精神状态与外在条件、个体与社会或物理数据之间的对比感，正是低级模仿文学的特征。在这个时代，主题诗人就如同浪漫主义时代的虚构英雄一样，是一位生活在比自然更高层次、更具想象力的体验秩序中的非凡人物。他创造了自己的世界，一个再现了前文提及的虚构浪漫主义诸多特征的世界。浪漫主义诗人的心灵通常与自然处于一种泛神论式的和谐状态，似乎对真正的邪恶侵袭具有奇特的免疫力。这是一种倾向，在早期的虚构爱情故事中也有类似的现象，将痛苦和恐惧转化为某种形式的愉悦，这体现在“浪漫主义的痛苦”中虐待狂式的描写和恶魔般的意象里。这一时期百科全书式的倾向是构建神话史诗，其中的神话代表着心理或主观的精神状态。《浮士德》，尤其是第二部分，是最接近典型的例子；布莱克的预言以及济慈和雪莱的神话诗则是英国最著名的代表。

With the low mimetic, where fictional forms deal with an intensely individualized society, there is only one thing for an analogy of myth to become, and that is an act of individual creation. The typical result of this is “Romanticism,” a thematic development which to a considerable extent turns away from contemporary forms of fiction and develops its own contrasting kind. The qualities necessary to create Hyperion and the qualities necessary to create Pride and Prejudice, though contemporary, seem curiously opposed to each other, as though there were a sharper division between fictional and thematic in the low mimetic than in other modes. To some extent this is true, for a sense of contrast between subjective and objective, mental state and outward condition, individual and social or physical data, is characteristic of the low mimetic. In this age the thematic poet becomes what the fictional hero was in the age of romance, an extraordinary person who lives in a higher and more imaginative order of experience than that of nature. He creates his own world, a world which reproduces many of the characteristics of fictional romance already touched on. The Romantic poet’s mind is normally in a state of pantheistic rapport with nature, and seems curiously invulnerable to the assaults of real evil. A tendency, also paralleled in the earlier fictional romance, to transmute pain and terror into a form of pleasure is reflected in the sadism and diabolic imagery of the “Romantic agony.” The encyclopaedic tendency of this period is toward the construction of mythological epics in which the myths represent psychological or subjective states of mind. Faust, especially in the second part, is the most nearly definitive example; the prophecies of Blake and the mythological poems of Keats and Shelley are the best known English representatives.

这一时期的主题诗人关注自身，这并非出于自负，而是因为他诗歌技巧的基础是个人化的，因而也是遗传和心理层面的。他运用生物学隐喻；他将有机体与死寂或机械的事物进行对比；他从天才与普通人之间的生物学差异出发进行社会思考，在他看来，天才是众多夭折种子中孕育出的肥沃种子。他以个体的身份直接面对自然，并且与大多数前人不同，他倾向于将文学传统视为个人经验的二手替代品。如同低俗模仿喜剧中的主人公，浪漫主义诗人常常具有社会攻击性：拥有创作天赋赋予其权威，其社会影响是革命性的。浪漫主义批评家常常提出诗歌是个人伟大修辞的理论。其核心主题是对主观心理状态的分析或呈现，这一主题通常被认为是伴随卢梭和拜伦的文学运动的典型特征。浪漫主义诗人比他的前辈们更容易做到在内容和态度上保持个性，同时在形式上保持连贯性。华兹华斯的许多短诗能够像早期诗歌汇集成史诗那样被纳入《序曲》之中，这本身就是一项意义重大的技术创新。

The thematic poet of this period is interested in himself, not necessarily out of egotism, but because the basis of his poetic skill is individual, and hence genetic and psychological. He uses biological metaphors; he contrasts the organic with the dead or mechanical; he thinks socially in terms of a biological difference between the genius and the ordinary man, and genius to him is a fertile seed among abortive ones. He confronts nature directly, as an individual, and, in contrast to most of his predecessors, is apt to think of literary tradition as a second-hand substitute for personal experience. Like the hero of low mimetic comedy, the Romantic poet is often socially aggressive: the possession of creative genius confers authority, and its social impact is revolutionary. Romantic critics often develop theories of poetry as the rhetoric of personal greatness. The central episodic theme is the analysis or presentation of the subjective mental state, a theme usually taken to be typical of the literary movements accompanying Rousseau and Byron. The Romantic poet finds it much easier than his predecessors to be at once individual in content and attitude and continuous in form. The fact that so many of Wordsworth’s shorter poems could be absorbed into the Prelude, in much the way in which primitive lays stick together to form epics, represents a technical innovation of some significance.

继浪漫主义之后的诗人，例如法国象征主义诗人，以一种反讽的姿态开始，他们背离了充斥着模糊音节和不明确含义的市场世界：他们摒弃了修辞、道德评判以及所有其他世俗偶像，将全部精力投入到诗人作为诗歌创作者的字面功能中。我们说过，反讽小说家除了技艺之外不受任何其他因素的影响，而反讽时代的主题诗人则更多地将自己视为工匠，而非创造者或“未被认可的”诗人。立法者。”也就是说，他极力淡化自己的个性，却极力展现自己的艺术——这种对比正是叶芝诗歌面具理论的基石。在他最好的状态下，他是一位虔诚的灵魂，一位诗歌的圣人或隐士。福楼拜、里尔克、马拉美、普鲁斯特，都以各自不同的方式成为了“纯粹的”艺术家。因此，贯穿全书的核心主题是纯粹而短暂的视野，是审美或永恒的瞬间，是兰波的顿悟，是乔伊斯的灵感，是现代德国思想的顿悟，也是象征主义和意象主义等术语所蕴含的那种非说教式的启示。

The poets who succeed the Romantics, the poets of French symbolisme for example, begin with the ironic gesture of turning away from the world of the market-place, with all its blurred sounds and imprecise meanings: they renounce rhetoric, moral judgement, and all other idols of the tribe, and devote their entire energy to the poet’s literal function as a maker of poems. We said that the ironic fiction-writer is influenced by no considerations except craftsmanship, and the thematic poet in the ironic age thinks of himself more as a craftsman than as a creator or “unacknowledged legislator.” That is, he makes the minimum claim for his personality and the maximum for his art—a contrast which underlies Yeats’s theory of the poetic mask. At his best he is a dedicated spirit, a saint or anchorite of poetry. Flaubert, Rilke, Mallarmé, Proust, were all in their very different ways “pure” artists. Hence the central episodic theme is the theme of the pure but transient vision, the aesthetic or timeless moment, Rimbaud’s illumination, Joyce’s epiphany, the Augenblick of modern German thought, and the kind of non-didactic revelation implied in such terms as symbolisme and imagism.

将此类瞬间与历史展开的宏大全景（“逝去的时光”）进行比较，是百科全书式倾向的主要主题。在普鲁斯特的作品中，某些经历在分散的时间间隔内反复出现，从而创造出这些超越时间的永恒瞬间；在《芬尼根守灵夜》中，整个历史本身被呈现为一个巨大的反顿悟。在较小但同样具有百科全书式的尺度上，艾略特的《荒原》和弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的最后一部也是最深刻的作品《幕间》有着共同之处（这一点尤其引人注目，因为它们除此之外并无其他共同之处）：它们都体现了一种对比感，即整个文明的进程与揭示其意义的微小而重要的瞬间之间的对比。正如浪漫主义诗人发现以连续的形式进行个人写作是可能的，反讽模式也通过诗歌本质不连续性的批评理论得到了合理化。这种既包罗万象又断断续续的诗歌技巧，如《荒原》和埃兹拉·庞德的《诗章》所采用的技巧，与华兹华斯的直接对立面一样，是一种技术创新，预示着一种新的模式的出现。

The comparison of such instants with the vast panorama unrolled by history (“temps perdu”) is the main theme of the encyclopaedic tendency. In Proust the repetitions of certain experiences at widely scattered intervals create these timeless moments out of time; in Finnegans Wake the whole of history itself is presented as a single gigantic anti-epiphany. On a smaller but still encyclopaedic scale, Eliot’s The Waste Land and Virginia Woolf’s last and most profound book, Between the Acts, have in common (a fact more striking because they have nothing else in common) a sense of contrast between the course of a whole civilization and the tiny flashes of significant moments which reveal its meaning. And just as the Romantic poet found it possible to write as an individual in continuous forms, so the ironic mode is rationalized by critical theories of the essential discontinuity of poetry. The paradoxical technique of the poetry which is encyclopaedic and yet discontinuous, the technique of The Waste Land and of Ezra Pound’s Cantos, is, like its direct opposite in Wordsworth, a technical innovation heralding a new mode.

同样的技巧细节也符合主题反讽的一般模式。这种言外之意的反讽手法，与马拉美避免直接陈述的理论不谋而合。省略谓语，仅仅并置意象而不对其关系做出任何断言，这种做法与避免雄辩修辞的努力是一致的。同样，为了模仿直接称呼，省略撇号和其他类似修辞手法也是如此。一项研究甚至表明，在反讽语境中，定冠词的使用显著增加，这种用法被认为与一种隐含的意义有关：一个心照不宣的群体意识到，在看似令人费解的反讽外表之下，隐藏着真实的含义。

Details of the same technique fit the general pattern of thematic irony. The ironic method of saying one thing and meaning something rather different is incorporated in Mallarmé’s doctrine of the avoidance of direct statement. The practice of cutting out predication, of simply juxtaposing images without making any assertions about their relationship, is consistent with the effort to avoid oratorical rhetoric. The same is true of the elimination of apostrophes and similar devices for including some mimesis of direct address. One study has even demonstrated a substantial increase in the use of the definite article in the ironic mode, a use said to be linked with the implicit sense of an initiated group aware of a real meaning behind an ironically baffling exterior.

我们在小说中观察到的反讽回归神话的现象，与反讽创作者回归神谕的倾向相呼应。这种倾向常常伴随着循环往复的历史理论，这些理论有助于合理化回归的概念，而此类理论的出现正是反讽模式的典型特征。例如，兰波及其“感官解构”（dérèglement de tous les sens），旨在使自己成为将神圣之火带给人类的普罗米修斯的转世，并恢复狂躁与预言之间古老的神话联系。里尔克一生都在紧张地聆听内心深处的神谕之声。尼采宣称人类身上出现了一种新的神力，但这种宣称却因包含着同质轮回理论而显得有些混乱。叶芝则告诉我们，西方循环即将结束，一个新的古典循环即将开始，届时丽达和天鹅将取代鸽子和处女。我们有乔伊斯和他维康式的历史理论，该理论认为我们所处的时代是一场受挫的末日浩劫，随后会立即回到特里斯特拉姆之前的时期。

The return of irony to myth that we noted in fiction is paralleled by some tendencies of the ironic craftsman to return to the oracular. This tendency is often accompanied by cyclical theories of history which help to rationalize the idea of a return, the appearance of such theories being a typical phenomenon of the ironic mode. We have Rimbaud and his “dérèglement de tous les sens” designed to make himself a reincarnation of the Prometheus who brought the divine fire to man and to restore the old mythical connection between the manic and the mantic. We have Rilke and his lifetime of tense listening to an oracular voice within him. We have Nietzsche proclaiming the advent of a new divine power in man, a proclamation which is somewhat confused by including a theory of identical recurrence. We have Yeats telling us that the Western cycle is nearly over and that a new Classical one, with Leda and the swan taking the place of the dove and the virgin, is about to begin. We have Joyce and his Viconian theory of history which sees our own age as a frustrated apocalypse followed instantly by a return to a period before Tristram.

从上述调查中可以得出一些推论，其中显而易见的一点是，许多当前的批评假设都缺乏历史背景。如今，一种反讽式的地域主义盛行，它在文学作品中处处寻求完全的客观性、摒弃道德评判、专注于纯粹的语言技巧以及其他类似的特质。另一种浪漫主义的地域主义则更为陈旧，它处处寻找天才和伟大个性的体现，但这种地域主义仍然存在。即使是崇尚高度模仿的批评模式，也曾出现过一些迂腐的拥护者，其中一些人甚至在十八世纪乃至十九世纪仍然试图将理想形式的准则应用于诗歌创作。由此可见，任何一套仅源于单一模式的批评标准都无法涵盖诗歌的全部真谛。

As for the inferences which may be made from the above survey, one is clearly that many current critical assumptions have a limited historical context. In our day an ironic provincialism, which looks everywhere in literature for complete objectivity, suspension of moral judgements, concentration on pure verbal craftsmanship, and similar virtues, is in the ascendant. A Romantic provincialism, which looks everywhere for genius and evidences of great personality, is more old-fashioned, but it is still around. The high mimetic mode also had its pedants, some of them still trying to apply canons of ideal form in the eighteenth and even the nineteenth centuries. The suggestion made here is that no set of critical standards derived from only one mode can ever assimilate the whole truth about poetry.

人们或许会注意到一种普遍的倾向，即对紧随其后的模式反应最为强烈，而对前一种模式的某些标准则稍有回避。因此，在模仿主义盛行的时代，人文主义者普遍鄙视那些创作中世纪浪漫故事的“说书人和夸夸其谈者”（斯宾塞在《EK》中如此称呼他们）。但是，正如我们在西德尼的作品中所看到的，他们从未厌倦过通过援引最初的神话阶段的社会重要性来为诗歌辩护。他们倾向于认为他们自视为自然秩序的世俗先知，如同预言家诗人一般，在社会和自然法则的框架内回应公共事务。而浪漫主义者，即低级模仿时期的主题诗人，则摒弃了前人追随自然的方式，回归浪漫主义模式。

There may be noticed a general tendency to react most strongly against the mode immediately preceding, and, to a lesser extent, to return to some of the standards of the modal grandfather. Thus the humanists of the high mimetic age were in general contemptuous of the “fablers and loud lyars,” as Spenser’s E.K. calls them, who produced medieval romance. But, as we can see in Sidney, they were never tired of justifying poetry by referring to the social importance of the original mythical phase. They tended to think of themselves as secular oracles of the order of nature, responding to the occasions of public affairs like the oracular poets, within a context of social and natural law. The Romantics, the thematic poets of the low mimetic period, set their faces against their predecessors’ methods of following nature, and went back to the mode of romance.

在英国文学中，浪漫主义标准主要由维多利亚时代继承，这表明该模式具有延续性；而始于1900年前后（法国文学则早几十年）的漫长反浪漫主义运动则标志着一种向反讽的转变。在新模式下，对小而紧密的群体的偏爱、对神秘主义的追求以及对贵族的怀旧，催生了艾略特的保皇主义、庞德的法西斯主义以及叶芝的骑士精神崇拜等截然不同的现象，而这些在某种程度上都体现了对高模仿标准的回归。诗人作为朝臣、诗歌作为侍奉君主的工具、以及宴饮或精英团体至高无上的重要性，这些都是二十世纪文学中反映的高模仿观念，尤其体现在从马拉美到乔治和里尔克的象征主义诗歌传统中。这种趋势的例外情况有时并不像表面看起来那么特殊。当萧伯纳最初加入费边社时，该社还是一个足够神秘的团体，连叶芝本人都感到满意；而当费边社会主义成为一场群众运动后，萧伯纳最终变成了一个毫无疑问的受挫的保皇党人。

The Romantic standards, in English literature, were in the main carried on by the Victorians, indicating a continuity of mode; the long anti-Romantic revolt that began around 1900 (several decades earlier in French literature) indicated a shift to the ironic. In the new mode the fondness for the small closely-knit group, the sense of the esoteric, and the nostalgia for the aristocratic that has produced such very different phenomena as the royalism of Eliot, the fascism of Pound, and the cult of chivalry in Yeats, are all in a way part of a reversion to high mimetic standards. The sense of the poet as courtier, of poetry as the service of a prince, of the supreme importance of the symposium or elite group, are among the high mimetic conceptions reflected in twentieth-century literature, especially in the poetry of the symboliste tradition from Mallarmé to George and Rilke. The exceptions to this tendency are sometimes less exceptional than they seem. The Fabian Society, when Bernard Shaw first joined it, was a group esoteric enough to satisfy Yeats himself: after Fabian socialism became a mass movement, Shaw turned into what became at length unmistakably a frustrated royalist.

再次，我们可以注意到，西方文化的每个时期都明显地借鉴了与其风格最接近的古典文学：中世纪时期浪漫化的荷马史诗；高模仿时期的维吉尔史诗、柏拉图的《宴饮》和奥维德的宫廷爱情；低模仿时期的罗马讽刺作品；以及于斯曼的《逆流》中反讽阶段的拉丁语晚期作品。

Again, we may note that each period of Western culture has made a conspicuous use of the Classical literature nearest to it in mode: romanticized versions of Homer in the Middle Ages; Virgilian epic, Platonic symposium, and Ovidian courtly love in the high mimetic; Roman satire in the low mimetic; the products of the latest possible period of Latin in the ironic phase of Huysmans’ À Rebours.

我们在对虚构模式的考察中看到，诗人从未模仿“生活”，因为生活本身并非他作品的内容。在每一种模式中，他都将同一种神话形式强加于其内容之上，但对其进行不同的改编。同样，在主题模式中，诗人也从未模仿思想，除非是将文学形式强加于其思想之上。未能理解这一点会导致一种谬误，我们可以将其统称为“存在投射”。假设一位作家他发现自己最擅长创作悲剧。他的作品必然充满阴郁和灾难，在结尾，人物们会围坐在一起，感叹命运的残酷无情、世事的变迁和宿命的不可抗拒。这些感伤是悲剧精神的一部分；但一位专攻悲剧的作家很可能会觉得这些感伤代表了最深刻的哲学，当被问及自己的人生哲学时，他自己也会开始发表类似的言论。另一方面，一位擅长喜剧和圆满结局的作家，会让笔下的人物在结尾围坐在一起，谈论天意的恩赐、意想不到的奇迹，以及我们都应该对生活的恩惠心怀感恩和喜悦。

We saw in our survey of fictional modes that the poet never imitates “life” in the sense that life becomes anything more than the content of his work. In every mode he imposes the same kind of mythical form on his content, but makes different adaptations of it. In thematic modes, similarly, the poet never imitates thought except in the same sense of imposing a literary form on his thought. The failure to understand this produces a fallacy to which we may give the general term “existential projection.” Suppose a writer finds that he is most successful with tragedies. His works will inevitably be full of gloom and catastrophe, and in his final scenes there will be characters standing around making remarks about the sternness of necessity, the vicissitudes of fortune, and the ineluctability of fate. Such sentiments are part of the dianoia of tragedy; but a writer who specializes in tragedy may well come to feel that they speak for the profoundest of all philosophies, and begin to emit similar utterances himself when asked what his own philosophy of life is. On the other hand, a writer whose specialty is comedy and happy endings will have his characters standing around at the end talking about the beneficence of providence, the miracles that come when we least expect them, the spirit of thankfulness and joy which we all ought to feel for the mercies of life.

因此，悲剧和喜剧自然而然地会将自身的影子投射到哲学领域，分别塑造出一种命运哲学和天意哲学。托马斯·哈代和萧伯纳都活跃于1900年前后，并且都对进化论感兴趣。哈代在悲剧创作方面更为出色，他将进化论视为一种斯多葛式的改良主义、叔本华式的内在意志，以及一种“偶然”或“巧合”的活动，在这种活动中，任何个体的生命都可能被牺牲。萧伯纳创作喜剧，他认为进化具有创造性，会导致革命性的政治、超人的出现，以及某种元生物学的出现。但显而易见，哈代和萧伯纳并非真正意义上的哲学家，他们的成就最终取决于他们在诗歌、小说和戏剧领域的成就。

It is natural, then, for tragedy and comedy to throw their shadows, so to speak, into philosophy and shape there a philosophy of fate and a philosophy of providence respectively. Thomas Hardy and Bernard Shaw both flourished around 1900 and both were interested in evolution. Hardy did better with tragedy, and saw evolution in terms of a stoical meliorism, a Schopenhauerian immanent will, and an activity of “chance” or “hap” in which any individual life may be expendable. Shaw, who wrote comedies, saw evolution as creative, leading to revolutionary politics, the advent of a Superman, and to whatever metabiology is. But it is obvious that Hardy and Shaw are not substantial philosophers, and they must stand or fall by their achievements in poetry, fiction, and drama.

同样，每一种文学模式都发展出其自身的存在投射。神话投射自身为神学：也就是说，神话诗人通常会接受某些神话为“真理”，并据此构建其诗歌结构。浪漫主义则以奇幻的、通常不可见的人物或力量来填充世界：天使、恶魔、仙女、幽灵、被施了魔法的动物、元素精灵，例如《暴风雨》和《科莫斯》中的那些。但丁以这种模式写作，但并非出于思辨：他接受了基督教教义所认可的精神存在，而对其他存在则不感兴趣。但对于一位对浪漫主义技巧感兴趣的晚期诗人——例如叶芝——这些神秘生物是否以及哪些“真正存在”的问题很可能会投射到他们的创作中。高级模仿文学主要投射一种准柏拉图式的理想形式哲学，例如斯宾塞赞美诗中的爱与美，或《仙后》中的美德。低级模仿论主要是一种关于起源和有机体的哲学，类似于歌德的哲学，它在万物中发现统一性和发展。反讽的存在主义投射或许就是存在主义本身；而反讽回归神话，不仅伴随着前文提及的历史循环理论，而且在后期还伴随着对圣礼哲学和教义神学的广泛兴趣。

Similarly, each mode of literature develops its own existential projection. Mythology projects itself as theology: that is, a mythopoeic poet usually accepts some myths as “true” and shapes his poetic structure accordingly. Romance peoples the world with fantastic, normally invisible personalities or powers: angels, demons, fairies, ghosts, enchanted animals, elemental spirits like those in The Tempest and Comus. Dante wrote in this mode, but not speculatively: he accepted the spiritual beings recognized by Christian doctrine, and concerns himself with no others. But for a late poet interested in the techniques of romance—Yeats, for instance—the question of whether and which of these mysterious creatures “really exist” is likely to project itself. The high mimetic projects mainly a quasi-Platonic philosophy of ideal forms, like the love and beauty of Spenser’s hymns or the virtues of The Faerie Queene, and the low mimetic mainly a philosophy of genesis and organism, like that of Goethe, which finds unity and development in everything. The existential projection of irony is, perhaps, existentialism itself; and the return of irony to myth is accompanied, not only by the cyclical theories of history mentioned above, but, in a later stage, by a widespread interest in sacramental philosophy and dogmatic theology.

艾略特先生区分了两种诗人：一种是创造属于自己的哲学体系的诗人，另一种是接受现成哲学体系的诗人。他认为，对于大多数诗人而言，后者更好，或者至少更安全。这种区分的根本在于主题诗人实践方式的差异，即低级模仿模式与反讽模式的差异。像布莱克、雪莱、歌德和维克多·雨果这样的诗人，由于其创作模式的惯例，不得不将意象的概念层面呈现为自我生成的；而上个世纪的诗人则有着不同的惯例和不同的创作动力。但是，如果这里对诗歌形式与内容关系的观点是正确的，那么无论诗人选择哪种方式，他们仍然会面临大致相同的技术难题。

Mr. Eliot distinguishes between the poet who creates a philosophy for himself, and the poet who takes over one that he finds to hand, and advances the view that the latter course is better, or at least safer, for most poets. The distinction is fundamentally a distinction between the practice of the thematic poets of the low mimetic and of the ironic modes. Such poets as Blake, Shelley, Goethe, and Victor Hugo were compelled by the conventions of their mode to present the conceptual aspect of their imagery as self-generated; the poets of the last century have different conventions and different compulsions. But if the view taken here of the relation of form to content in poetry is sound, then no matter which he does the poet will still have much the same technical problems to face.

自亚里士多德以来，批评界倾向于将文学视为本质上模仿的，并将其分为两类：一类是描写统治阶级人物的“高雅”史诗和悲剧，另一类是仅限于喜剧和讽刺作品、更关注像我们这样的普通人的“低雅”文学。本章提出的宏大框架，有望为理解柏拉图关于诗歌的不同且看似矛盾的论述提供有益的背景。《斐德罗篇》主要探讨诗歌作为神话的意义，并对柏拉图的神话论述进行了评注；《伊翁篇》以吟游诗人或吟游诗人的形象为中心，阐述了浪漫主义模式下典型的百科全书式和纪念式诗歌观念；《会饮篇》介绍了阿里斯托芬，并采纳了可能最接近柏拉图自身观点的“高雅”模仿规范。 《理想国》结尾处那场著名的讨论，就此成为对诗歌中低级模仿元素的批判；而在《克拉底鲁篇》中，我们则接触到了反讽的技巧，例如歧义、词语联想、谐音双关，以及如今正被批评界重新发掘的修辞手法。探讨反讽模式的诗歌——这种批评通过对反讽的进一步提炼，被称为“新”批评。

Ever since Aristotle criticism has tended to think of literature as essentially mimetic, and as divided between a “high” form of epic and tragedy dealing with ruling-class figures, and a “low” form confined to comedy and satire and more concerned with characters like ourselves. The larger scheme set forth in this chapter will, it is hoped, afford a useful background against which to relate the different and apparently contradictory remarks of Plato about poetry. Phaedrus deals largely with poetry as myth, and forms a commentary on Plato’s treatment of myth; Ion, which is centered on the figure of a minstrel or rhapsode, sets forth both the encyclopaedic and the memorial conceptions of poetry which are typical of the romantic mode; the Symposium, which introduces Aristophanes, adopts the high mimetic canons which are probably nearest to Plato’s own views. The famous discussion at the end of the Republic then falls into its place as a polemic against the low mimetic element in poetry, and in the Cratylus we are introduced to the ironic techniques of ambiguity, verbal association, paronomasia, and the apparatus now being revived by criticism to deal with the poetry of the ironic mode—the criticism which, by a further refinement of irony, is called “new” criticism.

再次强调，我们之前描述的虚构性和主题性之间的区别，对应于贯穿批评史的两种文学观之间的区别。这两种观点分别是审美观和创作观，亚里士多德式的和朗吉尼式的，文学作为产品和文学作为过程的观点。对亚里士多德而言，诗歌是一种技艺或审美产物：作为批评家，他主要关注的是更为客观的虚构形式，其核心概念是净化（catharsis）。净化意味着观众与艺术作品本身以及作者的分离。“审美距离”这一概念如今在批评界已被普遍接受，但这几乎是一种同义反复：凡是有审美感知的地方，就必然存在情感和理智上的分离。亚里士多德并未阐述其他虚构形式（如喜剧或讽刺作品）中净化的原则，因此此后也无人阐述。

Again, the difference in emphasis that we have described as fictional and thematic corresponds to a distinction between two views of literature that has run all through the history of criticism. These two views are the aesthetic and the creative, the Aristotelian and the Longinian, the view of literature as product and the view of literature as process. For Aristotle, the poem is a techne or aesthetic artifact: he is, as a critic, mainly interested in the more objective fictional forms, and his central conception is catharsis. Catharsis implies the detachment of the spectator, both from the work of art itself and from the author. The phrase “aesthetic distance” is generally accepted now in criticism, but it is almost a tautology: wherever there is aesthetic apprehension there is emotional and intellectual detachment. The principles of catharsis in other fictional forms than tragedy, such as comedy or satire, were not worked out by Aristotle, and have therefore never been worked out since.

在文学的主题层面，作者与读者之间的外部关系变得更加突出，此时，怜悯和恐惧等情感便被卷入其中或被抑制，而非被净化。在净化过程中，情感通过依附于客体而得到净化；而当情感与回应本身交织在一起时，它们便脱离了客体，成为心灵的先决条件。我们注意到，没有具体客体的恐惧，作为一种先于恐惧的心理状态，如今被视为焦虑或不安，这是一个略显狭隘的术语，它涵盖了从沉思者的愉悦到恶之花的痛苦等各种情感。在愉悦的范畴内，出现了崇高的概念，其中，简朴、阴郁、宏伟、忧郁，甚至威胁，都成为浪漫或沉思之情的源泉。

In the thematic aspect of literature, the external relation between author and reader becomes more prominent, and when it does, the emotions of pity and terror are involved or contained rather than purged. In catharsis the emotions are purged by being attached to objects; where they are involved with the response they are unattached and remain prior conditions in the mind. We have noticed that terror without an object, as a condition of mind prior to being afraid of anything, is now conceived as Angst or anxiety, a somewhat narrow term for a feeling that extends from the pleasure of Il Penseroso to the pain of the Fleurs du Mal. In the general area of pleasure comes the conception of the sublime, in which austerity, gloom, grandeur, melancholy, or even menace are a source of romantic or penseroso feelings.

同样，我们将无对象的怜悯定义为一种富有想象力的万物有灵论，它在自然界中处处发现人性的特质，并包含“美”——传统上，美是崇高（sublime）的对应词。美与渺小之间的关系，正如崇高与宏伟之间的关系，并且与精巧和精致的感觉密切相关。英国民间传说中的仙女变成了莎士比亚笔下的芥菜籽和德雷顿笔下的猪仔，而叶芝的万物有灵论则与他对“许多精巧可爱的事物”的感受，以及他在《驶向拜占庭》中对玩具鸟的描绘紧密相连。

Similarly, we defined pity without an object as an imaginative animism which finds human qualities everywhere in nature, and includes the “beautiful,” traditionally the corresponding term to the sublime. The beautiful has the same relation to the diminutive that the sublime has to bigness, and is closely related to the sense of the intricate and exquisite. The fairies of English folklore become Shakespeare’s Mustard-Seed and Drayton’s Pigwiggen, and Yeats’s animism is linked to his sense of “many ingenious lovely things,” and to his image of the toy bird in Sailing to Byzantium.

正如净化（catharsis）是亚里士多德文学理论的核心概念，狂喜（ecstasis）或沉浸（octinction）则是朗吉尼理论的核心概念。这是一种认同状态，读者、诗歌，有时（至少在理想情况下）诗人自身都参与其中。我们之所以强调“读者”，是因为朗吉尼的理论主要关注主题性或个体化的回应：它更适用于抒情诗，正如亚里士多德的理论更适用于戏剧一样。然而，有时常规的分析方法并不适用。正如艾略特先生所指出的，在《哈姆雷特》中，主人公所引发的情感远超其对象所能承受的范围；但从这一精辟的见解中得出的正确结论无疑是：《哈姆雷特》的最佳解读方式是将其视为一种焦虑或忧郁状态的悲剧，而非仅仅将其视为亚里士多德式的对某种行为的模仿。另一方面，包括约翰逊在内的一些人认为，《利西达斯》缺乏情感投入是这首诗的失败之处，但正确的结论肯定是， 《利西达斯》和《力士参孙》一样，应该从情感宣泄的角度来解读，所有激情都已耗尽。

Just as catharsis is the central conception of the Aristotelian approach to literature, so ecstasis or absorption is the central conception of the Longinian approach. This is a state of identification in which the reader, the poem, and sometimes, at least ideally, the poet also, are involved. We say reader, because the Longinian conception is primarily that of a thematic or individualized response: it is more useful for lyrics, just as the Aristotelian one is more useful for plays. Sometimes, however, the normal categories of approach are not the right ones. In Hamlet, as Mr. Eliot has shown, the amount of emotion generated by the hero is too great for its objects; but surely the correct conclusion to draw from this fine insight is that Hamlet is best approached as a tragedy of Angst or of melancholy as a state in itself, rather than purely as an Aristotelian imitation of an action. On the other hand, the lack of emotional involvement in Lycidas has been thought by some, including Johnson, to be a failure in that poem, but surely the correct conclusion is that Lycidas, like Samson Agonistes, should be read in terms of catharsis with all passion spent.

第二篇论文

：伦理批评：符号理论

SECOND ESSAY

Ethical Criticism: Theory of Symbols

第二篇论文

Second Essay

伦理批判：符号理论

ETHICAL CRITICISM: THEORY OF SYMBOLS

介绍

INTRODUCTION

诗学专业术语的匮乏引发了诸多问题，其中有两个尤其值得关注。正如前文所述，文学艺术作品竟然没有对应的词汇，这一点尤其令我困惑。有人或许会援引亚里士多德的权威来解释为何“诗”一词可以用于此义，但惯例表明，诗是一种韵律优美的作品，而将《汤姆·琼斯》称为诗则是对日常语言的滥用。人们或许会探讨伟大的散文作品是否配得上在更广义的意义上被称为诗，但答案最终只能取决于个人对定义的偏好。试图在诗的定义中引入价值判断（例如，“我们究竟如何定义一首诗——也就是说，什么才配得上‘诗’这个名称？”）只会加剧混乱。当然，那种关于韵律优越性的古老势利眼也同样如此，它使得“散文体”（prosy）一词带有了枯燥乏味的含义，“平淡无奇”（prosaic）一词则带有了平庸乏味的含义。我尽可能地使用“诗”及其近义词进行提喻，因为它们是简短的词语；但是，如果提喻会令人困惑，读者就不得不忍受诸如“假设的动词结构”之类的刺耳术语。

OF THE PROBLEMS arising from the lack of a technical vocabulary of poetics, two demand special attention. The fact, already mentioned, that there is no word for a work of literary art is one that I find particularly baffling. One may invoke the authority of Aristotle for using “poem” in this sense, but usage declares that a poem is a composition in metre, and to speak of Tom Jones as a poem would be an abuse of ordinary language. One may discuss the question whether great works of prose deserve to be called poetry in some more extended sense, but the answer can only be a matter of taste in definitions. The attempt to introduce a value-judgement into a definition of poetry (e.g., “What, after all, do we mean by a poem—that is, something worthy of the name of poem?”) only adds to the confusion. So of course does the antique snobbery about the superiority of metre which has given “prosy” the meaning of tedious and “prosaic” the meaning of pedestrian. As often as I can, I use “poem” and its relatives by synecdoche, because they are short words; but where synecdoche would be confusing, the reader will have to put up with such cacophonous jargon as “hypothetical verbal structure” and the like.

另一个问题涉及“符号”一词的使用。在本文中，“符号”指的是任何文学结构中可以被单独提取出来进行批判性分析的单元。一个词、一个短语或一个意象，如果带有某种特殊含义（这通常被理解为符号的含义），那么当它们在批判性分析中成为可区分的元素时，它们就都是符号。甚至作家用来拼写单词的字母，在这个意义上也是其符号体系的一部分：它们只有在特殊情况下才会被单独提取出来，例如头韵或方言拼写，但我们仍然意识到它们象征着声音。根据这个定义，批评整体而言始于对文学符号体系的系统化，并且主要由文学符号体系的系统化构成。由此可见，我们需要使用其他词语来对不同类型的符号体系进行分类。

The other matter concerns the use of the word “symbol,” which in this essay means any unit of any literary structure that can be isolated for critical attention. A word, a phrase, or an image used with some kind of special reference (which is what a symbol is usually taken to mean) are all symbols when they are distinguishable elements in critical analysis. Even the letters a writer spells his words with form part of his symbolism in this sense: they would be isolated only in special cases, such as alliteration or dialect spellings, but we are still aware that they symbolize sounds. Criticism as a whole, in terms of this definition, would begin with, and largely consist of, the systematizing of literary symbolism. It follows that other words must be used to classify the different types of symbolism.

因为文学批评必然有不同的类型：它绝不可能是一种简单或单一层次的活动。我们比较熟悉的批评类型是……随着对一部伟大文学作品的理解不断加深，这种理解的加深也愈发明显。此外，这种加深体现在对作品本身的理解上，而非对作品所能赋予的意义数量的增加。一部文学作品蕴含着多种或一系列意义，这一结论似乎是无可回避的。然而，自中世纪以来，批评界很少正面探讨这一问题。当时，人们从神学中汲取灵感，将一套精确的字面意义、寓言意义、道德意义和象征意义体系应用于文学领域。如今，人们更倾向于将文学意义问题视为符号逻辑和语义学问题的附属问题。在下文中，我将尽可能独立于后两者之外进行探讨，因为探寻文学意义理论的显而易见的起点，正是文学本身。

For there must be different types: the criticism of literature can hardly be a simple or one-level activity. The more familiar one is with a great work of literature, the more one’s understanding of it grows. Further, one has the feeling of growing in the understanding of the work itself, not in the number of things one can attach to it. The conclusion that a work of literary art contains a variety or sequence of meanings seems inescapable. It has seldom, however, been squarely faced in criticism since the Middle Ages, when a precise scheme of literal, allegorical, moral, and anagogic meanings was taken over from theology and applied to literature. Today there is more of a tendency to consider the problem of literary meaning as subsidiary to the problems of symbolic logic and semantics. In what follows I try to work as independently of the latter subjects as I can, on the ground that the obvious place to start looking for a theory of literary meaning is in literature.

但丁称之为“多重意义”或“多义性”的原则，不再是一种理论，更非早已破灭的迷信，而是一个既定的事实。确立这一原则的是现代批评学派的并行发展，每个学派在其分析中都做出了独特的符号选择。现代批判理论的学生面临着这样的选择：修辞学家谈论的是文本的质感和正面攻击；历史学家研究的是传统和史料；批评家运用心理学和人类学的素材；还有亚里士多德主义者、柯勒律治主义者、托马斯主义者、弗洛伊德主义者、荣格主义者、马克思主义者；以及研究神话、仪式、原型、隐喻、歧义和意义形式的学者。学生要么承认多重意义的原则，要么选择其中一个学派，然后试图证明其他学派的合法性不足。前者是学术研究之道，也是推动知识进步的途径；后者是迂腐之道，它给我们提供了广泛的目标选择，如今最引人注目的是奇幻学习或神话批判、争论学习或历史批判，以及精细学习或“新”批判。

The principle of manifold or “polysemous” meaning, as Dante calls it, is not a theory any more, still less an exploded superstition, but an established fact. The thing that has established it is the simultaneous development of several different schools of modern criticism, each making a distinctive choice of symbols in its analysis. The modern student of critical theory is faced with a body of rhetoricians who speak of texture and frontal assaults, with students of history who deal with traditions and sources, with critics using material from psychology and anthropology, with Aristotelians, Coleridgians, Thomists, Freudians, Jungians, Marxists, with students of myths, rituals, archetypes, metaphors, ambiguities, and significant forms. The student must either admit the principle of polysemous meaning, or choose one of these groups and then try to prove that all the others are less legitimate. The former is the way of scholarship, and leads to the advancement of learning; the latter is the way of pedantry, and gives us a wide choice of goals, the most conspicuous today being fantastical learning, or myth criticism, contentious learning, or historical criticism, and delicate learning, or “new” criticism.

一旦我们承认了多义性原则，我们可以止步于纯粹的相对主义和多元主义立场，也可以继续探讨是否存在数量有限的有效批判方法，以及它们是否可以被纳入单一理论之中。但这并不意味着所有意义都可以像中世纪的四级体系所暗示的那样，按照等级顺序排列，其中最初的步骤相对简单，而随着理解的深入，理解则变得越来越微妙和深奥。此处使用“层次”一词仅为方便起见，并不代表我认同存在一系列批判性入门的等级制度。此外，关于多义意义的概念，我仍需保留一些看法：文学作品的意义是更大整体的一部分。在前一篇文章中，我们看到意义或内涵（dianoia）是三个要素之一，另外两个要素是神话（mythos）或叙事，以及人物塑造（ethos）或人物刻画。因此，我们最好不要仅仅将意义视为一系列意义的序列，而是将其视为一系列语境或关系​​，整个文学作品可以置于其中，每个语境都有其独特的神话、内涵以及内涵或意义。我将这些语境或关系​​称为“阶段”。

Once we have admitted the principle of polysemous meaning, we can either stop with a purely relative and pluralistic position, or we can go on to consider the possibility that there is a finite number of valid critical methods, and that they can all be contained in a single theory. It does not follow that all meanings can be arranged, as the medieval four-level scheme implies, in a hierarchical sequence, in which the first steps are comparatively elementary and apprehension gets more subtle and rarefied as one goes on. The term “level” is used here only for convenience, and should not be taken as indicating any belief on my part in a series of degrees of critical initiation. Again, there is a general reservation to be made about the conception of polysemous meaning: the meaning of a literary work forms a part of a larger whole. In the previous essay we saw that meaning or dianoia was one of three elements, the other two being mythos or narrative and ethos or characterization. It is better to think, therefore, not simply of a sequence of meanings, but of a sequence of contexts or relationships in which the whole work of literary art can be placed, each context having its characteristic mythos and ethos as well as its dianoia or meaning. I call these contexts or relationships “phases.”

字面意义和描述性阶段：

符号作为母题和标志

LITERAL AND DESCRIPTIVE PHASES:

SYMBOL AS MOTIF AND AS SIGN

无论何时阅读，我们的注意力都会同时向两个方向移动。一个方向是向外或离心的，我们不断地跳出阅读本身，从单个词语延伸到它们所代表的事物，或者更实际地说，是回到我们对词语之间约定俗成关联的记忆。另一个方向是向内或向心的，我们试图从词语中提炼出它们所构成的更大的语言模式。在这两种情况下，我们都在处理符号，但当我们赋予一个词语外部意义时，除了词语符号本身，我们还有它所代表或象征的事物。实际上，我们拥有一系列这样的表征：词语符号“猫”是页面上的一组黑色标记，代表着一系列声音，这些声音代表着一个图像或记忆，而这个图像或记忆又代表着一种感官体验，最终代表着一只会喵喵叫的动物。如此理解的符号在这里可以被称为符号，即语言单位，它们约定俗成地、任意地代表并指向它们出现位置之外的事物。然而，当我们试图把握词语的语境时，“猫”这个词就成为了更大意义体系中的一个元素。它并非主要象征任何事物，因为就此而言，它并非代表，而是连接。我们甚至很难说它代表了作者将其置于此位置的意图，因为作者的意图一旦完成修改便不再作为一个独立因素存在。从内在或向外理解的语言元素，作为语言结构的一部分，作为符号而言，仅仅是语言元素或语言结构的单元。（“字面意义上”一词应保留）（记住。）我们可以借用音乐中的一个术语，将这样的元素称为主题。

Whenever we read anything, we find our attention moving in two directions at once. One direction is outward or centrifugal, in which we keep going outside our reading, from the individual words to the things they mean, or, in practice, to our memory of the conventional association between them. The other direction is inward or centripetal, in which we try to develop from the words a sense of the larger verbal pattern they make. In both cases we deal with symbols, but when we attach an external meaning to a word we have, in addition to the verbal symbol, the thing represented or symbolized by it. Actually we have a series of such representations: the verbal symbol “cat” is a group of black marks on a page representing a sequence of noises representing an image or memory representing a sense experience representing an animal that says meow. Symbols so understood may here be called signs, verbal units which, conventionally and arbitrarily, stand for and point to things outside the place where they occur. When we are trying to grasp the context of words, however, the word “cat” is an element in a larger body of meaning. It is not primarily a symbol “of” anything, for in this aspect it does not represent, but connects. We can hardly even say that it represents a part of the author’s intention in putting it there, for the author’s intention ceases to exist as a separate factor as soon as he has finished revising. Verbal elements understood inwardly or centripetally, as parts of a verbal structure, are, as symbols, simply and literally verbal elements, or units of a verbal structure. (The word “literally” should be kept in mind.) We may, borrowing a term from music, call such elements motifs.

这两种理解模式在所有阅读中同时发生。在阅读“猫”这个词时，不可能不联想到某种与该动物相关的具象；看到“猫”这个单独的符号，也不可能不去思考它属于哪个语境。但是，语言结构可以根据其意义的最终方向是外向还是内向进行分类。在描述性或陈述性写作中，意义的最终方向是外向的。在这种情况下，语言结构旨在代表其外部的事物，其价值取决于它代表这些事物的准确性。现象与语言符号之间的对应关系是真理；缺乏对应关系是谬误；无法建立联系是同义反复，一种纯粹的语言结构，它无法从自身出发产生意义。

These two modes of understanding take place simultaneously in all reading. It is impossible to read the word “cat” in a context without some representational flash of the animal so named; it is impossible to see the bare sign “cat” without wondering what context it belongs to. But verbal structures may be classified according to whether the final direction of meaning is outward or inward. In descriptive or assertive writing the final direction is outward. Here the verbal structure is intended to represent things external to it, and it is valued in terms of the accuracy with which it does represent them. Correspondence between phenomenon and verbal sign is truth; lack of it is falsehood; failure to connect is tautology, a purely verbal structure that cannot come out of itself.

在所有文学语言结构中，意义的最终方向都是向内的。在文学中，外在意义的标准是次要的，因为文学作品并不试图描述或断言，因此既非真也非假，也非同义反复，至少并非像“好比坏”这样的陈述那样的同义反复。文学意义或许最好被描述为假设性的，而与外部世界的假设性或假定性关系正是“想象力”一词通常含义的一部分。这个词应与“想象的”区分开来，后者通常指的是一种断言性的语言结构，但这种结构未能实现其断言。在文学中，事实或真理的问题服从于文学的首要目标——即为了结构本身而创造文字结构；符号的符号价值服从于它们作为相互关联的主题结构的重要性。凡是有这种自主语言结构的地方，我们就拥有了文学。凡是缺乏这种自主结构的地方，我们都有语言，也就是工具性地使用词语来帮助人类意识去做或理解其他事物。文学是语言的一种特殊形式，正如语言是交流的一种特殊形式一样。

In all literary verbal structures the final direction of meaning is inward. In literature the standards of outward meaning are secondary, for literary works do not pretend to describe or assert, and hence are not true, not false, and yet not tautological either, or at least not in the sense in which such a statement as “the good is better than the bad” is tautological. Literary meaning may best be described, perhaps, as hypothetical, and a hypothetical or assumed relation to the external world is part of what is usually meant by the word “imaginative.” This word is to be distinguished from “imaginary,” which usually refers to an assertive verbal structure that fails to make good its assertions. In literature, questions of fact or truth are subordinated to the primary literary aim of producing a structure of words for its own sake, and the sign-values of symbols are subordinated to their importance as a structure of interconnected motifs. Wherever we have an autonomous verbal structure of this kind, we have literature. Wherever this autonomous structure is lacking, we have language, words used instrumentally to help human consciousness do or understand something else. Literature is a specialized form of language, as language is of communication.

文学结构之所以存在，显然是因为其内在含义，即自洽的语言模式，是与愉悦、美感和趣味相关的各种反应的源泉。对一种独立模式（无论是否由文字构成）的沉思，显然是感知美感及其伴随的愉悦感的重要来源。这种模式最容易激发兴趣，这一点对于每一位文字工作者来说都耳熟能详。诗人与餐后演讲者一样，后者往往从慷慨激昂的演说中抽离出来，转而讲述一个自成一体、结构精巧的笑话。很多时候，一些原本以描述为主的文字作品，例如富勒和吉本的历史著作，在事实陈述价值消逝之后，却凭借其“风格”或引人入胜的语言模式而流传下来。

The reason for producing the literary structure is apparently that the inward meaning, the self-contained verbal pattern, is the field of the responses connected with pleasure, beauty, and interest. The contemplation of a detached pattern, whether of words or not, is clearly a major source of the sense of the beautiful, and of the pleasure that accompanies it. The fact that interest is most easily aroused by such a pattern is familiar to every handler of words, from the poet to the after-dinner speaker who digresses from an assertive harangue to present the self-contained structure of verbal interrelationships known as a joke. It often happens that an originally descriptive piece of writing, such as the histories of Fuller and Gibbon, survives by virtue of its “style,” or interesting verbal pattern, after its value as a representation of facts has faded.

诗歌旨在愉悦和教化，这句古老的格言听起来像是一个别扭的二元对立，因为我们通常不会觉得一首诗对我们产生了两种不同的影响。但如果我们将其与象征主义的这两个方面联系起来，就能理解它了。在文学中，娱乐性先于教化性，或者说，现实原则服从于愉悦原则。而在表达性语言结构中，这种优先顺序则相反。当然，这两种因素都无法从任何类型的写作中完全剔除。

The old precept that poetry is designed to delight and instruct sounds like an awkward hendiadys, as we do not usually feel that a poem does two different things to us, but we can understand it when we relate it to these two aspects of symbolism. In literature, what entertains is prior to what instructs, or, as we may say, the reality-principle is subordinate to the pleasure-principle. In assertive verbal structures the priority is reversed. Neither factor can, of course, ever be eliminated from any kind of writing.

文学最为人熟知且最重要的特征之一，便是缺乏对描述准确性的执着追求。我们或许会希望，历史剧的作者了解其主题的历史事实，并且不会无缘无故地篡改它们。但文学中存在这样的正当理由，这一点无人否认。它们似乎只存在于文学领域：历史学家选择史实，但若暗示他为了构建更对称的结构而操纵史实，则构成诽谤。某些其他类型的语言结构，例如神学和形而上学，被一些人宣称其最终意义具有向心性，因而属于同义反复（“纯粹的语言”）。对此我并无异议，只是认为在文学批评中，神学和形而上学必须被视为一种断言，因为它们游离于文学之外，而任何来自外部影响文学的事物，无论其指向的是绝对存在的本质，还是关于啤酒花种植的建议，都会在文学内部产生一种离心运动。显而易见，在不同的文学形式中，愉悦的娱乐感与启迪感（或对现实的觉醒感）之间的比例也会有所不同。例如，悲剧的现实感远高于喜剧，因为在喜剧中，事件的逻辑通常会让位于观众对美好结局的渴望。

One of the most familiar and important features of literature is the absence of a controlling aim of descriptive accuracy. We should, perhaps, like to feel that the writer of a historical drama knew what the historical facts of his theme were, and that he would not alter them without good reason. But that such good reasons may exist in literature is not denied by anyone. They seem to exist only there: the historian selects his facts, but to suggest that he had manipulated them to produce a more symmetrical structure would be grounds for libel. Some other types of verbal structures, such as theology and metaphysics, are declared by some to be centripetal in final meaning, and hence to be tautological (“purely verbal”). I have no opinion on this, except that in literary criticism theology and metaphysics must be treated as assertive, because they are outside literature, and everything that influences literature from without creates a centrifugal movement in it, whether it is directed toward the nature of absolute being or advice on the raising of hops. It is clear, too, that the proportion between the sense of being pleasantly entertained and the sense of being instructed, or awakened to reality, will vary in different forms of literature. The sense of reality is, for instance, far higher in tragedy than in comedy, as in comedy the logic of events normally gives way to the audience’s desire for a happy ending.

诗人似乎拥有无视事实的独特特权，这使他长期以来被认为是“有执照的说谎者”，也解释了为什么许多表示文学结构的词语，例如“寓言”、“小说”、“神话”等等，都带有“不真实”的引申义，就像……挪威语单词“digter”既指“诗人”，也指“说谎者”。但正如菲利普·西德尼爵士所言，“诗人从不断言”，因此，诗人既不说谎，也不说真话。诗人如同纯粹数学家，依赖的并非描述性的真理，而是符合其假设的前提。哈姆雷特中鬼魂的出现，提出了“哈姆雷特中存在鬼魂”这一假设。这与鬼魂是否存在无关，也与莎士比亚或他的观众是否相信鬼魂存在无关。如果一个读者质疑这些假设，仅仅因为他不相信有鬼魂存在或人们用五音步诗句说话而讨厌哈姆雷特，那么他显然不适合文学。他无法区分虚构与现实，与那些给广播电台捐款以救济肥皂剧中受苦女主角的人属于同一类人。我们不妨在此指出（这一点在后面会很重要），被接受的假设，即读者在开始阅读之前所同意的约定，与惯例是一回事。

The apparently unique privilege of ignoring facts has given the poet his traditional reputation as a licensed liar, and explains why so many words denoting literary structure, “fable,” “fiction,” “myth,” and the like, have a secondary sense of untruth, like the Norwegian word digter which is said to mean liar as well as poet. But, as Sir Philip Sidney remarked, “the poet never affirmeth,” and therefore does not lie any more than he tells the truth. The poet, like the pure mathematician, depends, not on descriptive truth, but on conformity to his hypothetical postulates. The appearance of a ghost in Hamlet presents the hypothesis “let there be a ghost in Hamlet.” It has nothing to do with whether ghosts exist or not, or whether Shakespeare or his audience thought they did. A reader who quarrels with postulates, who dislikes Hamlet because he does not believe that there are ghosts or that people speak in pentameters, clearly has no business in literature. He cannot distinguish fiction from fact, and belongs in the same category as the people who send cheques to radio stations for the relief of suffering heroines in soap operas. We may note here, as the point will be important later, that the accepted postulate, the contract agreed on by the reader before he can start reading, is the same thing as a convention.

那些无法理解文学惯例的人常被称作“字面思维”。但“字面”一词理应与文字有所关联，因此用“字面思维”来形容那些想象力丰富的文盲似乎有些奇怪。这种反常现象背后的原因很有意思，也对我们的论证至关重要。传统上，“字面意义”指的是没有歧义的描述性意义。我们通常说，当“猫”这个词恰如其分地指代猫，与会发出“喵”叫声的动物之间存在简单的代表性关系时，它就“字面意义”指的就是猫。这种“字面意义”的用法源于中世纪，可能与批评范畴的神学渊源有关。在神学中，圣经的字面意义通常指的是历史意义，即它作为事实或真理记录的准确性。但丁在评论《诗篇》中的经文“以色列人出埃及的时候”，时说：“单从字面意义来看，摩西时代以色列人出埃及到巴勒斯坦的事件，就是它向我们所指的（significatur nobis）。”这里的“指称”一词表明，其字面意义是最简单的描述性或象征性意义，正如圣经“字面主义者”所理解的那样。

The person who cannot be brought to understand literary convention is often said to be “literal-minded.” But as “literal” surely ought to have some connection with letters, it seems curious to use the phrase “literal-minded” for imaginative illiterates. The reason for the anomaly is interesting, and important to our argument. Traditionally, the phrase “literal meaning” refers to descriptive meaning that is free from ambiguity. We usually say that the word cat “means literally” a cat when it is an adequate sign for a cat, when it stands in a simple representative relation to the animal that says meow. This sense of the term literal comes down from medieval times, and may be due to the theological origin of critical categories. In theology, the literal meaning of Scripture is usually the historical meaning, its accuracy as a record of facts or truths. Dante says, commenting on the verse in the Psalms, “When Israel went out of Egypt,” “considering the letter only, the exodus of the Israelites to Palestine in the time of Moses is what is signified to us (significatur nobis).” The word “signified” shows that the literal meaning here is the simplest kind of descriptive or representational meaning, as it would still be to a Biblical “literalist.”

但这种将字面意义理解为简单描述意义的观点，对于文学批评而言是完全行不通的。历史事件的字面意义只能是历史事件；描述历史事件的散文叙事，其字面意义也只能是散文叙事。但丁《神曲》的字面意义并非历史性的，至少并非对但丁“真实经历”的简单描述。如果一首诗除了诗歌本身之外别无其他字面意义，那么诗歌意义的字面基础就只能是它的字母，是它内部相互交织的意象结构。在批评的语境下，如果我们说“这首诗的字面意义是……”，然后又用散文式的语言对其进行释义，那就大错特错了。所有释义都会抽象出其次要的或外在的意义。真正理解一首诗的字面意义，意味着理解它作为一个整体，作为一个独立存在的整体。这种理解始于心灵和感官完全臣服于作品整体的冲击力，并通过努力将各种象征符号融会贯通，最终感知到结构的整体性。 （这是斯蒂芬在乔伊斯《青年艺术家画像》中论证的关键要素的逻辑顺序，即完整性、连贯性和清晰度。我不知道心理顺序是什么，或者是否存在这样的顺序——我想格式塔理论中应该不存在。）字面理解在批评中占据着与观察（即心灵直接接触自然）在科学方法中相同的地位。“每一首诗都必然是一个完美的统一体，”布莱克说：正如其措辞所暗示的，这并非对所有现存诗歌的事实陈述，而是每个读者在试图理解哪怕是最混乱的诗歌时都会首先接受的假设。

But this conception of literal meaning as simple descriptive meaning will not do at all for literary criticism. An historical event cannot be literally anything but an historical event; a prose narrative describing it cannot be literally anything but a prose narrative. The literal meaning of Dante’s own Commedia is not historical, not at any rate a simple description of what “really happened” to Dante. And if a poem cannot be literally anything but a poem, then the literal basis of meaning in poetry can only be its letters, its inner structure of interlocking motifs. We are always wrong, in the context of criticism, when we say “this poem means literally”—and then give a prose paraphrase of it. All paraphrases abstract a secondary or outward meaning. Understanding a poem literally means understanding the whole of it, as a poem, and as it stands. Such understanding begins in a complete surrender of the mind and senses to the impact of the work as a whole, and proceeds through the effort to unite the symbols toward a simultaneous perception of the unity of the structure. (This is a logical sequence of critical elements, the integritas, consonantia, and claritas of Stephen’s argument in Joyce’s Portrait. I have no idea what the psychological sequence is, or whether there is a sequence—I suppose there would not be in a Gestalt theory.) Literal understanding occupies the same place in criticism that observation, the direct exposure of the mind to nature, has in the scientific method. “Every poem must necessarily be a perfect unity,” says Blake: this, as the wording implies, is not a statement of fact about all existing poems, but a statement of the hypothesis which every reader adopts in first trying to comprehend even the most chaotic poem ever written.

某种循环往复的原则似乎是所有艺术作品的根本，这种循环往复通常在时间维度上被称为节奏，在空间维度上被称为模式。因此，我们谈论音乐的节奏和绘画的模式。但稍加深入思考，我们便会开始谈论音乐的模式和绘画的节奏。由此可知，所有艺术都兼具时间性和空间性，无论哪一方面在呈现时占据主导地位。交响乐的乐谱可以作为一个整体来研究，如同一个展开的模式；一幅画作可以被视为视觉错综复杂的舞动轨迹。文学作品也像音乐一样在时间中流动，像绘画一样在图像中展开。“叙事”或“神话”一词传达了听觉捕捉到的运动感，“意义”或“意义性”一词传达了，或者至少保留了，视觉捕捉到的同时性感。我们聆听这首诗从头到尾的演变，但当整首诗同时涌入脑海时，我们才“明白”它的含义。更确切地说，这种反应不仅仅是整体，而是整体之中的整体：只要有可能同时领悟到意义或精神，我们就能获得这种领悟。

Some principle of recurrence seems to be fundamental to all works of art, and this recurrence is usually spoken of as rhythm when it moves along in time, and as pattern when it is spread out in space. Thus we speak of the rhythm of music and the pattern of painting. But a slight increase of sophistication will soon start us talking about the pattern of music and the rhythm of painting. The inference is that all arts possess both a temporal and a spatial aspect, whichever takes the lead when they are presented. The score of a symphony may be studied all at once, as a spread-out pattern: a painting may be studied as the track of an intricate dance of the eye. Works of literature also move in time like music and spread out in images like painting. The word narrative or mythos conveys the sense of movement caught by the ear, and the word meaning or dianoia conveys, or at least preserves, the sense of simultaneity caught by the eye. We listen to the poem as it moves from beginning to end, but as soon as the whole of it is in our minds at once we “see” what it means. More exactly, this response is not simply to the whole of it, but to a whole in it: we have a vision of meaning or dianoia whenever any simultaneous apprehension is possible.

既然诗歌本身就是一首诗，那么从字面上讲，它就属于诗歌这一范畴，而诗歌本身又属于艺术作品这一更大的范畴。从这个角度来看，诗歌一方面呈现出近似音乐的音韵流动，另一方面呈现出近似绘画的意象模式。因此，从字面上讲，诗歌的叙事就是它的节奏或词语的韵律。如果一位剧作家用散文写了一段演讲，然后又将其改写成无韵诗，那么他就做出了一个策略性的节奏变化，因此也改变了诗歌的叙事。即使他把“came a day”改成“a day came”，他也只是对顺序做了细微的改动，因此，从字面上讲，他的节奏和叙事也发生了改变。同样，诗歌的意义就在于它作为一种语言结构的模式或完整性。诗歌中的词语无法被分离出来并与符号值关联：一个词的所有可能的符号值都被吸收到复杂的语言关系之中。

Now as a poem is literally a poem, it belongs, in its literal context, to the class of things called poems, which in their turn form part of the larger class known as works of art. The poem from this point of view presents a flow of sounds approximating music on one side, and an integrated pattern of imagery approximating the pictorial on the other. Literally, then, a poem’s narrative is its rhythm or movement of words. If a dramatist writes a speech in prose, and then rewrites it in blank verse, he has made a strategic rhythmical change, and therefore a change in the literal narrative. Even if he alters “came a day” to “a day came” he has still made a tiny alteration of sequence, and so, literally, of his rhythm and narrative. Similarly, a poem’s meaning is literally its pattern or integrity as a verbal structure. Its words cannot be separated and attached to sign-values: all possible sign-values of a word are absorbed into a complexity of verbal relationships.

因此，从向心或内在意义的角度来看，这个词的含义是多变的或含糊的——借用批评界如今常用的一个术语——值得注意的是，这个术语在用于论断性写作时带有贬义。据说，蒲柏在《论批评》中用了九种不同的含义来使用“机智”一词。在论断性写作中，这种语义主题及其变化只会造成混乱不堪。在诗歌中，它表明了一个词可能具有的意义和语境范围。诗人并不将一个词等同于一个意义；他确立的是词语的功能或力量。但是，当我们把诗歌的符号视为语言符号时，诗歌就出现在一个完全不同的语境中，它的叙事和意义也随之改变。从描述的角度来看，诗歌首先不是一件艺术作品，而首先是一种语言结构或一组代表性词语，应该与其他语言结构（例如园艺书籍）归为一类。在此语境下，叙事指的是词语的顺序与类似于外部“生活”中事件的事件之间的关系；意义指的是其模式与一系列断言命题之间的关系；而其中涉及的象征意义的概念，是文学与其他文字结构而非艺术所共有的概念。

The word’s meaning is therefore, from the centripetal or inward-meaning point of view, variable or ambiguous, to use a term now familiar in criticism, a term which, significantly enough, is pejorative when applied to assertive writing. The word “wit” is said to be employed in Pope’s Essay on Criticism in nine different senses. In assertive writing, such a semantic theme with variations could produce nothing but hopeless muddle. In poetry, it indicates the ranges of meanings and contexts that a word may have. The poet does not equate a word with a meaning; he establishes the functions or powers of words. But when we look at the symbols of a poem as verbal signs, the poem appears in a different context altogether, and so do its narrative and meaning. Descriptively, a poem is not primarily a work of art, but primarily a verbal structure or set of representative words, to be classed with other verbal structures like books on gardening. In this context narrative means the relation of the order of words to events resembling the events in “life” outside; meaning means the relation of its pattern to a body of assertive propositions, and the conception of symbolism involved is the one which literature has in common, not with the arts, but with other structures in words.

在这个阶段，大量的抽象思维开始发挥作用。当我们把一首诗的叙事理解为对事件的描述时，我们……我们不再将叙事视为字面意义上的逐字逐句。我们更多地将其视为一系列粗略的事件，以及词序中那些显而易见、引人注目的元素。同样地，我们认为意义是一种话语意义，即诗歌的散文释义所能再现的意义。因此，象征主义的概念也出现了类似的抽象。在字面层面，符号是母题，任何单位，甚至细化到字母，都可能与我们的理解相关。但只有那些重要且引人注目的符号才有可能被批判性地视为符号：名词、动词以及由重要词语构成的短语。介词和连词几乎只是纯粹的连接词。字典本质上是一张约定俗成的符号值表，除非我们已经理解了这些词语，否则它无法告诉我们任何关于这些词语的信息。

A considerable amount of abstraction enters at this stage. When we think of a poem’s narrative as a description of events, we no longer think of the narrative as literally embracing every word and letter. We think rather of a sequence of gross events, of the obvious and externally striking elements in the word-order. Similarly, we think of meaning as the kind of discursive meaning that a prose paraphrase of the poem might reproduce. Hence a parallel abstraction comes into the conception of symbolism. On the literal level, where the symbols are motifs, any unit whatever, down to the letters, may be relevant to our understanding. But only large and striking symbols are likely to be treated critically as signs: nouns and verbs, and phrases built up out of important words. Prepositions and conjunctions are almost pure connectives. A dictionary, which is primarily a table of conventional sign-values, can tell us nothing about such words unless we already understand them.

因此，文学在其描述性语境中是一系列假想的语言结构。这些假想的语言结构介于描述或安排实际事件或历史的语言结构，以及描述或安排实际观念或表征物理对象的语言结构之间，例如哲学和科学的语言结构。空间世界与概念世界的关系显然无法在此探讨；但从文学批评的角度来看，描述性写作和说教性写作，对自然对象和观念的表征，仅仅是意义离心化的两个不同分支。我们可以用“情节”或“故事”来指代一系列粗略的事件，而故事与历史的联系在其词源中就有所体现。但是，用“思想”，甚至“思想内容”，来指代模式的表征层面或粗略的意义则更为困难，因为“思想”一词本身也描述了我们试图与之区分开来的对象。这就是诗学词汇的难题。

So literature in its descriptive context is a body of hypothetical verbal structures. The latter stand between the verbal structures that describe or arrange actual events, or histories, and those that describe or arrange actual ideas or represent physical objects, like the verbal structures of philosophy and science. The relation of the spatial to the conceptual world is one that we obviously cannot examine here; but from the point of view of literary criticism, descriptive writing and didactic writing, the representation of natural objects and of ideas, are simply two different branches of centrifugal meaning. We may use the word “plot” or “story” for the sequence of gross events, and the connection of story with history is indicated in its etymology. But it is more difficult to use “thought,” or even “thought-content,” for the representational aspect of pattern, or gross meaning, because “thought” also describes what we are here trying to distinguish it from. Such are the problems of a vocabulary of poetics.

当然，象征主义的字面意义和描述性两个阶段都存在于每一部文学作品中。但我们发现（正如我们将在其他阶段中发现的那样），每个阶段都与某种特定的文学类型以及某种特定的批评方法有着特别密切的联系。深受象征主义描述性方面影响的文学作品，其叙事往往趋向现实主义，意义则倾向于说教或描述。其主要节奏是直接引语的散文，其主要目标是在假设的结构框架下，尽可能清晰、真实地展现外部现实。在通常与以下名称相关的纪实自然主义作品中，左拉和德莱塞认为，文学对生活的再现已臻极致，评判其优劣的标准在于描述的准确性，而非文字结构的完整性，只要它仍能保持文学的本质，便可称之为文学。超越此限，文学中的假设或虚构元素便会开始消解。当然，此类文学表达的界限非常宽广，几乎所有伟大的现实主义诗歌、戏剧和散文小说都包含在其中。但我们注意到，纪实自然主义的鼎盛时期——十九世纪，同时也是浪漫主义诗歌的时代。浪漫主义诗歌注重想象的创造过程，体现了文学中假设元素与现实元素之间的一种张力。

The literal and the descriptive phases of symbolism are, of course, present in every work of literature. But we find (as we shall also find with the other phases) that each phase has a particularly close relationship to a certain kind of literature, and to a certain type of critical procedure as well. Literature deeply influenced by the descriptive aspect of symbolism is likely to tend toward the realistic in its narrative and toward the didactic or descriptive in its meaning. Its prevailing rhythm will be the prose of direct speech, and its main effort will be to give as clear and honest an impression of external reality as is possible with a hypothetical structure. In the documentary naturalism generally associated with such names as Zola and Dreiser, literature goes about as far as a representation of life, to be judged by its accuracy of description rather than by its integrity as a structure of words, as it could go and still remain literature. Beyond this point, the hypothetical or fictional element in literature would begin to dissolve. The limits of literary expression of this type are, of course, very wide, and nearly all the great empire of realistic poetry, drama, and prose fiction lies well within them. But we notice that the great age of documentary naturalism, the nineteenth century, was also the age of Romantic poetry, which, by concentrating on the process of imaginative creation, indicated a feeling of tension between the hypothetical and the assertive elements in literature.

这种张力最终在通常被称为象征主义的运动中得以消除。在这里，我们将“象征主义”一词扩展为涵盖整个传统，这一传统从马拉美和兰波的法国作品发展而来，贯穿瓦莱里、德国的里尔克以及英国的庞德和艾略特等众多作家。象征主义理论是对极端自然主义的补充，它强调意义的字面意义，并将文学视为一种向心性的语言模式，其中直接或可验证的陈述元素服从于该模式的完整性。“纯粹”诗歌的概念，或者说被断言意义所破坏的富有感染力的语言结构，是同一运动的一个次要产物。象征主义的强大之处在于它成功地提炼出了文学的假想萌芽，尽管在其早期阶段，由于它倾向于将这种提炼等同于整个创作过程，因此可能存在局限性。它的所有特征都牢固地建立在其对诗歌的理解之上，即诗歌关注的是意义的向心性。因此，批评中对字面意义的合理理解的形成，是文学领域相对较新的发展成果。
