This tension finally snaps off in the movement generally called symbolisme, a term which we expand here to take in the whole tradition which develops with a broad consistency through Mallarmé and Rimbaud to Valéry in France, Rilke in Germany, and Pound and Eliot in England. In the theory of symbolisme we have the complement to extreme naturalism, an emphasis on the literal aspect of meaning, and a treatment of literature as centripetal verbal pattern, in which elements of direct or verifiable statement are subordinated to the integrity of that pattern. The conception of “pure” poetry, or evocative verbal structure injured by assertive meaning, was a minor by-product of the same movement. The great strength of symbolisme was that it succeeded in isolating the hypothetical germ of literature, however limited it may have been in its earlier stages by its tendency to equate this isolation with the entire creative process. All its characteristics are solidly based on its conception of poetry as concerned with the centripetal aspect of meaning. Thus the achieving of an acceptable theory of literal meaning in criticism rests on a relatively recent development in literature.

象征主义，例如马拉美所阐述的，认为在阅读诗歌时，不应执着于对“这是什么意思？”这个问题的表象性解答，因为诗歌的象征意义主要在于其自身与诗歌的关系。因此，诗歌的统一性最好被理解为情绪的统一性，情绪是情感的一种状态，而情感则是指向体验愉悦或欣赏美的心理状态的常用词。由于情绪不会持续很长时间，因此，在象征主义看来，文学本质上是不连续的。较长的诗歌仅靠更适用于描述性写作的语法结构维系。诗歌意象本身并不陈述或指向任何事物，而是通过彼此呼应，暗示或唤起贯穿全诗的情绪。也就是说，它们表达或阐明了这种情绪。这种情感并非混乱或难以言喻：如果它没有化作诗歌，它就会保持这种状态；而当它化作诗歌时，它本身就是诗歌，而非隐藏在其后的某种东西。尽管如此，这些暗示和唤起的词语依然恰当，因为在象征主义中，词语并非呼应事物本身，而是呼应其他词语，因此象征主义带给读者的直接感受如同咒语一般，一种音韵的和谐，以及一种超越字面意义、不断丰富且日益增长的意义感。

Symbolisme, as expressed for instance in Mallarmé, maintains that the representational answer to the question “what does this mean?” should not be pressed in reading poetry, for the poetic symbol means primarily itself in relation to the poem. The unity of a poem, then, is best apprehended as a unity of mood, a mood being a phase of emotion, and emotion being the ordinary word for the state of mind directed toward the experiencing of pleasure or the contemplating of beauty. And as moods are not long sustained, literature, for symbolisme, is essentially discontinuous, longer poems being held together only by the use of the grammatical structures more appropriate to descriptive writing. Poetic images do not state or point to anything, but, by pointing to each other, they suggest or evoke the mood which informs the poem. That is, they express or articulate the mood. The emotion is not chaotic or inarticulate: it merely would have remained so if it had not turned into a poem, and when it does so, it is the poem, not something else still behind it. Nevertheless the words suggest and evoke are appropriate, because in symbolisme the word does not echo the thing but other words, and hence the immediate impact symbolisme makes on the reader is that of incantation, a harmony of sounds and the sense of a growing richness of meaning unlimited by denotation.

有些哲学家认为所有意义都是描述性的意义，他们认为，既然诗歌并非理性地描述事物，那么它必然是对某种情感的描述。按照这种观点，诗歌的字面核心就是一种“心声”（ cri de coeur），用一个优雅的表达来说，就是神经质的有机体面对某种似乎需要情感回应的事物时所发出的直接陈述，就像狗对着月亮嚎叫一样。根据这种理论，《快板》（L' Allegro）和《沉思者》（Il Penseroso）分别是“我感到快乐”和“我感到沉思”的延伸。然而，我们发现，诗歌的真正核心是一种微妙而难以捉摸的语言模式，它避免了，也并非导向这种直白的陈述。我们还注意到，在文学史上，谜语、神谕、咒语和隐喻都比对主观感受的呈现更为原始。那些认为诗歌表达的基础是反讽，或者说是一种背离显而易见（即描述性）含义的词语模式的评论家，至少在字面层面上，更接近文学经验的实际情况。文学结构之所以具有反讽性，是因为“它所说的”与“它所指的”在性质或程度上总是不同的。在论述性写作中，所说的话往往接近，理想情况下，甚至会等同于所指。

Some philosophers who assume that all meaning is descriptive meaning tell us that, as a poem does not describe things rationally, it must be a description of an emotion. According to this the literal core of poetry would be a cri de coeur, to use the elegant expression, the direct statement of a nervous organism confronted with something that seems to demand an emotional response, like a dog howling at the moon. L’Allegro and Il Penseroso would be respectively, according to this theory, elaborations of “I feel happy” and “I feel pensive.” We have found, however, that the real core of poetry is a subtle and elusive verbal pattern that avoids, and does not lead to, such bald statements. We notice too that in the history of literature the riddle, the oracle, the spell, and the kenning are more primitive than a presentation of subjective feelings. The critics who tell us that the basis of poetic expression is irony, or a pattern of words that turns away from obvious (i.e., descriptive) meaning, are much closer to the facts of literary experience, at least on the literal level. The literary structure is ironic because “what it says” is always different in kind or degree from “what it means.” In discursive writing what is said tends to approximate, ideally to become identified with, what is meant.

文学批评和创作都体现了象征主义字面意义和描述意义之间的区别。与研究和学术期刊相关的批评将诗歌视为一种文字文献，力求将其与所反映的历史和思想尽可能地联系起来。当诗歌最为直白、描述详尽，其想象性假设的核心也最容易被理解时，它对这类批评就最具价值。两者是分离的。（请注意，我指的是一种批评方式，而非某种批评家。）另一方面，如今所谓的“新批评”很大程度上是基于将诗歌视为诗歌本身的观念而进行的批评。它研究诗歌的象征意义，将其视为由相互交织的主题构成的模糊结构；它将诗歌的意义模式视为一种自洽的“肌理”；它认为诗歌的外部关系与其他艺术形式相关，只能以贺拉斯“ favete linguis”（热爱语言）的告诫来理解，而不能以历史或教诲的方式来理解。“肌理”一词，因其蕴含着复杂表面的含义，最能体现这种方法。批评的这两个方面常常被认为是相互对立的，正如上个世纪相应的作家群体也被认为是对立的一样。它们当然是互补的，而非对立的，但在我们继续探讨象征主义的第三阶段来解决这种对立之前，理解它们之间的侧重点差异仍然至关重要。

The criticism as well as the creation of literature reflects the distinction between literal and descriptive aspects of symbolism. The type of criticism associated with research and learned journals treats the poem as a verbal document, to be related as fully as possible to the history and the ideas that it reflects. The poem is most valuable to this kind of criticism when it is most explicit and descriptive, and when its core of imaginative hypothesis can be most easily separated. (Note that I am speaking of a kind of criticism, not of a kind of critic.) What is now called “new criticism,” on the other hand, is largely criticism based on the conception of a poem as literally a poem. It studies the symbolism of a poem as an ambiguous structure of interlocking motifs; it sees the poetic pattern of meaning as a self-contained “texture,” and it thinks of the external relations of a poem as being with the other arts, to be approached only with the Horatian warning of favete linguis, and not with the historical or the didactic. The word texture, with its overtones of a complicated surface, is a most expressive one for this approach. These two aspects of criticism are often thought of as antithetical, as were, in the previous century, the corresponding groups of writers. They are of course complementary, not antithetical, but still the difference in emphasis between them is important to grasp before we go on to try to resolve the antithesis in a third phase of symbolism.

形式阶段：符号即图像

FORMAL PHASE: SYMBOL AS IMAGE

我们如今已为文学批评确立了“字面意义”这一术语的新含义，并将文学作品与其他所有词语结构所共有的普通描述意义，作为其意义的次要方面之一，赋予了文学。然而，仅仅止步于愉悦与教诲、反讽地脱离现实与明确地与现实联系之间这种令人费解的对立，似乎并不令人满意。诚然，有人会说，我们忽略了文学作品中由最常用的批评术语—— “形式”——所表达的本质统一性。因为“形式”的通常联想似乎将这些看似矛盾的方面结合起来。一方面，形式蕴含着我们所说的字面意义，或者说结构的统一性；另一方面，它也蕴含着诸如内容和物质等互补的术语，表达了作品与外部自然之间的共通之处。诗歌的形式并非自然，但它却自然地与自然相联系，因此，再次引用西德尼的话，“实际上发展出一种第二自然”。

We have now established a new sense of the term “literal meaning” for literary criticism, and have also assigned to literature, as one of its subordinate aspects of meaning, the ordinary descriptive meaning that works of literature share with all other structures of words. But it seems unsatisfactory to stop with this quizzical antithesis between delight and instruction, ironic withdrawal from reality and explicit connection with it. Surely, it will be said, we have overlooked the essential unity, in works of literature, expressed by the commonest of all critical terms, the word form. For the usual associations of “form” seem to combine these apparently contradictory aspects. On the one hand, form implies what we have called the literal meaning, or unity of structure; on the other, it implies such complementary terms as content and matter, expressive of what it shares with external nature. The poem is not natural in form, but it relates itself naturally to nature, and so, to quote Sidney again, “doth grow in effect a second nature.”

由此，我们对叙事和意义有了更为统一的理解。亚里士多德谈到“模仿行为”（mimesis praxeos），即对行为的模仿，而且他似乎将这种模仿行为等同于“神话”（ mythos）。亚里士多德在此处的论述极为简略，需要一些重构。人类行为（praxis）主要通过历史（histories）或描述具体行为的语言结构来模仿。神话（mythos ）是对行为的二次模仿，这并非意味着它与现实相隔两层，而是说它描述的是典型的行为，更偏向哲学而非历史。人类的思想（theoria）主要通过论述性写作来模仿，这种写作做出具体而明确的预测。而论述（dianoia）则是对思想的二次模仿，一种对语言的模仿（mimesis logou），它关注的是典型的思想，关注的是那些孕育特定观念的意象、隐喻、图式和语言歧义。因此，诗歌比哲学更偏向历史，更注重意象和例证。因为显而易见，所有具有意义的语言结构都是对难以捉摸的心理和生理过程——即思想——的语言模仿。思想的过程跌跌撞撞地穿过情感纠葛、突如其来的非理性信念、不由自主的灵光一现、理性化的偏见以及恐慌和惰性的阻碍，最终达到一种完全无法言说的直觉。任何认为哲学不是对这一过程的语言模仿，而是这一过程本身的人，显然都没有进行过深入的思考。

Here we reach a more unified conception of narrative and meaning. Aristotle speaks of mimesis praxeos, an imitation of an action, and it appears that he identifies this mimesis praxeos with mythos. Aristotle’s greatly abbreviated account here needs some reconstruction. Human action (praxis) is primarily imitated by histories, or verbal structures that describe specific and particular actions. A mythos is a secondary imitation of an action, which means, not that it is at two removes from reality, but that it describes typical actions, being more philosophical than history. Human thought (theoria) is primarily imitated by discursive writing, which makes specific and particular predications. A dianoia is a secondary imitation of thought, a mimesis logou, concerned with typical thought, with the images, metaphors, diagrams, and verbal ambiguities out of which specific ideas develop. Poetry is thus more historical than philosophy, more involved in images and examples. For it is clear that all verbal structures with meaning are verbal imitations of that elusive psychological and physiological process known as thought, a process stumbling through emotional entanglements, sudden irrational convictions, involuntary gleams of insight, rationalized prejudices, and blocks of panic and inertia, finally to reach a completely incommunicable intuition. Anyone who imagines that philosophy is not a verbal imitation of this process, but the process itself, has clearly not done much thinking.

诗歌的形式，即所有细节所关联的本质，无论我们将其视为静止的，还是将其视为从头到尾的流动，都是相同的，正如音乐作品的形式，无论我们研究乐谱还是聆听演奏，其形式都相同。神话是动态的意象；意象是静止的神话。我们倾向于仅从意义的角度思考文学象征主义的原因之一是，我们通常没有一个词来描述文学作品中动态的意象集合。形式一词通常有两个互补的词：质料和内容，而将形式视为塑造原则还是包含原则，或许能起到一定的区分作用。作为塑造原则，它可以被视为叙事，在时间上组织弥尔顿在那个术语更为精确的时代称之为他诗歌“质料”的内容。作为包含原则，它可以被视为意义，将诗歌以一种同步的结构凝聚在一起。

The form of a poem, that to which every detail relates, is the same whether it is examined as stationary or as moving through the work from beginning to end, just as a musical composition has the same form when we study the score as it has when we listen to the performance. The mythos is the dianoia in movement; the dianoia is the mythos in stasis. One reason why we tend to think of literary symbolism solely in terms of meaning is that we have ordinarily no word for the moving body of imagery in a work of literature. The word form has normally two complementary terms, matter and content, and it perhaps makes some distinction whether we think of form as a shaping principle or as a containing one. As shaping principle, it may be thought of as narrative, organizing temporally what Milton called, in an age of more exact terminology, the “matter” of his song. As containing principle it may be thought of as meaning, holding the poem together in a simultaneous structure.

在十六至十八世纪西欧盛行的文学标准，通常被称为“古典”或“新古典”，与这一形式阶段最为接近。秩序和清晰尤为重要：秩序源于把握中心形式的重要性，清晰则源于这种形式不应消解或陷入歧义，而必须保持连贯性。回归自然本身的内容。这是历史意义上的“人文主义”的典型态度，这种态度一方面体现为对修辞和语言技巧的推崇，另一方面体现为对历史和伦理事务的强烈关注。

The literary standards generally called “Classical” or “neo-Classical,” which prevailed in Western Europe from the sixteenth to the eighteenth centuries, have the closest affinity with this formal phase. Order and clarity are particularly emphasized: order because of the sense of the importance of grasping a central form, and clarity because of the feeling that this form must not dissolve or withdraw into ambiguity, but must preserve a continuous relationship to the nature which is its own content. It is the attitude characteristic of “humanism” in the historical sense, an attitude marked on the one hand by a devotion to rhetoric and verbal craftsmanship, and on the other by a strong attachment to historical and ethical affairs.

形式主义阶段的典型作家——例如本·琼森——确信他们与现实保持联系，并遵循自然规律，但他们所产生的效果与十九世纪的描述性现实主义截然不同，这种差异主要体现在对模仿的理解上。在形式模仿，或亚里士多德式的模仿中，艺术作品并非反映外部事件和观念，而是存在于范例与准则之间。事件和观念如今成为作品内容的组成部分，而非外部的观察领域。历史小说并非旨在深入剖析某个历史时期，而是作为典范；它们展现行动，并以体现人类行为普遍模式的意义上的理想化。（语言的变幻莫测使得“典范的”既可以作“范例”，也可以作“准则”。）莎士比亚和琼森对历史抱有浓厚的兴趣，但他们的戏剧却似乎超越了时代；简·奥斯汀虽然没有创作历史小说，但由于她代表了一种更晚近、更外化的遵循自然的方法，她所描绘的摄政时期社会图景具有特殊的历史价值。

Writers typical of the formal phase—Ben Jonson for instance—are sure that they are in contact with reality and that they follow nature, yet the effect they produce is quite different from the descriptive realism of the nineteenth century, the difference being largely in the conception of imitation involved. In formal imitation, or Aristotelian mimesis, the work of art does not reflect external events and ideas, but exists between the example and the precept. Events and ideas are now aspects of its content, not external fields of observation. Historical fictions are not designed to give insight into a period of history, but are exemplary; they illustrate action, and are ideal in the sense of manifesting the universal form of human action. (The vagaries of language make “exemplary” the adjective for both example and precept.) Shakespeare and Jonson were keenly interested in history, yet their plays seem timeless; Jane Austen did not write historical fiction, yet, because she represents a later and more externalized method of following nature, the picture she gives of Regency society has a specific historical value.

哈姆雷特认为，诗歌如同镜子，映照出自然。尽管他谈论的是表演，但其诗歌形式遵循的是文艺复兴时期传统的诗学思路。我们应当仔细体会这句话的含义：诗歌本身并非一面镜子。它并非仅仅再现自然的影子，而是使自然在其所承载的形式中得以映照。因此，当形式批评家探讨象征意义时，他所分离出的单元，正是那些展现诗歌与其所模仿的自然之间比例相似性的单元。从这个意义上讲，象征或许更恰当地被称为意象。我们习惯于将“自然”一词主要与外部的物质世界联系起来，因此我们倾向于认为意象主要是对自然物体的复制。但当然，这两个词的含义远比这更为广泛：“自然”既包含概念或可理解的秩序，也包含空间秩序；而通常被称为“观念”的事物，也可能是一种诗歌意象。

A poem, according to Hamlet, who, though speaking of acting, is following a conventional Renaissance line of poetics, holds the mirror up to nature. We should be careful to notice what this implies: the poem is not itself a mirror. It does not merely reproduce a shadow of nature; it causes nature to be reflected in its containing form. When the formal critic comes to deal with symbols, therefore, the units he isolates are those which show an analogy of proportion between the poem and the nature which it imitates. The symbol in this aspect may best be called the image. We are accustomed to associate the term “nature” primarily with the external physical world, and hence we tend to think of an image as primarily a replica of a natural object. But of course both words are far more inclusive: nature takes in the conceptual or intelligible order as well as the spatial one, and what is usually called an “idea” may be a poetic image also.

文学作品中的事件并非真实发生，而是虚构的，这几乎是一条最基本的批评原则。然而，不知何故，这一点却从未得到一致的认可。人们明白，文学的思想并非真正的命题，而是模仿真正命题的语言公式。《人论》并非阐述一套建立在存在之链之上的形而上学乐观主义体系：它只是将这样的体系作为一种模型，以此构建一系列假设性陈述。这些陈述作为命题几乎毫无用处，但若置于恰当的语境中，作为警句来解读，则蕴含着无穷的丰富内涵和启发意义。作为警句，作为坚实、铿锵有力、具有向心性的语言结构，它们可以精准地应用于数百万种与形而上学乐观主义无关的人类境况。华兹华斯的泛神论、但丁的托马斯主义、卢克莱修的伊壁鸠鲁主义，都必须以同样的方式解读；吉本、麦考利或休谟的作品，若以风格而非主题来解读，也应如此。

One could hardly find a more elementary critical principle than the fact that the events of a literary fiction are not real but hypothetical events. For some reason it has never been consistently understood that the ideas of literature are not real propositions, but verbal formulas which imitate real propositions. The Essay on Man does not expound a system of metaphysical optimism founded on the chain of being: it uses such a system as a model on which to construct a series of hypothetical statements which are more or less useless as propositions, but inexhaustibly rich and suggestive when read in their proper context as epigrams. As epigrams, as solid, resonant, centripetal verbal structures, they may apply pointedly to millions of human situations which have nothing to do with metaphysical optimism. Wordsworth’s pantheism, Dante’s Thomism, Lucretius’ Epicureanism, all have to be read in the same way, as do Gibbon or Macaulay or Hume when they are read for style instead of subject-matter.

形式批评始于对诗歌意象的考察，旨在揭示其独特的模式。反复出现或出现频率最高的意象构成了诗歌的基调，而那些起到调节作用、穿插出现或孤立的意象则以一种层级结构与基调相关联，这种层级结构在批评上类似于诗歌本身的比例。每首诗都有其独特的意象光谱，这源于其体裁的要求、作者的偏好以及无数其他因素。例如，在《麦克白》中，鲜血和失眠的意象具有主题上的重要性，这对于一部关于谋杀和悔恨的悲剧而言自然是理所当然的。因此，在“将绿色的变成红色”这句诗中，两种颜色具有不同的主题强度。绿色是偶然出现的，用于对比；红色更接近整部剧的调性，更像是音乐中主音和弦的重复。马维尔的《花园》中红绿对比的情况则恰恰相反。

Formal criticism begins with an examination of the imagery of a poem, with a view to bringing out its distinctive pattern. The recurring or most frequently repeated images form the tonality, so to speak, and the modulating, episodic and isolated images relate themselves to this in a hierarchic structure which is the critical analogy to the proportions of the poem itself. Every poem has its peculiar spectroscopic band of imagery, caused by the requirements of its genre, the predilections of its author, and countless other factors. In Macbeth, for instance, the images of blood and of sleeplessness have a thematic importance, as is very natural for a tragedy of murder and remorse. Hence in the line “Making the green one red,” the colors are of different thematic intensities. Green is used incidentally and for contrast; red, being closer to the key of the play as a whole, is more like the repetition of a tonic chord in music. The opposite would be true of the contrast between red and green in Marvell’s The Garden.

无论从叙事角度还是意义角度研究，诗歌的形式都是相同的，因此， 《麦克白》中的意象结构既可以作为文本中衍生出的模式进行研究，也可以作为听众耳中反复出现的节奏进行研究。有一种模糊的观点认为，后一种方法能得出更简单的结果，因此可以作为一种常识性的修正，来弥补文本研究中那些令人费解的细微之处。音乐的类比或许会有所帮助。交响乐的普通听众对奏鸣曲式知之甚少，几乎错过了乐谱分析所揭示的所有微妙之处；然而，这些微妙之处确实存在，而且由于听众能够听到演奏的每一个音符，因此它们能够被音乐所触动。这一切都构成线性体验的一部分；意识层面有所减弱，但真实性却丝毫不减。对高度浓缩的诗意戏剧的意象的反应也是如此。

The form of the poem is the same whether it is studied as narrative or as meaning, hence the structure of imagery in Macbeth may be studied as a pattern derived from the text, or as a rhythm of repetition falling on an audience’s ear. There is a vague notion that the latter method produces a simpler result, and may therefore be used as a commonsense corrective to the niggling subtleties of textual study. The analogy of music again may be helpful. The average audience at a symphony knows very little about sonata form, and misses practically all the subtleties detected by an analysis of the score; yet those subtleties are really there, and as the audience can hear everything that is being played, it gets them all as part of a linear experience; the awareness is less conscious, but not less real. The same is true of the response to the imagery of a highly concentrated poetic drama.

当然，对反复出现的意象进行分析也是修辞批评或“新”批评的主要技巧之一：区别在于，形式批评在将意象与诗歌的核心形式联系起来之后，会将形式的某个方面转化为论述性写作的命题。换言之，形式批评是一种评注，而评注则是将诗歌中隐含的内容转化为明确或论述性语言的过程。好的评注自然不会将观念强加于诗歌之上；它解读并转化诗歌中已有的内容，而其存在的证据则来自对意象结构的研究，而这正是评注的起点。这种谨慎的态度，即避免将某个解读点“推向极端”，源于这样一个事实：批评中强调的重点比例通常应与诗歌中强调的重点比例大致相符。

The analysis of recurrent imagery is, of course, one of the chief techniques of rhetorical or “new” criticism as well: the difference is that formal criticism, after attaching the imagery to the central form of the poem, renders an aspect of the form into the propositions of discursive writing. Formal criticism, in other words, is commentary, and commentary is the process of translating into explicit or discursive language what is implicit in the poem. Good commentary naturally does not read ideas into the poem; it reads and translates what is there, and the evidence that it is there is offered by the study of the structure of imagery with which it begins. The sense of tact, of the desirability of not pushing a point of interpretation “too far,” is derived from the fact that the proportioning of emphasis in criticism should normally bear a rough analogy to the proportioning of emphasis in the poem.

在文学实践中，如果未能区分最基本的文学概念——虚构与事实、假设与断言、想象性写作与论述性写作——就会产生批评界所谓的“意图谬误”，即认为诗人的首要意图是向读者传达意义，而批评家的首要职责是重现这一意图。意图一词具有类比性：它暗示着两种事物之间的关系，通常是概念与行为之间的关系。一些相关术语更清晰地展现了这种二元性：“瞄准”某物意味着目标和导弹正在对齐。因此，这类术语理应只属于论述性写作，因为在论述性写作中，语言模式与其描述内容的对应关系至关重要。但诗人的首要任务是创作艺术作品，因此他的意图只能通过某种同义反复来表达。

The failure to make, in practice, the most elementary of all distinctions in literature, the distinction between fiction and fact, hypothesis and assertion, imaginative and discursive writing, produces what in criticism has been called the “intentional fallacy,” the notion that the poet has a primary intention of conveying meaning to a reader, and that the first duty of a critic is to recapture that intention. The word intention is analogical: it implies a relation between two things, usually a conception and an act. Some related terms show this duality even more clearly: to “aim at” something means that a target and a missile are being brought into alignment. Hence such terms properly belong only to discursive writing, where the correspondence of a verbal pattern with what it describes is of primary importance. But a poet’s primary concern is to produce a work of art, and hence his intention can only be expressed by some kind of tautology.

换句话说，诗人的意图是向心的。它指向的是词语的组合，而不是词语与意义的契合。如果我们像格列佛在格鲁布杜布德里布那样有幸召唤莎士比亚的亡灵，询问他某段文字的含义，我们得到的答案只会是令人抓狂的重复：“我把它作为剧本的一部分。”这种向心的意图甚至可以延伸到体裁层面，因为诗人想要创作的不仅仅是一首诗，而是一种……某些类型的诗歌。例如，在解读《祖莱卡·多布森》这首诗，将其视为对牛津生活的描述时，我们最好考虑到其中可能存在的讽刺意味。我们必须假定，作为一条基本的启发式公理，作品的最终呈现形式就是作者意图的最终记录。对于许多经验不足的评论家自以为发现的缺陷，一句“但它本来就应该是这样的”就足以解释一切。所有其他关于意图的陈述，无论多么详尽地记录在案，都值得怀疑。诗人可能会改变主意或心情；他可能原本想写一件事，结果却写了另一件事，然后为自己的行为辩解。 （几年前《纽约客》上的一幅漫画巧妙地引出了最后一个问题：漫画描绘了一位雕塑家凝视着他刚刚完成的雕像，对朋友说：“是啊，这头太大了。等我把它拿出来展览的时候，就叫它‘大头女人’吧。”）如果人们仍然认为诗歌本身就蕴含着作者的意图，那么这首诗就被视为不完整，就像一篇大学新生论文，读者不得不不断地猜测作者的本意。如果作者已经去世几个世纪了，那么这种猜测无论多么令人难以抗拒，都无法让我们深入了解作者的意图。

In other words, a poet’s intention is centripetally directed. It is directed towards putting words together, not towards aligning words with meanings. If we had the privilege of Gulliver in Glubb-dubdrib to call up the ghost of, say, Shakespeare, to ask him what he meant by such and such a passage, we could only get, with maddening iteration, the same answer: “I meant it to form part of the play.” One may pursue the centripetal intention as far as genre, as a poet intends to produce, not simply a poem, but a certain kind of poem. In reading, for instance, Zuleika Dobson as a description of life in Oxford, we should be well advised to allow for ironic intention. One has to assume, as an essential heuristic axiom, that the work as produced constitutes the definitive record of the writer’s intention. For many of the flaws which an inexperienced critic thinks he detects, the answer “But it’s supposed to be that way” is sufficient. All other statements of intention, however fully documented, are suspect. The poet may change his mind or mood; he may have intended one thing and done another, and then rationalized what he did. (A cartoon in a New Yorker of some years back hit off this last problem beautifully: it depicted a sculptor gazing at a statue he had just made and remarking to a friend: “Yes, the head is too large. When I put it in exhibition I shall call it ‘The Woman with the Large Head.’ ”) If intention is still thought to be apparent in the poem itself, the poem is being regarded as incomplete, like a freshman’s essay where the reader has continually to speculate about what the author may have had in his mind. If the author has been dead for centuries, such speculation cannot get us very far, however irresistibly it may suggest itself.

因此，诗人想要表达的，从字面上讲，就是诗歌本身；他在任何一段文字中想要表达的意思，从字面上看，都是诗歌的一部分。但我们已经看到，字面意义是多变的，也是模糊的。读者可能对莎士比亚的回答感到不满：他可能觉得，莎士比亚不像马拉美那样，是一位值得信赖的诗人，而且他希望这段文字本身就能被理解（即具有描述性或可改写的含义）。毫无疑问，他的确是这么想的，但这段文字与整部剧的关系赋予了它无数新的意义。正如一位优秀的画家用寥寥数笔就能勾勒出猫的生动素描，从而囊括了所有观赏者对猫的全部体验一样，我们所熟知的《哈姆雷特》中那精妙绝伦的文字结构，其蕴含的意义之丰富，即使是浩瀚且不断增长的剧评文献也无法穷尽。注释，即把隐含意义转化为显性意义，只能提取出对特定读者在特定时期而言合适或有趣的意义层面，无论大小。这种翻译活动与诗人关系不大。注释与诸如《圣经》或吠陀赞歌之类的圣书之间的关系，就更是如此。这令人震惊，也表明当诗歌结构达到一定程度的精炼或社会认可时，它所能承载的评论将是无穷无尽的。这一事实本身并不比科学家能够提出一条可以用远超其观察或计数范围的现象来佐证的定律更不可思议，也无需像戈德史密斯笔下的乡巴佬那样，疑惑一个诗人的小脑袋瓜里怎么能装下莎士比亚和但丁带给世界的那么多智慧、教诲和意义。

What the poet meant to say, then, is, literally, the poem itself; what he meant to say in any given passage is, in its literal meaning, part of the poem. But literal meaning, we have seen, is variable and ambiguous. The reader may be dissatisfied with the ghost of Shakespeare’s answer: he may feel that Shakespeare, unlike, say, Mallarmé, is a poet he can trust, and that he also meant his passage to be intelligible in itself (i.e., have descriptive or rephrasable meaning). Doubtless he did, but the relationship of the passage to the rest of the play creates myriads of new meanings for it. Just as a vivid sketch of a cat by a good draughtsman may contain in a few crisp lines the entire feline experience of everyone who looks at it, so the powerfully constructed pattern of words that we know as Hamlet may contain an amount of meaning which the vast and constantly growing library of criticism on the play cannot begin to exhaust. Commentary, which translates the implicit into the explicit, can only isolate the aspect of meaning, large or small, which is appropriate or interesting for certain readers to grasp at a certain time. Such translation is an activity with which the poet has very little to do. The relation in bulk between commentary and a sacred book, such as the Bible or the Vedic hymns, is even more striking, and indicates that when a poetic structure attains a certain degree of concentration or social recognition, the amount of commentary it will carry is infinite. This fact is in itself no more incredible than the fact that a scientist can state a law illustrated by more phenomena than he could ever observe or count, and there is no occasion for wondering, like the yokels in Goldsmith, how one small poet’s head can carry the amount of wit, wisdom, instruction, and significance that Shakespeare and Dante have given the world.

艺术中仍然蕴含着真正的神秘，也确实有令人惊叹之处。在《衣裳哲学》（Sartor Resartus）中，卡莱尔区分了外在符号（如十字架或国旗）和内在符号（包括艺术作品）。外在符号本身并无价值，它们只是某种存在意义的标志或指示。基于此，我们可以区分两种神秘。（第三种神秘，即谜题，一个需要解决和消除的问题，属于论述性思维，除了技术层面，与艺术关系不大。）未知或不可知的本质之神秘是一种外在神秘，只有当艺术也被用来阐释其他事物时，它才与艺术相关，例如宗教艺术对于主要关注崇拜的人来说。而内在神秘则是指无论被多么充分地了解，它本身仍然是一个谜，因此它并非与已知事物分离的神秘。《李尔王》或《麦克白》的伟大之处，其神秘之处不在于隐藏，而在于揭示；不在于作品中未知或不可知的事物，而在于作品中无限的事物。

Still there is a genuine mystery in art, and a real place for wonder. In Sartor Resartus Carlyle distinguishes extrinsic symbols, like the cross or the national flag, which are without value in themselves but are signs or indicators of something existential, from intrinsic symbols, which include works of art. On this basis we may distinguish two kinds of mystery. (A third kind, the mystery which is a puzzle, a problem to be solved and annihilated, belongs to discursive thought, and has little to do with the arts, except in matters of technique.) The mystery of the unknown or unknowable essence is an extrinsic mystery, which involves art only when art is also made illustrative of something else, as religious art is to the person concerned primarily with worship. But the intrinsic mystery is that which remains a mystery in itself no matter how fully known it is, and hence is not a mystery separated from what is known. The mystery in the greatness of King Lear or Macbeth comes not from concealment but from revelation, not from something unknown or unknowable in the work, but from something unlimited in it.

当然，可以说诗歌不仅是像论述性写作那样经过深思熟虑和自主意识行为的产物，也是潜意识、前意识、半意识或无意识过程的产物，无论人们偏爱哪种心理学隐喻。写诗需要极大的意志力，但其中一部分意志力必须用于放松意志，从而使写作的大部分成为无意识的。这无疑是事实，诗歌技巧，如同所有技巧一样，是一种习惯性的、因此也越来越无意识的技能。但我认为，从长远来看，文学数据只能在批评的框架内得到解释，我不愿用心理学的陈词滥调来解释文学事实。然而，在谈论艺术时，似乎几乎无法避免使用“创造性”这个词，以及它所暗示的所有生物学类比。而创造，无论是上帝的创造，人，或者说自然，似乎是一种活动，其唯一目的就是消除意图，消除对其他事物的最终依赖或关系，摧毁自身与其概念之间所存在的阴影。

It could be said, of course, that poetry is the product, not only of a deliberate and voluntary act of consciousness, like discursive writing, but of processes which are subconscious or preconscious or half-conscious or unconscious as well, whatever psychological metaphor one prefers. It takes a great deal of will power to write poetry, but part of that will power must be employed in trying to relax the will, so making a large part of one’s writing involuntary. This is no doubt true, and it is also true that poetic technique, like all technique, is a habitual, and therefore an increasingly unconscious, skill. But I feel that literary data are in the long run only explicable within criticism, and I am reluctant to explain literary facts by psychological clichés. Still, it seems now almost impossible to avoid the term “creative,” with all the biological analogies it suggests, when speaking of the arts. And creation, whether of God, man, or nature, seems to be an activity whose only intention is to abolish intention, to eliminate final dependence on or relation to something else, to destroy the shadow that falls between itself and its conception.

人们多么希望文学批评界也能有一位像塞缪尔·巴特勒那样的人物，来阐明艺术作品与有机体之间这种类比所涉及的一些悖论。我们可以客观地描述郁金香在春天盛开、菊花在秋天绽放的过程，但我们却无法从植物内部来描述，除非借助源自人类意识的隐喻，并将之归因于某种主体，例如上帝、自然、环境或生命冲动，或者归因于植物本身。说一朵花“知道”何时该开花，这是一种投射式的隐喻；当然，说“自然知道”只不过是将一种陈旧的母神崇拜引入生物学领域。我完全可以理解，在生物学领域，生物学家会觉得这种目的论的隐喻既不必要又令人困惑，这是一种错置具体性的谬误。批评也同样如此，因为批评必须处理意识或逻辑导向的意志之外的不可知论因素。如果一位评论家说另一位评论家在一位诗人的作品中发现了大量诗人可能完全没有意识到的微妙之处，那么这句话就凸显了生物学上的类比。雪花形成晶体的过程可能完全没有意识，但即便我们不去探究它内部的心理过程，它所做的事情也值得研究。

One wishes that literary criticism had a Samuel Butler to formulate some of the paradoxes involved in this parallel between the work of art and the organism. We can describe objectively what happens when a tulip blooms in spring and a chrysanthemum in autumn, but we cannot describe it from the inside of the plant, except by metaphors derived from human consciousness and ascribed to some agent like God or nature or environment or élan vital, or to the plant itself. It is projected metaphor to say that a flower “knows” when it is time for it to bloom, and of course to say that “nature knows” is merely to import a faded mother-goddess cult into biology. I can well understand that in their own field biologists would find such teleological metaphors both unnecessary and confusing, a fallacy of misplaced concreteness. The same would be true of criticism to the extent that criticism has to deal with imponderables other than consciousness or logically directed will. If one critic says that another has discovered a mass of subtleties in a poet of which that poet was probably quite unconscious, the phrase points up the biological analogy. A snowflake is probably quite unconscious of forming a crystal, but what it does may be worth study even if we are willing to leave its inner mental processes alone.

人们往往没有意识到，所有的评注都是一种寓言式的解读，即将思想与诗歌意象的结构联系起来。任何批评家一旦允许自己对一首诗做出真正的评论（例如，“在《哈姆雷特》中，莎士比亚似乎在描绘优柔寡断的悲剧”），他就已经开始了寓言式的解读。因此，评注将文学视为其形式阶段中事件和思想的潜在寓言。这种评注与诗歌本身的关系，正是浪漫主义时期一些批评家提出的“象征主义”与“寓言”对比的根源所在。这里的象征主义指的是具有主题意义的意象。这种对比体现在两种方法之间：一种是“具体”的象征方法，它从实际事物的意象出发，向外延伸至思想和命题；另一种是“抽象”的方法，它从思想出发，然后试图找到一个具体的意象来代表它。这种区分是完全合理的。寓言本身虽然是一个概念，但它在现代批评中留下了巨大的混乱，这主要是因为“寓言”一词被非常随意地用于指代各种各样的文学现象。

It is not often realized that all commentary is allegorical interpretation, an attaching of ideas to the structure of poetic imagery. The instant that any critic permits himself to make a genuine comment about a poem (e.g., “In Hamlet Shakespeare appears to be portraying the tragedy of irresolution”) he has begun to allegorize. Commentary thus looks at literature as, in its formal phase, a potential allegory of events and ideas. The relation of such commentary to poetry itself is the source of the contrast which was developed by several critics of the Romantic period between “symbolism” and “allegory,” symbolism here being used in the sense of thematically significant imagery. The contrast is between a “concrete” approach to symbols which begins with images of actual things and works outward to ideas and propositions, and an “abstract” approach which begins with the idea and then tries to find a concrete image to represent it. This distinction is valid enough in itself, but it has deposited a large terminal moraine of confusion in modern criticism, largely because the term allegory is very loosely employed for a great variety of literary phenomena.

当诗人明确指出其意象与例证和准则之间的联系，并试图以此引导读者如何解读他的作品时，我们就看到了真正的寓言。当一位作家清晰地表达“我以此也指那”时，他便运用了寓言。如果这种表达方式贯穿始终，我们可以谨慎地说，他所写的内容“就是”一则寓言。例如，在《仙后》中，叙事系统地引用了历史例证及其与道德准则的关联，而这些例证和准则本身也在诗歌中发挥着作用。因此，寓言是一种复调技巧，如同音乐中的经典模仿。但丁、斯宾塞、塔索和班扬的作品通篇都在运用寓言：他们的作品堪称文学中的弥撒曲和清唱剧。阿里奥斯托、歌德、易卜生和霍桑的写作风格自由奔放，寓言可以随意取用和舍弃。但即使是连续寓言，也仍然是图像的结构，而不是伪装的思想的结构，评论必须像评论所有其他文学作品一样进行，试图看看图像整体暗示了哪些准则和例子。

We have actual allegory when a poet explicitly indicates the relationship of his images to examples and precepts, and so tries to indicate how a commentary on him should proceed. A writer is being allegorical whenever it is clear that he is saying “by this I also (allos) mean that.” If this seems to be done continuously, we may say, cautiously, that what he is writing “is” an allegory. In The Faerie Queene, for instance, the narrative systematically refers to historical examples and the meaning to moral precepts, besides doing their own work in the poem. Allegory, then, is a contrapuntal technique, like canonical imitation in music. Dante, Spenser, Tasso, and Bunyan use it throughout: their works are the masses and oratorios of literature. Ariosto, Goethe, Ibsen, Hawthorne write in a freistimmige style in which allegory may be picked up and dropped again at pleasure. But even continuous allegory is still a structure of images, not of disguised ideas, and commentary has to proceed with it exactly as it does with all other literature, trying to see what precepts and examples are suggested by the imagery as a whole.

评论家往往对寓言抱有偏见，却不知其真正原因：连续的寓言设定了评论的方向，从而限制了其自由发挥。因此，他常常敦促我们阅读斯宾塞和班扬的作品时只关注故事本身，而忽略寓言，言下之意是他认为自己类型的评论更有意思。或者，他会构建一个将自己喜爱的诗歌排除在外的寓言定义。这样的评论家往往倾向于将所有寓言都视为朴素的寓言，或者仅仅是将思想转化为图像。

The commenting critic is often prejudiced against allegory without knowing the real reason, which is that continuous allegory prescribes the direction of his commentary, and so restricts its freedom. Hence he often urges us to read Spenser and Bunyan, for example, for the story alone and let the allegory go, meaning by that that he regards his own type of commentary as more interesting. Or else he will frame a definition of allegory that will exclude the poems he likes. Such a critic is often apt to treat all allegory as though it were naive allegory, or the translation of ideas into images.

朴素寓言是一种伪装的论述性写作形式，主要见于小学教育文学：例如课堂道德教诲、宗教典范、地方庆典等等。它的基础是教育和仪式所培养的习惯性或习俗性观念，其通常形式是短暂的奇观。在特定场合的激动下，熟悉的观念突然转化为感官体验，并随着场合的结束而消失。以健全的政府和鼓励贸易来战胜叛乱和纷争，将是正确的做法。一场旨在款待来访君主半小时的盛大庆典的主题，与“大众传媒”和“视听辅助工具”在当代教育中扮演的寓言角色类似。由于这种基于奇观的本质，朴素寓言的重心在于绘画艺术，并且当它被视为一种偶发性的幽默形式时，例如政治漫画，便能取得最大的艺术成功。而官方壁画和雕塑中那些更为庄严和持久的朴素寓言，则明显带有过时的倾向。

Naive allegory is a disguised form of discursive writing, and belongs chiefly to educational literature on an elementary level: schoolroom moralities, devotional exempla, local pageants, and the like. Its basis is the habitual or customary ideas fostered by education and ritual, and its normal form is that of transient spectacle. Under the excitement of a particular occasion familiar ideas suddenly become sense experiences, and vanish with the occasion. The defeat of Sedition and Discord by Sound Government and Encouragement of Trade would be the right sort of theme for a pageant designed only to entertain a visiting monarch for half an hour. The apparatus of “mass media” and “audiovisual aids” plays a similar allegorical role in contemporary education. Because of this basis in spectacle, naive allegory has its center of gravity in the pictorial arts, and is most successful as art when recognized to be a form of occasional wit, as it is in the political cartoon. The more solemn and permanent naive allegories of official murals and statuary show a marked tendency to date.

因此，在评论的一个极端，存在着一种天真的寓言，它急于表达自身的寓言观点，却缺乏真正的文学或假设中心。我所说的天真的寓言“过时”，是指任何拒绝进行意象分析的寓言——也就是说，任何仅仅是插入一两个例证的论述性文字——与其说是文学作品，不如说是思想史上的一份文献。例如，《以斯拉二书》的作者引入了鹰的寓言意象，然后说道：“看哪，右边长出了一根羽毛，它统治着整个大地。”显然，他对鹰作为诗意意象的兴趣不足以让他恪守文学表达的常规界限。诗歌表达的基础是隐喻，而天真的寓言的基础是混合隐喻。

At one extreme of commentary, then, there is the naive allegory so anxious to make its own allegorical points that it has no real literary or hypothetical center. When I say that naive allegory “dates,” I mean that any allegory which resists a primary analysis of imagery—that is, an allegory which is simply discursive writing with an illustrative image or two stuck into it—will have to be treated less as literature than as a document in the history of ideas. When the author of II Esdras, for instance, introduces an allegorical vision of an eagle, and then says, “Behold, on the right side there arose one feather, which reigned over all the earth,” it is clear that he is not sufficiently interested in his eagle as a poetic image to remain within the normal boundaries of literary expression. The basis of poetic expression is the metaphor, and the basis of naive allegory is the mixed metaphor.

在文学的范畴内，我们发现了一种滑动的标尺，从一端最直白的寓言式作品（完全符合文学的定义）到另一端最隐晦、反寓言式的作品。首先是连续寓言，例如《天路历程》和《仙后》，然后是前面提到的自由式寓言。接下来是具有强烈教条意义的诗歌结构，其内部虚构情节是范例，例如弥尔顿的史诗。然后，在正中间，我们看到的是一些作品，它们的意象结构虽然富有启发性，但仅与事件和思想存在隐性关联，莎士比亚的大部分作品就属于此类。再往下，诗歌意象开始脱离范例和教条，变得越来越具有讽刺和悖论性。现代批评家在这里感到更加自在，因为这种类型更符合现代对艺术的字面理解，即诗歌应从明确的陈述中抽离出来。

Within the boundaries of literature we find a kind of sliding scale, ranging from the most explicitly allegorical, consistent with being literature at all, at one extreme, to the most elusive, antiexplicit and anti-allegorical at the other. First we meet the continuous allegories, like The Pilgrim’s Progress and The Faerie Queene, and then the free-style allegories just mentioned. Next come the poetic structures with a large and insistent doctrinal interest, in which the internal fictions are exempla, like the epics of Milton. Then we have, in the exact center, works in which the structure of imagery, however suggestive, has an implicit relation only to events and ideas, and which includes the bulk of Shakespeare. Below this, poetic imagery begins to recede from example and precept and become increasingly ironic and paradoxical. Here the modern critic begins to feel more at home, the reason being that this type is more consistent with the modern literal view of art, the sense of the poem as withdrawn from explicit statement.

这种反讽和反寓言意象有好几种，我们都很熟悉。其中一种是形而上学学派的典型符号。巴洛克时期，“奇想”或刻意强行将通常毫不相干的事物联系起来。玄学诗的悖论技巧基于这样一种观念：艺术与自然的内在关系瓦解为外在关系。另一种技巧是象征主义的替代意象，它是一种暗示或唤起事物，避免直接命名的技巧。还有一种意象，正如艾略特先生所描述的，是客观对应物，它在诗歌中建立起情感的内在焦点，同时又替代了某种观念。还有一种意象与客观对应物密切相关，甚至可能相同，那就是纹章符号，它是我们在现代文学中想到“象征”一词时最先想到的核心象征意象。例如，我们会想到霍桑的红字、梅尔维尔的白鲸、詹姆斯的金碗，或是弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的灯塔。这种意象与形式寓言的意象不同，因为艺术与自然之间并不存在连续的联系。例如，与斯宾塞的寓言符号不同，纹章象征意象与叙事和意义之间都存在着一种悖论式的、反讽式的关系。作为意义的单元，它阻碍了叙事；作为叙事的单元，它又使意义变得复杂。它融合了卡莱尔所说的具有内在意义的符号和指向其他事物的外在符号的特质。这种象征手法基于一种强烈的对立感，即符号的字面意义和描述意义之间存在着一种潜在的对抗，正是这种对抗使得马拉美和左拉在十九世纪文学中形成了如此鲜明的对比。

Several types of this ironic and anti-allegorical imagery are familiar. One is the typical symbol of the metaphysical school of the Baroque period, the “conceit” or deliberately strained union of normally disparate things. The paradoxical techniques of metaphysical poetry are based on a sense of the breakdown of the internal relation of art and nature into an external one. Another is the substitute-image of symbolisme, part of a technique for suggesting or evoking things and avoiding the explicit naming of them. Still another is the kind of image described by Mr. Eliot as an objective correlative, the image that sets up an inward focus of emotion in poetry and at the same time substitutes itself for an idea. Still another, closely related to if not identical with the objective correlative, is the heraldic symbol, the central emblematic image which comes most readily to mind when we think of the word “symbol” in modem literature. We think, for example, of Hawthorne’s scarlet letter, Melville’s white whale, James’s golden bowl, or Virginia Woolf’s lighthouse. Such an image differs from the image of the formal allegory in that there is no continuous relationship between art and nature. In contrast to the allegorical symbols of Spenser, for instance, the heraldic emblematic image is in a paradoxical and ironic relation to both narrative and meaning. As a unit of meaning, it arrests the narrative; as a unit of narrative, it perplexes the meaning. It combines the qualities of Carlyle’s intrinsic symbol with significance in itself, and the extrinsic symbol which points quizzically to something else. It is a technique of symbolism which is based on a strong sense of a lurking antagonism between the literal and the descriptive aspects of symbols, the same antagonism that made Mallarmé and Zola so extreme a contrast in nineteenth-century literature.

在此之下，我们会遇到更多间接的技巧，例如私人联想、意在不被完全理解的象征主义、对达达主义的刻意戏仿，以及其他预示着文学表达边界即将到来之势的类似迹象。我们应该努力将所有这些可能的解读方式牢记于心，以便纠正中世纪和文艺复兴时期批评家的观点——他们认为所有重要的诗歌都应尽可能地被视为连续的寓言——以及现代批评家的观点——他们认为诗歌本质上是反寓言和悖论式的。

Below this we run into still more indirect techniques, such as private association, symbolism intended not to be fully understood, the deliberate spoofing of Dadaism, and kindred signs of another approaching boundary of literary expression. We should try to keep this whole range of possible commentary clearly in mind, so as to correct the perspective both of the medieval and Renaissance critics who assumed that all major poetry should be treated as far as possible as continuous allegory, and of the modern ones who maintain that poetry is essentially anti-allegorical and paradoxical.

我们现在所持有的是一种将文学视为假想创作的观念，这种观念既不一定涉及真理和事实的世界，也不一定脱离它们。但它可以与它们建立任何形式的关系，从最明确到最隐晦的都有。这让我们强烈地联想到数学与自然科学的关系。数学和文学一样，都是通过假设和内在一致性来发展的，而不是通过描述和对自然的外部忠实。当它被应用于外部事实时，验证的不是它的真理，而是它的适用性。既然我似乎在这篇文章中选择了猫作为我的语义象征，我注意到，叶芝和斯特奇·摩尔关于罗斯金的猫的问题的讨论，尖锐地体现了这一点。罗斯金把那只猫抱起来扔出了窗外，尽管它并不在那里。任何试图用外部现实来衡量自己思想的人，都必须诉诸于信仰的公理。经验事实和幻觉之间的区别并非理性之分，也无法通过逻辑证明。它仅仅因为在实践和情感上需要假定这种区别而被“证明”。对于诗人而言，作为诗人，这种必要性并不存在，也没有任何诗意的理由让他去肯定或否定任何猫的存在，无论是真实的还是罗斯金笔下的。

What we have now is a conception of literature as a body of hypothetical creations which is not necessarily involved in the worlds of truth and fact, nor necessarily withdrawn from them, but which may enter into any kind of relationship to them, ranging from the most to the least explicit. We are strongly reminded of the relationship of mathematics to the natural sciences. Mathematics, like literature, proceeds hypothetically and by internal consistency, not descriptively and by outward fidelity to nature. When it is applied to external facts, it is not its truth but its applicability that is being verified. As I seem to have fastened on the cat for my semantic emblem in this essay, I note that this point comes out sharply in the discussion between Yeats and Sturge Moore over the problem of Ruskin’s cat, the animal that was picked up and flung out of a window by Ruskin although it was not there. Anyone measuring his mind against an external reality has to fall back on an axiom of faith. The distinction between an empirical fact and an illusion is not a rational distinction, and cannot be logically proved. It is “proved” only by the practical and emotional necessity of assuming the distinction. For the poet, qua poet, this necessity does not exist, and there is no poetic reason why he should either assert or deny the existence of any cat, real or Ruskinian.

艺术与现实的关系既非直接也非消极，而是潜在的，这种观念最终解决了愉悦与教诲、风格与信息之间的二元对立。“愉悦”与快乐难以区分，因此，它为我们在引言中略微提及的审美享乐主义——即未能区分价值判断中的个人层面和非个人层面——打开了方便之门。传统的净化理论认为，对艺术的情感反应并非唤起某种实际的情感，而是将实际的情感提升并释放到某种其他事物的浪潮之中。我们或许可以将这种其他事物称为振奋或热情：一种从经验中解放出来的景象，一种读者因经验转化为模仿、生活转化为艺术、日常转化为游戏而产生的反应。在博雅教育的核心，某种东西理应得到解放。创造的隐喻引出了诞生的平行意象，即新生有机体进入独立生活的过程。创作的狂喜及其带来的回应，在创作努力的一个层面上，如同母鸡的咯咯声；在另一个层面上，则产生了意大利评论家称之为“ sprezzatura ”的特质，霍比在翻译卡斯蒂廖内的作品时称之为“鲁莽”，一种轻盈或释放的感觉。伴随完美自律而来的是，当我们再也无法将舞者和舞蹈区分开来时。

The conception of art as having a relation to reality which is neither direct nor negative, but potential, finally resolves the dichotomy between delight and instruction, the style and the message. “Delight” is not readily distinguishable from pleasure, and hence opens the way to that aesthetic hedonism we glanced at in the introduction, the failure to distinguish personal and impersonal aspects of valuation. The traditional theory of catharsis implies that the emotional response to art is not the raising of an actual emotion, but the raising and casting out of actual emotion on a wave of something else. We may call this something else, perhaps, exhilaration or exuberance: the vision of something liberated from experience, the response kindled in the reader by the transmutation of experience into mimesis, of life into art, of routine into play. At the center of liberal education something surely ought to get liberated. The metaphor of creation suggests the parallel image of birth, the emergence of a new-born organism into independent life. The ecstasy of creation and its response produce, on one level of creative effort, the hen’s cackle; on another, the quality that the Italian critics called sprezzatura and that Hoby’s translation of Castiglione calls “recklessness,” the sense of buoyancy or release that accompanies perfect discipline, when we can no longer know the dancer from the dance.

我们很难理解弥尔顿所谓的“华丽悲剧”为何会引发真实的忧郁或悲伤之情。埃斯库罗斯的《波斯人》和莎士比亚的《麦克白》固然是悲剧，但它们分别与萨拉米斯海战的胜利和詹姆斯一世的登基相关，而这两件事都是举国欢庆的盛事。一些评论家将这种关于真实情感的理论延伸到莎士比亚本人身上，并谈到他所谓的“悲剧时期”，认为他在1600年至1608年间情绪低落。大多数人如果刚刚写出一部像《李尔王》一样优秀的剧作，都会感到无比兴奋。虽然我们无权将这种情绪归于莎士比亚，但这无疑是描述我们对这部剧作感受的恰当方式。另一方面，令人震惊的是，格洛斯特被弄瞎这件事主要是一种娱乐，尤其令人震惊的是，我们从中获得的快感显然与虐待狂无关。如果任何文学作品在情感上令人“沮丧”，那么要么是作品本身有问题，要么是读者的反应有问题。艺术似乎能产生一种轻盈感，这种轻盈感虽然常被称作快乐（例如华兹华斯就这么称呼它），但它的含义远比快乐更广泛。“热情奔放即是美，”布莱克如是说。在我看来，这不仅为“美是什么”这个次要问题提供了一个近乎完美的答案，也为“净化”和“狂喜”这两个概念的真正含义这个更为重要的问题提供了答案。

It is impossible to understand the effect of what Milton called “gorgeous Tragedy” as producing a real emotion of gloom or sorrow. Aeschylus’s The Persians and Shakespeare’s Macbeth are certainly tragedies, but they are associated respectively with the victory of Salamis and the accession of James I, both occasions of national rejoicing. Some critics carry the theory of real emotion over into Shakespeare himself, and talk about a “tragic period,” in which he is supposed to have felt dismal from 1600 to 1608. Most people, if they had just finished writing a play as good as King Lear, would be in a mood of exhilaration, and while we have no right to ascribe this mood to Shakespeare, it is surely the right way to describe our response to the play. On the other hand, it comes as something of a shock to realize that the blinding of Gloucester is primarily entertainment, the more so as the pleasure we get from it obviously has nothing to do with sadism. If any literary work is emotionally “depressing,” there is something wrong with either the writing or the reader’s response. Art seems to produce a kind of buoyancy which, though often called pleasure, as it is for instance by Wordsworth, is something more inclusive than pleasure. “Exuberance is beauty,” said Blake. That seems to me a practically definitive solution, not only of the minor question of what beauty is, but of the far more important problem of what the conceptions of catharsis and ecstasis really mean.

这种热情当然既源于理智也源于情感：布莱克本人就曾将诗歌定义为“献给理智力量的寓言”。我们生活在一个受到三重外在强制的世界：行动或法律的强制；思考或事实的强制；以及情感的强制——无论这种快乐是来自《天堂篇》还是冰淇淋汽水，它都具有这种强制的特征。但在想象的世界里，存在着第四种力量，它包含道德、美和真理，却从不屈从于它们，它摆脱了所有这些强制的束缚。想象力的创造为我们展现的，并非诗人个人的伟大，而是某种非个人化且更为伟大的事物：一种决定性的精神自由行动的景象，一种人类自我重塑的景象。

Such exuberance is, of course, as much intellectual as it is emotional: Blake himself was willing to define poetry as “allegory addressed to the intellectual powers.” We live in a world of threefold external compulsion: of compulsion on action, or law; of compulsion on thinking, or fact; of compulsion on feeling, which is the characteristic of all pleasure whether it is produced by the Paradiso or by an ice cream soda. But in the world of imagination a fourth power, which contains morality, beauty, and truth but is never subordinated to them, rises free of all their compulsions. The work of imagination presents us with a vision, not of the personal greatness of the poet, but of something impersonal and far greater: the vision of a decisive act of spiritual freedom, the vision of the recreation of man.

神话阶段：符号作为原型

MYTHICAL PHASE: SYMBOL AS ARCHETYPE

在形式阶段，诗歌既不属于“艺术”范畴，也不属于“语言”范畴：它自成一类。因此，它的形式包含两个方面。首先，它是独一无二的，是一种技艺或人工制品，拥有其独特的意象结构，需要单独考察，无需直接参照其他类似事物。批评家在此从诗歌本身出发，而非从对诗歌的先入为主的观念或定义出发。其次，诗歌属于一类相似的形式。亚里士多德知道《俄狄浦斯王》在某种意义上不同于其他任何悲剧，但他同时也知道它属于悲剧这一范畴。我们这些接触过莎士比亚和拉辛作品的人可以进一步推断，悲剧远不止是希腊戏剧的一个阶段。我们甚至可以在非戏剧的文学作品中找到悲剧的影子。因此，要理解悲剧的本质，就必须超越单纯的历史层面，探究文学整体的本质。有了这首诗与其他诗歌的外部关系这一概念，批评中的两个考虑因素第一次变得重要起来：惯例和体裁。

In the formal phase the poem belongs neither to the class “art,” nor to the class “verbal”: it represents its own class. There are thus two aspects to its form. In the first place, it is unique, a techne or artifact, with its own peculiar structure of imagery, to be examined by itself without immediate reference to other things like it. The critic here begins with poems, not with a prior conception or definition of poetry. In the second place, the poem is one of a class of similar forms. Aristotle knows that Oedipus Tyrannus is in one sense not like any other tragedy, but he also knows that it belongs to the class called tragedy. We, who have experienced Shakespeare and Racine, can add the corollary that tragedy is something bigger than a phase of Greek drama. We may also find tragedy in literary works which are not dramas. To understand what tragedy is, therefore, takes us beyond the merely historical into the question of what an aspect of literature as a whole is. With this idea of the external relations of a poem with other poems, two considerations in criticism for the first time become important: convention and genre.

对体裁的研究基于形式上的类比。文献批评和历史批评的特点在于它们无法处理此类类比。它们可以颇具说服力地追溯影响，无论这种影响是否存在；但面对莎士比亚的悲剧和索福克勒斯的悲剧，仅仅因为它们都是悲剧而进行比较，历史批评家就只能局限于对人生严肃性的一般性思考。同样，修辞批评中最引人注目的莫过于对体裁的漠视：修辞批评家分析作品时，很少关注它是戏剧、抒情诗还是小说。他甚至可能断言文学中不存在体裁。这是因为他关注的是作品作为艺术作品的结构，而不是具有潜在功能的器物。但是，文学中有很多类比，完全不考虑来源和影响（当然，其中很多来源和影响根本不相似），注意到这些类比构成了我们对文学的实际体验的很大一部分，无论它在批评中迄今为止扮演了什么角色。

The study of genres is based on analogies in form. It is characteristic of documentary and historical criticism that it cannot deal with such analogies. It can trace influence with great plausibility, whether it exists or not, but confronted with a tragedy of Shakespeare and a tragedy of Sophocles, to be compared solely because they are both tragedies, the historical critic has to confine himself to general reflections about the seriousness of life. Similarly, nothing is more striking in rhetorical criticism than the absence of any consideration of genre: the rhetorical critic analyzes what is in front of him without much regard to whether it is a play, a lyric, or a novel. He may in fact even assert that there are no genres in literature. That is because he is concerned with his structure simply as a work of art, not as an artifact with a possible function. But there are many analogies in literature apart altogether from sources and influences (many of which, of course, are not analogous at all) and noticing such analogies forms a large part of our actual experience of literature, whatever its role so far in criticism.

形式阶段的核心原则——诗歌是对自然的模仿——虽然完全正确，但它仍然将单首诗歌孤立出来。显然，任何一首诗都可以被考察，不仅可以将其视为对自然的模仿，还可以将其视为……对其他诗歌的模仿。据蒲柏所言，维吉尔发现，追随自然最终等同于追随荷马。一旦我们将一首诗与其他诗歌联系起来，视为一个诗歌单元，我们便会明白，对诗歌体裁的研究必须建立在对诗歌惯例的研究之上。能够处理此类问题的批评必须以诗歌彼此关联的象征意义为基础，并将连接诗歌的符号作为其主要研究领域。其最终目标并非仅仅将诗歌视为对自然的模仿，而是将自然整体的秩序视为相应的文字秩序所模仿的对象。

The central principle of the formal phase, that a poem is an imitation of nature, is, though a perfectly sound one, still a principle which isolates the individual poem. And it is clear that any poem may be examined, not only as an imitation of nature, but as an imitation of other poems. Virgil discovered, according to Pope, that following nature was ultimately the same thing as following Homer. Once we think of a poem in relation to other poems, as a unit of poetry, we can see that the study of genres has to be founded on the study of convention. The criticism which can deal with such matters will have to be based on that aspect of symbolism which relates poems to one another, and it will choose, as its main field of operations, the symbols that link poems together. Its ultimate object is to consider, not simply a poem as an imitation of nature, but the order of nature as a whole as imitated by a corresponding order of words.

所有艺术都同样具有约定俗成的特质，但除非我们不习惯这种约定俗成，否则我们通常不会注意到这一点。在当今时代，文学中的约定俗成元素被版权法精心掩盖，该法假装每一件艺术作品都是足以获得专利的独特发明。因此，现代文学的约定俗成力量——例如，编辑的政策和读者的期望如何共同促成杂志内容的约定俗成——常常被忽视。如果A已去世，证明A对B的借鉴仅仅是学术研究；但如果A仍然在世，这却成了道德败坏的证据。这种现状使得我们难以评价包括乔叟在内的文学作品，乔叟的诗歌大多翻译或改写自他人；莎士比亚的戏剧有时几乎逐字逐句地照搬原作；以及弥尔顿，他从《圣经》中汲取了尽可能多的素材。并非只有缺乏经验的读者才会在这些作品中寻找残存的原创性。我们大多数人倾向于认为诗人真正的成就与他借鉴的成就截然不同，甚至截然相反，因此我们往往关注的是次要的而非核心的批评事实。例如，《复乐园》这首诗的核心伟大之处并非在于弥尔顿在其原作基础上添加的华丽辞藻，而在于其主题本身的伟大，弥尔顿正是将这一主题从原作传递给了读者。这种伟大诗人肩负伟大主题的理念对弥尔顿而言或许足够基础，但却违背了我们大多数人从小接受的关于创作的低级模仿偏见。

All art is equally conventionalized, but we do not ordinarily notice this fact unless we are unaccustomed to the convention. In our day the conventional element in literature is elaborately disguised by a law of copyright pretending that every work of art is an invention distinctive enough to be patented. Hence the conventionalizing forces of modern literature—the way, for instance, that an editor’s policy and the expectation of his readers combine to conventionalize what appears in a magazine—often go unrecognized. Demonstrating the debt of A to B is merely scholarship if A is dead, but a proof of moral delinquency if A is alive. This state of things makes it difficult to appraise a literature which includes Chaucer, much of whose poetry is translated or paraphrased from others; Shakespeare, whose plays sometimes follow their sources almost verbatim; and Milton, who asked for nothing better than to steal as much as possible out of the Bible. It is not only the inexperienced reader who looks for a residual originality in such works. Most of us tend to think of a poet’s real achievement as distinct from, or even contrasted with, the achievement present in what he stole, and we are thus apt to concentrate on peripheral rather than on central critical facts. For instance, the central greatness of Paradise Regained, as a poem, is not the greatness of the rhetorical decorations that Milton added to his source, but the greatness of the theme itself, which Milton passes on to the reader from his source. This conception of the great poet’s being entrusted with the great theme was elementary enough to Milton, but violates most of the low mimetic prejudices about creation that most of us are educated in.

对传统的轻视似乎是浪漫主义时期以来这种趋势的结果，甚至可能是其一部分。一种观点认为，个体理想地先于其社会而存在。与之相反的观点则认为，新生儿受到遗传和环境因素的影响，与一个既有的社会存在关联。无论从中可以推导出何种理论，这种观点的首要优势在于它更贴近其所探讨的事实。第二种观点的文学意义在于，新诗如同新生儿一样，诞生于一个既有的语言秩序之中，并体现了它所依附的诗歌结构。新生儿是其自身社会的体现，再次以个体性单元的形式出现；新诗与其诗歌社会之间也存在着类似的关联。

The underestimating of convention appears to be a result of, may even be a part of, the tendency, marked from Romantic times on, to think of the individual as ideally prior to his society. The view opposed to this, that the new baby is conditioned by a hereditary and environmental kinship to a society which already exists, has, whatever doctrines may be inferred from it, the initial advantage of being closer to the facts it deals with. The literary consequence of the second view is that the new poem, like the new baby, is born into an already existing order of words, and is typical of the structure of poetry to which it is attached. The new baby is his own society appearing once again as a unit of individuality, and the new poem has a similar relation to its poetic society.

很难接受那种将“原作”与“原始”混淆的批判观点，这种观点认为一位“富有创造力”的诗人只需拿起铅笔和一张白纸，就能在一种特殊的“无中生有”的创作行为中，最终写出一首新诗。人类的创作并非如此。正如一项新的科学发现揭示了自然秩序中早已存在的某种潜藏之物，同时又与现有科学的整体结构存在逻辑关联一样，一首新诗也揭示了文字秩序中早已存在的某种潜藏之物。文学可以包含生活、现实、经验、自然、想象的真理、社会状况，或者任何你认为合适的内容；但文学本身并非由这些构成。诗歌只能由其他诗歌构成；小说只能由其他小说构成。文学自我塑造，而非受外部塑造：文学形式不可能脱离文学而存在，正如奏鸣曲、赋格曲和回旋曲的形式不可能脱离音乐而存在一样。

It is hardly possible to accept a critical view which confuses the original with the aboriginal, and imagines that a “creative” poet sits down with a pencil and some blank paper and eventually produces a new poem in a special act of creation ex nihilo. Human beings do not create in that way. Just as a new scientific discovery manifests something that was already latent in the order of nature, and at the same time is logically related to the total structure of the existing science, so the new poem manifests something that was already latent in the order of words. Literature may have life, reality, experience, nature, imaginative truth, social conditions, or what you will for its content; but literature itself is not made out of these things. Poetry can only be made out of other poems; novels out of other novels. Literature shapes itself, and is not shaped externally: the forms of literature can no more exist outside literature than the forms of sonata and fugue and rondo can exist outside music.

在文学被私人企业同化、掩盖了诸多批评事实之前，这一切都清晰得多。当弥尔顿坐下来写一首关于爱德华·金的诗时，他问自己的不是：“我能写些什么关于金的事？”，而是“诗歌要求如何处理这样一个主题？”认为墨守成规表明缺乏情感，而诗人通过无视传统就能获得“真诚”（通常意味着清晰表达情感）的观点，与所有文学经验和历史事实都背道而驰。这种观点的根源在于，诗歌是对情感的描述，其“字面”意义是对诗人个人情感的断言。但任何严肃的文学研究都会很快表明，原创诗人与模仿诗人之间的真正区别仅仅在于前者模仿得更为深刻。原创性回归到……文学的起源，正如激进主义回归其根源。艾略特先生关于优秀诗人更倾向于借鉴而非模仿的论断，为我们提供了一种更为平衡的视角来看待传统，因为它表明诗歌是与其他诗歌具体关联的，而非模糊地与传统或风格等抽象概念相关。版权法及其相关的道德规范使得现代小说家几乎不可能从其他文学作品中窃取除标题以外的任何内容：因此，我们往往只有在《丧钟为谁而鸣》、《愤怒的葡萄》或《喧哗与骚动》这样的标题中，才能清晰地看到作者如何通过传统的共产主义获得多少非个人化的尊严和丰富的联想。

All this was much clearer before the assimilation of literature to private enterprise concealed so many of the facts of criticism. When Milton sat down to write a poem about Edward King, he did not ask himself: “What can I find to say about King?” but “How does poetry require that such a subject should be treated?” The notion that convention shows a lack of feeling, and that a poet attains “sincerity” (which usually means articulate emotion) by disregarding it, is opposed to all the facts of literary experience and history. The origin of this notion is, again, the view that poetry is a description of emotion, and that its “literal” meaning is an assertion about the emotions held by the individual poet. But any serious study of literature soon shows that the real difference between the original and the imitative poet is simply that the former is more profoundly imitative. Originality returns to the origins of literature, as radicalism returns to its roots. The remark of Mr. Eliot that a good poet is more likely to steal than to imitate affords a more balanced view of convention, as it indicates that the poem is specifically involved with other poems, not vaguely with such abstractions as tradition or style. The copyright law, and the mores attached to it, make it difficult for a modern novelist to steal anything except his title from the rest of literature: hence it is often only in such titles as For Whom the Bell Tolls, The Grapes of Wrath, or The Sound and the Fury, that we can clearly see how much impersonal dignity and richness of association an author can gain by the communism of convention.

如同其他神圣活动的产物一样，诗歌的“父亲”远比“母亲”更难辨认。任何严肃的批评都无法否认，诗歌的母亲永远是自然，是客观存在的领域，也是交流的场域。然而，只要我们假定诗歌的父亲就是诗人本人，我们就再次未能将文学与话语结构区分开来。话语作家写作是一种有意识的意志行为，而这种有意识的意志，连同他所使用的符号系统，都与他所描述的事物本身相对立。但诗人，他的写作是创造性的而非刻意的，他并非诗歌的父亲；他充其量是一位助产士，或者更准确地说，是自然母亲的子宫：可以说，他是自然母亲的私处。诗歌可以修改，诗人可以修改诗歌并非因为他更喜欢修改后的版本，而是因为修改后的版本更好，这一事实清楚地表明，诗人必须在诗歌于其脑海中酝酿的过程中孕育它。他有责任尽可能完好无损地交付它，如果这首诗是有生命的，它也同样渴望摆脱他，并呐喊着要从他自我的所有束缚和喂养管中挣脱出来。

As with other products of divine activity, the father of a poem is much more difficult to identify than the mother. That the mother is always nature, the realm of the objective considered as a field of communication, no serious criticism can ever deny. But as long as the father of a poem is assumed to be the poet himself, we have once again failed to distinguish literature from discursive verbal structures. The discursive writer writes as an act of conscious will, and that conscious will, along with the symbolic system he employs for it, is set over against the body of things he is describing. But the poet, who writes creatively rather than deliberately, is not the father of his poem; he is at best a midwife, or, more accurately still, the womb of Mother Nature herself: her privates he, so to speak. The fact that revision is possible, that a poet can make changes in a poem not because he likes them better but because they are better, shows clearly that the poet has to give birth to the poem as it passes through his mind. He is responsible for delivering it in as uninjured a state as possible, and if the poem is alive, it is equally anxious to be rid of him, and screams to be cut loose from all the navel-strings and feeding-tubes of his ego.

诗歌真正的父性或塑造精神在于诗歌的形式本身，而这种形式正是诗歌普世精神的体现。莎士比亚十四行诗的“唯一创造者”并非莎士比亚本人，更非那令人沮丧的幽灵——威廉·惠特克先生，而是莎士比亚的创作主题，他激情的主宰。当诗人谈及塑造诗歌的内在精神时，他往往会摒弃对缪斯女神的传统诉求，转而将自​​己视为与某位神祇或主宰——无论是阿波罗、狄俄尼索斯、厄洛斯、基督，还是（如弥尔顿笔下的）圣灵——存在着一种女性化的，或者至少是接纳性的关系。正如奥维德所说：“神在我们之中。”在现代，我们可以将尼采在《瞧！这个人》中关于他的灵感来源的言论与此进行比较。

The true father or shaping spirit of the poem is the form of the poem itself, and this form is a manifestation of the universal spirit of poetry, the “onlie begetter” of Shakespeare’s sonnets who was not Shakespeare himself, much less that depressing ghost Mr. W. H., but Shakespeare’s subject, the master-mistress of his passion. When a poet speaks of the internal spirit which shapes the poem, he is apt to drop the traditional appeal to female Muses and think of himself as in a feminine, or at least receptive, relation to some god or lord, whether Apollo, Dionysus, Eros, Christ, or (as in Milton) the Holy Spirit. Est deus in nobis, Ovid says: in modern times we may compare Nietzsche’s remarks about his inspiration in Ecce Homo.

惯例问题本质上是艺术如何传播的问题，因为文学显然与雄辩的语言结构一样，都是一种传播技巧。诗歌作为一个整体，不再仅仅是模仿自然的人工制品集合，而是人类技艺活动的整体体现。如果我们可以用“文明”一词来指代这一点，那么我们可以说，第四阶段将诗歌视为文明的技巧之一。因此，它关注的是诗歌的社会层面，是诗歌作为社群中心的作用。在这个阶段，符号是可传播的单元，我称之为原型：即典型的或反复出现的意象。我所说的原型是指将一首诗与另一首诗联系起来的符号，从而有助于统一和整合我们的文学体验。由于原型是可传播的符号，原型批评主要关注的是作为一种社会事实和一种传播方式的文学。通过研究惯例和体裁，它试图将诗歌融入诗歌的整体之中。

The problem of convention is the problem of how art can be communicable, for literature is clearly as much a technique of communication as assertive verbal structures are. Poetry, taken as a whole, is no longer simply an aggregate of artifacts imitating nature, but one of the activities of human artifice taken as a whole. If we may use the word “civilization” for this, we may say that our fourth phase looks at poetry as one of the techniques of civilization. It is concerned, therefore, with the social aspect of poetry, with poetry as the focus of a community. The symbol in this phase is the communicable unit, to which I give the name archetype: that is, a typical or recurring image. I mean by an archetype a symbol which connects one poem with another and thereby helps to unify and integrate our literary experience. And as the archetype is the communicable symbol, archetypal criticism is primarily concerned with literature as a social fact and as a mode of communication. By the study of conventions and genres, it attempts to fit poems into the body of poetry as a whole.

大量诗歌中反复出现某些常见的自然意象，例如大海或森林，这本身甚至不能称之为“巧合”（我们通常用“巧合”来形容一件设计作品，因为它毫无用处）。但这确实表明了诗歌所模仿的自然以及诗歌所参与的交流活动之间存在某种统一性。由于教育这一更广泛的交流语境，一个关于大海的故事有可能成为原型，并对从未离开过萨斯喀彻温省的读者产生深刻的想象影响。例如，当《利西达斯》中刻意运用田园意象，仅仅因为它们是约定俗成的，我们可以看到，田园的惯例使我们将这些意象与其他文学体验融会贯通。

The repetition of certain common images of physical nature like the sea or the forest in a large number of poems cannot in itself be called even “coincidence,” which is the name we give to a piece of design when we cannot find a use for it. But it does indicate a certain unity in the nature that poetry imitates, and in the communicating activity of which poetry forms part. Because of the larger communicative context of education, it is possible for a story about the sea to be archetypal, to make a profound imaginative impact, on a reader who has never been out of Saskatchewan. And when pastoral images are deliberately employed in Lycidas, for instance, merely because they are conventional, we can see that the convention of the pastoral makes us assimilate these images to other parts of literary experience.

我们首先想到的是田园诗的起源，它源自忒奥克里托斯，田园挽歌最初是作为阿多尼斯哀歌仪式的文学改编而出现的，经由忒奥克里托斯到维吉尔，再到整个田园传统，直至《牧羊人日历》 ，乃至更远的《利西达斯》本身。然后，我们想到圣经和基督教教会中错综复杂的田园象征意义，想到亚伯、诗篇第二十三篇和基督这位好牧人，想到“牧者”和“羊群”所蕴含的教会意味，以及古典时期与现代之间的联系。以及维吉尔《弥赛亚牧歌》中的基督教传统。然后，我们想到田园象征主义在西德尼的《阿卡迪亚》、莎士比亚的《仙后》、莎士比亚的森林喜剧等作品中的延伸；再想到弥尔顿之后雪莱、阿诺德、惠特曼和狄兰·托马斯等人的田园挽歌发展；或许还有绘画和音乐中的田园惯例。简而言之，我们只需选取一首传统诗歌，并追溯其原型在其他文学作品中的延伸，就能获得完整的博雅教育。像《利西达斯》这样一首公然遵循传统的诗歌迫切需要一种能够将其纳入文学整体研究的批评方法，而这种研究活动理应从第一位有修养的读者开始。在文学领域，这种情况更像是数学或科学，天才之作如此迅速地融入整个学科，以至于人们几乎察觉不到创作活动和批评活动之间的区别。

We think first of the pastoral’s descent from Theocritus, where the pastoral elegy first appears as a literary adaptation of the ritual of the Adonis lament, and through Theocritus to Virgil and the whole pastoral tradition to The Shepheardes Calender and beyond to Lycidas itself. Then we think of the intricate pastoral symbolism of the Bible and the Christian Church, of Abel and the twenty-third Psalm and Christ the Good Shepherd, of the ecclesiastical overtones of “pastor” and “flock,” and of the link between the Classical and Christian traditions in Virgil’s Messianic Eclogue. Then we think of the extensions of pastoral symbolism into Sidney’s Arcadia, The Faerie Queene, Shakespeare’s forest comedies, and the like; then of the post-Miltonic development of pastoral elegy in Shelley, Arnold, Whitman, and Dylan Thomas; perhaps too of pastoral conventions in painting and music. In short, we can get a whole liberal education simply by picking up one conventional poem and following its archetypes as they stretch out into the rest of literature. An avowedly conventional poem like Lycidas urgently demands the kind of criticism that will absorb it into the study of literature as a whole, and this activity is expected to begin at once, with the first cultivated reader. Here we have a situation in literature more like that of mathematics or science, where the work of genius is assimilated to the whole subject so quickly that one hardly notices the difference between creative and critical activity.

如果我们不接受诗歌间意象中存在的原型或惯例元素，那么单凭阅读文学作品就无法获得任何系统的思维训练。但如果我们除了渴望了解文学之外，还渴望了解我们如何了解它，我们就会发现，将意象扩展为文学的惯例原型，是我们所有阅读过程中无意识发生的自然过程。像大海或荒原这样的象征不可能仅仅局限于康拉德或哈代的作品：它必然会扩展到许多作品中，成为整个文学的原型象征。《白鲸》也不可能仅仅局限于梅尔维尔的小说：它已经融入了我们从旧约圣经开始对深海巨兽和巨龙的想象体验中。对于读者而言如此，对于诗人而言更是如此，诗人很快就会明白，除了研习自身辉煌的丰碑之外，没有其他途径可以滋养他们的灵魂。

If we do not accept the archetypal or conventional element in the imagery that links one poem with another, it is impossible to get any systematic mental training out of the reading of literature alone. But if we add to our desire to know literature a desire to know how we know it, we shall find that expanding images into conventional archetypes of literature is a process that takes place unconsciously in all our reading. A symbol like the sea or the heath cannot remain within Conrad or Hardy: it is bound to expand over many works into an archetypal symbol of literature as a whole. Moby Dick cannot remain in Melville’s novel: he is absorbed into our imaginative experience of leviathans and dragons of the deep from the Old Testament onward. And what is true for the reader is a fortiori true of the poet, who learns very quickly that there is no singing school for his soul except the study of the monuments of its own magnificence.

在象征主义的每个阶段，批评家都必然会突破诗人自身知识的局限。因此，历史批评家或文献批评家迟早会称但丁为“中世纪”诗人，而但丁对此概念既陌生又无法理解。在原型批评中，诗人的意识知识仅在诗人可能引用或模仿其他诗人（“来源”）或有意运用某种惯例时才被考虑。除此之外，诗人对其诗歌的控制仅限于诗歌本身。只有原型批评家才能关注诗歌与其他文学作品的关系。但在这里，我们又一次面临挑战。区分明确遵循传统规范的文学作品（例如《利西达斯》），与那些隐藏或忽略其传统联系的文学作品，至关重要。在《利西达斯》中，诗人开篇便提及了忒奥克里托斯、维吉尔、文艺复兴时期的田园诗人以及《圣经》。版权的概念以及低级模仿论创作观的革命性本质，也体现在版权时代作家普遍不愿接受对其意象的传统研究。在研究这一时期的作品时，大多数原型只能通过批判性的考察来确立。

In each phase of symbolism there is a point at which the critic is compelled to break away from the range of the poet’s own knowledge. Thus the historical or documentary critic has sooner or later to call Dante a “medieval” poet, a notion unknown and unintelligible to Dante. In archetypal criticism, the poet’s conscious knowledge is considered only so far as the poet may allude to or imitate other poets (“sources”) or make a deliberate use of a convention. Beyond that, the poet’s control over his poem stops with the poem. Only the archetypal critic can be concerned with its relationship to the rest of literature. But here again we have to distinguish between explicitly conventionalized literature, such as Lycidas, where the poet himself starts us off by referring to Theocritus, Virgil, Renaissance pastoralists, and the Bible, and literature which conceals or ignores its conventional links. The conception of copyright and the revolutionary nature of the low mimetic view of creation also extends to a general unwillingness on the part of authors of the copyright age to have their imagery studied conventionally, and in dealing with this period, most archetypes have to be established by critical inspection alone.

举个例子，十九世纪小说中一个非常常见的惯例是塑造两个女主角，一个肤色较深，一个肤色较浅。肤色较深的女主角通常热情奔放、傲慢自大、相貌平平、可能是外国人或犹太人，并且在某种程度上与不光彩的事物或禁忌之事（例如乱伦）联系在一起。当两个女主角都与同一个男主角有感情纠葛时，如果故事想要以圆满结局收尾，情节通常必须除掉肤色较深的女主角，或者让她成为男主角的妹妹。例如《艾凡赫》、《最后的莫希干人》、《白衣女人》、《丽姬娅》、《皮埃尔》（这是一部悲剧，因为男主角选择了肤色较深的女主角，而她也是他的妹妹）、《大理石牧神》以及无数其他作品都采用了这种手法。男性版本的“肤色较深的女主角”则构成了《呼啸山庄》的象征基础。这种手法与弥尔顿用维吉尔《牧歌》中的名字称呼爱德华·金一样，都是一种惯例，但它也体现了一种混乱的，或者说，一种“无意识的”对惯例的运用方式。同样，当我们在《失乐园》第九卷中看到男人、女人和蛇的意象时，毫无疑问，它们与《创世记》中类似的形象有着千丝万缕的联系。在哈德逊的《绿野仙踪》中，男女主人公在类似天堂的场景中，因一条蛇而初次相遇：作者并未就此意象的传统性给出任何解释。当一位评论家在斯宾塞的作品中看到手持白底红十字的圣乔治骑士时，他大致明白该如何解读这个形象。然而，当他在亨利·詹姆斯的《另一栋房子》中看到一位名叫罗斯·阿米格的女子，身着白裙，撑着红阳伞时，用现在的俚语来说，他却一头雾水。很明显，当代教育中经常被抱怨的一个缺陷，即共同文化基础的消失，使得现代诗人对《圣经》或古典神话的引用不如应有的那样重要，这与原型显性使用的减少有很大关系。

To give a random example, one very common convention of the nineteenth-century novel is the use of two heroines, one dark and one light. The dark one is as a rule passionate, haughty, plain, foreign or Jewish, and in some way associated with the undesirable or with some kind of forbidden fruit like incest. When the two are involved with the same hero, the plot usually has to get rid of the dark one or make her into a sister if the story is to end happily. Examples include Ivanhoe, The Last of the Mohicans, The Woman in White, Ligeia, Pierre (a tragedy because the hero chooses the dark girl, who is also his sister), The Marble Faun, and countless incidental treatments. A male version forms the symbolic basis of Wuthering Heights. This device is as much a convention as Milton’s calling Edward King by a name out of Virgil’s Eclogues, but it shows a confused, or, as we say, “unconscious” approach to conventions. Again, when we meet the images of a man, a woman, and a serpent in the ninth book of Paradise Lost, there is no doubt of their conventional links with similar figures in the Book of Genesis. In Hudson’s Green Mansions the hero and heroine first meet over a serpent in a quasi-Paradisal setting: here the conventional nature of the imagery is a matter on which the author gives us no help. When a critic meets St. George the Redcross Knight in Spenser, bearing a red cross on a white ground, he has some idea what to do with this figure. When he meets a female in Henry James’s The Other House called Rose Armiger with a white dress and a red parasol, he is, in the current slang, clueless. It is clear that a deficiency in contemporary education often complained of, the disappearance of a common cultural ground which makes a modern poet’s allusions to the Bible or to Classical mythology fall with less weight than they should, has much to do with the decline in the explicit use of archetypes.

众所周知，惠特曼是反原型主义的代言人。他对文学的看法是，他敦促缪斯女神忘却特洛伊的故事，去发展新的主题。这是一种低级的模仿偏见，因此对惠特曼来说恰如其分，因为他既对又错。错在，特洛伊的故事在可预见的未来仍将是西方文化遗产不可分割的一部分，因此，对于受过良好教育的读者而言，叶芝的《丽达》或艾略特的《夜莺中的斯威尼》中对阿伽门农的提及，依然具有历久弥新的意义。但他当然完全正确，他认为诗歌的内容通常与当下的环境息息相关。作为一位诗人，他将自己的诗作《当紫丁香最后一次在庭院中盛开》创作成一首悼念林肯的挽歌，而非一首传统的阿多尼斯式的哀歌，这是正确的。然而，他的挽歌在形式上却与《利西达斯》一样循规蹈矩，棺材上撒着紫色鲜花，西方垂下一颗巨大的星星，还有“永不落幕的春天”的意象等等。诗歌组织着诗人眼前流逝的世界内容，而组织这些内容的形式则源于诗歌自身的结构。

Whitman, as is well known, was a spokesman of an anti-archetypal view of literature, and urged the Muse to forget the matter of Troy and develop new themes. This is a low mimetic prejudice, and is consequently appropriate enough for Whitman, who is both right and wrong. He is wrong because the matter of Troy will always be, in the foreseeable future, an integral part of the Western cultural heritage, and hence references to Agamemnon in Yeats’s Leda or Eliot’s Sweeney among the Nightingales have as much cumulative power as ever for the properly instructed reader. But he is of course perfectly right in feeling that the content of poetry is normally an immediate and contemporary environment. He was right, being the kind of poet he was, in making the content of his own When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloomed an elegy on Lincoln and not a conventional Adonis lament. Yet his elegy is, in its form, as conventional as Lycidas, complete with purple flowers thrown on coffins, a great star drooping in the west, imagery of “ever-returning spring” and all the rest of it. Poetry organizes the content of the world as it passes before the poet, but the forms in which that content is organized come out of the structure of poetry itself.

原型是联想群，与符号不同，它们是复杂的变量。这种复杂的联想群通常包含大量特定的后天习得的联想，这些联想之所以能够传播，是因为特定文化中的许多人恰好都熟悉它们。当我们谈论日常生活中的“象征主义”时，我们通常会想到十字架或皇冠等后天习得的文化原型，或者想到诸如白色代表纯洁、绿色代表嫉妒等约定俗成的联想。作为一种原型，绿色可以象征希望、植物的特性、交通中的通行标志或爱尔兰的爱国主义，当然也可以象征嫉妒，但“绿色”一词作为语言符号总是指代某种特定的颜色。有些原型深深植根于约定俗成的联想之中，以至于它们几乎无法避免地暗示这种联想，例如十字架的几何图形必然会让人联想到基督之死。一种完全约定俗成的艺术，其原型或可传播的单元本质上就是一套深奥的符号。这种情况在艺术领域可能会发生——例如印度的一些神圣舞蹈——但在西方文学中尚未出现。现代作家不愿让自己的原型被“辨认”的原因，在于他们天生渴望保持原型的多样性，而不是将其局限于单一的解读。一位诗人可能正在展现一种深奥的……如果他像叶芝在其早期诗作的脚注中那样，特意指出某种联想，那么这种倾向就成立。联想并非必然存在：有些联想显而易见，例如黑暗与恐惧或神秘的关联，但并不存在必须始终存在的内在或固有对应关系。正如我们稍后将看到的，“普遍象征”这一短语在某些语境下才有意义，但并非此处所指的语境。然而，文学之流如同其他任何河流一样，总是首先寻找最便捷的途径：运用人们预期联想的诗人能够更快地传达信息。

Archetypes are associative clusters, and differ from signs in being complex variables. Within the complex is often a large number of specific learned associations which are communicable because a large number of people in a given culture happen to be familiar with them. When we speak of “symbolism” in ordinary life we usually think of such learned cultural archetypes as the cross or the crown, or of conventional associations, as of white with purity or green with jealousy. As an archetype, green may symbolize hope or vegetable nature or a go sign in traffic or Irish patriotism as easily as jealousy, but the word green as a verbal sign always refers to a certain color. Some archetypes are so deeply rooted in conventional association that they can hardly avoid suggesting that association, as the geometrical figure of the cross inevitably suggests the death of Christ. A completely conventionalized art would be an art in which the archetypes, or communicable units, were essentially a set of esoteric signs. This can happen in the arts—for instance in some of the sacred dances of India—but it has not happened in Western literature yet, and the resistance of modern writers to having their archetypes “spotted,” so to speak, is due to a natural anxiety to keep them as versatile as possible, not pinned down exclusively to one interpretation. A poet may be showing an esoteric tendency if he specifically points out one association, as Yeats does in his footnotes to some of his early poems. There are no necessary associations: there are some exceedingly obvious ones, such as the association of darkness with terror or mystery, but there are no intrinsic or inherent correspondences which must invariably be present. As we shall see later, there is a context in which the phrase “universal symbol” makes sense, but it is not this context. The stream of literature, however, like any other stream, seeks the easiest channels first: the poet who uses the expected associations will communicate more rapidly.

文学的一个极端是纯粹的约定俗成，诗人仅仅因为某种手法曾被反复以同样的方式使用而加以运用。这种情况在朴素诗歌中最为常见，例如中世纪传奇故事和民谣中固定的形容词和短语，朴素戏剧中一成不变的情节和人物类型，以及程度稍轻的修辞格或陈词滥调。这些陈词滥调如同文学中的其他理念一样，单独陈述时枯燥乏味，而作为文学结构原则运用时却丰富多彩。另一个极端是纯粹的变通，诗人刻意追求新颖或陌生感，因此对原型进行伪装或复杂化。这种技巧几乎等同于对文学交流功能的不信任。然而，正如柯勒律治所言，极端终会相遇，反传统的诗歌很快也会成为一种约定俗成，等待着那些习惯于文学荒漠的坚韧学者去探索。在这两个极端之间，惯例从最直白到最隐晦不等，其尺度与前文讨论过的寓言和悖论尺度平行。这两个尺度常常被混淆或混淆，但将意象转化为例证和格言，与将意象延伸到其他诗歌中，是截然不同的过程。

At one extreme of literature we have the pure convention, which a poet uses merely because it has often been used before in the same way. This is most frequent in naive poetry, in the fixed epithets and phrase-tags of medieval romance and ballad, in the invariable plots and character types of naive drama, and, to a lesser degree, in the topoi or rhetorical commonplaces which, like other ideas in literature, are so dull when stated as propositions, and so rich and variegated when they are used as structural principles in literature. At the other extreme we have the pure variable, where there is a deliberate attempt at novelty or unfamiliarity, and consequently a disguising or complicating of archetypes. Such techniques come very close to a distrust of communication itself as a function of literature. However, extremes meet, as Coleridge said, and anti-conventional poetry soon becomes a convention in its turn, to be explored by hardy scholars accustomed to the dreariness of literary bad lands. Between these extreme points conventions vary from the most explicit to the most indirect, along a scale parallel to the scale of allegory and paradox already dealt with. The two scales may be often confused or identified, but translating imagery into examples and precepts is a quite distinct process from following images into other poems.

纯粹的惯例接近极端的是翻译、释义，以及乔叟在《特洛伊罗斯与骑士的故事》中对薄伽丘作品的运用。接下来是刻意而明确的惯例，例如我们在《利西达斯》中看到的。再往后是悖论式或反讽式的惯例，包括戏仿——这通常表明某些处理惯例的风尚已经过时。然后是试图通过摒弃明确的惯例来追求原创性，这种尝试导致了我们在惠特曼的作品中发现的那种隐性惯例。最后是一种倾向将原创性等同于“实验性”写作，在当今社会，这种做法往往基于与科学发现的类比，并常被称作“打破常规”。当然，在文学的各个阶段，包括最后阶段，都存在着大量肤浅且不自然的惯例，从而产生了大多数文学研究者都不愿涉足的那种作品：平庸的伊丽莎白时代十四行诗和情歌、普劳图斯式的喜剧套路、十八世纪的田园诗、十九世纪的皆大欢喜结局小说，以及各种追随者、门徒和流派的作品。

Near the extreme of pure convention is translation, paraphrase, and the kind of use which Chaucer makes of Boccaccio in Troilus and The Knight’s Tale. Next we come to deliberate and explicit convention, such as we have noted in Lycidas. Next comes paradoxical or ironic convention, including parody—often a sign that certain vogues in handling conventions are getting worn out. Then comes the attempt to reach originality through turning one’s back on explicit convention, an attempt which results in implicit convention of the kind we detected in Whitman. Then comes a tendency to identify originality with “experimental” writing, based in our day on an analogy with scientific discovery, and which is frequently spoken of as “breaking with convention.” And, of course, at every stage of literature, including this last one, there is a great deal of superficial and inorganic convention, producing the kind of writing that most students of literature prefer to keep in the middle distance: run-of-the-mill Elizabethan sonnets and love lyrics, Plautine comedy-formulas, eighteenth-century pastorals, nineteenth-century happy-ending novels, works of followers and disciples and schools and trends generally.

由此可见，原型最容易在高度程式化的文学作品中进行研究：也就是说，在大多数朴素、原始和通俗的文学作品中，原型最为容易研究。因此，我提出原型批评的可能性，实际上是在暗示，可以将目前用于民间故事和民谣的比较和形态学研究方法扩展到其他文学作品中。如今，人们不再像过去那样将通俗文学和原始文学与普通文学泾渭分明地区分开来，这使得这种可能性更容易被理解。此外，我们还会发现，正是因为其程式化，这种肤浅的文学作品对原型批评具有极大的价值。如果在本书中，我提及通俗小说的频率与提及最伟大的长篇小说和史诗的频率一样高，那是因为，一位音乐家在试图解释对位法的基本原理时，至少在最初阶段，更有可能用《三只瞎老鼠》而不是巴赫复杂的赋格曲来举例说明。

It is clear from all this that archetypes are most easily studied in highly conventionalized literature: that is, for the most part, naive, primitive, and popular literature. In suggesting the possibility of archetypal criticism, then, I am suggesting the possibility of extending the kind of comparative and morphological study now made of folk tales and ballads into the rest of literature.
