This should be more easily conceivable now that it is no longer fashionable to mark off popular and primitive literature from ordinary literature as sharply as we used to do. Also, we shall find that superficial literature, of the kind just spoken of, is of great value to archetypal criticism simply because it is conventional. If throughout this book I refer to popular fiction as frequently as to the greatest novels and epics, it is for the same reason that a musician attempting to explain the rudimentary facts about counterpoint would be more likely, at least at first, to illustrate from “Three Blind Mice” than from a complex Bach fugue.

象征主义的每个阶段都有其独特的叙事和意义表达方式。在字面阶段，叙事是意义丰富的音韵流动，意义则是一种模糊而复杂的语言模式。在描述阶段，叙事是对真实事件的模仿，意义则是对实际物体或命题的模仿。在形式阶段，诗歌存在于例证与准则之间。例证事件中蕴含着重复的元素；准则，即关于“应然”的陈述中，则蕴含着强烈的欲望元素，或者说是所谓的“愿望思维”。这些重复和欲望的元素在原型批评中凸显出来，原型批评将诗歌视为整体的单元，将符号视为交流的单元。

Every phase of symbolism has its particular approach to narrative and to meaning. In the literal phase, narrative is a flow of significant sounds, and meaning an ambiguous and complex verbal pattern. In the descriptive phase, narrative is an imitation of real events, and meaning an imitation of actual objects or propositions. In the formal phase, poetry exists between the example and the precept. In the exemplary event there is an element of recurrence; in the precept, or statement about what ought to be, there is a strong element of desire, or what is called “wish-thinking.” These elements of recurrence and desire come into the foreground in archetypal criticism, which studies poems as units of poetry as a whole and symbols as units of communication.

从这个角度来看，文学的叙事方面是反复出现的象征性交流行为：换言之，是一种仪式。原型批评家将叙事视为对人类整体行为的仪式或模仿，而不仅仅是对某一行为的模仿。同样，在原型批评中，其重要内容是欲望与现实的冲突，而这种冲突的基础是梦的作用。因此，仪式和梦分别是文学原型层面的叙事内容和重要内容。对小说或戏剧情节的原型分析会从与仪式相似性的典型、反复出现或约定俗成的行为入手：例如婚礼、葬礼、知识和社会启蒙仪式、处决或模拟处决、驱逐替罪羊等等。对这类作品的意义或重要性的原型分析，会从其情绪和结局所体现的通用、反复出现或约定俗成的形式入手，无论是悲剧性的、喜剧性的、讽刺性的，还是其他什么，其中都表达了欲望和经验之间的关系。

From such a point of view, the narrative aspect of literature is a recurrent act of symbolic communication: in other words a ritual. Narrative is studied by the archetypal critic as ritual or imitation of human action as a whole, and not simply as a mimesis praxeos or imitation of an action. Similarly, in archetypal criticism the significant content is the conflict of desire and reality which has for its basis the work of the dream. Ritual and dream, therefore, are the narrative and significant content respectively of literature in its archetypal aspect. The archetypal analysis of the plot of a novel or play would deal with it in terms of the generic, recurring, or conventional actions which show analogies to rituals: the weddings, funerals, intellectual and social initiations, executions or mock executions, the chasing away of the scapegoat villain, and so on. The archetypal analysis of the meaning or significance of such a work would deal with it in terms of the generic, recurring, or conventional shape indicated by its mood and resolution, whether tragic, comic, ironic, or what not, in which the relationship of desire and experience is expressed.

循环与欲望相互交织，在仪式和梦境中都同样重要。在原型阶段，诗歌模仿自然，但并非像形式阶段那样模仿作为结构或系统的自然，而是模仿作为循环过程的自然。艺术节奏中的循环原则似乎源于自然界中使我们理解时间的重复。仪式围绕着太阳、月亮、季节和人类生命的循环运动而展开。每一个重要的周期性体验：黎明、日落、月相、播种和收获、春分、秋分、夏至、出生、成年礼、婚姻和死亡，都与相应的仪式紧密相连。仪式的吸引力在于纯粹的循环叙事，如果真有这种叙事存在的话，那便是自动的、无意识的重复。然而，在所有这些重复之中，存在着睡眠和清醒生活的核心循环，自我的日常挫败感，以及每晚巨大自我的觉醒。

Recurrence and desire interpenetrate, and are equally important in both ritual and dream. In its archetypal phase, the poem imitates nature, not (as in the formal phase) nature as a structure or system, but nature as a cyclical process. The principle of recurrence in the rhythm of art seems to be derived from the repetitions in nature that make time intelligible to us. Rituals cluster around the cyclical movements of the sun, the moon, the seasons, and human life. Every crucial periodicity of experience: dawn, sunset, the phases of the moon, seed-time and harvest, the equinoxes and the solstices, birth, initiation, marriage, and death, get rituals attached to them. The pull of ritual is toward pure cyclical narrative, which, if there could be such a thing, would be automatic and unconscious repetition. In the middle of all this recurrence, however, is the central recurrent cycle of sleeping and waking life, the daily frustration of the ego, the nightly awakening of a titanic self.

典型的批评家将诗歌视为诗歌的一部分进行研究，并将诗歌视为人类对自然整体模仿（即我们称之为文明的模仿）的一部分。文明不仅仅是对自然的模仿，而是将自然塑造成完整的人类形态的过程，而这一过程是由我们刚才称之为欲望的力量所驱动的。对食物和住所的欲望并不满足于根茎和洞穴：它创造了我们称之为农业和建筑的人类对自然的改造形态。因此，欲望并非对需求的简单反应，因为动物也可能……它并非指无需耕种就能获得食物，也并非仅仅是对某种特定事物的渴望或欲望。它既不局限于物质，也不被物质所满足，而是推动人类社会发展自身形态的能量。从这个意义上讲，欲望是我们在字面意义上所理解的情感的社会层面，是一种表达的冲动，若非诗歌赋予其表达形式，这种冲动将始终处于无形状态。同样，欲望的形式也因文明而得以解放和显现。文明的动力是劳动，而诗歌在其社会层面上的作用在于，它以语言的形式表达了对劳动目标和欲望形式的愿景。

The archetypal critic studies the poem as part of poetry, and poetry as part of the total human imitation of nature that we call civilization. Civilization is not merely an imitation of nature, but the process of making a total human form out of nature, and it is impelled by the force that we have just called desire. The desire for food and shelter is not content with roots and caves: it produces the human forms of nature that we call farming and architecture. Desire is thus not a simple response to need, for an animal may need food without planting a garden to get it, nor is it a simple response to want, or desire for something in particular. It is neither limited to nor satisfied by objects, but is the energy that leads human society to develop its own form. Desire in this sense is the social aspect of what we met on the literal level as emotion, an impulse toward expression which would have remained amorphous if the poem had not liberated it by providing the form of its expression. The form of desire, similarly, is liberated and made apparent by civilization. The efficient cause of civilization is work, and poetry in its social aspect has the function of expressing, as a verbal hypothesis, a vision of the goal of work and the forms of desire.

然而，欲望中蕴含着一种道德辩证法。花园的概念催生了“杂草”的概念，而建造羊圈则使狼成为更强大的敌人。因此，诗歌在其社会或原型层面上，不仅试图描绘欲望的实现，也试图界定实现欲望的障碍。仪式不仅是一种反复出现的行为，更是一种表达欲望与厌恶辩证法的行为：渴望丰饶或胜利，厌恶干旱或敌人。我们有社会融合的仪式，也有驱逐、处决和惩罚的仪式。梦境中也存在着类似的辩证法，既有愿望实现的梦，也有焦虑或厌恶的噩梦。因此，原型批评建立在两种组织节奏或模式之上，一种是循环的，另一种是辩证的。

There is however a moral dialectic in desire. The conception of a garden develops the conception “weed,” and building a sheepfold makes the wolf a greater enemy. Poetry in its social or archetypal aspect, therefore, not only tries to illustrate the fulfilment of desire, but to define the obstacles to it. Ritual is not only a recurrent act, but an act expressive of a dialectic of desire and repugnance: desire for fertility or victory, repugnance to drought or to enemies. We have rituals of social integration, and we have rituals of expulsion, execution, and punishment. In dream there is a parallel dialectic, as there is both the wish-fulfilment dream and the anxiety or nightmare dream of repugnance. Archetypal criticism, therefore, rests on two organizing rhythms or patterns, one cyclical, the other dialectic.

仪式与梦境以语言交流形式结合，便是神话。这与前一篇文章中“神话”一词的含义略有不同。首先，这种含义同样为人熟知，歧义并非出自我的本意，而是词典的缘故；其次，这两种含义之间存在着真正的联系，这一点在我们接下来的论述中会更加清晰。神话解释了仪式和梦境，并使之得以交流。仪式本身无法解释自身：它是前逻辑的、前语言的，在某种意义上也是前人类的。它与历法的关联似乎将人类生活与植物（在某种程度上也包括动物）仍然拥有的对自然循环的生物依赖联系起来。自然界中所有我们认为与艺术作品有相似之处的事物，例如花朵或鸟鸣，都源于生物体与其自然环境节奏（尤其是太阳年的节奏）之间的同步。动物的某些同步表现形式，就像鸟类的求偶舞一样，它们几乎可以被称为仪式。神话更具人类特色，因为即使是最聪明的鹧鸪也无法讲述一个荒诞的故事来解释它在交配季节为何鸣叫。同样，梦本身就是一个由隐晦的暗示构成的系统，指向做梦者自身的生活，做梦者本人也无法完全理解，或者至少就我们所知，这些暗示对他来说没有任何实际用途。但是，所有梦境中都包含着一种具有独立沟通能力的神话元素，这一点显而易见，不仅在俄狄浦斯的经典例子中如此，在任何民间故事集中也都能找到。因此，神话不仅赋予仪式意义，赋予梦境叙事意义，它更是将仪式与梦境等同起来，前者被视为后者的动态体现。除非仪式与梦境之间存在某种共同因素，使一方成为另一方的社会表达，否则这一切都不可能实现；而对这种共同因素的探究，我们将留待以后再谈。我们在这里需要说明的是，仪式是神话的原型，而梦是精神的原型。

The union of ritual and dream in a form of verbal communication is myth. This is a sense of the term myth slightly different from that used in the previous essay. But, first, the sense is equally familiar, and the ambiguity not mine but the dictionary’s; and, second, there is a real connection between the two senses which will become more apparent as we go on. The myth accounts for, and makes communicable, the ritual and the dream. Ritual, by itself, cannot account for itself: it is pre-logical, pre-verbal, and in a sense pre-human. Its attachment to the calendar seems to link human life to the biological dependence on the natural cycle which plants, and to some extent animals, still have. Everything in nature that we think of as having some analogy with works of art, like the flower or the bird’s song, grows out of a synchronization between an organism and the rhythms of its natural environment, especially that of the solar year. With animals some expressions of synchronization, like the mating dances of birds, could almost be called rituals. Myth is more distinctively human, as the most intelligent partridge cannot tell even the most absurd story explaining why it drums in the mating season. Similarly, the dream, by itself, is a system of cryptic allusions to the dreamer’s own life, not fully understood by him, or so far as we know of any real use to him. But in all dreams there is a mythical element which has a power of independent communication, as is obvious, not only in the stock example of Oedipus, but in any collection of folk tales. Myth, therefore, not only gives meaning to ritual and narrative to dream: it is the identification of ritual and dream, in which the former is seen to be the latter in movement. This would not be possible unless there were a common factor to ritual and dream which made one the social expression of the other; the investigation of this common factor we must leave for later treatment. All that we need to say here is that ritual is the archetypal aspect of mythos and dream the archetypal aspect of dianoia.

我们在第一篇文章中提到的虚构文学和主题文学之间的侧重点区别，在这里再次出现。某些文学形式，例如戏剧，能让我们格外清晰地联想到仪式，因为文学中的戏剧，如同宗教中的仪式，本质上是一种社会性或集体性的表演。另一些文学形式，例如爱情故事，则暗示着梦境的相似之处。仪式的相似之处最容易在非传统戏剧中发现，并非在受过良好教育的观众和固定剧院的戏剧中，而是在质朴或奇幻的戏剧中：例如民间剧、木偶戏、哑剧、闹剧、盛大游行，以及它们在假面剧、喜歌剧、商业电影和歌舞杂耍等衍生形式中的表现。梦境的相似之处在质朴爱情故事中体现得最为明显，这类故事包括民间故事和童话，它们与美好愿望成真的梦境以及食人魔和女巫的噩梦密切相关。当然，质朴戏剧和质朴爱情故事之间也存在着相互渗透的关系。朴素戏剧通常描绘的是某种浪漫故事，而浪漫故事与仪式之间的密切联系，可以从许多中世纪浪漫故事中看出，这些故事都与历法中的某些特定时刻相关，例如冬至、五月清晨或圣徒节前夕；或者与某些阶级仪式相关，例如比武大会。原型主要是一种可传播的符号，这一事实在很大程度上解释了民谣、民间故事和哑剧为何能够像其众多英雄一样，轻松地跨越语言和文化的障碍，在世界各地传播开来。我们最终还是回到了文学这一事实。受象征主义原型阶段影响最深的，给我们留下了原始而流行的印象。

The same distinction in emphasis that we noted in the first essay between fictional and thematic literature recurs here. Some literary forms, such as drama, remind us with particular vividness of analogies to rituals, for the drama in literature, like the ritual in religion, is primarily a social or ensemble performance. Others, such as romance, suggest analogies to dreams. Ritual analogies are most easily seen, not in the drama of the educated audience and the settled theatre, but in naive or spectacular drama: in the folk play, the puppet show, the pantomime, the farce, the pageant, and their descendants in masque, comic opera, commercial movie, and revue. Dream analogies are best studied in naive romance, which includes the folk tales and fairy tales that are so closely related to dreams of wonderful wishes coming true, and to nightmares of ogres and witches. Naive drama and naive romance, of course, also interpenetrate. What naive drama dramatizes is usually some kind of romance, and the close relation of romance to ritual can be seen in the number of medieval romances that are linked to some part of the calendar, the winter solstice, a May morning, or a saint’s eve; or else to some class ritual like the tournament. The fact that the archetype is primarily a communicable symbol largely accounts for the ease with which ballads and folk tales and mimes travel through the world, like so many of their heroes, over all barriers of language and culture. We come back here to the fact that literature most deeply influenced by the archetypal phase of symbolism impresses us as primitive and popular.

我用这些词分别指具备在时间和空间中进行交流的能力。除此之外，它们的意思基本相同。通俗艺术通常会被当时的文化人士斥为庸俗；随着新一代的成长，它会逐渐失去原有受众的青睐；然后，它开始融入“古雅”的柔和氛围，文化人士也开始对它产生兴趣；最终，它开始展现出原始艺术的古老尊严。每当我们发现伟大的艺术作品运用通俗形式时，这种古老感就会反复出现，例如莎士比亚晚期的作品，或者《圣经》以一个关于落难少女、英雄屠龙、邪恶女巫和一座珠宝璀璨的奇妙城市的童话故事结尾。古风是所有社会原型运用中一个常见的特征。苏联以其拖拉机的生产而自豪，但拖拉机要取代镰刀成为苏联国旗上的标志，还需要一段时间。

By these words I mean possessing the ability to communicate in time and space respectively. Otherwise they mean much the same thing. Popular art is normally decried as vulgar by the cultivated people of its time; then it loses favor with its original audience as a new generation grows up; then it begins to merge into the softer lighting of “quaint,” and cultivated people become interested in it, and finally it begins to take on the archaic dignity of the primitive. This sense of the archaic recurs whenever we find great art using popular forms, as Shakespeare does in his last period, or as the Bible does when it ends in a fairy tale about a damsel in distress, a hero killing dragons, a wicked witch, and a wonderful city glittering with jewels. Archaism is a regular feature of all social uses of archetypes. Soviet Russia is very proud of its production of tractors, but it will be some time before the tractor replaces the sickle on the Soviet flag.

正是在这一点上，我们必须注意到并避免神话契约理论的谬误。也就是说，如果我们把讨论局限于对当前社会结构的可观察事实，那么政治理论中或许存在社会契约。但是，当这些事实与一个发生在遥远过去的寓言故事联系起来时——而这个过去发生过的事情太过遥远，以至于没有任何证据可以推翻说书人的断言——当我们被告知曾经有人放弃、委托或被欺骗而放弃了权力时，政治理论就仅仅沦为柏拉图式的又一个灌输谎言。由于这个遥远事件的唯一证据是它与当前事实的类比，因此，当前的事实实际上是在与自身的影子进行比较。在关注神话的文学批评中，也发生了完全相同的寓言化过程，而这种批评几乎还没有摆脱其历史契约的阶段。

It is at this point that we must notice and avoid the fallacy of a theory of mythological contract. That is, there may be such a thing as a social contract in political theory, if we keep the discussion to observable facts about the present structure of society. But when these facts are attached to a fable about something that happened in a past too remote for any evidence to disturb the fabler’s assertions, and we are told that once upon a time men surrendered or delegated or were tricked into surrendering their power, political theory has merely become one of Plato’s indoctrinating lies. And because the only evidence for this remote event is its analogy to the present facts, the present facts are being compared with their own shadows. A precisely similar fabling process has taken place in the literary criticism concerned with myth, which has hardly yet emerged from its historical contract stage.

由于原型批评家关注仪式和梦境，他很可能会对当代人类学在仪式研究以及当代心理学在梦境研究方面所做的工作感兴趣。具体而言，弗雷泽的《金枝》中对朴素戏剧仪式基础的研究，以及荣格及其学派对朴素浪漫主义梦境基础的研究，对他来说最具直接价值。然而，人类学、心理学和文学批评这三个学科尚未完全分离，必须警惕决定论的危险。在文学批评家看来，仪式是戏剧行为的内容，而非其来源或起源。《金枝》从文学批评的角度来看，是一篇探讨朴素戏剧仪式内容的文章：也就是说，它重构了一种原型仪式，戏剧的结构和类型原则可以从中逻辑地而非时间上推导出来。对于文学批评家而言，这种仪式是否在历史上存在过无关紧要。弗雷泽假设的仪式很可能与现实中的仪式有许多引人注目的相似之处，而收集这些相似之处正是他论证的一部分。但是，相似之处并不必然是来源、影响、原因或雏形，更遑论同一性。仪式与戏剧的文学关系，如同人类行为的任何其他方面与戏剧的关系一样，仅仅是内容与形式的关系，而非来源与推导的关系。

As the archetypal critic is concerned with ritual and dream, it is likely that he would find much of interest in the work done by contemporary anthropology in ritual, and by contemporary psychology in dreams. Specifically, the work done on the ritual basis of naive drama in Frazer’s Golden Bough, and the work done on the dream basis of naive romance by Jung and the Jungians, are of most direct value to him. But the three subjects of anthropology, psychology, and literary criticism are not yet clearly separated, and the danger of determinism has to be carefully watched. To the literary critic, ritual is the content of dramatic action, not the source or origin of it. The Golden Bough is, from the point of view of literary criticism, an essay on the ritual content of naive drama: that is, it reconstructs an archetypal ritual from which the structural and generic principles of drama may be logically, not chronologically, derived. It does not matter two pins to the literary critic whether such a ritual had any historical existence or not. It is very probable that Frazer’s hypothetical ritual would have many and striking analogies to actual rituals, and collecting such analogies is part of his argument. But an analogy is not necessarily a source, an influence, a cause, or an embryonic form, much less an identity. The literary relation of ritual to drama, like that of any other aspect of human action to drama, is a relation of content to form only, not one of source to derivation.

因此，批评家只关注他所研究的对象中实际存在的仪式或梦境模式，无论这些模式是如何产生的。追随弗雷泽的古典学者们已经构建了一套关于希腊戏剧的奇观或仪式内容的普遍理论。《金枝》自称是一部人类学著作，但它对文学批评的影响远大于其自身所宣称的领域，而且它最终可能被证明是一部真正的文学批评著作。如果仪式模式存在于戏剧之中——例如， 《陶里斯的伊菲革涅亚》的主要主题之一是活人献祭，这是事实而非观点——那么批评家就不必在关于希腊戏剧仪式起源的完全独立的历史争论中选边站队。因此，作为行动内容，尤其是戏剧行动内容的仪式，持续潜藏于语言的秩序之中，并且完全独立于直接影响。即使到了十九世纪，我们仍然会发现即兴戏剧变得原始而流行，就像《米卡多》那样。再举个例子，弗雷泽的所有手法都回来了：国王的儿子、模拟献祭、与萨卡亚节的类比，以及许多其他吉尔伯特不了解也不在意的东西。它之所以回归，是因为它仍然是吸引观众注意力的最佳方式，而经验丰富的剧作家深谙此道。

The critic, therefore, is concerned only with the ritual or dream patterns which are actually in what he is studying, however they got there. The work of the Classical scholars who have followed Frazer’s lead has produced a general theory of the spectacular or ritual content of Greek drama. The Golden Bough purports to be a work of anthropology, but it has had more influence on literary criticism than in its own alleged field, and it may yet prove to be really a work of literary criticism. If the ritual pattern is in the plays—and it is fact, not opinion, that one of the main themes of Iphigeneia in Tauris, for example, is human sacrifice—the critic need not take sides in the quite separate historical controversy over the ritual origin of Greek drama. Hence ritual, as the content of action, and more particularly of dramatic action, is something continuously latent in the order of words, and is quite independent of direct influence. Even in the nineteenth century, we find that the instant drama becomes primitive and popular, as it does in The Mikado, to repeat an example given before, back comes all Frazer’s apparatus, the king’s son, the mock sacrifice, the analogy with the festival of the Sacaea, and many other things that Gilbert knew and cared nothing about. It comes back because it is still the best way of holding an audience’s attention, and the experienced dramatist knows it.

完全关注史料和历史传承的文献批评的威望，误导了一些典型的批评家，让他们认为所有此类仪式元素都应该像王室血统一样，直接追溯到某种自愿的暂停状态。怀疑论者会允许这种情况发生。由此产生的巨大时间跨度通常由某种种族记忆理论，或某种涉及秘密的阴谋论历史观来填补，这些秘密被神秘教派或传统严密守护了数个世纪。有趣的是，当原型批评家坚持某种历史框架时，他们几乎总是会提出某种假设，即从古代失落的黄金时代开始，世界不断衰落。例如，托马斯·曼的《约瑟夫》系列小说的序言就将我们几个核心神话追溯到亚特兰蒂斯，显然，亚特兰蒂斯作为原型概念比作为历史概念更有用。当原型批评在十九世纪随着太阳神话的流行而复兴时，有人试图通过同样令人信服地证明拿破仑也是一个太阳神话来嘲讽它。然而，这种嘲讽只对该方法的历史歪曲有效。每当我们谈到拿破仑事业的崛起、声望的巅峰或命运的衰落时，我们往往会把他比作太阳神话。

The prestige of documentary criticism, which deals entirely with sources and historical transmission, has misled some archetypal critics into feeling that all such ritual elements ought to be traced directly, like the lineage of royalty, as far back as a willing suspension of disbelief will allow. The vast chronological gaps resulting are usually bridged by some theory of race memory, or by some conspiratorial conception of history involving secrets jealously guarded for centuries by esoteric cults or traditions. It is curious that when archetypal critics hang on to a historical framework they almost invariably produce some hypothesis of continuous degeneration from a golden age lost in antiquity. Thus the prelude to Thomas Mann’s Joseph series traces back several of our central myths to Atlantis, Atlantis being clearly more useful as an archetypal idea than as a historical one. When archetypal criticism revived in the nineteenth century with a vogue for sun myths, an attempt was made to ridicule it by proving with equal plausibility that Napoleon was a sun myth. The ridicule is effective only against the historical distortion of the method. Archetypally, we turn Napoleon into a sun myth whenever we speak of the rise of his career, the zenith of his fame, or the eclipse of his fortunes.

社会文化史，即广义上的人类学，始终是批评语境的一部分；仪式研究的人类学视角与批评视角区分得越清晰，二者之间的相互影响就越有益。心理学与批评的关系亦是如此。诗歌最根本、最引人注目的单元，莫过于诗歌作者的整体创作，而非单首诗歌本身。传记始终是批评的一部分，传记作者自然会对传主的诗歌感兴趣，将其视为一份个人文献，记录其私密的梦想、联想、抱负以及表达或压抑的欲望。对这类问题的研究构成了批评的重要组成部分。我当然不是在谈论那些肤浅的研究，它们只是将作者自身的色情意味，披上理性化的临床外衣，投射到其研究对象身上；我指的是那些在心理学和批评领域都具备扎实技术功底的严肃研究，它们深知其中蕴含着多少推测，以及所有结论都必然是暂时的。

Social and cultural history, which is anthropology in an extended sense, will always be a part of the context of criticism, and the more clearly the anthropological and the critical treatments of ritual are distinguished, the more beneficial their influence on each other will be. The same is true of the relation of psychology to criticism. The first and most striking unit of poetry larger than the individual poem is the total work of the man who wrote the poem. Biography will always be a part of criticism, and the biographer will naturally be interested in his subject’s poetry as a personal document, recording his private dreams, associations, ambitions, and expressed or repressed desires. Studies of such matters form an essential part of criticism. I am not of course speaking of the silly ones, which simply project the author’s own erotica, in a rationalized clinical disguise, on his victim, but only of the serious studies which are technically competent both in psychology and in criticism, which are aware how much guesswork is involved and how tentative all the conclusions must be.

这种方法对于我们称之为低模仿性主题作家的作品最为简便有效——主要指浪漫主义诗人，因为诗人自身的心理过程往往是作品主题的一部分。而对于其他类型的作家，例如一位从他写下的第一个字就意识到“取悦他人者必得取悦他人方能生存”的剧作家，则存在着将诗人与其文学社群割裂开来的风险。假设……评论家发现，莎士比亚的戏剧中反复出现某种模式。如果莎士比亚在使用这种模式上是独一无二的、反常的，甚至是特例，那么他使用这种模式的原因至少部分是心理因素。如果有证据表明，即使这种模式未能取悦观众，他仍然坚持使用，那么其中存在个人心理因素的可能性就非常高。但是，如果我们能在他同时代的其他六位剧作家身上找到同样的模式，显然我们必须考虑到惯例因素。如果我们在十几位不同时代和文化的剧作家身上都发现了这种模式，我们就必须考虑到体裁因素，以及戏剧本身的结构要求。事实上，我们在莎士比亚的喜剧中确实发现同样的技巧被反复使用，而文学评论家的职责就是将这些技巧与其他剧作家的技巧进行比较，从而对喜剧形式进行形态学研究。否则，我们将失去对莎士比亚学术品质的完全合理的欣赏，失去在他喜剧中反复出现的技巧中所看到的喜剧赋格艺术。

Such an approach is easiest, and most rewarding, with what we have called thematic writers of the low mimetic—that is, chiefly, the Romantic poets, where the poet’s own psychological processes are often part of the theme. With other writers, say a dramatist who is aware from the first word he writes that “They who live to please must please to live,” there is danger of making an unreal abstraction of the poet from his literary community. Suppose a critic finds that a certain pattern is repeated time and again in the plays of Shakespeare. If Shakespeare is unique or anomalous, or even exceptional, in using this pattern, the reason for his use of it may be at least partly psychological. If there were any evidence that he had persisted in using it when it failed to please an audience, the probability of a personal psychological element would be very high. But if we can find the same pattern in half a dozen of his contemporaries, we clearly have to allow for convention. And if we find it in a dozen dramatists of different ages and cultures, we have to allow for genre, for the structural requirements of drama itself. Now as a matter of fact we do find in Shakespeare’s comedies that the same devices are used over and over, and it is the business of the literary critic to compare these devices with those of other dramatists, in a morphological study of comic form. Otherwise we shall deprive ourselves of the perfectly legitimate appreciation of the scholarly qualities of Shakespeare, of seeing in the repeated devices of his comedies a kind of Art of Fugue of comedy.

心理学家在分析一首诗时，往往会从中看到梦境般的景象——隐含内容与显性内容的混合。对文学批评家而言，诗歌的显性内容是其形式，因此其隐含内容便简化为实际内容，即其主题或意象。而这种原型层面的主题便是梦境，是欲望与现实冲突的呈现。我们似乎陷入了循环，但又不完全如此。对批评家而言，出现了一个纯粹的心理学分析所不存在的问题：可交流的隐含内容，可理解的梦境，柏拉图将艺术视为觉醒心灵的梦境这一概念。对心理学家来说，所有梦境符号都是私人的，由做梦者的个人生活所诠释。而对批评家而言，私人符号并不存在，或者说，即便存在，他们的职责也是确保它不会一直如此。

A psychologist examining a poem will tend to see in it what he sees in the dream, a mixture of latent and manifest content. For the literary critic the manifest content of the poem is its form, hence its latent content becomes simply its actual content, its dianoia or theme. And this dianoia on the archetypal level is a dream, a presentation of the conflict of desire and actuality. We seem to be going around in a circle, but not quite. For the critic, a problem appears which does not exist for a purely psychological analysis, the problem of communicable latent content, of intelligible dream, Plato’s conception of art as a dream for awakened minds. For the psychologist all dream symbols are private ones, interpreted by the personal life of the dreamer. For the critic there is no such thing as private symbolism, or, if there is, it is his job to make sure that it does not remain so.

弗洛伊德对《俄狄浦斯王》的解读中已经存在这个问题，他认为这部戏剧之所以如此震撼人心，很大程度上是因为它戏剧化地展现了俄狄浦斯情结。戏剧元素和心理元素可以联系起来，而无需提及索福克勒斯的个人生活，因为我们对他的个人生活一无所知。荣格及其学派发展了这种对非个人内容的强调，他们认为原型的可交流性源于……集体无意识理论——在我看来，这是文学批评中一个不必要的假设。

This problem is already present in Freud’s treatment of Oedipus Tyrannus as a play which owes much of its power to the fact that it dramatizes the Oedipus complex. The dramatic and psychological elements can be linked without any reference to the personal life of Sophocles, of which we know nothing whatever. This emphasis on impersonal content has been developed by Jung and his school, where the communicability of archetypes is accounted for by a theory of a collective unconscious—an unnecessary hypothesis in literary criticism, so far as I can judge.

我们发现，作者的意图同样适用于观众的注意力。两者都具有向心性，艺术作品的创作和回应都蕴含着观众无法明确意识到的含义。离散的意识只能捕捉到复杂回应中极少的细节。例如，正是这种状况使得丁尼生既因其语言的纯洁而备受赞誉，又因其强烈的色情感官体验而为人所读。这也使得当代评论家能够充分利用现代知识资源来解读艺术作品，而无需真正担心时代错置。

What we have found to be true of the writer’s intention is also true of the audience’s attention. Both are centripetally directed, and implications exist in the response to art as they do in the creation of it, implications of which the audience is not explicitly aware. Discrete conscious awareness can take in only a very few details of the complex of response. This state of things enabled Tennyson, for instance, to be praised for the chastity of his language and read for his powerful erotic sensuousness. It also makes it possible for a contemporary critic to draw on the fullest resources of modern knowledge in explicating a work of art without any real fear of anachronism.

例如，《无病呻吟》讲述的是一个男人，按照十七世纪的时代背景（无疑也包括莫里哀自己的理解），他并非真的生病，只是自以为生病了。现代评论家可能会反驳说，生活并非如此简单：无病呻吟完全有可能演变成真正的疾病，而阿尔冈的问题显然在于他不愿看到孩子们长大，这是一种幼稚的退行。他的妻子——顺便一提，是他的第二任妻子——通过溺爱他，并低声说着“可怜的小儿子”之类的话，表明她完全理解这一点。这样的评论家会在阿尔冈与小女孩路易松那场戏之后，在他不经意间说出的一句话中找到他所有行为的线索（评论家也会注意到这句话的色情意味）：“孩子已经不在了。”无论这种解读是对是错，它都并未偏离莫里哀的原著，但却丝毫没有揭示莫里哀本人的内心世界。这部剧作本质上是一部喜剧，因此必然以圆满结局收尾；阿尔冈必然会幡然醒悟；他的妻子，其戏剧作用在于使他深陷执念之中，因此必然会被“揭露”为与他为敌之人。剧情是一个仪式，最终走向以抛弃替罪羊为开端，随后步入婚姻殿堂；而主题则是非理性欲望与现实冲突的梦境模式。

For instance, Le Malade Imaginaire is a play about a man who, in seventeenth-century terms, including no doubt Molière’s own terms, was not really sick but just thought he was. A modern critic might object that life is not so simple: that it is perfectly possible for a malade imaginaire to be a malade véritable, and that what is wrong with Argan is clearly an unwillingness to see his children grow up, an infantile regression which his wife—his second wife, incidentally—shows that she understands completely by coddling him and murmuring such phrases as “pauvre petit fils.” Such a critic would find the clue to Argan’s whole behavior in his unguarded remark after the scene with the little girl Louison (the erotic nature of which the critic would also notice): “Il n’y a plus d’enfants.” Now whether this reading is right or wrong, it does not swerve from Molière’s text, yet it tells us nothing about Molière himself. The play is generically a comedy; it must therefore end happily; Argan must therefore be brought to see some reason; his wife, whose dramatic function it is to keep him within his obsession, must therefore be “exposed” as inimical to him. The plot is a ritual moving toward a scapegoat rejection followed by a marriage, and the theme is a dream-pattern of irrational desire in conflict with reality.

本书的另一篇文章将探讨原型批评的细节和实践：而本文仅关注其在整个批评体系中的地位。就其原型层面而言，艺术是文明的一部分，我们将文明定义为从自然中塑造人类形态的过程。这种人类形态在文明的发展过程中逐渐显现：其主要组成部分包括城市、花园、农场、羊圈等等，以及人类社会本身。原型符号通常是具有人类意义的自然物，它构成了一种批判性的艺术观，将艺术视为文明的产物，体现了人类劳动的目标。

Another essay in this book will be concerned with the details and practice of archetypal criticism: here we are concerned only with its place in the context of criticism as a whole. In its archetypal aspect, art is a part of civilization, and civilization we defined as the process of making a human form out of nature. The shape of this human form is revealed by civilization itself as it develops: its major components are the city, the garden, the farm, the sheepfold, and the like, as well as human society itself. An archetypal symbol is usually a natural object with a human meaning, and it forms part of the critical view of art as a civilized product, a vision of the goals of human work.

这种视野必然会理想化文明的某些方面，而嘲讽或忽视其他方面；换言之，艺术的社会语境也是其道德语境。所有艺术家都必须与他们的社群达成和解：许多艺术家，尤其是许多伟大的艺术家，都乐于成为社群的代言人。但就其道德意义而言，诗人会反思并保持一定的距离，关注其社群通过自身努力所取得的真正成就。因此，艺术家的道德观总是认为，他应当通过构建可行的假设来辅助其社会的工作，模仿人类的行为和思想，从而提出二者可实现的模式。如果他没有做到这一点，那么他的假设至少应该被明确地贴上“戏谑”或“奇幻”的标签。马克思主义或多或少地持有这种艺术观，从而重复了《理想国》结尾处的论点。如果我们简单地按照原意来理解，就会发现，根据正义或恰当的社会工作，画家的床是对工匠床的外在模仿。因此，艺术家要么只能反思，要么只能逃避真正的劳动者正在实现的现实世界。

Such a vision is bound to idealize some aspects of civilization and ridicule or ignore others; in other words the social context of art is also the moral context. All artists have to come to terms with their communities: many artists, and many great ones, are content to be the spokesmen of them. But in terms of his moral significance, the poet reflects, and follows at a distance, what his community really achieves through its work. Hence the moral view of the artist is invariably that he ought to assist the work of his society by framing workable hypotheses, imitating human action and thought in such a way as to suggest realizable modes of both. If he does not do this, his hypotheses should at least be clearly labelled as playful or fantastic. Marxism takes more or less this view of art, and thereby repeats the argument reached at the end of the Republic. We are told there, if we follow the argument simply as it stands, that according to justice, or social work properly done, the painter’s bed is an external imitation of the craftsman’s bed. The artist, therefore, is confined either to reflecting or to escaping from the world that the true worker is realizing.

本文采纳了这样一个原则：诗歌的事件和思想分别是历史和论述性写作的假想模仿，而历史和论述性写作本身又是对行动和思想的语言模仿。这一原则使我们接近于将诗歌视为对现实的二次模仿的观点。然而，我们对模仿的解读并非柏拉图式的“回忆”，而是将外在性解放为图像，将自然解放为艺术。从这个角度来看，艺术作品必须是其自身的客体：它不可能最终描述某种事物，也永远不可能最终与任何其他现象、标准、价值或最终原因体系相关联。所有这些外部关系都构成了“意图谬误”。诗歌是道德、真理和美的载体，但诗人的目标并非这些，而仅仅是内在的语言力量。诗人作为诗人，其意图仅仅是创作一首诗，而且通常情况下，并非艺术家本人，而是艺术家内心的自我，才是驱动诗歌创作的主体。他放下正事去做了，跑去追逐这些其他迷人的沼泽精灵。

We have adopted the principle in this essay that the events and ideas of poetry are hypothetical imitations of history and discursive writing respectively, which in their turn are verbal imitations of action and thought. This principle brings us close to the view of poetry as a secondary imitation of reality. We are interpreting mimesis, however, not as a Platonic “recollection” but as an emancipation of externality into image, nature into art. From this point of view the work of art must be its own object: it cannot be ultimately descriptive of something, and can never be ultimately related to any other system of phenomena, standards, values, or final causes. All such external relations form part of the “intentional fallacy.” Poetry is a vehicle for morality, truth, and beauty, but the poet does not aim at these things, but only at inner verbal strength. The poet qua poet intends only to write a poem, and as a rule it is not the artist, but the ego in the artist, who turns away from his proper work to go and chase these other seductive marshlights.

在批评中，一条基本公理是：从道德角度来看，狮子与羔羊可以同床共枕。班扬和罗切斯特、萨德和简·奥斯汀、《磨坊主的故事》和《第二个修女的故事》，都是博雅教育的组成部分，而唯一适用于它们的道德标准就是得体。同样，诗人作品中所体现的道德态度很大程度上源于作品的结构。因此，《无病呻吟》是一部喜剧，这仅仅是阿尔冈的妻子被塑造成伪君子的唯一原因——她必须被除掉，才能使这部剧以圆满结局收尾。

It is an elementary axiom in criticism that morally the lion lies down with the lamb. Bunyan and Rochester, Sade and Jane Austen, The Miller’s Tale and The Second Nun’s Tale, are all equally elements of a liberal education, and the only moral criterion to be applied to them is that of decorum. Similarly, the moral attitude taken by the poet in his work derives largely from the structure of that work. Thus the fact that Le Malade Imaginaire is a comedy is the only reason for making Argan’s wife a hypocrite—she must be got rid of to make the play end happily.

追求美比追求真理或善良更危险，因为它更容易诱使人沉溺于自我。美，如同真理和善良，在某种意义上可以说是所有伟大艺术的特质，但刻意追求美本身只会削弱创造力。艺术中的美如同道德中的幸福：它可以伴随行为，但不能成为行为的目的，正如我们不能“追求幸福”，而只能追求其他能够带来幸福的事物。追求美充其量只能产生吸引人的特质：这种美可以用“可爱”一词来形容，而这种特质取决于对题材和技法的精心选择。例如，宗教画家只有在教堂持续委托创作圣母像的情况下才能创作出这种特质：如果教堂要求他创作耶稣受难像，他就只能描绘残酷和恐怖的景象。

The pursuit of beauty is much more dangerous nonsense than the pursuit of truth or goodness, because it affords a stronger temptation to the ego. Beauty, like truth and goodness, is a quality that may in one sense be predicated of all great art, but the deliberate attempt to beautify can, in itself, only weaken the creative energy. Beauty in art is like happiness in morals: it may accompany the act, but it cannot be the goal of the act, just as one cannot “pursue happiness,” but only something else that may give happiness. Aiming at beauty produces, at best, the attractive: the quality of beauty represented by the word loveliness, a quality which depends on a carefully restricted choice of both subject and technique. A religious painter, for instance, can produce this quality only as long as churches keep commissioning Madonnas: if a church asks for a Crucifixion he must paint cruelty and horror instead.

当我们谈到人体“美丽”时，通常指的是十八到三十岁之间身体状况良好的人。例如，如果德加的画作描绘的是臀部丰满的妇人蹲在浴缸里，我们会将这种对自身审美观念的冲击解读为一种审美判断。然而，一旦“美”这个词被赋予可爱或吸引力的含义——而当它成为艺术的创作目的时，这种含义必然如此——它就变成了一种反动：它试图限制艺术家选择的主题或处理主题的方法，并调动一切伪善的力量，阻止艺术家将视野拓展到枯燥乏味的伪古典主义之外。罗斯金的许多精辟见解都因这种谬误而黯然失色；丁尼生也常常因此削弱了他诗歌的活力；在同一时期一些平庸的美学家身上，我们也能清楚地看到，这种将一切都美化的神经质冲动最终会导致什么后果。这导致了一种对风格的过度崇拜，一种让艺术作品（甚至戏剧）中的所有元素听起来都千篇一律，都像作者本人，而且是作者最令人印象深刻的风格。在这里，虚荣心再次取代了工匠的真诚自豪。

When we speak of the human body as “beautiful,” we usually mean the body of someone in good physical condition between eighteen and about thirty, and if Degas, for example, shows us pictures of thick-bottomed matrons squatting in hip baths, we interpret the shock to our propriety as an aesthetic judgement. Whenever the word beauty means loveliness or attractiveness, as it is bound to do whenever it is made the intention of art, it becomes reactionary: it tries to restrict either what the artist may choose for a subject or the method in which he may choose to treat it, and it marshals all the forces of prudery to keep him from expanding his vision beyond an arid and insipid pseudo-classicism. Ruskin spoiled many of his finest critical insights with this fallacy; Tennyson often hampered the vigor of his poetry by it, and in some of the lesser beauticians of the same period we can see clearly what the neurotic compulsion to beautify everything leads to. It leads to an exaggerated cult of style, a technique of making everything in a work of art, even a drama, sound all alike, and like the author, and like the author at his most impressive. Here again the vanity of the ego has replaced the honest pride of the craftsman.

叙事与意义的形式或第三阶段，尽管涵盖了文学与事件和思想的外部关系，但最终仍将我们带回到艺术作品的审美观，即艺术作品是沉思的对象，是一种为装饰和愉悦而非实用而设计的技艺。这种观点促使我们将审美对象与其他类型的物品区分开来，并假定一种与其它经验截然不同的审美体验。正如书目学观点将文学视为所有已创作的书籍、戏剧和诗歌的总和或集合体一样，我们发现审美批评的观点是一系列独立的、特殊的（有时带有模糊的神圣性）感知。没有理由否认这种文学体验观的有效性；只有当它排斥其他方法时，我们才会反对它。

The formal or third phase of narrative and meaning, although it includes the external relations of literature to events and ideas, nevertheless brings us back ultimately to the aesthetic view of the work of art as an object of contemplation, a techne designed for ornament and pleasure rather than use. This view encourages us to separate aesthetic objects from other kinds of artifacts and to postulate an aesthetic experience different in kind from other experiences. Corresponding to the bibliographical view of literature as the aggregate or pile of all the books and plays and poems that have been written, we find the aesthetic view of criticism as a discrete series of special (sometimes vaguely sacramental) apprehensions. There is no reason for not granting this view of literary experience its own validity; one objects to it only when it excludes other approaches.

文学原型观将文学视为一种整体形式，并将文学体验视为生命连续体的一部分，其中诗人的功能之一便是将人类工作的目标具象化。一旦我们将这种方法与其他三种方法结合起来，文学便成为一种伦理工具，我们便超越了克尔凯郭尔关于审美偶像崇拜与伦理自由之间“非此即彼”的困境，并且在此过程中不会有任何抛弃艺术的倾向。因此，在接受这种文学观的有效性之后，摒弃道德、美和真理等外在目标至关重要。这些目标的外在性使其最终沦为偶像崇拜，因而具有魔性。但是，如果从长远来看，没有任何社会、道德或审美标准能够从外部决定艺术的价值，那么，艺术作为文明一部分的原型阶段就不可能是最终阶段。我们还需要另一个阶段，在这个阶段中，我们可以从文明（诗歌仍然有用且实用）过渡到文化（文化是无私的、自由的，并且能够独立存在）。

The archetypal view of literature shows us literature as a total form and literary experience as a part of the continuum of life, in which one of the poet’s functions is to visualize the goals of human work. As soon as we add this approach to the other three, literature becomes an ethical instrument, and we pass beyond Kierkegaard’s “Either/Or” dilemma between aesthetic idolatry and ethical freedom, without any temptation to dispose of the arts in the process. Hence the importance, after accepting the validity of this view of literature, of rejecting the external goals of morality, beauty, and truth. The fact that they are external makes them ultimately idolatrous, and so demonic. But if no social, moral, or aesthetic standard is in the long run externally determinative of the value of art, it follows that the archetypal phase, in which art is part of civilization, cannot be the ultimate one. We need still another phase where we can pass from civilization, where poetry is still useful and functional, to culture, where it is disinterested and liberal, and stands on its own feet.

拟态阶段：符号即单子

ANAGOGIC PHASE: SYMBOL AS MONAD

在追溯文学象征主义的不同阶段时，我们沿着一条与中世纪批评平行的顺序向上追溯。的确，我们已经为这个词赋予了不同的含义。“字面意义”。这是我们的第二个层面，即描述层面，它对应于中世纪体系中的历史或字面层面，或者至少对应于但丁的版本。我们的第三个层面，即评注和诠释层面，对应于中世纪的第二个层面，即寓言层面。我们的第四个层面，即对神话以及作为社会交流技巧的诗歌的研究，对应于中世纪的第三个层面，即道德和修辞意义层面，它同时关注意义的社会层面和象征层面。中世纪将寓言区分为人们所信（quid credas），将道德区分为人们所行（quid agas），这种区分也体现在我们对形式阶段（审美或思辨）和原型阶段（社会性且是工作连续体的一部分）的理解中。现在，我们必须探究能否在现代找到与中世纪寓言或普遍意义概念相对应的对应物。

In tracing the different phases of literary symbolism, we have been going up a sequence parallel to that of medieval criticism. We have, it is true, established a different meaning for the word “literal.” It is our second or descriptive level that corresponds to the historical or literal one of the medieval scheme, or at any rate of Dante’s version of it. Our third level, the level of commentary and interpretation, is the second or allegorical level of the Middle Ages. Our fourth level, the study of myths, and of poetry as a technique of social communication, is the third medieval level of moral and tropological meaning, concerned at once with the social and the figurative aspect of meaning. The medieval distinction between the allegorical as what one believes (quid credas) and the moral as what one does (quid agas) is also reflected in our conception of the formal phase as aesthetic or speculative and the archetypal phase as social and part of the continuum of work. We have now to see if we can establish a modern parallel to the medieval conception of anagogy or universal meaning.

读者或许已经注意到，我们第一篇文章中提出的五种模式与本文中象征主义的各个阶段之间逐渐形成了一种平行关系。正如我们阐述的，字面意义与象征主义引入的主题反讽技巧以及许多“新”批评家认为诗歌本质上（即字面意义上的）反讽结构的观点密切相关。描述性象征主义在十九世纪的纪实自然主义中展现得最为淋漓尽致，似乎与低级模仿密切相关；而形式象征主义在文艺复兴和新古典主义作家的作品中最为容易研究，则与高级模仿密切相关。原型批评似乎在浪漫主义模式中找到了其重心，因为那时民谣、民间故事和通俗故事的交流最为频繁。如果这种类比成立，那么象征主义的最后一个阶段仍将像前一个阶段一样，关注文学的神话创作方面，但关注的是神话在其更狭义、更技术性的意义上，即与神圣或准神圣的存在和力量相关的虚构故事和主题。

Again, the reader may have noticed a parallelism gradually shaping up between the five modes of our first essay and the phases of symbolism in this one. Literal meaning, as we expounded it, has much to do with the techniques of thematic irony introduced by symbolisme, and with the view of many of the “new” critics that poetry is primarily (i.e., literally) an ironic structure. Descriptive symbolism, shown at its most uncompromising in the documentary naturalism of the nineteenth century, seems to bear a close connection with the low mimetic, and formal symbolism, most easily studied in Renaissance and neo-Classical writers, with the high mimetic. Archetypal criticism seems to find its center of gravity in the mode of romance, when the interchange of ballads, folk tales, and popular stories was at its easiest. If the parallel holds, then, the last phase of symbolism will still be concerned, as the previous one was, with the mythopoeic aspect of literature, but with myth in its narrower and more technical sense of fictions and themes relating to divine or quasi-divine beings and powers.

我们通常将原型和神话与原始文学和通俗文学联系起来。事实上，我们几乎可以这样定义通俗文学——尽管这种定义略显循环论证——即：它能让我们清晰地看到原型。这种特质在各种文学形式中都能找到：童话和民间故事、莎士比亚（尤其是他的大多数喜剧）、《圣经》（即便它不是一部神圣的书籍，也依然会是一本通俗读物）、班扬、理查森、狄更斯、爱伦·坡的作品，当然，还有大量昙花一现的垃圾作品。本书开篇我们便指出……我们不能将流行度与价值直接关联起来。但仍然存在简化文学的危险，或者说，假定文学本质上是原始的、通俗的。这种观点在十九世纪盛行一时，至今仍未消亡，但如果我们采纳它，就会切断原型批评的第三个也是最重要的信息来源。

We have associated archetypes and myths particularly with primitive and popular literature. In fact we could almost define popular literature, admittedly in a rather circular way, as literature which affords an unobstructed view of archetypes. We can find this quality on every level of literature: in fairy tales and folk tales, in Shakespeare (in most of the comedies), in the Bible (which would still be a popular book if it were not a sacred one), in Bunyan, in Richardson, in Dickens, in Poe, and of course in a vast amount of ephemeral rubbish as well. We began this book by remarking that we cannot correlate popularity and value. But there is still the danger of reduction, or assuming that literature is essentially primitive and popular. This view had a great vogue in the nineteenth century, and is by no means dead yet, but if we were to adopt it we should cut off a third and most important source of supply for archetypal criticism.

我们注意到，许多博学深奥、需要耐心研读其作品的作家，实际上都是神话创作者。例如但丁和斯宾塞，而到了二十世纪，几乎所有诗歌和散文领域的“晦涩”作家都属于此类。这类作品，如果是虚构作品，通常建立在朴素戏剧（如《浮士德》和《培尔·金特》）或朴素浪漫故事（如霍桑和梅尔维尔的作品）的基础之上。我们可以将查尔斯·威廉姆斯和C·S·刘易斯等当代作家的复杂寓言与《男孩自述》的套路进行比较。而像亨利·詹姆斯晚期作品和詹姆斯·乔伊斯作品中那样，博学的神话创作可能会变得极其复杂；但这种复杂性旨在揭示而非掩盖神话本身。我们不能想当然地认为，一个原始而流行的神话已经被像木乃伊一样包裹在繁复的文字之中——而这正是简化谬误所导致的。由此看来，博学和精妙的事物，就像原始和流行的事物一样，都趋向于想象体验的中心。

We notice that many learned and recondite writers whose work requires patient study are explicitly mythopoeic writers. Instances include Dante and Spenser, and in the twentieth century embrace nearly all the “difficult” writers in both poetry and prose. Such work, when fictional, is often founded on a basis of naive drama (Faust, Peer Gynt) or naive romance (Hawthorne, Melville: one may compare the sophisticated allegories of Charles Williams and C. S. Lewis in our day, which are largely based on the formulas of the Boy’s Own Paper). Learned mythopoeia, as we have it in the last period of Henry James and in James Joyce, for example, may become bewilderingly complex; but the complexities are designed to reveal and not to disguise the myth. We cannot assume that a primitive and popular myth has been swathed like a mummy in elaborate verbiage, which is the assumption that the fallacy of reduction would lead to. The inference seems to be that the learned and the subtle, like the primitive and the popular, tend toward a center of imaginative experience.

鉴于《维洛那二绅士》是莎士比亚早期的喜剧，《冬天的故事》是晚期作品，学生可能会预期后者更加微妙复杂；他们或许不会想到后者反而更加古老原始，更能让人联想到古代神话和仪式。后者也更受欢迎，当然，这种受欢迎并非指迎合中下阶层观众的口味。莎士比亚在其晚期创作中，通过不断增强戏剧内在形式的表达，最终触及了戏剧的基石——浪漫主义的奇观。所有更为专业的戏剧形式，例如悲剧和社会喜剧，都源于此，并最终回归于此。在但丁和莎士比亚最伟大的作品中，比如《暴风雨》或《炼狱篇》的高潮，我们感受到一种意义汇聚的氛围，一种即将领悟我们整个文学体验真谛的感受，一种进入语言秩序静谧中心的感受。批评即知识，批评本身就是……被迫继续谈论这个话题，意识到词语的顺序有一个中心。

Knowing that The Two Gentlemen of Verona is an early Shakespeare comedy and The Winter’s Tale a late one, the student would expect the later play to be more subtle and complex; he might not expect it to be more archaic and primitive, more suggestive of ancient myths and rituals. The later play is also more popular, though not popular of course in the sense of giving a lower-middle class audience what it thinks it wants. As a result of expressing the inner forms of drama with increasing force and intensity, Shakespeare arrived in his last period at the bedrock of drama, the romantic spectacle out of which all the more specialized forms of drama, such as tragedy and social comedy, have come, and to which they recurrently return. In the greatest moments of Dante and Shakespeare, in, say The Tempest or the climax of the Purgatorio, we have a feeling of converging significance, the feeling that here we are close to seeing what our whole literary experience has been about, the feeling that we have moved into the still center of the order of words. Criticism as knowledge, the criticism which is compelled to keep on talking about the subject, recognizes the fact that there is a center of the order of words.

除非存在这样一个中心，否则由惯例和体裁提供的类比就只能沦为一系列无休止的自由联想，或许具有启发性，甚至引人入胜，但永远无法构建真正的结构。对原型的研究，实际上是对作为整体组成部分的文学符号的研究。如果原型真的存在，那么我们就必须更进一步，设想一个自洽的文学宇宙的可能性。要么原型批评只是虚幻缥缈的幻影，一个没有出口的无尽迷宫；要么我们就必须假定文学是一种整体形式，而不仅仅是现有文学作品总和的名称。我们之前讨论过，神话式的文学观会导致这样一种观念：自然界的秩序整体被相应的语言秩序所模仿。

Unless there is such a center, there is nothing to prevent the analogies supplied by convention and genre from being an endless series of free associations, perhaps suggestive, perhaps even tantalizing, but never creating a real structure. The study of archetypes is the study of literary symbols as parts of a whole. If there are such things as archetypes at all, then, we have to take yet another step, and conceive the possibility of a self-contained literary universe. Either archetypal criticism is a will-o’-the-wisp, an endless labyrinth without an outlet, or we have to assume that literature is a total form, and not simply the name given to the aggregate of existing literary works. We spoke before of the mythical view of literature as leading to the conception of an order of nature as a whole being imitated by a corresponding order of words.

如果原型是可交流的符号，并且存在一个原型中心，那么我们应该期望在这个中心找到一组普遍适用的符号。我并非指存在一本所有人类社会无一例外都熟记于心的原型密码本。我的意思是，有些符号是所有人共通事物的意象，因此具有潜在的无限的交流力量。这类符号包括食物和饮料、探索或旅程、光明与黑暗以及性满足（通常以婚姻的形式出现）的象征。我们不应假定阿多尼斯或俄狄浦斯的神话是普遍适用的，或者某些联想（例如蛇与阳具的象征）是普遍适用的，因为当我们发现一群人对此类事物一无所知时，我们必须假定他们曾经知道但已经遗忘，或者知道但不愿透露，或者他们根本不属于人类。另一方面，如果他们无法理解食物的概念，那么他们很可能被排除在人类之外。因此，任何基于食物的象征意义都具有普遍性，因为它的范围无限广泛。也就是说，它的可理解性没有限制。

If archetypes are communicable symbols, and there is a center of archetypes, we should expect to find, at that center, a group of universal symbols. I do not mean by this phrase that there is any archetypal code book which has been memorized by all human societies without exception. I mean that some symbols are images of things common to all men, and therefore have a communicable power which is potentially unlimited. Such symbols include those of food and drink, of the quest or journey, of light and darkness, and of sexual fulfilment, which would usually take the form of marriage. It is inadvisable to assume that an Adonis or Oedipus myth is universal, or that certain associations, such as the serpent with the phallus, are universal, because when we discover a group of people who know nothing of such matters we must assume that they did know and have forgotten, or do know and won’t tell, or are not members of the human race. On the other hand, they may be confidently excluded from the human race if they cannot understand the conception of food, and so any symbolism founded on food is universal in the sense of having an indefinitely extensive scope. That is, there are no limits to its intelligibility.

在原型阶段，文学作品是一种神话，它将仪式与梦境融合在一起。通过这种方式，它限制了梦境：它使梦境变得合情合理，并被清醒的社会意识所接受。因此，作为文明中的一种道德事实，文学体现了梦境中被称为“审查者”的那种精神。但审查者阻碍了梦境的奔涌。当我们从整体上审视梦境时，会发现它有三点特点。首先，它的界限并非现实，而是可想象的。其次，可想象的界限是愿望圆满、摆脱一切焦虑和挫折的世界。第三，梦境的宇宙完全存在于做梦者的意识之中。

In the archetypal phase the work of literary art is a myth, and unites the ritual and the dream. By doing so it limits the dream: it makes it plausible and acceptable to a social waking consciousness. Thus as a moral fact in civilization, literature embodies a good deal of the spirit which in the dream itself is called the censor. But the censor stands in the way of the impetus of the dream. When we look at the dream as a whole, we notice three things about it. First, its limits are not the real, but the conceivable. Second, the limit of the conceivable is the world of fulfilled desire emancipated from all anxieties and frustrations. Third, the universe of the dream is entirely within the mind of the dreamer.

在寓意阶段，文学模仿人类的全部梦想，从而模仿人类心灵的思考——这种思考处于现实的边缘而非中心。我们在此看到，想象力革命的完成标志着从象征主义的描述阶段过渡到形式阶段的完成。在形式阶段，对自然的模仿从对外部自然的反映转变为以自然为内容的形式组织。但在形式阶段，诗歌仍然被自然所包含；在原型阶段，整个诗歌仍然被包含在自然或似是而非的范畴之内。当我们进入寓意阶段时，自然不再是容器，而是被包含之物；原型普遍象征——城市、花园、探索、婚姻——不再是人类在自然中构建的理想形式，而是自然本身的形式。自然如今存在于无限之人的心灵之中，他用银河系建造自己的城市。这并非现实，而是欲望的可设想或想象的极限，而欲望本身是无限的、永恒的，因此具有末世论的意味。我所说的末世论，主要是指对整个自然界的想象性构想，即它是一个无限永恒的生命体的内容，即使它并非人类，也比无生命体更接近人类。“人的欲望是无限的，”布莱克说，“拥有它也是无限的，它本身也是无限的。”如果有人认为布莱克在这一点上带有偏见，我们可以引用胡克的话：“要证明存在某种高于感官和理智完美的东西，无需其他证据，人类欲望的过程本身就足以证明这一点。欲望是自然的，如果没有某种更高层次的东西能让它最终感到满足，那么它就注定会受挫，而感官和理智的完美是无法做到这一点的。”

In the anagogic phase, literature imitates the total dream of man, and so imitates the thought of a human mind which is at the circumference and not at the center of its reality. We see here the completion of the imaginative revolution begun when we passed from the descriptive to the formal phase of symbolism. There, the imitation of nature shifted from a reflection of external nature to a formal organization of which nature was the content. But in the formal phase the poem is still contained by nature, and in the archetypal phase the whole of poetry is still contained within the limits of the natural, or plausible. When we pass into anagogy, nature becomes, not the container, but the thing contained, and the archetypal universal symbols, the city, the garden, the quest, the marriage, are no longer the desirable forms that man constructs inside nature, but are themselves the forms of nature. Nature is now inside the mind of an infinite man who builds his cities out of the Milky Way. This is not reality, but it is the conceivable or imaginative limit of desire, which is infinite, eternal, and hence apocalyptic. By an apocalypse I mean primarily the imaginative conception of the whole of nature as the content of an infinite and eternal living body which, if not human, is closer to being human than to being inanimate. “The desire of man being infinite,” said Blake, “the possession is infinite and himself infinite.” If Blake is thought a prejudiced witness on this point, we may cite Hooker: “That there is somewhat higher than either of these two (sensual and intellectual perfection), no other proof doth need than the very process of man’s desire, which being natural should be frustrate, if there were not some farther thing wherein it might rest at the length contented, which in the former it cannot do.”

如果我们转向仪式，就会发现其中是对自然的一种模仿，而这种模仿又蕴含着我们称之为魔法的强烈元素。魔法似乎起源于一种自愿的努力，旨在重新建立与自然循环之间失去的联系。这种刻意地重新获得某种已不再拥有之物的意识，是人类仪式的一个显著特征。仪式构建了一套历法，并力求模仿天体运行的精确性和灵敏性。人体及其对植物的反应。农民必须在一年中的特定时间收割庄稼，但正因为无论如何都必须这样做，收割本身并不严格意义上是一种仪式。它是人类在特定时期协调自身与自然能量的意愿的表达，由此产生了我们通常与仪式联系起来的丰收歌谣、丰收祭祀和丰收民俗。但仪式中魔法元素的驱动力显然指向一个宇宙，在这个宇宙中，愚钝而冷漠的自然不再是人类社会的容器，而是被人类社会所容纳，其晴雨完全取决于人类的意愿。正如前文所述，我们也注意到仪式不仅趋向于循环往复，而且趋向于百科全书式的包罗万象。因此，在象征主义阶段，诗歌将人类行为模仿为一种完整的仪式，从而模仿了一个包含自然所有力量的全能人类社会的行为。

If we turn to ritual, we see there an imitation of nature which has a strong element of what we call magic in it. Magic seems to begin as something of a voluntary effort to recapture a lost rapport with the natural cycle. This sense of a deliberate recapturing of something no longer possessed is a distinctive mark of human ritual. Ritual constructs a calendar and endeavors to imitate the precise and sensitive accuracy of the movements of the heavenly bodies and the response of vegetation to them. A farmer must harvest his crop at a certain time of the year, but because he must do this anyway, harvesting itself is not precisely a ritual. It is the expression of a will to synchronize human and natural energies at that time which produces the harvest songs, harvest sacrifices, and harvest folk customs that we associate with ritual. But the impetus of the magical element in ritual is clearly toward a universe in which a stupid and indifferent nature is no longer the container of human society, but is contained by that society, and must rain or shine at the pleasure of man. We notice too the tendency of ritual to become not only cyclical but encyclopaedic, as already noted. In its anagogic phase, then, poetry imitates human action as total ritual, and so imitates the action of an omnipotent human society that contains all the powers of nature within itself.

从寓意学的角度来看，诗歌将完整的仪式（或无限的社会行动）与完整的梦境（或无限的个人思想）结合起来。它的宇宙是无限的、无边无际的假设：它无法被任何现实的文明或道德价值观体系所容纳，正如任何意象结构都无法被限制于单一的寓意解释一样。在此，艺术的“精神”（dianoia）不再是模仿（mimesis logou），而是逻各斯（Logos），即塑造万物的言语，它既是理性，也是（正如歌德的《浮士德》所推测的）实践（praxis）或创造行为。艺术的“精神”（ethos）不再是自然环境中的一群人物，而是一个既是神又是普遍存在的人，或者说是一个以拟人化方式构想的神。

Anagogically, then, poetry unites total ritual, or unlimited social action, with total dream, or unlimited individual thought. Its universe is infinite and boundless hypothesis: it cannot be contained within any actual civilization or set of moral values, for the same reason that no structure of imagery can be restricted to one allegorical interpretation. Here the dianoia of art is no longer a mimesis logou, but the Logos, the shaping word which is both reason and, as Goethe’s Faust speculated, praxis or creative act. The ethos of art is no longer a group of characters within a natural setting, but a universal man who is also a divine being, or a divine being conceived in anthropomorphic terms.

受寓意阶段影响最深的文学形式是经文或启示录。无论是传统神祇、被颂扬的英雄，还是被神化的诗人，神都是诗歌用来传达无限力量（以人性化的形式呈现）的核心意象。许多此类经文本身也是宗教文献，因此是想象与存在主义的混合体。当它们失去存在主义内容时，便纯粹成为想象，正如古典神话在基督教兴起后所发生的那样。当然，它们通常都属于神话或神谱模式。我们也能在诗歌庞大的百科全书式结构中看到与寓意的关联。诗歌本身似乎就是一个完整的世界，在其文化中如同取之不尽的想象力宝库，并且似乎像物理宇宙中的引力或相对论一样，适用于或与文学的各个方面存在着类似的联系。宇宙。这类作品是权威的神话，或是完整的原型体系。它们包括我们在前一篇文章中称之为启示类比的作品：但丁和弥尔顿的史诗，以及其他模式中的对应作品。

The form of literature most deeply influenced by the anagogic phase is the scripture or apocalyptic revelation. The god, whether traditional deity, glorified hero, or apotheosized poet, is the central image that poetry uses in trying to convey the sense of unlimited power in a humanized form. Many of these scriptures are documents of religion as well, and hence are a mixture of the imaginative and the existential. When they lose their existential content they become purely imaginative, as Classical mythology did after the rise of Christianity. They belong in general, of course, to the mythical or theogonic mode. We see the relation to anagogy also in the vast encyclopaedic structure of poetry that seems to be a whole world in itself, that stands in its culture as an inexhaustible storehouse of imaginative suggestion, and seems, like theories of gravitation or relativity in the physical universe, to be applicable to, or have analogous connections with, every part of the literary universe. Such works are definitive myths, or complete organizations of archetypes. They include what in the previous essay we called analogies of revelation: the epics of Dante and Milton and their counterparts in the other modes.

但寓意学的视角并非仅限于那些看似包罗万象的作品，因为寓意学的原则并非仅仅是万物皆可作诗，而是任何事物都可作诗。诗歌无限多样的统一性之感，不仅可显性地源自末世史诗，也可隐性地源自任何诗歌。我们曾说过，只需选取一首传统诗歌，例如《利西达斯》，并追溯其原型在文学中的应用，便可获得完整的博雅教育。因此，文学宇宙的中心便是我们恰巧正在阅读的任何一首诗。更进一步，诗歌便展现为所有文学的缩影，是词语整体秩序的个体显现。由此，从寓意学的角度来看，符号是一个单子，所有符号都融合于一个无限永恒的语言符号之中，它既是智慧（dianoia），即逻各斯（Logos），又是神话（mythos），即完整的创造行为。乔伊斯将这种概念在主题上表达为“顿悟”，而霍普金斯则将其在形式上表达为“内在风景”。

But the anagogic perspective is not to be confined only to works that seem to take in everything, for the principle of anagogy is not simply that everything is the subject of poetry, but that anything may be the subject of a poem. The sense of the infinitely varied unity of poetry may come, not only explicitly from an apocalyptic epic, but implicitly from any poem. We said that we could get a whole liberal education by picking up one conventional poem, Lycidas for example, and following its archetypes through literature. Thus the center of the literary universe is whatever poem we happen to be reading. One step further, and the poem appears as a microcosm of all literature, an individual manifestation of the total order of words. Anagogically, then, the symbol is a monad, all symbols being united in a single infinite and eternal verbal symbol which is, as dianoia, the Logos, and, as mythos, total creative act. It is this conception which Joyce expresses, in terms of subject-matter, as “epiphany,” and Hopkins, in terms of form, as “inscape.”

例如，如果我们从象征学的角度来解读《利西达斯》，就会发现这首挽歌的主题与一位神祇相提并论，这位神祇既象征着夜晚落入西方海洋的太阳，也象征着秋季凋零的植物。在后一个方面，利西达斯就是阿多尼斯或塔穆兹，正如弥尔顿在其他地方所称的，他那“年复一年的伤痕”是地中海宗教仪式哀歌的主题，自忒奥克里托斯以来，这一主题就被融入了田园挽歌中，雪莱的《致多奈斯》的标题就更清晰地表明了这一点。作为诗人，利西达斯的原型是俄耳甫斯，他也英年早逝，与阿多尼斯的角色颇为相似，最终被抛入水中。作为祭司，他的原型是彼得，若非基督的帮助，彼得也会溺死在“加利利湖”上。利西达斯的每一个方面都提出了关于早逝的问题，这个问题与人类的生命、诗歌以及教会息息相关。但所有这些方面都包含在基督的形象之中：这位年轻的、即将死去的、却永远活着的上帝；祂是包含一切诗篇的圣言；祂是教会的头和身体；祂是好牧人，祂的牧养世界永不经历寒冬；祂是永不落下的公义之日，祂的力量能像彼得一样，将吕西达斯从波涛中救起，祂能将灵魂从阴间救赎出来，这是俄耳甫斯未能做到的。基督并非如此。他以一个角色的身份进入这首诗，但他完全渗透到诗的每一行，可以说，这首诗也进入了他的身体。

If we look at Lycidas anagogically, for example, we see that the subject of the elegy has been identified with a god who personifies both the sun that falls into the western ocean at night and the vegetable life that dies in the autumn. In the latter aspect Lycidas is the Adonis or Tammuz whose “annual wound,” as Milton calls it elsewhere, was the subject of a ritual lament in Mediterranean religion, and has been incorporated in the pastoral elegy since Theocritus, as the title of Shelley’s Adonais shows more clearly. As a poet, Lycidas’s archetype is Orpheus, who also died young, in much the same role as Adonis, and was flung into the water. As priest, his archetype is Peter, who would have drowned on the “Galilean lake” without the help of Christ. Each aspect of Lycidas poses the question of premature death as it relates to the life of man, of poetry, and of the Church. But all of these aspects are contained within the figure of Christ, the young dying god who is eternally alive, the Word that contains all poetry, the head and body of the Church, the good Shepherd whose pastoral world sees no winter, the Sun of righteousness that never sets, whose power can raise Lycidas, like Peter, out of the waves, as it redeems souls from the lower world, which Orpheus failed to do. Christ does not enter the poem as a character, but he pervades every line of it so completely that the poem, so to speak, enters him.

寓言式批评通常与宗教直接相关，主要体现在诗人较为自由奔放的言辞中。例如，在艾略特的四重奏中，诗人的文字被置于道成肉身的圣言语境中，便体现了这种批评。里尔克的一封信中对此有更为清晰的阐述，他将诗人的功能比作揭示现实的视角，如同一个天使，包容一切时间和空间，却又双目失明，只能审视自身。里尔克的天使是对更为常见的上帝或基督的变体，而他的论述之所以更具价值，恰恰在于它并非基督教的，而是明确地展现了寓言式视角的独立性，即诗人试图从现实的边缘而非中心发声，以及对任何特定宗教的认同。瓦雷里关于整体智慧的构想也表达或暗示了类似的观点，这种构想在他的泰斯特先生形象中以更为奇幻的方式呈现。叶芝关于永恒虚构的晦涩论述，以及在《塔》和其他作品中关于人作为万物创造者、生命与死亡创造者的论述；乔伊斯对神学术语“顿悟”的非神学式运用；狄兰·托马斯对普世人体的欢欣赞歌。我们不妨顺便指出，我们越能清晰地区分诗歌功能和批评功能，就越容易认真对待伟大作家对其作品的论述。

Anagogic criticism is usually found in direct connection with religion, and is to be discovered chiefly in the more uninhibited utterances of poets themselves. It comes out in those passages of Eliot’s quartets where the words of the poet are placed within the context of the incarnate Word. An even clearer statement is in a letter of Rilke, where he speaks of the function of the poet as revealing a perspective of reality like that of an angel, containing all time and space, who is blind and looking into himself. Rilke’s angel is a modification of the more usual god or Christ, and his statement is all the more valuable because it is explicitly not Christian, and illustrates the independence of the anagogic perspective, of the poet’s attempt to speak from the circumference instead of from the center of reality, from the acceptance of any specific religion. Similar views are expressed or implied in Valéry’s conception of a total intelligence which appears more fancifully in his figure of M. Teste; in Yeats’s cryptic utterances about the artifice of eternity, and, in The Tower and elsewhere, about man as the creator of all creation as well as of both life and death; in Joyce’s non-theological use of the theological term epiphany; in Dylan Thomas’s exultant hymns to a universal human body. We may note in passing that the more sharply we distinguish the poetic and the critical functions, the easier it is for us to take seriously what great writers have said about their work.

因此，这种寓意批评的观点将文学视为存在于其自身宇宙之中，不再是对生活或现实的评论，而是将生活和现实包含在一个语言关系系统中。从这个角度来看，批评家不再能将文学视为俯瞰着难以想象的庞大“生活”的小型艺术宫殿。“生活”对他而言已成为文学的种子地，是大量潜在文学形式的集合，其中只有少数能够成长为更广阔的文学宇宙。所有艺术都存在类似的宇宙。“我们为自己描绘事实的图像，”维特根斯坦说，但他所说的图像指的是代表性的插图，而这些插图并非真正的图像。作为图像的图像本身就是事实，并且只存在于一个图像化的宇宙中。“一切，”马拉美说，“都是为了与一本书有关。”

The anagogic view of criticism thus leads to the conception of literature as existing in its own universe, no longer a commentary on life or reality, but containing life and reality in a system of verbal relationships. From this point of view the critic can no longer think of literature as a tiny palace of art looking out upon an inconceivably gigantic “life.” “Life” for him has become the seed-plot of literature, a vast mass of potential literary forms, only a few of which will grow up into the greater world of the literary universe. Similar universes exist for all the arts. “We make to ourselves pictures of facts,” says Wittgenstein, but by pictures he means representative illustrations, which are not pictures. Pictures as pictures are themselves facts, and exist only in a pictorial universe. “Tout, au monde,” says Mallarmé, “existe pour aboutir à un livre.”

到目前为止，我们一直将符号视为孤立的单元，但是显然，两个符号之间的关系单位（相当于音乐中的乐句）同样重要。从亚里士多德开始，批评家们的论证似乎几乎一致认为，这种关系单位就是隐喻。隐喻的根本形式是对“A是B”类型的同一性的陈述，或者更确切地说，是对其恰当的假设形式的陈述，即“设X为Y”（字母为了音韵和谐而改变）。因此，隐喻背离了通常的描述意义，呈现出一种本质上具有反讽和悖论的结构。在通常的描述意义中，如果A是B，那么B就是A，我们实际上只是说A是它自身。而在隐喻中，两个事物被等同起来，但各自保持着自身的形式。因此，如果我们说“英雄是一头狮子”，我们就把英雄等同于狮子，同时英雄和狮子也都保持着它们自身的形式。文学艺术作品的统一性归功于与……的认同过程，而其多样性、清晰度和强度则归功于对……的认同。

So far we have been dealing with symbols as isolated units, but clearly the unit of relationship between two symbols, corresponding to the phrase in music, is of equal importance. The testimony of critics from Aristotle on seems fairly unanimous that this unit of relationship is the metaphor. And the metaphor, in its radical form, is a statement of identity of the “A is B” type, or rather, putting it into its proper hypothetical form, of the “let X be Y” type (letters altered for euphony). Thus the metaphor turns its back on ordinary descriptive meaning, and presents a structure which literally is ironic and paradoxical. In ordinary descriptive meaning, if A is B then B is A, and all we have really said is that A is itself. In the metaphor two things are identified while each retains its own form. Thus if we say “the hero was a lion” we identify the hero with the lion, while at the same time both the hero and the lion are identified as themselves. A work of literary art owes its unity to this process of identification with, and its variety, clarity, and intensity to identification as.

从字面意义层面来看，隐喻以其字面形式出现，即简单的并置。埃兹拉·庞德在解释隐喻的这一方面时，以汉字为例进行说明。汉字通过将一组元素并置在一起，无需谓语，便能表达复杂的意象。在庞德著名的黑板隐喻示例——两行诗《地铁站》中，人群中的面孔和黑色枝条上的花瓣并置在一起，没有任何谓语将它们连接起来。谓语属于断言和描述意义，而非诗歌的字面结构。

On the literal level of meaning, metaphor appears in its literal shape, which is simple juxtaposition. Ezra Pound, in explaining this aspect of metaphor, uses the illustrative figure of the Chinese ideogram, which expresses a complex image by throwing a group of elements together without predication. In Pound’s famous blackboard example of such a metaphor, the two-line poem “In a Station of the Metro,” the images of the faces in the crowd and the petals on the black bough are juxtaposed with no predicate of any kind connecting them. Predication belongs to assertion and descriptive meaning, not to the literal structure of poetry.

在描述层面，我们可以从语言结构及其所关联的现象两个角度来看待问题。这里的含义是“字面意义上的”，也就是我们之前解释过的，这种字面意义不适用于批评，它要求词语与事实之间没有歧义。因此，从描述的角度来看，所有的隐喻都是明喻。当我们在日常散文中使用隐喻时，我们并非断言A就是B；我们“实际上”是在说A在某些方面与B相似；当我们提取诗歌的描述性或可释义的含义时，情况也是如此。“英雄是一头狮子”，从描述层面来看，就是一个明喻，省略了“像”这个词，目的是为了更生动地表达，并更清楚地表明这种类比仅仅是假设性的。在惠特曼的诗歌《摇篮曲》中，我们看到影子“缠绕扭动，仿佛有生命”，月亮“仿佛泪流满面”。既然没有诗意的理由阻止影子拥有生命或月亮流泪，我们或许可以从谨慎的“仿佛”中看到一种低级模仿性散文意识的运作。

On the descriptive level we have the double perspective of the verbal structure and the phenomena to which it is related. Here meaning is “literal” in the common sense which we explained would not do for criticism, an unambiguous alignment of words and facts. Descriptively, then, all metaphors are similes. When we are writing ordinary discursive prose and use a metaphor, we are not asserting that A is B; we are “really” saying that A is in some respects comparable with B; and similarly when we are extracting the descriptive or paraphrasable meaning of a poem. “The hero was a lion,” then, on the descriptive level, is a simile with the word “like” omitted for greater vividness, and to show more clearly that the analogy is only a hypothetical one. In Whitman’s poem Out of the Cradle Endlessly Rocking, we find shadows “twining and twisting as if they were alive,” and the moon swollen “as if with tears.” As there is no poetic reason why shadows should not be alive or the moon tearful, we may perhaps see in the cautious “as if” the working of a low mimetic discursive prose conscience.

在形式层面，符号是被视为物质或内容的图像或自然现象，而隐喻则是对自然比例的类比。从字面上讲，隐喻是并置；我们简单地说“A；B”。描述性的是“A像B”。但形式上的是“A如同B”。因此，比例类比需要四个项，其中两项有一个共同因素。例如，“英雄是一头狮子”作为一种以自然为内在内容的表达形式，意味着英雄之于人类的勇气，正如狮子之于动物的勇气，而勇气正是第三项和第四项的共同因素。

On the formal level, where symbols are images or natural phenomena conceived as matter or content, the metaphor is an analogy of natural proportion. Literally, metaphor is juxtaposition; we say simply “A; B.” Descriptively, we say “A is (like) B.” But formally we say “A is as B.” An analogy of proportion thus requires four terms, of which two have a common factor. Thus “the hero was a lion” means, as a form of expression which has nature for its internal content, that the hero is to human courage as the lion is to animal courage, courage being the factor common to the third and fourth terms.

原型隐喻中，象征符号构成一个联想群，而隐喻则将两个独立的意象联系起来，每个意象都是某一类别或属的特定代表。但丁《天堂篇》中的玫瑰和叶芝早期抒情诗中的玫瑰分别象征着不同的事物，但它们都代表着所有的玫瑰——当然，指的是所有诗意的玫瑰，而非所有植物学意义上的玫瑰。因此，原型隐喻运用了所谓的具体普遍性，即个体与其所属类别相联系，正如华兹华斯所说的“众生之树”。当然，诗歌中并不存在真正的普遍性，只有诗意的普遍性。亚里士多德在《诗学》中对隐喻的论述也提到了隐喻的这四个方面，尽管有时论述得非常简略和省略。

Archetypally, where the symbol is an associative cluster, the metaphor unites two individual images, each of which is a specific representative of a class or genus. The rose in Dante’s Paradiso and the rose in Yeats’s early lyrics are identified with different things, but both stand for all roses—all poetic roses, of course, not all botanical ones. Archetypal metaphor thus involves the use of what has been called the concrete universal, the individual identified with its class, Wordsworth’s “tree of many one.” Of course there are no real universals in poetry, only poetic ones. All four of these aspects of metaphor are recognized in Aristotle’s discussion of metaphor in the Poetics, though sometimes very briefly and elliptically.

在意义的象征层面，“A即B”这种激进的隐喻形式便得以充分展现。在这里，我们探讨的是诗歌的整体性，在这个整体中，“A即B”的公式可以假设性地应用于任何事物，因为没有任何隐喻，哪怕是“黑即白”，读者可以事先质疑。因此，文学世界是一个万物皆有可能彼此相同的世界。但这并不意味着其中的任何两个事物都是分离且非常相似的，就像豌豆荚里的豌豆一样，或者像我们常说的同卵双胞胎那样，在俚语中被误解。如果双胞胎真的完全相同，他们就应该是同一个人。另一方面，一个成年人会觉得自己与七岁时的自己是同一的，尽管这种身份的两种表现形式——男人和男孩——在相似性或相像性方面几乎没有任何共同之处。在形式、物质、个性、时间和空间方面，男人和男孩截然不同。这是我唯一能想到的能说明识别两个过程的图像类型。独立的形式。因此，所有诗歌的运作方式都如同所有诗歌意象都包含在一个单一的普遍整体之中。同一性与相似性或相像性相反，而完全的同一性并非统一，更非单调，而是各种事物的统一。

In the anagogic aspect of meaning, the radical form of metaphor, “A is B,” comes into its own. Here we are dealing with poetry in its totality, in which the formula “A is B” may be hypothetically applied to anything, for there is no metaphor, not even “black is white,” which a reader has any right to quarrel with in advance. The literary universe, therefore, is a universe in which everything is potentially identical with everything else. This does not mean that any two things in it are separate and very similar, like peas in a pod, or in the slangy and erroneous sense of the word in which we speak of identical twins. If twins were really identical they would be the same person. On the other hand, a grown man feels identical with himself at the age of seven, although the two manifestations of this identity, the man and the boy, have very little in common as regards similarity or likeness. In form, matter, personality, time, and space, man and boy are quite unlike. This is the only type of image I can think of that illustrates the process of identifying two independent forms. All poetry, then, proceeds as though all poetic images were contained within a single universal body. Identity is the opposite of similarity or likeness, and total identity is not uniformity, still less monotony, but a unity of various things.

最后，认同不仅存在于诗歌的结构中，也存在于批评的结构中，至少存在于评注的结构中。诠释既通过隐喻，也通过创造，甚至更为明确地进行。例如，当圣保罗诠释《创世记》中亚伯拉罕妻子的故事时，他说夏甲“就是”阿拉伯的西奈山。柯勒律治说，诗歌是知识的同一性。

Finally, identification belongs not only to the structure of poetry, but to the structure of criticism as well, at least of commentary. Interpretation proceeds by metaphor as well as creation, and even more explicitly. When St. Paul interprets the story of Abraham’s wives in Genesis, for instance, he says that Hagar “is” Mount Sinai in Arabia. Poetry, said Coleridge, is the identity of knowledge.

然而，诗歌的宇宙是一个文学宇宙，而非一个独立的存在宇宙。启示录意味着启示，当艺术具有启示性时，它便会揭示。但它只能按照自身的语境和形式进行揭示：它并不描述或呈现一种独立的启示内容。当诗人与批评家从原型阶段过渡到寓意阶段时，他们便进入了一个只有宗教，或者像宗教那样无限广阔的事物，才能构成其外部目标的阶段。除非诗歌的想象力以哈代和豪斯曼的想象力所受到的独特方式进行自我约束，否则当它被允许只谈论人性和非人性时，就很容易陷入幽闭恐惧；诗人作为宗教的仆人比作为政治的仆人更快乐，因为宗教的超越性和启示性的视角能够极大地解放想象力。如果人们被迫在无神论和迷信之间做出令人沮丧的选择，正如培根很久以前指出的那样，科学家会被迫选择无神论，而诗人则会被迫选择迷信，因为即使是迷信，由于其价值的混乱，也比教条地否定想象力的无限性更能激发他的想象力。但是，无论是最高尚的宗教，还是最粗俗的迷信，对于诗人而言，作为诗人，其存在的意义都如同神灵降临叶芝一般，是为了赋予他诗歌的隐喻。

The universe of poetry, however, is a literary universe, and not a separate existential universe. Apocalypse means revelation, and when art becomes apocalyptic, it reveals. But it reveals only on its own terms, and in its own forms: it does not describe or represent a separate content of revelation. When poet and critic pass from the archetypal to the anagogic phase, they enter a phase of which only religion, or something as infinite in its range as religion, can possibly form an external goal. The poetic imagination, unless it disciplines itself in the particular way in which the imaginations of Hardy and Housman were disciplined, is apt to get claustrophobia when it is allowed to talk only about human nature and subhuman nature; and poets are happier as servants of religion than of politics, because the transcendental and apocalyptic perspective of religion comes as a tremendous emancipation of the imaginative mind. If men were compelled to make the melancholy choice between atheism and superstition, the scientist, as Bacon pointed out long ago, would be compelled to choose atheism, but the poet would be compelled to choose superstition, for even superstition, by its very confusion of values, gives his imagination more scope than a dogmatic denial of imaginative infinity does. But the loftiest religion, no less than the grossest superstition, comes to the poet, qua poet, only as the spirits came to Yeats, to give him metaphors for poetry.

文学研究引导我们把诗歌视为对无限社会行动和无限人类思想的模仿，是对一个包罗万象之人的心灵的模仿，是对包含一切词语的普遍创造性语言的模仿。关于这个人与这个词语，作为批评家，我们在本体论上只能说一件事：我们既没有理由假定它们存在，也没有理由假定它们不存在。如果我们所说的“神圣”指的是无限的或投射的人类，那么我们可以称它们为神圣的。但批评家作为批评家，对于宗教基于这些概念所作出的断言，既无赞同也无反对之分。如果基督教想要将文学世界中无限的“道”与“人”等同于上帝的圣言、基督的位格、历史上的耶稣、圣经或教会教义，那么任何诗人或批评家都可以接受这些等同，而不会损害他们的作品——这种接受甚至可能澄清和深化他们的作品，这取决于他们的性情和处境。但这些等同永远无法被诗歌整体或批评本身所接受。文学批评家如同历史学家一样，不得不以宗教彼此对待的方式来对待每一种宗教，将其视为一种人类的假设，无论他在其他语境中可能持有何种观点。《歌者奥义书》开篇对普世圣言的探讨（其中以神圣的“唵”字为象征）与《第四福音书》开篇的探讨一样，对文学批评而言既相关又无关。柯勒律治认为“逻各斯”是他作为批评家的工作目标，这种想法是正确的；但他认为他的诗歌逻各斯必然会被基督吸收，从而使文学批评成为一种自然神学，这种想法是错误的。

The study of literature takes us toward seeing poetry as the imitation of infinite social action and infinite human thought, the mind of a man who is all men, the universal creative word which is all words. About this man and word we can, speaking as critics, say only one thing ontologically: we have no reason to suppose either that they exist or that they do not exist. We can call them divine if by divine we mean the unlimited or projected human. But the critic, qua critic, has nothing to say for or against the affirmations that a religion makes out of these conceptions. If Christianity wishes to identify the infinite Word and Man of the literary universe with the Word of God, the person of Christ, the historical Jesus, the Bible or church dogma, these identifications may be accepted by any poet or critic without injury to his work—the acceptance may even clarify and intensify his work, depending on his temperament and situation. But they can never be accepted by poetry as a whole, or by criticism as such. The literary critic, like the historian, is compelled to treat every religion in the same way that religions treat each other, as though it were a human hypothesis, whatever else he may in other contexts believe it to be. The discussion of the universal Word at the opening of the Chhandogya Upanishad (where it is symbolized by the sacred word “Aum”) is exactly as relevant and as irrelevant to literary criticism as the discussion at the opening of the Fourth Gospel. Coleridge was right in thinking that the “Logos” was the goal of his work as a critic, but not right in thinking that his poetic Logos would so inevitably be absorbed into Christ as to make literary criticism a kind of natural theology.

批评的“整体逻各斯”本身永远不可能成为信仰的对象或本体论人格。整体道的概念基于这样的假设：存在一种词语秩序，而研究这种秩序的批评本身就具有（或可能具有）完整的意义。亚里士多德的《物理学》引出了在物理宇宙边缘存在一个不动的第一推动者的概念。这本身就意味着物理学本质上拥有一个宇宙。除非所有运动现象都能与统一的原则联系起来，而这些原则又能与一个整体的、统一的运动原则联系起来（这个原则本身并非仅仅是另一种运动现象），否则对运动的系统研究是不可能的。如果神学将亚里士多德的不动推动者等同于创造万物的上帝，那是神学的范畴；物理学作为物理学本身不会受到影响。基督教批评家或许会像中世纪批评家那样，将他们的整体道视为基督的类比，但正如文学本身可以在文化中与任何宗教相伴一样，批评也必须相应地与宗教保持距离。简而言之，文学研究属于“人文学科”，而人文学科，顾名思义，只能从人类的角度看待超人类。

The total Logos of criticism by itself can never become an object of faith or an ontological personality. The conception of a total Word is the postulate that there is such a thing as an order of words, and that the criticism which studies it makes, or could make, complete sense. Aristotle’s Physics leads to the conception of an unmoved first mover at the circumference of the physical universe. This, in itself, means essentially that physics has a universe. The systematic study of motion would be impossible unless all phenomena of motion could be related to unifying principles, and those in their turn to a total unifying principle of movement which is not itself merely another phenomenon of motion. If theology identifies Aristotle’s unmoved mover with a creating God, that is the business of theology; physics as physics will be unaffected by it. Christian critics may see their total Word as an analogy of Christ, as medieval critics did, but as literature itself may be accompanied in culture by any religion, criticism must detach itself accordingly. In short, the study of literature belongs to the “humanities,” and the humanities, as their name indicates, can take only the human view of the superhuman.

寓意概念之间的密切相似性批评与宗教之间的关系，使许多人误以为二者只能通过一种至高无上、另一种从属的方式来关联。选择宗教的人，如柯勒律治，会像他一样，试图将批评转化为一种自然神学；选择文化的人，如阿诺德，则会试图将宗教还原为客观化的文化神话。然而，为了保持二者的纯粹性，必须保障二者的自主性。文化在日常生活与宗教生活之间，构建了一种关于各种可能性的全面视野，并坚持其整体性——因为任何被宗教或国家排除在文化之外的事物，终将以某种方式得到报复。因此，文化对宗教的根本贡献在于摧毁知识上的偶像崇拜，即宗教中反复出现的倾向，即用其对崇拜对象的现有理解和方法来取代崇拜对象本身。正如任何支持宗教或政治教义的论证，若非出于理性的诚实，因而无法保障逻辑的独立性，便毫无价值可言；同样，任何宗教或政治神话，若非假定文化的独立性，亦无价值或有效性。文化的独立性可暂且定义为社会及其传统中所有想象性假设的总和。在我看来，捍卫这种意义上的文化独立性，乃是现代社会中“知识分子”的社会使命：若如此，捍卫文化对任何形式的整体综合（无论是宗教的还是政治的）的服从，便是真正的“知识分子背叛”。

The close resemblance between the conceptions of anagogic criticism and those of religion has led many to assume that they can only be related by making one supreme and the other subordinate. Those who choose religion, like Coleridge, will, like him, try to make criticism a natural theology; those who choose culture, like Arnold, will try to reduce religion to objectified cultural myth. But for the purity of each the autonomy of each must be guaranteed. Culture interposes, between the ordinary and the religious life, a total vision of possibilities, and insists on its totality—for whatever is excluded from culture by religion or state will get its revenge somehow. Thus culture’s essential service to a religion is to destroy intellectual idolatry, the recurrent tendency in religion to replace the object of its worship with its present understanding and forms of approach to that object. Just as no argument in favor of a religious or political doctrine is of any value unless it is an intellectually honest argument, and so guarantees the autonomy of logic, so no religious or political myth is either valuable or valid unless it assumes the autonomy of culture, which may be provisionally defined as the total body of imaginative hypothesis in a society and its tradition. To defend the autonomy of culture in this sense seems to me the social task of the “intellectual” in the modern world: if so, to defend its subordination to a total synthesis of any kind, religious or political, would be the authentic form of the trahison des clercs.

此外，想象文化的本质就在于它超越了自然可能和道德可接受的界限。认为任何以社会本身为目的的人类社会都容不下诗人的论点，即便在上帝的子民中也依然无法反驳。因为宗教也是一种社会制度，就其社会制度而言，它对艺术的限制与马克思主义或柏拉图式的国家并无二致。基督教神学同样是一种革命性的辩证法，是理论与社会实践不可分割的结合。宗教尽管视野开阔，但作为社会制度，它们无法容纳无限假设的艺术。反过来，艺术也必然会释放出讽刺、现实主义、粗俗和幻想的强大力量，试图溶解所有阻碍它们存在的现实束缚。艺术家常常不得不像上帝在《浮士德》中所说的那样，“muss als Teufel schaffen”（必须像魔鬼一样工作），我想这远不止意味着他必须像魔鬼一样工作。宗教之间的“这就是”与诗歌的“但假设这就是”，必然存在某种张力，直到可能与现实在无限处相遇。没有人想要一个完美无缺的诗人，而且，正如诗人自己所说，除了上帝之外，没有人能容忍上帝之城里出现一个捣蛋鬼。

Besides, it is of the essence of imaginative culture that it transcends the limits both of the naturally possible and of the morally acceptable. The argument that there is no room for poets in any human society which is an end in itself remains unanswerable even when the society is the people of God. For religion is also a social institution, and so far as it is one, it imposes limitations on the arts just as a Marxist or Platonic state would do. Christian theology is no less of a revolutionary dialectic, or indissoluble union of theory and social practice. Religions, in spite of their enlarged perspective, cannot as social institutions contain an art of unlimited hypothesis. The arts in their turn cannot help releasing the powerful acids of satire, realism, ribaldry, and fantasy in their attempt to dissolve all the existential concretions that get in their way. The artist often enough has to find that, as God says in Faust, he “muss als Teufel schaffen,” which I suppose means rather more than that he has to work like the devil. Between religion’s “this is” and poetry’s “but suppose this is,” there must always be some kind of tension, until the possible and the actual meet at infinity. Nobody wants a poet in the perfect human state, and, as even the poets tell us, nobody but God himself can tolerate a poltergeist in the City of God.

第三篇论文

：原型批评：神话理论

THIRD ESSAY

Archetypal Criticism: Theory of Myths

第三篇论文

Third Essay

原型批评：神话理论

ARCHETYPAL CRITICISM: THEORY OF MYTHS

介绍

INTRODUCTION

在绘画艺术中，结构和表现两个要素显而易见。一幅画通常是“描绘”某物的：它描绘或阐释一个“主题”，这个主题由类似于感官经验中“物体”的事物构成。与此同时，绘画设计中也存在某些要素：画面所表现的内容被组织成特定的结构模式和惯例，而这些模式和惯例只存在于绘画之中。“内容”和“形式”这两个词经常被用来描述绘画的这些互补方面。“写实主义”强调的是画面所表现的内容；而风格化，无论是原始的还是复杂的，都强调的是画面的结构。极致的写实主义，例如错视画或假象画，几乎是画家在一种强调方式上所能达到的极限；而抽象画，或者更准确地说，非客观绘画，则是他在另一个方向上所能达到的极限。 （“非具象绘画”这个说法在我看来是不合逻辑的，因为绘画本身就是一种再现。）然而，难以捉摸的画家无法摆脱绘画惯例，非具象绘画在亚里士多德的意义上仍然是一种模仿艺术，因此我们可以毫不担心自相矛盾地说，绘画的全部艺术在于绘画的“形式”或结构与绘画的“内容”或主题的结合。

IN THE ART of painting it is easy to see both structural and representational elements. A picture is normally a picture “of” something: it depicts or illustrates a “subject” made up of things analogous to “objects” in sense experience.
