At the same time there are present certain elements of pictorial design: what a picture represents is organized into structural patterns and conventions which are found only in pictures. The words “content” and “form” are often employed to describe these complementary aspects of painting. “Realism” connotes an emphasis on what the picture represents; stylization, whether primitive or sophisticated, connotes an emphasis on pictorial structure. Extreme realism of the illusive or trompe ľœil type is about as far as the painter can go in one kind of emphasis; abstract, or, more strictly, non-objective painting is about as far as he can go in the other direction. (The phrase “non-representational painting” seems to me illogical, a painting being itself a representation.) The illusive painter however cannot escape from pictorial conventions, and non-objective painting is still an imitative art in Aristotle’s sense, and so we may say without much fear of effective contradiction that the whole art of painting lies within a combination of pictorial “form” or structure and pictorial “content” or subject.

不知何故，西方绘画的实践和理论传统都严重制约了模仿或具象表现。即使是古典绘画，我们也继承了一些令人沮丧的故事，比如鸟啄食彩绘葡萄等等，这暗示着希腊画家最大的骄傲在于创作错视画。文艺复兴时期透视画法的发展赋予了这种技巧极高的声望，在二维媒介中营造三维效果本质上就是一种错视画法。现代艺术画廊里的旁听者很容易发现，画家们普遍认为，在作品中达到可辨识的相似度，并将这种相似度作为画面的首要目标，是他们的道德义务。近半个世纪以来，绘画实验运动的怪诞之处在于它反抗具象谬误的暴政。

For some reason the traditions of both practice and theory in Western painting have weighed down heavily on the imitative or representational end. Even from Classical painting we have inherited a number of depressing stories, of birds pecking painted grapes and the like, suggesting that Greek painters took their greatest pride in concocting trompe ľœil puzzles. The development of perspective painting in the Renaissance gave a great prestige to such skills, the suggesting of three dimensions in a two-dimensional medium being essentially a trompe ľœil device. An eavesdropper in a modern art gallery may easily discover the strength and persistence of the feeling that to achieve recognizable likeness in a subject, and to make this likeness the primary thing in his picture, is a moral obligation on the painter. A good deal of the freakishness of experimental movements in painting during the last half-century or so has been due to the energy of its revolt against the tyranny of the representational fallacy.

当然，一位独具匠心的画家深知，当公众要求作品与实物相似时，他们通常想要的恰恰相反，是与他们熟悉的绘画惯例相符的作品。因此，当他打破这些惯例时，他常常会声称自己不过是一只眼睛，他只是如实地描绘他所看到的，等等。他之所以会说这些看似荒谬的话，其动机显而易见：他想表达的是，绘画并非仅仅是简单的装饰，而是需要艰难地克服一些非常现实的空间问题。但即便承认这一点，也并不意味着认同绘画的形式根源在于画外——如果认真对待这种说法，将会摧毁整个艺术。他实际上所做的，是顺从一种隐晦却深刻的冲动，反抗他所处时代的既定惯例，以便在更深的层次上重新发现惯例。通过与巴比松画派决裂，马奈发现了自己与戈雅和委拉斯凯兹更深层次的共鸣；与印象派决裂后，塞尚与夏尔丹和马萨乔产生了更深层次的共鸣。拥有原创性并不能使艺术家特立独行；它反而会促使他更加循规蹈矩，遵循艺术本身的法则——艺术不断地从自身深处重塑自我，它通过天才进行蜕变，也通过平庸之辈进行变异。

An original painter knows, of course, that when the public demands likeness to an object, it generally wants the exact opposite, likeness to the pictorial conventions it is familiar with. Hence when he breaks with these conventions, he is often apt to assert that he is nothing but an eye, that he merely paints what he sees as he sees it, and the like. His motive in talking such nonsense is clear enough: he wishes to say that painting is not merely facile decoration, and involves a difficult conquest of some very real spatial problems. But this may be freely admitted without agreeing that the formal cause of a picture is outside the picture, an assertion which would destroy the whole art if it were taken seriously. What he has actually done is to obey an obscure but profound impulse to revolt against the conventions established in his own day, in order to rediscover convention on a deeper level. By breaking with the Barbizon school, Manet discovered a deeper affinity with Goya and Velasquez; by breaking with the impressionists, Cézanne discovered a deeper affinity with Chardin and Masaccio. The possession of originality cannot make an artist unconventional; it drives him further into convention, obeying the law of the art itself, which seeks constantly to reshape itself from its own depths, and which works through its geniuses for metamorphosis, as it works through minor talents for mutation.

音乐的批评理论与绘画形成了鲜明的对比。当透视法在绘画中被发现时，音乐本可能朝着类似的方向发展，但事实上，具象音乐或“标题音乐”的发展受到了极大的限制。听众或许仍然能从音乐中巧妙模仿的外部声音中获得愉悦，但没有人会因为作曲家未能创作此类模仿作品就断言他是颓废的或江湖骗子。人们也不认为这些模仿比音乐形式本身更重要，更遑论它们构成了音乐形式。因此，音乐的结构原则清晰易懂，甚至可以教给儿童。

Music affords a refreshing contrast to painting in its critical theory. When perspective was discovered in painting, music might well have gone in a similar direction, but in fact the development of representational or “program” music has been severely restricted. Listeners may still derive pleasure from hearing external sounds cleverly imitated in music, but no one asserts that a composer is being a decadent or a charlatan if he fails to produce such imitations. Nor is it believed that these imitations are prior in importance to the forms of music itself, still less that they constitute those forms. The result is that the structural principles of music are clearly understood, and can be taught even to children.

例如，假设本书是一本音乐理论入门读物，而非诗学入门读物。那么我们可以从可听声音的范围内，分离出八度音程，并解释八度音程在理论上被分为十二个部分。等分的半音构成了一个十二音音阶，其中包含了读者通常会听到的所有旋律和和声。然后，我们可以从这个音阶中提炼出两个休止点——大调和小调和弦，并解释二十四个相互交错的调性体系以及调性惯例，即乐曲通常应以同一调开始和结束。我们可以将节奏的基础描述为每两拍或每三拍的重音，以此类推，直至涵盖所有基本节奏。

Suppose, for example, that the present book were an introduction to musical theory instead of poetics. Then we could begin by isolating, from the range of audible sounds, the interval of the octave, and explain that the octave is divided into twelve theoretically equal semitones, forming a scale of twelve notes which contains potentially all the melodies and harmonies that the reader of the book will ordinarily hear. Then we could abstract the two points of repose in this scale, the major and minor common chords, and explain the system of twenty-four interlocking keys and the conventions of tonality which require that a piece should normally open and close in the same key. We could describe the basis of rhythm as an accentuation of every second or every third beat, and so on through the whole list of rudiments.

这样的概述将对1600年至1900年间西方音乐的结构进行理性阐述，并以一种更为灵活但本质上并无二致的形式，涵盖本书读者通常所理解的“音乐”的一切。如果我们愿意，可以在正式开始讨论之前，将所有西方传统之外的音乐都单独禁锢在序言章节中。有人可能会反对说，十二平均律（其中升C和降D是同一个音）是一种人为的虚构。另一个人可能会反对说，作曲家不应该被如此僵化的音乐元素所束缚，音乐的表达方式应该像空气一样自由。第三个人可能会反对说，我们根本就不是在讨论音乐：尽管朱庇特交响曲是C大调，贝多芬第五交响曲是C小调，但解释这两个调之间的区别并不能让任何人真正理解这两部交响曲之间的区别。所有这些反对意见都可以被完全忽略。我们的手册不会给读者提供完整的音乐教育，也不会描述上帝心中的音乐或天使的实践——但它足以达到其目的。

Such an outline would give a rational account of the structure of Western music from 1600 to 1900, and, in a qualified and more flexible but not essentially different form, of everything that the user of the book would be accustomed to call music. If we chose, we could lock up all the music outside the Western tradition in the solitary confinement of a prefatory chapter, before we got down to serious business. Someone might object that the system of equal temperament, in which C# and Db are the same note, is an arbitrary fiction. Another might object that a composer ought not to be tied down to so rigidly conventionalized a set of musical elements, and that the resources of expression in music ought to be as free as the air. A third might object that we are not talking about music at all: that while the Jupiter Symphony is in C major and Beethoven’s Fifth is in C minor, explaining the difference between the two keys will give nobody any real notion of the difference between the two symphonies. All these objectors could be quite safely ignored. Our handbook would not give the reader a complete musical education, nor would it give an account of music as it exists in the mind of God or the practice of angels—but it would do for its purposes.

本书旨在概述文学表达的一些基本语法原理，以及与音乐元素（如调性、简单和复合节奏、卡诺式模仿等）相对应的文学要素。其目的是在古典和基督教传统的背景下，对西方文学的一些结构原则进行理性阐释。我们认为，语言表达的资源（如果可以用这个词的话）受到节奏和调性等文学元素的限制，但这并不意味着，正如音乐中并非如此，语言表达的资源在艺术上是无穷无尽的。毫无疑问，我们会遇到与音乐领域类似的反对者，他们会说：有人认为我们的分类是人为的，无法充分展现文学的多样性，或者与读者自身的阅读体验无关。然而，文学的结构原则究竟是什么，这个问题本身就值得探讨；而且，既然文学是一门语言艺术，那么找到合适的词语来描述它，至少应该像找到音乐中的奏鸣曲或赋格曲这样的词汇一样容易。

In this book we are attempting to outline a few of the grammatical rudiments of literary expression, and the elements of it that correspond to such musical elements as tonality, simple and compound rhythm, canonical imitation, and the like. The aim is to give a rational account of some of the structural principles of Western literature in the context of its Classical and Christian heritage. We are suggesting that the resources of verbal expression are limited, if that is the word, by the literary equivalents of rhythm and key, though that does not mean, any more than it means in music, that its resources are artistically exhaustible. We doubtless have objectors similar to those just imagined for music, saying that our categories are artificial, that they do not do justice to the variety of literature, or that they are not relevant to their own experiences in reading. However, the question of what the structural principles of literature actually are seems important enough to discuss; and, as literature is an art of words, it should be at least as easy to find words to describe them as to find such words as sonata or fugue in music.

在文学领域，如同绘画一样，无论在实践还是理论上，传统上都强调再现或“栩栩如生”。例如，当我们拿起狄更斯的小说时，我们最直接的冲动——一种受我们所了解的所有批评熏陶而养成的习惯——就是将其与“生活”进行比较，无论这种“生活”是我们自己的生活，还是狄更斯同时代人的生活。然后，我们遇到了像希普或奎尔普这样的角色，由于我们和维多利亚时代的人们都从未真正了解过与这些奇特怪物“相似”的事物，这种方法很快就失效了。一些读者会抱怨狄更斯又回到了“纯粹的”漫画式描写（仿佛漫画式描写很容易似的）；而另一些读者则更明智地放弃了栩栩如生的标准，转而欣赏作品本身的魅力。

In literature, as in painting, the traditional emphasis in both practice and theory has been on representation or “lifelikeness.” When, for instance, we pick up a novel of Dickens, our immediate impulse, a habit fostered in us by all the criticism we know, is to compare it with “life,” whether as lived by us or by Dickens’s contemporaries. Then we meet such characters as Heep or Quilp, and, as neither we nor the Victorians have ever known anything much “like” these curious monsters, the method promptly breaks down. Some readers will complain that Dickens has relapsed into “mere” caricature (as though caricature were easy); others, more sensibly, simply give up the criterion of lifelikeness and enjoy the creation for its own sake.

绘画的结构原则常常用平面几何（或者更进一步类比，立体几何）中的对应物来描述。塞尚的一封著名信件谈到绘画形式与球体和立方体的近似，而抽象画家的实践似乎也印证了他的观点。几何形状只是与绘画形式类似，绝非等同；绘画真正的结构原则并非源于与外部事物的类比，而是源于艺术本身的内在类比。同样，文学的结构原则也应源于原型批评和寓意批评，因为只有这两种批评方式才假定文学整体的更广阔语境。但我们在第一篇文章中看到，随着小说模式从神话走向低级模仿和反讽，它们逐渐接近极端的“现实主义”，或者说对生活的再现性。由此可见，神话模式，即讲述神祇故事的模式，其中人物拥有最大的行动力，是所有文学模式中最抽象、最程式化的，正如其他艺术形式（例如拜占庭宗教绘画）中相应的模式在其结构上展现出最高的程式化程度一样。因此，文学的结构原则与神话和比较宗教学密切相关。绘画与几何学之间存在着联系。本文将运用《圣经》的象征意义，以及在较小程度上运用古典神话，作为文学原型的一种语法。

The structural principles of painting are frequently described in terms of their analogues in plane geometry (or solid, by a further reach of analogy). A famous letter of Cézanne speaks of the approximation of pictorial form to the sphere and the cube, and the practice of abstract painters seems to confirm his point. Geometrical shapes are analogous only to pictorial forms, not by any means identical with them; the real structural principles of painting are to be derived, not from an external analogy with something else, but from the internal analogy of the art itself. The structural principles of literature, similarly, are to be derived from archetypal and anagogic criticism, the only kinds that assume a larger context of literature as a whole. But we saw in the first essay that, as the modes of fiction move from the mythical to the low mimetic and ironic, they approach a point of extreme “realism” or representative likeness to life. It follows that the mythical mode, the stories about gods, in which characters have the greatest possible power of action, is the most abstract and conventionalized of all literary modes, just as the corresponding modes in other arts—religious Byzantine painting, for example—show the highest degree of stylization in their structure. Hence the structural principles of literature are as closely related to mythology and comparative religion as those of painting are to geometry. In this essay we shall be using the symbolism of the Bible, and to a lesser extent Classical mythology, as a grammar of literary archetypes.

在埃及传说《两兄弟》中（据信是约瑟传说中波提乏妻子故事的来源），哥哥的妻子试图勾引与他们同住的未婚弟弟，弟弟拒绝后，妻子便指控他企图强奸自己。弟弟被迫逃亡，愤怒的哥哥紧追不舍。到目前为止，这些情节或多或少地反映了现实生活中可信的事实。随后，弟弟向太阳神拉祈求帮助，恳求他伸张正义；拉神在他和哥哥之间设置了一个大湖，并在神力驱使下，湖中充满了鳄鱼。这一情节与之前的任何情节一样，都并非虚构，其逻辑关联也与其他情节并无二致。但它却放弃了与“生活”的直接类比：我们说，这种事只会发生在故事里。因此，埃及传说在其神话般的情节中，获得了一种抽象的文学特质。而且，由于讲故事的人完全可以用更“现实”的方式解决他的小问题，看来埃及文学和其他艺术一样，更倾向于一定程度的风格化。

In the Egyptian tale of The Two Brothers, thought to be the source of the Potiphar’s wife story in the Joseph legend, an elder brother’s wife attempts to seduce an unmarried younger brother who lives with them, and, when he resists her, accuses him of attempting to rape her. The younger brother is then forced to run away, with the enraged elder brother in pursuit. So far, the incidents reproduce more or less credible facts of life. Then the younger brother prays to Ra for assistance, pleading the justice of his cause; Ra places a large lake between him and his brother, and, in a burst of divine exuberance, fills it full of crocodiles. This incident is no more a fictional episode than anything that has preceded it, nor is it less logically related than any other episode to the plot as a whole. But it has given up the external analogy to “life”: this, we say, is the kind of thing that happens only in stories. The Egyptian tale has acquired, then, in its mythical episode, an abstractly literary quality; and, as the story-teller could just as easily have solved his little problem in a more “realistic” way, it appears that literature in Egypt, like the other arts, preferred a certain degree of stylization.

同样，一位头戴巨大装饰光环的中世纪圣人，或许看起来像个老人，但光环这一神话特征，既赋予了画作一种更为抽象的结构，也使圣人呈现出一种只有在绘画中才能见到的形象。在原始社会，神话和民间故事的繁荣发展通常伴随着造型艺术中对几何装饰的偏爱。在我们的传统中，我们重视逼真性，重视对人类经验的巧妙而一致的模仿。偶尔出现的将虚构内容呈现甚至被当作事实的骗局，例如笛福的《瘟疫年代日记》或塞缪尔·巴特勒的《美丽的港湾》，就如同绘画中的错视画法。而在另一个极端，我们则有神话，或者说是抽象的虚构故事，其中神灵和其他类似的生物为所欲为，而实际上，这意味着故事讲述者可以随心所欲。我们在第一篇文章中提到的反讽回归神话的现象，与抽象主义、表现主义、立体主义以及其他类似的绘画流派同时出现，并与之并行发展，这些流派都强调自洽的画面结构。六十年前，萧伯纳强调了易卜生戏剧及其自身作品中主题的社会意义。如今，艾略特先生让我们注意到《鸡尾酒会》中的阿尔刻提斯原型和《机密职员》中的伊翁原型。前者属于马奈和德加的时代；后者属于布拉克和格雷厄姆·萨瑟兰的时代。

Similarly, a medieval saint with a huge decorated halo around his head may look like an old man, but the mythical feature, the halo, both imparts a more abstract structure to the painting and gives the saint the kind of appearance that one sees only in pictures. In primitive societies, a flourishing development in myth and folk tale usually accompanies a taste for geometrical ornament in the plastic arts. In our tradition we have a place for verisimilitude, for human experience skilfully and consistently imitated. The occasional hoaxes in which fiction is presented, or even accepted, as fact, such as Defoe’s Journal of the Plague Year or Samuel Butler’s The Fair Haven, correspond to trompe l’œil illusions in painting. At the other extreme we have myths, or abstract fictional designs in which gods and other such beings do whatever they like, which in practice means whatever the story-teller likes. The return of irony to myth that we noted in the first essay is contemporary with, and parallel to, abstraction, expressionism, cubism, and similar efforts in painting to emphasize the self-contained pictorial structure. Sixty years ago, Bernard Shaw stressed the social significance of the themes in Ibsen’s plays and his own. Today, Mr. Eliot calls our attention to the Alcestis archetype in The Cocktail Party, to the Ion archetype in The Confidential Clerk. The former is of the age of Manet and Degas; the latter of the age of Braque and Graham Sutherland.

因此，我们对原型的研究始于神话世界，一个抽象的或纯粹文学的虚构主题世界，不受对熟悉经验的合理改编准则的影响。就叙事而言，神话是对接近或达到欲望极限的行为的模仿。诸神享受着美丽的女子，以惊人的力量彼此争斗，安慰和帮助人类，或者从他们永恒自由的巅峰俯瞰人类的苦难。神话运作于人类欲望的最高层次，但这并不意味着它必然将自身的世界呈现为人类已经达到或可以达到的。就意义或意象而言，神话是同一个世界，只不过它被视为一个活动领域或场域，同时要牢记我们的原则：诗歌的意义或模式是一种具有概念内涵的意象结构。神话意象的世界通常以宗教中的天堂或乐园的概念来表现，它是末世论的，正如前面解释过的，它是一个完全隐喻的世界，在这个世界里，一切都可能与其他一切相同，仿佛它们都在一个无限的物体之内。

We begin our study of archetypes, then, with a world of myth, an abstract or purely literary world of fictional and thematic design, unaffected by canons of plausible adaptation to familiar experience. In terms of narrative, myth is the imitation of actions near or at the conceivable limits of desire. The gods enjoy beautiful women, fight one another with prodigious strength, comfort and assist man, or else watch his miseries from the height of their immortal freedom. The fact that myth operates at the top level of human desire does not mean that it necessarily presents its world as attained or attainable by human beings. In terms of meaning or dianoia, myth is the same world looked at as an area or field of activity, bearing in mind our principle that the meaning or pattern of poetry is a structure of imagery with conceptual implications. The world of mythical imagery is usually represented by the conception of heaven or Paradise in religion, and it is apocalyptic, in the sense of that word already explained, a world of total metaphor, in which everything is potentially identical with everything else, as though it were all inside a single infinite body.

现实主义，或者说逼真性的艺术，会引发“这和我们所知的多么相似啊！”这样的反应。当文字与已知事物相似时，我们就拥有了一种延伸的或隐含的明喻艺术。正如现实主义是一种隐含明喻的艺术，神话也是一种隐含的隐喻同一性的艺术。“太阳神”一词，用连字符代替谓语，在庞德的术语中是一个纯粹的表意符号，或者在我们看来是一个字面隐喻。在神话中，我们看到文学的结构原则被孤立地呈现出来；在现实主义中，我们看到同样的结构原则（而非相似的原则）融入到一个合情合理的语境中。 （同样，在音乐中，珀塞尔的一首曲子和本杰明·布里顿的一首曲子可能一点也不相似，但如果它们都是D大调，那么它们的调性就相同。）然而，现实主义小说中神话结构的存在，给使其可信带来了一些技术上的难题，而解决这些问题的手段可以统称为“置换”。

Realism, or the art of verisimilitude, evokes the response “How like that is to what we know!” When what is written is like what is known, we have an art of extended or implied simile. And as realism is an art of implicit simile, myth is an art of implicit metaphorical identity. The word “sun-god,” with a hyphen used instead of a predicate, is a pure ideogram, in Pound’s terminology, or literal metaphor, in ours. In myth we see the structural principles of literature isolated; in realism we see the same structural principles (not similar ones) fitting into a context of plausibility. (Similarly in music, a piece by Purcell and a piece by Benjamin Britten may not be in the least like each other, but if they are both in D major their tonality will be the same.) The presence of a mythical structure in realistic fiction, however, poses certain technical problems for making it plausible, and the devices used in solving these problems may be given the general name of displacement.

因此，神话是文学设计的一个极端；自然主义是另一个极端，而介于两者之间的则是整个浪漫主义领域，这里使用“浪漫主义”一词指的并非第一篇文章中的历史模式，而是……正如本文后文所述，这种倾向在于将神话向人性化的方向转移，但与“现实主义”相反，又将内容程式化，使其趋向理想化。这种转移的核心原则是，神话中可以用隐喻来指代的事物，在浪漫故事中只能通过某种形式的明喻来联系：类比、意义深远的联想、偶然出现的意象等等。在神话中，我们可以有太阳神或树神；在浪漫故事中，我们可能会有一个与太阳或树木有着密切联系的人物。而在更现实主义的叙事模式中，这种联系变得不那么重要，更多地成为一种偶然的、甚至是巧合或意外的意象。在圣乔治和珀尔修斯家族的屠龙传说中（下文将对此进行更详细的阐述），一个年老体衰的国王统治下的国家饱受恶龙的蹂躏，恶龙最终索要国王的女儿，但被英雄珀尔修斯所杀。这似乎是对一个关于荒芜之地被丰饶之神复活的神话的一种浪漫化的类比（或许在这个例子中，它还是一个衍生版本）。因此，在神话中，巨龙和老国王被等同起来。事实上，我们可以将这个神话进一步浓缩成一个俄狄浦斯式的幻想故事，其中英雄不是老国王的女婿而是他的儿子，而获救的少女则是英雄的母亲。如果这个故事只是一个私人梦境，这样的等同关系自然而然就会出现。但为了使它成为一个合情合理、对称且符合道德规范的故事，大量的身份转换是必要的，只有在对这类故事进行比较研究之后，其中蕴含的隐喻结构才会逐渐显现。

Myth, then, is one extreme of literary design; naturalism is the other, and in between lies the whole area of romance, using that term to mean, not the historical mode of the first essay, but the tendency, noted later in the same essay, to displace myth in a human direction and yet, in contrast to “realism,” to conventionalize content in an idealized direction. The central principle of displacement is that what can be metaphorically identified in a myth can only be linked in romance by some form of simile: analogy, significant association, incidental accompanying imagery, and the like. In a myth we can have a sun-god or a tree-god; in a romance we may have a person who is significantly associated with the sun or trees. In more realistic modes the association becomes less significant and more a matter of incidental, even coincidental or accidental, imagery. In the dragon-killing legend of the St. George and Perseus family, of which more hereafter, a country under an old feeble king is terrorized by a dragon who eventually demands the king’s daughter, but is slain by the hero. This seems to be a romantic analogy (perhaps also, in this case, a descendant) of a myth of a waste land restored to life by a fertility god. In the myth, then, the dragon and the old king would be identified. We can in fact concentrate the myth still further into an Oedipus fantasy in which the hero is not the old king’s son-in-law but his son, and the rescued damsel the hero’s mother. If the story were a private dream such identifications would be made as a matter of course. But to make it a plausible, symmetrical, and morally acceptable story a good deal of displacement is necessary, and it is only after a comparative study of the story type has been made that the metaphorical structure within it begins to emerge.

在霍桑的《大理石牧神》中，赋予故事标题的雕像与一个名叫多纳泰罗的人物紧密相连，以至于读者除非异常迟钝或粗心，否则不可能忽略多纳泰罗“就是”那尊雕像这一事实。后来，我们遇到了一位名叫希尔达的女孩，她纯洁温柔，住在鸽子环绕的塔楼里。鸽子们非常喜欢她；另一个人物称她为自己的“鸽子”，作者和故事中的人物都曾提到她与鸽子有着某种特殊的亲近感。如果我们说希尔达是像维纳斯一样的鸽子女神，与她的鸽子融为一体，那么我们就不是在准确地解读这个故事，而是把它直接翻译成了神话。但是，承认霍桑在这里与神话的联系如此紧密，也并非不公平。也就是说，我们认识到《大理石牧神》并非典型的低级模仿小说：它主要关注的是既回顾虚构的浪漫故事，又展望未来的……反讽式的神话作家，例如卡夫卡和科克托，在下一个世纪颇具影响力。这种兴趣常被称为寓言，但霍桑本人称之为浪漫主义或许更为恰当。我们可以看出，这种兴趣在人物刻画上趋向抽象，如果我们除了低级的模仿性规范之外别无所知，就会对此抱怨不已。

In Hawthorne’s The Marble Faun the statue which gives the story that name is so insistently associated with a character named Donatello that a reader would have to be unusually dull or inattentive to miss the point that Donatello “is” the statue. Later on we meet a girl named Hilda, of singular purity and gentleness, who lives in a tower surrounded by doves. The doves are very fond of her; another character calls her his “dove,” and remarks indicating some special affinity with doves are made about her by both author and characters. If we were to say that Hilda is a dove-goddess like Venus, identified with her doves, we should not be reading the story quite accurately in its own mode; we should be translating it into straight myth. But to recognize how close Hawthorne is to myth here is not unfair. That is, we recognize that The Marble Faun is not a typical low mimetic fiction: it is dominated by an interest that looks back to fictional romance and forward to the ironic mythical writers of the next century—to Kafka, for instance, or Cocteau. This interest is often called allegory, but probably Hawthorne himself was right in calling it romance. We can see how this interest tends toward abstraction in character-drawing, and if we know no other canons than low mimetic ones, we complain of this.

或者，我们再来看看神话中珀耳塞福涅的故事，她每年有六个月的时间消失在冥界。纯粹的神话显然讲述的是死亡与复活；我们所听到的故事略有不同，但神话模式显而易见。同样的结构元素也经常出现在莎士比亚的喜剧中，在那里它必须被改编到相当高的模仿可信度水平。《无事生非》中的希罗已经死了，甚至有一首葬礼歌曲，而合理的解释被推迟到剧终之后。《辛白林》中的伊莫金使用假名，坟墓空空，但她也得到了一些葬礼仪式。然而，赫敏和珀狄塔的故事与德墨忒尔和珀耳塞福涅的神话如此接近，以至于几乎没有任何严肃的合理解释。赫敏失踪后，曾以鬼魂的形象在梦中出现过一次。她从雕像中复活，这颠覆了皮格马利翁的神话，据说需要信仰的觉醒。然而，从某种程度上来说，她根本就不是雕像，除了无伤大雅的骗局之外，什么也没发生。我们注意到，主题作家比虚构作家更擅长运用抽象的神话手法：例如，斯宾塞笔下的弗洛里梅尔在冬天消失于海底，无人过问，只留下一个“雪人”代替她，并在第四部结尾伴随着春季洪水的爆发而回归。

Or, again, we have, in myth, the story of Proserpine, who disappears into the underworld for six months of every year. The pure myth is clearly one of death and revival; the story as we have it is slightly displaced, but the mythical pattern is easy to see. The same structural element often recurs in Shakespearean comedy, where it has to be adapted to a roughly high mimetic level of credibility. Hero in Much Ado is dead enough to have a funeral song, and plausible explanations are postponed until after the end of the play. Imogen in Cymbeline has an assumed name and an empty grave, but she too gets some funeral obsequies. But the story of Hermione and Perdita is so close to the Demeter and Proserpine myth that hardly any serious pretence of plausible explanations is made. Hermione, after her disappearance, returns once as a ghost in a dream, and her coming to life from a statue, a displacement of the Pygmalion myth, is said to require an awakening of faith, even though, on one level of plausibility, she has not been a statue at all, and nothing has taken place except a harmless deception. We notice how much more abstractly mythical a thematic writer can be than a fictional one: Spenser’s Florimell, for instance, disappears under the sea for the winter with no questions asked, leaving a “snowy lady” in her place and returning with a great outburst of spring floods at the end of the fourth book.

在低级模仿中，我们能看出女主人公死亡与复活的相同结构模式，例如埃丝特·萨默森患上天花，或者洛娜·杜恩在婚礼上被枪杀。但我们越来越接近现实主义的惯例，尽管洛娜的眼神“黯淡无光”，但我们知道，如果作者打算让她复活，那么他指的并非真正的死亡。这里，我们可以将《大理石牧神》与《冬天的故事》进行比较，这部作品中大量描写了雕塑家以及雕像与活人之间的关系，以至于我们几乎期待着类似《冬天的故事》的结局。希尔达神秘失踪，在她失踪期间，她的情人，雕塑家肯扬，从土里挖出了一个……他将这座雕像与希尔达联系起来。之后希尔达回来了，最终为她的缺席找到了一个看似合理的解释，但霍桑本人也发表了一些相当尖锐且任性的评论，大意是他无意编造合理的解释，并希望读者能给他更多创作自由。然而，霍桑的这些顾虑似乎至少部分是他自己设下的，这一点我们可以从爱伦·坡的《丽姬娅》中看出，在《丽姬娅》中，直接的神话死亡与复活模式被毫不掩饰地呈现出来。爱伦·坡显然比霍桑是一位更为激进的抽象主义者，这也是他对我们这个世纪的影响更为直接的原因之一。

In the low mimetic, we recognize the same structural pattern of the death and revival of the heroine when Esther Summerson gets smallpox, or Lorna Doone is shot at her marriage altar. But we are getting closer to the conventions of realism, and although Lorna’s eyes are “dim with death,” we know that the author does not really mean death if he is planning to revive her. Here again it is interesting to compare The Marble Faun, where there is so much about sculptors and the relation of statues to living people that we almost expect some kind of denouement like that of The Winter’s Tale. Hilda mysteriously disappears, and during her absence her lover, the sculptor Kenyon, digs out of the earth a statue that he associates with Hilda. After that Hilda returns, with a plausible reason eventually assigned for her absence, but not without some rather pointed and petulant remarks from Hawthorne himself to the effect that he has no interest in concocting plausible explanations, and that he wishes his reading public would give him a bit more freedom. Yet Hawthorne’s inhibitions seem to be at least in part self-imposed, as we can see if we turn to Poe’s Ligeia, where the straight mythical death and revival pattern is given without apology. Poe is clearly a more radical abstractionist than Hawthorne, which is one reason why his influence on our century is more immediate.

神话与抽象文学之间的这种关联，揭示了小说的诸多方面，尤其体现在那些情节足够现实、合情合理的通俗小说中，而这些小说又足够浪漫，堪称“好故事”，也就是说，它们都经过精心构思。例如，引入预兆或征兆，或者将整个故事作为对开篇预言的实现，便是这种手法的体现。这种手法在其存在主义层面上，暗示着一种无法逃避的命运或某种隐藏的全能意志。实际上，这是一种纯粹的文学设计，它使开头与结尾形成某种对称关系，而其中唯一不可抗拒的意志，便是作者自身的意志。因此，我们常常能在那些天性并不热衷于预兆的作家身上发现这种手法。例如，在《安娜·卡列尼娜》中，开篇铁路搬运工的死被安娜视为她自身的预兆。同样地，如果我们在索福克勒斯的作品中发现预兆和征兆，那主要是因为它们符合他创作的戏剧悲剧的结构，并不能证明剧作家或观众对命运持有任何明确的信念。

This affinity between the mythical and the abstractly literary illuminates many aspects of fiction, especially the more popular fiction which is realistic enough to be plausible in its incidents and yet romantic enough to be a “good story,” which means a clearly designed one. The introduction of an omen or portent, or the device of making a whole story the fulfilment of a prophecy given at the beginning, is an example. Such a device suggests, in its existential projection, a conception of ineluctable fate or hidden omnipotent will. Actually, it is a piece of pure literary design, giving the beginning some symmetrical relationship with the end, and the only ineluctable will involved is that of the author. Hence we often find it even in writers not temperamentally much in sympathy with the portentous. In Anna Karenina, for instance, the death of the railway porter in the opening book is accepted by Anna as an omen for herself. Similarly, if we find portents and omens in Sophocles, they are there primarily because they fit the structure of his type of dramatic tragedy, and prove nothing about any clear-cut beliefs in fate held by either dramatist or audience.

因此，文学中神话和原型符号的组织形式可分为三种。第一种是未移位的神话，通常与神或恶魔有关，其形式为两个完全隐喻化的对比世界，一个是理想的，另一个是不理想的。这些世界通常与同时期宗教中存在的天堂和地狱相对应。我们将这两种隐喻组织形式分别称为末世论和恶魔论。第二种是我们称之为浪漫主义的普遍倾向，即在一个更紧密相关的世界中暗示隐含的神话模式。第三，我们倾向于“现实主义”（我对这个蹩脚的词的反感体现在引号里），它更注重内容和表现形式，而非故事的结构。反讽文学始于现实主义，并趋向神话，其神话模式通常更倾向于暗示恶魔而非末日，尽管有时它只是延续了浪漫主义的风格化传统。霍桑、爱伦·坡、康拉德、哈代和弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫都是例证。

We have, then, three organizations of myths and archetypal symbols in literature. First, there is undisplaced myth, generally concerned with gods or demons, and which takes the form of two contrasting worlds of total metaphorical identification, one desirable and the other undesirable. These worlds are often identified with the existential heavens and hells of the religions contemporary with such literature. These two forms of metaphorical organization we call the apocalyptic and the demonic respectively. Second, we have the general tendency we have called romantic, the tendency to suggest implicit mythical patterns in a world more closely associated with human experience. Third, we have the tendency of “realism” (my distaste for this inept term is reflected in the quotation marks) to throw the emphasis on content and representation rather than on the shape of the story. Ironic literature begins with realism and tends toward myth, its mythical patterns being as a rule more suggestive of the demonic than of the apocalyptic, though sometimes it simply continues the romantic tradition of stylization. Hawthorne, Poe, Conrad, Hardy and Virginia Woolf all provide examples.

欣赏一幅画作时，我们或许会近距离观察，分析笔触和调色刀的细节。这大致相当于文学批评中新批评家的修辞分析。稍稍拉开距离，构图便清晰可见，我们更多地关注画面所呈现的内容：例如，对于写实的荷兰画作而言，这是最佳的观赏距离，因为我们某种程度上是在“阅读”这幅画。距离越远，我们越能意识到构图的组织结构。比如，从远处观看一幅圣母像，我们看到的只是圣母的原型——一个巨大的向心蓝色色块，中心有一个对比鲜明的焦点。在文学批评中，我们也常常需要“退后一步”，才能看清诗歌的原型结构。如果我们“退后一步”观看斯宾塞的《变幻之歌》，会看到有序的圆形光影背景，以及一个阴森的黑色色块从低处凸显出来——这与《约伯记》开篇的原型形状极为相似。如果我们从《哈姆雷特》第五幕的开头“退后一步” ，我们会看到舞台上出现一个坟墓的开口，主人公、他的敌人和女主人公进入其中，随后在上层世界展开一场生死搏斗。如果我们从托尔斯泰的《复活》或左拉的《萌芽》这样的现实主义小说中“退后一步” ，我们也能看到这些标题所暗示的神话意象。下文将列举更多例子。

In looking at a picture, we may stand close to it and analyze the details of brush work and palette knife. This corresponds roughly to the rhetorical analysis of the new critics in literature. At a little distance back, the design comes into clearer view, and we study rather the content represented: this is the best distance for realistic Dutch pictures, for example, where we are in a sense reading the picture. The further back we go, the more conscious we are of the organizing design. At a great distance from, say, a Madonna, we can see nothing but the archetype of the Madonna, a large centripetal blue mass with a contrasting point of interest at its center. In the criticism of literature, too, we often have to “stand back” from the poem to see its archetypal organization. If we “stand back” from Spenser’s Mutabilitie Cantoes, we see a background of ordered circular light and a sinister black mass thrusting up into the lower foreground—much the same archetypal shape that we see in the opening of the Book of Job. If we “stand back” from the beginning of the fifth act of Hamlet, we see a grave opening on the stage, the hero, his enemy, and the heroine descending into it, followed by a fatal struggle in the upper world. If we “stand back” from a realistic novel such as Tolstoy’s Resurrection or Zola’s Germinal, we can see the mythopoeic designs indicated by those titles. Other examples will be given in what follows.

我们首先阐述两个未曾改变的世界——末世和魔界——的意象结构（或称“dianoia”），并大量借鉴《圣经》——我们传统中未曾改变的神话的主要来源。然后，我们探讨两种中间意象结构，最后论述作为这些意象结构动态表现的通用叙事（或称“mythoi”） 。

We proceed to give an account first of the structure of imagery, or dianoia, of the two undisplaced worlds, the apocalyptic and the demonic, drawing heavily on the Bible, the main source for undisplaced myth in our tradition. Then we go on to the two intermediate structures of imagery, and finally to the generic narratives or mythoi which are these structures of imagery in movement.

原型意义理论（1）：末世意象

THEORY OF ARCHETYPAL MEANING (1): APOCALYPTIC IMAGERY

让我们按照“二十问”游戏的总体方案进行，或者，如果我们愿意的话，按照“存在之链”的总体方案进行，这是对感官数据进行分类的传统方案。

Let us proceed according to the general scheme of the game of Twenty Questions, or, if we prefer, of the Great Chain of Being, the traditional scheme for classifying sense data.

末世世界，即宗教中的天堂，首先呈现的是人类欲望形式的现实范畴，这些范畴体现在人类文明活动所塑造的形态之中。例如，人类劳动和欲望赋予植物世界的形式，便是花园、农场、树林或公园。人类对动物世界的形式，便是家畜的世界，其中绵羊在古典和基督教的隐喻中都占据着传统的优先地位。人类对矿物世界的形式，即人类劳动将石头转化为的形式，便是城市。城市、花园和羊圈是《圣经》和大多数基督教象征体系的组织性隐喻，它们在被明确称为《启示录》或《启示录》的书中得到了完整的隐喻统一。这本书经过精心设计，旨在为整本《圣经》构建一个浑然一体的神话式结论。从我们的角度来看，这意味着《圣经启示录》是我们理解末世意象的语法。

The apocalyptic world, the heaven of religion, presents, in the first place, the categories of reality in the forms of human desire, as indicated by the forms they assume under the work of human civilization. The form imposed by human work and desire on the vegetable world, for instance, is that of the garden, the farm, the grove, or the park. The human form of the animal world is a world of domesticated animals, of which the sheep has a traditional priority in both Classical and Christian metaphor. The human form of the mineral world, the form into which human work transforms stone, is the city. The city, the garden, and the sheepfold are the organizing metaphors of the Bible and of most Christian symbolism, and they are brought into complete metaphorical identification in the book explicitly called the Apocalypse or Revelation, which has been carefully designed to form an undisplaced mythical conclusion for the Bible as a whole. From our point of view this means that the Biblical Apocalypse is our grammar of apocalyptic imagery.

根据前文所述的原型隐喻原则（我们记得这是具体的普遍概念），城市、花园和羊圈这三个类别彼此相同，并且与其中的每一个个体也相同。因此，神圣世界和人间世界同样与羊圈、城市和花园相同，它们各自的社会层面和个体层面也相同。由此可见，圣经中的末世世界呈现出以下模式：

Each of these three categories, the city, the garden, and the sheepfold, is, by the principle of archetypal metaphor dealt with in the previous essay, and which we remember is the concrete universal, identical with the others and with each individual within it. Hence the divine and human worlds are, similarly, identical with the sheepfold, city and garden, and the social and individual aspects of each are identical. Thus the apocalyptic world of the Bible presents the following pattern:

“基督”这一概念将所有这些范畴统一起来：基督既是唯一的神，也是唯一的人；既是神的羔羊，又是生命树或葡萄树（我们是枝子），又是那块石头。建造者们弃置了原先的圣殿，而重建的圣殿则与他复活的身体完全一致。宗教意义上的和诗歌意义上的这两种象征意义仅在于意图不同，前者是存在性的，后者是隐喻性的。在中世纪批评中，这种区别并不重要，“ figura ”一词，当用于指代某个象征与基督的关联时，通常同时包含这两种含义。

The conception “Christ” unites all these categories in identity: Christ is both the one God and the one Man, the Lamb of God, the tree of life, or vine of which we are the branches, the stone which the builders rejected, and the rebuilt temple which is identical with his risen body. The religious and poetic identifications differ in intention only, the former being existential and the latter metaphorical. In medieval criticism the difference was of little importance, and the word “figura,” as applied to the identification of a symbol with Christ, usually implies both kinds.

现在让我们稍微扩展一下这个模式。在基督教中，具体的普遍概念以三位一体的形式应用于神圣世界。基督教坚持认为，无论常规思维过程如何错位，上帝都是三个位格，却又是一位上帝。位格和实体的概念体现了将隐喻延伸到逻辑时遇到的一些困难。当然，在纯粹的隐喻中，上帝的合一可以很容易地适用于五个、十七个甚至一百万个神圣位格，就像适用于三个位格一样。我们甚至可以在三位一体之外的诗歌中找到神圣的具体普遍概念。当宙斯在《伊利亚特》第八卷开头说道，他可以随时将整个存在链拉回自身时，我们可以看出，对于荷马来说，奥林匹斯山存在某种双重视角的概念，一群争吵不休的神祇可以随时突然融合为一个单一的神圣意志。在维吉尔的作品中，我们首先看到的是一个心怀恶意、骄纵任性的朱诺，但几行之后埃涅阿斯对他的部下说的“上帝也曾如此惩罚他”表明，埃涅阿斯也存在类似的双重视角。我们或许可以将其与《约伯记》进行比较，约伯和他的朋友们过于虔诚，以至于他们根本无法想象约伯会因为上帝和撒旦之间半开玩笑的打赌而遭受如此苦难。从某种意义上说，他们的想法是对的，而书中关于撒旦在天堂的信息则是错误的。撒旦在诗歌的结尾被删去了，无论造成这种变化的原因是什么，我们仍然很难理解约伯最终的顿悟是如何从单一神圣意志的概念完全回归到开篇场景的氛围的。

Now let us expand this pattern a little. In Christianity the concrete universal is applied to the divine world in the form of the Trinity. Christianity insists that, whatever dislocations of customary mental processes may be involved, God is three persons and yet one God. The conceptions of person and substance represent a few of the difficulties in extending metaphor to logic. In pure metaphor, of course, the unity of God could apply to five or seventeen or a million divine persons as easily as three, and we may find the divine concrete universal in poetry outside the Trinitarian orbit. When Zeus remarks, at the beginning of the eighth book of the Iliad, that he can pull the whole chain of being up into himself whenever he likes, we can see that for Homer there was some conception of a double perspective in Olympus, where a group of squabbling deities may at any time suddenly compose into the form of a single divine will. In Virgil we first meet a malicious and spoiled Juno, but the comment of Aeneas to his men a few lines later on, “deus dabit his quoque finem,” indicates that a similar double perspective existed for him. We may compare perhaps the Book of Job, where Job and his friends are much too devout for it ever to occur to them that Job could have suffered so as a result of a half-jocular bet between God and Satan. There is a sense in which they are right, and the information given to the reader about Satan in heaven wrong. Satan is dropped out of the end of the poem, and whatever rewritings may be responsible for this, it is still difficult to see how the final enlightenment of Job could ever have returned completely from the conception of a single divine will to the mood of the opening scene.

至于人类社会，我们同属一个整体的隐喻贯穿了从柏拉图到我们今天的绝大多数政治理论。弥尔顿的“一个国家应当像一个巨大的基督教人物，一个雄伟壮丽、正直无私的人”正是这一隐喻的基督教化版本。在这个版本中，如同三位一体教义一样，“基督既是神又是人”的完整隐喻表述是正统的，而阿里乌斯派和幻影论派则持相反观点。以明喻或相似性来表述的论述被视为异端邪说。霍布斯的《利维坦》也与这种类比手法有所关联，其原版扉页描绘了众多小人儿栖身于一个巨人的体内。柏拉图的《理想国》同样建立在这种比喻之上，书中将个人的理性、意志和欲望分别比作哲人王、卫兵和工匠。事实上，我们至今在谈论一群人或一个整体时，仍然会使用这种比喻。

As for human society, the metaphor that we are all members of one body has organized most political theory from Plato to our own day. Milton’s “A Commonwealth ought to be but as one huge Christian personage, one mighty growth, and stature of an honest man” belongs to a Christianized version of this metaphor, in which, as in the doctrine of the Trinity, the full metaphorical statement “Christ is God and Man” is orthodox, and the Arian and Docetic statements in terms of simile or likeness condemned as heretical. Hobbes’s Leviathan, with its original frontispiece depicting a number of mannikins inside the body of a single giant, has also some connection with the same type of identification. Plato’s Republic, in which the reason, will, and desire of the individual appear as the philosopher-king, guards, and artisans of the state, is also founded on this metaphor, which in fact we still use whenever we speak of a group or aggregate of human beings as a “body.”

当然，在性象征中，运用“一体”这一隐喻——两个身体因爱而合二为一——仍然更为简便。约翰·邓恩的《狂喜》便是众多以此意象为核心的诗歌之一，而莎士比亚的《凤凰与斑鸠》则巧妙地展现了这种身份认同对“理性”造成的冲击。忠诚、英雄崇拜、忠实追随者等主题也同样运用了这一隐喻。

In sexual symbolism, of course, it is still easier to employ the “one flesh” metaphor of two bodies made into the same body by love. Donne’s The Extasie is one of the many poems organized on this image, and Shakespeare’s Phoenix and the Turtle makes great play with the outrage done to the “reason” by such identity. Themes of loyalty, hero-worship, faithful followers, and the like also employ the same metaphor.

在基督教的圣餐变体论中，动物世界和植物世界彼此等同，也与神圣世界和人类世界等同。植物世界的基本人性形式——食物和饮料、收成和葡萄、面包和葡萄酒——象征着羔羊的身体和血，而羔羊既是人又是神，我们如同在城邦或圣殿中一般，存在于祂的身体之中。正统教义在此再次强调隐喻而非明喻，而实体概念也再次展现了逻辑在理解隐喻时所面临的挑战。从《法律篇》的开篇可以清楚地看出，柏拉图认为宴饮也具有类似的共融象征意义。很难找到比圣餐更简单、更生动的人类文明意象，它展现了人类试图将自然融入自身（社会）身体的尝试。

The animal and vegetable worlds are identified with each other, and with the divine and human worlds as well, in the Christian doctrine of transubstantiation, in which the essential human forms of the vegetable world, food and drink, the harvest and the vintage, the bread and the wine, are the body and blood of the Lamb who is also Man and God, and in whose body we exist as in a city or temple. Here again the orthodox doctrine insists on metaphor as against simile, and here again the conception of substance illustrates the struggles of logic to digest the metaphor. It is clear from the opening of the Laws that the symposium had something of the same communion symbolism for Plato. It would be hard to find a simpler or more vivid image of human civilization, where man attempts to surround nature and put it inside his (social) body, than the sacramental meal.

在动物世界中，绵羊所受到的传统尊崇为我们提供了田园意象的核心原型，也为宗教中的“牧羊人”和“羊群”等隐喻提供了基础。国王如同牧羊人一般的隐喻可以追溯到古埃及。或许，这种特殊习俗的运用源于绵羊愚钝、温顺、群居且易受惊吓，它们组成的社会与人类社会最为相似。当然，在诗歌中，如果诗人的读者有所准备，任何其他动物都可以作为象征：例如，在《广林奥义书》的开篇，祭祀用的马——其身躯蕴含着整个宇宙——就如同基督教诗人一般被赋予了象征意义。会如何对待上帝的羔羊？在鸟类中，鸽子历来象征着普世的和谐或爱，既代表着金星，也代表着基督教的圣灵。将神灵与动物或植物等同起来，再将动物或植物与人类社会等同起来，构成了图腾象征主义的基础。某些起源民间故事，讲述超自然生物如何变成我们所知的动植物，代表了同一种隐喻的简化形式，并以奥维德笔下为人熟知的“变形”原型流传至今。

The conventional honors accorded the sheep in the animal world provide us with the central archetype of pastoral imagery, as well as with such metaphors as “pastor” and “flock” in religion. The metaphor of the king as the shepherd of his people goes back to ancient Egypt. Perhaps the use of this particular convention is due to the fact that, being stupid, affectionate, gregarious, and easily stampeded, the societies formed by sheep are most like human ones. But of course in poetry any other animal would do as well if the poet’s audience were prepared for it: at the opening of the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, for instance, the sacrificial horse, whose body contains the whole universe, is treated in the same way that a Christian poet would treat the Lamb of God. Of birds, too, the dove has traditionally represented the universal concord or love both of Venus and of the Christian Holy Spirit. Identifications of gods with animals or plants and of those again with human society form the basis of totemic symbolism. Certain types of etiological folk tale, the stories of how supernatural beings were turned into the animals and plants that we know, represent an attentuated form of the same type of metaphor, and survive as the “metamorphosis” archetype familiar from Ovid.

类似的灵活性也体现在植物意象上。在《圣经》的其他篇章中，生命树的叶子或果实被用作圣餐的象征，代替了面包和葡萄酒。或者，具体的普世意义不仅可以应用于树木，还可以应用于单个果实或花朵。在西方，玫瑰在末世花卉中享有传统上的地位：人们很容易想到《天堂篇》中玫瑰作为圣餐象征的用法；在《仙后》第一卷中，圣乔治的徽章——白底红十字——不仅与基督复活的身体及其伴随的圣礼象征意义相关，还与都铎王朝红白玫瑰的结合有关。在东方，莲花或中国的“金莲花”常常取代玫瑰的位置，而在德国浪漫主义时期，矢车菊也曾短暂流行。

Similar flexibility is possible with vegetable images. Elsewhere in the Bible the leaves or fruit of the tree of life are used as communion symbols in place of the bread and wine. Or the concrete universal may be applied not simply to a tree but to a single fruit or flower. In the West the rose has a traditional priority among apocalyptic flowers: the use of the rose as a communion symbol in the Paradiso comes readily to mind, and in the first book of The Faerie Queene the emblem of St. George, a red cross on a white ground, is connected not only with the risen body of Christ and the sacramental symbolism which accompanies it, but with the union of the red and white roses in the Tudor dynasty. In the East the lotus or the Chinese “golden flower” often occupied the place of the rose, and in German Romanticism the blue cornflower enjoyed a brief vogue.

人体与植物世界的同一性为我们提供了田园意象的原型，例如马维尔笔下的绿色世界、莎士比亚的森林喜剧、罗宾汉以及其他潜伏在浪漫森林中的绿人——后者在浪漫主义中对应着树神的隐喻神话。在马维尔的《花园》中，我们看到了这种概念的进一步延伸，即人类灵魂与栖息在生命之树枝头的鸟儿相提并论，尽管这种延伸仍然属于传统范畴。橄榄树及其橄榄油则为“受膏者”君主提供了另一种象征意义。

The identity of the human body and the vegetable world gives us the archetype of Arcadian imagery, of Marvell’s green world, of Shakespeare’s forest comedies, of the world of Robin Hood and other green men who lurk in the forests of romance, these last the counterparts in romance of the metaphorical myth of the tree-god. In Marvell’s The Garden we meet a further but still conventional extension in the identification of the human soul with a bird sitting in the branches of the tree of life. The olive tree and its oil has supplied another identification in the “anointed” ruler.

这座城市，无论是否被称为耶路撒冷，在末世论意义上都等同于一座单一的建筑或圣殿，一座“多居所的房屋”，其中的个体如同“活石”，借用新约圣经中的另一句话。人类对无机世界的利用既包括公路或道路，也包括拥有街道的城市，“道路”这一隐喻与所有探索文学密不可分，无论其是否像《天路历程》那样明确地带有基督教色彩。几何和建筑意象也包含在内：但丁和叶芝的塔和螺旋楼梯、雅各布的天梯、新柏拉图主义爱情诗人的天梯、上升的螺旋或丰饶角、忽必烈汗颁布的“庄严的享乐穹顶”、布朗在艺术和自然界的各个角落寻找的十字和梅花图案、作为永恒象征的圆形、沃恩的“纯净无尽的光环”等等。

The city, whether called Jerusalem or not, is apocalyptically identical with a single building or temple, a “house of many mansions,” of which individuals are “lively stones,” to use another New Testament phrase. The human use of the inorganic world involves the highway or road as well as the city with its streets, and the metaphor of the “way” is inseparable from all quest-literature, whether explicitly Christian as in The Pilgrim’s Progress or not. To this category also belong geometrical and architectural images: the tower and the winding stairway of Dante and Yeats, Jacob’s ladder, the ladder of the Neo-platonic love poets, the ascending spiral or cornucopia, the “stately pleasure dome” that Kubla Khan decreed, the cross and quincunx patterns which Browne sought in every corner of art and nature, the circle as the emblem of eternity, Vaughan’s “ring of pure and endless light,” and so on.

在原型层面，诗歌是人类文明的产物，自然是人类的容器。在启示层面，人类是自然的容器，其城市和花园不再是地球表面的小小凹陷，而是人类宇宙的形态。因此，在末世象征主义中，我们不能将人类局限于土和气这两种自然元素，象征主义在从一个层面过渡到另一个层面时，必须像《魔笛》中的塔米诺一样，经历水与火的考验。诗歌象征主义通常将火置于人类今世生活的之上，将水置于其之下。但丁必须穿越火环和伊甸河，才能从炼狱山（它仍然位于我们这个世界的表面）到达天堂或真正的末世世界。圣经中天使周围环绕着光与火的意象，五旬节降临的火焰，以及撒拉弗将火炭涂抹在以赛亚的口中，都将火与介于人与神之间的灵界或天使世界联系起来。在古典神话中，普罗米修斯的故事也暗示了火的类似起源，宙斯与雷霆或闪电之火的关联也印证了这一点。简而言之，天空，即包含太阳、月亮和星辰等炽热天体的天空，通常被认为是通往末世天堂的通道，或者等同于末世神话中的天堂。

On the archetypal level proper, where poetry is an artifact of human civilization, nature is the container of man. On the anagogic level, man is the container of nature, and his cities and gardens are no longer little hollowings on the surface of the earth, but the forms of a human universe. Hence in apocalyptic symbolism we cannot confine man only to his two natural elements of earth and air, and, in going from one level to the other, symbolism must, like Tamino in The Magic Flute, pass the ordeals of water and fire. Poetic symbolism usually puts fire just above man’s life in this world, and water just below it. Dante had to pass through a ring of fire and the river of Eden to go from the mountain of purgatory, which is still on the surface of our own world, to Paradise or the apocalyptic world proper. The imagery of light and fire surrounding the angels in the Bible, the tongues of flame descending at Pentecost, and the coal of fire applied to the mouth of Isaiah by the seraph, associates fire with a spiritual or angelic world midway between the human and the divine. In Classical mythology the story of Prometheus indicates a similar provenance for fire, as does the association of Zeus with the thunderbolt or fire of lightning. In short, heaven in the sense of the sky, containing the fiery bodies of sun, moon, and stars, is usually identified with, or thought of as the passage to, the heaven of the apocalyptic world.

因此，我们所有其他类别都可以与火联系起来，或者被视为燃烧。犹太教-基督教神祇在火焰中显现，周围环绕着火焰天使（炽天使）和光明天使（智天使），这一点无需赘述。献祭仪式中燃烧的动物，将动物的身体融入神圣世界与人间世界的交流之中，这体现在所有与祭坛的火焰和烟雾、升腾的香火等等相关的意象中。燃烧的人出现在圣徒的光环和国王的王冠中，两者都是太阳神的象征：人们还可以将之与索斯韦尔圣诞颂歌中的“燃烧的婴儿”进行比较。诗歌中，燃烧的鸟的意象出现在传说中的凤凰身上。生命之树也可能是一棵燃烧的树，摩西未燃尽的燃烧荆棘，犹太教仪式中的烛台，或是后世神秘学中的“玫瑰十字架”。在炼金术中，植物、矿物和水分别对应着玫瑰、宝石和灵药；花卉和宝石的原型则对应着佛教祈祷文中的“莲花中的宝石”。火、醉人的美酒和动物滚烫的鲜血之间的联系也十分常见。

Hence all our other categories can be identified with fire or thought of as burning. The appearance of the Judaeo-Christian deity in fire, surrounded by angels of fire (seraphim) and light (cherubim), needs only to be mentioned. The burning animal of the ritual of sacrifice, the incorporating of an animal body in a communion between divine and human worlds, modulates into all the imagery connected with the fire and smoke of the altar, ascending incense, and the like. The burning man is represented in the saint’s halo and the king’s crown, both of which are analogues of the sun-god: one may compare also the “burning babe” of Southwell’s Christmas poem. The image of the burning bird appears in the legendary phoenix. The tree of life may also be a burning tree, the unconsumed burning bush of Moses, the candlestick of Jewish ritual, or the “rosy cross” of later occultism. In alchemy the vegetable, mineral, and water worlds are identified in its rose, stone, and elixir; flower and jewel archetypes are identified in the “jewel in the lotus” of the Buddhist prayer. The links between fire, intoxicating wine, and the hot red blood of animals are also common.

将城市与火联系起来，解释了为何《启示录》中的上帝之城被描绘成一片闪耀着光芒的金银宝石，每一颗宝石都仿佛燃烧着坚硬如宝石般的火焰。因为在启示录的象征意义中，天上的火体——太阳、月亮和星辰——都包含在宇宙的神圣与人性之中。炼金术的象征意义也属于同一类型的启示录象征：自然的中心，即隐藏在地下的金银珠宝，最终将与天上的太阳、月亮和星辰融为一体；精神世界的中心，即人的灵魂，也将与神融为一体。因此，净化人类灵魂与将大地转化为黄金之间存在着密切的联系，这里的黄金不仅指实际的黄金，更指构成天体的炽热本质之金。《驶向拜占庭》中那棵金色的树和它的机械鸟，以类似炼金术的形式象征着植物世界和矿物世界。

The identification of the city with fire explains why the city of God in the Apocalypse is presented as a glowing mass of gold and precious stones, each stone presumably burning with a hard gemlike flame. For in apocalyptic symbolism the fiery bodies of heaven, sun, moon, and stars, are all inside the universal divine and human body. The symbolism of alchemy is apocalyptic symbolism of the same type: the center of nature, the gold and jewels hidden in the earth, is eventually to be united to its circumference in the sun, moon, and stars of the heavens; the center of the spiritual world, the soul of man, is united to its circumference in God. Hence there is a close association between the purifying of the human soul and the transmuting of earth to gold, not only literal gold but the fiery quintessential gold of which the heavenly bodies are made. The golden tree with its mechanical bird in Sailing to Byzantium identifies vegetable and mineral worlds in a form reminiscent of alchemy.

另一方面，水传统上属于人类生命之下的存在领域，代表着普通死亡之后的混沌或消亡状态，或是还原为无机物的状态。因此，灵魂在死亡时常常穿越水面或沉入水中。在末世象征中，我们有“生命之水”，即伊甸园中四重河流，它在上帝之城重现，并在仪式中以洗礼的形式呈现。根据以西结书的记载，这条河的回归使海水变淡，这显然也是《启示录》的作者所说的末世不再有海的原因。因此，从末世的角度来看，水在宇宙整体中循环，如同血液在个体身体中循环一样。或许我们应该用“蕴含于其中”而非“循环”，以避免将血液循环的知识与圣经主题联系起来的时代错置。当然，几个世纪以来，血液一直是四种“体液”之一，正如生命之河传统上也是四重的一样。

Water, on the other hand, traditionally belongs to a realm of existence below human life, the state of chaos or dissolution which follows ordinary death, or the reduction to the inorganic. Hence the soul frequently crosses water or sinks into it at death. In apocalyptic symbolism we have the “water of life,” the fourfold river of Eden which reappears in the City of God, and is represented in ritual by baptism. According to Ezekiel the return of this river turns the sea fresh, which is apparently why the author of Revelation says that in the apocalypse there is no more sea. Apocalyptically, therefore, water circulates in the universal body like the blood in the individual body. Perhaps we should say “is held within” instead of “circulates,” to avoid the anachronism of connecting a knowledge of the circulation of the blood with Biblical themes. For centuries, of course, the blood was one of four “humors,” or bodily liquids, just as the river of life was traditionally fourfold.

原型意义理论（a）：恶魔意象

THEORY OF ARCHETYPAL MEANING (a) : DEMONIC IMAGERY

与末世象征主义相对立的是欲望彻底排斥的世界：一个噩梦与替罪羊的世界，一个充满束缚、痛苦与混乱的世界；一个在人类想象力开始塑造它之前，在任何人类欲望的意象（例如城市或花园）稳固确立之前的世界；一个充斥着扭曲或浪费的劳动、废墟与地下墓穴、酷刑刑具和愚行纪念碑的世界。正如诗歌中的末世意象与宗教天堂紧密相连，其辩证对立面也与存在主义地狱紧密相连，例如但丁的《神曲·地狱篇》，或者与人类在地球上创造的地狱紧密相连，例如《1984》、《禁闭》和《正午的黑暗》（后两部作品的标题本身就足以说明问题）。因此，恶魔意象的核心主题之一是戏仿，即通过暗示艺术的模仿与“现实生活”的相似性来嘲讽其奔放的创作。

Opposed to apocalyptic symbolism is the presentation of the world that desire totally rejects: the world of the nightmare and the scapegoat, of bondage and pain and confusion; the world as it is before the human imagination begins to work on it and before any image of human desire, such as the city or the garden, has been solidly established; the world also of perverted or wasted work, ruins and catacombs, instruments of torture and monuments of folly. And just as apocalyptic imagery in poetry is closely associated with a religious heaven, so its dialectic opposite is closely linked with an existential hell, like Dante’s Inferno, or with the hell that man creates on earth, as in 1984, No Exit, and Darkness at Noon, where the titles of the last two speak for themselves. Hence one of the central themes of demonic imagery is parody, the mocking of the exuberant play of art by suggesting its imitation in terms of “real life.”

在科技不发达的社会眼中，这个充满魔性的神界很大程度上象征着自然界庞大、可怕而又愚钝的力量。在这样的世界里，天堂的象征往往与遥不可及的天空联系在一起，由此而来的核心思想便是不可捉摸的命运或外在的必然性。命运的机器由一群遥远而隐形的诸神掌控，他们的自由和享乐具有讽刺意味，因为他们将人类排除在外，他​​们干预人类事务主要是为了维护自身的特权。他们要求献祭，惩罚傲慢，并将对自然法则和道德法则的服从视为最终目的。我们在此并非试图描述例如希腊悲剧中的诸神：我们试图揭示的是，在大多数悲剧的人生观中，人类与神圣秩序之间的疏离感和无力感，尽管这只是众多要素之一，但却是所有悲剧中不可或缺的要素。在后世，诗人对这种神性观点表达得更加直言不讳：布莱克的《无名之辈》、雪莱的《朱庇特》、斯温伯恩的《至高无上的邪恶，上帝》、哈代的《糊涂的威尔》以及豪斯曼的《野蛮人与恶棍》都是例证。

The demonic divine world largely personifies the vast, menacing, stupid powers of nature as they appear to a technologically undeveloped society. Symbols of heaven in such a world tend to become associated with the inaccessible sky, and the central idea that crystallizes from it is the idea of inscrutable fate or external necessity. The machinery of fate is administered by a set of remote invisible gods, whose freedom and pleasure are ironic because they exclude man, and who intervene in human affairs chiefly to safeguard their own prerogatives. They demand sacrifices, punish presumption, and enforce obedience to natural and moral law as an end in itself. Here we are not trying to describe, for instance, the gods in Greek tragedy: we are trying to isolate the sense of human remoteness and futility in relation to the divine order which is only one element among others in most tragic visions of life, though an essential one in all. In later ages poets become much more outspoken about this view of divinity: Blake’s Nobodaddy, Shelley’s Jupiter, Swinburne’s “supreme evil, God,” Hardy’s befuddled Will, and Housman’s “brute and blackguard” are examples.

恶魔般的人类世界是一个由自我意识构成的分子级张力维系的社会，这种自我意识对群体或领导者的忠诚削弱了个人，或者充其量只是将个人的享乐与责任或荣誉对立起来。这样的社会是悲剧困境的无尽源泉。就像哈姆雷特和安提戈涅那样。在末世论式的人生观中，我们发现了三种实现方式：个体、性和社会。在险恶的人类世界中，个体的一极是暴君领袖，他深不可测、冷酷无情、忧郁寡欢，且意志永不满足，只有当他足够自我中心，能够代表其追随者的集体自我时，才能赢得忠诚。另一极则由祭品或牺牲品代表，必须被杀死才能增强其他人的力量。在最浓缩的恶魔式戏仿中，两者合二为一。弗雷泽笔下弑君的仪式，无论在人类学中如何解读，在文学批评中都是悲剧和讽刺结构的恶魔式或未被取代的激进形式。

The demonic human world is a society held together by a kind of molecular tension of egos, a loyalty to the group or the leader which diminishes the individual, or, at best, contrasts his pleasure with his duty or honor. Such a society is an endless source of tragic dilemmas like those of Hamlet and Antigone. In the apocalyptic conception of human life we found three kinds of fulfilment: individual, sexual, and social. In the sinister human world one individual pole is the tyrant-leader, inscrutable, ruthless, melancholy, and with an insatiable will, who commands loyalty only if he is egocentric enough to represent the collective ego of his followers. The other pole is represented by the pharmakos or sacrificed victim, who has to be killed to strengthen the others. In the most concentrated form of the demonic parody, the two become the same. The ritual of the killing of the divine king in Frazer, whatever it may be in anthropology, is in literary criticism the demonic or undisplaced radical form of tragic and ironic structures.

在宗教中，精神世界是与物质世界截然不同的现实。在诗歌中，物质或现实并非与精神存在相对立，而是与假设相对立。我们在第一篇文章中探讨了这样一个原则：将行为转化为模仿，从表演仪式发展到扮演仪式，是野蛮走向文明的核心特征之一。我们很容易在网球和足球中看到对冲突的模仿，但正因如此，网球和足球运动员所代表的文化高于学生决斗者和角斗士的文化。将字面行为转化为游戏是生活自由化的基本形式，在更高层次的知识层面表现为博雅教育，即事实向想象的释放。与此相符的是，末世世界中圣餐的象征意义，即植物、动物、人类和神灵身体的隐喻性等同，其恶魔般的戏仿意象是食人行为。但丁对人间地狱的最后描绘是乌戈利诺啃噬折磨者的头骨；斯宾塞最后重要的寓言式描绘是塞雷娜被剥光衣服，准备成为食人盛宴的祭品。食人意象通常不仅包含酷刑和肢解的画面，还包括技术上被称为“撕裂”（sparagmos）的仪式，即撕碎祭品的尸体，这种意象在奥西里斯、俄耳甫斯和彭透斯的神话中都有出现。民间故事中的食人巨人或食人魔，在文学作品中以波吕斐摩斯的形象出现，也属于此类，从提埃斯忒斯的故事到夏洛克的契约，一系列与血肉有关的邪恶交易也同样如此。弗雷泽所描述的历史上的原始形式，在文学批评中却变成了激进的恶魔形式。福楼拜的《萨朗波》就是一个例证。这些恶魔形象在当时被认为是考古发现，但后来却被证明是预言性的。

In religion the spiritual world is a reality distinct from the physical world. In poetry the physical or actual is opposed, not to the spiritually existential, but to the hypothetical. We met in the first essay the principle that the transmutation of act into mime, the advance from acting out a rite to playing at the rite, is one of the central features of the development from savagery into culture. It is easy to see a mimesis of conflict in tennis and football, but, precisely for that very reason, tennis and football players represent a culture superior to the culture of student duellists and gladiators. The turning of literal act into play is a fundamental form of the liberalizing of life which appears in more intellectual levels as liberal education, the release of fact into imagination. It is consistent with this that the Eucharist symbolism of the apocalyptic world, the metaphorical identification of vegetable, animal, human, and divine bodies, should have the imagery of cannibalism for its demonic parody. Dante’s last vision of human hell is of Ugolino gnawing his tormentor’s skull; Spenser’s last major allegorical vision is of Serena stripped and prepared for a cannibal feast. The imagery of cannibalism usually includes, not only images of torture and mutilation, but of what is technically known as sparagmos or the tearing apart of the sacrificial body, an image found in the myths of Osiris, Orpheus, and Pentheus. The cannibal giant or ogre of folk tales, who enters literature as Polyphemus, belongs here, as does a long series of sinister dealings with flesh and blood from the story of Thyestes to Shylock’s bond. Here again the form described by Frazer as the historically original form is in literary criticism the radical demonic form. Flaubert’s Salammbo is a study of demonic imagery which was thought in its day to be archaeological but turned out to be prophetic.

这种恶魔般的性欲关系会演变成一种狂暴而毁灭性的激情，它违背忠诚，或令拥有者感到沮丧。它通常以妓女、女巫、塞壬或其他诱人的女性形象为象征，这些女性是欲望的化身，被当作占有物来追求，因此永远无法真正拥有。这种恶魔般的婚姻，或称两魂合一的结合，可能表现为雌雄同体、乱伦（最常见的形式）或同性恋。其社会关系如同暴民，本质上是人类社会在寻找一种名为“药”（pharmakos ）的灵药，而暴民常常与某种邪恶的动物形象联系在一起，例如九头蛇、维吉尔笔下的“名声”（Fama），或是斯宾塞《赤裸裸的野兽》（Blatant Beast）中对它的诠释。

The demonic erotic relation becomes a fierce destructive passion that works against loyalty or frustrates the one who possesses it. It is generally symbolized by a harlot, witch, siren, or other tantalizing female, a physical object of desire which is sought as a possession and therefore can never be possessed. The demonic parody of marriage, or the union of two souls in one flesh, may take the form of hermaphroditism, incest (the most common form), or homosexuality. The social relation is that of the mob, which is essentially human society looking for a pharmakos, and the mob is often identified with some sinister animal image such as the hydra, Virgil’s Fama, or its development in Spenser’s Blatant Beast.

其他世界可以简要概括。动物世界被描绘成怪物或猛兽。狼（绵羊的传统敌人）、老虎、秃鹫、冰冷而栖息于地的蛇以及龙都是常见的形象。在《圣经》中，邪恶的社会以埃及和巴比伦为代表，两国的统治者都被比作怪兽：尼布甲尼撒在《但以理书》中变成了一头野兽，法老在《以西结书》中被称为河龙。龙尤其贴切，因为它不仅怪诞邪恶，而且充满奇幻色彩，因此象征着邪恶既是道德事实又是永恒否定的矛盾本质。在《启示录》中，龙被称为“先前有，如今没有，以后再有的兽”。

The other worlds can be briefly summarized. The animal world is portrayed in terms of monsters or beasts of prey. The wolf, the traditional enemy of the sheep, the tiger, the vulture, the cold and earth-bound serpent, and the dragon are all common. In the Bible, where the demonic society is represented by Egypt and Babylon, the rulers of each are identified with monstrous beasts: Nebuchadnezzar turns into a beast in Daniel, and Pharaoh is called a river-dragon by Ezekiel. The dragon is especially appropriate because it is not only monstrous and sinister but fabulous, and so represents the paradoxical nature of evil as a moral fact and an eternal negation. In the Apocalypse the dragon is called “the beast that was, and is not, and yet is.”

植物世界就像《科莫斯》或《地狱篇》开篇所描绘的那种阴森森林，或是莎士比亚到哈代笔下常与悲剧命运联系在一起的荒原，又或是勃朗宁《罗兰王子》或艾略特《荒原》中描绘的那种荒野。它也可能是喀耳刻及其文艺复兴时期后继者塔索和斯宾塞笔下那种阴森诡谲的魔法花园。在《圣经》中，荒原以其具体的普遍形式出现在死亡之树、《创世记》中的禁忌知识之树、福音书中的不结果实的无花果树以及十字架上。火刑柱，以及系在上面的蒙面异端、黑人或女巫，就是燃烧的火树和地狱世界的躯体。绞刑架、绞刑架、枷锁、示众柱、鞭子和桦树枝条都是或可能是这种象征的变体。叶芝的诗《两棵树》优美地表达了生命之树与死亡之树的对比。

The vegetable world is a sinister forest like the ones we meet in Comus or the opening of the Inferno, or a heath, which from Shakespeare to Hardy has been associated with tragic destiny, or a wilderness like that of Browning’s Childe Roland or Eliot’s Waste Land. Or it may be a sinister enchanted garden like that of Circe and its Renaissance descendants in Tasso and Spenser. In the Bible the waste land appears in its concrete universal form in the tree of death, the tree of forbidden knowledge in Genesis, the barren fig-tree of the Gospels, and the cross. The stake, with the hooded heretic, the black man or the witch attached to it, is the burning tree and body of the infernal world. Scaffolds, gallows, stocks, pillories, whips, and birch rods are or could be modulations. The contrast of the tree of life and the tree of death is beautifully expressed in Yeats’s poem The Two Trees.

无机世界或许仍保持着未经开发的原始形态，如沙漠、岩石和荒芜之地。毁灭之城和恐怖之夜也属于此地，骄傲的伟大废墟，从巴别塔到奥西曼德斯的宏伟工程，皆是如此。扭曲劳动的意象也属于此地：酷刑机器、战争武器、盔甲，以及死寂机械的形象——它不人性化自然，因此既非自然也非人道。与启示录中的神庙或“一号建筑”相对应，我们有监狱或地牢，如同但丁笔下的狄斯城，一个封闭的、没有光明的炼狱。几何意象的邪恶对应物也在此出现：邪恶的螺旋（漩涡、漩涡或卡律布狄斯），邪恶的十字架，以及邪恶的圆圈，命运之轮。将圆圈与蛇——通常被视为恶魔的动物——联系起来，便产生了衔尾蛇，即衔尾蛇的形象。与以赛亚预言的末世之路或笔直道路，即上帝在沙漠中开辟的大道相对应，在现实世界中，我们看到的是迷宫，它象征着迷失方向，其核心往往潜藏着像弥诺陶洛斯那样的怪物。以色列人在沙漠中迷宫般的徘徊，以及耶稣与魔鬼（或如马可福音中所说的“野兽”）为伴时所经历的迷宫，都符合同样的模式。迷宫也可以是阴森的森林，例如在《科莫斯》中。地下墓穴在《大理石牧神》中也被巧妙地运用在同样的语境中。当然，如果进一步强化隐喻，迷宫还可以化身为那邪恶怪物体内蜿蜒曲折的内脏。

The inorganic world may remain in its unworked form of deserts, rocks, and waste land. Cities of destruction and dreadful night belong here, and the great ruins of pride, from the tower of Babel to the mighty works of Ozymandias. Images of perverted work belong here too: engines of torture, weapons of war, armor, and images of a dead mechanism which, because it does not humanize nature, is unnatural as well as inhuman. Corresponding to the temple or One Building of the apocalypse, we have the prison or dungeon, the sealed furnace of heat without light, like the City of Dis in Dante. Here too are the sinister counterparts of geometrical images: the sinister spiral (the maelstrom, whirlpool, or Charybdis), the sinister cross, and the sinister circle, the wheel of fate or fortune. The identification of the circle with the serpent, conventionally a demonic animal, gives us the ouroboros, or serpent with its tail in its mouth. Corresponding to the apocalyptic way or straight road, the highway in the desert for God prophesied by Isaiah, we have in this world the labyrinth or maze, the image of lost direction, often with a monster at its heart like the Minotaur. The labyrinthine wanderings of Israel in the desert, repeated by Jesus when in the company of the devil (or “wild beasts,” according to Mark), fit the same pattern. The labyrinth can also be a sinister forest, as in Comus. The catacombs are effectively used in the same context in The Marble Faun, and of course in a further concentration of metaphor, the maze would become the winding entrails inside the sinister monster himself.

火的世界是一个充满邪恶恶魔的世界，例如鬼火或从地狱坠落的亡灵，它以火刑（auto da fe）的形式出现在这个世界上，正如前文所述，也以索多玛等燃烧的城市的形式出现。它与炼狱之火或洁净之火（例如但以理书中的烈火窑）形成鲜明对比。水的世界是死亡之水，通常与流淌的鲜血联系在一起，例如在耶稣受难和但丁的历史象征中，尤其是“深不可测、咸涩、令人疏离的海洋”，它吞噬了世间所有的河流，但在末日审判中消失，取而代之的是淡水的循环。在《圣经》中，海洋和动物怪兽被等同于利维坦的形象，这种海怪也与巴比伦和埃及的社会暴政联系在一起。

The world of fire is a world of malignant demons like the will-o’-the-wisps, or spirits broken from hell, and it appears in this world in the form of the auto da fe, as mentioned, or such burning cities as Sodom. It is in contrast to the purgatorial or cleansing fire, like the fiery furnace in Daniel. The world of water is the water of death, often identified with spilled blood, as in the Passion and in Dante’s symbolic figure of history, and above all the “unplumbed, salt, estranging sea,” which absorbs all rivers in this world, but disappears in the apocalypse in favor of a circulation of fresh water. In the Bible the sea and the animal monster are identified in the figure of the leviathan, a sea-monster also identified with the social tyrannies of Babylon and Egypt.

原型意义理论（3）：类比意象

THEORY OF ARCHETYPAL MEANING (3) : ANALOGICAL IMAGERY

当然，诗歌中的大多数意象所描绘的世界远没有通常被描绘成永恒不变的天堂和地狱那样极端。末世意象适用于神话模式，而恶魔意象则适用于反讽模式，尤其是在其回归神话的后期阶段。在其他三种模式中，这两种结构辩证地运作，引导读者走向作品中隐喻和神话的永恒核心。因此，我们应该预期存在三种中间意象结构，大致对应于浪漫主义、高度模仿和低度模仿模式。然而，为了保留本文开头提到的两种永恒结构中浪漫主义和“现实主义”倾向的更简洁模式，我们将对高度模仿意象着墨不多。

Most imagery in poetry has of course to deal with much less extreme worlds than the two which are usually projected as the eternal unchanging worlds of heaven and hell. Apocalyptic imagery is appropriate to the mythical mode, and demonic imagery to the ironic mode in the late phase in which it returns to myth. In the other three modes these two structures operate dialectically, pulling the reader toward the metaphorical and mythical undisplaced core of the work. We should therefore expect three intermediate structures of imagery, corresponding roughly to the romantic, high mimetic, and low mimetic modes. We shall give little attention to high mimetic imagery, however, in order to preserve the simpler pattern of the romantic and “realistic” tendencies within the two undisplaced structures given at the beginning of this essay.

这三种结构并非严格意义上的隐喻，而是意义深远的意象组合，它们共同构成了我们通常略显笨拙地称之为“氛围”的东西。浪漫主义模式呈现了一个理想化的世界：在浪漫故事中，英雄勇敢，女主角美丽，反派邪恶，而日常生活中的挫折、困惑和尴尬则被轻描淡写地一带而过。因此，它的意象展现了一个与末世世界相对应的、我们可以称之为“纯真类比”的人间世界。我们最熟悉的并非浪漫主义时代本身，而是后来的浪漫化作品：文艺复兴时期的《科莫斯》、《暴风雨》和《仙后》第三卷；以及浪漫主义时期布莱克的《纯真之歌》和“比尤拉”意象、济慈的《恩底弥翁》和雪莱的《爱恋颂》。

These three structures are less rigorously metaphorical, and are rather significant constellations of images, which, when found together, make up what is often called, somewhat helplessly, “atmosphere.” The mode of romance presents an idealized world: in romance heroes are brave, heroines beautiful, villains villainous, and the frustrations, ambiguities, and embarrassments of ordinary life are made little of. Hence its imagery presents a human counterpart of the apocalyptic world which we may call the analogy of innocence. It is best known to us, not from the age of romance itself, but from later romanticizings: Comus, The Tempest, and the third book of The Faerie Queene in the Renaissance; Blake’s songs of innocence and “Beulah” imagery, Keats’s Endymion and Shelley’s Epipsychidion in the Romantic period proper.

在纯真这一比喻中，神圣或精神形象通常是长辈般的人物，例如拥有魔法的睿智老人，如普洛斯彼罗，或是友善的守护神，如亚当堕落前的拉斐尔。在人类形象中，儿童占据重要地位，因此与童年和纯真状态最紧密相关的德行——贞洁——也占据重要地位。在这种意象结构中，贞洁通常包含童贞。在《科莫斯》中，女士的贞洁如同普洛斯彼罗的智慧一样，与魔法联系在一起，斯宾塞笔下布里托玛特的坚不可摧的贞洁也是如此。贞洁最容易与年轻女性联系起来——但丁笔下的玛特尔达和莎士比亚笔下的米兰达就是例证——但男性的贞洁也同样重要，正如圣杯传奇所展现的那样。加拉哈德爵士的丁尼生诗中关于他纯洁的心灵赋予他十倍力量的描述，与他所属世界的意象相符。在纯洁的世界里，火通常是净化的象征，一个只有绝对纯洁之人才能通过的火焰世界，例如斯宾塞笔下的布西拉纳城堡、但丁炼狱顶端的炼狱之火，以及阻止堕落的亚当和夏娃进入天堂的火焰之剑。在睡美人的故事中（与此相关），火焰之墙被荆棘之墙所取代；然而，瓦格纳的《女武神》却保留了火焰，令舞台监督们感到不安。月亮，作为所有炽热天体中最凉爽、因而也最纯洁的，在这个世界里具有特殊的意义。

In the analogy of innocence the divine or spiritual figures are usually parental, wise old men with magical powers like Prospero, or friendly guardian spirits like Raphael before Adam’s fall. Among the human figures children are prominent, and so is the virtue most closely associated with childhood and the state of innocence—chastity, a virtue which in this structure of imagery usually includes virginity. In Comus the Lady’s chastity is, like Prospero’s wisdom, associated with magic, as is the invincible chastity of Spenser’s Britomart. It is easiest to associate with young women—Dante’s Matelda and Shakespeare’s Miranda are examples—but male chastity is important too, as the Grail romances show. Sir Galahad’s remark in Tennyson about his purity of heart giving him tenfold strength is consistent with the imagery of the world he belongs in. Fire in the innocent world is usually a purifying symbol, a world of flame that none but the perfectly chaste can pass, as in Spenser’s castle of Busirane, the refining fire at the top of Dante’s purgatory, and the flaming sword that keeps the fallen Adam and Eve away from Paradise. In the story of the sleeping beauty, which belongs here, the wall of flame is replaced by one of thorns and brambles: Wagner’s Die Walküre, however, retains the fire, to the discomposure of stage managers. The moon, the coolest and hence most chaste of all the fiery heavenly bodies, has a special importance for this world.

在动物中，最显而易见的莫过于田园牧歌中的绵羊和羔羊，以及浪漫爱情故事中象征忠诚与奉献的骏马和猎犬。独角兽，作为贞洁的传统象征和处女的爱人，在此也占据着重要的地位；海豚亦是如此，它与阿里翁的关联使其成为吞噬一切的利维坦的纯真对比；此外，还有一种截然不同的动物——驴，因其谦逊和顺从而入选。驴的戏剧性节日，与少年主教的节日一样，都属于这种意象结构。莎士比亚在仙境中放置驴头并非如罗宾逊的诗歌所暗示的那样独树一帜，而是延续了阿普列乌斯笔下卢修斯聆听丘比特与普赛克故事的传统。鸟类、蝴蝶（因为这是普赛克的世界，而普赛克的意思是蝴蝶），以及像爱丽儿和哈德逊的里玛这样的精灵及其特质，都是其他归化的居民。

Of animals, the most obvious are the pastoral sheep and lambs, along with the horses and hounds of romance, in their gentler aspects of fidelity and devotion. The unicorn, the traditional emblem of chastity and the lover of virgins, has an honored place here; so does the dolphin, whose association with Arion makes him the innocent contrast to the devouring leviathan; and also, for its humility and submissiveness, a very different animal—the ass. The dramatic festival of the ass, no less than that of the Boy Bishop, belongs to this structure of imagery, and when Shakespeare put an ass’s head in Fairyland he was not doing something unique, as Robinson’s poem implies, but following a tradition that goes back to the transformed Lucius listening to the story of Cupid and Psyche in Apuleius. Birds, butterflies (for this is Psyche’s world, and Psyche means butterfly), and spirits with their qualities, like Ariel and Hudson’s Rima, are other naturalized denizens.

正如我们所见，天堂花园和生命之树属于末世论的范畴，但圣经和弥尔顿笔下的伊甸园本身则更属于此范畴，但丁将其置于《天堂篇》之下。斯宾塞的《阿多尼斯花园》（《科莫斯》中的侍从精灵即源于此）与此平行，中世纪所有关于“世外桃源”（locus amoenus）主题的发展亦是如此。尤其值得注意的是，圣母的身体象征着“封闭花园”（hortus conclusus） ，源自《雅歌》。生命之树的浪漫对应物出现在魔法师赋予生命的魔杖中，以及《唐豪瑟》中盛开的花杖等类似的象征。

The paradisal garden and the tree of life belong in the apocalyptic structure, as we saw, but the garden of Eden itself, as presented in the Bible and Milton, belongs rather to this one, and Dante puts it just below his Paradiso. Spenser’s Gardens of Adonis, from which the attendant spirit in Comus comes, are parallel, along with all the medieval developments of the theme of the locus amoenus. Of special significance is the symbol of the body of the Virgin as a hortus conclusus, derived from the Song of Songs. A romantic counterpart to the tree of life appears in the magician’s life-giving wand, and such parallel symbols as the blossoming rod in Tannhaüser.

城市与这片土地的田园风光格格不入，塔楼和城堡，偶尔点缀着小屋或隐居处，构成了主要的居住象征。水的象征意义也体现在其中。主要是喷泉和水池、滋润大地的雨水，以及偶尔出现的溪流，将男女分隔开来，从而守护着他们的贞洁，如同但丁笔下的忘川河。《伯恩特·诺顿》开篇的玫瑰园场景，对纯真这一比喻的象征意义进行了简短却极其完整的概括；人们也可以将其与奥登的《时机与逻各斯》第二部分进行比较。

Cities are more alien to the pastoral and rural spirit of this world, and the tower and the castle, with an occasional cottage or hermitage, are the chief images of habitation. Water symbolism features chiefly fountains and pools, fertilizing rains, and an occasional stream separating a man from a woman and so preserving the chastity of each, like the river of Lethe in Dante. The opening rose-garden episode of Burnt Norton gives a brief but extraordinarily complete summary of the symbols of the analogy of innocence; one may also compare the second section of Auden’s Kairos and Logos.

纯真的世界既不像末世那样充满生机，也不像我们的世界那样死寂沉沉：它是一个万物有灵的世界，充满了元素精灵。《科莫斯》中的所有人物，除了夫人和她的兄弟们之外，都是元素精灵。爱丽儿与风精灵、帕克与火精灵（伯顿说火精灵“我们通常称它们为帕克”）、卡利班与土精灵之间的联系显而易见。在斯宾塞的作品中，我们发现了弗洛里梅尔和马里内尔，他们的名字表明他们分别是花神和水精灵，一个是珀耳塞福涅，一个是阿多尼斯。此外，在《科莫斯》和《圣诞颂歌》中，纯真无邪或未堕落的自然，作为神圣秩序的自然，常常以天体音乐那无声的和谐来象征。

The innocent world is neither totally alive, like the apocalyptic one, nor mostly dead, like ours: it is an animistic world, full of elemental spirits. All the characters of Comus are elemental spirits except the Lady and her brothers, and the connections of Ariel with air-spirits, of Puck with fire-spirits (Burton says of fire-spirits that “we commonly call them Pucks”), and of Caliban with earth-spirits are clear enough. In Spenser we find Florimell and Marinell, whose names indicate that they are spirits of flowers and water, a Proserpine and an Adonis. Often, too, as in Comus and the Nativity Ode, innocent or unfallen nature, nature as a divinely sanctioned order, is represented by the inaudible harmony of the music of the spheres.

正如浪漫主义的组织理念是贞洁和魔法，高级模仿领域的组织理念似乎也是爱与形式。浪漫意象领域可被称为纯真之类比，高级模仿意象领域也可被称为自然与理性之类比。我们在此发现，高级模仿的特征在于强调焦点或向心凝视，以及将神圣和精神世界的人类代表理想化的倾向。神性环绕着国王，宫廷爱情的情妇是女神；对二者的爱是一种教化和启迪的力量，使人与精神和神圣世界合而为一。天使世界的火焰在国王的王冠和女士的眼中燃烧。动物象征着骄傲的美丽：鹰和狮子代表忠诚者对王室的愿景，马和猎鹰代表“骑士精神”或骑马的贵族；孔雀和天鹅是众人瞩目的鸟类，而凤凰或独特的火鸟则是诗歌中备受喜爱的象征，尤其在英国，它象征着伊丽莎白女王。花园的象征意义退居幕后，正如城市在浪漫主义作品中的象征意义一样；虽然建筑周围确实存在着正式的花园，但花园世界的概念仍然带有浪漫色彩。魔法师的魔杖化作了皇家权杖，魔法树则变成了飘扬的旗帜。城市的核心是首都，宫廷也坐落于此。其核心在于宫廷内部一系列循序渐进的入宫仪式，最终以皇室的“临在”达到高潮。我们注意到，随着诗歌风格的深入，越来越多的诗意意象取材于真实的社会生活。水的象征意义集中于规整的河流，在英国，泰晤士河在斯宾塞的诗中潺潺流淌，而在丹纳姆的诗中则呈现出新古典主义的韵律，这条河流最恰当的装饰便是皇家驳船。

Just as the organizing ideas of romance are chastity and magic, so the organizing ideas of the high mimetic area seem to be love and form. And as the field of romantic images may be called an analogy of innocence, so the field of high mimetic imagery may be called an analogy of nature and reason. We find here the emphasis on cynosure or centripetal gaze, and the tendency to idealize the human representatives of the divine and the spiritual world, which are characteristic of the high mimetic. Divinity hedges the king and the Courtly Love mistress is a goddess; love of both is an educating and informing power which brings one into unity with the spiritual and divine worlds. The fire of the angelic world blazes in the king’s crown and the lady’s eyes. The animals are those of proud beauty: the eagle and the lion stand for the vision of the royal by the loyal, the horse and falcon for “chivalry” or the aristocracy on horseback; the peacock and the swan are the birds of cynosure, and the phoenix or unique fire-bird is a favorite poetic emblem, especially, in England, for Queen Elizabeth. Garden symbolism recedes into the background, as city symbolism does in romance; there are formal gardens in close association with buildings, but the idea of a garden world is still a romantic one. The magician’s wand is metamorphosed into the royal sceptre, and the magic tree to the fluttering banner. The city is preeminently the capital city, with the court at its center and a series of initiatory degrees of approach within the court, climaxed by the royal “presence.” We note that as we go down the modes an increasing number of poetic images are taken from actual social conditions of life. Water-symbolism centers on the disciplined river, in England the Thames which runs softly in Spenser and in neo-Classical rhythms in Denham, a river whose most appropriate ornament is the royal barge.

在低级模仿领域，我们进入了一个可以称之为经验类比的世界，它与魔界的关系，正如浪漫主义的纯真世界与末世世界的关系。除了这种潜在的讽刺意味之外，除了少数神圣的或特别指定的象征符号，例如霍桑的红字和亨利·詹姆斯的金碗与象牙塔之外，这些意象都是普通的经验意象，无需在此赘述，只需对一些可能有用的特定特征稍作说明即可。低级模仿的组织理念似乎是创世和工作。神圣和精神的存在在低级模仿小说中几乎没有实际作用，在主题写作中，它们常常被刻意地重新发现，或被当作审美替代品。《埃瑞璜》（Erewhon ）中给未出生者的建议（显然与巴特勒的观点接近，因为他在《生活与习惯》中也重复了这一观点）是，如果存在一个精神世界，人们应该背弃它，在当下的工作中重新发现它。通过行为重新发现信仰的同一教义也出现在卡莱尔、罗斯金、莫里斯和萧伯纳的作品中。在诗人中，即使是那些明确带有圣礼色彩的诗人，也存在类似的倾向。从许多角度来看，华兹华斯在《丁登寺》中发现的“运动与精神”与霍普金斯在《风筝》中发现的“骑士”之间的对比可谓天壤之别，然而，将精神愿景锚定于经验性的心理体验这一倾向却是二者的共同之处。

In the low mimetic area we enter a world that we may call the analogy of experience, and which bears a relation to the demonic world corresponding to the relation of the romantic innocent world to the apocalyptic one. Except for this potentially ironic connection, and except for a certain number of hieratic or specially indicated symbols like Hawthorne’s scarlet letter and Henry James’s golden bowl and ivory tower, the images are the ordinary images of experience, and need no further explanation here beyond a few comments about some particular features that may be of use. The organizing low mimetic ideas seem to be genesis and work. Divine and spiritual beings have little functional place in low mimetic fiction, and in thematic writing they are often deliberately rediscovered or treated as aesthetic surrogates. The advice is given to the unborn in Erewhon (apparently close to Butler’s own view, as he repeats the idea in Life and Habit) that if there is a spiritual world, one should turn one’s back on it and find it again in immediate work. The same doctrine of the rediscovery of faith through works may be found in Carlyle, Ruskin, Morris, and Shaw. In poets, even in explicitly sacramental ones, there are parallel tendencies. From many points of view there could hardly be a greater contrast than the contrast between the “motion and a spirit” discovered by Wordsworth in Tintern Abbey and the “chevalier” discovered by Hopkins in the windhover, yet the tendency to anchor a spiritual vision in an empirical psychological experience is common to both.

对人类社会的低模仿性处理，当然反映了华兹华斯的理论，即对诗人而言，人类的基本境况是常见且典型的境况。与此同时，他对浪漫主义中理想化的生活进行了大量的戏仿，这种戏仿也延伸到了宗教和审美体验领域。至于动物世界，托马斯·赫胥黎提及人类与猿和虎所共有的特质，这显然是一种低模仿性的选择。猿一直以来都是模仿动物的典范。早在进化论出现之前，他就一直是人类的模仿者。然而，进化论的兴起暗示了一种比例上的类比，即现在的人类会变成未来对应物种的猿猴，正如尼采在《查拉图斯特拉如是说》中所阐述的那样。赫胥黎将猿猴与老虎并置，让人想起人们普遍认为猿猴和“穴居人”都具有冷酷无情、亘古不变的凶猛本性。这种观点似乎与独角兽和凤凰一样缺乏证据，但它也像独角兽和凤凰一样，展现了一种从诗意隐喻的框架内审视自然历史的倾向。低级模仿并非动物象征的丰富领域，但赫胥黎笔下的猿猴和老虎在吉卜林的《丛林之书》中再次出现。在《丛林之书》中，猴子们像知识分子一样在树梢上无意义地喋喋不休，而人类则在丛林深处学习着黑豹的黑暗掠食智慧。

The low mimetic treatment of human society reflects, of course, Wordsworth’s doctrine that the essential human situations, for the poet, are the common and typical ones. Along with this goes a good deal of parody of the idealization of life in romance, a parody that extends to religious and aesthetic experience. As for the animal world, Thomas Huxley’s reference to the qualities that humanity shares with the ape and the tiger is a significantly low mimetic choice. The ape has always been par excellence the mimetic animal, and long before evolution he was specifically the imitator of man. The rise of evolution however suggested an analogy of proportion in which present man becomes the ape of his counterpart in the future, as in Nietzsche’s Zarathustra. Huxley’s coupling of the ape and the tiger recalls the popular belief in the implacable and invariable ferocity of both apes and “cavemen,” a belief for which there seems to be little more evidence than for unicorns and phoenixes, but which, like them, shows a tendency to look at natural history from within the appropriate framework of poetic metaphors. The low mimetic is not a rich field for animal symbolism, but Huxley’s ape and tiger recur in Kipling’s Jungle Book, where the monkeys chatter in the tree-tops to no purpose, like intellectuals, while the human animal learns instead the dark predatory wisdom of the panther in the jungle below.

在低级模仿文学中，花园被农田和锄头夫的辛勤劳作所取代，农民或金雀花收割者在哈代笔下如同人性的化身，既“饱受轻视又坚韧不拔”。城市自然呈现出迷宫般的现代大都市的形态，其主要情感冲击在于孤独和缺乏交流。正如纯真世界中水的象征意义主要由喷泉和溪流构成，低级模仿文学的意象也追寻康拉德笔下的“毁灭元素”——大海，通常伴随着某种拟人化的巨兽或巨船，大小不一，从哈代笔下的泰坦尼克号到雪莱笔下那艘容易倾覆的敞篷小船——讽刺的是，这艘小船甚至在文学作品中也极为罕见。 《白鲸》则将我们带回了更为传统的巨兽形象。值得注意的是，出现在H·G·威尔斯《托诺-邦盖》结尾的毁灭者，出自一位不太喜欢引入庄严象征的低级模仿文学作家之手。火的象征意义往往带有讽刺和毁灭的意味，例如在《波因顿的战利品》中，大火最终结束了故​​事。然而，在工业时代，为人类盗取火种的普罗米修斯，却成为了诗人最喜爱的神话人物之一，甚至可以说是最受欢迎的。

Gardens in the low mimetic give place to farms and the painful labor of the man with the hoe, the peasant or furze cutter who stands in Hardy as an image of man himself, “slighted and enduring.” Cities take of course the shape of the labyrinthine modern metropolis, where the main emotional stress is on loneliness and lack of communication. And just as water symbolism in the world of innocence consists largely of fountains and running streams, so low mimetic imagery seeks Conrad’s “destructive element” the sea, generally with some humanized leviathan or bateau ivre on it of any size from the Titanic in Hardy to the capsizable open boat which is, with an irony rare even in literature, a favorite image of Shelley. Moby Dick returns us to a more traditional form of the leviathan. The destroyer which appears at the end of H. G. Wells’s Tono-Bungay is notable as coming from a low mimetic writer not much given to introducing hieratic symbols. Fire symbolism is often ironic and destructive, as in the fire which ends the action of The Spoils of Poynton. In the industrial age, however, Prometheus, who stole fire for man’s use, is one of the favorite, if not the actual favorite, mythological figure among poets.
