天真与经验与末世和恶魔意象之间的关系，揭示了我们迄今为止鲜少提及的一种错位：向道德方向的错位。这两种辩证结构本质上分别是可取与不可取。刑架和地牢之所以出现在阴森的景象中，并非因为它们在道德上被禁止，而是因为它们根本不可能被使用。使它们成为欲望的对象。另一方面，即使性满足在道德上受到谴责，人们也可能渴望它。文明倾向于使欲望与道德相一致。比较神话学的学生偶尔会在一些原始或古代的宗教仪式中发现一些不受约束的神话创作，这让他意识到所有高等宗教是如何将其末世景象完全限制在道德可接受的范围内的。犹太教、希腊教和其他神话的发展背后显然存在着大量的净化；或者，正如维多利亚时代的神话学者常说的那样，一种令人厌恶和怪诞的野蛮行径被日益增长的道德修养所净化。埃及神话始于一位通过手淫创造世界的神——这是一种象征“上帝创造”过程的合乎逻辑的方式，但我们不应该期望在荷马史诗中找到这种象征，更不用说在《旧约》中了。只要诗歌跟随宗教走向道德，宗教原型和诗歌原型就会非常接近，就像它们在但丁的作品中那样。在这种影响下，例如，末日般的性意象往往会转化为婚姻或贞洁的意象；乱伦、同性恋和通奸则被归入邪恶的一方。亚里士多德称之为“ spoudaios”、马修·阿诺德译为“高度严肃性”的艺术特质，正是源于宗教与诗歌在共同道德框架内的融合。

The relation of innocence and experience to apocalyptic and demonic imagery illustrates an aspect of displacement which we have so far said little about: displacement in the direction of the moral. The two dialectical structures are, radically, the desirable and the undesirable. Racks and dungeons belong in the sinister vision not because they are morally forbidden but because it is impossible to make them objects of desire. Sexual fulfilment, on the other hand, may be desired even if it is morally condemned. Civilization tends to try to make the desirable and the moral coincide. The student of comparative mythology occasionally turns up, in a primitive or ancient cult, a bit of uninhibited mythopoeia that makes him realize how completely all the higher religions have limited their apocalyptic visions to morally acceptable ones. A good deal of expurgation clearly lies behind the development of Jewish, Greek, and other mythologies; or, as Victorian students of myth used to say, a repulsive and grotesque barbarism has been purified by a growing ethical refinement. Egyptian mythology begins with a god who creates the world by masturbation—a logical enough way of symbolizing the process of creation de Deo, but not one that we should expect to find in Homer, to say nothing of the Old Testament. As long as poetry follows religion towards the moral, religious and poetic archetypes will be very close together, as they are in Dante. Under such influence apocalyptic sexual imagery, for instance, tends to become matrimonial or virginal; the incestuous, the homosexual, and the adulterous go on the demonic side. The quality in art that Aristotle called spoudaios and that Matthew Arnold translated as “high seriousness” results from this rapprochement of religion and poetry within a common moral framework.

但诗歌总是倾向于调整自身的平衡，回归欲望的模式，远离传统和道德。它通常以讽刺的形式来实现这一点，讽刺是与“严肃性”最相去甚远的文体，但并非总是如此。道德与欲望之间存在许多重要而深刻的联系，但道德——它与经验和必然性相契合——是一回事，而欲望——它试图逃避必然性——则是另一回事。因此，文学通常比道德更灵活，而它之所以能成为一门自由艺术，很大程度上归功于此。那些被道德和宗教视为粗俗、淫秽、颠覆性、下流和亵渎的特质，在文学中占有不可或缺的地位，但它们往往只能通过巧妙的移置手法才能得以表达。

But poetry continually tends to right its own balance, to return to the pattern of desire and away from the conventional and moral. It usually does this in satire, the genre which is furthest removed from “high seriousness,” but not always. The moral and the desirable have many important and significant connections, but still morality, which comes to terms with experience and necessity, is one thing, and desire, which tries to escape from necessity, is quite another. Thus literature is as a rule less inflexible than morality, and it owes much of its status as a liberal art to that fact. The qualities that morality and religion usually call ribald, obscene, subversive, lewd, and blasphemous have an essential place in literature, but often they can achieve expression only through ingenious techniques of displacement.

此类技巧中最简单的一种现象，我们可以称之为“恶魔调制”，即刻意颠覆原型通常的道德联想。任何符号的意义主要都来源于其语境：在中世纪的浪漫故事中，龙可能是邪恶的象征，而在中国故事中，龙则可能是友善的象征；一座岛屿可能……普洛斯彼罗的岛屿，或是喀耳刻的岛屿。但由于文学中存在大量博学而传统的象征符号，某些次要的联想便成了惯例。蛇，由于其在伊甸园故事中的角色，通常在西方文学中被归为不祥之物；雪莱的革命情怀促使他在《伊斯兰的叛乱》中使用了一条无辜的蛇。或者，自由平等的社会可以用一群强盗、海盗或吉普赛人来象征；或者，真爱可以用婚外情战胜婚姻来象征，正如大多数三角恋喜剧中那样；可以用同性恋情（如果维吉尔第二首牧歌中歌颂的是真爱）或乱伦情来象征，正如许多浪漫主义作品中那样。在十九世纪，随着恶魔神话的兴起，这种颠倒的象征主义被组织成各种“浪漫主义痛苦”的模式，主要包括虐待狂、普罗米修斯主义和魔鬼崇拜。在某些“颓废派”作品中，这些模式似乎具备了迷信的所有弊端，却没有宗教的任何益处。然而，魔鬼崇拜并非总是复杂的产物：例如，哈克贝利·费恩宁愿与被追捕的朋友一同下地狱，也不愿进入白人奴隶主所信奉的天堂，从而赢得了我们的同情和钦佩。另一方面，传统上与​​恶魔相关的意象也可以被用作救赎运动的起点，例如《天路历程》中的毁灭之城。炼金术的象征主义将衔尾蛇、雌雄同体（合一）以及传统的浪漫主义龙置于这种救赎的语境中。

The simplest of such techniques is the phenomenon that we may call “demonic modulation,” or the deliberate reversal of the customary moral associations of archetypes. Any symbol at all takes its meaning primarily from its context: a dragon may be sinister in a medieval romance or friendly in a Chinese one; an island may be Prospero’s island or Circe’s. But because of the large amount of learned and traditional symbolism in literature, certain secondary associations become habitual. The serpent, because of its role in the garden of Eden story, usually belongs on the sinister side of our catalogue in Western literature; the revolutionary sympathies of Shelley impel him to use an innocent serpent in The Revolt of Islam. Or a free and equal society may be symbolized by a band of robbers, pirates, or gypsies; or true love may be symbolized by the triumph of an adulterous liaison over marriage, as in most triangle comedy; by a homosexual passion (if it is true love that is celebrated in Virgil’s second eclogue) or an incestuous one, as in many Romantics. In the nineteenth century, with demonic myth approaching, this kind of reversed symbolism is organized into all the patterns of the “Romantic agony,” chiefly sadism, Prometheanism, and diabolism, which in some of the “decadents” seem to provide all the disadvantages of superstition with none of the advantages of religion. Diabolism is not however invariably a sophisticated development: Huckleberry Finn, for example, wins our sympathy and admiration by preferring hell with his hunted friend to the heaven of the white slave-owners’ god. On the other hand, imagery traditionally demonic may be used for the starting-point of a movement of redemption, like the City of Destruction in The Pilgrim’s Progress. Alchemical symbolism takes the ouroboros and the hermaphrodite (res bina), as well as the traditional romantic dragon, in this redemptive context.

末世象征主义展现了无限的渴望，其中人类的欲望和野心与神灵等同、适应或投射。天真无邪的类比艺术，涵盖了大部分喜剧（尤其是其圆满结局）、田园诗、浪漫主义、虔诚、颂扬、理想化和魔幻元素，其主要目的是以人性化的、熟悉的、可实现的、且符合道德的方式呈现渴望。魔界与经验类比的关系也大体如此。例如，悲剧是对已发生之事的描绘，也是我们必须接受之事。从这个意义上讲，它是对人类面对一切阻碍其欲望的痛苦怨恨的一种道德且合理的转移。无论我们多么觉得索福克勒斯的《埃阿斯》中的雅典娜是邪恶的，这部悲剧都清楚地表明，我们必须接受她拥有力量的事实，即使是在我们的思想中。一位相信希腊的基督徒如果批评者认为神明不过是魔鬼，那么他批评索福克勒斯的悲剧时，就会做出一种不加修饰或带有魔性色彩的解读。这种解读会揭示索福克勒斯试图回避的一切；尽管如此，它也可能是一种对作品潜在或内在魔性结构的精辟批评。同样的解读也适用于许多描写上帝公义之怒的基督教诗歌段落，这些段落中往往包含着令人憎恶的“父亲”形象，而魔鬼的意味也同样存在。在指出文学作品中潜在的末世或魔性模式时，我们不应错误地认为这种潜在内容就是被谎言掩盖的真实内容。它仅仅是全面批评分析的一个相关因素。然而，它往往是将一部文学作品从单纯的历史范畴中提升出来的关键因素。

Apocalyptic symbolism presents the infinitely desirable, in which the lusts and ambitions of man are identified with, adapted to, or projected on the gods. The art of the analogy of innocence, which includes most of the comic (in its happy-ending aspect), the idyllic, the romantic, the reverent, the panegyrical, the idealized, and the magical, is largely concerned with an attempt to present the desirable in human, familiar, attainable, and morally allowable terms. Much the same is true of the relation of the demonic world to the analogy of experience. Tragedy, for instance, is a vision of what does happen and must be accepted. To this extent it is a moral and plausible displacement of the bitter resentments that humanity feels against all obstacles to its desires. However malignant we may feel Athene to be in Sophocles’ Ajax, the tragedy clearly implies that we must come to terms with her possession of power, even in our thoughts. A Christian who believed the Greek gods to be nothing but devils would, if he were criticizing a tragedy of Sophocles, make an undisplaced or demonic interpretation of it. Such an interpretation would bring out everything that Sophocles was trying not to say; but it could be a shrewd criticism of its latent or underlying demonic structure for all that. The same kind of interpretation would be equally possible for many passages of Christian poetry dealing with the just wrath of God, the demonic content of which is often a hated father-figure. In pointing out the latent apocalyptic or demonic patterns in a literary work, we should not make the error of assuming that this latent content is the real content hypocritically disguised by a lying censor. It is simply one factor which is relevant to a full critical analysis. It is often, however, the factor which lifts a work of literature out of the category of the merely historical.

神话理论：引言

THEORY OF MYTHOS: INTRODUCTION

诗歌的意义，即其意象结构，是一种静态的模式。我们提出的五种意义结构，借用另一个音乐的比喻，就像是谱写和最终解决它们的调式；但叙事却包含着从一种结构到另一种结构的转换。这种转换的主要领域显然是三个中间领域。末世和恶魔世界，作为纯粹隐喻同一性的结构，暗示着永恒不变，很容易被投射为存在主义意义上的天堂和地狱，那里生命持续不断，却没有生命的过程。天真与经验的类比代表了神话对自然的适应：它们呈现给我们的不是人类视野最终目标——城市和花园，而是建造和播种的过程。过程的基本形式是循环运动，是成功与衰落、努力与休息、生命与死亡的交替，这便是过程的节奏。因此，我们提出的七类意象也可以被视为不同形式的旋转或循环运动。由此可见：

The meaning of a poem, its structure of imagery, is a static pattern. The five structures of meaning we have given are, to use another musical analogy, the keys in which they are written and finally resolve; but narrative involves movement from one structure to another. The main area of such movement obviously has to be the three intermediate fields. The apocalyptic and demonic worlds, being structures of pure metaphorical identity, suggest the eternally unchanging, and lend themselves very readily to being projected existentially as heaven and hell, where there is continuous life but no process of life. The analogies of innocence and experience represent the adaptation of myth to nature: they give us, not the city and the garden at the final goal of human vision, but the process of building and planting. The fundamental form of process is cyclical movement, the alternation of success and decline, effort and repose, life and death which is the rhythm of process. Hence our seven categories of images may also be seen as different forms of rotary or cyclical movement. Thus:

1. 在神圣世界中，核心过程或运动是神祇的死亡与重生、消失与回归、化身与隐退。这种神圣活动通常与自然界的一个或多个循环过程相关联。神祇可能是太阳神，在夜晚死去，在黎明重生；也可能在冬至日进行年度重生；或者他他可能是植物之神，秋季凋零，春季复苏；或者（如佛陀的诞生故事中所述），他可能是化身为人的神，经历一系列人类或动物的生命周期。由于神几乎必然是不朽的，因此所有此类神话的共同特征是，垂死的神会以同一人的身份重生。由此可见，循环的神话或抽象结构原则在于，个体生命中从出生到死亡的身份连续性，也从死亡延伸到重生。所有其他循环模式通常都被同化到这种相同的轮回模式——同一人的死亡与复苏。当然，在普遍接受轮回转世教义的东方文化中，这种同化程度可能比西方文化更高。

1. In the divine world the central process or movement is that of the death and rebirth, or the disappearance and return, or the incarnation and withdrawal, of a god. This divine activity is usually identified or associated with one or more of the cyclical processes of nature. The god may be a sun-god, dying at night and reborn at dawn, or else with an annual rebirth at the winter solstice; or he may be a god of vegetation, dying in autumn and reviving in spring, or (as in the birth stories of the Buddha) he may be an incarnate god going through a series of human or animal life-cycles. As a god is almost by definition immortal, it is a regular feature of all such myths that the dying god is reborn as the same person. Hence the mythical or abstract structural principle of the cycle is that the continuum of identity in the individual life from birth to death is extended from death to rebirth. To this pattern of identical recurrence, the death and revival of the same individual, all other cyclical patterns are as a rule assimilated. The assimilation can be of course much closer in Eastern culture, where the doctrine of reincarnation is generally accepted, than in the West.

2. 天体之火的世界为我们呈现了三种重要的循环韵律。最显而易见的是太阳神每日在天空中的运行，人们常将其比作驾驭船只或战车，随后太阳神神秘地穿过黑暗的冥界（有时被想象成吞噬一切的怪兽的腹中），最终回到起点。太阳年的冬至和夏至循环延续了同样的象征意义，并融入了我们的圣诞文学中。圣诞文学更强调新生之光受到黑暗力量威胁的主题。无论其史前作用如何，月相周期在西方历史诗歌中总体上并不那么重要。但其关键的“旧月”、“月间洞穴”和“新月”序列，或许正是我们复活节象征中死亡、消失和复活的三日循环的源头，因为它显然与之密切相关。

2. The fire-world of heavenly bodies presents us with three important cyclical rhythms. Most obvious is the daily journey of the sun-god across the sky, often thought of as guiding a boat or chariot, followed by a mysterious passage through a dark underworld, sometimes conceived as the belly of a devouring monster, back to the starting point. The solstitial cycle of the solar year supplies an extension of the same symbolism, incorporated in our Christmas literature. Here there is more emphasis on the theme of a newborn light threatened by the powers of darkness. The lunar cycle has been on the whole of less importance to Western poetry in historic times, whatever its prehistoric role. But its crucial sequence of old moon, “interlunar cave,” and new moon may be the source, as it is clearly a close analogy, of the three-day rhythm of death, disappearance, and resurrection which we have in our Easter symbolism.

3. 人类世界介于精神与动物之间，其循环节奏反映了这种二元性。与太阳昼夜循环紧密相连的是清醒与梦境的想象循环。这一循环构成了前文已论述的经验想象与纯真想象的对立面。因为人类的节奏与太阳的节奏截然相反：当太阳沉睡时，巨大的欲望觉醒；白昼的光明往往是欲望的黑暗。然而，与动物一样，人类也经历着生死轮回，其中存在着普遍的重生，而非个体的重生。

3. The human world is midway between the spiritual and the animal, and reflects that duality in its cyclical rhythms. Closely parallel to the solar cycle of light and darkness is the imaginative cycle of waking and of dreaming life. This cycle underlies the antithesis of the imagination of experience and of innocence already dealt with. For the human rhythm is the opposite of the solar one: a titanic libido wakes when the sun sleeps, and the light of day is often the darkness of desire. Then again, in common with animals, man exhibits the ordinary cycle of life and death, in which there is generic but not individual rebirth.

4. 无论在文学作品中还是在现实生活中，即使是家养动物，能够平静地走完一生，最终安然离世，也实属罕见。像奥德修斯的狗这样的例外，恰好契合了“回归”（nostos）或循环运动圆满结束的主题。动物的生命，人类的生命同样受制于自然秩序，这更常暗示着生命的悲剧过程，即生命因意外、牺牲、凶猛或某种压倒性的需求而被暴力地中断，而悲剧行为之后延续下去的，并非生命本身。

4. It is rare, in literature as in life, to find even a domesticated animal peacefully living through its full span of life to reach a final nunc dimittis. The exceptions, such as Odysseus’ dog, are appropriate to the theme of nostos or full close of a cyclical movement. Animal lives, and human lives similarly subject to the order of nature, suggest more frequently the tragic process of life cut off violently by accident, sacrifice, ferocity, or some overriding need, the continuity which flows on after the tragic act being something other than the life itself.

5. 当然，植物界为我们提供了四季更迭的年度循环，这通常与一位神祇联系在一起或由其象征，这位神祇在秋季凋零，或在收割庄稼和葡萄时被杀死，在冬季消失，并在春季复苏。这位神祇可以是男性（阿多尼斯）或女性（珀耳塞福涅），但由此产生的象征意义略有不同。

5. The vegetable world supplies us of course with the annual cycle of seasons, often identified with or represented by a divine figure which dies in the autumn or is killed with the gathering of the harvest and the vintage, disappears in winter, and revives in spring. The divine figure may be male (Adonis) or female (Proserpine), but the symbolic structures resulting differ somewhat.

6. 诗人与批评家一样，通常都带有斯宾格勒式的倾向，因为在诗歌中，正如在斯宾格勒的理论中一样，文明生活常常被等同于有机体的生长、成熟、衰落、死亡以及在另一个个体形式中重生的循环。过去黄金时代或英雄时代的景象、未来千年的憧憬、社会事务中命运的轮回、哀歌式的哀歌、对废墟的沉思、对逝去田园牧歌式生活的怀念、对帝国崩溃的惋惜或欢欣，都属于此类主题。

6. Poets, like critics, have generally been Spenglerians, in the sense that in poetry, as in Spengler, civilized life is frequently assimilated to the organic cycle of growth, maturity, decline, death, and rebirth in another individual form. Themes of a golden or heroic age in the past, of a millennium in the future, of the wheel of fortune in social affairs, of the ubi sunt elegy, of meditations over ruins, of nostalgia for a lost pastoral simplicity, of regret or exultation over the collapse of an empire, belong here.

7. 水的象征意义也有其自身的循环，从雨水到泉水，从泉水和喷泉到小溪和河流，从河流到大海或冬雪，然后再回到雨水和泉水。

7. Water-symbolism has also its own cycle, from rains to springs, from springs and fountains to brooks and rivers, from rivers to the sea or the winter snow, and back again.

这些循环符号通常分为四个主要阶段，一年四季分别对应一天中的四个时段（早晨、中午、傍晚、夜晚）、水循环的四个方面（雨、泉水、河流、海洋或雪）、人生的四个阶段（青年、成熟、老年、死亡），等等。我们在济慈的《恩底弥翁》中可以找到大量来自第一和第二阶段的符号，而在《荒原》中则可以找到大量来自第三和第四阶段的符号（这里还需要加上西方文化的四个阶段：中世纪、文艺复兴时期、十八世纪和当代）。值得注意的是，空气并没有循环：风随心所欲地吹，而与“精神”运动相关的意象往往与不可预测性或突发危机的主题联系在一起。

These cyclical symbols are usually divided into four main phases, the four seasons of the year being the type for four periods of the day (morning, noon, evening, night), four aspects of the water-cycle (rain, fountains, rivers, sea or snow), four periods of life (youth, maturity, age, death), and the like. We find a great number of symbols from phases one and two in Keats’s Endymion, and of symbols from phases three and four in The Waste Land (where we have to add four stages of Western culture, medieval, Renaissance, eighteenth-century, and contemporary). We may note that there is no cycle of air: the wind bloweth where it listeth, and images dealing with the movement of “spirit” are likely to be associated with the theme of unpredictability or sudden crisis.

在研读《神曲》或《失乐园》这类鸿篇巨制时，我们会发现必须学习大量的宇宙论知识。当然，这种宇宙论被呈现为当时的科学，一种对应关系的图式，它为我们提供了一个不太高效的历法和一些诸如……之类的词语。“冷静的”和“欢快的”这两个词在科学领域早已过时。还有一些诗歌也融入了同样过时的科学概念，例如《紫色岛屿》、《植物之爱》和《养生之道》，它们如今主要以奇闻轶事的形式流传下来。文学评论家不应忽视这些诗歌的存在本身就对诗歌的一种肯定，但即便如此，诗歌化的科学仍然保留了科学的描述性结构，从而将一种非诗意的形式强加于诗歌之上。要使之成为成功的诗歌，需要极高的技巧，然而，那些最被此类主题吸引的人往往是缺乏技巧的诗人。但丁和弥尔顿的诗才无疑优于达尔文或弗莱彻：然而，或许更恰当的说法是，正是他们更敏锐的直觉和判断力，引导他们走向了宇宙论而非科学或描述性的主题。

In studying poems of immense scope, such as the Commedia or Paradise Lost, we find that we have to learn a good deal of cosmology. This cosmology is presented, quite correctly of course, as the science of its day, a schematism of correspondences which, after supplying us with a not too efficient calendar and a few words like “phlegmatic” and “jovial,” became defunct as science. There are also other poems incorporating equally obsolete science, such as The Purple Island, The Loves of the Plants, The Art of Preserving Health, which survive chiefly as curiosities. A literary critic should not overlook the compliment to poetry implied by the existence of such poems, but still versified science, as such, keeps the descriptive structure of science, and so imposes a non-poetic form on poetry. To make it successful as poetry a great deal of tact is required, yet those most attracted to such themes are very apt to be tactless poets. Dante and Milton were certainly better poets than Darwin or Fletcher: perhaps, however, it would be more fruitful to say that it was their finer instincts and judgements that led them to cosmological, as distinct from scientific or descriptive, themes.

因为宇宙论的形式显然更接近诗歌，由此不禁让人想到，对称宇宙论或许是神话的一个分支。如果真是如此，那么它就像神话一样，是诗歌的结构原则；而在科学本身中，对称宇宙论正如培根所言，不过是戏剧的偶像。或许，这套包含三位一体、四种体液、五种元素、七大行星、九重天、十二星座等等的伪科学体系，实际上正如其在实践中那样，属于文学意象的语法范畴。人们早已注意到，托勒密宇宙论比哥白尼宇宙论提供了一个更完善的象征框架，包含了象征主义所需的所有同一性、关联性和对应关系。或许它不仅提供了一个诗歌象征的框架，它本身就是一个象征框架，或者至少在失去其科学效力之后，就变成了一个象征框架，正如古典神话在其神谕停止之后，就变成了纯粹的诗歌一样。同样的原理也可以解释过去一两个世纪的诗人为何会被神秘的对应体系所吸引，以及像叶芝的《幻象》和坡的《尤里卡》这样的概念。

For the form of cosmology is clearly much closer to that of poetry, and the thought suggests itself that symmetrical cosmology may be a branch of myth. If so, then it would be, like myth, a structural principle of poetry, whereas in science itself, symmetrical cosmology is exactly what Bacon said it was, an idol of the theatre. Perhaps, then, this whole pseudo-scientific world of three spirits, four humors, five elements, seven planets, nine spheres, twelve zodiacal signs, and so on, belongs in fact, as it does in practice, to the grammar of literary imagery. It has long been noticed that the Ptolemaic universe provides a better framework of symbolism, with all the identities, associations, and correspondences that symbolism demands, than the Copernican one does. Perhaps it not only provides a framework of poetic symbols but is one, or at any rate becomes one after it loses its validity as science, just as Classical mythology became purely poetic after its oracles had ceased. The same principle would account for the attraction of poets in the last century or two to occult systems of correspondences, and to such constructs as Yeats’s Vision and Poe’s Eureka.

但丁和弥尔顿都认为，天上是天堂，地上是地狱，两者之间是循环往复的宇宙或自然秩序，这种概念构成了他们作品的基本框架（mu tatis mutandis）。同样的框架也体现在《最后的审判》的绘画作品中，画中救赎者在右侧升起，受诅咒者在左侧坠落，形成一种旋转的运动。我们可以将这种结构应用于我们的原则，即叙事存在两种基本运动：一种是自然秩序内部的循环运动，另一种是从这种秩序出发的辩证运动。进入上方的末日世界。（进入下方的恶魔世界非常罕见，因为自然秩序内的持续轮回本身就是恶魔般的。）

The conception of a heaven above, a hell beneath, and a cyclical cosmos or order of nature in between forms the ground plan, mutatis mutandis, of both Dante and Milton. The same plan is in paintings of the Last Judgement, where there is a rotary movement of the saved rising on the right and the damned falling on the left. We may apply this construct to our principle that there are two fundamental movements of narrative: a cyclical movement within the order of nature, and a dialectical movement from that order into the apocalyptic world above. (The movement to the demonic world below is very rare, because a constant rotation within the order of nature is demonic in itself.)

自然循环的上半部分是浪漫的世界和纯真无邪的类比；下半部分是“现实主义”的世界和经验的类比。因此，神话运动主要有四种类型：浪漫内部、经验内部、向下和向上。向下运动是悲剧运动，命运之轮从纯真走向过错，再从过错走向灾难。向上运动是喜剧运动，从充满威胁的复杂局面走向圆满结局，并普遍假定每个人都能从此过上幸福快乐的生活。在但丁的作品中，向上运动是通过炼狱实现的。

The top half of the natural cycle is the world of romance and the analogy of innocence; the lower half is the world of “realism” and the analogy of experience. There are thus four main types of mythical movement: within romance, within experience, down, and up. The downward movement is the tragic movement, the wheel of fortune falling from innocence toward hamartia, and from hamartia to catastrophe. The upward movement is the comic movement, from threatening complications to a happy ending and a general assumption of post-dated innocence in which everyone lives happily ever after. In Dante the upward movement is through purgatory.

由此，我们已经回答了这个问题：是否存在比普通文学体裁更宽泛，或者在逻辑上先于普通文学体裁的叙事文学类别？这样的类别有四种：浪漫主义、悲剧、喜剧和讽刺/反讽。如果我们考察这些术语的通常含义，也能得到同样的答案。悲剧和喜剧最初可能是两种戏剧的名称，但我们也用这些术语来描述文学作品的一般特征，而不再局限于体裁。如果坚持认为喜剧只能指某种类型的舞台剧，并且绝不能与乔叟或简·奥斯汀的作品联系起来，那就太荒谬了。乔叟本人对喜剧的定义，正如他笔下的僧侣对悲剧的定义一样，肯定要宽泛得多。如果我们被告知即将阅读的作品是悲剧或喜剧，我们期待的是某种特定的结构和氛围，而不是某种特定的体裁。 “浪漫”一词亦是如此，反讽和讽刺这两个词也一样，它们通常被认为是经验文学的要素，我们在此将用它们来代替“现实主义”。由此，我们便有了四种文学叙事的前类型要素，我称之为“神话”或“类型情节”。

We have thus answered the question: are there narrative categories of literature broader than, or logically prior to, the ordinary literary genres? There are four such categories: the romantic, the tragic, the comic, and the ironic or satiric. We get the same answer by inspection if we look at the ordinary meanings of these terms. Tragedy and comedy may have been originally names for two species of drama, but we also employ the terms to describe general characteristics of literary fictions, without regard to genre. It would be silly to insist that comedy can refer only to a certain type of stage play, and must never be employed in connection with Chaucer or Jane Austen. Chaucer himself would certainly have defined comedy, as his monk defines tragedy, much more broadly than that. If we are told that what we are about to read is tragic or comic, we expect a certain kind of structure and mood, but not necessarily a certain genre. The same is true of the word romance, and also of the words irony and satire, which are, as generally employed, elements of the literature of experience, and which we shall here adopt in place of “realism.” We thus have four narrative pregeneric elements of literature which I shall call mythoi or generic plots.

如果我们回顾一下自己对这些神话的体验，就会发现它们构成了两组对立的元素。悲剧与喜剧是对比而非融合，浪漫与讽刺亦是如此，它们分别代表着理想与现实。另一方面，喜剧在一端会不知不觉地融入讽刺，在另一端则会融入浪漫；浪漫可以是喜剧式的，也可以是悲剧式的；悲剧的范畴从崇高的浪漫主义延伸到苦涩而讽刺的现实主义。

If we think of our experience of these mythoi, we shall realize that they form two opposed pairs. Tragedy and comedy contrast rather than blend, and so do romance and irony, the champions respectively of the ideal and the actual. On the other hand, comedy blends insensibly into satire at one extreme and into romance at the other; romance may be comic or tragic; tragic extends from high romance to bitter and ironic realism.

春天的神话：喜剧

THE MYTHOS OF SPRING: COMEDY

戏剧喜剧是虚构喜剧的主要渊源，而戏剧喜剧的结构原则和人物类型却异常顽固。萧伯纳曾说过，喜剧剧作家可以通过借鉴莫里哀的创作手法和狄更斯的人物设定来博得大胆创新的名声：如果我们把米南德和阿里斯托芬的作品当作莫里哀和狄更斯的作品来读，这句话也同样适用，至少从总体上看是如此。现存最早的欧洲喜剧——阿里斯托芬的《阿卡奈人》 ——中就包含着夸夸其谈的军事吹牛大王形象，这种形象在卓别林的《大独裁者》中依然盛行；奥凯西的《朱诺与孔雀》中的乔克瑟·戴利与两千五百年前的寄生虫有着相同的性格和戏剧功能；而如今，在《青蛙》开场时就被认为过时的笑话，在杂耍剧、连环漫画和电视节目中依然能逗得观众捧腹大笑。

Dramatic comedy, from which fictional comedy is mainly descended, has been remarkably tenacious of its structural principles and character types. Bernard Shaw remarked that a comic dramatist could get a reputation for daring originality by stealing his method from Molière and his characters from Dickens: if we were to read Menander and Aristophanes for Molière and Dickens the statement would be hardly less true, at least as a general principle. The earliest extant European comedy, Aristophanes’ The Acharnians, contains the miles gloriosus or military braggart who is still going strong in Chaplin’s Great Dictator; the Joxer Daly of O’Casey’s Juno and the Paycock has the same character and dramatic function as the parasites of twenty-five hundred years ago, and the audiences of vaudeville, comic strips, and television programs still laugh at the jokes that were declared to be outworn at the opening of The Frogs.

普劳图斯和泰伦提乌斯所传述的古希腊新喜剧的情节结构，与其说是一种形式，不如说是一种模式，它已成为大多数喜剧的基础，尤其是在高度程式化的戏剧形式中，直至今日。从戏剧出发来阐述喜剧结构理论最为便捷，小说中的例证仅作辅助。通常情况下，一个年轻男子爱上了一个年轻女子，他的愿望遭到某种阻碍，通常是来自父亲的阻挠，而在剧终时，情节的某种转折使主人公如愿以偿。在这个简单的模式中蕴含着几个复杂的要素。首先，喜剧的叙事通常是从一种社会形态向另一种社会形态的转变。在剧作的开篇，阻碍者掌控着剧中的社会，观众也意识到他们是篡位者。在剧终时，剧情中将男女主角联系在一起的装置导致一个新的社会围绕着男主角凝聚起来，而这种凝聚发生的那一刻就是剧情的解决点，即喜剧性的发现、顿悟或认知。

The plot structure of Greek New Comedy, as transmitted by Plautus and Terence, in itself less a form than a formula, has become the basis for most comedy, especially in its more highly conventionalized dramatic form, down to our own day. It will be most convenient to work out the theory of comic construction from drama, using illustrations from fiction only incidentally. What normally happens is that a young man wants a young woman, that his desire is resisted by some opposition, usually paternal, and that near the end of the play some twist in the plot enables the hero to have his will. In this simple pattern there are several complex elements. In the first place, the movement of comedy is usually a movement from one kind of society to another. At the beginning of the play the obstructing characters are in charge of the play’s society, and the audience recognizes that they are usurpers. At the end of the play the device in the plot that brings hero and heroine together causes a new society to crystallize around the hero, and the moment when this crystallization occurs is the point of resolution in the action, the comic discovery, anagnorisis or cognitio.

这种新社会的出现通常以某种宴会或庆典仪式为标志，这些仪式要么出现在剧终，要么被认为紧随其后。婚礼最为常见，有时甚至多到令人眼花缭乱，例如《皆大欢喜》结尾的四重婚礼。这也暗示了舞蹈中常见的成双成对的场景，这也是常见的结局，也是假面剧的惯常结局。《驯悍记》结尾的宴会可以追溯到古希腊中古喜剧；在普劳图斯的作品中，观众有时会被戏谑地邀请参加一场想象中的宴会；古希腊喜剧，就像现代的圣诞哑剧一样，则更加慷慨，偶尔会向观众抛洒食物。由于喜剧最终达到的社会状态正是观众一直以来所认可的恰当且理想的状态，因此与观众进行交流是必要的。悲剧演员和喜剧演员一样都期待得到掌声，然而，在罗马喜剧结尾出现的“plaudite”（起立鼓掌）一词，即邀请观众加入喜剧社会，在悲剧结尾似乎显得有些格格不入。可以说，喜剧的结局来自舞台的观众席。在悲剧中，死亡来自另一个神秘的世界。而在电影中，黑暗的氛围迎合了更具情色意味的观众，剧情通常会走向一个发生在幕后的场景，如同希腊悲剧中的死亡一般，并以一个最后的拥抱作为象征。

The appearance of this new society is frequently signalized by some kind of party or festive ritual, which either appears at the end of the play or is assumed to take place immediately afterward. Weddings are most common, and sometimes so many of them occur, as in the quadruple wedding at the end of As You Like It, that they suggest also the wholesale pairing off that takes place in a dance, which is another common conclusion, and the normal one for the masque. The banquet at the end of The Taming of the Shrew has an ancestry that goes back to Greek Middle Comedy; in Plautus the audience is sometimes jocosely invited to an imaginary banquet afterwards; Old Comedy, like the modern Christmas pantomime, was more generous, and occasionally threw bits of food to the audience. As the final society reached by comedy is the one that the audience has recognized all along to be the proper and desirable state of affairs, an act of communion with the audience is in order. Tragic actors expect to be applauded as well as comic ones, but nevertheless the word “plaudite” at the end of a Roman comedy, the invitation to the audience to form part of the comic society, would seem rather out of place at the end of a tragedy. The resolution of comedy comes, so to speak, from the audience’s side of the stage; in a tragedy it comes from some mysterious world on the opposite side. In the movie, where darkness permits a more erotically oriented audience, the plot usually moves toward an act which, like death in Greek tragedy, takes place offstage, and is symbolized by a closing embrace.

因此，阻碍主人公愿望的障碍构成了喜剧的情节，而克服这些障碍则构成了喜剧的结局。这些障碍通常来自父母，因此喜剧往往围绕着儿子与父亲意志的冲突展开。所以，喜剧作家通常是为年轻男性观众创作，而几乎所有社会中的年长者都倾向于认为喜剧具有某种颠覆性。这无疑是戏剧遭受社会迫害的原因之一，这种迫害并非清教徒甚至基督徒所独有，因为泰伦斯在异教罗马时期也遇到了与本·琼森类似的社会反对。普劳图斯的剧作中有一幕，一对父子与同一位妓女寻欢作乐，儿子尖锐地问父亲是否真的爱母亲。我们必须将这一幕置于罗马家庭生活的背景下理解，才能明白它作为一种心理宣泄手段的重要性。即使在莎士比亚的作品中，也时常出现戏弄年长男性的惊人情节；而在当代电影中，青春的胜利如此无情，以至于电影制作人很难吸引超过十七岁的观众。

The obstacles to the hero’s desire, then, form the action of the comedy, and the overcoming of them the comic resolution. The obstacles are usually parental, hence comedy often turns on a clash between a son’s and a father’s will. Thus the comic dramatist as a rule writes for the younger men in his audience, and the older members of almost any society are apt to feel that comedy has something subversive about it. This is certainly one element in the social persecution of drama, which is not peculiar to Puritans or even Christians, as Terence in pagan Rome met much the same kind of social opposition that Ben Jonson did. There is one scene in Plautus where a son and father are making love to the same courtesan, and the son asks his father pointedly if he really does love mother. One has to see this scene against the background of Roman family life to understand its importance as psychological release. Even in Shakespeare there are startling outbreaks of baiting older men, and in contemporary movies the triumph of youth is so relentless that the moviemakers find some difficulty in getting anyone over the age of seventeen into their audiences.

如果不是父亲，那么反对英雄愿望的人通常是与父亲关系更密切、与既定家庭关系更紧密的人。社会：也就是说，一个年轻气盛却财力雄厚的竞争对手。在普劳图斯和泰伦斯的作品中，他通常要么是拥有女孩的皮条客，要么是带着现金四处游荡的士兵。这些角色被激怒并最终被逐出舞台，表明他们是父亲的化身；即便不是，他们仍然是篡位者，他们对女孩的占有必须被揭露为某种欺诈。简而言之，他们是骗子，而他们所拥有的权力程度，暗示着对赋予他们权力的社会的一种批判。在普劳图斯和泰伦斯的作品中，这种批判很少超越妓院和职业妓女的道德沦丧，但在包括本·琼森在内的文艺复兴时期剧作家的作品中，对金钱日益增长的权力及其所构建的统治阶级有着敏锐的观察。

The opponent to the hero’s wishes, when not the father, is generally someone who partakes of the father’s closer relation to established society: that is, a rival with less youth and more money. In Plautus and Terence he is usually either the pimp who owns the girl, or a wandering soldier with a supply of ready cash. The fury with which these characters are baited and exploded from the stage shows that they are father-surrogates, and even if they were not, they would still be usurpers, and their claim to possess the girl must be shown up as somehow fraudulent. They are, in short, impostors, and the extent to which they have real power implies some criticism of the society that allows them their power. In Plautus and Terence this criticism seldom goes beyond the immorality of brothels and professional harlots, but in Renaissance dramatists, including Jonson, there is some sharp observation of the rising power of money and the sort of ruling class it is building up.

喜剧的倾向是尽可能地将更多的人纳入其最终的社会：那些阻碍社会发展的角色往往最终得到和解或转变，而非被简单地抛弃。喜剧通常包含一种驱逐替罪羊的仪式，以此清除某些不可调和的角色，但这种揭露和耻辱却能引发悲情，甚至悲剧。《威尼斯商人》似乎几乎是一次实验，旨在尽可能地打破喜剧的平衡。如果夏洛克这个角色的戏剧性表现稍有夸张——通常情况下，当剧团的领衔演员扮演这个角色时，就会出现这种情况——那么这种平衡就会被打破，整部剧就变成了带有喜剧结尾的《威尼斯犹太人》的悲剧。《福尔蓬》以一连串的苦役和划桨刑罚告终，人们不禁会觉得，社会的解放似乎并不需要如此艰苦的劳动；但《福尔蓬》的特殊之处在于，它是一种对悲剧的喜剧式模仿，福尔蓬的傲慢自大被刻画得淋漓尽致。

The tendency of comedy is to include as many people as possible in its final society: the blocking characters are more often reconciled or converted than simply repudiated. Comedy often includes a scapegoat ritual of expulsion which gets rid of some irreconcilable character, but exposure and disgrace make for pathos, or even tragedy. The Merchant of Venice seems almost an experiment in coming as close as possible to upsetting the comic balance. If the dramatic role of Shylock is ever so slightly exaggerated, as it generally is when the leading actor of the company takes the part, it is upset, and the play becomes the tragedy of the Jew of Venice with a comic epilogue. Volpone ends with a great bustle of sentences to penal servitude and the galleys, and one feels that the deliverance of society hardly needs so much hard labor; but then Volpone is exceptional in being a kind of comic imitation of a tragedy, with the point of Volpone’s hybris carefully marked.

对于那些主要功能是取悦观众的角色而言，转变的原则就更加清晰了。普劳图斯笔下最初的“光荣的迈尔斯”（ miles gloriosus）是朱庇特和维纳斯的儿子，他声称自己徒手杀死了一头大象，并在一天之内击败了七千人。换句话说，他是在努力表演：他夸夸其谈的热情有助于戏剧的成功。按照惯例，吹牛大王必须被揭穿、嘲笑、欺骗和痛打。但是，为什么一位职业剧作家，尤其是他自己，会如此费尽心思去折磨一个正在表演——而且是他自己的表演——的角色呢？当我们在《风流娘儿们》中看到福斯塔夫被邀请参加最后的宴会，卡利班被赦免，有人试图安抚马伏里奥，安杰洛和帕罗勒斯也被允许洗清他们的耻辱时，我们看到喜剧的一个基本原则正在发挥作用。喜剧社会倾向于包容而非排斥，这正是寄生虫这一角色传统上重要性的原因——他们本不该出现在最后的庆典上，却偏偏在那里。“优雅”一词，从卡斯蒂廖内笔下优雅的廷臣到基督教慈悲的上帝，都带有浓厚的文艺复兴色彩，是莎士比亚喜剧中一个极其重要的主题词。

The principle of conversion becomes clearer with characters whose chief function is the amusing of the audience. The original miles gloriosus in Plautus is a son of Jove and Venus who has killed an elephant with his fist and seven thousand men in one day’s fighting. In other words, he is trying to put on a good show: the exuberance of his boasting helps to put the play over. The convention says that the braggart must be exposed, ridiculed, swindled, and beaten. But why should a professional dramatist, of all people, want so to harry a character who is putting on a good show—his show at that? When we find Falstaff invited to the final feast in The Merry Wives, Caliban reprieved, attempts made to mollify Malvolio, and Angelo and Parolles allowed to live down their disgrace, we are seeing a fundamental principle of comedy at work. The tendency of the comic society to include rather than exclude is the reason for the traditional importance of the parasite, who has no business to be at the final festival but is nevertheless there. The word “grace,” with all its Renaissance overtones from the graceful courtier of Castiglione to the gracious God of Christianity, is a most important thematic word in Shakespearean comedy.

喜剧从一个社会中心转移到另一个社会中心的过程，与诉讼的运作方式颇为相似：原告和被告构建同一情境的不同版本，最终一个版本被判定为真实，另一个版本被判定为虚幻。喜剧修辞与法学修辞的这种相似性，自古以来就为人所知。一本名为《科伊斯林论》（Tractatus Coislinianus）的小册子，与亚里士多德的《诗学》密切相关，仅用一页半的篇幅就阐述了喜剧的所有基本要素，它将喜剧的论证（ dianoia）分为两部分：意见（pistis）和论证（gnosis）。这两者大致分别对应于篡夺的社会和理想的社会。论证（即实现更幸福社会的手段）又细分为誓言、契约、证人、神判（或酷刑）和法律——换句话说，就是《修辞学》中列举的法律案件中的五种实质性证据形式。我们注意到，莎士比亚喜剧的剧情往往以一些荒谬、残酷或不合情理的法律开篇：例如《错误的喜剧》中处死叙拉古人的法律、 《仲夏夜之梦》中的强制婚姻法、确认夏洛克契约的法律、安杰洛试图通过立法使人们变得正义等等，而喜剧的剧情随后往往会规避或打破这些法律。契约通常是主人公所在社会形成的阴谋；证人，例如偷听到谈话的人或拥有特殊知识的人（比如主人公那位对胎记记忆力惊人的老奶妈），是促成喜剧情节发生的常用手段。考验（basanoi）通常是对英雄品格的考验或试金石：希腊语单词也指试金石，这似乎与莎士比亚笔下的巴萨尼奥的经历相呼应，巴萨尼奥的考验是判断金属的价值。

The action of comedy in moving from one social center to another is not unlike the action of a lawsuit, in which plaintiff and defendant construct different versions of the same situation, one finally being judged as real and the other as illusory. This resemblance of the rhetoric of comedy to the rhetoric of jurisprudence has been recognized from earliest times. A little pamphlet called the Tractatus Coislinianus, closely related to Aristotle’s Poetics, which sets down all the essential facts about comedy in about a page and a half, divides the dianoia of comedy into two parts, opinion (pistis) and proof (gnosis). These correspond roughly to the usurping and the desirable societies respectively. Proofs (i.e., the means of bringing about the happier society) are subdivided into oaths, compacts, witnesses, ordeals (or tortures), and laws—in other words the five forms of material proof in law cases listed in the Rhetoric. We notice how often the action of a Shakespearean comedy begins with some absurd, cruel, or irrational law: the law of killing Syracusans in the Comedy of Errors, the law of compulsory marriage in A Midsummer Night’s Dream, the law that confirms Shylock’s bond, the attempts of Angelo to legislate people into righteousness, and the like, which the action of the comedy then evades or breaks. Compacts are as a rule the conspiracies formed by the hero’s society; witnesses, such as overhearers of conversations or people with special knowledge (like the hero’s old nurse with her retentive memory for birthmarks), are the commonest devices for bringing about the comic discovery. Ordeals (basanoi) are usually tests or touchstones of the hero’s character: the Greek word also means touchstones, and seems to be echoed in Shakespeare’s Bassanio whose ordeal it is to make a judgement on the worth of metals.

喜剧形式的发展有两种途径：一种是将重点放在人物的行动上；另一种是将重点放在发现和和解的场景上。喜剧反讽、讽刺、现实主义等是一种普遍趋势。另一种倾向是风俗喜剧；另一种倾向是莎士比亚式和其他类型的浪漫喜剧。在风俗喜剧中，主要的伦理意义通常落在阻碍剧情发展的角色身上。技术上的男女主角往往并不十分有趣：普劳图斯和泰伦斯笔下的少年们都千篇一律，就像狄米特律斯和莱桑德一样，在黑暗中难以区分，而狄米特律斯和莱桑德或许正是对他们的戏仿。通常，主人公的性格具有中立性，使他能够代表一种愿望的实现。这与吝啬或凶残的父母、自夸或浮夸的对手，以及其他阻碍剧情发展的角色截然不同。在莫里哀的作品中，我们看到一个简单却行之有效的模式，其中伦理意义集中在一个阻碍剧情发展的角色身上，例如严厉的父亲、守财奴、厌世者、伪君子或疑病症患者。我们记住的都是这些人物，剧作通常也以他们的名字命名，但我们却很少能记住那些从他们手中挣脱出来的瓦伦丁和安吉莉克。在《风流娘儿们》中，技术上的英雄芬顿只是个配角，这部剧似乎借鉴了普劳图斯的《卡西娜》，在《卡西娜》中，男女主角甚至根本没有登台。虚构的喜剧，尤其是狄更斯的作品，常常遵循着同样的套路，将一些有趣的人物围绕着一对略显平庸的技术型主角展开。即使是汤姆·琼斯，尽管人物形象更加丰满，但正如他那平凡的名字所示，仍然刻意与传统和典型联系在一起。

There are two ways of developing the form of comedy: one is to throw the main emphasis on the blocking characters; the other is to throw it forward on the scenes of discovery and reconciliation. One is the general tendency of comic irony, satire, realism, and studies of manners; the other is the tendency of Shakespearean and other types of romantic comedy. In the comedy of manners the main ethical interest falls as a rule on the blocking characters. The technical hero and heroine are not often very interesting people: the adulescentes of Plautus and Terence are all alike, as hard to tell apart in the dark as Demetrius and Lysander, who may be parodies of them. Generally the hero’s character has the neutrality that enables him to represent a wish-fulfilment. It is very different with the miserly or ferocious parent, the boastful or foppish rival, or the other characters who stand in the way of the action. In Molière we have a simple but fully tested formula in which the ethical interest is focussed on a single blocking character, a heavy father, a miser, a misanthrope, a hypocrite, or a hypochondriac. These are the figures that we remember, and the plays are usually named after them, but we can seldom remember all the Valentins and Angeliques who wriggle out of their clutches. In The Merry Wives the technical hero, a man named Fenton, has only a bit part, and this play has picked up a hint or two from Plautus’s Casina, where the hero and heroine are not even brought on the stage at all. Fictional comedy, especially Dickens, often follows the same practice of grouping its interesting characters around a somewhat dullish pair of technical leads. Even Tom Jones, though far more fully realized, is still deliberately associated, as his commonplace name indicates, with the conventional and typical.

喜剧通常以大团圆结局收尾，观众对大团圆结局的通常反应是“就该如此”，这听起来像是道德评判。的确如此，只不过这种评判并非狭义上的道德评判，而是社会评判。它的反面不是邪恶，而是荒诞，喜剧认为马伏里奥的美德与安杰洛的恶习一样荒诞。莫里哀笔下的愤世嫉俗者，由于坚持真诚（这本身就是一种美德），在道德上处于有利地位，但观众很快就会意识到，他的朋友菲兰特为了维护他人的尊严，甚至乐于撒谎，反而比马伏里奥更加真诚。当然，完全可以创作一部道德喜剧，但其结果往往是那种我们称之为“无幽默喜剧”的情节剧，它以一种自以为是的语气来达成大团圆结局，而大多数喜剧都力求避免这种语气。很难想象一部戏剧没有冲突，也很难想象一场冲突没有某种敌意。但正如爱情一样，包括性爱在内的情感与欲望截然不同，因此敌意也与仇恨大相径庭。当然，在悲剧中，敌意几乎总是包含仇恨；喜剧则不同，人们感觉社会对荒诞的评判更接近于喜剧的常态，而非道德对邪恶的评判。

Comedy usually moves toward a happy ending, and the normal response of the audience to a happy ending is “this should be,” which sounds like a moral judgement. So it is, except that it is not moral in the restricted sense, but social. Its opposite is not the villainous but the absurd, and comedy finds the virtues of Malvolio as absurd as the vices of Angelo. Molière’s misanthrope, being committed to sincerity, which is a virtue, is morally in a strong position, but the audience soon realizes that his friend Philinte, who is ready to lie quite cheerfully in order to enable other people to preserve their self-respect, is the more genuinely sincere of the two. It is of course quite possible to have a moral comedy, but the result is often the kind of melodrama that we have described as comedy without humor, and which achieves its happy ending with a self-righteous tone that most comedy avoids. It is hardly possible to imagine a drama without conflict, and it is hardly possible to imagine a conflict without some kind of enmity. But just as love, including sexual love, is a very different thing from lust, so enmity is a very different thing from hatred. In tragedy, of course, enmity almost always includes hatred; comedy is different, and one feels that the social judgement against the absurd is closer to the comic norm than the moral judgement against the wicked.

那么问题来了，是什么让这种阻挠型角色显得荒谬呢？本·琼森用他的“幽默”理论解释了这一点，这种角色受制于蒲柏所说的支配性激情。这种幽默的戏剧功能在于表达一种可以称之为仪式性束缚的状态。他被自己的幽默所困扰，他在剧中的主要作用就是重复这种困扰。病人不是幽默的化身，但疑病症患者是，因为作为疑病症患者，他永远无法承认自己身体健康，也永远无法做出任何与他为自己设定的角色相悖的事情。守财奴的言行举止都与藏匿黄金或积攒金钱有关。在琼森最接近莫里哀结构的作品《沉默的女人》中，整个剧情都围绕着忧郁症患者的幽默展开，他决心消除生活中的喧嚣，却因此产生了喋喋不休的喜剧效果。

The question then arises of what makes the blocking character absurd. Ben Jonson explained this by his theory of the “humor,” the character dominated by what Pope calls a ruling passion. The humor’s dramatic function is to express a state of what might be called ritual bondage. He is obsessed by his humor, and his function in the play is primarily to repeat his obsession. A sick man is not a humor, but a hypochondriac is, because, qua hypochondriac, he can never admit to good health, and can never do anything inconsistent with the role that he has prescribed for himself. A miser can do and say nothing that is not connected with the hiding of gold or saving of money. In The Silent Woman, Jonson’s nearest approach to Molière’s type of construction, the whole action recedes from the humor of Morose, whose determination to eliminate noise from his life produces so loquacious a comic action.

幽默的原则在于，不加修饰的重复，即文学上对仪式性束缚的模仿，本身就具有滑稽效果。在悲剧中——《俄狄浦斯王》就是一个典型的例子——重复必然导致灾难。过度重复或毫无进展的重复则属于喜剧的范畴，因为笑声部分是一种反射，而与其他反射一样，它可以通过简单的重复模式来调节。在辛格的《骑马入海》中，一位母亲在海上失去了丈夫和五个儿子后，最终又失去了最后一个儿子，这造就了一部非常优美动人的戏剧。但如果它是一部冗长的悲剧，沉重地讲述七个溺水事件接连发生，那么观众在剧终之前就会因为缺乏同情心而发出无奈的笑声。无论是本·琼森的幽默观还是我们现代的幽默，重复都是幽默的基础，这一点漫画家们都深谙此道。在漫画中，人物往往被塑造成寄生虫、贪婪之徒（通常只吃一道菜）或泼妇，而当这些特点连续几个月每天都被重复时，人物便开始变得滑稽可笑。同样，连续播出的喜剧广播节目也更受老听众的喜爱，而非新听众。福斯塔夫的肥胖和堂吉诃德的幻觉都基于类似的喜剧规律。E ·M·福斯特先生对狄更斯笔下的米考伯太太不屑一顾，因为她除了永远不会离开之外，什么也不说。米考伯先生：这里明显存在着一种对比，即一位文笔优美、对流行套路过于挑剔的作家，与一位无情地利用流行套路的著名作家形成了鲜明的对比。

The principle of the humor is the principle that unincremental repetition, the literary imitation of ritual bondage, is funny. In a tragedy—Oedipus Tyrannus is the stock example—repetition leads logically to catastrophe. Repetition overdone or not going anywhere belongs to comedy, for laughter is partly a reflex, and like other reflexes it can be conditioned by a simple repeated pattern. In Synge’s Riders to the Sea a mother, after losing her husband and five sons at sea, finally loses her last son, and the result is a very beautiful and moving play. But if it had been a full-length tragedy plodding glumly through the seven drownings one after another, the audience would have been helpless with unsympathetic laughter long before it was over. The principle of repetition as the basis of humor both in Jonson’s sense and in ours is well known to the creators of comic strips, in which a character is established as a parasite, a glutton (often confined to one dish), or a shrew, and who begins to be funny after the point has been made every day for several months. Continuous comic radio programs, too, are much more amusing to habitués than to neophytes. The girth of Falstaff and the hallucinations of Quixote are based on much the same comic laws. Mr. E. M. Forster speaks with disdain of Dickens’s Mrs. Micawber, who never says anything except that she will never desert Mr. Micawber: a strong contrast is marked here between the refined writer too finicky for popular formulas, and the major one who exploits them ruthlessly.

喜剧中的幽默通常源于拥有相当社会声望和权力的人物，他们能够迫使剧中的大部分社会成员屈从于他们的执念。因此，幽默与荒诞或非理性法则的主题紧密相连，而喜剧的剧情最终也走向了打破这种法则的极端。值得注意的是，我们最早的幽默喜剧《黄蜂》中的主人公痴迷于法律案件：夏洛克也同样将对法律的渴望与复仇的幽默结合起来。荒诞的法律常常以一个困惑的暴君的异想天开的形式出现，他的意志即是法律，例如利昂特斯或莎士比亚笔下幽默的弗雷德里克公爵，他们会做出一些武断的决定或轻率的承诺：在这里，“法律”被“誓言”所取代，而“誓言”在《逻辑哲学论》中也有提及。或者，它也可能以虚假的乌托邦的形式出现，一个由幽默或迂腐的意志所构建的仪式性束缚的社会，例如《爱的徒劳》中的学术隐居。这个主题也与阿里斯托芬一样古老，他在《鸟》和《教会》中对柏拉图式的社会方案进行了戏仿，探讨了这一主题。

The humor in comedy is usually someone with a good deal of social prestige and power, who is able to force much of the play’s society into line with his obsession. Thus the humor is intimately connected with the theme of the absurd or irrational law that the action of comedy moves toward breaking. It is significant that the central character of our earliest humor comedy, The Wasps, is obsessed by law cases: Shylock, too, unites a craving for the law with the humor of revenge. Often the absurd law appears as a whim of a bemused tyrant whose will is law, like Leontes or the humorous Duke Frederick in Shakespeare, who makes some arbitrary decision or rash promise: here law is replaced by “oath,” also mentioned in the Tractatus. Or it may take the form of a sham Utopia, a society of ritual bondage constructed by an act of humorous or pedantic will, like the academic retreat in Love’s Labor’s Lost. This theme is also as old as Aristophanes, whose parodies of Platonic social schemes in The Birds and Ecclesiazusae deal with it.

与此相反，喜剧结尾所展现的社会代表了一种道德规范，或者说是一种务实的自由社会。它的理想很少被定义或阐述：定义和阐述属于体液的范畴，它们追求的是可预测的活动。我们只需明白，这对新婚夫妇将从此过上幸福的生活，或者至少他们会以一种相对冷静理智的方式相处。这正是成功主人公的性格常常缺乏深入刻画的原因之一：他的真实生活始于剧终，我们必须相信他可能是一个比表面看起来更有趣的人物。在泰伦提乌斯的《爱的代价》中，严厉的父亲德米亚与他溺爱的弟弟米西奥形成鲜明对比。米西奥更加开明，引领了喜剧的结局，并感化了德米亚，但随后德米亚指出米西奥的开明很大程度上源于他的懒惰，从而使他摆脱了与之互补的幽默束缚。

The society emerging at the conclusion of comedy represents, by contrast, a kind of moral norm, or pragmatically free society. Its ideals are seldom defined or formulated: definition and formulation belong to the humors, who want predictable activity. We are simply given to understand that the newly-married couple will live happily ever after, or that at any rate they will get along in a relatively unhumorous and clear-sighted manner. That is one reason why the character of the successful hero is so often left undeveloped: his real life begins at the end of the play, and we have to believe him to be potentially a more interesting character than he appears to be. In Terence’s Adelphoi, Demea, a harsh father, is contrasted with his brother Micio, who is indulgent. Micio being more liberal, he leads the way to the comic resolution, and converts Demea, but then Demea points out the indolence inspiring a good deal of Micio’s liberality, and releases him from a complementary humorous bondage.

因此，从pistis到gnosis的转变，即从一个受习惯、仪式束缚、任意法律和老一辈人控制的社会，到一个受青年和务实自由控制的社会，从根本上来说，正如希腊语所暗示的那样，是从幻觉到现实的转变。幻觉是任何固定或可定义的事物，而现实则是现实。最好将其理解为它的否定：无论现实是什么，它都不是你所看到的。因此，在喜剧中，创造和消除幻觉这一主题至关重要：这些幻觉是由伪装、痴迷、虚伪或身世不明等因素造成的。

Thus the movement from pistis to gnosis, from a society controlled by habit, ritual bondage, arbitrary law and the older characters to a society controlled by youth and pragmatic freedom is fundamentally, as the Greek words suggest, a movement from illusion to reality. Illusion is whatever is fixed or definable, and reality is best understood as its negation: whatever reality is, it’s not that. Hence the importance of the theme of creating and dispelling illusion in comedy: the illusions caused by disguise, obsession, hypocrisy, or unknown parentage.

喜剧的结局通常是通过情节反转来实现的。在罗马喜剧中，女主角通常是奴隶或妓女，但最终却发现她是某个体面人的女儿，这样男主角才能体面地娶她为妻。喜剧中的“认亲”（cognitio） ——即人物发现彼此的亲属关系，以及异性中还有哪些人不是亲戚，因而可以结婚——是喜剧中鲜少改变的特征之一：《密探》这部剧作表明，它至今仍然吸引着剧作家的关注。在《芭芭拉少校》的结尾，有一个精彩的“认知”（cognitio）戏仿（该剧主人公是一位希腊语教授，这或许表明他与欧里庇得斯和米南德的戏剧惯例有着异乎寻常的亲近感）。剧中，安德谢夫特得以打破不能立女婿为继承人的规则，因为他女婿的父亲在澳大利亚娶了他已故妻子的妹妹，所以女婿既是他的堂兄，也是他本人。这听起来很复杂，但喜剧的情节往往复杂，因为复杂本身就带有某种荒诞性。由于喜剧中主角的关注点通常集中在失败者身上，因此喜剧经常展现出任意情节战胜人物性格一致性的现象。由此可见，与悲剧截然不同，就单部剧作的情节而言，几乎不存在必然的喜剧。也就是说，我们或许知道喜剧的惯例必然会带来某种皆大欢喜的结局，但剧作家仍然必须为每一部剧创作一个独特的“噱头”或“小把戏”（借用好莱坞对顿悟的两种不敬的同义词） 。皆大欢喜的结局并非让我们觉得真实，而是让我们觉得美好，而它们往往是人为操控的结果。观看死亡和悲剧的人除了坐着等待不可避免的结局之外别无他事；但在喜剧的结尾，某种东西诞生了，而观看诞生的人则是忙碌社会中的一员。

The comic ending is generally manipulated by a twist in the plot. In Roman comedy the heroine, who is usually a slave or courtesan, turns out to be the daughter of somebody respectable, so that the hero can marry her without loss of face. The cognitio in comedy, in which the characters find out who their relatives are, and who is left of the opposite sex not a relative, and hence available for marriage, is one of the features of comedy that have never changed much: The Confidential Clerk indicates that it still holds the attention of dramatists. There is a brilliant parody of a cognitio at the end of Major Barbara (the fact that the hero of this play is a professor of Greek perhaps indicates an unusual affinity to the conventions of Euripides and Menander), where Undershaft is enabled to break the rule that he cannot appoint his son-in-law as successor by the fact that the son-in-law’s own father married his deceased wife’s sister in Australia, so that the son-in-law is his own first cousin as well as himself. It sounds complicated, but the plots of comedy often are complicated because there is something inherently absurd about complications. As the main character interest in comedy is so often focussed on the defeated characters, comedy regularly illustrates a victory of arbitrary plot over consistency of character. Thus, in striking contrast to tragedy, there can hardly be such a thing as inevitable comedy, as far as the action of the individual play is concerned. That is, we may know that the convention of comedy will make some kind of happy ending inevitable, but still for each play the dramatist must produce a distinctive “gimmick” or “weenie,” to use two disrespectful Hollywood synonyms for anagnorisis. Happy endings do not impress us as true, but as desirable, and they are brought about by manipulation. The watcher of death and tragedy has nothing to do but sit and wait for the inevitable end; but something gets born at the end of comedy, and the watcher of birth is a member of a busy society.

情节的操纵并非总是涉及人物的转变，但即便如此，也并不违反喜剧的规范。出人意料的转变、奇迹般的变化和天意的帮助都是喜剧不可或缺的一部分。此外，无论出现什么，都应该是永久性的：如果一个脾气古怪的人……当他变得可爱时，我们便明白他不会立刻重蹈覆辙，再次陷入仪式性的恶习。那些强调理想而非现实、重视宗教而非科学视角的文明，几乎完全以喜剧的视角来看待戏剧。据说，在印度古典戏剧中，悲剧结局被视为低俗，正如那些热衷于讽刺现实主义的小说家认为喜剧中人为安排的结局低俗一样。

The manipulation of plot does not always involve metamorphosis of character, but there is no violation of comic decorum when it does. Unlikely conversions, miraculous transformations, and providential assistance are inseparable from comedy. Further, whatever emerges is supposed to be there for good: if the curmudgeon becomes lovable, we understand that he will not immediately relapse again into his ritual habit. Civilizations which stress the desirable rather than the real, and the religious as opposed to the scientific perspective, think of drama almost entirely in terms of comedy. In the classical drama of India, we are told, the tragic ending was regarded as bad taste, much as the manipulated endings of comedy are regarded as bad taste by novelists interested in ironic realism.

喜剧的整体神话（通常只呈现其中一小部分）通常具有音乐中所谓的“三段式”结构：英雄的社会反抗老年人的社会并取得胜利，但英雄的社会本身就像一场农神节，一种社会标准的颠倒，让人想起剧中主要情节开始之前的黄金时代。因此，我们看到一个稳定和谐的秩序被愚蠢、执念、遗忘、“傲慢与偏见”或角色自身无法理解的事件所打破，然后又得以恢复。通常，剧中会有一位仁慈的长者，他凌驾于由幽默阻隔所设定的情节之上，从而连接起第一部分和第三部分。例如，《威克菲尔德教区牧师》中，邪恶乡绅的叔叔伯切尔先生（伪装成普通人）就是如此。像印度的《沙恭达罗》这样的长剧，可能会呈现所有三个阶段；像米南德的许多作品那样极其复杂的作品，或许能勾勒出它们的轮廓。但当然，很多时候，第一阶段根本不会呈现：观众只是理解了一种理想的状态，他们知道这种状态比剧中展现的更好，并且他们也意识到这种状态正是剧情最终走向的。这种三段式的剧情，从仪式上看，就像一场夏冬之战，其中冬季占据了中间阶段；从心理上看，它就像是移除了一种神经症或阻塞点，恢复了能量和记忆的畅通无阻。本·琼森式的假面剧，中间穿插着反假面剧，则呈现了一种高度程式化或“抽象”的版本。

The total mythos of comedy, only a small part of which is ordinarily presented, has regularly what in music is called a ternary form: the hero’s society rebels against the society of the senex and triumphs, but the hero’s society is a Saturnalia, a reversal of social standards which recalls a golden age in the past before the main action of the play begins. Thus we have a stable and harmonious order disrupted by folly, obsession, forgetfulness, “pride and prejudice,” or events not understood by the characters themselves, and then restored. Often there is a benevolent grandfather, so to speak, who overrules the action set up by the blocking humor and so links the first and third parts. An example is Mr. Burchell, the disguised uncle of the wicked squire, in The Vicar of Wakefield. A very long play, such as the Indian Sakuntala, may present all three phases; a very intricate one, such as many of Menander’s evidently were, may indicate their outlines. But of course very often the first phase is not given at all: the audience simply understands an ideal state of affairs which it knows to be better than what is revealed in the play, and which it recognizes as like that to which the action leads. This ternary action is, ritually, like a contest of summer and winter in which winter occupies the middle action; psychologically, it is like the removal of a neurosis or blocking point and the restoring of an unbroken current of energy and memory. The Jonsonian masque, with the antimasque in the middle, gives a highly conventionalized or “abstract” version of it.

现在我们来谈谈喜剧的典型人物。在戏剧中，人物塑造取决于功能；人物的性格取决于他在剧中要做的事情。戏剧功能又取决于剧本的结构；人物之所以要做某些事情，是因为剧本具有某种特定的结构。剧本的结构又取决于剧本的类型；如果是喜剧，其结构就需要一个喜剧式的结局。普遍存在的喜剧氛围。因此，当我们谈论典型人物时，我们并非试图将栩栩如生的人物简化为刻板类型，尽管我们确实认为，将栩栩如生的人物与刻板类型对立起来的感伤观念是一种庸俗的错误。所有栩栩如生的人物，无论是在戏剧还是小说中，其一致性都源于与其戏剧功能相符的刻板类型的恰当性。这种刻板类型并非人物本身，但它对于人物而言，就像骨架对于扮演它的演员一样必不可少。

We pass now to the typical characters of comedy. In drama, characterization depends on function; what a character is follows from what he has to do in the play. Dramatic function in its turn depends on the structure of the play; the character has certain things to do because the play has such and such a shape. The structure of the play in its turn depends on the category of the play; if it is a comedy, its structure will require a comic resolution and a prevailing comic mood. Hence when we speak of typical characters, we are not trying to reduce lifelike characters to stock types, though we certainly are suggesting that the sentimental notion of an antithesis between the lifelike character and the stock type is a vulgar error. All lifelike characters, whether in drama or fiction, owe their consistency to the appropriateness of the stock type which belongs to their dramatic function. That stock type is not the character but it is as necessary to the character as a skeleton is to the actor who plays it.

关于喜剧人物的刻画，《逻辑哲学论》列举了三种喜剧人物：冒名顶替者（ alazons）、自嘲者（ eirons ）和丑角（ bomolochoi ）。这份清单与《伦理学》中的一段文字密切相关，该段文字对比了前两种人物，并进一步将丑角与亚里士多德称之为粗鄙者（agroikos ，字面意思是“乡巴佬”）的人物进行了对比。我们可以合理地将粗鄙者视为第四种人物类型，这样我们就有了两组对立的人物。自嘲者和冒名顶替者的较量构成了喜剧情节的基础，而丑角和粗鄙者则使喜剧氛围两极分化。

With regard to the characterization of comedy, the Tractatus lists three types of comic characters: the alazons or impostors, the eirons or self-deprecators, and the buffoons (bomolochoi). This list is closely related to a passage in the Ethics which contrasts the first two, and then goes on to contrast the buffoon with a character whom Aristotle calls agroikos or churlish, literally rustic. We may reasonably accept the churl as a fourth character type, and so we have two opposed pairs. The contest of eiron and alazon forms the basis of the comic action, and the buffoon and the churl polarize the comic mood.

我们之前讨论过“eiron”和“alazon”这两个词。喜剧中那些滑稽的、令人啼笑皆非的角色几乎都是冒名顶替者，尽管他们更常见的特征是缺乏自知之明，而非单纯的虚伪。大量喜剧场景中，一个角色自鸣得意地独白，而另一个角色则对着观众冷嘲热讽，这最纯粹地展现了“eiron”和“alazon”之间的较量，同时也表明观众更倾向于“eiron”一方。在“alazon”阵营中，最核心的角色是“ senex iratus”（老顽固），或者说“重父亲”，他暴怒、威胁、执念重重、又容易轻信他人，这些都与浪漫故事中的一些恶魔角色（例如波吕斐摩斯）颇为相似。有时，某个角色可能具有这类人物的戏剧功能，却不具备其相应的特征：例如《汤姆·琼斯》中的奥尔沃西乡绅，就剧情而言，他的行为几乎和韦斯特恩乡绅一样愚蠢。在众多扮演父亲角色的人物中，有人提到了“光荣的迈尔斯”（miles gloriosus）：他之所以受欢迎，很大程度上是因为他只会夸夸其谈，却鲜有实际行动，因此对于剧作家而言，他比任何沉默寡言的英雄都更有用。文艺复兴时期喜剧中的学究（通常是神秘学的学生）、纨绔子弟或自命不凡之辈，以及类似的人物，无需赘述。女性阿莱宗（alazon）则较为罕见：卡塔琳娜（Katharina）泼妇在某种程度上代表了女性版的“光荣的迈尔斯”，而可笑的贵妇则代表了女性版的学究，但阻碍真正女英雄的“威胁”或妖女，更多地是作为情节剧或浪漫剧中的阴险人物出现，而不是作为喜剧中的滑稽人物出现。

We have previously dealt with the terms eiron and alazon. The humorous blocking characters of comedy are nearly always impostors, though it is more frequently a lack of self-knowledge than simple hypocrisy that characterizes them. The multitudes of comic scenes in which one character complacently soliloquizes while another makes sarcastic asides to the audience show the contest of eiron and alazon in its purest form, and show too that the audience is sympathetic to the eiron side. Central to the alazon group is the senex iratus or heavy father, who with his rages and threats, his obsessions and his gullibility, seems closely related to some of the demonic characters of romance, such as Polyphemus. Occasionally a character may have the dramatic function of such a figure without his characteristics: an example is Squire Allworthy in Tom Jones, who as far as the plot is concerned behaves almost as stupidly as Squire Western. Of heavy-father surrogates, the miles gloriosus has been mentioned: his popularity is largely due to the fact that he is a man of words rather than deeds, and is consequently far more useful to a practising dramatist than any tight-lipped hero could ever be. The pedant, in Renaissance comedy often a student of the occult sciences, the fop or coxcomb, and similar humors, require no comment. The female alazon is rare: Katharina the shrew represents to some extent a female miles gloriosus, and the précieuse ridicule a female pedant, but the “menace” or siren who gets in the way of the true heroine is more often found as a sinister figure of melodrama or romance than as a ridiculous figure in comedy.

需要对“伪善人物”（eiron persons ）进行更多关注。这一群体的核心是英雄，他之所以是伪善人物，是因为正如前文所述，剧作家往往会淡化他的形象，使他性格较为中立且不鲜明。其次是女主角，她也常常被弱化：在古希腊喜剧中，当一位女孩陪伴男主角凯旋时，她通常只是一个舞台道具，一个之前未曾介绍过的“变身人物”（muta persona） 。当女主角乔装打扮或通过其他手段促成喜剧结局时，一种更为复杂的认知方式得以实现，使得英雄苦苦寻觅之人，最终竟是一直在寻找他的人。莎士比亚对这种“屈尊求爱”主题的偏爱在此只需一提，因为它更自然地属于浪漫主义神话的范畴。

The eiron figures need a little more attention. Central to this group is the hero, who is an eiron figure because, as explained, the dramatist tends to play him down and make him rather neutral and unformed in character. Next in importance is the heroine, also often played down: in Old Comedy, when a girl accompanies a male hero in his triumph, she is generally a stage prop, a muta persona not previously introduced. A more difficult form of cognitio is achieved when the heroine disguises herself or through some other device brings about the comic resolution, so that the person whom the hero is seeking turns out to be the person who has sought him. The fondness of Shakespeare for this “she stoops to conquer” theme needs only to be mentioned here, as it belongs more naturally to the mythos of romance.

另一个核心人物是受托策划阴谋诡计、最终促成英雄胜利的角色。在罗马喜剧中，这类角色几乎总是狡猾的奴隶（dolosus servus）；在文艺复兴时期的喜剧中，他变成了在欧洲大陆戏剧中常见的诡计多端的男仆；在西班牙戏剧中，他被称为“ gracioso” （滑稽男仆）。现代观众最熟悉的此类角色是《费加罗的婚礼》和《唐璜》中的莱波雷洛。通过像米考伯和斯科特《圣罗南井》中的托奇伍德这样带有丑角色彩的十九世纪中间人物（他们和gracioso一样，都带有滑稽人物的特征），这类角色演变成了现代小说中的业余侦探。P·G·伍德豪斯笔下的吉夫斯则是更直接的继承者。通常，剧中还会引入一些来自同一家族的女性知己，以推动剧情的顺利发展。伊丽莎白时代的喜剧中还有另一种类型的骗子，以拉尔夫·罗伊斯·多伊斯笔下的马修·梅里格里克为代表。人们普遍认为，这个角色源于道德剧中的恶习或不法行为：无论历史学家如何解释其起源，这种类比通常都相当贴切。这个恶习，姑且这么称呼他吧，对喜剧作家来说非常有用，因为他纯粹出于恶作剧的爱好而行动，只需极少的动机就能引发喜剧情节。这个恶习可能像帕克一样轻松愉快，也可能像《无事生非》中的唐璜一样阴险狡诈，但通常来说，尽管名字里带有“恶”，他的所作所为却是出于善意。普劳图斯笔下的一个狡猾奴隶在独白中自诩为喜剧情节的“建筑师”：这类角色执行着作者的意愿，最终导向一个皆大欢喜的结局。他实际上是喜剧的灵魂，而莎士比亚笔下最鲜明的两个此类角色——帕克和爱丽儿——也都是具有精神特质的存在。狡猾的奴隶往往将自身的自由视为其辛勤劳作的最终回报：爱丽儿对自由的渴望也源于此。

Another central eiron figure is the type entrusted with hatching the schemes which bring about the hero’s victory. This character in Roman comedy is almost always a tricky slave (dolosus servus), and in Renaissance comedy he becomes the scheming valet who is so frequent in Continental plays, and in Spanish drama is called the gracioso. Modern audiences are most familiar with him in Figaro and in the Leporello of Don Giovanni. Through such intermediate nineteenth-century figures as Micawber and the Touchwood of Scott’s St. Ronan’s Well, who, like the gracioso, have buffoon affiliations, he evolves into the amateur detective of modern fiction. The Jeeves of P. G. Wodehouse is a more direct descendant. Female confidantes of the same general family are often brought in to oil the machinery of the well-made play. Elizabethan comedy had another type of trickster, represented by the Matthew Merrygreek of Ralph Roister Doister, who is generally said to be developed from the vice or iniquity of the morality plays: as usual, the analogy is sound enough, whatever historians decide about origins. The vice, to give him that name, is very useful to a comic dramatist because he acts from pure love of mischief, and can set a comic action going with the minimum of motivation. The vice may be as light-hearted as Puck or as malignant as Don John in Much Ado, but as a rule the vice’s activity is, in spite of his name, benevolent. One of the tricky slaves in Plautus, in a soliloquy, boasts that he is the architectus of the comic action: such a character carries out the will of the author to reach a happy ending. He is in fact the spirit of comedy, and the two clearest examples of the type in Shakespeare, Puck and Ariel, are both spiritual beings. The tricky slave often has his own freedom in mind as the reward of his exertions: Ariel’s longing for release is in the same tradition.

恶习的角色往往擅长伪装，而且这种类型的恶习通常可以通过伪装来识别。一个很好的例子是本·琼森的《人各有癖》中的脑虫，它将剧中的情节称为它的“变形日”。同样，爱丽儿也必须克服“隐形入场”这一棘手的舞台指示。当英雄是一个厚脸皮、不计后果的年轻人，他精心策划自己的阴谋，欺骗富有的父亲或叔叔，骗取遗产和心仪的女孩时，恶习就与英雄结合在一起。

The role of the vice includes a great deal of disguising, and the type may often be recognized by disguise. A good example is the Brainworm of Jonson’s Every Man in His Humour, who calls the action of the play the day of his metamorphoses. Similarly Ariel has to surmount the difficult stage direction of “Enter invisible.” The vice is combined with the hero whenever the latter is a cheeky, improvident young man who hatches his own schemes and cheats his rich father or uncle into giving him his patrimony along with the girl.

另一种“隐士”类型鲜为人知。这类角色通常是一位年长的男性，他在剧作开始时选择退出，最终又回归。他往往是一位父亲，其动机是观察儿子的行动。《人各有志》的剧情就是由老诺威尔以这种方式展开的。《炼金术士》中，屋主洛维特的消失与回归也具有同样的戏剧功能，尽管人物塑造有所不同。莎士比亚作品中最典型的例子是《一报还一报》中的公爵，但莎士比亚对这类角色的运用远比乍看之下更为频繁。在莎士比亚的作品中，这种“隐士”很少是真正的“建筑师”：帕克和爱丽儿都是奉一位年长男性的命令行事——如果可以暂时将奥伯龙称为“人”的话。在《暴风雨》中，莎士比亚回归了阿里斯托芬开创的喜剧模式，在阿里斯托芬的喜剧模式中，一位年长男性并非退出剧情，而是在舞台上推动剧情发展。在莎士比亚的戏剧中，当女主角扮演反派角色时，她往往与父亲有着密切的联系，即便父亲并未出场，例如海伦娜的父亲将医学知识传授给她，或是波西亚的父亲安排了匣子计划。一个更为传统的例子是，在《鸡尾酒会》中，精神科医生也扮演了类似的仁慈的普洛斯彼罗式角色。此外，我们还可以将其与《贵妇不宜焚烧》中女主角的父亲——那位神秘的炼金术士相比较。这种模式并非喜剧所独有：例如，波洛涅斯……文学教育的诸多弊端之一，便是三次试图扮演退隐的父权角色，一次就太多了。 《哈姆雷特》和《李尔王》都包含一些讽刺性的副线情节，这些情节是对老套喜剧主题的戏仿，格洛斯特的故事就是一个常见的喜剧主题：一个容易上当受骗的老头被一个聪明却不择手段的儿子欺骗。

Another eiron type has not been much noticed. This is a character, generally an older man, who begins the action of the play by withdrawing from it, and ends the play by returning. He is often a father with the motive of seeing what his son will do. The action of Every Man in His Humour is set going in this way by Knowell Senior. The disappearance and return of Lovewit, the owner of the house which is the scene of The Alchemist, has the same dramatic function, though the characterization is different. The clearest Shakespearean example is the Duke in Measure for Measure, but Shakespeare is more addicted to the type than might appear at first glance. In Shakespeare the vice is rarely the real architectus: Puck and Ariel both act under orders from an older man. if one may call Oberon a man for the moment. In The Tempest Shakespeare returns to a comic action established by Aristophanes, in which an older man, instead of retiring from the action, builds it up on the stage. When the heroine takes the vice role in Shakespeare, she is often significantly related to her father, even when the father is not in the play at all, like the father of Helena, who gives her his medical knowledge, or the father of Portia, who arranges the scheme of the caskets. A more conventionally treated example of the same benevolent Prospero figure turned up recently in the psychiatrist of The Cocktail Party, and one may compare the mysterious alchemist who is the father of the heroine of The Lady’s Not for Burning. The formula is not confined to comedy: Polonius, who shows so many of the disadvantages of a literary education, attempts the role of a retreating paternal eiron three times, once too often. Hamlet and King Lear contain subplots which are ironic versions of stock comic themes, Gloucester’s story being the regular comedy theme of the gullible senex swindled by a clever and unprincipled son.

现在我们来谈谈丑角，这类角色的作用在于烘托节日气氛，而非推动剧情发展。与罗马喜剧不同，文艺复兴时期的喜剧中这类角色种类繁多，包括职业弄臣、小丑、侍童、歌手，以及一些带有固定喜剧习惯的配角，例如用词不当或带有外国口音。这类配角中最古老的是寄生虫，他们或许会被赋予一些任务，例如本·琼森在《狐狸》中赋予莫斯卡一个恶习的角色，但作为寄生虫，他们除了谈论自己的食欲来取悦观众之外，别无他事。寄生虫主要源于古希腊中古喜剧，而古希腊喜剧似乎充满了美食元素。在古希腊中古喜剧中，寄生虫自然而然地与另一种常见的丑角——厨师——紧密联系在一起。厨师是一个典型的喜剧角色，他会在喜剧中穿插出现，忙碌地忙碌着，发号施令，并就烹饪的奥秘发表长篇大论。在厨师这个角色中，滑稽演员或艺人并非像寄生虫那样只是个无关紧要的配角，而更像是司仪，是喜剧氛围的中心。莎士比亚的作品中并没有厨师这个角色，尽管在《错误的喜剧》中有对厨师的精彩描写，但类似的角色常常与一位热情健谈的主人联系在一起，例如《风流娘儿们》中的“疯主人”或《鞋匠的节日》中的西蒙·艾尔。在米德尔顿的《捉拿老人的计谋》中，疯主人的形象与恶习结合在一起。在福斯塔夫和托比·贝尔奇爵士身上，我们可以看到滑稽演员或艺人与寄生虫以及狂欢大师之间的相似之处。如果我们仔细研究这个娱乐者或主持人的角色，我们很快就会意识到，它是阿里斯托芬喜剧中合唱队所代表的角色的发展，而合唱队又可以追溯到喜剧起源的狂欢节或庆祝活动。

We pass now to the buffoon types, those whose function it is to increase the mood of festivity rather than to contribute to the plot. Renaissance comedy, unlike Roman comedy, had a great variety of such characters, professional fools, clowns, pages, singers, and incidental characters with established comic habits like malapropism or foreign accents. The oldest buffoon of this incidental nature is the parasite, who may be given something to do, as Jonson gives Mosca the role of a vice in Volpone, but who, qua parasite, does nothing but entertain the audience by talking about his appetite. He derives chiefly from Greek Middle Comedy, which appears to have been very full of food, and where he was, not unnaturally, closely associated with another established buffoon type, the cook, a conventional figure who breaks into comedies to bustle and order about and make long speeches about the mysteries of cooking. In the role of cook the buffoon or entertainer appears, not simply as a gratuitous addition like the parasite, but as something more like a master of ceremonies, a center for the comic mood. There is no cook in Shakespeare, though there is a superb description of one in the Comedy of Errors, but a similar role is often attached to a jovial and loquacious host, like the “mad host” of The Merry Wives or the Simon Eyre of The Shoemakers Holiday. In Middleton’s A Trick to Catch the Old One the mad host type is combined with the vice. In Falstaff and Sir Toby Belch we can see the affinities of the buffoon or entertainer type both with the parasite and with the master of revels. If we study this entertainer or host role carefully we shall soon realize that it is a development of what in Aristophanic comedy is represented by the chorus, and which in its turn goes back to the komos or revel from which comedy is said to be descended.

最后，还有第四类人，我们用“agroikos”一词来指代，它通常根据语境指粗鲁或乡土气息浓厚的人。这类人也可以扩展到伊丽莎白时代的傻瓜，以及杂耍剧中所谓的“捧哏”——那些严肃或不善言辞的角色，他们允许……可以说，幽默感与他相得益彰。我们会在吝啬、势利或自命不凡的角色身上发现粗鄙之人的影子，他们拒绝参加庆祝活动，扫兴地试图阻止欢乐，或者像马伏里奥那样，把食物和饮料锁起来而不是分发出去。《皆大欢喜》中忧郁的雅克在最后的庆祝活动中愤然离去，与此密切相关。在《皆大欢喜》中闷闷不乐、以自我为中心的伯特伦身上，这种类型与英雄形象的结合非常独特而巧妙。然而，更常见的情况是，粗鄙之人属于“阿莱宗”一类，喜剧中所有吝啬的老头，包括夏洛克，都是粗鄙之人。在《暴风雨》中，卡利班与粗鄙之人的关系，与爱丽儿与恶习或狡猾的奴隶的关系非常相似。但通常情况下，在气氛较为轻松愉悦的剧作中，我们可以简单地将“agroikos”翻译为“乡巴佬”，例如在都市戏剧中为观众带来欢乐的无数乡绅和类似角色。这类角色并非否定欢庆的氛围，而是凸显了这种氛围的广度。在田园喜剧中，理想化的乡村生活美德可以由一位代表田园理想的淳朴男子来体现，例如《皆大欢喜》中的科林。科林扮演的角色与都市喜剧中的“乡巴佬”或“土包子”类似，但其道德态度却截然相反。由此可见，戏剧结构是文学作品中一个恒定不变的因素，而道德态度则是一个可变的因素。

Finally, there is a fourth group to which we have assigned the word agroikos, and which usually means either churlish or rustic, depending on the context. This type may also be extended to cover the Elizabethan gull and what in vaudeville used to be called the straight man, the solemn or inarticulate character who allows the humor to bounce off him, so to speak. We find churls in the miserly, snobbish, or priggish characters whose role is that of the refuser of festivity, the killjoy who tries to stop the fun, or, like Malvolio, locks up the food and drink instead of dispensing it. The melancholy Jaques of As You Like It, who walks out on the final festivities, is closely related. In the sulky and self-centered Bertram of All’s Well there is a most unusual and ingenious combination of this type with the hero. More often, however, the churl belongs to the alazon group, all miserly old men in comedies, including Shylock, being churls. In The Tempest Caliban has much the same relation to the churlish type that Ariel has to the vice or tricky slave. But often, where the mood is more light-hearted, we may translate agroikos simply by rustic, as with the innumerable country squires and similar characters who provide amusement in the urban setting of drama. Such types do not refuse the mood of festivity, but they mark the extent of its range. In a pastoral comedy the idealized virtues of rural life may be represented by a simple man who speaks for the pastoral ideal, like Corin in As You Like It. Corin has the same agroikos role as the “rube” or “hayseed” of more citified comedies, but the moral attitude to the role is reversed. Again we notice the principle that dramatic structure is a permanent and moral attitude a variable factor in literature.

在一部极具讽刺意味的喜剧中，可能会出现另一种类型的角色扮演拒绝庆祝的角色。喜剧越是讽刺，社会就越荒诞，而荒诞的社会可能会受到谴责，或者至少会与一个我们称之为“直言不讳者”的角色形成对比。这个角色直言不讳地倡导某种道德规范，并赢得了观众的同情。威彻利的《曼利》虽然为这类角色命名，但他并不是一个特别好的例子：更好的例子是《伪君子》中的克莱昂特。当剧作的基调足够讽刺，以至于让观众对社会规范的理解感到困惑时，这样的角色就显得恰当了：他大致相当于悲剧中的合唱队，合唱队存在的目的也类似。当语气从讽刺加深到苦涩时，平实的人可能会变成一个不满现状的人或愤世嫉俗者，他可能在道德上优于他的社会，就像马斯顿的同名戏剧中的人物那样，但他也可能因为嫉妒而变得过于邪恶，只不过是他所在社会邪恶的另一个方面，就像忒耳西忒斯，或者在某种程度上像阿佩曼图斯。

In a very ironic comedy a different type of character may play the role of the refuser of festivity. The more ironic the comedy, the more absurd the society, and an absurd society may be condemned by, or at least contrasted with, a character that we may call the plain dealer, an outspoken advocate of a kind of moral norm who has the sympathy of the audience. Wycherley’s Manly, though he provides the name for the type, is not a particularly good example of it: a much better one is the Cléante of Tartuffe. Such a character is appropriate when the tone is ironic enough to get the audience confused about its sense of the social norm: he corresponds roughly to the chorus in a tragedy, which is there for a similar reason. When the tone deepens from the ironic to the bitter, the plain dealer may become a malcontent or railer, who may be morally superior to his society, as he is to some extent in Marston’s play of that name, but who may also be too motivated by envy to be much more than another aspect of his society’s evil, like Thersites, or to some extent Apemantus.

在悲剧中，怜悯和恐惧，即道德上的吸引和排斥，被唤起又被释放。喜剧似乎比悲剧更有效地运用了社会乃至道德判断，然而喜剧似乎也以同样的方式唤起并释放了相应的同情和嘲讽。喜剧的范畴从最尖刻的讽刺到最梦幻的愿望实现的浪漫故事，但其结构模式和人物塑造在整个范围内却大同小异。这种喜剧结构在各种态度下保持统一的原则在阿里斯托芬的作品中体现得淋漓尽致。阿里斯托芬是最具个人风格的作家，他对所有问题的看法都贯穿于他的戏剧之中。我们知道他渴望与斯巴达和平相处，并且憎恨克里昂，因此，当他的喜剧描绘和平的达成和克里昂的战败时，我们知道他对此表示赞同，也希望他的观众对此表示赞同。但在《公民大会》中，一群乔装打扮的妇女强行通过了一项共产主义计划，该计划是对柏拉图式共和制的拙劣模仿，她们还以一些惊人的改进开启了其性共产主义的先河。想必阿里斯托芬并未完全赞同这一做法，但这部喜剧遵循了相同的模式和结局。在《鸟》中，挑战宙斯并用其“云中世界”遮蔽奥林匹斯山的皮斯泰泰罗斯，与飞升天堂并为雅典带来黄金时代的和平使者特里盖奥斯一样，获得了同样的胜利。

In tragedy, pity and fear, the emotions of moral attraction and repulsion, are raised and cast out. Comedy seems to make a more functional use of the social, even the moral judgement, than tragedy, yet comedy seems to raise the corresponding emotions, which are sympathy and ridicule, and cast them out in the same way. Comedy ranges from the most savage irony to the most dreamy wish-fulfilment romance, but its structural patterns and characterization are much the same throughout its range. This principle of the uniformity of comic structure through a variety of attitudes is clear in Aristophanes. Aristophanes is the most personal of writers, and his opinions on every subject are written all over his plays. We know that he wanted peace with Sparta and that he hated Cleon, so when his comedy depicts the attaining of peace and the defeat of Cleon we know that he approved and wanted his audience to approve. But in Ecclesiazusae a band of women in disguise railroad a communistic scheme through the Assembly which is a horrid parody of a Platonic republic, and proceed to inaugurate its sexual communism with some astonishing improvements. Presumably Aristophanes did not altogether endorse this, yet the comedy follows the same pattern and the same resolution. In The Birds the Peisthetairos who defies Zeus and blocks out Olympus with his Cloud-Cuckoo-Land is accorded the same triumph that is given to the Trygaios of the Peace who flies to heaven and brings a golden age back to Athens.

现在让我们来考察一下介于讽刺和浪漫之间的各种喜剧结构。喜剧一端与讽刺和讽刺相融合，另一端与浪漫相融合，因此，如果喜剧结构存在不同的阶段或类型，那么其中一些将与某些讽刺和浪漫类型密切相关。此时，我们的论证中出现了一种略显晦涩的对称性，这似乎与音乐中的五度循环在文学上有一些相似之处。我识别出每种神话体系的六个阶段，其中三个阶段与相邻神话体系的阶段平行。喜剧的前三个阶段与讽刺和讽刺的前三个阶段平行，后三个阶段与浪漫的后三个阶段平行。讽刺喜剧和喜剧讽刺之间的区别，或者浪漫喜剧和喜剧浪漫之间的区别，虽然模糊不清，但并非毫无区别。

Let us look now at a variety of comic structures between the extremes of irony and romance. As comedy blends into irony and satire at one end and into romance at the other, if there are different phases or types of comic structure, some of them will be closely parallel to some of the types of irony and of romance. A somewhat forbidding piece of symmetry turns up in our argument at this point, which seems to have some literary analogy to the circle of fifths in music. I recognize six phases of each mythos, three being parallel to the phases of a neighboring mythos. The first three phases of comedy are parallel to the first three phases of irony and satire, and the second three to the second three of romance. The distinction between an ironic comedy and a comic satire, or between a romantic comedy and a comic romance, is tenuous, but not quite a distinction without a difference.

喜剧的第一阶段，或者说最具讽刺意味的阶段，自然是幽默的社会取得胜利或保持不败的阶段。这种喜剧的一个例子是《炼金术士》，剧中，归来的“铁匠”洛夫维特加入了恶棍们的行列，而朴实无华的苏利则被愚弄。《乞丐歌剧》的结局也有类似的转折：（假想的）作者认为主人公被绞死是一个喜剧结局，但经理告诉他，无论麦克希斯的道德状况如何，观众的喜剧礼仪要求赦免他。这一阶段的喜剧展现了文艺复兴时期评论家所说的“世事之道” （speculum consuetudinis ， cosi fan tutte）。当幽默的社会彻底瓦解，没有任何事物取而代之时，就会产生更强烈的讽刺效果，例如《伤心之家》和契诃夫作品中经常出现的情况。

The first or most ironic phase of comedy is, naturally, the one in which a humorous society triumphs or remains undefeated. A good example of a comedy of this type is The Alchemist, in which the returning eiron Lovewit joins the rascals, and the plain dealer Surly is made a fool of. In The Beggar’s Opera there is a similar twist to the ending: the (projected) author feels that the hanging of the hero is a comic ending, but is informed by the manager that the audience’s sense of comic decorum demands a reprieve, whatever Macheath’s moral status. This phase of comedy presents what Renaissance critics called speculum consuetudinis, the way of the world, cosi fan tutte. A more intense irony is achieved when the humorous society simply disintegrates without anything taking its place, as in Heartbreak House and frequently in Chekhov.

在讽刺喜剧中，我们注意到魔鬼的世界总是如影随形。罗马喜剧中，愤怒的老者（senex iratus）的怒火主要指向那些狡猾的奴隶，他们会受到磨坊的折磨、鞭笞致死、钉十字架、将头浸入焦油中点燃等等的威胁——所有这些刑罚在现实生活中都可能也确实会加诸于奴隶身上。普劳图斯的一部作品的尾声告诉我们，那个在台词中失态的奴隶演员即将被鞭打；在米南德的一部残篇中，一个奴隶被绑起来，在舞台上被火把烧死。人们有时会觉得，普劳图斯和泰伦提乌斯时代的观众在观看耶稣受难时会全程哄堂大笑。我们或许会将此归因于奴隶社会的残酷，但我们随后会想起，《米卡多》中也出现了沸油刑和活埋（“如此闷热的死法”）。现代舞台上两部生动有趣的喜剧是《鸡尾酒会》和《淑女不宜焚烧》，但前者以十字架为背景，后者则以火刑柱为背景。夏洛克的刀和安杰洛的绞刑架出现在莎士比亚的作品中：在《一报还一报》中，每个男性角色都曾面临死亡的威胁。喜剧的情节往往朝着某种荒谬却并非无害的困境发展。我们也能注意到，喜剧作家常常试图让剧情尽可能接近英雄的灾难性失败，然后又迅速扭转局面。逃避或违反残酷的法律往往是一场险象环生的较量。 《伪君子》结尾国王的干预是刻意为之：剧中的情节本身并没有阻止伪君子获胜的因素。在最后一本书中，汤姆·琼斯被指控犯有谋杀、乱伦、债务和欺诈罪，被朋友、监护人和爱人抛弃，在这一切变成幻象之前，他确实是一个悲惨的人物。任何读者都能想到许多喜剧，在这些喜剧中，对死亡的恐惧，有时甚至是可怕的死亡，一直笼罩着主角直到最后，但这种恐惧很快就消失了，以至于人们几乎感觉像是从噩梦中醒来。

We notice in ironic comedy that the demonic world is never far away. The rages of the senex iratus in Roman comedy are directed mainly at the tricky slave, who is threatened with the mill, with being flogged to death, with crucifixion, with having his head dipped in tar and set on fire, and the like, all penalties that could be and were exacted from slaves in life. An epilogue in Plautus informs us that the slave-actor who has blown up in his lines will now be flogged; in one of the Menander fragments a slave is tied up and burned with a torch on the stage. One sometimes gets the impression that the audience of Plautus and Terence would have guffawed uproariously all through the Passion. We may ascribe this to the brutality of a slave society, but then we remember that boiling oil and burying alive (“such a stuffy death”) turn up in The Mikado. Two lively comedies of the modern stage are The Cocktail Party and The Lady’s Not for Burning, but the cross appears in the background of the one and the stake in the background of the other. Shylock’s knife and Angelo’s gallows appear in Shakespeare: in Measure for Measure every male character is at one time or another threatened with death. The action of comedy moves toward a deliverance from something which, if absurd, is by no means invariably harmless. We notice too how frequently a comic dramatist tries to bring his action as close to a catastrophic overthrow of the hero as he can get it, and then reverses the action as quickly as possible. The evading or breaking of a cruel law is often a very narrow squeeze. The intervention of the king at the end of Tartuffe is deliberately arbitrary: there is nothing in the action of the play itself to prevent Tartuffe’s triumph. Tom Jones in the final book, accused of murder, incest, debt, and double-dealing, cast off by friends, guardian, and sweetheart, is a woeful figure indeed before all these turn into illusions. Any reader can think of many comedies in which the fear of death, sometimes a hideous death, hangs over the central character to the end, and is dispelled so quickly that one has almost the sense of awakening from nightmare.

有时，救赎者的确是​​神明，例如《佩里克利斯》中的狄安娜；在《伪君子》中，救赎者是国王，他被视为观众的一部分，是观众意志的化身。大量的喜剧故事，无论是戏剧还是小说，似乎都在临近结尾时走向潜在的悲剧危机，我称之为“仪式性死亡点”——这个表达略显笨拙，我很乐意用一个更贴切的词来代替。评论家们很少注意到这个特点，但一旦出现，它就如同赋格曲中的紧缩音一样清晰可辨，两者在某些方面颇为相似。在斯莫利特的《汉弗莱·克林克》（我选择这部作品是因为没有人会怀疑斯莫利特是刻意虚构神话，而只会认为他是在遵循惯例，至少就情节而言），主人公们在一场马车翻覆的事故中险些溺水身亡；随后，他们被带到附近的一所房子里晾干身体，并进行一场“认罪仪式”（cognitio）。仪式中，他们的家庭关系被重新梳理，身世之谜被揭开，名字也被更改。类似的仪式性死亡节点几乎出现在所有主人公被囚禁或女主人公身患绝症最终迎来圆满结局的故事中。

Sometimes the redeeming agent actually is divine, like Diana in Pericles; in Tartuffe it is the king, who is conceived as a part of the audience and the incarnation of its will. An extraordinary number of comic stories, both in drama and fiction, seem to approach a potentially tragic crisis near the end, a feature that I may call the “point of ritual death”—a clumsy expression that I would gladly surrender for a better one. It is a feature not often noticed by critics, but when it is present it is as unmistakably present as a stretto in a fugue, which it somewhat resembles. In Smollett’s Humphry Clinker (I select this because no one will suspect Smollett of deliberate mythopoeia but only of following convention, at least as far as his plot is concerned), the main characters are nearly drowned in an accident with an upset carriage; they are then taken to a nearby house to dry off, and a cognitio takes place, in the course of which their family relationships are regrouped, secrets of birth brought to light, and names changed. Similar points of ritual death may be marked in almost any story that imprisons the hero or gives the heroine a nearly mortal illness before an eventually happy ending.

有时，仪式性死亡的意义并不重要，它并非情节要素，而仅仅是一种基调的转变。每个人都会注意到，在喜剧作品中，即使是一些非常琐碎的电影和杂志故事，临近结尾时，基调也会突然变得严肃、感伤，或是预示着潜在的灾难。在奥尔德斯·赫胥黎的《铬黄》中，主人公丹尼斯在自我反思的过程中，几乎萌生了自杀的念头；在赫胥黎后期的大多数作品中，类似的暴力行为（通常是自杀）都会在相应的节点出现。在《达洛维夫人》中，塞普蒂默斯的自杀在女主人公的宴会上，成为了她仪式性死亡的转折点。莎士比亚的作品中也有一些有趣的变体：例如，小丑会在临近结尾发表一段演讲，此时小丑的面具突然脱落，我们得以直视一个饱受殴打和嘲笑的奴隶的脸庞。例如， 《错误的喜剧》中以“我真是个蠢驴”开头的德罗米奥的演讲，以及《皆大欢喜》中小丑以“我是个林中人”开头的演讲。
