Sometimes the point of ritual death is vestigial, not an element in the plot but a mere change of tone. Everyone will have noted in comic actions, even in very trivial movies and magazine stories, a point near the end at which the tone suddenly becomes serious, sentimental, or ominous of potential catastrophe. In Aldous Huxley’s Chrome Yellow, the hero Denis comes to a point of self-evaluation in which suicide nearly suggests itself: in most of Huxley’s later books some violent action, generally suicidal, occurs at the corresponding point. In Mrs. Dalloway the actual suicide of Septimus becomes a point of ritual death for the heroine in the middle of her party. There are also some interesting Shakespearean variations of the device: a clown, for instance, will make a speech near the end in which the buffoon’s mask suddenly falls off and we look straight into the face of a beaten and ridiculed slave. Examples are the speech of Dromio of Ephesus beginning “I am an ass indeed” in the Comedy of Errors, and the speech of the Clown in All’s Well beginning “I am a woodland fellow.”

喜剧的第二阶段，最简单的形式是这样的：主人公并不改变一个滑稽的社会，而只是逃离或躲避它，留下它原有的结构。这一阶段的讽刺更为复杂：当一个社会由主人公构建或围绕他构建时，这个社会却不够真实或强大，无法真正发挥作用。在这种情况下，主人公本身通常至少在某种程度上是滑稽幽默或精神上的逃亡者，我们看到的要么是主人公的幻想被更强大的现实所挫败，要么是两种幻想的冲突。这是喜剧的堂吉诃德式阶段，对于戏剧来说是一个难以处理的阶段，尽管《野鸭》是一个相当纯粹的例子，但在戏剧中，它通常作为另一个阶段的次要主题出现。因此，在《炼金术士》中，伊壁鸠鲁·玛门爵士关于如何使用贤者之石的梦想，如同堂吉诃德的梦想一样，是一个宏大的梦想，使他成为浮士德（剧中也提到了浮士德）的讽刺模仿，正如堂吉诃德是阿玛迪斯和兰斯洛特的讽刺模仿一样。当基调更加轻松时，喜剧式的结局可能足以抹去所有堂吉诃德式的幻想。在《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》中，主题是喜剧中最古老的主题之一——解放奴隶，而剧情的展开告诉我们，吉姆在汤姆·索亚的迂腐弄巧成拙之前就已经获得了自由。由于这一阶段蕴含着无与伦比的双关讽刺机会，因此它深受亨利·詹姆斯的喜爱：或许他对这一阶段最深入的研究是《圣泉》，其中的主人公是对普洛斯彼罗式人物的讽刺模仿，他试图在眼前的社会基础上创造另一个社会。

The second phase of comedy, in its simplest form, is a comedy in which the hero does not transform a humorous society but simply escapes or runs away from it, leaving its structure as it was before. A more complex irony in this phase is achieved when a society is constructed by or around a hero, but proves not sufficiently real or strong to impose itself. In this situation the hero is usually himself at least partly a comic humor or mental runaway, and we have either a hero’s illusion thwarted by a superior reality or a clash of two illusions. This is the quixotic phase of comedy, a difficult phase for drama, though The Wild Duck is a fairly pure example of it, and in drama it usually appears as a subordinate theme of another phase. Thus in The Alchemist Sir Epicure Mammon’s dream of what he will do with the philosopher’s stone is, like Quixote’s, a gigantic dream, and makes him an ironic parody of Faustus (who is mentioned in the play), in the same way that Quixote is an ironic parody of Amadis and Lancelot. When the tone is more light-hearted, the comic resolution may be strong enough to sweep over all quixotic illusions. In Huckleberry Finn the main theme is one of the oldest in comedy, the freeing of a slave, and the cognitio tells us that Jim had already been set free before his escape was bungled by Tom Sawyer’s pedantries. Because of its unrivalled opportunities for double-edged irony, this phase is a favorite of Henry James: perhaps his most searching study of it is The Sacred Fount, where the hero is an ironic parody of a Prospero figure creating another society out of the one in front of him.

喜剧的第三阶段是我们一直在讨论的正常阶段，在这个阶段中，老年人的滑稽幽默或其他幽默让位于年轻人的欲望。喜剧规范的观念如此根深蒂固，以至于当莎士比亚试图在《皆大欢喜》中颠覆这一模式，让两位长者强迫伯特伦娶海伦娜时，结果却成了一部不受欢迎的“问题剧”，其中还暗示着某种不祥之兆。我们已经注意到，喜剧的认知（cognitio）非常注重厘清新社会的细节，区分新娘与姐妹、父母与养父母。儿子和父亲之间经常发生冲突，这意味着他们经常会为了同一个女孩而成为竞争对手，而主人公的新娘和母亲之间的心理联盟也常常被明确表达或暗示出来。喜剧中偶尔出现的“恶作剧”，例如在复辟时期，不仅与婚姻不忠有关，还与某种喜剧式的幽默密切相关。俄狄浦斯情结是指主人公取代父亲成为情人。在康格里夫的《爱之恋》中，有两个俄狄浦斯主题相互对立：主人公欺骗父亲，夺走了女主人公；他的挚友玷污了女主人公监护人——一位阳痿老人的妻子。在现实生活中会被视为一种幼稚退行的表现——主人公假装阳痿以进入女性住所——这一主题在威彻利的《乡村妻子》中有所体现，其灵感来源于泰伦斯的《太监》。

The third phase of comedy is the normal one that we have been discussing, in which a senex iratus or other humor gives way to a young man’s desires. The sense of the comic norm is so strong that when Shakespeare, by way of experiment, tried to reverse the pattern in All’s Well, in having two older people force Bertram to marry Helena, the result has been an unpopular “problem” play, with a suggestion of something sinister about it. We have noted that the cognitio of comedy is much concerned with straightening out the details of the new society, with distinguishing brides from sisters and parents from foster-parents. The fact that the son and father are so often in conflict means that they are frequently rivals for the same girl, and the psychological alliance of the hero’s bride and the mother is often expressed or implied. The occasional “naughtiness” of comedy, as in the Restoration period, has much to do, not only with marital infidelity, but with a kind of comic Oedipus situation in which the hero replaces his father as a lover. In Congreve’s Love for Love there are two Oedipus themes in counterpoint: the hero cheats his father out of the heroine, and his best friend violates the wife of an impotent old man who is the heroine’s guardian. A theme which would be recognized in real life as a form of infantile regression, the hero pretending to be impotent in order to gain admission to the women’s quarters, is employed in Wycherley’s Country Wife, where it is taken from Terence’s Eunuchus.

乱伦的可能性是喜剧的一个次要主题。费加罗被许配的令人厌恶的老妇人最终竟是他的母亲，而对玷污母亲的恐惧也出现在《汤姆·琼斯》中。易卜生在《群鬼》和《小艾约尔夫》中运用了主人公爱慕的对象是其妹妹这一老套情节（这一主题与米南德一样古老），令听众震惊不已，他们将其视为社会革命的预兆。在莎士比亚的作品中，这种反复出现且略带神秘色彩的父女关系在《佩里克利斯》的开头以乱伦的形式出现，与主人公在结尾与妻子和女儿的结合形成了鲜明的对比。喜剧的主导天才在于爱欲，而爱欲必须适应社会的道德现实：俄狄浦斯和乱伦主题表明，情欲在其原始或神话起源中具有更大的多样性。

The possibilities of incestuous combinations form one of the minor themes of comedy. The repellent older woman offered to Figaro in marriage turns out to be his mother, and the fear of violating a mother also occurs in Tom Jones. When in Ghosts and Little Eyolf Ibsen employed the old chestnut about the object of the hero’s affections being his sister (a theme as old as Menander), his startled hearers took it for a portent of social revolution. In Shakespeare the recurring and somewhat mysterious father-daughter relationship already alluded to appears in its incestuous form at the beginning of Pericles, where it forms the demonic antithesis of the hero’s union with his wife and daughter at the end. The presiding genius of comedy is Eros, and Eros has to adapt himself to the moral facts of society: Oedipus and incest themes indicate that erotic attachments have in their undisplaced or mythical origin a much greater versatility.

矛盾的态度自然而然地产生，而这种矛盾显然是贯穿喜剧史的双重人物这一奇特特征的主要原因。在罗马喜剧中，经常会出现一对年轻男子，进而也会出现一对年轻女子，其中一位通常与其中一位男子有亲属关系，而与另一位女子则是异族通婚。老者形象的双重出现，有时使男女主角都拥有严厉的父亲形象，如《冬天的故事》；有时则使男女主角都拥有严厉的父亲形象，同时又拥有慈祥的叔叔形象，如泰伦提乌斯的《阿德尔福伊》和《伪君子》等等。喜剧的情节，如同基督教圣经的情节一样，从法律走向自由。法律中包含着被废除的仪式性束缚，以及被奉行的习惯或习俗。老者令人难以忍受的特质代表了前者，并在喜剧法则的演变过程中与后者达成了妥协。

Ambivalent attitudes naturally result, and ambivalence is apparently the main reason for the curious feature of doubled characters which runs all through the history of comedy. In Roman comedy there is often a pair of young men, and consequently a pair of young women, of which one is often related to one of the men and exogamous to the other. The doubling of the senex figure sometimes gives us a heavy father for both the hero and the heroine, as in The Winter’s Tale, sometimes a heavy father and benevolent uncle, as in Terence’s Adelphoi and in Tartuffe, and so on. The action of comedy, like the action of the Christian Bible, moves from law to liberty. In the law there is an element of ritual bondage which is abolished, and an element of habit or convention which is fulfilled. The intolerable qualities of the senex represent the former and compromise with him the latter in the evolution of the comic nomos.

随着喜剧的第四阶段到来，我们开始走出……从经验世界过渡到纯真浪漫的理想世界。我们说过，通常喜剧结尾所建立的更幸福的社会是未加定义的，这与体液的仪式性束缚形成对比。但喜剧也可以在两个社会层面上展现其情节，其中一个层面更受青睐，并因此在某种程度上被理想化。在柏拉图的《理想国》开篇，我们看到了讽刺家特拉西马科斯和反讽家苏格拉底之间激烈的辩论。对话本可以像柏拉图的其他一些对话一样就此结束，以苏格拉底战胜某种体液及其所暗示的社会模式而告终。但在《理想国》中，包括特拉西马科斯在内的其他角色，仿佛跟随苏格拉底进入了他的内心世界，在那里思考公正国家的模式。在阿里斯托芬的喜剧中，喜剧情节往往带有讽刺意味，但在《阿卡米亚人》中，我们看到一位名叫狄凯奥波利斯（意为正义之城或公民）的英雄，他与斯巴达私下达成和平协议，与家人一起庆祝和平的狄俄尼索斯节，并在舞台上建立了一种温和的社会秩序模式。这种秩序贯穿全剧，怪人、偏执狂、奸诈之徒和恶棍都被逐出其中。这种典型的喜剧情节，在我们最早的喜剧作品中得到了最清晰的展现，其清晰度丝毫不逊于此后的任何作品。

With the fourth phase of comedy we begin to move out of the world of experience into the ideal world of innocence and romance. We said that normally the happier society established at the end of the comedy is left undefined, in contrast to the ritual bondage of the humors. But it is also possible for a comedy to present its action on two social planes, of which one is preferred and consequently in some measure idealized. At the beginning of Plato’s Republic we have a sharp contest between the alazon Thrasymachus and the ironic Socrates. The dialogue could have stopped there, as several of Plato’s dialogues do, with a negative victory over a humor and the kind of society he suggests. But in the Republic the rest of the company, including Thrasymachus, follow Socrates inside Socrates’s head, so to speak, and contemplate there the pattern of the just state. In Aristophanes the comic action is often ironic, but in The Achamians we have a comedy in which a hero with the significant name of Dicaeopolis (righteous city or citizen) makes a private peace with Sparta, celebrates the peaceful festival of Dionysos with his family, and sets up the pattern of a temperate social order on the stage, where it remains throughout the play, cranks, bigots, sharpers, and scoundrels all being beaten away from it. One of the typical comic actions is at least as clearly portrayed in our earliest comedy as it has ever been since.

莎士比亚的浪漫喜剧类型沿袭了皮尔开创、格林和莱利发展的传统，与中世纪的季节性仪式剧有着密切的联系。我们可以称之为“绿色世界的戏剧”，其情节与生命和爱情战胜荒芜之地的仪式主题相契合。在《维洛那二绅士》中，主人公瓦伦丁成为森林中一群亡命之徒的首领，其他所有角色都被聚集到这片森林中，并最终皈依了这片森林。因此，这部喜剧的情节始于一个被描绘成正常世界的世界，随后进入绿色世界，在那里经历一场蜕变，最终达到喜剧的结局，然后又回到正常世界。这部剧中的森林是《仲夏夜之梦》中仙境、《皆大欢喜》中阿登森林、《风流娘儿们》中温莎森林以及《冬天的故事》中神话般的海滨波西米亚田园世界的雏形。在所有这些喜剧中，都存在着从正常世界到奇幻世界再到正常世界的相同节奏性运动。在《威尼斯商人》中，第二个世界以波西亚在贝尔蒙特的神秘宅邸的形式出现，那里有神奇的匣子和奇妙的宇宙观。第五幕中由此展开的和谐旋律。我们还注意到，在更具讽刺意味的喜剧《皆大欢喜》和《一报还一报》中，第二个世界并不存在。

Shakespeare’s type of romantic comedy follows a tradition established by Peele and developed by Greene and Lyly, which has affinities with the medieval tradition of the seasonal ritual-play. We may call it the drama of the green world, its plot being assimilated to the ritual theme of the triumph of life and love over the waste land. In The Two Gentlemen of Verona the hero Valentine becomes captain of a band of outlaws in a forest, and all the other characters are gathered into this forest and become converted. Thus the action of the comedy begins in a world represented as a normal world, moves into the green world, goes into a metamorphosis there in which the comic resolution is achieved, and returns to the normal world. The forest in this play is the embryonic form of the fairy world of A Midsummer Night’s Dream, the Forest of Arden in As You Like It, Windsor Forest in The Merry Wives, and the pastoral world of the mythical sea-coasted Bohemia in The Winter’s Tale. In all these comedies there is the same rhythmic movement from normal world to green world and back again. In The Merchant of Venice the second world takes the form of Portia’s mysterious house in Belmont, with its magic caskets and the wonderful cosmological harmonies that proceed from it in the fifth act. We notice too that this second world is absent from the more ironic comedies All’s Well and Measure for Measure.

绿色的世界赋予喜剧以象征夏季战胜冬季的意味，这一点在《爱的徒劳》中体现得尤为明显，剧中喜剧的竞争最终演变成了中世纪关于冬春之争的辩论。在《风流娘儿们》中，有一个繁复的仪式，民俗学家称之为“迎杀死神”，以此来战胜冬季，而福斯塔夫正是这个仪式的受害者；福斯塔夫一定觉得，在被扔进水里、被装扮成女巫、被诅咒着赶出家门、最后被戴上兽头、被蜡烛灼烧之后，他已经完成了所有对一个生育之灵所能合理要求的事情。

The green world charges the comedies with the symbolism of the victory of summer over winter, as is explicit in Love’s Labor’s Lost, where the comic contest takes the form of the medieval debate of winter and spring at the end. In The Merry Wives there is an elaborate ritual of the defeat of winter known to folklorists as “carrying out Death,” of which Falstaff is the victim; and Falstaff must have felt that, after being thrown into the water, dressed up as a witch and beaten out of a house with curses, and finally supplied with a beast’s head and singed with candles, he had done about all that could reasonably be asked of any fertility spirit.

在仪式和神话中，孕育重生的土地通常被描绘成女性形象；而在浪漫喜剧中，人物的死亡与复活，或消失与隐退，通常都与女主角有关。女主角常常通过男扮女装来化解喜剧冲突，这已是众所周知的套路。《无事生非》中的希罗、《皆大欢喜》中的海伦娜、《泰伊思·佩里克利斯》中的泰莎、 《辛白林》中的菲德尔、 《冬天的故事》中的赫敏，这些人物都体现了一种手法的反复运用：随着剧情的推进，对情节合理性的追求逐渐降低，珀耳塞福涅式的神话形象也愈发清晰。这些都是莎士比亚戏剧中以仪式性攻击女性中心人物为主题的喜剧范例，这一主题从米南德的作品一直延续到当代的肥皂剧。米南德的许多剧作标题都使用了阴性分词，暗示了剧中女主人公所遭受的特殊屈辱。据说，肥皂剧的惯用手法就是“让女主人公陷入困境，并让她一直处于这种困境之中”。对这一主题的处理方式可能像《夺发记》那样轻松诙谐，也可能像《帕梅拉》那样执拗而执拗。然而，重生这一主题并非总是与女性相关：阿里斯托芬的《骑士》中老者的返老还童，以及《皆大欢喜》中基于民间传说中阳痿国王痊愈的类似主题，都令人印象深刻。

In the rituals and myths the earth that produces the rebirth is generally a female figure, and the death and revival, or disappearance and withdrawal, of human figures in romantic comedy generally involves the heroine. The fact that the heroine often brings about the comic resolution by disguising herself as a boy is familiar enough. The treatment of Hero in Much Ado, of Helena in All’s Well, of Thaisa in Pericles, of Fidele in Cymbeline, of Hermione in The Winter’s Tale, show the repetition of a device in which progressively less care is taken of plausibility and in which in consequence the mythical outline of a Proserpine figure becomes progressively clearer. These are Shakespearean examples of the comic theme of ritual assault on a central female figure, a theme which stretches from Menander to contemporary soap operas. Many of Menander’s plays have titles which are feminine participles indicating the particular indignity the heroine suffers in them, and the working formula of the soap opera is said to be to “put the heroine behind the eight-ball and keep her there.” Treatments of the theme may be as light-hearted as The Rape of the Lock or as doggedly persistent as Pamela. However, the theme of rebirth is not invariably feminine in context: the rejuvenation of the senex in Aristophanes’ The Knights, and a similar theme in All’s Well based on the folklore motif of the healing of the impotent king, come readily to mind.

绿色世界不仅与充满仪式感的丰饶世界有相似之处，也与我们由自身欲望创造的梦境世界有相似之处。这个梦境世界与经验世界中的跌跌撞撞和盲目愚昧相碰撞，与忒修斯时代的雅典及其愚蠢的行径相碰撞。婚姻法、弗雷德里克公爵及其忧郁的暴政、莱昂特斯及其疯狂的嫉妒、宫廷党人的阴谋诡计，这一切都构成了莎士比亚喜剧的基调，它强大到足以将欲望的形式强加于其上。因此，莎士比亚喜剧如同我们所拥有的任何神话一样，清晰地展现了文学在描绘欲望世界中的原型功能，它并非逃避“现实”，而是将欲望世界呈现为人类生活试图模仿的真实世界。

The green world has analogies, not only to the fertile world of ritual, but to the dream world that we create out of our own desires. This dream world collides with the stumbling and blinded follies of the world of experience, of Theseus’ Athens with its idiotic marriage law, of Duke Frederick and his melancholy tyranny, of Leontes and his mad jealousy, of the Court Party with their plots and intrigues, and yet proves strong enough to impose the form of desire on it. Thus Shakespearean comedy illustrates, as clearly as any mythos we have, the archetypal function of literature in visualizing the world of desire, not as an escape from “reality,” but as the genuine form of the world that human life tries to imitate.

在喜剧的第五阶段，我们已预见到一些主题，它进入了一个更加浪漫、更少乌托邦色彩、更多田园牧歌式、更少欢庆、更多沉思的世界。在这个阶段，喜剧的结局与其说取决于情节的走向，不如说取决于观众的视角。当我们比较莎士比亚第四阶段的喜剧和第五阶段晚期的“传奇剧”时，我们会发现后者更适合严肃的情节：它们并非回避悲剧，而是将悲剧融入其中。其情节似乎不仅是从“冬天的故事”走向春天，更是从混乱的底层世界走向秩序井然的上层世界。《冬天的故事》的结尾让我们思考的，不仅仅是从悲剧和离别到幸福和回归的循环往复，更是身体的蜕变以及从一种生活方式到另一种生活方式的转变。《伯里克利》或《冬天的故事》的素材如此老套，以至于人们会“像嘲笑老掉牙的故事一样嘲笑它们”，但它们似乎既牵强附会又必然正确，既冒犯了现实，又同时向我们介绍了一个孩童般的纯真世界，而这个世界总是比现实更有意义。

In the fifth phase of comedy, some of the themes of which we have already anticipated, we move into a world that is still more romantic, less Utopian and more Arcadian, less festive and more pensive, where the comic ending is less a matter of the way the plot turns out than of the perspective of the audience. When we compare the Shakespearean fourth-phase comedies with the late fifth-phase “romances,” we notice how much more serious an action is appropriate to the latter: they do not avoid tragedies but contain them. The action seems to be not only a movement from a “winter’s tale” to spring, but from a lower world of confusion to an upper world of order. The closing scene of The Winter’s Tale makes us think, not simply of a cyclical movement from tragedy and absence to happiness and return, but of bodily metamorphosis and a transformation from one kind of life to another. The materials of the cognitio of Pericles or The Winter’s Tale are so stock that they would be “hooted at like an old tale,” yet they seem both far-fetched and inevitably right, outraging reality and at the same time introducing us to a world of childlike innocence which has always made more sense than reality.

在这个阶段，读者或观众感觉自己凌驾于剧情之上，克里斯托弗·斯莱正是这种情境的讽刺模仿对象。《佩里克利斯》中克里昂和狄俄尼索斯的阴谋，或是《暴风雨》中宫廷党人的阴谋，在我们看来都不过是寻常或典型的人类行为：剧情，或者至少是剧情的悲剧含义，被呈现得如同戏中戏一般，我们可以同时从各个维度观看。简而言之，我们是从一个更高、更有序的世界的视角来看待剧情的。正如莎士比亚笔下的森林通常象征着与现实冲突并强加自身形态的梦境世界，大海则通常象征着低级或混乱的世界，剧中人物，或者其中重要的一部分，最终从中获救。“海洋”喜剧包括《错误的喜剧》、《第十二夜》、《佩里克利斯》等等。《暴风雨》是一部错误的喜剧，虽然改编自普劳图斯的原作，但其意象更接近阿普列乌斯的世界，而非普劳图斯的世界。该剧的主要情节——从海难和分离到在以弗所神庙的重逢——在后来的剧作《佩里克利斯》中也有所体现。正如“问题”喜剧中的两个世界缺席一样，在“海洋”系列的两部作品—— 《第十二夜》和《暴风雨》——中，所有情节都发生在第二个世界。在《一报还一报》中，公爵在剧情中消失，直到结尾才回归；《暴风雨》似乎将同样的情节反过来呈现，所有角色都跟随普洛斯彼罗隐居，并在那里被塑造成一个新的社会秩序。

In this phase the reader or audience feels raised above the action, in the situation of which Christopher Sly is an ironic parody. The plotting of Cleon and Dionyza in Pericles, or of the Court Party in The Tempest, we look down on as generic or typical human behavior: the action, or at least the tragic implication of the action, is presented as though it were a play within a play that we can see in all dimensions at once. We see the action, in short, from the point of view of a higher and better ordered world. And as the forest in Shakespeare is the usual symbol for the dream world in conflict with and imposing its form on experience, so the usual symbol for the lower or chaotic world is the sea, from which the cast, or an important part of it, is saved. The group of “sea” comedies includes A Comedy of Errors, Twelfth Night, Pericles, and The Tempest. A Comedy of Errors, though based on a Plautine original, is much closer to the world of Apuleius than to that of Plautus in its imagery, and the main action, moving from shipwreck and separation to reunion in a temple in Ephesus, is repeated in the much later play of Pericles. And just as the second world is absent from the two “problem” comedies, so in two of the “sea” group, Twelfth Night and The Tempest, the entire action takes place in the second world. In Measure for Measure the Duke disappears from the action and returns at the end; The Tempest seems to present the same type of action inside out, as the entire cast follows Prospero into his retreat, and is shaped into a new social order there.

喜剧的这五个阶段可以被视为一个被救赎的社会生命历程中的一系列阶段。纯粹的讽刺喜剧展现了这个社会的萌芽状态，它被它本应取代的社会所包裹和窒息。堂吉诃德式的喜剧则展现了它的青春期，它对世事尚不了解，尚不足以掌控一切。在第三阶段，它走向成熟并取得胜利；在第四阶段，它已经成熟稳固。在第五阶段，它成为自始至终存在的既定秩序的一部分，这个秩序日益呈现出宗教色彩，似乎完全脱离了人类经验。此时，原本未被取代的喜剧，即但丁《天堂篇》中的景象，从我们的神话圈中脱离出来，进入了凌驾于其上的末世或抽象的神话世界。这时我们才意识到，普劳图斯最粗糙的喜剧公式与基督教的核心神话本身有着非常相似的结构，即神圣的儿子平息了父亲的愤怒，并救赎了一个既是社会又是新娘的事物。

These five phases of comedy may be seen as a sequence of stages in the life of a redeemed society. Purely ironic comedy exhibits this society in its infancy, swaddled and smothered by the society it should replace. Quixotic comedy exhibits it in adolescence, still too ignorant of the ways of the world to impose itself. In the third phase it comes to maturity and triumphs; in the fourth it is already mature and established. In the fifth it is part of a settled order which has been there from the beginning, an order which takes on an increasingly religious cast and seems to be drawing away from human experience altogether. At this point the undisplaced commedia, the vision of Dante’s Paradiso, moves out of our circle of mythoi into the apocalyptic or abstract mythical world above it. At this point we realize that the crudest of Plautine comedy-formulas has much the same structure as the central Christian myth itself, with its divine son appeasing the wrath of a father and redeeming what is at once a society and a bride.

至此，喜剧也进入了其最后一个阶段，即第六阶段，喜剧社会崩溃瓦解的阶段。在这个阶段，喜剧的社会单元变得狭小而神秘，甚至局限于单个个体。秘密而隐蔽的地方、月光下的森林、僻静的山谷和幸福的岛屿变得更加突出，浪漫的沉思氛围、对神秘和奇幻的热爱、以及个体脱离日常生活的感受也随之增强。在这种喜剧中，我们最终离开了机智和觉醒的批判智慧的世界，走向了截然相反的极端——一种神谕般的庄严，如果我们不加批判地接受它，它将带来一种令人愉悦的颤栗感。这就是鬼故事、惊悚片和哥特式浪漫故事的世界，以及，更进一步来说，这种高雅的意境，类似于于斯曼的《逆流》中所描绘的那种想象力的退隐。德·埃桑特所处环境的阴郁与悲剧无关：德·埃桑特只是一个试图自娱自乐的业余爱好者。喜剧社会已经走过了从婴儿到死亡的完整历程，在其最后阶段，与回归子宫在心理上紧密相关的神话是恰当的。

At this point too comedy proper enters its final or sixth phase, the phase of the collapse and disintegration of the comic society. In this phase the social units of comedy become small and esoteric, or even confined to a single individual. Secret and sheltered places, forests in moonlight, secluded valleys, and happy islands become more prominent, as does the penseroso mood of romance, the love of the occult and the marvellous, the sense of individual detachment from routine existence. In this kind of comedy we have finally left the world of wit and the awakened critical intelligence for the opposite pole, an oracular solemnity which, if we surrender uncritically to it, will provide a delightful frisson. This is the world of ghost stories, thrillers, and Gothic romances, and, on a more sophisticated level, the kind of imaginative withdrawal portrayed in Huysmans’ À Rebours. The somberness of Des Esseintes’ surroundings has nothing to do with tragedy: Des Esseintes is a dilettante trying to amuse himself. The comic society has run the full course from infancy to death, and in its last phase myths closely connected psychologically with a return to the womb are appropriate.

夏日神话：浪漫篇

THE MYTHOS OF SUMMER: ROMANCE

在所有文学形式中，浪漫小说最接近于愿望实现的梦想，因此它在社会中扮演着一种奇特的悖论角色。在每个时代，统治阶级或知识分子都倾向于以某种浪漫小说的形式投射其理想，其中品德高尚的英雄和美丽的女主角代表着理想，而反派则代表着对其统治地位的威胁。这便是中世纪骑士浪漫小说、文艺复兴时期贵族浪漫小说、十八世纪以来资产阶级浪漫小说以及当代俄罗斯革命浪漫小说的普遍特征。然而，浪漫小说中也存在着一种真正的“无产阶级”元素，它从不满足于自身的各种形式，事实上，这些形式本身就表明，无论社会发生多么巨大的变化，浪漫小说都会再次出现，一如既往地渴望着新的希望和欲望。浪漫小说永恒的童真特质体现在其异常持久的怀旧情怀上，体现在其对某种想象中的黄金时代的追寻上。据我所知，英国文学中从未有过哥特式时期，但哥特式复兴者的名单却贯穿了英国文学的整个历史，从《贝奥武夫》的诗人到我们这个时代的作家。

The romance is nearest of all literary forms to the wish-fulfilment dream, and for that reason it has socially a curiously paradoxical role. In every age the ruling social or intellectual class tends to project its ideals in some form of romance, where the virtuous heroes and beautiful heroines represent the ideals and the villains the threats to their ascendancy. This is the general character of chivalric romance in the Middle Ages, aristocratic romance in the Renaissance, bourgeois romance since the eighteenth century, and revolutionary romance in contemporary Russia. Yet there is a genuinely “proletarian” element in romance too which is never satisfied with its various incarnations, and in fact the incarnations themselves indicate that no matter how great a change may take place in society, romance will turn up again, as hungry as ever, looking for new hopes and desires to feed on. The perennially childlike quality of romance is marked by its extraordinarily persistent nostalgia, its search for some kind of imaginative golden age in time or space. There has never to my knowledge been any period of Gothic English literature, but the list of Gothic revivalists stretches completely across its entire history, from the Beowulf poet to writers of our own day.

爱情故事的核心要素是冒险，这意味着爱情故事本质上是一种循序渐进的形式，因此我们对它的了解更多地来自小说而非戏剧。在最天真的版本中，爱情故事是一种永无止境的形式，主人公永远不会成长或衰老，经历着一个又一个的冒险，直到作者本人去世。我们在连环画中可以看到这种形式，其中的主人公仿佛被冷冻了一样，永生不死，持续多年。然而，没有任何书籍能够与报纸的连载性相媲美，一旦爱情故事发展成一种文学形式，它往往就会局限于一系列小型冒险。通常，故事一开始就会交代一个重大或高潮迭起的冒险事件，而这个冒险事件的完成也为整个故事画上了句号。我们可以把这个重大冒险事件，也就是赋予浪漫故事文学形式的要素，称为“探险”。

The essential element of plot in romance is adventure, which means that romance is naturally a sequential and processional form, hence we know it better from fiction than from drama. At its most naive it is an endless form in which a central character who never develops or ages goes through one adventure after another until the author himself collapses. We see this form in comic strips, where the central characters persist for years in a state of refrigerated deathlessness. However, no book can rival the continuity of the newspaper, and as soon as romance achieves a literary form, it tends to limit itself to a sequence of minor adventures leading up to a major or climacteric adventure, usually announced from the beginning, the completion of which rounds off the story. We may call this major adventure, the element that gives literary form to the romance, the quest.

完整的传奇故事显然是成功的冒险之旅，而这种完整的故事包含三个主要阶段：危险的旅程和前期的小冒险；至关重要的斗争，通常是一场战斗，英雄或他的敌人，或双方都必须牺牲；以及英雄的荣耀。我们可以用希腊语分别称这三个阶段为：agon（冲突）、pathos（生死搏斗）和anagnorisis（发现），即对英雄的认可，即使他未能在冲突中幸存，也已充分证明了自己的英雄身份。因此，传奇故事比喜剧更清晰地表达了从斗争到象征性死亡再到最终认可的转变过程。这种三段式结构在传奇故事的许多特征中都有体现——例如，成功的英雄通常是第三个儿子，或是第三个踏上冒险之旅的人，或是第三次尝试才取得成功的人。在阿提斯和其他垂死之神的传说中，死亡、消失和复活的三天节奏就更直接地体现了这一点，并且已经融入了我们的复活节中。

The complete form of the romance is clearly the successful quest, and such a completed form has three main stages: the stage of the perilous journey and the preliminary minor adventures; the crucial struggle, usually some kind of battle in which either the hero or his foe, or both, must die; and the exaltation of the hero. We may call these three stages respectively, using Greek terms, the agon or conflict, the pathos or death-struggle, and the anagnorisis or discovery, the recognition of the hero, who has clearly proved himself to be a hero even if he does not survive the conflict. Thus the romance expresses more clearly the passage from struggle through a point of ritual death to a recognition scene that we discovered in comedy. A threefold structure is repeated in many features of romance—in the frequency, for instance, with which the successful hero is a third son, or the third to undertake the quest, or successful on his third attempt. It is shown more directly in the three-day rhythm of death, disappearance and revival which is found in the myth of Attis and other dying gods, and has been incorporated in our Easter.

包含冲突的冒险故事通常设定有两个主要角色：主角或英雄，以及反派或敌人。（为了方便部分读者理解，我特此补充说明，我已阅读过福勒《现代英语用法》中关于“主角”一词的条目。）敌人可能是普通人，但浪漫故事越接近神话，英雄身上就越会带有神性，而敌人则越会展现出恶魔般的神秘特质。浪漫故事的核心形式是辩证的：一切都围绕着英雄与敌人之间的冲突展开，读者的所有价值观都与英雄紧密相连。因此，浪漫故事中的英雄类似于来自上界的神话救世主或救星，而他的敌人则类似于来自下界的恶魔力量。然而，冲突发生在我们的世界，或者至少主要与我们的这个世界相关，我们的世界位于中间，并以自然界的循环运动为特征。因此，自然循环的对立两极被等同于英雄与其敌人的对立。敌人则与冬季、黑暗、混乱、荒芜、垂死的生命联系在一起。以及衰老，英雄则象征着春天、黎明、秩序、丰饶、活力和青春。由于所有循环现象都易于关联或识别，因此，任何试图证明一个浪漫故事是否类似于太阳神话，或者其英雄是否类似于太阳神的努力，都可能是徒劳的。如果故事属于这一范畴，循环意象很可能出现，而太阳意象通常在循环意象中占据显著位置。如果一个浪漫故事中的英雄乔装打扮，从冒险归来，脱下乞丐的破烂衣衫，披上王子的华丽猩红色斗篷，我们看到的并非一个必然源自太阳神话的主题；而是一种文学手法——移置。英雄做了某件事，我们可以随意将其与太阳黎明归来的神话联系起来，也可以不联系起来。如果我们以评论家的身份，着眼于结构原则来阅读这个故事，我们自然会联想到太阳，因为太阳的比喻解释了为什么主人公的行为既有效又符合常规。如果我们只是为了娱乐而阅读这个故事，则无需费心：也就是说，我们反应中某种模糊的“潜意识”因素会促成这种联想。

A quest involving conflict assumes two main characters, a protagonist or hero, and an antagonist or enemy. (No doubt I should add, for the benefit of some readers, that I have read the article “Protagonist” in Fowler’s Modern English Usage.) The enemy may be an ordinary human being, but the nearer the romance is to myth, the more attributes of divinity will cling to the hero and the more the enemy will take on demonic mythical qualities. The central form of romance is dialectical: everything is focussed on a conflict between the hero and his enemy, and all the reader’s values are bound up with the hero. Hence the hero of romance is analogous to the mythical Messiah or deliverer who comes from an upper world, and his enemy is analogous to the demonic powers of a lower world. The conflict however takes place in, or at any rate primarily concerns, our world, which is in the middle, and which is characterized by the cyclical movement of nature. Hence the opposite poles of the cycles of nature are assimilated to the opposition of the hero and his enemy. The enemy is associated with winter, darkness, confusion, sterility, moribund life, and old age, and the hero with spring, dawn, order, fertility, vigor, and youth. As all the cyclical phenomena can be readily associated or identified, it follows that any attempt to prove that a romantic story does or does not resemble, say, a solar myth, or that its hero does or does not resemble a sun-god, is likely to be a waste of time. If it is a story within this general area, cyclical imagery is likely to be present, and solar imagery is normally prominent among cyclical images. If the hero of a romance returns from a quest disguised, flings off his beggar’s rags, and stands forth in the resplendent scarlet cloak of the prince, we do not have a theme which has necessarily descended from a solar myth; we have the literary device of displacement. The hero does something which we may or may not, as we like, associate with the myth of the sun returning at dawn. If we are reading the story as critics, with an eye to structural principles, we shall make the association, because the solar analogy explains why the hero’s act is an effective and conventional incident. If we are reading the story for fun, we need not bother: that is, some murky “subconscious” factor in our response will take care of the association.

我们通过英雄的行动力来区分神话和传奇：在真正的神话中，英雄是神；在真正的传奇中，英雄是人。这种区分在神学上比在诗歌上更为鲜明，神话和传奇都属于神话文学的范畴。然而，赋予神话主要人物神性，往往会使神话获得另一个之前提到的独特之处，即占据核心的经典地位。大多数文化对某些故事的尊崇程度高于其他故事，要么是因为这些故事被认为是历史真实的，要么是因为它们承载了更为沉重的概念意义。因此，无论诗人是否相信亚当和夏娃在伊甸园的故事的历史真实性，它在我们传统中都占据着经典地位。经典神话之所以更深刻，并非仅仅源于传统，而是因为它能够进行更高程度的隐喻式解读。在文学批评中，神话通常是解读浪漫主义作品中人物移位现象的关键隐喻，因此，圣经中的探寻神话在下文中至关重要。但由于经典神话往往存在删减和说教的倾向，因此，相对自由的传说和民间故事领域通常蕴含着同样丰富的神话意义。

We have distinguished myth from romance by the hero’s power of action: in the myth proper he is divine, in the romance proper he is human. This distinction is much sharper theologically than it is poetically, and myth and romance both belong in the general category of mythopoeic literature. The attributing of divinity to the chief characters of myth, however, tends to give myth a further distinction, already referred to, of occupying a central canonical position. Most cultures regard certain stories with more reverence than others, either because they are thought of as historically true or because they have come to bear a heavier weight of conceptual meaning. The story of Adam and Eve in Eden has thus a canonical position for poets in our tradition whether they believe in its historicity or not. The reason for the greater profundity of canonical myth is not solely tradition, but the result of the greater degree of metaphorical identification that is possible is myth. In literary criticism the myth is normally the metaphorical key to the displacements of romance, hence the importance of the quest-myth of the Bible in what follows. But because of the tendency to expurgate and moralize in canonical myth, the less inhibited area of legend and folk tale often contains an equally great concentration of mythical meaning.

冒险爱情故事的核心形式是屠龙主题，圣乔治和珀尔修斯的故事便是例证，前文已提及。一个由年迈无助的国王统治的国度被海怪蹂躏，海怪接连不断地将年轻人献祭给它，直到轮到国王的女儿：此时，英雄出现，杀死巨龙，娶了国王的女儿，并继承了王位。与喜剧一样，我们看到的是一个看似简单的模式，却蕴含着许多复杂的元素。神话中的仪式类比表明，巨怪象征着土地的贫瘠，而这种贫瘠则体现在国王的年老体衰和无能为力上，他有时还患有不治之症或伤痛，如同瓦格纳歌剧中的安福塔斯。他的处境如同阿多尼斯被冬日野猪所征服，阿多尼斯传统的大腿伤在象征意义上和解剖学意义上都接近于阉割。

The central form of quest-romance is the dragon-killing theme exemplified in the stories of St. George and Perseus, already referred to. A land ruled by a helpless old king is laid waste by a sea-monster, to whom one young person after another is offered to be devoured, until the lot falls on the king’s daughter: at that point the hero arrives, kills the dragon, marries the daughter, and succeeds to the kingdom. Again, as with comedy, we have a simple pattern with many complex elements. The ritual analogies of the myth suggest that the monster is the sterility of the land itself, and that the sterility of the land is present in the age and impotence of the king, who is sometimes suffering from an incurable malady or wound, like Amfortas in Wagner. His position is that of Adonis overcome by the boar of winter, Adonis’s traditional thigh-wound being as close to castration symbolically as it is anatomically.

在《圣经》中，我们看到一种通常被称为利维坦的海怪，它被描述为弥赛亚的敌人，弥赛亚注定要在“耶和华的日子”将其杀死。利维坦是社会贫瘠的根源，因为它与压迫以色列的埃及和巴比伦联系在一起，并在《约伯记》中被描述为“骄傲之子”的王。它似乎也与堕落世界的自然贫瘠密切相关，与撒旦将约伯、伊甸园中的蛇将亚当抛入的充满挣扎、贫困和疾病的荒芜世界紧密相连。在《约伯记》中，上帝对约伯的启示主要由对利维坦及其陆地近亲贝希摩斯的描述构成。因此，这些怪物显然代表了撒旦所掌控的堕落自然秩序。 （我试图理解我们现在所拥有的《约伯记》的含义，前提是其现存版本的作者有其创作该版本的理由。猜测这首诗最初的内容或含义毫无意义，因为只有我们所知的版本才对我们的文学产生了影响。）在《启示录》中，利维坦、撒旦和伊甸园的蛇都被明确地指认出来。这种指认构成了基督教象征体系中一个精心设计的屠龙隐喻的基础，其中英雄是基督（在艺术作品中通常被描绘成站在一个俯卧的怪物身上），恶龙是撒旦，无能的老王亚当（他的儿子基督就是亚当的化身），而获救的新娘则是教会。

In the Bible we have a sea-monster usually named leviathan, who is described as the enemy of the Messiah, and whom the Messiah is destined to kill in the “day of the Lord.” The leviathan is the source of social sterility, for it is identified with Egypt and Babylon, the oppressors of Israel, and is described in the Book of Job as “king over all the children of pride.” It also seems closely associated with the natural sterility of the fallen world, with the blasted world of struggle and poverty and disease into which Job is hurled by Satan and Adam by the serpent in Eden. In the Book of Job God’s revelation to Job consists largely of descriptions of the leviathan and a slightly less sinister land cousin named behemoth. These monsters thus apparently represent the fallen order of nature over which Satan has some control. (I am trying to make sense of the meaning of the Book of Job as we now have it, on the assumption that whoever was responsible for its present version had some reason for producing that version. Guesswork about what the poem may originally have been or meant is useless, as it is only the version we know that has had any influence on our literature.) In the Book of Revelation the leviathan, Satan, and the Edenic serpent are all identified. This identification is the basis for an elaborate dragon-killing metaphor in Christian symbolism in which the hero is Christ (often represented in art standing on a prostrate monster), the dragon Satan, the impotent old king Adam, whose son Christ becomes, and the rescued bride the Church.

如果利维坦象征着亚当堕落的整个充满罪恶、死亡和暴政的堕落世界，那么亚当的子孙就出生、生活、最​​终也死在它的腹中。因此，如果弥赛亚要通过杀死利维坦来拯救我们，那么他实际上是在释放我们。在民间传说中屠龙的故事里，我们注意到，龙死后，之前被它杀死的受害者往往又活着出来。同样地，如果我们身处龙腹之中，而英雄前来帮助我们，那么这幅画面就暗示着英雄像约拿（耶稣将他视为自己的原型）一样，进入巨兽张开的喉咙，然后带着被救赎的人返回。这就是“地狱之旅”的象征意义所在，地狱在图像学中经常被描绘成“一条老鲨鱼布满牙齿的喉咙”（借用一句现代的说法）。从路奇安到今天，世俗作品中都有关于进入怪物体内的旅程，甚至特洛伊木马最初可能也与这个主题有所关联。怪物腹中那黑暗蜿蜒的迷宫意象十分自然，也经常出现在英雄的冒险故事中，尤其是忒修斯的故事。如果忒修斯的故事版本更贴近现实，他或许会带领着一群此前被献祭给弥诺陶洛斯的雅典青年和少女，从迷宫中走出。在许多太阳神话中，英雄也会在日落到日出之间，险象环生地穿越充满怪物的黑暗迷宫般的冥界。这一主题可以成为任何层次的虚构作品的结构原则。人们或许会在童话或儿童故事中找到它，事实上，如果我们跳出汤姆·索亚的视角，就能看到一个失去双亲的少年带着一位少女从迷宫般的洞穴中走出，身后留下一个被囚禁的、以蝙蝠为食的恶魔。但在亨利·詹姆斯晚期最复杂、最难以捉摸的小说《往事之感》中，也运用了同样的主题。在这个故事里，迷宫般的冥界象征着一段逝去的时光，主人公通过牺牲一位女英雄——一位类似阿里阿德涅的人物——才得以从中解脱。如同许多民间故事一样，这篇小说也运用了兄弟二人因某种感应魔法而联系在一起的主题。

Now if the leviathan is the whole fallen world of sin and death and tyranny into which Adam fell, it follows that Adam’s children are born, live, and die inside his belly. Hence if the Messiah is to deliver us by killing the leviathan, he releases us. In the folk tale versions of dragon-killing stories we notice how frequently the previous victims of the dragon come out of him alive after he is killed. Again, if we are inside the dragon, and the hero comes to help us, the image is suggested of the hero going down the monster’s open throat, like Jonah (whom Jesus accepted as a prototype of himself), and returning with his redeemed behind him. Hence the symbolism of the Harrowing of Hell, hell being regularly represented in iconography by the “toothed gullet of an aged shark,” to quote a modern reference to it. Secular versions of journeys inside monsters occur from Lucian to our day, and perhaps even the Trojan horse had originally some links with the same theme. The image of the dark winding labyrinth for the monster’s belly is a natural one, and one that frequently appears in heroic quests, notably that of Theseus. A less displaced version of the story of Theseus would have shown him emerging from the labyrinth at the head of a procession of the Athenian youths and maidens previously sacrificed to the Minotaur. In many solar myths, too, the hero travels perilously through a dark labyrinthine underworld full of monsters between sunset and sunrise. This theme may become a structural principle of fiction on any level of sophistication. One would expect to find it in fairy tales or children’s stories, and in fact if we “stand back” from Tom Sawyer we can see a youth with no father or mother emerging with a maiden from a labyrinthine cave, leaving a bat-eating demon imprisoned behind him. But in the most complex and elusive of the later stories of Henry James, The Sense of the Past, the same theme is used, the labyrinthine underworld being in this case a period of past time from which the hero is released by the sacrifice of a heroine, an Ariadne figure. In this story, as in many folktales, the motif of the two brothers connected by sympathetic magic of some sort is also employed.

在旧约中，弥赛亚摩西带领他的子民出埃及。以西结将埃及法老比作利维坦，而幼年摩西被法老的女儿所救，这使得法老在某种程度上扮演了残酷的父亲形象，一心想要杀死这位英雄。这也被狂怒的希律王在神迹剧中利用。摩西和以色列人穿越迷宫般的沙漠，之后律法的统治结束，约书亚征服了应许之地，他的名字与耶稣相同。因此，当天使加百列告诉圣母玛利亚给她的儿子取名耶稣时，其象征意义在于律法的时代已经结束，对应许之地的征服即将开始。由此可见，圣经中存在两个同心圆式的探索神话：创世记-启示录神话和出埃及记-千禧年神话。在前一个神话中，亚当被逐出伊甸园，失去了生命河和生命树，在人类历史的迷宫中徘徊，直到弥赛亚将他恢复到原本的状态。在后一个神话中，以色列人被逐出他们的产业，在埃及和巴比伦的囚禁迷宫中徘徊，直到他们在应许之地恢复到原本的状态。因此，伊甸园和应许之地在象征意义上是相同的，正如埃及和巴比伦的暴政以及律法的旷野也是如此。《复乐园》讲述了基督受撒旦诱惑的故事，正如迈克尔在《失乐园》中所说，这正是弥赛亚屠龙神话的真正形式。基督的处境如同律法下的以色列，在旷野中漂泊：他的胜利既是征服应许之地（正如他的同名先祖约书亚所象征的那样），也是在旷野中重建伊甸园。

In the Old Testament the Messiah-figure of Moses leads his people out of Egypt. The Pharaoh of Egypt is identified with the leviathan by Ezekiel, and the fact that the infant Moses was rescued by Pharaoh’s daughter gives to the Pharaoh something of the role of the cruel father-figure who seeks the hero’s death, a role also taken by the raging Herod of the miracle plays. Moses and the Israelites wander through a labyrinthine desert, after which the reign of the law ends and the conquest of the Promised Land is achieved by Joshua, whose name is the same as that of Jesus. Thus when the angel Gabriel tells the Virgin to call her son Jesus, the typological meaning is that the era of the law is over, and the assault on the Promised Land is about to begin. There are thus two concentric quest-myths in the Bible, a Genesis-apocalypse myth and an Exodus-millennium myth. In the former Adam is cast out of Eden, loses the river of life and the tree of life, and wanders in the labyrinth of human history until he is restored to his original state by the Messiah. In the latter Israel is cast out of his inheritance and wanders in the labyrinths of Egyptian and Babylonian captivity until he is restored to his original state in the Promised Land. Eden and the Promised Land, therefore, are typologically identical, as are the tyrannies of Egypt and Babylon and the wilderness of the law. Paradise Regained deals with the temptation of Christ by Satan, which is, Michael tells us in Paradise Lost, the true form of the dragon-killing myth assigned to the Messiah. Christ is in the situation of Israel under the law, wandering in the wilderness: his victory is at once the conquest of the Promised Land typified by his namesake Joshua and the raising of Eden in the wilderness.

利维坦通常指海怪，这象征着它就是大海。以西结书中关于上帝将钩住并捕获利维坦的预言，与启示录中关于大海将不复存在的预言如出一辙。因此，作为利维坦腹中的居民，我们也象征性地处于水下。这解释了福音书中捕鱼的重要性，使徒们被称为“得人如得鱼”的人，他们将渔网撒入这世界的海洋。这也解释了后来在《荒原》中提到的亚当或无能的国王被描绘成无能的“渔王”的情节。在同一首诗中，也恰当地将利维坦与《暴风雨》中普洛斯彼罗从海中拯救一个社会的故事联系起来。在其他喜剧中，从《沙恭达罗》到《鲁登斯》，也常常从海里捞出对剧情或认知至关重要的东西，许多冒险英雄，包括贝奥武夫，都在水下完成了他们最伟大的壮举。强调基督能够驾驭海洋也属于同样的象征意义。而利维坦，作为堕落世界的象征，包含了所有形式的……生命被囚禁于自身之中，正如海洋囚禁着赋予生命的雨水，雨水的到来标志着春天的到来。吞噬世间所有水源，最终被戏弄、欺骗或强迫吐出的怪兽，是民间故事中常见的题材，美索不达米亚的一个版本紧随《创世记》的创世故事之后。在许多太阳神话中，太阳神被描绘成乘船航行于我们世界的表面。

The leviathan is usually a sea-monster, which means metaphorically that he is the sea, and the prophecy that the Lord will hook and land the leviathan in Ezekiel is identical with the prophecy in Revelation that there shall be no more sea. As denizens of his belly, therefore, we are also metaphorically under water. Hence the importance of fishing in the Gospels, the apostles being “fishers of men” who cast their nets into the sea of this world. Hence, too, the later development, referred to in The Waste Land, of Adam or the impotent king as an ineffectual “fisher king.” In the same poem the appropriate link is also made with Prospero’s rescuing of a society out of the sea in The Tempest. In other comedies, too, ranging from Sakuntala to Rudens, something indispensable to the action or the cognitio is fished out of the sea, and many quest heroes, including Beowulf, achieve their greatest feats under water. The insistence on Christ’s ability to command the sea belongs to the same aspect of symbolism. And as the leviathan, in his aspect as the fallen world, contains all forms of life imprisoned within himself, so as the sea he contains the imprisoned life-giving rain waters whose coming marks the spring. The monstrous animal who swallows all the water in the world and is then teased or tricked or forced into disgorging it is a favorite of folk tales, and a Mesopotamian version lies close behind the story of Creation in Genesis. In many solar myths the sun god is represented as sailing in a boat on the surface of our world.

最后，如果利维坦象征死亡，英雄必须进入死亡之躯，那么英雄就必须死去；如果他的征程完成，那么最终阶段，从循环论证的角度来看，就是重生；从辩证论证的角度来看，就是复活。在圣乔治戏剧中，英雄在与巨龙搏斗中死去，后被医生救活；同样的象征意义贯穿所有关于垂死之神的传说。因此，征程神话并非只有三个方面，而是有四个可区分的方面。首先是对抗或冲突本身。其次是悲怆或死亡，通常是英雄与怪物的共同死亡。第三是英雄的消失，这一主题通常以撕裂或肢解的形式出现。有时，英雄的遗体被分给他的追随者，如同圣餐的象征意义；有时，它被散布到自然界各处，如同俄耳甫斯的故事，尤其是奥西里斯的故事。第四，英雄的重现和认可，圣礼基督教遵循隐喻逻辑：那些在堕落的世界中分享了救赎者分裂的身体的人，与他复活的身体合而为一。

Lastly, if the leviathan is death, and the hero has to enter the body of death, the hero has to die, and if his quest is completed the final stage of it is, cyclically, rebirth, and, dialectically, resurrection. In the St. George plays the hero dies in his dragon-fight and is brought to life by a doctor, and the same symbolism runs through all the dying-god myths. There are thus not three but four distinguishable aspects to the quest-myth. First, the agon or conflict itself. Second, the pathos or death, often the mutual death of hero and monster. Third, the disappearance of the hero, a theme which often takes the form of sparagmos or tearing to pieces. Sometimes the hero’s body is divided among his followers, as in Eucharist symbolism: sometimes it is distributed around the natural world, as in the stories of Orpheus and more especially Osiris. Fourth, the reappearance and recognition of the hero, where sacramental Christianity follows the metaphorical logic: those who in the fallen world have partaken of their redeemer’s divided body are united with his risen body.

我们所探讨的四种神话——喜剧、浪漫、悲剧和讽刺——可以被视为一个核心统一神话的四个方面。冲突（Agon）是浪漫的基础或原型主题，浪漫的根本在于一系列奇妙的冒险。悲情（ Pathos），无论是胜利还是失败，都是悲剧的原型主题。混乱（Sparagmos），即英雄主义和有效行动的缺失、混乱或注定失败，以及混乱和无政府状态统治世界，是讽刺和反讽的原型主题。顿悟（Anagnorisis） ，即对一个围绕着一位仍然有些神秘的英雄及其新娘而崛起的新生社会的认识，是喜剧的原型主题。

The four mythoi that we are dealing with, comedy, romance, tragedy, and irony, may now be seen as four aspects of a central unifying myth. Agon or conflict is the basis or archetypal theme of romance, the radical of romance being a sequence of marvellous adventures. Pathos or catastrophe, whether in triumph or in defeat, is the archetypal theme of tragedy. Sparagmos, or the sense that heroism and effective action are absent, disorganized or foredoomed to defeat, and that confusion and anarchy reign over the world, is the archetypal theme of irony and satire. Anagnorisis, or recognition of a newborn society rising in triumph around a still somewhat mysterious hero and his bride, is the archetypal theme of comedy.

我们曾将弥赛亚式的英雄视为社会的救赎者，但在世俗的冒险故事中，更显而易见的动机和奖励则更为常见。通常，龙卫从齐格弗里德传奇到诺斯特罗莫号，寻找埋藏的宝藏一直是浪漫故事的核心主题，而且这一主题似乎永远不会被穷尽。宝藏意味着财富，在神话浪漫故事中，财富通常指其理想化的形式：权力和智慧。下界，即守护巨龙内部或背后的世界，通常居住着预言家女巫，那里充满神谕和秘密，例如沃登为了获得这些秘密，甘愿自残。残害或身体残疾，融合了残害和仪式性死亡的主题，通常是获得非凡智慧或力量的代价，例如跛足铁匠韦兰或赫菲斯托斯，以及雅各布的祝福故事。《一千零一夜》中充满了关于残害成因的故事。此外，寻宝的奖励通常是或包含一位新娘。这种新娘形象是暧昧的：在俄狄浦斯情结的幻想中，她与母亲的心理联系比在喜剧中更为强烈。她常常身处危险、禁忌或不祥之地，例如布伦希尔德的火墙或睡美人的荆棘墙，当然，她也常常从另一个（通常更年长的）男性的不怀好意的拥抱中，或从巨人、强盗或其他篡位者的手中被解救出来。消除女主人公身上的某种污名在浪漫故事和喜剧中都占据着重要地位，从乔叟《巴斯妇人的故事》中“丑陋的女人”到《何西阿书》中被宽恕的妓女，不一而足。《雅歌》中“黑发却美丽”的新娘也属于同一范畴。

We have spoken of the Messianic hero as a redeemer of society, but in the secular quest-romances more obvious motives and rewards for the quest are more common. Often the dragon guards a board: the quest for buried treasure has been a central theme of romance from the Siegfried cycle to Nostromo, and is unlikely to be exhausted yet. Treasure means wealth, which in mythopoeic romance often means wealth in its ideal forms, power and wisdom. The lower world, the world inside or behind the guarding dragon, is often inhabited by a prophetic sibyl, and is a place of oracles and secrets, such as Woden was willing to mutilate himself to obtain. Mutilation or physical handicap, which combines the themes of sparagmos and ritual death, is often the price of unusual wisdom or power, as it is in the figure of the crippled smith Weyland or Hephaistos, and in the story of the blessing of Jacob. The Arabian Nights are full of stories of what may be called the etiology of mutilation. Again, the reward of the quest usually is or includes a bride. This bride-figure is ambiguous: her psychological connection with the mother in an Oedipus fantasy is more insistent than in comedy. She is often to be found in a perilous, forbidden, or tabooed place, like Brunnhilde’s wall of fire or the sleeping beauty’s wall of thorns, and she is, of course, often rescued from the unwelcome embraces of another and generally older male, or from giants or bandits or other usurpers. The removal of some stigma from the heroine figures prominently in romance as in comedy, and ranges from the “loathly lady” theme of Chaucer’s Wife of Bath’s Tale to the forgiven harlot of the Book of Hosea. The “black but comely” bride of the Song of Songs belongs in the same complex.

这种寻觅式的浪漫情怀与仪式和梦境都有相似之处，弗雷泽对仪式的研究和荣格对梦境的研究都展现出形式上的显著相似性，这正是我们对两种象征性结构（指同一事物）的预期。用梦境的术语来说，寻觅式的浪漫情怀是力比多或欲望自我寻求一种能够使其摆脱现实焦虑却又包含现实的满足感的过程。寻觅中的反派通常是邪恶的人物，如巨人、食人魔、女巫和魔法师，他们显然具有父系起源；然而，正如弗洛伊德和荣格的心理探索中那样，被救赎和解放的父系形象也参与其中。用仪式的术语来说，寻觅式的浪漫情怀是丰饶战胜荒芜之地。丰饶意味着食物和饮料，面包和葡萄酒，身体和血液，以及男性和女性的结合。从寻觅中带回的珍贵物品，或因寻觅而见、获得的珍贵物品，有时，仪式和心理联想会结合在一起。例如，圣杯与基督教圣餐的象征意义相关；它与丰饶角等神奇的食物供应器物有关，或源自于此；而且，与其他杯子和空心器皿一样，它也具有女性的性象征意义，据说其男性对应物是流血的长矛。固体食物和液体滋养的结合在圣经启示录中的可食用树木和生命之水之间反复出现。

The quest-romance has analogies to both rituals and dreams, and the rituals examined by Frazer and the dreams examined by Jung show the remarkable similarity in form that we should expect of two symbolic structures analogous to the same thing. Translated into dream terms, the quest-romance is the search of the libido or desiring self for a fulfilment that will deliver it from the anxieties of reality but will still contain that reality. The antagonists of the quest are often sinister figures, giants, ogres, witches and magicians, that clearly have a parental origin; and yet redeemed and emancipated paternal figures are involved too, as they are in the psychological quests of both Freud and Jung. Translated into ritual terms, the quest-romance is the victory of fertility over the waste land. Fertility means food and drink, bread and wine, body and blood, the union of male and female. The precious objects brought back from the quest, or seen or obtained as a result of it, sometimes combine the ritual and the psychological associations. The Holy Grail, for instance, is connected with Christian Eucharist symbolism; it is related to or descended from a miraculous food-provider like the cornucopia, and, like other cups and hollow vessels, it has female sexual affinities, its masculine counterpart being, we are told, the bleeding lance. The pairing of solid food and liquid refreshment recurs in the edible tree and the water of life in the Biblical apocalypse.

我们或许可以将《仙后》的第一卷视为英国文学中最接近圣经冒险爱情主题的作品：它甚至比《天路历程》更接近圣经冒险爱情主题，后者之所以与它相似，是因为它们都与圣经相似。试图在不参考圣经的情况下比较班扬和斯宾塞，或者将他们的相似之处追溯到世俗爱情故事的共同起源，或多或少都是荒谬的。在斯宾塞笔下，英格兰守护圣人圣乔治的冒险故事中，主人公代表了英国的基督教教会，因此他的冒险是对基督冒险的模仿。斯宾塞笔下的红十字骑士由身着黑纱的乌娜女士引领，前往她父母的王国，那里正遭受恶龙的蹂躏。这条恶龙体型异常庞大，至少在象征意义上是如此。我们得知，乌娜的父母曾掌控着“整个世界”，直到恶龙“摧毁了他们所有的土地，并将他们驱逐出去”。尤娜的父母是亚当和夏娃；他们的王国是伊甸园，也就是未堕落的世界；而龙，象征着整个堕落的世界，被认为是利维坦、伊甸园中的蛇、撒旦以及《启示录》中的野兽。因此，圣乔治的使命，与基督的使命如出一辙，即通过杀死巨龙，在旷野中重建伊甸园，使英格兰恢复到伊甸园的状态。这种将理想的英格兰与伊甸园联系起来的观念，得益于西方海洋中一座幸福岛屿的传说，以及赫斯珀里得斯的故事与伊甸园故事的相似性，至少从格林的《培根修士》结尾一直延续到布莱克的《耶路撒冷》赞美诗，贯穿于英国文学之中。圣乔治与尤娜同行或独自跋涉，与以色列人在旷野中，在埃及和应许之地之间漂泊的经历如出一辙，他们肩扛着遮蔽的约柜，却又随时准备膜拜金牛犊。

We may take the first book of The Faerie Queene as representing perhaps the closest following of the Biblical quest-romance theme in English literature: it is closer even than The Pilgrim’s Progress, which resembles it because they both resemble the Bible. Attempts to compare Bunyan and Spenser without reference to the Bible, or to trace their similarities to a common origin in secular romance, are more or less perverse. In Spenser’s account of the quest of St. George, the patron saint of England, the protagonist represents the Christian Church in England, and hence his quest is an imitation of that of Christ. Spenser’s Redcross Knight is led by the lady Una (who is veiled in black) to the kingdom of her parents, which is being laid waste by a dragon. The dragon is of somewhat unusual size, at least allegorically. We are told that Una’s parents held “all the world” in their control until the dragon “Forwasted all their land, and them expelled.” Una’s parents are Adam and Eve; their kingdom is Eden or the unfallen world, and the dragon, who is the entire fallen world, is identified with the leviathan, the serpent of Eden, Satan, and the beast of Revelation. Thus St. George’s mission, a repetition of that of Christ, is by killing the dragon to raise Eden in the wilderness and restore England to the status of Eden. The association of an ideal England with Eden, assisted by legends of a happy island in the western ocean and by the similarity of the Hesperides story to that of Eden, runs through English literature at least from the end of Greene’s Friar Bacon to Blake’s “Jerusalem” hymn. St. George’s wanderings with Una, or without her, are parallel to the wandering of the Israelites in the wilderness, between Egypt and the Promised Land, bearing the veiled ark of the covenant and yet ready to worship a golden calf.

与恶龙的战斗自然持续了三天：在前两天结束时，圣乔治每次都被击败，但随后又分别因生命之水和生命树的滋养而恢复力量。这象征着改革教会的两项圣礼。接受；它们是伊甸园中将在启示录中恢复给人类的两大特征，并且与圣餐礼有着更广泛的联系。圣乔治的标志是白底红十字，这与传统圣像画中基督从地狱巨龙手中凯旋归来时所持的旗帜相同。红色和白色象征着复活身体的两个方面：血肉、面包和酒，在斯宾塞的著作中，它们与教会领袖的红白玫瑰结合有着历史渊源。红色和白色象征意义的圣礼层面和性层面之间的联系在炼金术中有所体现，斯宾塞显然对炼金术有所了解，在炼制长生不老药的关键阶段被称为“红王与白王后的结合”。

The battle with the dragon lasts, of course, three days: at the end of each of the first two days St. George is beaten back and is strengthened, first by the water of life, then by the tree of life. These represent the two sacraments which the reformed church accepted; they are the two features of the garden of Eden to be restored to man in the apocalypse, and they have also a more general Eucharist connection. St. George’s emblem is a red cross on a white ground, which is the flag borne by Christ in traditional iconography when he returns in triumph from the prostrate dragon of hell. The red and white symbolize the two aspects of the risen body, flesh and blood, bread and wine, and in Spenser they have a historical connection with the union of red and white roses in the reigning head of the church. The link between the sacramental and the sexual aspects of the red and white symbolism is indicated in alchemy, with which Spenser was clearly acquainted, in which a crucial phase of the production of the elixir of immortality is known as the union of the red king and the white queen.

浪漫小说的人物塑造遵循其一般的辩证结构，这意味着微妙和复杂性并不被重视。人物往往要么支持探险，要么反对探险。如果他们协助探险，就会被理想化为英勇或纯洁；如果他们阻碍探险，就会被丑化为邪恶或懦弱。因此，浪漫小说中的每个典型人物都倾向于与他的道德对立面对抗，就像国际象棋中的黑白棋子一样。在浪漫小说中，那些为探险而奋斗的“白棋”对应于喜剧中的反讽群体，尽管这个词在浪漫小说中已不再适用，因为讽刺在浪漫小说中几乎没有立足之地。浪漫小说中与喜剧中仁慈的退让反讽相对应的，是荣格所说的“老智者”形象，例如普洛斯彼罗、梅林，或是斯宾塞第二次探险中的帕尔默，他们通常是一位魔法师，能够影响他所注视的事件。 《仙后》中的亚瑟王虽然并非老人，但也扮演着这样的角色。他有一个女性对应物，即先知般的智慧母亲形象，通常是像《培尔·金特》中的索尔维格那样的潜在新娘，她静静地待在家中，等待英雄结束游历归来。后者通常是英雄为了她或遵从她的旨意而踏上征程的女子：在斯宾塞的笔下，她是仙后；在珀尔修斯的故事中，她是雅典娜。她们是白棋中的国王和王后，尽管在实际的国际象棋中，她们的走法当然是相反的。如果让王后成为英雄的情妇，除了政治意义之外，还有一个缺点，那就是她会破坏英雄在旅途中与那些身处困境、往往被诱人捆绑的少女们寻欢作乐的乐趣。她们赤身裸体地倚靠在岩石或树木上，如同阿里奥斯托笔下的安德洛墨达或安杰莉卡。由此便可构建出一种对立的形象：一位是尽职尽责的淑女，另一位是追求享乐的淑女——我们此前已在维多利亚时代浪漫小说中光明与黑暗的女主角身上略窥一二。一个简单的解决办法是让前者成为后者的婆婆：由此通常会产生一种在敌意和嫉妒之后和解的主题，例如阿普列乌斯笔下普赛克和维纳斯的关系。如果最终没有和解，年长的女性则会保持阴险的形象，如同民间故事中残酷的继母。

The characterization of romance follows its general dialectic structure, which means that subtlety and complexity are not much favored. Characters tend to be either for or against the quest. If they assist it they are idealized as simply gallant or pure; if they obstruct it they are caricatured as simply villainous or cowardly. Hence every typical character in romance tends to have his moral opposite confronting him, like black and white pieces in a chess game. In romance the “white” pieces who strive for the quest correspond to the eiron group in comedy, though the word is no longer appropriate, as irony has little place in romance. Romance has a counterpart to the benevolent retreating eiron of comedy in its figure of the “old wise man,” as Jung calls him, like Prospero, Merlin, or the palmer of Spenser’s second quest, often a magician who affects the action he watches over. The Arthur of The Faerie Queene, though not an old man, has this function. He has a feminine counterpart in the sibylline wise mother-figure, often a potential bride like Solveig in Peer Gynt, who sits quietly at home waiting for the hero to finish his wanderings and come back to her. This latter figure is often the lady for whose sake or at whose bidding the quest is performed: she is represented by the Faerie Queene in Spenser and by Athene in the Perseus story. These are the king and queen of the white pieces, though their power of movement is of course reversed in actual chess. The disadvantage of making the queen-figure the hero’s mistress, in anything more than a political sense, is that she spoils his fun with the distressed damsels he meets on his journey, who are often enticingly tied naked to rocks or trees, like Andromeda or Angelica in Ariosto. A polarization may thus be set up between the lady of duty and the lady of pleasure—we have already glanced at a late development of this in the light and dark heroines of Victorian romance. One simple way out is to make the former the latter’s mother-in-law: a theme of reconciliation after enmity and jealousy most commonly results, as in the relations of Psyche and Venus in Apuleius. Where there is no reconciliation, the older female remains sinister, the cruel stepmother of folk tale.

邪恶的魔法师和女巫，斯宾塞笔下的阿基玛戈和杜埃萨，分别是黑国王和黑后。荣格恰如其分地称后者为“可怕的母亲”，并将她与乱伦的恐惧以及美杜莎之类的女巫联系起来，这些女巫似乎都带有某种情色变态的暗示。除了新娘之外，其他被救赎的人物通常都过于软弱，难以塑造鲜明的形象。英雄的忠实伙伴或阴影人物在叛徒身上有其对立面，女主角在塞壬或美丽的巫婆身上有其对立面，龙在浪漫故事中常见的友好或乐于助人的动物身上有其对立面，其中，陪伴英雄踏上征程的马自然占据着核心地位。我们在喜剧中注意到的父子冲突在浪漫故事中也反复出现：在《圣经》中，第二个亚当拯救了第一个亚当；在圣杯传说中，纯洁的儿子加拉哈德完成了他那不纯洁的父亲兰斯洛特未能完成的使命。

The evil magician and the witch, Spenser’s Archimago and Duessa, are the black king and queen. The latter is appropriately called by Jung the “terrible mother,” and he associates her with the fear of incest and with such hags as Medusa who seem to have a suggestion of erotic perversion about them. The redeemed figures, apart from the bride, are generally too weak to be strongly characterized. The faithful companion or shadow figure of the hero has his opposite in the traitor, the heroine her opposite in the siren or beautiful witch, the dragon his opposite in the friendly or helping animals that are so conspicuous in romance, among which the horse who gets the hero to his quest has naturally a central place. The conflict of son and father that we noted in comedy recurs in romance: in the Bible the second Adam comes to the rescue of the first one, and in the Grail cycle the pure son Galahad accomplishes what his impure father Lancelot failed in.

那些游离于英雄与恶棍道德对立之外的角色，通常是自然精灵，或者暗示着自然精灵的存在。他们既代表着自然界中间世界的道德中立性，也代表着一个神秘莫测、只能瞥见却永远无法真正了解的世界，一个一旦靠近便会退却的世界。这类女性角色包括古典传说中羞涩的仙女，以及那些难以捉摸、半野性的生物，她们或许可以被视为女儿的化身，例如斯宾塞笔下的弗洛里梅尔、霍桑笔下的珀尔、瓦格纳笔下的昆德里和哈德逊笔下的里玛。与她们对应的男性角色则更为多样。吉卜林笔下的莫格利是最著名的野孩子；一个绿皮肤的男孩潜伏在中世纪英格兰的森林中，他曾化身为罗宾汉，也曾是高文爵士冒险故事中的骑士。在斯宾塞笔下，“拾荒者”萨提兰是文艺复兴时期人们最喜爱的人物之一，这位笨拙但忠诚、头发蓬乱的巨人几个世纪以来一直友好地穿梭于浪漫故事之中。

The characters who elude the moral antithesis of heroism and villainy generally are or suggest spirits of nature. They represent partly the moral neutrality of the intermediate world of nature and partly a world of mystery which is glimpsed but never seen, and which retreats when approached. Among female characters of this type are the shy nymphs of Classical legends and the elusive halfwild creatures who might be called daughter-figures, and include Spenser’s Florimell, Hawthorne’s Pearl, Wagner’s Kundry, and Hudson’s Rima. Their male counterparts have a little more variety. Kipling’s Mowgli is the best known of the wild boys; a green man lurked in the forests of medieval England, appearing as Robin Hood and as the knight of Gawain’s adventure; the “salvage man,” represented in Spenser by Satyrane, is a Renaissance favorite, and the awkward but faithful giant with unkempt hair has shambled amiably through romance for centuries.

这类人物或多或少都是大自然的孩子，他们能够他们被带到主人公身边服侍，就像鲁滨逊的星期五一样，但却保留着他们神秘莫测的出身。作为主人公的仆人或朋友，他们赋予主人公与自然之间那种神秘的联系，而这种联系往往是浪漫故事中主人公的标志。在浪漫故事中，这些自然之子大多是“超自然”生物这一悖论并不像在逻辑小说中那样令人困惑。乐于助人的仙女、感恩的亡灵、在危机时刻恰好拥有主人公所需能力的奇妙仆人，这些都是民间故事中常见的角色。他们是滑稽狡猾的奴隶（作者笔下的“建筑师”）在浪漫主义中的强化版。在詹姆斯·瑟伯的《十三座钟》中，这类人物被称为“戈卢克斯”（Golux），而这个词完全可以作为一个批评术语来使用。

Such characters are, more or less, children of nature, who can be brought to serve the hero, like Crusoe’s Friday, but retain the inscrutability of their origin. As servants or friends of the hero, they impart the mysterious rapport with nature that so often marks the central figure of romance. The paradox that many of these children of nature are “supernatural” beings is not as distressing in romance as in logic. The helpful fairy, the grateful dead man, the wonderful servant who has just the abilities the hero needs in a crisis, are all folk tale commonplaces. They are romantic intensifications of the comic tricky slave, the author’s architectus. In James Thurber’s The Thirteen Clocks this character type is called the “Golux,” and there is no reason why the word should not be adopted as a critical term.

浪漫小说和喜剧中似乎都存在四种人物塑造模式。英雄与敌人的斗争对应于喜剧中“爱神”与“恶神”的较量。前文提到的自然精灵在浪漫小说中与喜剧中的丑角或司仪有相似之处：也就是说，他们的功能是强化浪漫氛围并使其成为焦点。至于浪漫小说中是否存在类似于喜剧中“乡野小丑”（agroikos）的角色，即拒绝参加宴会或扮演乡村小丑的角色，还有待观察。

In romance, as in comedy, there seem to be four poles of characterization. The struggle of the hero with his enemy corresponds to the comic contest of eiron and alazon. In the nature-spirits just referred to we find the parallel in romance to the buffoon or master of ceremonies in comedy: that is, their function is to intensify and provide a focus for the romantic mood. It remains to be seen if there is a character in romance corresponding to the agroikos type in comedy, the refuser of festivity or rustic clown.

这样的角色会让人注意到生活中的现实层面，例如面对危险时的恐惧，这些都会威胁到浪漫氛围的统一性。在斯宾塞的小说中，圣乔治和尤娜身边就有一个背着“必需品”的侏儒。他不像另一个背着袋子的犹大·伊斯卡里奥特那样是个叛徒，但他“胆小”，会在行进艰难时劝他们撤退。这个背着必需品的侏儒，在浪漫的梦幻世界里，象征着现实生活中萎缩而苍老的形象：故事越现实，这样的角色就越重要，直到我们在《堂吉诃德》中看到另一个极端，他才最终化身为桑丘·潘萨，达到神化的境界。在其他浪漫故事中，我们也能找到一些傻瓜和弄臣，他们被允许表达恐惧或发表现实的评论，为现实主义提供了一个局部的安全阀，而不会破坏浪漫的传统。在马洛里的作品中，迪纳丹爵士扮演了类似的角色。书中详细解释说，他实际上是一位英勇的骑士，同时也是一位弄臣：因此，当他讲笑话时，“国王和兰斯洛特笑得都坐不住了”——这种过度和歇斯底里的笑声在心理上非常贴切。

Such a character would call attention to realistic aspects of life, like fear in the presence of danger, which threaten the unity of the romantic mood. St. George and Una in Spenser are accompanied by a dwarf who carries a bag of “needments.” He is not a traitor, like the other bag-carrier Judas Iscariot, but he is “fearful,” and urges retreat when the going is difficult. This dwarf with his needments represents, in the dream world of romance, the shrunken and wizened form of practical waking reality: the more realistic the story, the more important such a figure would become, until, when we reach the opposite pole in Don Quixote, he achieves his apotheosis as Sancho Panza. In other romances we find fools and jesters who are licensed to show fear or make realistic comments, and who provide a localized safety valve for realism without allowing it to disrupt the conventions of romance. In Malory a similar role is assumed by Sir Dinadan, who, it is carefully explained, is really a gallant knight as well as a jester: hence when he makes jokes “the king and Launcelot laughed that they might not sit”— the suggestion of excessive and hysterical laughter being psychologically very much to the point.

爱情故事如同喜剧，也分为六个独立的阶段。从悲剧到喜剧，爱情故事的前三个阶段与悲剧的前三个阶段相对应，后三个阶段则与喜剧的后三个阶段相对应（后者已从喜剧的角度进行了分析）。这些阶段在爱情故事主人公的一生中构成了一个循环往复的序列。

Romance, like comedy, has six isolatable phases, and as it moves from the tragic to the comic area, the first three are parallel to the first three phases of tragedy and the second three to the second three phases of comedy, already examined from the comic point of view. The phases form a cyclical sequence in a romantic hero’s life.

第一阶段是英雄诞生的神话，其形态在民间传说中已被详细研究。这个神话通常与洪水联系在一起，洪水是循环开始和结束的常用象征。幼小的英雄常常被放在漂浮在海上的方舟或箱子里，例如珀尔修斯的故事；他随后漂流到陆地上，例如《贝奥武夫》的序言；或者像摩西的故事那样，在河岸的芦苇丛中被救起。在但丁攀登炼狱山的旅程伊始，出现了一幅水、船和芦苇交织的景象，其中有很多暗示表明灵魂在这一阶段如同新生婴儿。在陆地上，婴儿可能被动物救起，也可能被动物救起；许多英雄在幼年时期都曾在森林中被动物抚养长大。当歌德笔下的浮士德开始寻找他的海伦娜时，他在佩纽斯的芦苇丛中寻找，然后找到了一位半人马，在她还是个孩子的时候，半人马背着她逃到了安全的地方。

The first phase is the myth of the birth of the hero, the morphology of which has been studied in some detail in folklore. This myth is often associated with a flood, the regular symbol of the beginning and the end of a cycle. The infant hero is often placed in an ark or chest floating on the sea, as in the story of Perseus; from there he drifts to land, as in the exordium to Beowulf, or is rescued from among reeds and bulrushes on a river bank, as in the story of Moses. A landscape of water, boat, and reeds appears at the beginning of Dante’s journey up the mount of Purgatory, where there are many suggestions that the soul is in that stage a newborn infant. On dry land the infant may be rescued either from or by an animal, and many heroes are nurtured by animals in a forest during their nonage. When Goethe’s Faust begins to look for his Helena, he searches in the reeds of the Peneus, and then finds a centaur who carried her to safety on his back when she was a child.

从心理学角度来看，这种意象与子宫中的胚胎有关，未出生的世界通常被认为是液态的；从人类学角度来看，它与埋葬在冰雪或沼泽死寂世界中的新生命种子有关。巨龙的宝藏与封存在箱子中的神秘婴儿生命紧密相连。财富的真正来源是潜在的生育能力或新生命（无论是植物还是人类），这一观点贯穿了从古代神话到罗斯金的《金河之王》的浪漫主义文学，罗斯金在其经济学著作中对财富的论述本质上是对这个童话故事的诠释。在《织工马南》中，宝藏与婴儿生命之间类似的关联以更合乎情理的形式出现。从欧里庇得斯到狄更斯，神秘身世这一主题在文学史上有着悠久的历史，这一点已在前文提及。

Psychologically, this image is related to the embryo in the womb, the world of the unborn often being thought of as liquid; anthropologically, it is related to the image of seeds of new life buried in a dead world of snow or swamp. The dragon’s treasure hoard is closely linked with this mysterious infant life enclosed in a chest. The fact that the real source of wealth is potential fertility or new life, vegetable or human, has run through romance from ancient myths to Ruskin’s King of the Golden River, Ruskin’s treatment of wealth in his economic works being essentially a commentary on this fairy tale. A similar association of treasure hoard and infant life appears in more plausible guise in Silas Marner. The long literary history of the theme of mysterious parentage from Euripides to Dickens has already been mentioned.

在《圣经》中，一个历史周期的结束和新周期的开始以平行的象征符号来标志。首先是普世洪水和一艘方舟，方舟中蕴藏着未来一切生命的潜力，漂浮在水面上；然后是埃及军队在红海中被淹没，以色列人获得自由，肩负起他们的使命。方舟穿越旷野，这一意象被但丁用作其炼狱象征体系的基础。《新约》以马槽中的婴孩开篇，而将外部世界描绘成被冰雪覆盖的传统，也使耶稣的降生与这一原型阶段联系起来。随后，春天回归的意象接踵而至：诺亚故事中的彩虹、摩西从磐石中取出水、基督的洗礼，所有这些都象征着循环从死亡的寒冬之水转向复苏的生命之水。那些具有神助作用的鸟儿，诺亚故事中的乌鸦和鸽子、旷野中喂养以利亚的乌鸦、盘旋在耶稣头顶的鸽子，都属于同一象征体系。

In the Bible the end of a historical cycle and the birth of a new one is marked by parallel symbols. First we have a universal deluge and an ark, with the potency of all future life contained in it, floating on the waters; then we have the story of the Egyptian host drowned in the Red Sea and the Israelites set free to carry their ark through the wilderness, an image adopted by Dante as the basis of his purgatorial symbolism. The New Testament begins with an infant in a manger, and the tradition of depicting the world outside as sunk in snow relates the Nativity to the same archetypal phase. Images of returning spring soon follow: the rainbow in the Noah story, the bringing of water out of a rock by Moses, the baptism of Christ, all show the turning of the cycle from the wintry water of death to the reviving waters of life. The providential birds, the raven and dove in the Noah story, the ravens feeding Elijah in the wilderness, the dove hovering over Jesus, belong to the same complex.

通常，故事中还会出现寻找孩子的情节，孩子必须被藏匿于秘密之地。由于英雄身世成谜，他的真实生父往往被隐瞒，一个假父亲出现，意图置孩子于死地。珀尔修斯故事中的阿克里西俄斯、赫西俄德神话中试图吞噬自己孩子的克洛诺斯、旧约中杀害孩子的法老以及新约中的希律王，都扮演着这样的角色。在后来的文学作品中，他常常演变成篡位邪恶的叔叔，莎士比亚的作品中就多次出现过这样的角色。因此，母亲常常成为嫉妒的受害者，遭受迫害或诽谤，就像珀尔修斯的母亲或《律师的故事》中的康斯坦丝一样。这种版本在心理上与儿子和可恨的父亲争夺母亲的主题非常接近。在维多利亚时代的通俗剧中，被恶毒的父亲将受辱的女儿连人带子赶出家门，通常是赶到雪地里的故事，依然令观众潸然泪下。与此同时，文学作品中也涌现出许多关于被追捕的母亲的故事，从《汤姆叔叔的小屋》中伊莉莎穿越冰面，到《亚当·比德》和《远离尘嚣》，不一而足。假母亲，也就是臭名昭著的恶毒继母，也十分常见：她的受害者当然通常是女性，由此产生的冲突在许多民谣和灰姑娘式的民间故事中都有所描绘。真正的父亲有时由一位睿智的老人或教师​​来扮演：例如普洛斯彼罗与费迪南德的关系，以及半人马喀戎与阿喀琉斯的关系。真正的母亲的化身则出现在收养摩西的法老女儿身上。在更现实主义的作品中，恶毒的父母则以狭隘的公众舆论的口吻或形式出现。

Often, too, there is a search for the child, who has to be hidden away in a secret place. The hero being of mysterious origin, his true paternity is often concealed, and a false father appears who seeks the child’s death. This is the role of Acrisius in the Perseus story, of the Cronos of Hesiodic myth who tries to swallow his children, of the child-killing Pharaoh in the Old Testament, and of Herod in the New. In later fiction he often modulates to the usurping wicked uncle who appears several times in Shakespeare. The mother is thus often the victim of jealousy, persecuted or calumniated like the mother of Perseus or like Constance in the Man of Law’s Tale. This version is very close psychologically to the theme of the rivalry of the son and a hateful father for possession of the mother. The theme of the calumniated girl ordered out of the house with her child by a cruel father, generally into the snow, still drew tears from audiences of Victorian melodramas, and literary developments of the theme of the hunted mother in the same period extend from Eliza crossing the ice in Uncle Tom’s Cabin to Adam Bede and Far from the Madding Crowd. The false mother, the celebrated cruel stepmother, is also common: her victim is of course usually female, and the resulting conflict is portrayed in many ballads and folktales of the Cinderella type. The true father is sometimes represented by a wise old man or teacher: this is the relation of Prospero to Ferdinand, as well as of Chiron the centaur to Achilles. The double of the true mother appears in the daughter of Pharaoh who adopts Moses. In more realistic modes the cruel parent speaks with the voice of, or takes the form of, a narrowminded public opinion.

第二阶段将我们带入英雄天真无邪的少年时代，这一阶段我们最熟悉的莫过于亚当和夏娃的故事。堕落前的伊甸园。在文学作品中，这一阶段展现了一个田园牧歌般的阿卡迪亚世界，通常是风景宜人的林间田园，遍布林间空地、荫凉山谷、潺潺溪流、明月以及其他与女性或母性意象紧密相关的意象。其象征色为绿色和金色，传统上代表着逝去的青春：人们会想到桑德堡的诗作《两个世界之间》。这通常是一个充满魔法或理想法则的世界，故事往往围绕着一位年轻的英雄展开，他仍笼罩在父母的光环之下，身边围绕着一群年轻的伙伴。情欲纯真的原型与其说是婚姻，不如说是婚前那种“纯洁”的爱；兄妹之爱，或是两个男孩之间的爱。因此，尽管在后来的阶段，它常常被人们回忆为逝去的幸福时光或黄金时代，但那种徘徊在道德禁忌边缘的感觉却十分常见，正如伊甸园的故事本身所展现的那样。约翰逊的《拉塞拉斯》、坡的《埃莉诺拉》和布莱克的《塞尔之书》向我们展示了一种监狱天堂或未出生的世界，中心人物渴望从中逃到下层世界，而同样的忧郁和渴望进入行动世界的感觉在英国文学中对这一阶段最详尽的处理——济慈的《恩底弥翁》中再次出现。

The second phase brings us to the innocent youth of the hero, a phase most familiar to us from the story of Adam and Eve in Eden before the Fall. In literature this phase presents a pastoral and Arcadian world, generally a pleasant wooded landscape, full of glades, shaded valleys, murmuring brooks, the moon, and other images closely linked with the female or maternal aspect of sexual imagery. Its heraldic colors are green and gold, traditionally the colors of vanishing youth: one thinks of Sandburg’s poem Between Two Worlds. It is often a world of magic or desirable law, and it tends to center on a youthful hero, still overshadowed by parents, surrounded by youthful companions. The archetype of erotic innocence is less commonly marriage than the kind of “chaste” love that precedes marriage; the love of brother for sister, or of two boys for each other. Hence, though in later phases it is often recalled as a lost happy time or Golden Age, the sense of being close to a moral taboo is very frequent, as it is of course in the Eden story itself. Johnson’s Rasselas, Poe’s Eleanora, and Blake’s Book of Thel introduce us to a kind of prison-Paradise or unborn world from which the central characters long to escape to a lower world, and the same feeling of malaise and longing to enter a world of action recurs in the most exhaustive treatment of the phase in English literature, Keats’s Endymion.

在这一阶段，性隔阂的主题以多种形式出现：伊甸园故事中的蛇在《绿屋》中重现；斯宾塞笔下的阿莫雷特与她的爱人斯库达穆尔之间，被一道火焰屏障隔开。在《炼狱篇》的结尾，灵魂重返未堕落的童年或失落的黄金时代，因此但丁发现自己身处伊甸园，与少女玛特尔达隔着忘川河。这条分隔的河流在威廉·莫里斯的奇特故事《洪水》中再次出现，其中射过河面的箭象征着性接触。在与《失乐园》中的伊甸园故事和《拉塞拉斯》都密切相关的《忽必烈汗》中，“圣河”之后紧接着出现一位歌唱少女的远景幻象。梅尔维尔的《皮埃尔》以对这一阶段的讽刺性模仿开篇，主人公仍然受制于他的母亲，却称她为妹妹。这个世界的许多意象都可以在《仙后》第六卷中找到，尤其是在特里斯特拉姆和帕斯托雷拉的故事中。

The theme of the sexual barrier in this phase takes many forms: the serpent of the Eden story recurs in Green Mansions, and a barrier of fire separates Amoret in Spenser from her lover Scudamour. At the end of the Purgatorio the soul reaches again its unfallen childhood or lost Golden Age, and Dante consequently finds himself in the garden of Eden, separated from the young girl Matelda by the river Lethe. The dividing river recurs in William Morris’s curious story The Sundering Flood, where an arrow shot over it has to do for the symbol of sexual contact. In Kubla Khan, which is closely related both to the Eden story in Paradise Lost and to Rasselas, a “sacred river” is closely followed by the distant vision of a singing damsel. Melville’s Pierre opens with a sardonic parody of this phase, the hero still dominated by his mother but calling her his sister. A good deal of the imagery of this world may be found in the sixth book of The Faerie Queene, especially in the stories of Tristram and Pastorella.

第三阶段是我们一直在讨论的常规任务主题，目前无需赘述。第四阶段对应于喜剧的第四阶段，在这个阶段中，更幸福的社会或多或少会贯穿整个剧情。这种状态往往在最后时刻才显现。在浪漫故事中，这一阶段的核心主题是抵御经验的冲击，维护纯真世界的完整性。因此，它常常以道德寓言的形式出现，例如弥尔顿的《科莫斯》、班扬的《圣战》以及许多道德剧，包括《坚忍城堡》 。相比之下，《坎特伯雷故事集》的模式则简单得多，其中唯一的冲突是如何在争吵中维护节日和庆典的气氛，但不知何故，这种模式似乎并不常见。

The third phase is the normal quest theme that we have been discussing, and needs no further comment at this point. The fourth phase corresponds to the fourth phase of comedy, in which the happier society is more or less visible throughout the action instead of emerging only in the last few moments. In romance the central theme of this phase is that of the maintaining of the integrity of the innocent world against the assault of experience. It thus often takes the form of a moral allegory, such as we have in Milton’s Comus, Bunyan’s Holy War, and many morality plays, including The Castell of Perseveraunce. The much simpler scheme of the Canterbury Tales, where the only conflict is to preserve the mood of holiday and festivity against bickering, seems for some reason to be less frequent.

需要捍卫的整体可以是个人层面的，也可以是社会层面的，或者两者兼而有之。在《仙后》第二卷中，节制的寓言展现了其个人层面。第二卷是第一卷的自然延续，探讨了在完成第一次伟大冒险之后，如何在这个世界上巩固英雄的纯真这一更为艰深的主题。节制骑士盖昂的主要对手是极乐花园的女主人阿克拉西亚和玛门。他们分别代表“美貌与金钱”，即被扭曲为外在目标的工具性财富。节制的心灵将善蕴藏于自身，而自制是其前提，因此它属于我们所说的纯真世界。放纵的心灵则在经验世界的外部对象中寻求善。节制和放纵都可以被称为自然，但前者属于作为秩序的自然，后者属于作为堕落世界的自然。科莫斯对夫人的诱惑也基于自然意义的类似歧义。这一浪漫阶段的核心意象是饱受围困的城堡，斯宾塞笔下的阿尔玛之家便是这一意象的象征，它被描述为与人体机能的运作机制相关。

The integrated body to be defended may be individual or social, or both. The individual aspect of it is presented in the allegory of temperance in the second book of The Faerie Queene, which forms a natural sequel to the first book, dealing as it does with the more difficult theme of consolidating heroic innocence in this world after the first great quest has been completed. Guyon, the knight of temperance, has as his main antagonists Acrasia, the mistress of the Bower of Bliss, and Mammon. These represent “Beauty and money,” in their aspects as instrumental goods perverted into external goals. The temperate mind contains its good within itself, continence being its prerequisite, hence it belongs to what we have called the innocent world. The intemperate mind seeks its good in the external object of the world of experience. Both temperance and intemperance could be called natural, but one belongs to nature as an order and the other to nature as a fallen world. Comus’s temptation of the Lady is based on a similar ambiguity in the meaning of nature. A central image in this phase of romance is that of the beleaguered castle, represented in Spenser by the House of Alma, which is described in terms of the economy of the human body.

《仙后》第五卷——正义的传说——探讨了同一阶段的社会层面，其中权力是正义的先决条件，这与节制中的自律相对应。在伊西斯和奥西里斯的幻象中，我们看到了第四阶段的意象：处女驯服并控制了怪物。这一意象在第一卷中也零星出现，与乌娜驯服萨堤尔和狮子的故事相关。其古典原型是雅典娜盾牌上的戈耳工头像。从《以赛亚书》中孩童引领猛兽，到《伯里克利》中妓院里的玛丽娜，文学作品中都出现了类似的意象，例如无敌的纯真或贞洁，并在后来的小说中反复出现。故事讲述的是一位性情暴戾的男主角最终被女主角驯服。阿里斯托芬的《吕西斯特拉忒》正是以讽刺戏仿的方式呈现了这一主题。

The social aspect of the same phase is treated in the fifth book of The Faerie Queene, the legend of justice, where power is the prerequisite of justice, corresponding to continence in relation to temperance. Here we meet, in the vision of Isis and Osiris, the fourth-phase image of the monster tamed and controlled by the virgin, an image which appears episodically in Book One in connection with Una, who tames satyrs and a lion. The Classical prototype of it is the Gorgon’s head on the shield of Athene. The theme of invincible innocence or virginity is associated with similar images in literature from the child leading the beasts of prey in Isaiah to Marina in the brothel in Pericles, and it reappears in later fictions in which an unusually truculent hero is brought to heel by the heroine. An ironic parody of the same theme forms the basis of Aristophanes’ Lysistrata.

第五阶段对应于喜剧的第五阶段，它如同喜剧一样，是一种从高处俯瞰、反思性的田园式体验，其中自然循环的运行通常占据着显著地位。它描绘的世界与第二阶段非常相似，只是其氛围并非青春期的准备，而是行动之后或行动的沉思式退隐。与第二阶段一样，它也是一个充满情欲的世界，但它将体验呈现为一种已被理解而非神秘的状态。莫里斯的大部分浪漫故事、霍桑的《布莱斯代尔传奇》、成熟而纯真的《富兰克林的故事》以及《仙后》第三卷的大部分意象都属于这一世界。在《仙后》以及莎士比亚晚期的浪漫故事中，尤其是《佩里克利斯》和《暴风雨》，我们都注意到人物道德分层的倾向。真正的恋人处于一种可称之为情欲模仿的等级制度的顶端，而其他等级则依次是不同程度的欲望和激情，直至堕落（例如斯宾塞笔下的阿尔冈特和奥利芬特；《伯里克利》中的安条克和他的女儿）。这种人物安排与这一时期人们对社会所持的超脱和沉思的态度相一致。

The fifth phase corresponds to the fifth phase of comedy, and like it is a reflective, idyllic view of experience from above, in which the movement of the natural cycle has usually a prominent place. It deals with a world very similar to that of the second phase except that the mood is a contemplative withdrawal from or sequel to action rather than a youthful preparation for it. It is, like the second phase, an erotic world, but it presents experience as comprehended and not as a mystery. This is the world of most of Morris’s romances, of Hawthorne’s Blithedale Romance, of the mature innocent wisdom of The Franklin’s Tale, and of most of the imagery of the third book of The Faerie Queene. In this last, as well as in the late Shakespearean romances, notably Pericles, and even The Tempest, we notice a tendency to the moral stratification of characters. The true lovers are on top of a hierarchy of what might be called erotic imitations, going down through the various grades of lust and passion to perversion (Argante and Oliphant in Spenser; Antiochus and his daughter in Pericles). Such an arrangement of characters is consistent with the detached and contemplative view of society taken in this phase.

第六阶段，即沉思阶段，是浪漫主义和喜剧的最后一个阶段。在喜剧中，它展现了喜剧式的社会分裂成一个个小团体或个体；在浪漫主义中，它标志着从积极的冒险到沉思的冒险的转变的结束。这一阶段的核心意象，也是叶芝钟爱的意象，是高塔中的老人，一个沉浸于神秘学或魔法研究的孤独隐士。在更大众化、更社会化的层面上，它涵盖了所谓的“温馨小说”：与舒适的床铺、壁炉旁的椅子或温暖舒适的场所相关的浪漫故事。这一阶段的一个显著特征是带有引号的故事，开头描绘了一小群友善的人，然后由其中一人讲述真正的故事。在《螺丝在拧紧》中，一大群人在乡间别墅里讲鬼故事；然后一些人离开，一个更小、更亲密的圈子聚集在一起，围绕着关键的故事。开篇遣散慕道友的情节完全符合这一阶段的精神和惯例。这些手法的效果是，通过一种轻松沉思的氛围来呈现故事，使其具有娱乐性。可以说，悲剧并没有直接降临到我们身上，而是以一种隐晦的方式降临到我们身上。

The sixth or penseroso phase is the last phase of romance as of comedy. In comedy it shows the comic society breaking up into small units or individuals; in romance it marks the end of a movement from active to contemplative adventure. A central image of this phase, a favorite of Yeats, is that of the old man in the tower, the lonely hermit absorbed in occult or magical studies. On a more popular and social level it takes in what might be called cuddle fiction: the romance that is physically associated with comfortable beds or chairs around fireplaces or warm and cosy spots generally. A characteristic feature of this phase is the tale in quotation marks, where we have an opening setting with a small group of congenial people, and then the real story told by one of the members. In The Turn of the Screw a large party is telling ghost stories in a country house; then some people leave, and a much smaller and more intimate circle gathers around the crucial tale. The opening dismissal of catechumens is thoroughly in the spirit and conventions of this phase. The effect of such devices is to present the story through a relaxed and contemplative haze as something that entertains us without, so to speak, confronting us, as direct tragedy confronts us.

以《十日谈》等会饮式结构为基础的故事集就属于这一范畴。莫里斯的《尘世乐园》便是同一阶段的典型范例：书中将希腊和北欧文化中的许多伟大原型神话拟人化为一群在中世纪弃世而去的老人，他们拒绝成为国王或神祇，如今在一个虚幻的梦境中交换着各自的神话。孤独的老人、亲密的群体以及口述故事的主题在此交织在一起。故事的编排也与自然循环的象征意义相呼应。弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的《幕间》则是对这一阶段的另一种高度集中的诠释。书中，一出展现英国生活史的戏剧在观众面前上演。这段历史不仅被构想为一个进程，更被构想为一个循环，而观众既是循环的终点，正如最后一页所示，也是循环的起点。

Collections of tales based on a symposium device like the Decameron belong here. Morris’s Earthly Paradise is a very pure example of the same phase: there a number of the great archetypal myths of Greek and Northern culture are personified as a group of old men who forsook the world during the Middle Ages, refusing to be made either kings or gods, and who now interchange their myths in an ineffectual land of dreams. Here the themes of the lonely old men, the intimate group, and the reported tale are linked. The calendar arrangement of the tales links it also with the symbolism of the natural cycle. Another and very concentrated treatment of the phase is Virginia Woolf’s Between the Acts, where a play representing the history of English life is acted before a group. The history is conceived not only as a progression but as a cycle of which the audience is the end, and, as the last page indicates, the beginning as well.

从瓦格纳的《尼伯龙根的指环》到科幻小说，我们或许会注意到“洪水”这一主题越来越受欢迎。它通常表现为某种宇宙灾难摧毁了整个虚构社会，只留下一小群人幸存下来，并在某个避难所重新开始生活。这一主题与那种与世隔绝的舒适小团体之间的相似之处显而易见，这又让我们联想到漂浮在海面上的神秘新生儿的形象。

From Wagner’s Ring to science fiction, we may notice an increasing popularity of the flood archetype. This usually takes the form of some cosmic disaster destroying the whole fictional society except a small group, which begins life anew in some sheltered spot. The affinities of this theme to that of the cosy group which has managed to shut the rest of the world out are clear enough, and it brings us around again to the image of the mysterious newborn infant floating on the sea.

诗歌象征主义中还有一个重要的细节值得探讨。那就是，它象征性地呈现了末世世界与自然循环世界最终契合的点，我们称之为“顿悟点”。它最常见的象征物包括山顶、岛屿、高塔、灯塔以及梯子或楼梯。民间故事和神话中充满了关于天地之间最初联系的传说。例如，箭梯、被顽皮的鸟啄断的绳索等等：这些故事常常与圣经中关于堕落的故事遥相呼应，并流传于杰克的魔豆、长发公主的长发，甚至还有被称为“印第安绳索戏法”的奇特民间传说。从一个世界到另一个世界的转换可以用从太阳降临的金色火焰来象征，正如达那厄神话的起源。故事及其引发的人类反应，点燃了祭坛上的火焰。在爱伦·坡的故事中，一只“金甲虫”被绳子拴着，从树上骷髅头的眼孔中垂下，落在埋藏的宝藏上——这提醒我们埃及圣甲虫是太阳的象征。这里的原型与我们正在探讨的复杂意象密切相关，尤其与某些炼金术版本相关。

One important detail in poetic symbolism remains to be considered.
