This is the symbolic presentation of the point at which the undisplaced apocalyptic world and the cyclical world of nature come into alignment, and which we propose to call the point of epiphany. Its most common settings are the mountain-top, the island, the tower, the lighthouse, and the ladder or staircase. Folk tales and mythologies are full of stories of an original connection between heaven or the sun and earth. We have ladders of arrows, ropes pecked in two by mischievous birds, and the like: such stories are often analogues of the Biblical stories of the Fall, and survive in Jack’s beanstalk, Rapunzel’s hair, and even the curious bit of floating folklore known as the Indian rope trick. The movement from one world to the other may be symbolized by the golden fire that descends from the sun, as in the mythical basis of the Danae story, and by its human response, the fire kindled on the sacrificial altar. The “gold bug” in Poe’s story, which reminds us that the Egyptian scarab was a solar emblem, is dropped from above on the end of a string through the eyehole of a skull on a tree and falls on top of a buried treasure: the archetype here is closely related to the complex of images we are dealing with, especially to some alchemical versions of it.

在《圣经》中，我们有雅各的天梯，在《失乐园》中，它与弥尔顿的宇宙图解相关联——一个球形宇宙悬挂在天上，顶部有一个洞。圣经中有几处山顶显灵的场景，其中最著名的是耶稣显圣容，而摩西在旷野尽头的毗斯迦山上看到的异象——他从那里看到了遥远的应许之地——在象征意义上与之相关。只要诗人接受托勒密的宇宙观，显灵的自然地点就是月亮下方的一座山峰，月亮是最低的天体。在但丁的《炼狱》中，炼狱是一座巨大的山，一条螺旋上升的小路环绕着它，在山顶上，随着朝圣者逐渐恢复失去的纯真并摆脱原罪，便是伊甸园。正是在这里，《炼狱篇》最后几章中那惊人的末世显灵得以实现。人世间也存在着一种介于末日世界和循环世界之间的感觉，正如伊甸园中所有植物生命的种子都落回了现实世界，而人类的生命却不断消逝。

In the Bible we have Jacob’s ladder, which in Paradise Lost is associated with Milton’s cosmological diagram of a spherical cosmos hanging from heaven with a hole in the top. There are several mountain-top epiphanies in the Bible, the Transfiguration being the most notable, and the mountain vision of Pisgah, the end of the road through the wilderness from which Moses saw the distant Promised Land, is typologically linked. As long as poets accepted the Ptolemaic universe, the natural place for the point of epiphany was a mountain-top just under the moon, the lowest heavenly body. Purgatory in Dante is an enormous mountain with a path ascending spirally around it, on top of which, as the pilgrim gradually recovers his lost innocence and casts off his original sin, is the garden of Eden. It is at this point that the prodigious apocalyptic epiphany of the closing cantos of the Purgatorio is achieved. The sense of being between an apocalyptic world above and a cyclical world below is present too, as from the garden of Eden all seeds of vegetable life fall back into the world, while human life passes on.

在《仙后》第一卷中，圣乔治攀登至沉思之山，远眺天城，便见了皮斯加山的幻象。他必须斩杀的巨龙象征着堕落的世界，因此，这则寓言也蕴含着更深层次的意义：巨龙代表着他与遥远天城之间的空间。在阿里奥斯托的相应章节中，山巅与月相之间的联系则更为清晰。然而，斯宾塞对这一主题最完整的诠释，当属其精彩绝伦的玄学喜剧《变幻之歌》。在这部作品中，存在与生成、宙斯与变幻、秩序与变化之间的冲突，最终在月相层面得以化解。变幻的证据是自然界的循环运动，但这种证据最终却被反驳，证明它并非仅仅是变化，而是自然界秩序的原则。在这首诗中，天体与末世的关系并非像但丁《天堂篇》中那样是一种隐喻式的等同关系（至少在诗歌惯例上是如此） ，而是相似性：它们仍然属于自然范畴，并且只有在诗歌的最后一节中，真正的末日世界才出现。

In The Faerie Queene there is a Pisgah vision in the first book, when St. George climbs the mountain of contemplation and sees the heavenly city from a distance. As the dragon he has to kill is the fallen world, there is a level of the allegory in which his dragon is the space between himself and the distant city. In the corresponding episode of Ariosto the link between the mountain-top and the sphere of the moon is clearer. But Spenser’s fullest treatment of the theme is the brilliant metaphysical comedy known as the Mutabilitie Cantoes, where the conflict of being and becoming, Jove and Mutability, order and change, is resolved at the sphere of the moon. Mutability’s evidence consists of the cyclical movements of nature, but this evidence is turned against her and proved to be a principle of order in nature instead of mere change. In this poem the relation of the heavenly bodies to the apocalyptic world is not metaphorical identification, as it is, at least as a poetic convention, in Dante’s Paradiso, but likeness: they are still within nature, and only in the final stanza of the poem does the real apocalyptic world appear.

此处对层次的区分暗示着顿悟点可能存在类似的形态。例如，它可以被描绘成一个性满足的场所，那里没有世界末日的景象，而仅仅是一种抵达自然体验巅峰的感觉。这种自然形式的顿悟点在斯宾塞的诗中被称为“阿多尼斯花园”。它在济慈的《恩底弥翁》中也以这个名称出现，并且是雪莱的《伊斯兰的叛乱》结尾处恋人们进入的世界。阿多尼斯花园如同但丁笔下的伊甸园，是一个种子之地，一切遵循自然循环秩序的事物在死亡时进入其中，并在出生时由此而出。弥尔顿的早期诗作，如同《变幻之歌》一样，充满了对自然作为神圣秩序、天体音乐的本质，以及自然作为堕落且大多混乱的世界之间的区分。前者以科莫斯的阿多尼斯花园为象征，侍奉女神的精灵由此降临守护女神。这一原型的核心意象——维纳斯守护阿多尼斯——（用现代的区分来说）在爱欲层面相当于博爱层面中的圣母子。

The distinction of levels here implies that there may be analogous forms of the point of epiphany. For instance, it may be presented in erotic terms as a place of sexual fulfilment, where there is no apocalyptic vision but simply a sense of arriving at the summit of experience in nature. This natural form of the point of epiphany is called in Spenser the Gardens of Adonis. It recurs under that name in Keats’s Endymion and is the world entered by the lovers at the end of Shelley’s Revolt of Islam. The Gardens of Adonis, like Eden in Dante, are a place of seed, into which everything subject to the cyclical order of nature enters at death and proceeds from at birth. Milton’s early poems are, like the Mutabilitie Cantoes, full of the sense of a distinction between nature as a divinely sanctioned order, the nature of the music of the spheres, and nature as a fallen and largely chaotic world. The former is symbolized by the Gardens of Adonis in Comus, from whence the attendant spirit descends to watch over the Lady. The central image of this archetype, Venus watching over Adonis, is (to use a modern distinction) the analogue in terms of Eros to the Madonna and Son in the context of Agape.

弥尔顿在《复乐园》中延续了毗斯迦山异象的主题，其依据是圣经预表论的一个基本原则：基督的生平事迹与以色列的历史遥相呼应。以色列人前往埃及，由约瑟带领，躲过屠杀无辜百姓的劫难，被红海与埃及隔绝，组成十二支派，在旷野漂流四十年，从西奈山领受律法，被铜蛇从杆上救出，渡过约旦河，在“耶稣所称的外邦人约书亚”的带领下进入应许之地。耶稣在婴孩时期，由约瑟带领前往埃及，躲过屠杀，受洗并被尊为弥赛亚，在旷野漂流四十天，聚集十二门徒，宣讲登山宝训，被钉在杆上舍命拯救世人，最终如同真正的约书亚一般征服了应许之地。在弥尔顿的作品中，耶稣受试探的场景与摩西在毗斯迦山上的异象相对应，只是目光转向了相反的方向。这标志着耶稣对律法顺服的巅峰，紧随其后，在他积极救赎世界之前。这一系列的试探将世界、肉体和魔鬼融为一体，最终指向撒旦。此处象征着耶稣的顿悟。在圣殿的顶端，撒旦从那里坠落，而耶稣则静立于其上。撒旦的坠落提醒我们，顿悟之点也是命运之轮的顶端，是悲剧英雄坠落之处。这种对顿悟之点的讽刺性运用在《圣经》巴别塔的故事中也有体现。

Milton picks up the theme of the Pisgah vision in Paradise Regained, which assumes an elementary principle of Biblical typology in which the events of Christ’s life repeat those of the history of Israel. Israel goes to Egypt, brought down by Joseph, escapes a slaughter of innocents, is cut off from Egypt by the Red Sea, organizes into twelve tribes, wanders forty years in the wilderness, receives the law from Sinai, is saved by a brazen serpent on a pole, crosses the Jordan, and enters the Promised Land under “Joshua, whom the Gentiles Jesus call.” Jesus goes to Egypt in infancy, led by Joseph, escapes a slaughter of innocents, is baptized and recognized as the Messiah, wanders forty days in the wilderness, gathers twelve followers, preaches the Sermon on the Mount, saves mankind by dying on a pole, and thereby conquers the Promised Land as the real Joshua. In Milton the temptation corresponds to the Pisgah vision of Moses, except that the gaze is turned in the opposite direction. It marks the climax of Jesus’ obedience to the law, just before his active redemption of the world begins, and the sequence of temptations consolidates the world, flesh, and devil into the single form of Satan. The point of epiphany is here represented by the pinnacle of the temple, from which Satan falls away as Jesus remains motionless on top of it. The fall of Satan reminds us that the point of epiphany is also the top of the wheel of fortune, the point from which the tragic hero falls. This ironic use of the point of epiphany occurs in the Bible in the story of the Tower of Babel.

托勒密宇宙论最终消逝，但顿悟的契机却并未消失，尽管在近代文学中，它常常被讽刺性地逆转，或被纳入更高的可信度要求之中。即便如此，我们仍然可以在易卜生的《当我们死而复生时》的结尾山顶场景以及弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的《到灯塔去》的核心意象中看到同样的原型。在叶芝和艾略特的后期诗歌中，它成为一个核心的统一意象。《塔》和《蜿蜒的楼梯》等标题表明了它对叶芝的重要性，《塔》和《驶向拜占庭》中月亮的象征意义和末世意象都完全一致。在艾略特的《荒原》中，它是火的布道中所达到的火焰，与象征着水的自然循环形成对比；它也是《空心人》中的“多叶玫瑰”。圣灰星期三又把我们带回了炼狱的螺旋楼梯，而小吉丁则回到了燃烧的玫瑰，那里有火焰的下降运动，象征着五旬节的火焰之舌，以及火焰的上升运动，象征着赫拉克勒斯的火葬堆和“火焰衬衫”。

The Ptolemaic cosmos eventually disappeared, but the point of epiphany did not, though in more recent literature it is often ironically reversed, or brought to terms with greater demands for credibility. Allowing for this, one may still see the same archetype in the final mountain-top scene of Ibsen’s When We Dead Awaken and in the central image of Virginia Woolf’s To the Lighthouse. In the later poetry of Yeats and Eliot it becomes a central unifying image. Such titles as The Tower and The Winding Stair indicate its importance for Yeats, and the lunar symbolism and the apocalyptic imagery of The Tower and Sailing to Byzantium are both thoroughly consistent. In Eliot it is the flame reached in the fire sermon of The Waste Land, in contrast to the natural cycle which is symbolized by water, and it is also the “multifoliate rose” of The Hollow Men. Ash Wednesday brings us back again to the purgatorial winding stair, and Little Gidding to the burning rose, where there is a descending movement of fire symbolized by the Pentecostal tongues of flame and an ascending one symbolized by Hercules’ pyre and “shirt of flame.”

秋季神话：悲剧

THE MYTHOS OF AUTUMN: TRAGEDY

一如既往，多亏了亚里士多德，悲剧理论比其他三种神话体系（mythoi）要完善得多，因此我们可以更简明扼要地探讨它，因为它的基础更为熟悉。如果没有悲剧，所有文学虚构作品都可以被合理地解释为情感依恋的表达，无论是愿望的实现还是厌恶的表达：悲剧虚构作品可以说保证了文学体验的客观性。正是通过希腊文化中的悲剧，人类性格的真实自然基础才得以进入文学领域。在浪漫故事中，人物大多仍是梦境中的人物；在讽刺作品中，他们往往是漫画式的形象；在喜剧中，他们的行为被扭曲以迎合皆大欢喜的结局。在真正的悲剧中，主人公从梦境中解放出来，这种解放同时也是一种限制。因为自然秩序依然存在。无论悲剧中充斥着多少鬼魂、预兆、女巫或神谕，我们都知道，悲剧英雄不可能简单地摩擦神灯召唤精灵来摆脱困境。

Thanks as usual to Aristotle, the theory of tragedy is in considerably better shape than the other three mythoi, and we can deal with it more briefly, as the ground is more familiar. Without tragedy, all literary fictions might be plausibly explained as expressions of emotional attachments, whether of wish-fulfilment or of repugnance: the tragic fiction guarantees, so to speak, a disinterested quality in literary experience. It is largely through the tragedies of Greek culture that the sense of the authentic natural basis of human character comes into literature. In romance the characters are still largely dream-characters; in satire they tend to be caricatures; in comedy their actions are twisted to fit the demands of a happy ending. In full tragedy the main characters are emancipated from dream, an emancipation which is at the same time a restriction, because the order of nature is present. However thickly strewn a tragedy may be with ghosts, portents, witches, or oracles, we know that the tragic hero cannot simply rub a lamp and summon a genie to get him out of his trouble.

与喜剧一样，悲剧最好也最容易在戏剧学中进行研究，但它并非局限于戏剧，也并非仅限于以灾难告终的行为。通常被称为或归类为悲剧的剧作，其结局往往是平静的，例如《辛白林》；甚至是喜悦的，例如《阿尔刻提斯》或拉辛的《以斯帖》 ；或者是一种难以定义的暧昧情绪，例如《菲罗克忒忒斯》。另一方面，虽然阴郁的氛围是悲剧结构统一性的一部分，但过分强调氛围并不能增强悲剧效果：如果真是如此，《泰特斯·安德洛尼克斯》或许会成为莎士比亚所有悲剧中最震撼人心的一部。正如亚里士多德所指出的，悲剧效果的根源必须从悲剧神话或情节结构中寻找。

Like comedy, tragedy is best and most easily studied in drama, but it is not confined to drama, nor to actions that end in disaster. Plays that are usually called or classified with tragedies end in serenity, like Cymbeline, or even joy, like Alcestis or Racine’s Esther, or in an ambiguous mood that is hard to define, like Philoctetes. On the other hand, while a predominantly sombre mood forms part of the unity of the tragic structure, concentrating on mood does not intensify the tragic effect: if it did, Titus Andronicus might well be the most powerful of Shakespeare’s tragedies. The source of tragic effect must be sought, as Aristotle pointed out, in the tragic mythos or plot-structure.

评论界普遍认为，喜剧往往关注社会群体中的人物，而悲剧则更集中于单个个体。我们在第一篇文章中阐述了为何典型的悲剧英雄介于神性和“过于人性化”之间。即使是垂死的神祇也应如此：普罗米修斯身为神，不会死亡，但他却因同情“垂死之人”（brotoi ）或“凡人”而遭受苦难，甚至苦难本身也蕴含着某种超凡脱俗的特质。与我们相比，悲剧英雄无比伟大，但除此之外，还有某种东西，某种与观众相对的存在，与之相比，他显得渺小。这“其他的东西”可以被称为上帝、诸神、命运、意外、机遇、必然、境遇，或是它们的任意组合，但无论它是什么，悲剧英雄都是我们与它之间的媒介。

It is a commonplace of criticism that comedy tends to deal with characters in a social group, whereas tragedy is more concentrated on a single individual. We have given reasons in the first essay for thinking that the typical tragic hero is somewhere between the divine and the “all too human.” This must be true even of dying gods: Prometheus, being a god, cannot die, but he suffers for his sympathy with the “dying ones” (brotoi) or “mortal” men, and even suffering has something subdivine about it. The tragic hero is very great as compared with us, but there is something else, something on the side of him opposite the audience, compared to which he is small. This something else may be called God, gods, fate, accident, fortune, necessity, circumstance, or any combination of these, but whatever it is the tragic hero is our mediator with it.

悲剧英雄通常处于命运之轮的顶端，介于尘世的人类社会与天上的至高存在之间。普罗米修斯、亚当和基督悬于天地之间，徘徊于天堂般的自由世界与奴役的世界之间。悲剧英雄在他们所处的人类世界里如此显赫，以至于他们似乎成了周围力量的必然导体，如同参天大树比一丛小草更容易被闪电击中。当然，导体也可能是神圣闪电的工具，也可能是受害者：弥尔顿笔下的参孙以身殉非利士人的神庙，哈姆雷特在自己的陨落中几乎将丹麦宫廷彻底摧毁。尼采那种高高在上、重新审视一切的姿态，似乎也萦绕在悲剧英雄身上：他的思想他的功绩并不属于我们，即便他像浮士德一样，因这些功绩而被拖入地狱。无论他多么能言善辩、和蔼可亲，其背后都隐藏着一种难以捉摸的矜持。即使是阴险的英雄——帖木儿、麦克白、克瑞翁——也保留着这种矜持，这提醒我们，人们会为邪恶或残暴的人忠诚赴死，却不会为一个和蔼可亲、阿谀奉承之辈而死。那些最能赢得他人拥戴的人，往往最能以自己的言行举止暗示自己并不需要这种拥戴。从哈姆雷特的温文尔雅到埃阿斯的阴郁凶狠，悲剧英雄们都笼罩在一种神秘的氛围中，他们与某种我们只能透过他们才能窥见的事物相连，而这既是他们力量的源泉，也是他们命运的根源。在叶芝非常着迷的这句话中，悲剧英雄让仆人替他“谋生”，悲剧的中心在于英雄的孤立，而不是恶人的背叛，即使恶人（通常情况下）是英雄自身的一部分。

The tragic hero is typically on top of the wheel of fortune, halfway between human society on the ground and the something greater in the sky. Prometheus, Adam, and Christ hang between heaven and earth, between a world of paradisal freedom and a world of bondage. Tragic heroes are so much the highest points in their human landscape that they seem the inevitable conductors of the power about them, great trees more likely to be struck by lightning than a clump of grass. Conductors may of course be instruments as well as victims of the divine lightning: Milton’s Samson destroys the Philistine temple with himself, and Hamlet nearly exterminates the Danish court in his own fall. Something of Nietzsche’s mountain-top air of transvaluation clings to the tragic hero: his thoughts are not ours any more than his deeds, even if, like Faustus, he is dragged off to hell for having them. Whatever eloquence or affability he may have, an inscrutable reserve lies behind it. Even sinister heroes—Tamburlaine, Macbeth, Creon—retain this reserve, and we are reminded that men will die loyally for a wicked or cruel man, but not for an amiable backslapper. Those who attract most devotion from others are those who are best able to suggest in their manner that they have no need of it, and from the urbanity of Hamlet to the sullen ferocity of Ajax, tragic heroes are wrapped in the mystery of their communion with that something beyond which we can see only through them, and which is the source of their strength and their fate alike. In the phrase which so fascinated Yeats, the tragic hero leaves his servants to do his “living” for him, and the center of tragedy is in the hero’s isolation, not in a villain’s betrayal, even when the villain is, as he often is, a part of the hero himself.

至于超越尘世的存在，它的名称虽多，但其显现的形式却相当恒定。无论语境是希腊的、基督教的，还是未被定义的，悲剧似乎都指向对法则的顿悟，即对存在与必然之物的揭示。五世纪雅典和十七世纪欧洲悲剧的两大发展与爱奥尼亚科学和文艺复兴时期科学的兴起几乎同时发生，这绝非偶然。在这种世界观中，自然被视为一种非人格化的进程，人类的法律竭力模仿它，而人与自然法则的这种直接关系则被置于首要位置。希腊悲剧中命运凌驾于神明之上的观念，实际上意味着神明的存在主要是为了维护自然秩序，而任何存在，即使是神明，如果拥有真正否决法则的权力，他也极不可能行使这种权力。在基督教中，基督的人格与天父深不可测的旨意之间的关系，也大致如此。同样，莎士比亚笔下的悲剧进程也具有自然性，它自然而然地发生，无论其起因、解释或关联如何。剧中人物或许会苦苦思索那些以杀戮为乐的神祇，或是塑造我们命运的神明，但悲剧的进程不会接受我们的疑问，这一事实常常被归咎于莎士比亚的性格。

As for the something beyond, its names are variable but the form in which it manifests itself is fairly constant. Whether the context is Greek, Christian, or undefined, tragedy seems to lead up to an epiphany of law, of that which is and must be. It can hardly be an accident that the two great developments of tragic drama, in fifth-century Athens and in seventeenth-century Europe, were contemporary with the rise of Ionian and of Renaissance science. In such a world-view nature is seen as an impersonal process which human law imitates as best it can, and this direct relation of man and natural law is in the foreground. The sense in Greek tragedy that fate is stronger than the gods really implies that the gods exist primarily to ratify the order of nature, and that if any personality, even a divine one, possesses a genuine power of veto over law, it is most unlikely that he will want to exercise it. In Christianity much the same is true of the personality of Christ in relation to the inscrutable decrees of the Father. Similarly the tragic process in Shakespeare is natural in the sense that it simply happens, whatever its cause, explanation, or relationships. Characters may grope about for conceptions of gods that kill us for their sport, or for a divinity that shapes our ends, but the action of tragedy will not abide our questions, a fact often transferred to the personality of Shakespeare.

法律（堤坝）的理念在其最基本的形式中体现为同态复仇法。英雄挑起仇恨，或继承遗产。仇恨的局面，以及复仇者的归来，构成了这场灾难。复仇悲剧是一种简单的悲剧结构，而如同大多数简单的结构一样，它却能产生强大的力量，即使在最复杂的悲剧中，也常常作为核心主题保留下来。在这里，引发复仇的最初行为开启了一个对立或平衡的进程，而这一进程的完成则解决了这场悲剧。这种情况如此常见，以至于我们几乎可以将整个悲剧神话描述为二元的，这与喜剧的三段式结构形成鲜明对比。

In its most elementary form, the vision of law (dike) operates as lex talionis or revenge. The hero provokes enmity, or inherits a situation of enmity, and the return of the avenger constitutes the catastrophe. The revenge-tragedy is a simple tragic structure, and like most simple structures can be a very powerful one, often retained as a central theme even in the most complex tragedies. Here the original act provoking the revenge sets up an antithetical or counterbalancing movement, and the completion of the movement resolves the tragedy. This happens so often that we may almost characterize the total mythos of tragedy as binary, in contrast to the three-part saturnalia movement of comedy.

然而，我们注意到，复仇往往来自另一个世界，通过神灵、鬼魂或神谕。这种手法拓展了自然和法则的概念，使其超越了显而易见和可触及的范畴。但它并未因此超越这些概念，因为悲剧行为所体现​​的仍然是自然法则。在这里，我们看到悲剧英雄扰乱了自然界的平衡，而自然被视为一种横跨可见与不可见两个领域的秩序，这种平衡迟早会自我恢复。希腊人将这种平衡的恢复称为复仇（nemesis）：复仇的媒介或工具可以是人类的复仇、鬼魂的复仇、神圣的复仇、神圣的正义、意外、命运或事件的逻辑，但关键在于复仇的发生，而且是客观的、不受任何个人因素影响的，正如俄狄浦斯王所展现的那样，它不受人类动机的道德属性的影响。在《奥瑞斯忒亚》中，我们从一系列复仇事件中逐渐走向对自然法的最终理解，这是一种包含道德律的普世契约，并得到了众神（以智慧女神的化身）的认可。在这里，复仇女神的复仇（nemesis）如同基督教中的摩西律法一样，并非被废除，而是得到了实现：它从复仇女神所代表的机械或任意的秩序重建，发展为雅典娜所阐释的理性秩序重建。雅典娜的出现并没有将《奥瑞斯忒亚》变成喜剧，而是阐明了其悲剧的本质。

We notice however the frequency of the device of making the revenge come from another world, through gods or ghosts or oracles. This device expands the conceptions of both nature and law beyond the limits of the obvious and tangible. It does not thereby transcend those conceptions, as it is still natural law that is manifested by the tragic action. Here we see the tragic hero as disturbing a balance in nature, nature being conceived as an order stretching over the two kingdoms of the visible and the invisible, a balance which sooner or later must right itself. The righting of the balance is what the Greeks called nemesis: again, the agent or instrument of nemesis may be human vengeance, ghostly vengeance, divine vengeance, divine justice, accident, fate or the logic of events, but the essential thing is that nemesis happens, and happens impersonally, unaffected, as Oedipus Tyrannus illustrates, by the moral quality of human motivation involved. In the Oresteia we are led from a series of revenge-movements into a final vision of natural law, a universal compact in which moral law is included and which the gods, in the person of the goddess of wisdom, endorse. Here nemesis, like its counterpart the Mosaic law in Christianity, is not abolished but fulfilled: it is developed from a mechanical or arbitrary sense of restored order, represented by the Furies, to the rational sense of it expounded by Athene. The appearance of Athene does not turn the Oresteia into a comedy, but clarifies its tragic vision.

有两种简化的公式常被用来解释悲剧。两者都不够完善，但都接近完美，而且由于它们相互矛盾，因此必然代表了对悲剧的极端或局限的观点。其中一种理论认为，所有悲剧都展现了外部命运的全能性。当然，绝大多数悲剧确实让我们感受到非人格力量的至高无上以及人类努力的局限性。但是，这种宿命论式的悲剧简化却混淆了……悲剧的境况与悲剧的过程：在悲剧中，命运通常只有在悲剧过程开始之后才会对主人公产生外在的影响。希腊神话中的命运女神（ananke或moira）在其正常或悲剧之前的形式中，是生命内在的平衡状态。只有当这种平衡状态遭到破坏之后，它才会以外在的或对立的必然性出现，正如正义是正直之人的内在状态，却是罪犯的外在对立面一样。荷马在谈到埃癸斯托斯时，借宙斯之口使用了一句意义深远的短语来阐释悲剧理论，称其“超越了命运”（hyper moron）。

There are two reductive formulas which have often been used to explain tragedy. Neither is quite good enough, but each is almost good enough, and as they are contradictory, they must represent extreme or limiting views of tragedy. One of these is the theory that all tragedy exhibits the omnipotence of an external fate. And, of course, the overwhelming majority of tragedies do leave us with a sense of the supremacy of impersonal power and of the limitation of human effort. But the fatalistic reduction of tragedy confuses the tragic condition with the tragic process: fate, in a tragedy, normally becomes external to the hero only after the tragic process has been set going. The Greek ananke or moira is in its normal, or pre-tragic, form the internal balancing condition of life. It appears as external or antithetical necessity only after it has been violated as a condition of life, just as justice is the internal condition of an honest man, but the external antagonist of the criminal. Homer uses a profoundly significant phrase for the theory of tragedy when he has Zeus speak of Aegisthus as going hyper moron, beyond fate.

对悲剧的宿命论式简化并不能区分悲剧与讽刺，而我们谈论的是命运的讽刺而非其悲剧性，这一点同样意义重大。讽刺并不需要一位非凡的中心人物：通常情况下，当讽刺本身成为目的时，英雄越是卑微，讽刺就越是尖锐。正是英雄主义的融入，赋予了悲剧独特的辉煌和振奋人心的力量。悲剧英雄通常拥有非凡的、近乎神圣的命运，几乎触手可及，而这种最初愿景的光辉在悲剧中从未完全消逝。悲剧的修辞需要最伟大的诗人所能创作的最崇高的语言，虽然灾难是悲剧的通常结局，但这与同样重要的最初伟大——失落的天堂——相平衡。

The fatalistic reduction of tragedy does not distinguish tragedy from irony, and it is again significant that we speak of the irony of fate rather than of its tragedy. Irony does not need an exceptional central figure: as a rule, the dingier the hero the sharper the irony, when irony alone is aimed at. It is the admixture of heroism that gives tragedy its characteristic splendor and exhilaration. The tragic hero has normally had an extraordinary, often a nearly divine, destiny almost within his grasp, and the glory of that original vision never quite fades out of tragedy. The rhetoric of tragedy requires the noblest diction that the greatest poets can produce, and while catastrophe is the normal end of tragedy, this is balanced by an equally significant original greatness, a paradise lost.

另一种还原论的悲剧理论认为，引发悲剧进程的行为必然是对道德法则的违背，无论这种法则是人间的还是神圣的；简而言之，亚里士多德所说的“缺陷”（hamartia）必然与罪恶或不当行为有着本质的联系。诚然，绝大多数悲剧英雄都具有傲慢（hybris），即骄傲、激情、执迷或狂妄的头脑，这种傲慢最终导致了道德上可以理解的堕落。这种傲慢通常是灾难的诱发因素，正如在喜剧中，圆满结局的原因通常是某种谦卑的行为，由奴隶或伪装卑微的女主角来代表一样。在亚里士多德看来，悲剧英雄的缺陷与他关于“追求目标”（proairesis）的伦理观念相关，即自由选择目标，而亚里士多德也确实倾向于认为悲剧在道德上，甚至在物理层面上，都是可以理解的。然而，已有观点指出，亚里士多德悲剧观的核心——净化（catharsis）概念——与对悲剧的道德解读并不相符。怜悯和恐惧是道德情感，它们与悲剧情境相关，但并非依附于悲剧情境。莎士比亚尤其喜欢在其笔下英雄的两侧设置道德上的“避雷针”，以转移人们的怜悯和恐惧：我们之前提到过《奥赛罗》。伊阿古和苔丝狄蒙娜簇拥着他，而哈姆雷特身边是克劳狄斯和奥菲莉娅，李尔王身边是他的女儿们，甚至麦克白身边也是麦克白夫人和邓肯。所有这些悲剧都蕴含着某种深远的神秘感，而这种道德上可以理解的过程仅仅是其中的一部分。英雄的行为启动了一台比他自身生命甚至他所处的社会更为庞大的机器。

The other reductive theory of tragedy is that the act which sets the tragic process going must be primarily a violation of moral law, whether human or divine; in short, that Aristotle’s hamartia or “flaw” must have an essential connection with sin or wrongdoing. Again it is true that the great majority of tragic heroes do possess hybris, a proud, passionate, obsessed or soaring mind which brings about a morally intelligible downfall. Such hybris is the normal precipitating agent of catastrophe, just as in comedy the cause of the happy ending is usually some act of humility, represented by a slave or by a heroine meanly disguised. In Aristotle the hamartia of the tragic hero is associated with Aristotle’s ethical conception of proairesis, or free choice of an end, and Aristotle certainly does tend to think of tragedy as morally, almost physically, intelligible. It has already been suggested, however, that the conception of catharsis, which is central to Aristotle’s view of tragedy, is inconsistent with moral reductions of it. Pity and terror are moral feelings, and they are relevant but not attached to the tragic situation. Shakespeare is particularly fond of planting moral lightning-rods on both sides of his heroes to deflect the pity and terror: we have mentioned Othello flanked by Iago and Desdemona, but Hamlet is flanked by Claudius and Ophelia, Lear by his daughters, and even Macbeth by Lady Macbeth and Duncan. In all these tragedies there is a sense of some far-reaching mystery of which this morally intelligible process is only a part. The hero’s act has thrown a switch in a larger machine than his own life, or even his own society.

所有关于悲剧在道德上可解释的理论，迟早都会遇到这样一个问题：悲剧中的无辜受难者（即诗意意义上的无辜者），比如伊菲革涅亚、科迪莉亚、柏拉图《申辩篇》中的苏格拉底、耶稣受难记中的基督，难道不是悲剧人物吗？试图为这些人物找出关键的道德缺陷并不令人信服。科迪莉亚拒绝奉承父亲，展现出一种高尚的精神，或许还带有一丝任性，结果却被绞死。席勒笔下的圣女贞德对一位英国士兵流露出了一丝柔情，结果被活活烧死——如果席勒没有为了维护其道德理论的面子而牺牲事实的话。在这里，我们似乎已经偏离了悲剧的范畴，而接近于一种近乎疯狂的警世寓言，就像皮普钦太太的小男孩因为问了些棘手的问题而被公牛顶死一样。简而言之，悲剧似乎摆脱了道德责任与任意命运的对立，就像它摆脱了善与恶的对立一样。

All theories of tragedy as morally explicable sooner or later run into the question: is an innocent sufferer in tragedy (i.e., poetically innocent), Iphigeneia, Cordelia, Socrates in Plato’s Apology, Christ in the Passion, not a tragic figure? It is not very convincing to try to provide crucial moral flaws for such characters. Cordelia shows a high spirit, perhaps a touch of wilfulness, in refusing to flatter her father, and Cordelia gets hanged. Joan of Arc in Schiller has a moment of tenderness for an English soldier, and Joan is burned alive, or would have been if Schiller had not decided to sacrifice the facts to save the face of his moral theory. Here we are getting away from tragedy, and close to a kind of insane cautionary tale, like Mrs. Pipchin’s little boy who was gored to death by a bull for asking inconvenient questions. Tragedy, in short, seems to elude the antithesis of moral responsibility and arbitrary fate, just as it eludes the antithesis of good and evil.

在《失乐园》第三卷中，弥尔顿笔下的上帝辩称，他创造人“足以站立，却也自由堕落”。上帝知道亚当会堕落，但并未强迫他堕落，并以此为由否认自己负有法律责任。这种论证如此站不住脚，以至于弥尔顿如果想要逃避反驳，将其归咎于上帝倒也无可厚非。思想与行为并非如此割裂：如果上帝拥有预知能力，那么他在创造亚当的那一刻就必然知道，他创造的是一个会堕落的生命。然而，这段文字却依然令人难以忘怀，发人深省。因为《失乐园》并非仅仅是一部悲剧的创作，而是对弥尔顿所认为的悲剧原型神话的阐释。因此，这段文字是存在主义投射的又一例证：弥尔顿笔下上帝与亚当关系的真正基础，正是悲剧诗人与其笔下英雄之间的关系。悲剧诗人深知其笔下的主人公将身陷悲剧，但他竭力避免给人以为自身目的操纵悲剧的印象。他向我们展现的主人公，如同上帝向天使展现亚当一般。如果主人公不足以屹立不倒，那么这种风格便是纯粹的反讽；如果他无法自由地走向毁灭，那么这种风格便是纯粹的浪漫。这是一个关于无敌英雄的故事，只要故事围绕他展开，他就能战胜所有对手。如今，大多数悲剧理论都以一部伟大的悲剧为标准：例如，亚里士多德的理论很大程度上建立在《俄狄浦斯王》之上，黑格尔的理论则建立在《安提戈涅》之上。弥尔顿在亚当的故事中看到了人类悲剧的原型，这当然与整个犹太-基督教文化传统相符。或许，从亚当的故事中引申出的论点在文学批评领域比在那些不得不假定亚当真实存在（无论是作为事实还是仅仅作为法律虚构）的领域更有说服力。乔叟笔下的僧侣显然明白自己在做什么，他从路西法和亚当的故事入手，我们或许应该效仿他的做法。

In the third book of Paradise Lost, Milton represents God as arguing that he made man “Sufficient to have stood, though free to fall.” God knew that Adam would fall, but did not compel him to do so, and on that basis he disclaims legal responsibility. This argument is so bad that Milton, if he was trying to escape refutation, did well to ascribe it to God. Thought and act cannot be so separated: if God had foreknowledge he must have known in the instant of creating Adam that he was creating a being who would fall. Yet the passage is a most haunting and suggestive one nonetheless. For Paradise Lost is not simply an attempt to write one more tragedy, but to expound what Milton believed to be the archetypal myth of tragedy. Hence the passage is another example of existential projection: the real basis of the relation of Milton’s God to Adam is the relation of the tragic poet to his hero. The tragic poet knows that his hero will be in a tragic situation, but he exerts all his power to avoid the sense of having manipulated that situation for his own purposes. He exhibits his hero to us as God exhibits Adam to the angels. If the hero was not sufficient to have stood, the mode is purely ironic; if he was not free to fall, the mode is purely romantic, the story of an invincible hero who will conquer all his antagonists as long as the story is about him. Now most theories of tragedy take one great tragedy as their norm: thus Aristotle’s theory is largely founded on Oedipus Tyrannus, and Hegel’s on Antigone. In seeing the archetypal human tragedy in the story of Adam, Milton was, of course, in agreement with the whole Judaeo-Christian cultural tradition, and perhaps arguments drawn from the story of Adam may have better luck in literary criticism than in subjects compelled to assume Adam’s real existence, either as fact or as a merely legal fiction. Chaucer’s monk, who clearly understood what he was doing, began with Lucifer and Adam, and we may be well advised to follow his example.

因此，亚当身处一个英雄般的境地：他站在命运之轮的顶端，几乎触手可及神明的命运。他放弃了这份命运，这在一些人看来是道德责任的体现，而在另一些人看来则是命运的阴谋。他所做的，是用无限的自由换取了交换行为所带来的后果，正如一个故意跳下悬崖的人，万有引力定律在他短暂的余生中扮演着命运的角色一样。弥尔顿将这种交换本身描绘成一种自由行为或“ proairesis”（放弃自由），即利用自由去失去自由。正如喜剧常常设定一条任意的法则，然后安排行动去打破或规避它一样，悲剧则呈现了相反的主题，将相对自由的生活限制在一个因果关系的过程中。麦克白接受了篡位的逻辑，哈姆雷特接受了复仇的逻辑，李尔王接受了退位的逻辑，这些都导致了同样的悲剧结局。悲剧结尾的顿悟或顿悟并非仅仅是主人公对自身遭遇的认知——《俄狄浦斯王》虽然被视为典型的悲剧，但在这方面却是一个特例——而是主人公认识到自己所创造的既定人生模式，并将其与他所放弃的未创造的潜在人生进行隐晦的对比。弥尔顿在描写魔鬼堕落时所作的诗句“啊，他们堕落的地方多么不同啊！”既呼应了维吉尔的“从天而降”（quantum mutatus ab illo），又呼应了以赛亚的“明亮之子，你何竟从天坠落”，它融合了古典悲剧和基督教悲剧的原型——因为撒旦当然也像亚当一样，拥有着最初的荣耀。在弥尔顿的画作中，亚当站在命运之轮上的景象与之相呼应。基督站在圣殿的顶端，被撒旦诱惑而坠入轮子的世界，却一动不动。

Adam, then, is in a heroic human situation: he is on top of the wheel of fortune, with the destiny of the gods almost within his reach. He forfeits that destiny in a way which suggests moral responsibility to some and a conspiracy of fate to others. What he does is to exchange a fortune of unlimited freedom for the fate involved in the consequences of the act of exchange, just as, for a man who deliberately jumps off a precipice, the law of gravitation acts as fate for the brief remainder of his life. The exchange is presented by Milton as itself a free act or proairesis, a use of freedom to lose freedom. And just as comedy often sets up an arbitrary law and then organizes the action to break or evade it, so tragedy presents the reverse theme of narrowing a comparatively free life into a process of causation. This happens to Macbeth when he accepts the logic of usurpation, to Hamlet when he accepts the logic of revenge, to Lear when he accepts the logic of abdication. The discovery or anagnorisis which comes at the end of the tragic plot is not simply the knowledge by the hero of what has happened to him —Oedipus Tyrannus, despite its reputation as a typical tragedy, is rather a special case in that regard—but the recognition of the determined shape of the life he has created for himself, with an implicit comparison with the uncreated potential life he has forsaken. The line of Milton dealing with the fall of the devils, “O how unlike the place from whence they fell!”, referring as it does both to Virgil’s quantum mutatus ab illo and Isaiah’s “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer son of the morning,” combines the Classical and the Christian archetypes of tragedy—for Satan, of course, like Adam, possessed an original glory. In Milton the complement to the vision of Adam on top of the wheel of fortune and falling into the world of the wheel is Christ standing on the pinnacle of the temple, urged by Satan to fall, and remaining motionless.

亚当堕落后，便进入了他自己创造的生命，这生命也正是我们所知的自然秩序。因此，亚当的悲剧，如同所有其他悲剧一样，最终都归结于自然法则的显现。他进入了一个存在本身即悲剧的世界，而非被某种行为——无论是有意的还是无意的——所改变的存在。仅仅存在本身就扰乱了自然的平衡。每一个自然人都是黑格尔式命题的体现，并蕴含着一种反作用：每一次新生都预示着复仇之死的到来。这一事实本身就充满讽刺意味，如今被称为“焦虑”（Angst），而当它与一种失去的、原本更高尚的命运感相结合时，便更添悲剧色彩。因此，亚里士多德所说的“过失”（hamartia）是存在的条件，而非生成的原因：弥尔顿之所以将他那可疑的论证归咎于上帝，是因为他急于将上帝从预定的因果序列中剔除。悲剧英雄的一侧是获得自由的机会，另一侧则是失去自由的必然结果。弥尔顿笔下拉斐尔和米迦勒的独白分别展现了亚当处境的这两种面向。即使是无辜的英雄或殉道者，也会面临同样的境况：在耶稣受难的故事中，基督在客西马尼园的祷告便体现了这一点。悲剧似乎会推进到某个关键时刻，从这个时刻，通往“可能”的道路和通往“将要”的道路可以同时被观众看到：如果英雄处于傲慢自大的状态，他就无法看到这一点，因为在这种情况下，关键时刻对他而言只是一阵眩晕，命运之轮开始其不可避免的下坠循环。

As soon as Adam falls, he enters his own created life, which is also the order of nature as we know it. The tragedy of Adam, therefore, resolves, like all other tragedies, in the manifestation of natural law. He enters a world in which existence is itself tragic, not existence modified by an act, deliberate or unconscious. Merely to exist is to disturb the balance of nature. Every natural man is a Hegelian thesis, and implies a reaction: every new birth provokes the return of an avenging death. This fact, in itself ironic and now called Angst, becomes tragic when a sense of a lost and originally higher destiny is added to it. Aristotle’s hamartia, then, is a condition of being, not a cause of becoming: the reason why Milton ascribes his dubious argument to God is that he is so anxious to remove God from a predetermined causal sequence. On one side of the tragic hero is an opportunity for freedom, on the other the inevitable consequence of losing that freedom. These two sides of Adam’s situation are represented in Milton by the speeches of Raphael and Michael respectively. Even with an innocent hero or martyr the same situation arises: in the Passion story it occurs in Christ’s prayer in Gethsemane. Tragedy seems to move up to an Augenblick or crucial moment from which point the road to what might have been and the road to what will be can be simultaneously seen. Seen by the audience, that is: it cannot be seen by the hero if he is in a state of hybris, for in that case the crucial moment is for him a moment of dizziness, when the wheel of fortune begins its inevitable cyclical movement downward.

在亚当的处境中，有一种感觉——这种感觉在基督教传统中至少可以追溯到圣奥古斯丁——即时间始于堕落；从自由堕入自然循环也开启了我们所知的时空流动。在其他悲剧中，我们也能感受到复仇女神与时间流动的紧密联系，无论是人类事务中潮汐的错失，还是对时间错位的认知，亦或是将时间视为生命的吞噬者、前一刻的地狱之口——潜能永远转化为现实——又或是，在最极致的恐怖中，麦克白将时间仅仅视为时钟滴答声的流逝。在喜剧中，时间扮演着救赎的角色：它揭示并照亮了幸福结局的关键所在。格林的《潘多斯托》 （ 《冬天的故事》的灵感来源）的副标题是“时间的胜利”，这恰如其分地描述了莎士比亚戏剧的本质——时间被塑造成一个合唱队。但在悲剧中，认知（cognitio）通常是对时间中因果序列必然性的认识，而围绕着它的不祥预感和讽刺意味则基于一种循环往复的观念。

In Adam’s situation there is a feeling, which in Christian tradition can be traced back at least to St. Augustine, that time begins with the fall; that the fall from liberty into the natural cycle also started the movement of time as we know it. In other tragedies too we can trace the feeling that nemesis is deeply involved with the movement of time, whether as the missing of a tide in the affairs of men, as a recognition that the time is out of joint, as a sense that time is the devourer of life, the mouth of hell at the previous moment, when the potential passes forever into the actual, or, in its ultimate horror, Macbeth’s sense of it as simply one clock-tick after another. In comedy time plays a redeeming role: it uncovers and brings to light what is essential to the happy ending. The subtitle of Greene’s Pandosto, the source of The Winter’s Tale, is “The Triumph of Time,” and it well describes the nature of Shakespeare’s action, where time is introduced as a chorus. But in tragedy the cognitio is normally the recognition of the inevitability of a causal sequence in time, and the forebodings and ironic anticipations surrounding it are based on a sense of cyclical return.

与悲剧不同，在反讽中，时间之轮完全包围着事件，使人感觉不到与相对永恒的世界有任何最初的联系。在《圣经》中，亚当的悲剧性堕落之后，紧接着是历史的重演——以色列人沦为埃及的奴役，这可以说是对亚当堕落的一种反讽式的印证。只要杰弗里·特洛伊的英国历史版本被人们接受，特洛伊的陷落就被视为英国历史上与之对应的事件。由于特洛伊的陷落始于对苹果的偶像崇拜式误用，两者之间甚至存在象征性的相似之处。莎士比亚最具反讽意味的剧作《特洛伊罗斯与克瑞西达》中，尤利西斯以世俗智慧的视角，雄辩地阐述了堕落世界中悲剧反讽视角的两大主要范畴：时间和等级森严的存在体系。尼采的《查拉图斯特拉如是说》对时间悲剧性的非凡处理，将英雄式的循环往复的接受转变为阴郁而又兴高采烈的对同一循环宇宙论的接受，标志着一个充满讽刺的时代的影响。

In irony, as distinct from tragedy, the wheel of time completely encloses the action, and there is no sense of an original contact with a relatively timeless world. In the Bible the tragic fall of Adam is followed by its historical repetition, the fall of Israel into Egyptian bondage, which is, so to speak, its ironic confirmation. As long as the Geoffrey version of British history was accepted, the fall of Troy was the corresponding event in the history of Britain, and, as the fall of Troy began with an idolatrous misapplication of an apple, there were even symbolic parallels. Shakespeare’s most ironic play, Troilus and Cressida, presents in Ulysses the voice of worldly wisdom, expounding with great eloquence the two primary categories of the perspective of tragic irony in the fallen world, time and the hierarchic chain of being. The extraordinary treatment of the tragic vision of time by Nietzsche’s Zarathustra, in which the heroic acceptance of cyclical return becomes a glumly cheerful acceptance of a cosmology of identical recurrence, marks the influence of an age of irony.

任何习惯于从原型角度思考文学的人都会在悲剧中看到对牺牲的模仿。悲剧是一种悖论式的结合：既有恐惧的正义感（英雄必须陨落），又有怜悯的错误感（他陨落实在太可惜了）。牺牲的两个要素也存在类似的悖论。其一是共融，即将英雄或神圣的身体分割给一群人，使他们与该身体融为一体，并成为该身体的一部分。其二是赎罪，即尽管存在共融，身体实际上仍然属于另一个更伟大、也可能充满愤怒的力量。与心理层面的相似之处相比，仪式层面的相似之处更为明显，因为代表噩梦或焦虑之梦的并非悲剧，而是反讽。但是，正如文学评论家认为弗洛伊德对喜剧理论最具启发性，荣格对浪漫主义理论最具启发性一样，对于悲剧理论，人们自然会转向阿德勒和尼采阐述的权力意志心理学。在这里，我们发现了一种“狄俄尼索斯式”的侵略性意志，它沉醉于自身全能的梦想，并冲击着一种“阿波罗式”的意志。一种外在的、不可动摇的秩序感。作为仪式的模仿，悲剧英雄并非真的被杀死或被吃掉，但艺术中相应的事件依然发生——一种死亡的景象将幸存者凝聚成一种新的统一体。作为梦境的模仿，这位深不可测的悲剧英雄，如同骄傲而沉默的天鹅，在死亡的瞬间变得清晰可闻，而观众，如同《忽必烈汗》中的诗人，在内心深处重新吟唱起他的歌谣。随着他的陨落，他那庞大灵魂所封闭的更广阔的世界瞬间显现，但同时也伴随着对那个世界的神秘和遥远的感受。

Anyone accustomed to think archetypally of literature will recognize in tragedy a mimesis of sacrifice. Tragedy is a paradoxical combination of a fearful sense of rightness (the hero must fall) and a pitying sense of wrongness (it is too bad that he falls). There is a similar paradox in the two elements of sacrifice. One of these is communion, the dividing of a heroic or divine body among a group which brings them into unity with, and as, that body. The other is propitiation, the sense that in spite of the communion the body really belongs to another, a greater, and a potentially wrathful power. The ritual analogies to tragedy are more obvious than the psychological ones, for it is irony, not tragedy, that represents the nightmare or anxiety-dream. But, just as the literary critic finds Freud most suggestive for the theory of comedy, and Jung for the theory of romance, so for the theory of tragedy one naturally looks to the psychology of the will to power, as expounded in Adler and Nietzsche. Here one finds a “Dionysiac” aggressive will, intoxicated by dreams of its own omnipotence, impinging upon an “Apollonian” sense of external and immovable order. As a mimesis of ritual, the tragic hero is not really killed or eaten, but the corresponding thing in art still takes place, a vision of death which draws the survivors into a new unity. As a mimesis of dream, the inscrutable tragic hero, like the proud and silent swan, becomes articulate at the point of death, and the audience, like the poet in Kubla Khan, revives his song within itself. With his fall, a greater world beyond which his gigantic spirit had blocked out becomes for an instant visible, but there is also a sense of the mystery and remoteness of that world.

如果我们关于浪漫、悲剧、讽刺和喜剧都是一个完整的探索神话的不同片段的观点是正确的，那么我们就能理解为什么喜剧本身也蕴含着潜在的悲剧。在神话中，英雄是神，因此他不会真正死去，而是经历死亡和复活。喜剧净化作用背后的仪式模式是死亡之后的复活，是复活英雄的顿悟或显现。在阿里斯托芬的作品中，英雄往往经历某种仪式性的死亡，之后被视为复活的神，被誉为新的宙斯，或被赋予奥林匹克冠军的准神荣誉。在新喜剧中，新的人类躯体既是英雄，也是一个社会群体。埃斯库罗斯三部曲则发展为喜剧萨提尔剧，据说这种剧与春季节日有着某种关联。基督教也将悲剧视为神圣喜剧中的一个插曲，是救赎与复活这一宏大计划的一部分。悲剧作为喜剧序曲的观念似乎与任何明确的基督教教义都密不可分。如果作曲家和听众不知道故事背后还有更深层的含义，那么《马太受难曲》结尾双合唱的宁静便难以达到。同样，如果参孙不是复活的基督的预表，并在恰当的时刻与凤凰相伴，那么参孙之死也不会带来“内心的平静，所有激情都已消散”。

If we are right in our suggestion that romance, tragedy, irony and comedy are all episodes in a total quest-myth, we can see how it is that comedy can contain a potential tragedy within itself. In myth, the hero is a god, and hence he does not die, but dies and rises again. The ritual pattern behind the catharsis of comedy is the resurrection that follows the death, the epiphany or manifestation of the risen hero. In Aristophanes the hero, who often goes through a point of ritual death, is treated as a risen god, hailed as a new Zeus, or given the quasi-divine honors of the Olympic victor. In New Comedy the new human body is both a hero and a social group. The Aeschylean trilogy proceeds to the comic satyr-play, which is said to have affinities with spring festivals. Christianity, too, sees tragedy as an episode in the divine comedy, the larger scheme of redemption and resurrection. The sense of tragedy as a prelude to comedy seems almost inseparable from anything explicitly Christian. The serenity of the final double chorus in the St. Matthew Passion would hardly be attainable if composer and audience did not know that there was more to the story. Nor would the death of Samson lead to “calm of mind, all passion spent,” if Samson were not a prototype of the rising Christ, associated at the appropriate moment with the phoenix.

这正是神话如何解释人们熟知的文学事实背后的结构原则的一个例子，在这个例子中，它解释了这样一个事实：让一个悲惨的事件以幸福的结局收尾很容易，而逆转这一过程却几乎不可能。（当然，我们天生不喜欢看到美好的事物最终走向灾难，但如果诗人创作时遵循的是坚实的结构基础，那么我们天生的喜好就无关紧要了。）即使是无所不能的莎士比亚，也从未真正做到这一点。《李尔王》的情节似乎正朝着某种平静的方向发展，却突然发生了悲剧性的转变。科迪莉亚被绞死，令莎士比亚陷入极度痛苦之中，这一结局在之后的一百多年里，舞台都拒绝将其搬上舞台。然而，莎士比亚的任何一部悲剧都不像是一部失败的喜剧—— 《罗密欧与朱丽叶》中或许隐约可见这种结构，但也仅仅只是暗示而已。因此，尽管悲剧中​​可能包含喜剧元素，但这些元素通常只是作为次要的对比或副线情节而穿插出现。

This is an example of the way in which myths explain the structural principles behind familiar literary facts, in this case the fact that to make a sombre action end happily is easy enough, and to reverse the procedure almost impossible. (Of course we have a natural dislike of seeing pleasant situations turn out disastrously, but if a poet is working on a solid structural basis, our natural likes and dislikes have nothing to do with the matter.) Even Shakespeare, who can do anything, never does quite this. The action of King Lear, which seems heading for some kind of serenity, is suddenly wrenched into agony by the hanging of Cordelia, providing a conclusion which the stage refused to act for over a century, but none of Shakespeare’s tragedies impresses us as a comedy gone wrong—Romeo and Juliet has a suggestion of such a structure, but it is only a suggestion. Hence while of course a tragedy may contain a comic action, it contains it only episodically as a subordinate contrast or underplot.

悲剧的人物塑造与喜剧的人物塑造非常相似，只是方向相反。复仇女神的源头，无论它是什么，都是一个“厄运”（eiron），它可以以各种各样的角色出现，从愤怒的神祇到虚伪的恶棍。在喜剧中，我们注意到三种主要的“厄运”角色：一位仁慈的、隐退后又回归的人物；狡猾的奴隶或恶习；以及英雄和女主角。在悲剧中，与隐退的“厄运”相对应的，是主宰悲剧事件的神祇，例如《阿贾克斯》中的雅典娜或《希波吕托斯》中的阿芙洛狄忒；基督教的例子是《失乐园》中的圣父。他也可以是一个鬼魂，例如哈姆雷特的父亲；或者他根本不是一个人，而是一种只能通过其影响来感知的无形力量，例如当帖木儿的死神悄然降临在他身上时。通常情况下，就像复仇悲剧一样，悲剧本身是某个行为发生之前的事件，而该行为本身则是该事件的结果。

The characterization of tragedy is very like that of comedy in reverse. The source of nemesis, whatever it is, is an eiron, and may appear in a great variety of agents, from wrathful gods to hypocritical villains. In comedy we noticed three main types of eiron characters: a benevolent withdrawing and returning figure, the tricky slave or vice, and the hero and heroine. We have the tragic counterpart to the withdrawn eiron in the god who decrees the tragic action, like Athene in Ajax or Aphrodite in Hippolytus; a Christian example is God the Father in Paradise Lost. He may also be a ghost, like Hamlet’s father; or it may not be a person at all but simply an invisible force known only by its effects, like the death that quietly seizes on Tamburlaine when the time has come for him to die. Often, as in the revenge-tragedy, it is an event previous to the action of which the tragedy itself is the consequence.

在预言家或先知身上，我们或许能找到与恶习或狡诈奴隶相对应的悲剧人物，他们预见了不可避免的结局，甚至比英雄预见得更透彻，例如忒瑞西阿斯。伊丽莎白时代戏剧中的马基雅维利式反派则更为贴切，他如同喜剧中的恶习一般，是推动剧情发展的便捷催化剂，因为他几乎不需要任何动机，本身就是邪恶的化身。与喜剧中的恶习一样，他也是作者意志的某种体现或投射，在这种情况下，是为了促成悲剧的结局。“我描绘了这幅夜曲，”韦伯斯特笔下的洛多维科说道，“这是我最好的作品。”伊阿古在《奥赛罗》中几乎主宰了剧情，堪称浪漫故事中黑国王或邪恶魔法师的悲剧对应人物。马基雅维利式的恶棍与魔鬼有着天然的相似之处，他或许像墨菲斯托费勒斯一样是真正的魔鬼，但作为灾难制造者所散发的可怕气息，也可能使他更像是祭祀仪式中的大祭司。韦伯斯特笔下的博索拉就带有这种特质。《李尔王》中的埃德蒙就是一个典型的马基雅维利式恶棍，而埃德蒙与埃德加形成了鲜明的对比。埃德加的种种行径令人眼花缭乱。他善于伪装，以不同的角色出现在盲人或疯子面前，并且总是在号角第三次响起时出现，像古代喜剧中的灾难一样突然降临，这似乎是一种新型的实验，一种悲剧性的“美德”（如果我可以用类比的方式创造这个词的话），在自然秩序中与守护天使或浪漫故事中类似的侍从相对应。

A tragic counterpart to the vice or tricky slave may be discerned in the soothsayer or prophet who foresees the inevitable end, or more of it than the hero does, like Teiresias. A closer example is the Machiavellian villain of Elizabethan drama, who, like the vice in comedy, is a convenient catalyzer of the action because he requires the minimum of motivation, being a self-starting principle of malevolence. Like the comic vice, too, he is something of an architectus or projection of the author’s will, in this case for a tragic conclusion. “I limned this night-piece,” says Webster’s Lodovico, “and it was my best.” Iago dominates the action of Othello almost to the point of being a tragic counterpart to the black king or evil magician of romance. The affinities of the Machiavellian villain with the diabolical are naturally close, and he may be an actual devil like Mephistopheles, but the sense of awfulness belonging to an agent of catastrophe can also make him something more like the high priest of a sacrifice. There is a touch of this in Webster’s Bosola. King Lear has a Machiavellian villain in Edmund, and Edmund is contrasted with Edgar. Edgar, with his bewildering variety of disguises, his appearance to blind or mad people in different roles, and his tendency to appear on the third sound of the trumpet and to come pat like the catastrophe of the old comedy, seems to be an experiment in a new type, a kind of tragic “virtue,” if I may coin this word by analogy, a counterpart in the order of nature to a guardian angel or similar attendant in romance.

悲剧英雄通常属于“阿勒宗”（alazon）一类，他们是冒名顶替者，因为他们自欺欺人或被傲慢蒙蔽了双眼。在许多悲剧中，他们最初都是半神般的人物——至少在他们自己眼中是如此——然后，一种无情的辩证法开始发挥作用，将神圣的伪装与人性的现实分离。“他们告诉我我无所不能，”李尔王说，“那是谎言；我并非百毒不侵。”悲剧英雄通常被赋予至高无上的权力，但他们的处境往往更为暧昧，如同暴君（ tyrannos ）一般，其统治依赖于自身的能力，而非像邓肯那样纯粹的世袭或法理上的君主（basileus）。后者更直接地象征着最初的愿景或与生俱来的权利，并且常常是某种程度上可悲的受害者，例如理查二世，甚至是阿伽门农。悲剧中的父母形象与其他所有形式的人物一样，都具有同样的矛盾性。

The tragic hero usually belongs of course to the alazon group, an impostor in the sense that he is self-deceived or made dizzy by hybris. In many tragedies he begins as a semi-divine figure, at least in his own eyes, and then an inexorable dialectic sets to work which separates the divine pretence from the human actuality. “They told me I was everything,” says Lear: “’tis a lie; I am not ague-proof.” The tragic hero is usually vested with supreme authority, but is often in the more ambiguous position of a tyrannos whose rule depends on his own abilities, rather than a purely hereditary or de jure monarch (basileus) like Duncan. The latter is more directly a symbol of the original vision or birthright, and is often a somewhat pathetic victim, like Richard II, or even Agamemnon. Parental figures in tragedy have the same ambivalence that they have in all other forms.

我们在喜剧中发现，“小丑”（ bomolochos ）一词并非仅限于闹剧，其含义可以扩展到主要以娱乐为目的的喜剧角色，其作用在于增强或强化喜剧氛围。悲剧中与之对应的角色类型是“求助者”，通常是女性，她们展现出一种彻底的无助和贫困。这样的人物形象令人怜悯，而悲情（pathos）虽然看似比悲剧更温和、更轻松，却也更加恐怖。悲情的基础是个人被群体排斥，因此它触及了我们内心深处最深层的恐惧——这种恐惧远比相对舒适、人际交往的地狱景象更加深刻。在“求助者”这一形象中，怜悯和恐惧被推向了极致，而拒绝“求助者”给所有相关人员带来的可怕后果，正是希腊悲剧的核心主题。“求助者”通常是面临死亡或强奸威胁的女性，或是像《约翰王》中的亚瑟王子那样的儿童。莎士比亚笔下奥菲莉娅的脆弱，体现了她与“乞求者”这一形象的相似之处。此外，乞求者往往处于一种结构性的悲剧境地，即失去了曾经的辉煌：这体现在《失乐园》第十卷中亚当和夏娃的处境，以及特洛伊妇女堕落后的境况。例如《特洛伊战争》中的俄狄浦斯，《科罗诺斯》中的俄狄浦斯，等等。在希腊悲剧中，信使通常扮演着烘托悲剧氛围的次要角色，他们负责宣告灾难的发生。而在喜剧的最后一幕，当作者试图让所有角色同时登场时，我们常常会注意到一个新角色的出现，他通常是一个带来缺失信息（cognitio）的信使，例如《皆大欢喜》中的雅克·德·博伊斯，或是《皆大欢喜》中温和的收敛者，后者代表着喜剧的对立面。

We found in comedy that the term bomolochos or buffoon need not be restricted to farce, but could be extended to cover comic characters who are primarily entertainers, with the function of increasing or focussing the comic mood. The corresponding contrasting type in tragedy is the suppliant, the character, often female, who presents a picture of unmitigated helplessness and destitution. Such a figure is pathetic, and pathos, though it seems a gentler and more relaxed mood than tragedy, is even more terrifying. Its basis is the exclusion of an individual from a group, hence it attacks the deepest fear in ourselves that we possess—a fear much deeper than the relatively cosy and sociable bogey of hell. In the figure of the suppliant pity and terror are brought to the highest possible pitch of intensity, and the awful consequences of rejecting the suppliant for all concerned is a central theme of Greek tragedy. Suppliant figures are often women threatened with death or rape, or children, like Prince Arthur in King John. The fragility of Shakespeare’s Ophelia marks an affinity with the suppliant type. Often, too, the suppliant is in the structurally tragic position of having lost a place of greatness: this is the position of Adam and Eve in the tenth book of Paradise Lost, of the Trojan women after the fall of Troy, of Oedipus in the Colonus play, and so on. A subordinate figure who plays the role of focussing the tragic mood is the messenger who regularly announces the catastrophe in Greek tragedy. In the final scene of comedy, when the author is usually trying to get all his characters on the stage at once, we often notice the introduction of a new character, generally a messenger bearing some missing piece of the cognitio, such as Jaques de Boys in As You Like It or the gentle astringer in All’s Well, who represents the comic counterpart.

最后，喜剧中拒绝欢庆的角色在悲剧中也有对应的反面，那就是悲剧中的“坦率之人”。这类人可能是英雄的忠实朋友，例如《哈姆雷特》中的霍拉旭，但通常也是悲剧进程的直言不讳的批评者，例如《李尔王》中的肯特或《安东尼与克莉奥佩特拉》中的埃诺巴布斯。这类角色处于拒绝，或者至少是抵制悲剧走向灾难的境地。《失乐园》中撒旦悲剧中的阿卜迪尔的角色与之类似。卡珊德拉和忒瑞西阿斯这两个我们熟知的角色则兼具预言家的双重身份。当这类角色出现在没有合唱队的悲剧中时，他们通常被称为“合唱队角色”，因为他们体现了悲剧合唱队的重要功能之一。在喜剧中，英雄周围会形成一个社会；而在悲剧中，合唱队，无论多么忠诚，通常代表的是英雄逐渐与之疏离的社会。因此，它所表达的是一种社会规范，英雄的傲慢自大便可以此为衡量标准。合唱队绝非英雄良心的代言人，但它也极少鼓励英雄的傲慢自大，或唆使他做出灾难性的举动。可以说，合唱队或合唱队角色是悲剧中喜剧元素的萌芽，正如拒绝参加宴会的忧郁的雅克或阿尔塞斯特是喜剧中悲剧元素的萌芽一样。

Finally, a tragic counterpart of the comic refuser of festivity may be discerned in a tragic type of plain dealer who may be simply the faithful friend of the hero, like Horatio in Hamlet, but is often an outspoken critic of the tragic action, like Kent in King Lear or Enobarbus in Antony and Cleopatra. Such a character is in the position of refusing, or at any rate resisting, the tragic movement toward catastrophe. Abdiel’s role in the tragedy of Satan in Paradise Lost is similar. The familiar figures of Cassandra and Teiresias combine this role with that of the soothsayer. Such figures, when they occur in a tragedy without a chorus, are often called chorus characters, as they illustrate one of the essential functions of the tragic chorus. In comedy a society forms around the hero: in tragedy the chorus, however faithful, usually represents the society from which the hero is gradually isolated. Hence what it expresses is a social norm against which the hero’s hybris may be measured. The chorus is not the voice of the hero’s conscience by any means, but very seldom does it encourage him in his hybris or prompt him to disastrous action. The chorus or chorus character is, so to speak, the embryonic germ of comedy in tragedy, just as the refuser of festivity, the melancholy Jaques or Alceste, is a tragic germ in comedy.

在喜剧中，主人公的情欲和社会情感在最后一幕中融合统一；而悲剧通常将爱情与社会结构描绘成不可调和的对立力量，这种冲突将爱情简化为激情，将社会活动简化为一种令人畏惧的强制性义务。喜剧更关注家庭的整合以及家庭与社会整体的融合；而悲剧则更关注家庭的瓦解以及家庭与社会其他部分的对抗。这便构成了安提戈涅的悲剧原型，古典法国戏剧中爱情与荣誉的冲突、席勒作品中“荣誉”（ Neigung）与“义务”（Pflicht）的冲突、以及激情与……的冲突，都体现了安提戈涅的悲剧本质。詹姆斯一世时期的权威，都是经过道德化简化的。正如喜剧中的女主角常常将剧情串联起来一样，悲剧中的核心女性人物也常常会使悲剧冲突走向极端。夏娃、海伦、格特鲁德以及《骑士的故事》中的艾米莉就是很好的例子；《伊利亚特》中布里塞伊斯所扮演的结构性角色也与之类似。喜剧会安排人物之间恰当的关系，避免英雄与自己的姐妹或母亲结婚；而悲剧则展现了俄狄浦斯的悲剧或齐格蒙德的乱伦。悲剧中有很多关于种族自豪感和出身的描写，但其总体趋势是将统治家族或贵族家族与社会其他阶层隔离开来。

In comedy the erotic and social affinities of the hero are combined and unified in the final scene; tragedy usually makes love and the social structure irreconcilable and contending forces, a conflict which reduces love to passion and social activity to a forbidding and imperative duty. Comedy is much concerned with integrating the family and adjusting the family to society as a whole; tragedy is much concerned with breaking up the family and opposing it to the rest of society. This gives us the tragic archetype of Antigone, of which the conflict of love and honor in Classical French drama, of Neigung and Pflicht in Schiller, of passion and authority in the Jacobeans, are all moralized simplifications. Again, just as the heroine of comedy often ties together the action, so it is obvious that the central female figure of a tragic action will often polarize the tragic conflict. Eve, Helen, Gertrude, and Emily in the Knight’s Tale are some ready instances: the structural role of Briseis in the Iliad is similar. Comedy works out the proper relations of its characters and prevents heroes from marrying their sisters or mothers; tragedy presents the disaster of Oedipus or the incest of Siegmund. There is a great deal in tragedy about pride of race and birthright, but its general tendency is to isolate a ruling or noble family from the rest of society.

悲剧的阶段从英雄阶段过渡到讽刺阶段，前三个阶段对应浪漫故事的前三个阶段，后三个阶段对应讽刺故事的最后三个阶段。悲剧的第一阶段，中心人物与其他人物形成鲜明对比，被赋予了最高的尊严，如同雄鹿被狼群围攻一般。尊严的来源是勇气和纯真，在这个阶段，英雄或女主角通常是纯真的。这一阶段与浪漫故事中英雄诞生的神话相对应，这一主题偶尔也会被融入悲剧结构中，例如拉辛的《阿塔莉娅》。但由于塑造一个引人入胜的戏剧角色异常困难，这一阶段的核心和典型人物是受诽谤的女性，通常是其子女合法性受到质疑的母亲。一系列以格里塞尔达形象为蓝本的悲剧都属于这一范畴，从塞内卡的《奥克塔维娅》到哈代的《苔丝》，甚至包括《冬天的故事》中赫敏的悲剧。如果我们要将《阿尔刻提斯》解读为一部悲剧，就必须将其视为这一阶段的悲剧：阿尔刻提斯先是被死神玷污，随后又因死而复活，从而证明了她的忠贞。《辛白林》也属于这一范畴：在这部剧中，英雄诞生的主题以隐晦的方式呈现，因为辛白林是基督诞生时的英国国王，而剧终时那宁静祥和的景象也暗含着对这段历史的隐喻。

The phases of tragedy move from the heroic to the ironic, the first three corresponding to the first three phases of romance, the last three to the last three of irony. The first phase of tragedy is the one in which the central character is given the greatest possible dignity in contrast to the other characters, so that we get the perspective of a stag pulled down by wolves. The sources of dignity are courage and innocence, and in this phase the hero or heroine usually is innocent. This phase corresponds to the myth of the birth of the hero in romance, a theme which is occasionally incorporated into a tragic structure, as in Racine’s Athalie. But owing to the unusual difficulty of making an interesting dramatic character out of an infant, the central and typical figure of this phase is the calumniated woman, often a mother the legitimacy of whose child is suspected. A whole series of tragedies based on a Griselda figure belong here, stretching from the Senecan Octavia to Hardy’s Tess, and including the tragedy of Hermione in The Winter’s Tale. If we are to read Alcestis as a tragedy, we have to see it as a tragedy of this phase in which Alcestis is violated by Death and then has her fidelity vindicated by being restored to life. Cymbeline belongs here too: in this play the theme of the birth of the hero appears offstage, for Cymbeline was the king of Britain at the time of the birth of Christ, and the halcyon peace in which the play concludes has a suppressed reference to this.

一个更清晰的例子，也是英国文学中最伟大的例子之一，是《马尔菲公爵夫人》。公爵夫人在一个病态而忧郁的社会中，拥有着充沛生命的纯真，而她“青春靓丽”的美貌恰恰是她遭人憎恨的原因。她也提醒我们，一个至关重要的特征是……殉道者身上的纯真体现在她不愿赴死。当博索拉前来谋害她时，他精心策划，试图让她半爱上安详的死亡，并暗示死亡实际上是一种解脱。这种尝试源于一种冷酷克制的怜悯，大致相当于耶稣受难剧中的醋海绵。当公爵夫人背靠着墙说“我依然是马尔菲公爵夫人”时，“依然”一词蕴含着“永远”的全部意义，我们由此明白，即使在她死后，她那无形的存在仍然是剧中最重要的人物。白魔鬼则是对同一阶段的讽刺性戏仿。

An even clearer example, and certainly one of the greatest in English literature, is The Duchess of Malfi. The Duchess has the innocence of abundant life in a sick and melancholy society, where the fact that she has “youth and a little beauty” is precisely why she is hated. She reminds us too that one of the essential characteristics of innocence in the martyr is an unwillingness to die. When Bosola comes to murder her he makes elaborate attempts to put her half in love with easeful death and to suggest that death is really a deliverance. The attempt is motivated by a grimly controlled pity, and is roughly the equivalent of the vinegar sponge in the Passion. When the Duchess, her back to the wall, says “I am the Duchess of Malfi still,” “still” having its full weight of “always,” we understand how it is that even after her death her invisible presence continues to be the most vital character in the play. The White Devil is an ironic parody-treatment of the same phase.

第二阶段对应于浪漫英雄的青年时期，在某种程度上是天真无邪的悲剧，指的是缺乏经验，通常涉及年轻人。它可能仅仅是青春逝去的悲剧，例如伊菲革涅亚和耶弗他的女儿、罗密欧与朱丽叶的故事；或者，在更复杂的情境中，希波吕托斯因理想主义和迂腐的迷茫交织而走向毁灭。萧伯纳笔下的琼的纯真和缺乏世故也使她处于这一阶段。然而，对我们而言，这一阶段主要由绿色和金色世界的原型悲剧所主导，即亚当和夏娃失去纯真。无论他们肩负着多么沉重的教义负担，他们始终在戏剧性地处于孩童的姿态，对初次接触成人世界感到困惑不已。在许多此类悲剧中，主人公最终幸存下来，故事以主人公适应新的、更成熟的经历而告终。“从此我明白，服从是最好的，”亚当说道，他和夏娃手牵手走向他们面前的世界。菲罗克忒忒斯（他的蛇伤让人想起亚当）被带离岛屿，参加特洛伊战争，结局虽不那么明确，但与之类似。易卜生的《小艾约尔夫》也是这一阶段的悲剧，结局同样延续，剧中年长的角色通过一个孩子的死亡而得到启迪。

The second phase corresponds to the youth of the romantic hero, and is in one way or another the tragedy of innocence in the sense of inexperience, usually involving young people. It may be simply the tragedy of a youthful life cut off, as in the stories of Iphigeneia and Jephthah’s daughter, of Romeo and Juliet, or, in a more complex situation, in the bewildered mixture of idealism and priggishness that brings Hippolytus to disaster. The simplicity of Shaw’s Joan and her lack of worldly wisdom place her here also. For us however the phase is dominated by the archetypal tragedy of the green and golden world, the loss of the innocence of Adam and Eve, who, no matter how heavy a doctrinal load they have to carry, will always remain dramatically in the position of children baffled by their first contact with an adult situation. In many tragedies of this type the central character survives, so that the action closes with some adjustment to a new and more mature experience. “Henceforth I learn that to obey is best,” says Adam, as he and Eve go hand in hand out to the world before them. A less clear cut but similar resolution occurs when Philoctetes, whose serpent-wound reminds us a little of Adam, is taken off his island to enter the Trojan war. Ibsen’s Little Eyolf is a tragedy of this phase, and with the same continuing conclusion, in which it is the older characters who are educated through the death of a child.

第三阶段对应于浪漫故事的核心探索主题，即悲剧，其中着重强调英雄成就的成功或圆满。耶稣受难记属于这一阶段，所有英雄与基督有任何关联或作为基督原型的悲剧，例如《力士参孙》，也属于这一阶段。悲剧中胜利的悖论可以通过情节的双重视角来表达。参孙在非利士人的狂欢节上是个丑角，同时在以色列人眼中又是一位悲剧英雄，但悲剧……以胜利告终，狂欢节却以灾难收场。受难中的基督也同样如此。但正如第二阶段往往以对更成熟人生的期盼告终一样，这一阶段也常常是先前悲剧或英雄行为的延续，并出现在英雄人生的终点。最伟大的戏剧范例之一是《俄狄浦斯在科罗诺斯》，其中我们看到了由先前悲剧行为引发的典型二元悲剧模式，而这一次的结局并非第二次灾难，而是一种超越对命运的顺从的、完整而丰富的宁静。在叙事文学中，我们可以引用贝奥武夫与巨龙的最后决战，这是他与格伦德尔战斗的呼应。莎士比亚的《亨利五世》是一部成功完成的浪漫冒险剧，但其隐含的背景却使其变得悲剧：人人都知道亨利国王几乎立刻就去世了，随后英格兰经历了六十年的连绵不断的灾难——至少，如果莎士比亚的观众中有人不知道这一点，那他的无知当然不是莎士比亚的错。

The third phase, corresponding to the central quest-theme of romance, is tragedy in which a strong emphasis is thrown on the success or completeness of the hero’s achievement. The Passion belongs here, as do all tragedies in which the hero is in any way related to or a prototype of Christ, like Samson Agonistes. The paradox of victory within tragedy may be expressed by a double perspective in the action. Samson is a buffoon of a Philistine carnival and simultaneously a tragic hero to the Israelites, but the tragedy ends in triumph and the carnival in catastrophe. Much the same is true of the mocked Christ in the Passion. But just as the second phase often ends in anticipation of greater maturity, so this one is often a sequel to a previous tragic or heroic action, and comes at the end of a heroic life. One of the greatest dramatic examples is Oedipus at Colonus, where we find the usual binary form of a tragedy conditioned by a previous tragic act, ending this time not in a second disaster, but in a full rich serenity that goes far beyond a mere resignation to Fate. In narrative literature we may cite Beowulf’s last fight with the dragon, the pendant to his Grendel quest. Shakespeare’s Henry V is a successfully completed romantic quest made tragic by its implicit context: everybody knows that King Henry died almost immediately and that sixty years of unbroken disaster followed for England—at least, if anyone in Shakespeare’s audience did not know that, his ignorance was certainly no fault of Shakespeare’s.

第四阶段是英雄因傲慢和过失而走向堕落的典型过程，我们之前已经讨论过。在这个阶段，我们跨越了从天真无邪到世故老练的界限，而这正是英雄堕落的方向。在第五阶段，讽刺意味增强，英雄气概减弱，人物的视野也变得更加狭隘和局限。《雅典的泰门》给我们的印象是比其他更广为人知的悲剧更具讽刺意味，英雄气概则有所减弱，这不仅仅是因为泰门是一个出身中产阶级的英雄，他所拥有的权力需要靠金钱来换取，更是因为泰门的自杀似乎未能完全展现出英雄气概，这种感觉非常强烈。泰门在最后的高潮中显得格外孤立，阿尔西比亚德斯与雅典人之间的裂痕在他头顶上彻底闭合，这与其他大多数悲剧的结局形成了鲜明的对比——在其他悲剧中，没有人能够抢走主角的风头。

The fourth phase is the typical fall of the hero through hybris and hamartia that we have already discussed. In this phase we cross the boundary line from innocence to experience, which is also the direction in which the hero falls. In the fifth phase the ironic element increases, the heroic decreases, and the characters look further away and in a smaller perspective. Timon of Athens impresses us as more ironic and less heroic than the better known tragedies, not simply because Timon is a more middle-class hero who has to buy what authority he has, but because the feeling that Timon’s suicide has somehow failed to make a fully heroic point is very strong. Timon is oddly isolated from the final action, in which the breach between Alcibiades and the Athenians closes up over his head, in striking contrast with the conclusions of most of the other tragedies, where nobody is allowed to steal the show from the central character.

悲剧的讽刺视角是通过将剧中人物置于比观众更低的自由状态来实现的。对于基督教观众而言，旧约或异教背景在此意义上具有讽刺意味，因为它展现了剧中人物按照某种法则（无论是犹太法则还是自然法则）行事，而观众至少在理论上已经摆脱了这种法则的束缚。《力士参孙》虽然在英语文学中独树一帜，但它融合了古典形式和希伯来题材，而当代最伟大的悲剧作家拉辛在其晚年创作的《阿塔莉娅》中也达到了同样的境界。以斯帖。同样，乔叟的《特洛伊罗斯》的尾声将宫廷爱情悲剧置于其与“古老仪式的代价”的历史关系之中。蒙茅斯的杰弗里所著的英国历史中的事件被认为与旧约圣经中的事件同时代，而《李尔王》中处处体现着律法之下的生活观念。同样的结构原则也解释了占星术和其他与命运之轮相关的宿命论机制的运用。罗密欧与朱丽叶注定悲剧收场，特洛伊罗斯失去克丽西达是因为每隔五百年，木星和土星就会在巨蟹座与新月相遇，夺走另一个受害者。第五阶段的悲剧行动主要展现了迷失方向和缺乏知识的悲剧，这与第二阶段颇为相似，只是背景设定在成人的世界。《俄狄浦斯王》属于此类，所有悲剧和悲剧情节都暗示了宿命论的存在主义投射，并且像《约伯记》中的许多章节一样，似乎提出了形而上学或神学问题，而不是社会或道德问题。

The ironic perspective in tragedy is attained by putting the characters in a state of lower freedom than the audience. For a Christian audience an Old Testament or pagan setting is ironic in this sense, as it shows its characters moving according to the conditions of a law, whether Jewish or natural, from which the audience has been, at least theoretically, redeemed. Samson Agonistes, though unique in English literature, presents a combination of Classical form and Hebrew subject-matter that the greatest contemporary tragedian, Racine, also reached at the end of his life in Athalie and Esther. Similarly the epilogue to Chaucer’s Troilus puts a Courtly Love tragedy into its historical relation to “payens corsed olde rites.” The events in Geoffrey of Monmouth’s British history are supposed to be contemporary with those of the Old Testament, and the sense of life under the law is present everywhere in King Lear. The same structural principle accounts for the use of astrology and other fatalistic machinery connected with the turning wheels of fate or fortune. Romeo and Juliet are star-crossed, and Troilus loses Criseyde because every five hundred years Jupiter and Saturn meet the crescent moon in Cancer and claim another victim. The tragic action of the fifth phase presents for the most part the tragedy of lost direction and lack of knowledge, not unlike the second phase except that the context is the world of adult experience. Oedipus Tyrannus belongs here, and all tragedies and tragic episodes which suggest the existential projection of fatalism, and, like much of the Book of Job, seem to raise metaphysical or theological questions rather than social or moral ones.

然而， 《俄狄浦斯王》已经进入悲剧的第六阶段，一个充满震惊和恐怖的世界，其核心意象是“残害”（sparagmos），即食人、肢解和酷刑。这种被称为“震惊”的特定反应，恰好与残酷或暴行的情境相符。（由暴行引发的、针对某种情感依恋或执念的次要或虚假的震惊，例如在对《无名的裘德》或《尤利西斯》的评论中，在批评界毫无地位，因为虚假的震惊是对文化自主性的伪装抵抗。）任何悲剧都可能包含一个或多个令人震惊的场景，但第六阶段的悲剧则以其整体效果带来震撼。这一阶段更常作为悲剧的次要方面，而非其主要主题，因为纯粹的恐惧或绝望会造成一种难以把握的节奏。《被缚的普罗米修斯》是这一阶段的悲剧，尽管这在某种程度上是一种错觉，因为它与所属的三部曲相隔甚远。在这样的悲剧中，主人公往往承受着巨大的痛苦或屈辱，以至于无法摆出英雄的姿态，因此通常更容易将他塑造成一个反派英雄，例如马洛笔下的巴拉巴斯，尽管《浮士德》也属于同一阶段。塞内卡钟爱这一阶段，并将对恐怖元素的兴趣传承给了伊丽莎白时代的作家，这种兴趣通常与肢体残害有关，例如费迪南德向马尔菲公爵夫人伸出手，却递给她一只死人的手。《泰特斯·安德洛尼克斯》是塞内卡第六阶段恐怖小说的一次实验，影片中充斥着大量的肢体残害，并且从开场就对悲剧的献祭象征意义表现出浓厚的兴趣。

Oedipus Tyrannus, however, is already moving into the sixth phase of tragedy, a world of shock and horror in which the central images are images of sparagmos, that is, cannibalism, mutilation, and torture. The specific reaction known as shock is appropriate to a situation of cruelty or outrage. (The secondary or false shock produced by the outrage done to some emotional attachment or fixation, as in the critical reception of Jude the Obscure or Ulysses, has no status in criticism, as false shock is a disguised resistance to the autonomy of culture.) Any tragedy may have one or more shocking scenes in it, but sixth-phase tragedy shocks as a whole, in its total effect. This phase is more common as a subordinate aspect of tragedy than as its main theme, as unqualified horror or despair makes a difficult cadence. Prometheus Bound is a tragedy of this phase, though this is partly an illusion due to its isolation from the trilogy to which it belongs. In such tragedies the hero is in too great agony or humiliation to gain the privilege of a heroic pose, hence it is usually easier to make him a villainous hero, like Marlowe’s Barabas, although Faustus also belongs to the same phase. Seneca is fond of this phase, and bequeathed to the Elizabethans an interest in the gruesome, an effect which usually has some connection with mutilation, as when Ferdinand offers to shake hands with the Duchess of Malfi and gives her a dead man’s hand. Titus Andronicus is an experiment in Senecan sixth-phase horror which makes a great deal of mutilation, and shows also a strong interest, from the opening scene on, in the sacrificial symbolism of tragedy.

在这一阶段的尾声，我们抵达了恶魔显现的境界，在那里，我们看到或瞥见了那未曾移位的恶魔景象——地狱的景象。除了监狱和疯人院之外，其主要象征便是酷刑致死的工具，日落下的十字架与月光下的高塔形成鲜明对比。公开惩罚和类似的暴民娱乐中蕴含着强烈的恶魔仪式元素，这被悲剧和讽刺的神话所利用。车轮碾碎成了李尔王的火轮；斗熊象征着格洛斯特和麦克白；而对于被钉在十字架上的普罗米修斯来说，暴露的羞辱，被注视的恐惧，比痛苦本身更加难以忍受。“Derkou theama”（看啊，这景象！快点结束你的凝视吧！）是他最痛苦的呐喊。弥尔顿笔下失明的参孙无法直视他人，这是他最大的痛苦，也正是这种痛苦迫使他在所有悲剧中最可怕的段落之一中，对着黛利拉大喊，如果她碰他，他就要把她撕成碎片。

At the end of this phase we reach a point of demonic epiphany, where we see or glimpse the undisplaced demonic vision, the vision of the Inferno. Its chief symbols, besides the prison and the madhouse, are the instruments of a torturing death, the cross under the sunset being the antithesis of the tower under the moon. A strong element of demonic ritual in public punishments and similar mob amusements is exploited by tragic and ironic myth. Breaking on the wheel becomes Lear’s wheel of fire; bear-baiting is an image for Gloucester and Macbeth, and for the crucified Prometheus the humiliation of exposure, the horror of being watched, is a greater misery than the pain. Derkou theama (behold the spectacle; get your staring over with) is his bitterest cry. The inability of Milton’s blind Samson to stare back is his greatest torment, and one which forces him to scream at Delilah, in one of the most terrible passages of all tragic drama, that he will tear her to pieces if she touches him.

冬日神话：反讽与讽刺

THE MYTHOS OF WINTER: IRONY AND SATIRE

现在我们来探讨经验的神话模式，即试图为非理想化存在中变幻莫测的模糊性和复杂性赋予形式的尝试。我们不能仅仅在文学作品的模仿或再现层面找到这些模式，因为那层面关乎内容而非形式。作为一种结构，反讽神话的核心原则最好被理解为对浪漫故事的戏仿：将浪漫的神话形式应用于更为现实的内容，并以出人意料的方式与之契合。唐吉诃德抗议道，在浪漫故事中，从来没有人会问谁来支付主人公的住宿费用。

We come now to the mythical patterns of experience, the attempts to give form to the shifting ambiguities and complexities of unidealized existence. We cannot find these patterns merely in the mimetic or representational aspect of such literature, for that aspect is one of content and not form. As structure, the central principle of ironic myth is best approached as a parody of romance: the application of romantic mythical forms to a more realistic content which fits them in unexpected ways. No one in a romance, Don Quixote protests, ever asks who pays for the hero’s accommodation.

讽刺与反讽的主要区别在于，讽刺是一种激进的反讽：它的道德规范相对清晰，并设定了衡量怪诞和荒谬的标准。纯粹的谩骂或人身攻击（“唇枪舌战”）是一种讽刺，其中反讽成分相对较少；另一方面，当读者不确定作者的态度或自己的立场时，我们便会看到反讽成分相对较少的作品。菲尔丁的《乔纳森·怀尔德》就是讽刺性的反讽：叙述者做出的某些直白的道德判断（例如第十二章中对巴格肖特的描述）符合作品的格调，但在其他作品中则显得格格不入。例如，《包法利夫人》。反讽既符合内容的完全现实主义，也符合作者对自身态度的克制。讽刺至少需要一些象征性的幻想，一些读者能识别为怪诞的内容，以及至少一种隐含的道德标准，后者对于一种激进的经验态度至关重要。有些现象，例如疾病的肆虐，或许可以称之为怪诞，但嘲笑它们并非有效的讽刺。讽刺作家必须选择他所关注的荒谬之处，而选择本身就是一种道德行为。

The chief distinction between irony and satire is that satire is militant irony: its moral norms are relatively clear, and it assumes standards against which the grotesque and absurd are measured. Sheer invective or name-calling (“flyting”) is satire in which there is relatively little irony: on the other hand, whenever a reader is not sure what the author’s attitude is or what his own is supposed to be, we have irony with relatively little satire. Fielding’s Jonathan Wild is satiric irony: certain flat moral judgements made by the narrator (as in the description of Bagshot in chapter twelve) are in accord with the decorum of the work, but would be out of key in, say, Madame Bovary. Irony is consistent both with complete realism of content and with the suppression of attitude on the part of the author. Satire demands at least a token fantasy, a content which the reader recognizes as grotesque, and at least an implicit moral standard, the latter being essential in a militant attitude to experience. Some phenomena, such as the ravages of disease, may be called grotesque, but to make fun of them would not be very effective satire. The satirist has to select his absurdities, and the act of selection is a moral act.

斯威夫特的《一个温和的建议》的论证有一种令人信服的合理性：人们几乎会觉得叙述者不仅通情达理，甚至还颇具人性；然而，任何一个理智的人都无法摆脱这种“几乎”的感觉，只要这种感觉存在，这个温和的建议就既荒谬又不道德。在另一段文字中，斯威夫特在讨论爱尔兰的贫困时突然说道：“但我的心太沉重了，无法再继续这种讽刺了”，他指的是讽刺，当其内容过于压抑地真实，以至于无法维持奇幻或假设的语调时，讽刺就会失效。因此，讽刺是一种在结构上接近喜剧的反讽：两个社会——一个正常，一个荒诞——之间的喜剧性冲突体现在其道德与幻想的双重关注点上。缺乏讽刺的反讽是悲剧中非英雄式的残余，其主题是困惑的失败。

The argument of Swift’s Modest Proposal has a brain-softening plausibility about it: one is almost led to feel that the narrator is not only reasonable but even humane; yet the “almost” can never drop out of any sane man’s reaction, and as long as it remains there the modest proposal will be both fantastic and immoral. When in another passage Swift suddenly says, discussing the poverty of Ireland, “But my Heart is too heavy to continue this Irony longer,” he is speaking of satire, which breaks down when its content is too oppressively real to permit the maintaining of the fantastic or hypothetical tone. Hence satire is irony which is structurally close to the comic: the comic struggle of two societies, one normal and the other absurd, is reflected in its double focus of morality and fantasy. Irony with little satire is the non-heroic residue of tragedy, centering on a theme of puzzled defeat.

因此，讽刺的要素有二：一是基于幻想或怪诞荒诞感的机智或幽默，二是攻击对象。缺乏幽默的攻击，或纯粹的谴责，构成了讽刺的界限之一。这条界限非常模糊，因为谩骂是文学艺术中最易读的形式之一，正如颂词是最枯燥乏味的形式之一。文学界早已形成一条公认的规律：我们喜欢听人被咒骂，对人被赞美感到厌倦；几乎任何谴责，只要足够有力，都会让读者感到愉悦，并很快露出微笑。要攻击任何事物，作者和读者都必须认同其令人反感之处，这意味着大量基于民族仇恨、势利眼、偏见和个人怨恨的讽刺作品很快就会过时。

Two things, then, are essential to satire; one is wit or humor founded on fantasy or a sense of the grotesque or absurd, the other is an object of attack. Attack without humor, or pure denunciation, forms one of the boundaries of satire. It is a very hazy boundary, because invective is one of the most readable forms of literary art, just as panegyric is one of the dullest. It is an established datum of literature that we like hearing people cursed and are bored with hearing them praised, and almost any denunciation, if vigorous enough, is followed by a reader with the kind of pleasure that soon breaks into a smile. To attack anything, writer and audience must agree on its undesirability, which means that the content of a great deal of satire founded on national hatreds, snobbery, prejudice, and personal pique goes out of date very quickly.

但文学作品中的攻击永远不可能仅仅是个人仇恨，甚至社会仇恨的纯粹表达，无论其动机如何，因为表达仇恨（区别于敌意）的词汇范围太窄。我们所能使用的词汇几乎只有……讽刺源于动物世界，但称人为猪、臭鼬或称女人为母狗所带来的快感却十分有限，因为动物身上大多数令人不快的特质都是人类的投射。正如莎士比亚笔下的忒耳西忒斯评价墨涅拉俄斯时所说：“他本该如此，何况是那掺杂着恶意的智慧，以及那掺杂着智慧的恶意呢？对他而言，他算什么？他既像驴又像牛；对他而言，他算什么？他既像牛又像驴。” 要想有效攻击，我们必须达到某种非个人化的层面，而这便意味着攻击者，即便只是间接地，也必须遵循某种道德标准。讽刺作家通常秉持着较高的道德立场。蒲柏声称自己“只对美德及其朋友为友”，这表明，当他思考那位抛弃他的女士内衣是否干净时，他的真实想法正是如此。

But attack in literature can never be a pure expression of merely personal or even social hatred, whatever the motivation for it may be, because the words for expressing hatred, as distinct from enmity, have too limited a range. About the only ones we have are derived from the animal world, but calling a man a swine or a skunk or a woman a bitch affords a severely restricted satisfaction, as most of the unpleasant qualities of the animal are human projections. As Shakespeare’s Thersites says of Menelaus, “to what form, but that he is, should wit larded with malice, and malice forced with wit, turn him to? To an ass, were nothing; he is both ass and ox; to an ox, were nothing; he is both ox and ass.” For effective attack we must reach some kind of impersonal level, and that commits the attacker, if only by implication, to a moral standard. The satirist commonly takes a high moral line. Pope asserts that he is “To Virtue only and her friends a friend,” suggesting that that is what he is really being when he is reflecting on the cleanliness of the underwear worn by the lady who had jilted him.

幽默，如同攻击，都建立在约定俗成的基础上。幽默的世界是一个僵化的程式化世界，慷慨的苏格兰人、顺从的妻子、慈祥的岳母以及思维敏捷的教授都不被允许存在。所有幽默都要求人们认同某些事物，例如漫画中妻子殴打丈夫的画面，是符合约定俗成的笑料。如果引入一幅丈夫殴打妻子的漫画，读者会感到不适，因为这意味着要学习一种新的约定俗成。纯粹幻想的幽默，是讽刺的另一边界，属于浪漫主义范畴，尽管它在那里显得有些格格不入，因为幽默感知的是不协调之处，而浪漫主义的约定俗成又是理想化的。大多数幻想作品最终都会被一股强大的暗流拉回讽刺的范畴，这股暗流通常被称为寓言，可以被描述为在感知不协调之处时对经验的隐喻。《爱丽丝梦游仙境》中的白骑士认为人应该事事周全，因此给马的脚踝戴上脚镣以防鲨鱼咬伤，这或许可以被归类为纯粹的幻想。但当他继续演唱一首精心模仿华兹华斯的歌曲时，我们开始嗅到辛辣的讽刺气息；当我们再次审视白骑士时，我们意识到他是一个与堂吉诃德和喜剧学究都密切相关的角色类型。

Humor, like attack, is founded on convention. The world of humor is a rigidly stylized world in which generous Scotchmen, obedient wives, beloved mothers-in-law, and professors with presence of mind are not permitted to exist. All humor demands agreement that certain things, such as a picture of a wife beating her husband in a comic strip, are conventionally funny. To introduce a comic strip in which a husband beats his wife would distress the reader, because it would mean learning a new convention. The humor of pure fantasy, the other boundary of satire, belongs to romance, though it is uneasy there, as humor perceives the incongruous, and the conventions of romance are idealized. Most fantasy is pulled back into satire by a powerful undertow often called allegory, which may be described as the implicit reference to experience in the perception of the incongruous. The White Knight in Alice who felt that one should be provided for everything, and therefore put anklets around his horse’s feet to guard against the bites of sharks, may pass as pure fantasy. But when he goes on to sing an elaborate parody of Wordsworth we begin to sniff the acrid, pungent smell of satire, and when we take a second look at the White Knight we recognize a character type closely related both to Quixote and to the pedant of comedy.

鉴于此神话体系中存在两个词的难题，如果读者已经熟悉我们提出的六个阶段的顺序，那么最简单的办法或许是按顺序描述这些阶段，而不是先抽象出一个典型形式进行讨论。前三个阶段是讽刺的阶段，与喜剧的前三个阶段（即反讽阶段）相对应。

As in this mythos we have the difficulty of two words to contend with, it may be simplest, if the reader is now accustomed to our sequence of six phases, to start with them and describe them in order, instead of abstracting a typical form and discussing it first. The first three are phases of satire, and correspond to the first three or ironic phases of comedy.

第一阶段对应于讽刺喜剧的第一阶段，在这个阶段中，幽默的社会结构并未发生位移。这种喜剧的荒诞感，如同反噬或回溯一般，在作品观看或阅读之后才显现。一旦我们读完，虚无的荒漠便在我们眼前展开，尽管作品充满幽默，我们却感到一种噩梦般的恐惧，仿佛与某种恶魔近在咫尺。即使在非常轻松的喜剧中，我们也能感受到这种感觉的痕迹：如果《傲慢与偏见》的主题是柯林斯和夏洛特·卢卡斯的婚姻生活，人们不禁会想，柯林斯还能保持多久的幽默感。因此，即使是像蒲柏关于女性性格的第二篇道德论著这样基调轻松的讽刺作品，最终达到道德高度的恐怖高潮，也是合情合理的。

The first phase corresponds to the first phase of ironic comedy in which there is no displacement of the humorous society. The sense of absurdity about such a comedy arises as a kind of backfire or recall after the work has been seen or read. Once we have finished with it, deserts of futility open up on all sides, and we have, in spite of the humor, a sense of nightmare and a close proximity to something demonic. Even in very light-hearted comedy we may get a trace of this feeling: if the main theme of Pride and Prejudice had been the married life of Collins and Charlotte Lucas, one wonders how long Collins would continue to be funny. Hence it is in decorum for even a satire prevailingly light in tone, such as Pope’s second Moral Essay on the characters of women, to rise to a terrifying climax of moral intensity.

这一阶段的典型讽刺可称为低级规范的讽刺。它假定世界充满反常、不公、愚昧和罪恶，却又永恒不变。其原则是，任何想要在这样的世界中保持平衡的人，首先必须学会睁大眼睛，闭上嘴巴。自古埃及时代起，劝诫读者采取“铁人”角色的审慎之言在文学中就十分盛行。它所推崇的是传统生活的最佳状态：对自身和他人的人性有敏锐的洞察力，避免一切幻想和强迫行为，依靠观察和时机而非攻击性。这就是智慧，是经过实践检验的生活方式，它不质疑社会习俗的逻辑，而只是遵循那些确实有助于人们日复一日保持平衡的程序。低级规范的“铁人”采取了一种灵活的实用主义态度；他认为，如果社会有机会，其行为或多或少会像勃朗宁诗中卡利班的塞特博斯那样，因此他的行为也遵循这一原则。在所有有争议的行为准则上，他最坚定的信念就是墨守成规。然而，无论人们如何看待精通礼仪的循规蹈矩的行为，它无疑是所有行为形式中最难讽刺的，正如任何拥有全新行为理论的人，即便他是圣人或先知，也最容易被嘲笑为怪人一样。

The satire typical of this phase may be called the satire of the low norm. It takes for granted a world which is full of anomalies, injustices, follies, and crimes, and yet is permanent and undisplaceable. Its principle is that anyone who wishes to keep his balance in such a world must learn first of all to keep his eyes open and his mouth shut. Counsels of prudence, urging the reader in effect to adopt an eiron role, have been prominent in literature from Egyptian times. What is recommended is conventional life at its best: a clairvoyant knowledge of human nature in oneself and others, an avoidance of all illusion and compulsive behavior, a reliance on observation and timing rather than on aggressiveness. This is wisdom, the tried and tested way of life, which does not question the logic of social convention, but merely follows the procedures which in fact do serve to maintain one’s balance from one day to the next. The eiron of the low norm takes an attitude of flexible pragmatism; he assumes that society will, if given any chance, behave more or less like Caliban’s Setebos in Browning’s poem, and he conducts himself accordingly. On all doubtful points of behavior convention is his deepest conviction. And however good or bad expertly conventional behavior may be thought to be, it is certainly the most difficult of all forms of behavior to satirize, just as anyone with a new theory of behavior, even if saint or prophet, is the easiest of all people to ridicule as a crank.

因此，讽刺作家可能会塑造一个朴实、务实、循规蹈矩的人物形象，以此来衬托社会上的各种丑恶现象。这样的人物可以是作者本人，也可以是叙述者，他相当于喜剧中的直言不讳的商贩或悲剧中的直率顾问。与作者不同，他通常被描绘成一个带有田园牧歌色彩的乡巴佬，这体现了他与喜剧中“乡巴佬”（agroikos）角色的联系。以《比格洛文集》（Biglow Papers）、《杜利先生》（Mr. Dooley）、《阿特姆斯·沃德》（Artemus Ward）和《威尔·罗杰斯》（Will Rogers）为代表的那种被视为民间幽默的美国讽刺作品，大量运用了这种形象。而这种体裁与北美地区《穷理查年鉴》（Poor Richard's Almanac）和《萨姆·斯利克文集》（Sam Slick papers）中“审慎之言”的兴起密切相关。其他例子也很容易找到，既有我们预料之中的，例如克拉布（Crabbe）的《赞助人》（​​The Patron） ，它也属于“审慎之言”的范畴；也有我们意想不到的，例如伊拉斯谟（Erasmus）《对话录》（Colloquies）中的“食鱼者”（Fish-Eater）对话。乔叟将自己描绘成朝圣队伍中一位腼腆、谦逊、不起眼的成员，礼貌地附和每个人（“我也说他的意见不错”），丝毫没有向朝圣者们展现出他向读者们所展现的敏锐洞察力。因此，我们并不惊讶地发现，他“自己”创作的故事之一竟然属于审慎劝诫的传统范畴。

Hence the satirist may employ a plain, common-sense, conventional person as a foil for the various alazons of society. Such a person may be the author himself or a narrator, and he corresponds to the plain dealer in comedy or the blunt adviser in tragedy. When distinguished from the author, he is often a rustic with pastoral affinities, illustrating the connection of his role with the agroikos type in comedy. The kind of American satire that passes as folk humor, exemplified by the Biglow Papers, Mr. Dooley, Artemus Ward, and Will Rogers, makes a good deal of him, and this genre is closely linked with the North American development of the counsel of prudence in Poor Richard’s Almanac and the Sam Slick papers. Other examples are easy enough to find, both where we expect them, as in Crabbe, whose tale The Patron also belongs to the counsel-of-prudence genre, and where we might not expect them, as in the Fish-Eater dialogue in Erasmus’s Colloquies. Chaucer represents himself as a shy, demure, inconspicuous member of his pilgrimage, agreeing politely with everybody (“And I seyde his opinion was good”), and showing to the pilgrims none of the powers of observation that he displays to his reader.
