We are not surprised therefore to find that one of his “own” tales is in the counsel of prudence tradition.

低俗讽刺最精妙的形式是中世纪盛行的百科全书式，这种形式与布道密切相关，通常以七宗罪的百科全书式体系为基础。这种形式一直延续到伊丽莎白时代，例如纳什的《皮尔斯·皮尼莱斯》和洛奇的《W ·伊斯泰尔塞》。伊拉斯谟的《愚人颂》也属于这一传统，其中与相应的喜剧阶段——一个由体液和主导性激情支配的颠倒世界——的联系清晰可见。当布道者甚至知识分子采用低俗讽刺手法时，它就隐含了一种“当然”的论证：如果人们连基本的常识或教堂门廊上的美德都达不到，那么将他们与任何更高的标准进行比较就毫无意义。

The most elaborate form of low-norm satire is the encyclopaedic form favored by the Middle Ages, closely allied to preaching, and generally based on the encyclopaedic scheme of the seven deadly sins, a form which survived as late as Elizabethan times in Nashe’s Pierce Penilesse and Lodge’s Wits Miserie. Erasmus’s Praise of Folly belongs to this tradition, in which the link with the corresponding comic phase, the view of an upside-down world dominated by humors and ruling passions, can be clearly seen. When adopted by a preacher, or even an intellectual, the low norm device is part of an implied a fortiori argument: if people cannot reach even ordinary common sense, or church porch virtue, there is little point in comparing them with any higher standards.

在以欢乐为主导的讽刺作品中，我们看到的是一种从根本上接受社会习俗，但强调在习俗范围内保持宽容和灵活的态度。在接近传统规范的作品中，我们发现了可爱的怪人，比如托比叔叔或贝齐·特罗伍德，他们以不挑战既定行为准则的方式丰富了这些行为。这类人物身上带着许多孩子气，而孩子的行为通常被认为是趋向于既定标准，而不是背离它。在以攻击为主导的作品中，我们看到的是一种不引人注目、不张扬的“铁标准” ，它与掌控社会的“阿勒松”或“阻挠者”形成鲜明对比。这种情况的典型代表是一种讽刺。这与浪漫故事中“以弱胜强”的主题遥相呼应。社会的存续离不开对教会、军队、各行各业以及政府等组织团体的声望和影响力的委托，而这些团体中的个体又因其所属机构而获得超越个人的权力。如果一位讽刺作家将一位神职人员描绘成傻瓜或伪君子，那么作为讽刺作家，他攻击的既不是个人，也不是教会。前者缺乏文学或假设意义，而后者则超出了讽刺的范畴。他攻击的是一个受教会庇护的恶人，这样的人简直就是一个巨大的怪物：他之所以可怕，是因为他违背了应有的品行；他之所以巨大，是因为他的地位以及正直神职人员的声望都保护了他。如果不是因为讽刺，僧袍或许真的能造就一个僧侣。

Where gaiety predominates in such satire, we have an attitude which fundamentally accepts social conventions but stresses tolerance and flexibility within their limits. Close to the conventional norm we find the lovable eccentric, the Uncle Toby or Betsey Trotwood who diversifies, without challenging, accepted codes of behavior. Such characters have much of the child about them, and a child’s behavior is usually thought of as coming towards an accepted standard instead of moving away from it. Where attack predominates, we have an inconspicuous, unobtrusive eiron standard contrasted with the alazons or blocking humors who are in charge of society. This situation has for its archetype an ironic counterpart of the romance theme of giant-killing. For society to exist at all there must be a delegation of prestige and influence to organized groups such as the church, the army, the professions and the government, all of which consist of individuals given more than individual power by the institutions to which they belong. If a satirist presents, say, a clergyman as a fool or hypocrite, he is, qua satirist, attacking neither a man nor a church. The former has no literary or hypothetical point, and the latter carries him outside the range of satire. He is attacking an evil man protected by his church, and such a man is a gigantic monster: monstrous because not what he should be, gigantic because protected by his position and by the prestige of good clergymen. The cowl might make the monk if it were not for satire.

弥尔顿说：“萨提尔（讽刺剧演员）既然诞生于悲剧，就应该像它的出身一样，敢于直击要害，大胆地讽刺最伟大的人物身上最显著的恶习。”撇开词源不谈，这需要补充一点：严重的恶习并不一定需要伟大的人物来代表。我们曾在《炼金术士》中提到过伊壁鸠鲁·玛门的梦境规模巨大：堕落的人类意志的全部奥秘都蕴藏其中，然而做梦者的彻底无能为力才是讽刺的精髓。同样，如果我们不认真地将主人公乔纳森·怀尔德视为对伟大或虚假社会价值标准的讽刺，我们就无法理解他的许多意义。但总的来说，对于讽刺剧的反面人物而言，我们可以接受这样的原则：他们越强大，就越容易失败。在低俗讽刺作品中，阿勒宗就像巨人歌利亚遇到身材矮小的大卫，大卫用突如其来的恶石猛击他；巨人被一个冷静、观察入微却几乎隐形的敌人激怒，陷入盲目的狂怒之中，然后被悠闲地消灭。这种情境贯穿了从波吕斐摩斯和布伦德伯尔的故事到卓别林电影（后者在更具讽刺意味和模棱两可的语境下）的讽刺作品。德莱顿将他的受害者描绘成皮包骨头、脑子像花生米一样的奇幻恐龙；他似乎真的被奥格“伟大而威猛”的身躯和诗人多伊格的狂怒能量所震撼。

Milton says, “for a Satyr as it was born out of a Tragedy, so ought to resemble his parentage, to strike high, and adventure dangerously at the most eminent vices among the greatest persons.” Apart from the etymology, this needs one qualification: a great vice does not need a great person to represent it. We have mentioned the gigantic size of Sir Epicure Mammon’s dream in The Alchemist: the whole mystery of the corrupted human will is in it, yet the utter impotence of the dreamer is essential to the satire. Similarly, we miss much of the point of Jonathan Wild unless we take the hero seriously as a parody of greatness, or false social standards of valuation. But in general the principle may be accepted for the satirist’s antagonists that the larger they come, the easier they fall. In low-norm satire the alazon is a Goliath encountered by a tiny David with his sudden and vicious stones, a giant prodded by a cool and observant but almost invisible enemy into a blind, stampeding fury and then polished off at leisure. This situation has run through satire from the stories of Polyphemus and Blunderbore to, in a much more ironic and equivocal context, the Chaplin films. Dryden transforms his victims into fantastic dinosaurs of bulging flesh and peanut brains; he seems genuinely impressed by the “goodly and great” bulk of Og and by the furious energy of the poet Doeg.

低等英雄形象是讽刺中英雄的替代品，当他从讽刺作品中被剥离出来时，我们就能更清楚地看到，神话的核心主题之一是英雄的消亡。这正是虚构讽刺作品中盛行“翁法勒原型”（Omphale archetype）的主要原因，即被女性欺凌或支配的男性形象，这一形象在……中尤为突出。讽刺贯穿其整个历史，并涵盖了当代幽默的广阔领域，既包括通俗的，也包括高雅的。同样，当我们剥离巨人或怪物的外衣，便会发现它其实是社会的神话形态，是九头蛇或满嘴长舌的恶灵，是斯宾塞笔下至今仍然逍遥法外的公然怪兽。虽然那些怀揣新奇想法的怪人显然是讽刺的对象，但社会习俗本质上仍然是僵化的教条，而低俗讽刺所诉诸的标准，正是一套大多由已故怪人发明的习俗。循规蹈矩之人的力量不在于习俗本身，而在于他们运用常识处理习俗的方式。因此，讽刺的逻辑本身就驱动着它从最初对非传统事物的常规讽刺，发展到第二阶段，在这一阶段，习俗的来源和价值本身也成为了嘲讽的对象。

The figure of the low-norm eiron is irony’s substitute for the hero, and when he is removed from satire we can see more clearly that one of the central themes of the mythos is the disappearance of the heroic. This is the main reason for the predominance in fictional satire of what may be called the Omphale archetype, the man bullied or dominated by women, which has been prominent in satire all through its history, and embraces a vast area of contemporary humor, both popular and sophisticated. Similarly, when the giant or monster is removed we can see that he is the mythical form of society, the hydra or fama full of tongues, Spenser’s blatant beast which is still at large. And while the crank with his new idea is an obvious target for satire, still social convention is mainly fossilized dogma, and the standard appealed to by low-norm satire is a set of conventions largely invented by dead cranks. The strength of the conventional person is not in the conventions but in his common-sense way of handling them. Hence the logic of satire itself drives it on from its first phase of conventional satire on the unconventional to a second phase in which the sources and values of conventions themselves are objects of ridicule.

喜剧第二阶段最简单的形式是逃亡喜剧，主人公逃往一个更合他心意的社会，却并未改变他原本的社会。与之对应的讽刺作品是流浪汉小说，讲述的是那些成功的无赖的故事，从《狐狸列那》开始，他们让传统社会显得愚蠢，却并未树立任何积极的榜样。流浪汉小说是社会讽刺的一种形式，随着《堂吉诃德》的出现，这种讽刺逐渐演变为一种更具知识性的讽刺，其本质需要进一步阐释。

The simplest form of the corresponding second phase of comedy is the comedy of escape, in which a hero runs away to a more congenial society without transforming his own. The satiric counterpart of this is the picaresque novel, the story of the successful rogue who, from Reynard the Fox on, makes conventional society look foolish without setting up any positive standard. The picaresque novel is the social form of what with Don Quixote modulates into a more intellectualized satire, the nature of which needs some explanation.

根据尤维纳利斯那句虽老套却实用的论断，讽刺作品关注的是人类的一切行为。而哲学家则教导某种生活方式或方法；他强调某些方面，鄙视另一些方面；他所推荐的都是从人类生活的经验中精心挑选出来的；他不断地对社会行为做出道德评判。他的态度是教条式的，而讽刺作家的态度则是实用主义的。因此，讽刺作品常常体现了从经验中汲取的标准与“经验远大于任何关于经验的信念”这一观点之间的冲突。讽刺作家通过揭示人类行为的无穷多样性，展现了不仅无法告诉人们应该做什么，甚至无法系统化或构建一个连贯的行为模式的徒劳。人生哲学是对生活的抽象，而抽象意味着忽略那些不便之处。讽刺作家会提出这些不便的数据，有时以替代性的、同样合理的理论的形式提出，例如埃瑞璜对犯罪和疾病的处理，或者斯威夫特对精神机械运作的论证。

Satire, according to Juvenal’s useful if hackneyed formula, has an interest in anything men do. The philosopher, on the other hand, teaches a certain way or method of living; he stresses some things and despises others; what he recommends is carefully selected from the data of human life; he continually passes moral judgements on social behavior. His attitude is dogmatic; that of the satirist pragmatic. Hence satire may often represent the collision between a selection of standards from experience and the feeling that experience is bigger than any set of beliefs about it. The satirist demonstrates the infinite variety of what men do by showing the futility, not only of saying what they ought to do, but even of attempts to systematize or formulate a coherent scheme of what they do. Philosophies of life abstract from life, and an abstraction implies the leaving out of inconvenient data. The satirist brings up these inconvenient data, sometimes in the form of alternative and equally plausible theories, like the Erewhonian treatment of crime and disease or Swift’s demonstration of the mechanical operation of spirit.

因此，讽刺的第二阶段，即堂吉诃德式的阶段，其核心主题在于将各种理念、概括、理论和教条与它们本应解释的生活进行对比。卢奇安的对话录《卖命记》清晰地展现了这一主题。在文中，一系列奴隶哲学家带着各自的论证和保证，依次向一位买家展示，买家不得不考虑是否要与他们共同生活。的确，他买下了几位，但只是作为奴隶，而非主人或教师。卢奇安对希腊哲学的态度，在伊拉斯谟和拉伯雷对经院哲学家、斯威夫特和塞缪尔·巴特勒一世对笛卡尔和皇家学会、伏尔泰对莱布尼茨学派、皮科克对浪漫主义者、塞缪尔·巴特勒二世对达尔文主义者、奥尔德斯·赫胥黎对行为主义者的态度中均有体现。我们注意到，低俗讽刺往往沦为反智主义，这种倾向在克拉布（参见《博学的男孩》）甚至斯威夫特的作品中都有体现。低俗讽刺在美国文化中的影响，导致大众普遍鄙视长发族和象牙塔，这或许可以称之为诗意投射的谬误，即把文学惯例当作生活常识。然而，真正的反智主义讽刺，是基于对系统性思维相对幼稚的认知，不应被怀疑或愤世嫉俗等现成词汇所局限。

The central theme in the second or quixotic phase of satire, then, is the setting of ideas and generalizations and theories and dogmas over against the life they are supposed to explain. This theme is presented very clearly in Lucian’s dialogue The Sale of Lives, in which a series of slave-philosophers pass in review, with all their arguments and guarantees, before a buyer who has to consider living with them. He buys a few, it is true, but as slaves, not as masters or teachers. Lucian’s attitude to Greek philosophy is repeated in the attitude of Erasmus and Rabelais to the scholastics, of Swift and Samuel Butler I to Descartes and the Royal Society, of Voltaire to the Leibnitzians, of Peacock to the Romantics, of Samuel Butler II to the Darwinians, of Aldous Huxley to the behaviorists. We notice that low-norm satire often becomes merely anti-intellectual, a tendency that crops up in Crabbe (vide The Learned Boy) and even in Swift. The influence of low-norm satire in American culture has produced a popular contempt for longhairs and ivory towers, an example of what may be called a fallacy of poetic projection, or taking literary conventions to be facts of life. Anti-intellectual satire proper, however, is based on a sense of the comparative naivete of systematic thought, and should not be limited by such ready-made terms as skeptical or cynical.

怀疑主义本身可能是一种教条主义的态度，或者演变成一种对显而易见的证据持怀疑态度的滑稽幽默。犬儒主义则更接近讽刺的规范：梅尼普斯讽刺剧的创始人梅尼普斯就是一位犬儒主义者，而犬儒主义者通常与知识分子特尔西忒斯的角色联系在一起。例如，利利的戏剧《坎帕斯佩》中出现了柏拉图、亚里士多德和第欧根尼，但前两位令人厌烦，而第欧根尼——他根本不是哲学家，而是一个伊丽莎白时代愤世嫉俗的小丑——却抢尽了风头。然而，犬儒主义仍然是一种哲学，它可能会滋生出佩雷格里努斯那种奇异的精神傲慢，卢奇安对佩雷格里努斯进行了深刻而可怕的分析。在《卖命记》中，犬儒主义者和怀疑论者依次被拍卖，后者是最后一个被卖掉的，他被拖走，他的怀疑论本身就被驳斥，而驳斥的方式不是辩论，而是生活。伊拉斯谟和伯顿自称“小德谟克利特”，是那位嘲笑人类的哲学家的追随者，但卢奇安的买家认为德谟克利特也矫揉造作了。讽刺作家若要表达自己的“立场”，那就是实践重于理论，经验重于形而上学。卢奇安去请教他的老师梅尼普斯时，梅尼普斯告诉他，智慧之道在于实践。这正是唾手可得的，伏尔泰的《老实人》中也曾提及， 《埃瑞璜》中对未出生者的训诫也同样如此。因此，哲学上的迂腐最终会像所有讽刺对象一样，变成一种浪漫主义，或者说是将过于简单化的理想强加于经验之上。

Skepticism itself may be or become a dogmatic attitude, a comic humor of doubting plain evidence. Cynicism is a little closer to the satiric norm: Menippus, the founder of the Menippean satire, was a cynic, and cynics are generally associated with the role of intellectual Thersites. Lyly’s play Campaspe, for instance, presents Plato, Aristotle, and Diogenes, but the first two are bores, and Diogenes, who is not a philosopher at all but an Elizabethan clown of the malcontent type, steals the show. But still cynicism is a philosophy, and one that may produce the strange spiritual pride of the Peregrinus of whom Lucian makes a searching and terrible analysis. In the Sale of Lives the cynic and the skeptic are auctioned in their turn, and the latter is the last to be sold, dragged off to have his very skepticism refuted, not by argument but by life. Erasmus and Burton called themselves Democritus Junior, followers of the philosopher who laughed at mankind, but Lucian’s buyer considers that Democritus too has overdone his pose. Insofar as the satirist has a “position” of his own, it is the preference of practice to theory, experience to metaphysics. When Lucian goes to consult his master Menippus, he is told that the method of wisdom is to do the task that lies to hand, advice repeated in Voltaire’s Candide and in the instructions given to the unborn in Erewhon. Thus philosophical pedantry becomes, as every target of satire eventually does, a form of romanticism or the imposing of over-simplified ideals on experience.

此处的讽刺态度既非哲学性的，也非反哲学性的，而是对一种假想艺术形式的表达。讽刺思想，恰恰是捍卫自身创作超脱性的特殊艺术形式。对思想秩序的需求催生了各种知识体系：其中一些体系吸引并转化了艺术家，但正如一位同样伟大的诗人也能同样出色地捍卫任何其他体系一样，没有任何一个体系能够完全涵盖所有艺术形式。因此，一个系统性的推理者，一旦掌握权力，就很可能在艺术领域建立等级制度，或者像柏拉图试图对荷马那样进行审查和删改。讽刺推理体系，尤其是讽刺此类体系的社会影响，是艺术抵御一切此类入侵的第一道防线。

The satiric attitude here is neither philosophical nor anti-philosophical, but an expression of the hypothetical form of art. Satire on ideas is only the special kind of art that defends its own creative detachment. The demand for order in thought produces a supply of intellectual systems: some of these attract and convert artists, but as an equally great poet could defend any other system equally well, no one system can contain the arts as they stand. Hence a systematic reasoner, given the power, would be likely to establish hierarchies in the arts, or censor and expurgate as Plato wished to do to Homer. Satire on systems of reasoning, especially on the social effects of such systems, is art’s first line of defence against all such invasions.

在科学与迷信的斗争中，讽刺作家们功不可没。讽刺本身似乎起源于古希腊的讽刺诗（silloi），这些诗篇是对迷信的科学批判。在英国文学中，乔叟和本·琼森用炼金术士的术语反击，令他们哑口无言；纳什和斯威夫特将占星家逼入绝境；勃朗宁的《灵媒斯莱奇》彻底摧毁了唯灵论者；而胡迪布拉斯的出现，则让一群神秘主义者、命理学家、毕达哥拉斯学派和玫瑰十字会成员尸横遍野。对科学家而言，讽刺作品如此平静地嘲弄正统天文学家（如《月亮上的大象》）、实验室（如《格列佛游记》）、达尔文和马尔萨斯宇宙论（如《埃瑞璜》） 、条件反射（如《美丽新世界》）、技术效率（如《1984》），这或许显得近乎荒谬。查尔斯·福特是本世纪少数几位延续知识分子讽刺传统的作家之一，他讽刺科学家们摆脱迷信本身，这种理性态度如同所有理性态度一样，仍然拒绝审视所有证据，从而使讽刺的车轮绕回了原点。

In the warfare of science against superstition, the satirists have done famously. Satire itself appears to have begun with the Greek silloi which were pro-scientific attacks on superstition. In English literature, Chaucer and Ben Jonson riddled the alchemists with a cross-fire of their own jargon; Nashe and Swift hounded astrologers into premature graves; Browning’s Sludge the Medium annihilated the spiritualists, and a rabble of occultists, numerologists, Pythagoreans, and Rosicrucians lie sprawling in the wake of Hudibras. To the scientist it may seem little short of perverse that satire placidly goes on making fun of legitimate astronomers in The Elephant in the Moon, of experimental laboratories in Gulliver’s Travels, of Darwinian and Malthusian cosmology in Erewhon, of conditioned reflexes in Brave New World, of technological efficiency in 1984. Charles Fort, one of the few who have continued the tradition of intellectual satire in this century, brings the wheel full circle by mocking the scientists for their very freedom from superstition itself, a rational attitude which, like all rational attitudes, still refuses to examine all the evidence.

宗教亦是如此。讽刺作家或许会像卢奇安那样认为，消除迷信也会消除宗教；或者像伊拉斯谟那样认为，消除迷信会恢复宗教的健康。但宙斯是否存在尚属疑问；而那些认为他邪恶愚蠢的人却坚持认为他能改变天气，这却是公认的事实。无论是嘲讽者还是虔诚者，都会受到讽刺。任何真正虔诚的人肯定都会欢迎一位讽刺作家，他以辛辣的笔触揭露虚伪和迷信，视其为真正宗教的盟友。然而，一旦一个听起来像个好人的伪君子被彻底揭露，那么这位好人本身也可能显得比以前更加黯淡无光。那些甚至认同《流浪汉》中“圣威利的祈祷”理论部分的人，看起来就像是圣威利本人。同样，人们也会觉得，尽管伊拉斯谟、拉伯雷、斯威夫特和伏尔泰对制度化宗教的个人态度大相径庭，但他们的讽刺作品的效果却大同小异。对宗教的讽刺包括对英国新教圣礼生活的戏仿（从弥尔顿的离婚小册子到《众生之路》），以及尼采、叶芝和D·H·劳伦斯基于耶稣是另一种浪漫理想主义者的观念而对基督教的敌视。

Similarly with religion. The satirist may feel with Lucian that the eliminating of superstition would also eliminate religion, or with Erasmus that it would restore health to religion. But whether Zeus exists or not is a question; that men who think him vicious and stupid will insist that he change the weather is a fact, accepted by scoffer and devout alike. Any really devout person would surely welcome a satirist who cauterized hypocrisy and superstition as an ally of true religion. Yet once a hypocrite who sounds exactly like a good man is sufficiently blackened, the good man also may begin to seem a little dingier than he was. Those who would agree even with the theoretical parts of Holy Willie’s Prayer in Bums look rather like Holy Willies themselves. One feels similarly that while the personal attitudes of Erasmus, Rabelais, Swift, and Voltaire to institutional religion varied a good deal, the effect of their satire varies much less. Satire on religion includes the parody of the sacramental life in English Protestantism that runs from Milton’s divorce pamphlets to The Way of All Flesh, and the antagonism to Christianity in Nietzsche, Yeats, and D. H. Lawrence based on the conception of Jesus as another kind of romantic idealist.

《埃瑞璜》的叙述者指出，尽管大多数埃瑞璜居民的真正宗教信仰，无论他们如何自称，都是对低级规范习俗（女神伊德格伦）的接受，但也有少数“高级伊德格伦信徒”，他们是埃瑞璜在埃瑞璜遇到的最优秀的人。这些人的态度让我们想起蒙田：他们拥有埃隆人那种对长期建立且如今无害的习俗价值的认知；他们也拥有埃隆人那种对任何人的理性（包括他们自己的理性）能否将社会改造得更好的能力的怀疑。但他们在理智上又与他们所遵循的习俗保持着距离，能够看到这些习俗的反常之处和荒谬之处，以及它们所具有的稳定作用和保守性。

The narrator in Erewhon remarks that while the real religion of most of the Erewhonians was, whatever they said it was, the acceptance of low-norm conventionality (the goddess Ydgrun), there was also a small group of “high Ydgrunites” who were the best people he found in Erewhon. The attitude of these people reminds us rather of Montaigne: they had the eiron’s sense of the value of conventions that had been long established and were now harmless; they had the eiron’s distrust of the ability of anyone’s reason, including their own, to transform society into a better structure. But they were also intellectually detached from the conventions they lived with, and were capable of seeing their anomalies and absurdities as well as their stabilizing conservatism.

在第二阶段的讽刺作品中，伊德格伦主义盛行时期所产生的文学形式，我们可以称之为“天真者”形式，这个名称源自伏尔泰的同名对话。在这种形式中，一个社会局外人，在本例中是一位美洲原住民，代表着低等标准：他没有自己的教条式观点，但他也不认同任何使社会荒谬之处在习以为常的人看来合乎逻辑的前提。他实际上是一个田园牧歌式的人物，而田园牧歌这种形式本身就适合讽刺，他将一套简单的标准与社会复杂的理性化进行对比。但我们刚才已经看到，讽刺作家所坚持的恰恰是经验数据的复杂性，以及他对那套简单标准的怀疑。这就是为什么“天真者”是一个局外人；他来自另一个世界，一个要么遥不可及，要么与某种令人不快的事物联系在一起的世界。如果我们不介意成为蒙田笔下的食人族，他们就拥有我们所不具备的所有美德。食人族。莫尔的《乌托邦》是一个理想国度，但要进入其中，我们必须放弃基督教信仰。慧骃比我们更懂得理性与自然的生活方式，但格列佛发现自己生来就是个野胡，这样的生活更接近于天赋异禀的动物而非人类。每当“另一个世界”出现在讽刺作品中，它都以反讽的方式呈现，与我们的世界相对应，颠覆了既定的社会准则。卢奇安的《卡塔普洛斯》和《卡戎》就体现了这种讽刺形式，这两部作品都描绘了前往另一个世界的旅程，其中我们这个世界的显赫人物在异世界中做着合乎情理却又不寻常的事情；拉伯雷的作品以及中世纪的死亡之舞也采用了这种形式。在死亡之舞中，死亡的简单平等与生命的复杂不平等形成了鲜明的对比。

The literary form that high Ydgrunism produces in second-phase satire we may call the ingenu form, after Voltaire’s dialogue of that name. Here an outsider to the society, in this case an American Indian, is the low norm: he has no dogmatic views of his own, but he grants none of the premises which make the absurdities of society look logical to those accustomed to them. He is really a pastoral figure, and like the pastoral, a form congenial to satire, he contrasts a set of simple standards with the complex rationalizations of society. But we have just seen that it is precisely the complexity of data in experience which the satirist insists on and the simple set of standards which he distrusts. That is why the ingenu is an outsider; he comes from another world which is either unattainable or associated with something else undesirable. Montaigne’s cannibals have all the virtues we have not, if we don’t mind being cannibals. More’s Utopia is an ideal state except that to enter it we must give up the idea of Christendom. The Houyhnhnms live the life of reason and nature better than we, but Gulliver finds that he is born a Yahoo, and that such a life would be nearer the capacities of gifted animals than of humans. Whenever the “other world” appears in satire, it appears as an ironic counterpart to our own, a reversal of accepted social standards. This form of satire is represented in Lucian’s Kataplous and Charon, journeys to the other world in which the eminent in this one are shown doing appropriate but unaccustomed things, a form incorporated in Rabelais, and in the medieval danse macabre. In the last named the simple equality of death is set against the complex inequalities of life.

知识分子式的讽刺捍卫了艺术创作中的超脱性，但艺术本身也倾向于寻求社会认可的观念，并反过来成为一种社会固化的体现。我们曾谈到，浪漫主义的理想化艺术尤其体现在上层阶级倾向于表达自我的形式中，因此，中世纪欧洲新兴的中产阶级自然而然地转向了戏仿浪漫主义。其他形式的讽刺也具有类似的功能，无论其创作意图如何。死亡之舞和卡塔普洛斯舞是对我们严肃的来世观中所体现的那种浪漫主义的反讽式颠覆。例如，在但丁的作品中，来世的审判通常与今世的标准相符，而天堂里几乎所有的营房都只供军官居住。这种讽刺的文化影响并非贬低浪漫主义，而是防止任何一套惯例主导整个文学体验。第二阶段的讽刺作品展现了文学承担的特殊分析功能，即打破陈规陋习、僵化观念、迷信恐惧、怪诞理论、迂腐教条、压抑风尚以及一切阻碍社会自由流动（当然，未必是进步）的事物。这种讽刺作品完成了被称为“归谬法”（reductio ad absurdum ）的逻辑过程，其目的并非使人永远受困，而是引导人摆脱错误的思维模式。

Intellectual satire defends the creative detachment in art, but art too tends to seek out socially accepted ideas and become in its turn a social fixation. We have spoken of the idealized art of romance as in particular the form in which an ascendant class tends to express itself, and so the rising middle class in medieval Europe naturally turned to mock-romance. Other forms of satire have a similar function, whether so intended or not. The danse macabre and the kataplous are ironic reversals of the kind of romanticism that we have in the serious vision of the other world. In Dante, for instance, the judgements of the next world usually confirm the standards of this one, and in heaven itself nearly the whole available billeting is marked for officers only. The cultural effect of such satire is not to denigrate romance, but to prevent any group of conventions from dominating the whole of literary experience. Second-phase satire shows literature assuming a special function of analysis, of breaking up the lumber of stereotypes, fossilized beliefs, superstitious terrors, crank theories, pedantic dogmatisms, oppressive fashions, and all other things that impede the free movement (not necessarily, of course, the progress) of society. Such satire is the completion of the logical process known as the reductio ad absurdum, which is not designed to hold one in perpetual captivity, but to bring one to the point at which one can escape from an incorrect procedure.

浪漫主义对完美形式之美的迷恋，无论在艺术领域还是其他领域，也自然而然地成为了讽刺的对象。“讽刺”（satire）一词据说源于“satura”，意为“杂乱无章”，而对形式的戏仿似乎贯穿了其整个传统，源于这种混合。从早期讽刺作品中散文和诗歌的运用，到拉伯雷作品中场景的生硬切换（我指的是一种略显古老的电影风格），《项狄传》和《唐璜》都清晰地展现了讽刺修辞中持续存在的自我戏仿倾向，这种倾向甚至阻止了写作过程本身沦为一种过于简单的惯例或理想。在《唐璜》中，我们既阅读诗歌，又观看诗人创作的过程：我们仿佛在偷听他的联想，他为押韵而苦苦思索，他尝试却最终放弃的计划，以及他选择细节时所受到的主观偏好（例如：“她身材高挑——我讨厌矮胖的女人”），还有他决定是“严肃”还是用幽默掩饰自己。所有这些，甚至更多，在《项狄传》中都得到了体现。刻意冗长、离题万里的叙述手法，在讽刺小说中屡见不鲜，甚至到了专门赞美离题本身的地步。精心设计的滑稽效果或故弄玄虚的悬念，例如阿普列乌斯和拉伯雷作品中令人费解的、类似神谕般的结尾，以及斯特恩数百页篇幅中始终拒绝让主人公出生，都是讽刺小说的惯用手法。许多伟大的讽刺作品都是残篇、未完成或匿名的。在反讽小说中，许多利用沟通障碍的手法，例如通过一个白痴的视角来讲述故事，也达到了同样的效果。弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的《海浪》正是由人物的言辞构成，而这些言辞恰恰是由他们未说出口的话，以及他们尽管没有说出口，却依然通过行为和态度所表达出来的东西构成的。

The romantic fixation which revolves around the beauty of perfect form, in art or elsewhere, is also a logical target for satire. The word satire is said to come from satura, or hash, and a kind of parody of form seems to run all through its tradition, from the mixture of prose and verse in early satire to the jerky cinematic changes of scene in Rabelais (I am thinking of a somewhat archaic type of cinema). Tristram Shandy and Don Juan illustrate very clearly the constant tendency to self-parody in satiric rhetoric which prevents even the process of writing itself from becoming an oversimplified convention or ideal. In Don Juan we simultaneously read the poem and watch the poet at work writing it: we eavesdrop on his associations, his struggles for rhymes, his tentative and discarded plans, the subjective preferences organizing his choice of details (e.g.: “Her stature tall—I hate a dumpy woman”), his decisions whether to be “serious” or mask himself with humor. All of this and even more is true of Tristram Shandy. A deliberate rambling digressiveness, which in A Tale of a Tub reaches the point of including a digression in praise of digressions, is endemic in the narrative technique of satire, and so is a calculated bathos or art of sinking in its suspense, such as the quizzical mock-oracular conclusions in Apuleius and Rabelais and in the refusal of Sterne for hundreds of pages even to get his hero born. An extraordinary number of great satires are fragmentary, unfinished, or anonymous. In ironic fiction a good many devices turning on the difficulty of communication, such as having a story presented through an idiot mind, serve the same purpose. Virginia Woolf’s The Waves is made up of speeches of characters constructed precisely out of what they do not say, but what their behavior and attitudes say in spite of them.

这种解构技巧将我们带入了讽刺的第三阶段——对高尚规范的讽刺。第二阶段的讽刺或许会在策略上捍卫实用主义对抗教条主义，但在这里，我们甚至必须放弃将日常常识作为评判标准。因为常识本身也隐含着某些教条，尤其是感官经验的数据是可靠且一致的，以及我们对事物的习惯性联想构成了解释现在和预测未来的坚实基础。讽刺作家如果不质疑这些假设，就无法探索其作品形式的所有可能性。这就是为什么他经常赋予日常生活一种逻辑自洽的视角转变。他会突然用望远镜向我们展示社会，将其描绘成姿态庄重的侏儒；或者用显微镜向我们展示社会，将其描绘成丑陋恶臭的巨人；又或者，他会将笔下的主人公变成一头驴，向我们展示从驴的视角看人性是什么样的。这种类型的幻想它打破了惯常的联想，将感官体验简化为众多可能类别之一，并揭示了我们所有思维的试探性基础。爱默生认为，这种视角转换带来“低层次的崇高”，但实际上，它带来的东西具有更重要的艺术意义——高度的荒诞。而且，与讽刺作为戏仿浪漫的普遍基础相一致，它们通常是对浪漫主题的改编：小矮人的仙境、巨人的国度、魔法动物的世界，以及卢西安《真实历史》中戏仿的奇幻世界。

This technique of disintegration brings us well into the third phase of satire, the satire of the high norm. Second-phase satire may make a tactical defence of the pragmatic against the dogmatic, but here we must let go even of ordinary common sense as a standard. For common sense too has certain implied dogmas, notably that the data of sense experience are reliable and consistent, and that our customary associations with things form a solid basis for interpreting the present and predicting the future. The satirist cannot explore all the possibilities of his form without seeing what happens if he questions these assumptions. That is why he so often gives to ordinary life a logical and self-consistent shift of perspective. He will show us society suddenly in a telescope as posturing and dignified pygmies, or in a microscope as hideous and reeking giants, or he will change his hero into an ass and show us how humanity looks from an ass’s point of view. This type of fantasy breaks down customary associations, reduces sense experience to one of many possible categories, and brings out the tentative, als ob basis of all our thinking. Emerson says that such shifts of perspective afford “a low degree of the sublime,” but actually they afford something of far greater artistic importance, a high degree of the ridiculous. And, consistently with the general basis of satire as parody-romance, they are usually adaptations of romance themes: the fairyland of little people, the land of giants, the world of enchanted animals, the wonderlands parodied in Lucian’s True History.

当我们从信仰和理性的庇护下退回到感官的现实时，讽刺便如影随形。视角稍有转变，情感色彩稍稍变淡，坚实的尘世便会变成令人难以忍受的恐怖。《格列佛游记》将人描绘成毒鼠，人成丑陋笨拙的庞然大物，人的心灵如同熊窝，人的肉体则由污秽与凶残交织而成。但斯威夫特只是顺应了他讽刺的天赋，而这种天赋似乎也引导着几乎每一位伟大的讽刺作家走向了世人眼中的“淫秽”。社会习俗意味着人们彼此攀比，而维护这种习俗要求人们将某些男人的尊严和某些女人的美丽与排泄、性交以及类似的尴尬行为割裂开来。不断提及这些令人尴尬的事物，最终会将我们引向一种类似于死亡之舞中死亡民主的身体民主。斯威夫特对死亡之舞传统的亲近在他对斯特鲁德布鲁格人的描述中显露无疑，而他的《致仆人指南》以及他那些鲜为人知的诗篇，则继承了中世纪布道者的传统，他们描绘了暴食和好色的丑恶。因为正如讽刺作品中处处可见的那样，这里也蕴含着道德寓意：吃喝玩乐固然美好，但死亡终究会来临。

When we fall back from the outworks of faith and reason to the tangible realities of the senses, satire follows us up. A slight shift of perspective, a different tinge in the emotional coloring, and the solid earth becomes an intolerable horror. Gulliver’s Travels shows us man as a venomous rodent, man as a noisome and clumsy pachyderm, the mind of man as a bear-pit, and the body of man as a compound of filth and ferocity. But Swift is simply following where his satiric genius leads him, and genius seems to have led practically every great satirist to become what the world calls obscene. Social convention means people parading in front of each other, and the preservation of it demands that the dignity of some men and the beauty of some women should be thought of apart from excretion, copulation, and similar embarrassments. Constant reference to these latter brings us down to a bodily democracy paralleling the democracy of death in the danse macabre. Swift’s affinity with the danse macabre tradition is marked in his description of the Struldbrugs, and his Directions to Servants and his more unquotable poems are in the tradition of the medieval preachers who painted the repulsiveness of gluttony and lechery. For here as everywhere else in satire there is a moral reference: it is all very well to eat, drink, and be merry, but one cannot always put off dying until tomorrow.

在拉伯雷、佩特罗尼乌斯和阿普列乌斯笔下喧闹混乱的讽刺中，讽刺最终战胜了常识。当我们从他们那些怪诞却又合乎逻辑的关于放荡、梦境和谵妄的幻想中醒来时，我们不禁思考帕拉塞尔苏斯的观点是否正确：谵妄中看到的事物是否真的存在，就像白昼中的星星一样，只是因为同样的原因而看不见。卢修斯接受了启蒙，却又巧妙地从我们手中溜走，无论他说的是真话还是假话，正如圣奥古斯丁略带恼怒地说道；拉伯雷承诺给我们一个最终的预言，却让我们对着一个空瓶子发呆。乔伊斯的《哈迪斯·卡罗尔德·卡罗尔德》苦苦挣扎了数页才得以觉醒，但就在我们似乎即将触及某些具体事物时，却又被拉回到了书的第一页。《萨蒂里孔》像是从一部历史中撕下的残片，讲述的是某个沉入海底、醉醺醺的亚特兰蒂斯怪物种族的故事。

In the riotous chaos of Rabelais, Petronius, and Apuleius satire plunges through to its final victory over common sense. When we have finished with their weirdly logical fantasies of debauch, dream, and delirium we wake up wondering if Paracelsus’ suggestion is right that the things seen in delirium are really there, like stars in daytime, and invisible for the same reason. Lucius becomes initiated and slips evasively out of our grasp, whether he lied or told the truth, as St. Augustine says with a touch of exasperation; Rabelais promises us a final oracle and leaves us staring at an empty bottle; Joyce’s HCE struggles for pages toward wakening, but just as we seem on the point of grasping something tangible we are swung around to the first page of the book again. The Satyricon is a torn fragment from what seems like a history of some monstrous Atlantean race that vanished in the sea, still drunk.

讽刺的第一阶段以巨人杀手的形象为主导，但在这种对稳定宇宙的撕裂中，讽刺本身也涌现出一股强大的力量。当非利士巨人出来与光明之子交战时，他自然期望遇到一个与他势均力敌的对手，一个远胜以色列所有人的巨人。这样的巨人必须凭借强大的言辞压制对手，因此必须精通那种我们称之为谩骂的滔滔不绝的攻击技巧。拉伯雷笔下的巨人形象，《芬尼根守灵夜》中被束缚或沉睡的巨人苏醒的形象，以及《格列佛游记》开篇所展现的形象，都体现了一种创造力的奔涌。这种创造力最典型、最明显的特征便是语言的风暴，即在目录、谩骂的绰号和博学的技术细节中倾泻而出的惊人文字。自《以赛亚书》第三章（一部讽刺女性装饰的作品）以来，这种语言风暴就一直是第三阶段讽刺作品的特征，甚至几乎垄断了这一领域。英国文学中这种语言风暴的黄金时代，正是伯顿、纳什、马斯顿和克罗马蒂的厄克特（拉伯雷的无拘无束的译者）的时代。厄克特在业余时间里，正如纳什所说的，是一位“学术喷墨作家”，创作了诸如《三部曲》（Trissotetras）、《万物之轮》（Pantochronochanon）、《埃克斯库巴劳龙》（Exkubalauron）和《逻各斯·潘德克泰森》（Logo- pandecteison ）之类的作品。除了乔伊斯之外，现代英语作家中几乎没有人持续不断地努力延续这种语言奔放的传统：从这个角度来看，即使是卡莱尔，也远逊于伯顿和厄克特。在美国文化中，这种传统体现在民间传说吹嘘者的“夸夸其谈”上，惠特曼和《白鲸》中也有一些文学上的类似例子。

The first phase of satire is dominated by the figure of the giant-killer, but in this rending of the stable universe a giant power rears up in satire itself. When the Philistine giant comes out to battle with the children of light, he naturally expects to find someone his own size ready to meet him, someone who is head and shoulders over every man in Israel. Such a Titan would have to bear down his opponent by sheer weight of words, and hence be a master of that technique of torrential abuse which we call invective. The gigantic figures in Rabelais, the awakened forms of the bound or sleeping giants that meet us in Finnegans Wake and the opening of Gulliver’s Travels, are expressions of a creative exuberance of which the most typical and obvious sign is the verbal tempest, the tremendous outpouring of words in catalogues, abusive epithets and erudite technicalities which since the third chapter of Isaiah (a satire on female ornament) has been a feature, and almost a monopoly, of third-phase satire. Its golden age in English literature was the age of Burton, Nashe, Marston, and Urquhart of Cromarty, the uninhibited translator of Rabelais, who in his spare time was what Nashe would call a “scholastical squitter-book,” producing books with such titles as Trissotetras, Pantochronochanon, Exkubalauron and Logo-pandecteison. Nobody except Joyce has in modern English made much sustained effort to carry on this tradition of verbal exuberance: even Carlyle, from this point of view, is a sad comedown after Burton and Urquhart. In American culture it is represented by the “tall talk” of the folklore boaster, which has some literary congeners in the catalogues of Whitman and Moby Dick.

到了第四阶段，我们转向悲剧的讽刺层面，讽刺开始减弱。悲剧英雄的陨落，尤其是在莎士比亚的作品中，情感的平衡如此微妙，以至于我们几乎只需强调其中任何一个元素，都会使其显得过分。其中一个元素便是挽歌式的情感，在这种情感中，讽刺的成分极少，取而代之的是一种温柔而庄重的悲怆感，这种情感通常以音乐为象征，例如赫拉克勒斯抛弃安东尼、亨利八世中被抛弃的凯瑟琳王后梦见自己、哈姆雷特的“暂时离开幸福”，以及奥赛罗的……阿勒颇演讲。当然，即便在这里也能发现讽刺意味，正如艾略特先生在前文中发现的那样，但主要的情感分量无疑落在了反面。然而我们也意识到，哈姆雷特死于一场疯狂混乱的复仇行动中，这场行动夺去了八条人命而非一条；克莉奥佩特拉在精心寻找轻松的死法后，带着极大的尊严消逝；科里奥兰纳斯被母亲弄得一头雾水，并强烈反感被称作“男孩”。这种悲剧性的讽刺与讽刺不同，它并非意在嘲弄人物，而只是为了清晰地展现悲剧中“过于人性化”的一面，而非英雄主义的一面。李尔王试图通过他作为国王和父亲的身份来获得英雄般的尊严，却最终在饱受苦难的人性中找到了它：因此，在《李尔王》中，我们看到了所谓的“怪诞喜剧”，即对悲剧情境的讽刺性模仿，而且这种模仿发展得最为精妙。

With the fourth phase we move around to the ironic aspect of tragedy, and satire begins to recede. The fall of the tragic hero, especially in Shakespeare, is so delicately balanced emotionally that we almost exaggerate any one element in it merely by calling attention to it. One of these elements is the elegiac aspect in which irony is at a minimum, the sense of gentle and dignified pathos, often symbolized by music, which marks the desertion of Antony by Hercules, the dream of the rejected Queen Catherine in Henry VIII, Hamlet’s “absent thee from felicity awhile,” and Othello’s Aleppo speech. One can of course find irony even here, as Mr. Eliot has found it in the last named, but the main emotional weight is surely thrown on the opposite side. Yet we are also aware that Hamlet dies in the middle of a frantically muddled effort at revenge which has taken eight lives instead of one, that Cleopatra fades away with great dignity after a careful search for easy ways to die, that Coriolanus is badly confused by his mother and violently resents being called a boy. Such tragic irony differs from satire in that there is no attempt to make fun of the character, but only to bring out clearly the “all too human,” as distinct from the heroic, aspects of the tragedy. King Lear attempts to achieve heroic dignity through his position as a king and father, and finds it instead in his suffering humanity: hence it is in King Lear that we find what has been called the “comedy of the grotesque,” the ironic parody of the tragic situation, most elaborately developed.

第四阶段本身就是一种反讽，它从底层视角审视悲剧，从经验状态的道德和现实主义角度出发。它强调主人公的人性，淡化悲剧中仪式性的必然性，为灾难提供社会和心理层面的解释，并尽可能地使人类的苦难，用梭罗的话来说，显得“多余且可避免”。这是最真诚、最明确的现实主义阶段：它总体上是托尔斯泰的创作阶段，也是哈代和康拉德许多作品的创作阶段。其核心主题之一是斯坦因对康拉德笔下“浪漫”的吉姆老爷问题的回答：“沉浸于毁灭性因素之中。”这句话并没有嘲讽吉姆老爷，却依然揭示了他性格中堂吉诃德式的浪漫情怀，并从经验的角度对其进行了批判。梅尔维尔的《皮埃尔》中关于钟表和计时器的章节也持类似的观点。

As a phase of irony in its own right, the fourth phase looks at tragedy from below, from the moral and realistic perspective of the state of experience. It stresses the humanity of its heroes, minimizes the sense of ritual inevitability in tragedy, supplies social and psychological explanations for catastrophe, and makes as much as possible of human misery seem, in Thoreau’s phrase, “superfluous and evitable.” This is the phase of most sincere, explicit realism: it is in general Tolstoy’s phase, and also that of a good deal of Hardy and Conrad. One of its central themes is Stein’s answer to the problem of the “romantic” Lord Jim in Conrad: “in the destructive element immerse.” This remark, without ridiculing Jim, still brings out the quixotic and romantic element in his nature and criticizes it from the point of view of experience. The chapter on watches and chronometers in Melville’s Pierre takes a similar attitude.

第五阶段，对应于宿命论或第五阶段悲剧，是一种反讽，其主要强调自然循环，即命运之轮持续不断的运转。它以我们今天的方式看待经验，认为顿悟的契机已经关闭，其格言是勃朗宁的“或许有天堂，但必然有地狱”。与相应的悲剧阶段一样，它较少关注道​​德，而更注重普遍性和形而上学，较少追求改良，而更倾向于坚忍和顺从。《战争与和平》和《王朝》中对拿破仑的处理，很好地对比了反讽的第四阶段和第五阶段。古英语《迪奥尔的抱怨》中的反复出现： “Thaes ofereode; thisses swa maeg”（自由地）这句话可以翻译为“其他人都能挺过来；也许我也能”）表达了一种斯多葛主义，这种斯多葛主义不是那种保持浪漫尊严的“不可战胜”式的，而是在讽刺的平行第二阶段中也发现的一种感觉，即实际的、眼前的状况可能比对其的理论解释更值得尊重。

The fifth phase, corresponding to fatalistic or fifth-phase tragedy, is irony in which the main emphasis is on the natural cycle, the steady unbroken turning of the wheel of fate or fortune. It sees experience, in our terms, with the point of epiphany closed up, and its motto is Browning’s “there may be heaven; there must be hell.” Like the corresponding phase of tragedy, it is less moral and more generalized and metaphysical in its interest, less melioristic and more stoical and resigned. The treatment of Napoleon in War and Peace and in The Dynasts affords a good contrast between the fourth and fifth phases of irony. The refrain in the Old English Complaint of Deor: “Thaes ofereode; thisses swa maeg” (freely translatable as “Other people got through things; maybe I can”) expresses a stoicism not of the “invictus” type, which maintains a romantic dignity, but rather a sense, found also in the parallel second phase of satire, that the practical and immediate situation is likely to be worthy of more respect than the theoretical explanation of it.

第六阶段将人类生活描绘成一种几乎无法摆脱的奴役状态。其场景包括监狱、疯人院、私刑暴徒和刑场，它与纯粹的地狱的主要区别在于，在人类的经验中，苦难最终会以死亡告终。在当今时代，这一阶段的主要形式是社会暴政的噩梦，《1984》或许是最为人熟知的例子。我们经常在“邪恶幻象”（visio malefica）的边缘地带发现对宗教符号的戏仿，暗示着某种形式的撒旦或反基督崇拜。在卡夫卡的《在流放地》中，军官的一句话“罪孽不容置疑”就体现了对原罪的戏仿。在《1984》的最后几幕中，对宗教的戏仿则更为精妙：例如，当主人公遭受酷刑时，他竟然恳求将酷刑施加在女主人公身上，这便是对赎罪的戏仿。这个故事的前提假设是，统治阶级对虐待狂式权力的渴望强大到足以无限期地持续下去，而这恰恰是接受正统地狱图景所必须对魔鬼做出的假设。“电视屏幕”这一装置讽刺地展现了“ derkou theama”（被敌视或嘲讽的目光持续注视的屈辱）这一悲剧主题。

The sixth phase presents human life in terms of largely unrelieved bondage. Its settings feature prisons, madhouses, lynching mobs, and places of execution, and it differs from a pure inferno mainly in the fact that in human experience suffering has an end in death. In our day the chief form of this phase is the nightmare of social tyranny, of which 1984 is perhaps the most familiar. We often find, on this boundary of the visio malefica, the use of parody-religious symbols suggesting some form of Satan or Antichrist worship. In Kafka’s In the Penal Colony a parody of original sin appears in the officer’s remark, “Guilt is never to be doubted.” In 1984 the parody of religion in the final scenes is more elaborate: there is a parody of the atonement, for instance, when the hero is tortured into urging that the torments be inflicted on the heroine instead. The assumption is made in this story that the lust for sadistic power on the part of the ruling class is strong enough to last indefinitely, which is precisely the assumption one has to make about devils in order to accept the orthodox picture of hell. The “telescreen” device brings into irony the tragic theme of derkou theama, the humiliation of being constantly watched by a hostile or derisive eye.

这一阶段的人物形象，当然都是苦难或疯狂的化身，通常是对浪漫角色的戏仿。例如，《毛猿》和《人鼠之间》都戏仿了乐于助人的巨人仆人的浪漫主题，《喧哗与骚动》中的本杰明则戏仿了浪漫的介绍人或普洛斯彼罗式的人物，他愚钝的头脑中包含了小说的全部情节，却又无法理解。阴险的父母形象自然也比比皆是，因为这是食人魔和女巫的世界，是波德莱尔笔下黑巨人女巨人和蒲柏笔下愚钝女神的世界，后者身上也带有许多戏仿神祇的特质（“光明在你无生之言面前消逝！”），是长发如囚笼般笼罩着人心的塞壬，当然还有蛇蝎美人或阴险狡诈、咧嘴而笑的女性，正如帕特所说，“她比她所坐的岩石还要古老”。

The human figures of this phase are, of course, desdichado figures of misery or madness, often parodies of romantic roles. Thus the romantic theme of the helpful servant giant is parodied in The Hairy Ape and Of Mice and Men, and the romantic presenter or Prospero figure is parodied in the Benjy of The Sound and the Fury whose idiot mind contains, without comprehending, the whole action of the novel. Sinister parental figures naturally abound, for this is the world of the ogre and the witch, of Baudelaire’s black giantess and Pope’s goddess Dullness, who also has much of the parody deity about her (“Light dies before thy uncreating word!”), of the siren with the imprisoning image of shrouding hair, and, of course, of the femme fatale or malignant grinning female, “older than the rocks among which she sits,” as Pater says of her.

这就又把我们带回到了恶魔显现的那一刻，那座黑暗的高塔，那座无尽痛苦的监狱；那座沙漠中令人恐惧的黑夜之城；或者，用更博学的讽刺来说，是那条虚幻的旅程——那并不存在的探寻目标。但在这片荒芜丑陋、愚昧无知的世界的另一边，一个没有怜悯也没有希望的世界，讽刺再次开始。在但丁笔下的地狱底部，也就是球形地球的中心，但丁看到撒旦直立在冰环之中。他小心翼翼地跟随维吉尔，从邪恶巨人的臀部和大腿上滑落，抓住他皮肤上的毛发，缓缓下降。他越过中心，发现自己不再向下，而是向上攀升，爬到了世界的另一边，再次看到了星空。从这个角度来看，魔鬼不再是直立的，而是倒立着，保持着他从天堂被抛到地球另一边时的姿势。悲剧和悲剧性的讽刺会将我们带入一个不断缩小的漩涡，最终让我们看到万恶之源以某种人格化的形式出现。悲剧无法引领我们走得更远；但如果我们坚持运用讽刺和挖苦的理论，我们将越过死胡同，最终看到那位温文尔雅的黑暗王子倒立的真面目。

This brings us around again to the point of demonic epiphany, the dark tower and prison of endless pain, the city of dreadful night in the desert, or, with a more erudite irony, the tour abolie, the goal of the quest that isn’t there. But on the other side of this blasted world of repulsiveness and idiocy, a world without pity and without hope, satire begins again. At the bottom of Dante’s hell, which is also the center of the spherical earth, Dante sees Satan standing upright in the circle of ice, and as he cautiously follows Virgil over the hip and thigh of the evil giant, letting himself down by the tufts of hair on his skin, he passes the center and finds himself no longer going down but going up, climbing out on the other side of the world to see the stars again. From this point of view, the devil is no longer upright, but standing on his head, in the same attitude in which he was hurled downward from heaven upon the other side of the earth. Tragedy and tragic irony take us into a hell of narrowing circles and culminate in some such vision of the source of all evil in a personal form. Tragedy can take us no farther; but if we persevere with the mythos of irony and satire, we shall pass a dead center, and finally see the gentlemanly Prince of Darkness bottom side up.

第四篇论文

修辞批评：文体理论

FOURTH ESSAY

Rhetorical Criticism: Theory of Genres

第四篇论文

Fourth Essay

修辞批评：体裁理论

RHETORICAL CRITICISM: THEORY OF GENRES

介绍

INTRODUCTION

本书采用了一种自柏拉图时代以来便在诗学中沿用的图解框架。这种框架将“善”分为三大领域，其中艺术、美、情感和品味的世界居于中心，两侧分别是社会行动和事件的世界，以及个人思想和观念的世界。从左至右阅读，这种三元结构将人类的各种能力分为意志、情感和理性。它将这些能力所产生的精神建构分为历史、艺术以及科学和哲学。它将对这些能力产生约束或要求的理想分为法律、美和真理。爱伦·坡给出了他自己对这一图解的诠释（从右至左）：纯粹理智、品味和道德感。“我把品味放在中间，”爱伦·坡说，“因为它在人的心灵中恰好占据这个位置。”在有人能够反驳这一精辟的解释之前，我们将继续沿用这种传统的结构。诚然，我们曾暗示过，或许还有另一种看待这个问题的方式，在这种方式中，中间世界并非仅仅是三个世界之一，而是一个包含所有三个世界的三位一体。但迄今为止，这种较为简单的概念对我们来说远未失去其价值。

THE PRESENT BOOK employs a diagrammatic framework that has been used in poetics ever since Plato’s time. This is the division of “the good” into three main areas, of which the world of art, beauty, feeling, and taste is the central one, and is flanked by two other worlds. One is the world of social action and events, the other the world of individual thought and ideas. Reading from left to right, this threefold structure divides human faculties into will, feeling, and reason. It divides the mental constructs which these faculties produce into history, art, and science and philosophy. It divides the ideals which form compulsions or obligations on these faculties into law, beauty, and truth. Poe gives his version of the diagram (right to left) as Pure Intellect, Taste, and the Moral Sense. “I place Taste in the middle,” said Poe, “because it is just this position which in the mind it occupies.” Until someone can refute this admirable explanation, we shall retain the traditional structure. True, we have hinted that there may be another way of looking at it in which the middle world is not simply one of three but a trinity containing them all. But as yet the simpler conception has by no means exhausted its usefulness for us.

同样，我们将诗歌符号描绘成介于事件与观念、例证与准则、仪式与梦境之间的中间体，并最终将其展现为亚里士多德的伦理（ethos），即人性与人类处境，它介于神话（mythos）和精神（dianoia）之间，并由二者构成，而神话和精神分别是对行动和思想的语言模仿。然而，这幅图景还有另一个层面。社会行动与事件的世界，时间与过程的世界，与耳朵有着尤为密切的联系。耳朵聆听，并将所听到的内容转化为实际行为。个体思想与观念的世界也相应地与眼睛密切相关，从古希腊的理论（theoria）开始，我们几乎所有表达思想的方式都与视觉隐喻相连。此外，不仅艺术整体似乎是事件和观念的核心，文学在某种程度上似乎也是艺术的核心。文学诉诸听觉，因此具有音乐的本质，但音乐是一种更为集中于听觉和对时间的想象感知的艺术。文学至少诉诸于内在的视觉，因此具有造型艺术的本质，但造型艺术，尤其是绘画，则更为集中于视觉和空间世界。我们注意到，亚里士多德列出了诗歌的六个要素，其中三个——神话（mythos）、伦理（ethos）和精神（dianoia） ——我们已经探讨过。另外三个要素——旋律（ melos）、词汇（lexis）和视觉（ opsis，即场景）——则涉及同一图表的第二个方面。作为一种语言结构，文学的词汇结合了另外两个要素：旋律（melos），一个类似于音乐或与之相关的要素；以及视觉（opsis），它与造型艺术有着类似的联系。当我们将“lexis”理解为耳朵捕捉到的一系列叙事性声音时，它可以被翻译为“措辞”；而当我们将其理解为在精神“视觉”活动中同时形成的意义模式时，它可以被翻译为“意象”。接下来，我们将探讨文学的第二个方面，即修辞层面。这一层面将我们带回叙事和意义的“字面”层面，这正是埃兹拉·庞德在谈到诗歌创作的三种特质——旋律创作（melopoeia）、语调创作（logopoeia）和意象创作（phanopoeia）时所指的语境。在文学批评中，“音乐性”和“图像性”这两个术语经常被用作比喻，我们将尝试考察它们作为批评术语的真正意义究竟有多大。

Similarly, we have portrayed the poetic symbol as intermediate between event and idea, example and precept, ritual and dream, and have finally displayed it as Aristotle’s ethos, human nature and the human situation, between and made up of mythos and dianoia, which are verbal imitations of action and thought respectively. There is however still another aspect of the same diagram. The world of social action and event, the world of time and process, has a particularly close association with the ear. The ear listens, and the ear translates what it hears into practical conduct. The world of individual thought and idea has a correspondingly close association with the eye, and nearly all our expressions for thought, from the Greek theoria down, are connected with visual metaphors. Further, not only does art as a whole seem to be central to events and ideas, but literature seems in a way to be central to the arts. It appeals to the ear, and so partakes of the nature of music, but music is a much more concentrated art of the ear and of the imaginative perception of time. Literature appeals to at least the inner eye, and so partakes of the nature of the plastic arts, but the plastic arts, especially painting, are much more concentrated on the eye and on the spatial world. We notice that Aristotle gives a list of six elements of poetry, three of which, mythos, ethos and dianoia, we have been considering. The other three, melos, lexis, and opsis (spectacle), deal with this second aspect of the same diagram. Considered as a verbal structure, literature presents a lexis which combines two other elements: melos, an element analogous to or otherwise connected with music, and opsis, which has a similar connection with the plastic arts. The word lexis itself may be translated “diction” when we are thinking of it as a narrative sequence of sounds caught by the ear, and as “imagery” when we are thinking of it as forming a simultaneous pattern of meaning apprehended in an act of mental “vision.” This second or rhetorical aspect of literature we must now turn to examine. It is an aspect which returns us to the “literal” level of narrative and meaning, the context that Ezra Pound has in mind when he speaks of the three qualities of poetic creation as melopoeia, logopoeia, and phanopoeia. The terms musical and pictorial are often employed figuratively in literary criticism, and we shall attempt among other things to see how much genuine sense they make as critical terms.

“修辞学”一词让我们联想到另一个三元组：传统上，基于词语的研究被划分为语法、修辞和逻辑这“三艺”。虽然语法和逻辑已成为具体学科的名称，但它们仍然与所有语言结构的叙事和意义方面保持着某种更普遍的联系。语法可以被称为排列词语的艺术，因此在某种意义上——字面意义上——语法和叙事是同一回事；逻辑可以被称为产生意义的艺术，因此在某种意义上逻辑和意义是同一回事。这句话的后半部分更为传统，因此也更为人熟知。而前半部分则没有历史依据，因为构建叙事的艺术（例如“构思”、“布局”等）历来都是修辞学的一部分。然而，尽管历史纷争不断，我们不妨先从叙事与语法之间的联系入手。这里的语法主要理解为句法，即使词语按正确的（叙事）顺序排列；而逻辑也同样重要。意义和逻辑主要被理解为词语按照特定模式排列并具有特定含义。语法是语言结构的语言学方面；逻辑是“意义”，它是翻译中永恒的共同因素。

The word “rhetoric” reminds us of yet another triad: the traditional division of studies based on words into a “trivium” of grammar, rhetoric, and logic. While grammar and logic have become the names of specific sciences, they also retain something of a more general connection with the narrative and significant aspects respectively of all verbal structures. As grammar may be called the art of ordering words, there is a sense—a literal sense—in which grammar and narrative are the same thing; as logic may be called the art of producing meaning, there is a sense in which logic and meaning are the same thing. The second part of this sentence is more traditional, and hence more familiar. There is no historical justification for the first part, as the art of constructing narrative (“invention,” “disposition,” and the like) has traditionally formed a part of rhetoric. Let us, however, in spite of history, begin with an association between narrative and grammar, grammar being understood primarily as syntax or getting words in the right (narrative) order, and between logic and meaning, logic being understood primarily as words arranged in a pattern with significance. Grammar is the linguistic aspect of a verbal structure; logic is the “sense” which is the permanent common factor in translation.

我们所说的陈述性、描述性或事实性写作，往往是语法与逻辑的直接结合，或者说力图实现这种结合。一个论证若非语言正确，即用词恰当、句法关系合理，则其逻辑必然正确。同样，一段叙述若非具有连贯的意义，也无法向读者传达任何信息。因此，在陈述性写作中，修辞这种中间概念似乎几乎没有立足之地。事实上，我们常常发现，在哲学家、科学家、法学家、评论家、历史学家和神学家中，修辞往往受到某种程度的质疑和不信任。

What we have been calling assertive, descriptive, or factual writing tends to be, or attempts to be, a direct union of grammar and logic. An argument cannot be logically correct unless it is verbally correct, the right words chosen and the proper syntactical relations among them established. Nor does a verbal narrative communicate anything to a reader unless it has continuous significance. In assertive writing, therefore, there seems to be little place for any such middle term as rhetoric, and in fact we often find that among philosophers, scientists, jurists, critics, historians, and theologians, rhetoric is looked upon with some distrust.

修辞自始便包含两层含义：装饰性言辞和说服性言辞。这两者在心理上似乎截然相反，因为装饰的欲望本质上是无私的，而说服的欲望则恰恰相反。事实上，装饰性修辞与文学本身密不可分，或者说，它与我们所说的为自身而存在的假想语言结构密不可分。说服性修辞则是应用文学，即运用文学艺术来增强论证的力量。装饰性修辞对听众的作用是静态的，引导他们欣赏自身的优美或机智；而说服性修辞则试图引导他们采取某种行动。前者表达情感，后者则操纵情感。无论我们如何最终确定演说的文学地位，装饰性修辞无疑是诗歌的词汇或语言结构。亚里士多德在《诗学》中论述词汇时指出，词汇更应归入修辞学的范畴。因此，我们可以提出以下假设：如果语法与逻辑的直接结合是非文学语言结构的特征，那么文学就可以被描述为语法与逻辑的修辞组织。文学形式的大多数特征，例如韵律、头韵、格律、对立平衡、例证的使用等，也都是修辞模式。

Rhetoric has from the beginning meant two things: ornamental speech and persuasive speech. These two things seem psychologically opposed to each other, as the desire to ornament is essentially disinterested, and the desire to persuade essentially the reverse. In fact ornamental rhetoric is inseparable from literature itself, or what we have called the hypothetical verbal structure which exists for its own sake. Persuasive rhetoric is applied literature, or the use of literary art to reinforce the power of argument. Ornamental rhetoric acts on its hearers statically, leading them to admire its own beauty or wit; persuasive rhetoric tries to lead them kinetically toward a course of action. One articulates emotion; the other manipulates it. And whatever we decide about the ultimate literary status of oratory, there seems little doubt that ornamental rhetoric is the lexis or verbal texture of poetry. Aristotle remarks, when he comes to lexis in the Poetics, that that subject belongs more properly to rhetoric. We may, then, adopt the following tentative postulate: that if the direct union of grammar and logic is characteristic of non-literary verbal structures, literature may be described as the rhetorical organization of grammar and logic. Most of the features characteristic of literary form, such as rhyme, alliteration, metre, antithetical balance, the use of exempla, are also rhetorical schemata.

创作的心理并非我们探讨的主题，但作家在毫无创作意图的情况下开始写作的情况应该极为罕见。因此，在诗人的脑海中，存在着某种控制和协调的力量，柯勒律治称之为……“主动性”很早就确立自身，逐渐将一切纳入其中，最终显露出其作为作品承载形式的作用。这种主动性显然并非一个单一的整体，而是由诸多因素构成的复杂体系。主题便是其中之一；营造出某种意象恰当而另一些则不恰当的情绪统一感是另一个因素。如果最终呈现的是一首格律规整的诗，那么格律便是第三个因素；否则，就会存在某种其他的整合节奏。我们之前也提到过，诗人创作诗歌的意图通常包含体裁，即创作某种特定语言结构的意图。因此，诗人不断地决定某些事物——无论这些事物能否被他自己从批判的角度加以解释——是否应该属于他的作品结构，以及他在修改过程中删减的内容是否应该属于他的作品结构，即使这些内容本身可能足够优秀，可以归入其他位置。但由于作品结构本身是复杂的，因此这些决定也与各种诗歌元素或一系列主动性相关。在前一篇文章中，我们重点讨论了其中的主题和意象的选择；这里我们关注的是体裁和融合的节奏。

The psychology of creation is not our theme, but it must happen very rarely that a writer sits down to write without any notion of what he proposes to produce. In the poet’s mind, then, some kind of controlling and coordinating power, what Coleridge called the “initiative,” establishes itself very early, gradually assimilates everything to itself, and finally reveals itself to be the containing form of the work. This initiative is clearly not a unit but a complex of factors. The theme is one such factor; the sense of the unity of mood which makes certain images appropriate and others not is another. If what is produced is to be a poem in a regular metre, the metre will be a third: if not, some other integrating rhythm will be present. We remarked earlier, too, that the poet’s intention to produce a poem normally includes the genre, the intention of producing a specific kind of verbal structure. The poet thus is incessantly deciding that certain things, whether they can be critically accounted for by himself or not, belong in his structure, and that what he cuts out in revising does not, though it may be good enough in itself to belong somewhere else. But as the structure is complex, so these decisions relate to a variety of poetic elements, or a group of initiatives. Of these, theme and the choice of images engaged our attention in the previous essay; genre and the integrating rhythm concern us here.

我们在引言中抱怨说，体裁理论在批评领域尚不成熟。我们有戏剧、史诗和抒情诗这三个源自古希腊的体裁术语，但后两者主要被用作行话或行业俚语，分别指长诗和短诗（或更短的诗）。中等长度的诗歌甚至没有一个专门的术语来描述它，而任何长诗都会被称作史诗，尤其是像勃朗宁的《指环与书》那样被分成十几个部分的诗歌。这首诗采用了戏剧结构，讲述了一个嫉妒的丈夫、忍耐的妻子和英勇的情人卷入一场谋杀案审判的三角关系，其中包含法庭和死刑室的场景，并通过人物的独白来展开整个故事。这是一部令人叹为观止的杰作，但只有当我们把它看作是戏剧体裁的一次实验，一种颠覆传统的戏剧时，才能真正理解它的价值所在。同样，我们称雪莱的《西风颂》为抒情诗，或许是因为它本身就是一首抒情诗；如果我们犹豫是否要称《爱之颂》为抒情诗，也完全不清楚它究竟是什么，我们总可以称其为一位本质上具有抒情天赋的天才的杰作。它比《伊利亚特》短，而且是有结尾的。

We complained in our introduction that the theory of genres was an undeveloped subject in criticism. We have the three generic terms drama, epic, and lyric, derived from the Greeks, but we use the latter two chiefly as jargon or trade slang for long and short (or shorter) poems respectively. The middle-sized poem does not even have a jargon term to describe it, and any long poem gets to be called an epic, especially if it is divided into a dozen or so parts, like Browning’s Ring and the Book. This poem takes a dramatic structure, a triangle of jealous husband, patient wife, and chivalrous lover involved in a murder trial with courtroom and death-house scenes, and works it all out through the soliloquies of the characters. It is an astounding tour de force, but we can fully appreciate this only when we see it as a generic experiment in drama, a drama turned inside out, as it were. Similarly, we call Shelley’s Ode to the West Wind a lyric, perhaps because it is a lyric; if we hesitate to call Epipsychidion a lyric, and have no idea what it is, we can always call it the product of an essentially lyrical genius. It is shorter than the Iliad, and there’s an end of it.

然而，“戏剧”、“史诗”和“抒情诗”这几个词的词源表明，体裁的核心原则其实很简单。文学体裁区分的基础似乎在于表现方式的根本差异。文字可以表演给观众看；可以朗诵给听众听；可以歌唱或吟诵；也可以写成文字供读者阅读。我们无奈地顺便提一下，批评中并没有一个词来指代作者的读者群体中的个体成员，而“读者”一词本身也并非涵盖所有文体，因为将一本书的读者称为“读者”略显不合逻辑。无论如何，文体批评的基础是修辞性的，因为文体是由诗人与其读者之间建立的条件决定的。

However, the origin of the words drama, epic, and lyric suggests that the central principle of genre is simple enough. The basis of generic distinctions in literature appears to be the radical of presentation. Words may be acted in front of a spectator; they may be spoken in front of a listener; they may be sung or chanted; or they may be written for a reader. Criticism, we note resignedly in passing, has no word for the individual member of an author’s audience, and the word “audience” itself does not really cover all genres, as it is slightly illogical to describe the readers of a book as an audience. The basis of generic criticism in any case is rhetorical, in the sense that the genre is determined by the conditions established between the poet and his public.

在印刷时代，如果表演、口语和书面语言之间的区别要具有任何意义，我们就必须探讨呈现方式的根本性变化。人们可以印刷抒情诗或朗读小说，但这些偶然的变化本身并不足以改变其体裁。尽管莎士比亚戏剧的印刷文本得到了应有的精心呵护，但它们本质上仍然是表演剧本，属于戏剧体裁。如果一位浪漫主义诗人赋予他的诗歌戏剧形式，他可能并不期待甚至想要任何舞台演出；他可能完全从印刷和读者的角度思考；他甚至可能像许多浪漫主义者一样，认为舞台戏剧是一种不纯粹的形式，因为它限制了个人表达。然而，这首诗仍然与某种戏剧形式相关联，无论这种关联多么虚幻。小说被创作出来，但当康拉德运用叙述者来帮助他讲述故事时，书面语言的体裁就被同化为口语的体裁。

We have to speak of the radical of presentation if the distinctions of acted, spoken, and written word are to mean anything in the age of the printing press. One may print a lyric or read a novel aloud, but such incidental changes are not enough in themselves to alter the genre. For all the loving care that is rightfully expended on the printed texts of Shakespeare’s plays, they are still radically acting scripts, and belong to the genre of drama. If a Romantic poet gives his poem a dramatic form, he may not expect or even want any stage representation; he may think entirely in terms of print and readers; he may even believe, like many Romantics, that the stage drama is an impure form because of the limitations it puts on individual expression. Yet the poem is still being referred back to some kind of theatre, however much of a castle in the air. A novel is written, but when Conrad employs a narrator to help him tell his story, the genre of the written word is being assimilated to that of the spoken one.

如何对这类小说进行分类，远不如认识到其中存在两种截然不同的呈现方式这一事实重要。或许用更简洁的说法——无论实际情况如何——来代替“呈现方式”这一术语，更恰当的表述是文学作品理想的呈现方式之一。但例如，弥尔顿在创作《失乐园》时，似乎并没有预设朗诵者和听众的理想形象；他似乎满足于将其作为一首诗，以书籍的形式呈现。当他运用祈祷的惯例，将诗歌纳入口语体裁时，这一惯例的意义在于表明他的作品主要属于哪个传统，以及它与哪些传统最为密切相关。体裁批评的目的与其说是分类，不如说是阐明这些传统和关联，从而揭示大量文学关系。只要没有为其建立背景，就不会有人注意到它们。

The question of how we are to classify such a novel is less important than the recognition of the fact that two different radicals of presentation exist in it. It might be thought simpler, instead of using the term radical, to say that the generic distinctions are among the ways in which literary works are ideally presented, whatever the actualities are. But Milton, for example, seems to have no ideal of reciter and audience in mind for Paradise Lost; he seems content to leave it, in practice, a poem to be read in a book. When he uses the convention of invocation, thus bringing the poem into the genre of the spoken word, the significance of the convention is to indicate what tradition his work primarily belongs to and what its closest affinities are with. The purpose of criticism by genres is not so much to classify as to clarify such traditions and affinities, thereby bringing out a large number of literary relationships that would not be noticed as long as there were no context established for them.

口语体裁及其听众很难用英语准确描述，但其中一部分与希腊语中的“ ta epe”一词含义相符，指的是旨在朗诵的诗歌，并非一定是传统意义上篇幅巨大的史诗。这类“史诗”题材并非必须采用韵律，因为散文故事和散文演说也是重要的口语形式。韵律与散文之间的区别显然并非体裁上的差异，戏剧的例子便可证明这一点，尽管它们往往会演变成体裁上的差异。在本文中，我使用“epos”一词来描述以口头表达为根本呈现方式的作品，而“epic”一词则保留其通常用法，指代《伊利亚特》、《奥德赛》、《埃涅阿斯纪》和《失乐园》等史诗体裁。因此，“epos”涵盖了所有试图保留朗诵和听众这一传统的诗歌或散文文学作品。

The genre of the spoken word and the listener is very difficult to describe in English, but part of it is what the Greeks meant by the phrase ta epe, poems intended to be recited, not necessarily epics of the conventional jumbo size. Such “epic” material does not have to be in metre, as the prose tale and the prose oration are important spoken forms. The difference between metre and prose is evidently not in itself a generic difference, as the example of drama shows, though it tends to become one. In this essay I use the word “epos” to describe works in which the radical of presentation is oral address, keeping the word epic for its customary use as the name of the form of the Iliad, Odyssey, Aeneid, and Paradise Lost. Epos thus takes in all literature, in verse or prose, which makes some attempt to preserve the convention of recitation and a listening audience.

希腊人为我们提供了四种文学体裁中的三种的名称：但他们没有提供一个词来指代通过书籍与读者交流的体裁，而我们自然也没有创造出一个属于我们自己的词。最接近的词是“历史”（history），但尽管有《汤姆·琼斯》这样的电影，这个词早已超越了文学的范畴，而拉丁语中的“经文”（scripture）含义又过于具体。既然我必须选择一个词，我就随意地选择“小说”（fiction）来描述印刷品的体裁。我知道我在第一篇文章中曾在不同的语境下使用过这个词，但似乎与其引入太多新术语增加本书的难度，不如在目前这种混乱的术语体系下做出妥协。音乐中的键盘或许可以类比小说与其他实际存在于书籍中的体裁之间的区别。书籍就像键盘一样，是一种机械装置，它将整个艺术结构置于一个人的诠释控制之下。但是，正如我们可以将真正的钢琴音乐与歌剧或交响乐的钢琴乐谱区分开来一样，我们也可以区分真正的“书籍文学”与包含朗诵或表演作品的简化文本乐谱的书籍。

The Greeks gave us the names of three of our four genres: they did not give us a word for the genre that addresses a reader through a book, and naturally we have not invented one of our own. The nearest to it is “history,” but this word, in spite of Tom Jones, has gone outside literature, and the Latin “scripture” is too specialized in meaning. As I have to have some word, I shall make an arbitrary choice of “fiction” to describe the genre of the printed page. I know that I used this word in the first essay in a different context, but it seems better to compromise with the present confused terminology than to increase the difficulties of this book by introducing too many new terms. The analogy of the keyboard in music may illustrate the difference between fiction and other genres which for practical purposes exist in books. A book, like a keyboard, is a mechanical device for bringing an entire artistic structure under the interpretive control of a single person. But just as it is possible to distinguish genuine piano music from the piano score of an opera or symphony, so we may distinguish genuine “book literature” from books containing the reduced textual scores of recited or acted pieces.

诗人与听众之间的联系，在荷马或乔叟的作品中或许是真实的，但很快便变得越来越理论化，史诗也因此不知不觉地过渡到了虚构。我们甚至可以半开玩笑地提出，弥尔顿笔下运用得炉火纯青的盲吟诗人这一传奇形象，这表明，面向非公开听众的趋势很早就出现了。但当同一素材同时适用于两种体裁时，两种体裁之间的区别便立刻显现出来。主要区别并非简单的篇幅差异，而是在于史诗是片段式的，而小说是连续的。狄更斯的小说作为书籍是小说；作为面向家庭阅读的杂志连载作品，它们本质上仍然是小说，尽管更接近史诗。但当狄更斯开始朗读自己的作品时，体裁就完全转变为史诗；此时，重点转向了在可见听众面前的即时效果。

The connection between a speaking poet and a listening audience, which may be actual in Homer or Chaucer, soon becomes increasingly theoretical, and as it does so epos passes insensibly into fiction. One may even suggest, not quite seriously, that the legendary figure of the blind bard, which is used so effectively by Milton, indicates that the drift toward an unseen audience sets in very early. But whenever the same material does duty for both genres, the distinction between the genres becomes immediately apparent. The chief distinction, though not a simple one of length, is involved with the fact that epos is episodic and fiction continuous. The novels of Dickens are, as books, fiction; as serial publications in a magazine designed for family reading, they are still fundamentally fiction, though closer to epos. But when Dickens began to give readings from his own works, the genre changed wholly to epos; the emphasis was then thrown on immediacy of effect before a visible audience.

在戏剧中，故事中的虚构人物或内部人物直接与观众对话，因此戏剧的特点是作者对观众的隐蔽性。在许多电影等极具视觉冲击力的戏剧中，作者的重要性相对较低。戏剧如同音乐，是为观众而进行的集体表演，音乐和戏剧最有可能在具有强烈社会意识的社会中蓬勃发展，例如伊丽莎白时代的英国。当一个社会变得个人主义和竞争激烈时，例如维多利亚时代的英国，音乐和戏剧也随之衰落，文字几乎垄断了文学。在史诗中，作者直接与读者对话，故事中的虚构人物则被隐藏起来。当作者由吟游诗人或吟游艺人代表时，理论上作者仍然存在，因为后者是以诗人的身份而非诗歌中的角色来朗诵。在书面文学中，作者及其笔下的人物都对读者隐蔽起来。

In drama, the hypothetical or internal characters of the story confront the audience directly, hence the drama is marked by the concealment of the author from his audience. In very spectacular drama, such as we get in many movies, the author is of relatively little importance. Drama, like music, is an ensemble performance for an audience, and music and drama are most likely to flourish in a society with a strong consciousness of itself as a society, like Elizabethan England. When a society becomes individualized and competitive, like Victorian England, music and drama suffer accordingly, and the written word almost monopolizes literature. In epos, the author confronts his audience directly, and the hypothetical characters of his story are concealed. The author is still theoretically there when he is being represented by a rhapsode or minstrel, for the latter speaks as the poet, not as a character in the poem. In written literature both the author and his characters are concealed from the reader.

第四种可能的安排，即诗人对听众的隐瞒，体现在抒情诗中。抒情诗中通常没有专门指代听众的词语：它需要的是一个类似于“合唱队”的概念，但并不暗示同时在场或戏剧性的语境。回到本书开头提到的密尔的格言，抒情诗首先是一种被偷听到的话语。抒情诗人通常假装在自言自语，或者与他人对话：自然之灵、缪斯（注意它与史诗的区别，在史诗中，缪斯通过诗人说话）、私人朋友、爱人、神灵、拟人化的抽象概念，或自然物体。正如斯蒂芬·迪达勒斯在乔伊斯的《青年艺术家画像》中所说，抒情诗是诗人将自身形象呈现出来的：从修辞学的角度来看，它之于史诗，正如祈祷之于布道。呈现的根本在于此。歌词中呈现的是一种在宗教中被称为“我-你”关系的假想形式。诗人仿佛背对着听众，尽管他可能代表他们发声，尽管他们可能在他之后重复他的一些话语。

The fourth possible arrangement, the concealment of the poet’s audience from the poet, is presented in the lyric. There is, as usual, no word for the audience of the lyric: what is wanted is something analogous to “chorus” which does not suggest simultaneous presence or dramatic context. The lyric is, to go back to Mill’s aphorism referred to at the beginning of this book, preeminently the utterance that is overheard. The lyric poet normally pretends to be talking to himself or to someone else: a spirit of nature, a Muse (note the distinction from epos, where the Muse speaks through the poet), a personal friend, a lover, a god, a personified abstraction, or a natural object. The lyric is, as Stephen Dedalus says in Joyce’s Portrait, the poet presenting the image in relation to himself: it is to epos, rhetorically, as prayer is to sermon. The radical of presentation in the lyric is the hypothetical form of what in religion is called the “I-Thou” relationship. The poet, so to speak, turns his back on his listeners, though he may speak for them, and though they may repeat some of his words after him.

史诗和小说构成了文学的核心领域，戏剧和抒情诗分列其两侧。戏剧与仪式有着一种独特的密切联系，而抒情诗则与梦境或幻象，即个体与自身的对话，有着密切的联系。本书开篇我们提到，文学中不存在直接对话，但直接对话是自然的交流方式，文学可以模仿它，就像它可以模仿自然界中的任何其他事物一样。在史诗中，诗人面对着他的读者，我们看到的正是对直接对话的模仿。史诗和小说最初以经文和神话的形式出现，然后是传统故事，接着是叙事诗和说教诗（包括真正的史诗），以及演说散文，最后是小说和其他书面形式。随着我们沿着历史的脉络探索这五种文学模式，小说逐渐超越了史诗，而对直接对话的模仿也随之转变为对自信写作的模仿。反过来，这种做法，加上纪实或说教式的散文，就变成了实际的断言，从而脱离了文学的范畴。

Epos and fiction make up the central area of literature, and are flanked by the drama on one side and by the lyric on the other. Drama has a peculiarly intimate connection with ritual, and lyric with dream or vision, the individual communing with himself. We said at the beginning of this book that there is no such thing as direct address in literature, but direct address is natural communication, and literature may imitate it as it may imitate anything else in nature. In epos, where the poet faces his audience, we have a mimesis of direct address. Epos and fiction first take the form of scripture and myth, then of traditional tales, then of narrative and didactic poetry, including the epic proper, and of oratorical prose, then of novels and other written forms. As we progress historically through the five modes, fiction increasingly overshadows epos, and as it does, the mimesis of direct address changes to a mimesis of assertive writing. This in its turn, with the extremes of documentary or didactic prose, becomes actual assertion, and so passes out of literature.

抒情诗是对声音和意象的内在模仿，与戏剧这种对声音和意象的外在模仿（或称外在表现）截然相反。这两种形式都避免了直接对话的模仿。戏剧中的人物彼此交谈，理论上，他们在旁白或独白中也是在自言自语。即使他们意识到有观众，他们也不是在替诗人说话，除非在一些特殊情况下，例如古希腊喜剧的旁白或洛可可戏剧的序幕和尾声，这些情况下确实发生了从戏剧到史诗的体裁转变。在萧伯纳的作品中，喜剧的旁白从剧作中间移到了单独的散文序言中，这标志着从戏剧到小说的转变。

The lyric is an internal mimesis of sound and imagery, and stands opposite the external mimesis, or outward representation of sound and imagery, which is drama. Both forms avoid the mimesis of direct address. The characters in a play talk to each other, and are theoretically talking to themselves in an aside or soliloquy. Even if they are conscious of an audience, they are not speaking for the poet, except in special cases like the parabasis of Old Comedy or the prologues and epilogues of the rococo theatre, where there is an actual generic change from drama to epos. In Bernard Shaw the comic parabasis is transferred from the middle of the play to a separate prose preface, which is a change from drama to fiction.

史诗中往往以某种相对规整的韵律为主：即使是演说散文，无论在句法还是标点上，也展现出许多韵律特征。小说中则往往以散文为主，因为只有散文才具有适合小说这种连续形式的连贯节奏。戏剧没有其特有的节奏，但早期戏剧与史诗最为接近，后期戏剧则与小说最为接近。抒情诗则往往以一种诗意的节奏为主，这种节奏未必符合韵律。接下来，我们将逐一考察每种文体，以探究其主要特征。由于接下来的内容主要关注措辞和语言要素，因此我们必须将考察范围限定于一种特定语言，即英语：这意味着我们所说的很多内容仅适用于英语，但我们希望其主要原则也能适用于其他语言。

In epos some kind of comparatively regular metre tends to predominate: even oratorical prose shows many metrical features, both in its syntax and in its punctuation. In fiction prose tends to predominate, because only prose has the continuous rhythm appropriate for the continuous form of the book. Drama has no controlling rhythm peculiar to itself, but it is most closely related to epos in the earlier modes and to fiction in the later ones. In the lyric a rhythm which is poetic but not necessarily metrical tends to predominate. We proceed to examine each genre in turn with a view to discovering what its chief features are. As in what immediately follows we are largely concerned with diction and linguistic elements, we must limit our survey mainly to a specific language, which will be English: this means that a good deal of what we say will be true only of English, but it is hoped that the main principles can be adapted to other languages as well.

循环的节奏：EPOS

THE RHYTHM OF RECURRENCE: EPOS

传统上，诗歌与散文的区别在于其规律的韵律，这种韵律往往成为史诗或长篇演说体作品的组织节奏。韵律是重复的一种体现，而表示重复的两个词——节奏和模式——表明，无论其主要影响是时间上的还是空间上的，重复都是所有艺术的结构原则。除了韵律本身，数量和重音（或重读）也是诗歌重复的要素，尽管在现代英语中，数量并非规律性重复的要素，除非是在诗人必须即兴创作、自行制定规则的实验性作品中。重音或重读与韵律的关系，或许需要一种不同于通常解释的方式来阐述。

The regular pulsating metre that traditionally distinguishes verse from prose tends to become the organizing rhythm in epos or extended oratorical forms. Metre is an aspect of recurrence, and the two words for recurrence, rhythm and pattern, show that recurrence is a structural principle of all art, whether temporal or spatial in its primary impact. Besides metre itself, quantity and accent (or stress) are elements in poetic recurrence, though quantity is not an element of regular recurrence in modern English, except in experiments in which the poet has to make up his own rules as he goes along. The relation of accent or stress to metre needs, perhaps, a different kind of explanation from what is usually given it.

四音步诗行似乎是英语语言结构中固有的组成部分。它是早期诗歌的主流节奏，尽管在中世纪英语中，它的韵律模式从头韵转变为押韵；它是各个时期通俗诗歌、民谣和大多数童谣的常见节奏。在民谣中，八六八六四音步诗节是连续的四音步诗行，每隔一行末尾有一个“休止符”。这种休止符的原则，或者说在实际的静默点上出现一个音节，在古英语中就已经确立。抑扬格五音步提供了一个切分音的领域，在这个领域中，重音和韵律可以在某种程度上相互抵消。如果我们“自然地”阅读许多抑扬格五音步诗，像在英语口语中那样，给重要的词语赋予重音，那么古老的四音步诗行就会在其韵律背景下清晰地凸显出来。因此：

A four-stress line seems to be inherent in the structure of the English language. It is the prevailing rhythm of the earlier poetry, though it changes its scheme from alliteration to rhyme in Middle English; it is the common rhythm of popular poetry in all periods, of ballads and of most nursery rhymes. In the ballad, the eight-six-eight-six quatrain is a continuous four-beat line, with a “rest” at the end of every other line. This principle of the rest, or a beat coming at a point of actual silence, was already established in Old English. The iambic pentameter provides a field of syncopation in which stress and metre can to some extent neutralize one another. If we read many iambic pentameters “naturally,” giving the important words the heavy accent that they do have in spoken English, the old four-stress line stands out in clear relief against its metrical background. Thus:

成为还是不成为：这就是问题。

To bé, or nót to be: thát is the quéstion.

或许，在精神层面上，忍受痛苦才是更高尚的。

Whether ’tis nóbler in the mind to súffer

命运的无情打击和伤痛，

The slíngs and árrows of outrágeous fórtune,

或者拿起武器来应对纷繁的麻烦……

Or táke up árms against a séa of tróubles …

人类的第一次不服从，以及果实

Of mán’s fírst disobédience, and the frúit

那棵禁树，其凡人的味道

Of that forbídden trée, whose mórtal táste

给世界带来了死亡和我们所有的不幸，

Brought déath into the wórld and áll our wóe,

失去伊甸园，直到一个更大的曼

With lóss of Éden, till one gréater Mán

恢复我们的状态，重新坐上幸福的座位……

Restóre us, and regáin the blissful séat …

正如我们所预料的那样，德莱顿和蒲柏的停顿双行诗中五重音诗行的比例较高，但任何节奏上的自由发挥，例如女性化的停顿，都可能使旧节奏恢复原状：

The stopped couplet of Dryden and Pope, as we should expect, has a higher percentage of five-stress lines, but any rhythmical license such as a feminine caesura is likely to bring back the old beat:

忘记他们的仇恨，并同意恐惧。 （沃勒）

Forgét their hátred, and consént to féar.    (Waller)

Nor héll a fúry, like a wóman scórn'd. (Congreve)

Nor héll a fúry, like a wóman scórn’d.   (Congreve)

浅尝辄止是件危险的事。（教皇）

A líttle leárning is a dángerous thíng.   (Pope)

任何韵律不确定或过渡时期都会凸显四音步诗行的固有优势。乔叟去世后，随着中古英语向现代英语的转变，我们发现自己置身于利德盖特奇特的韵律世界，我们很可能会将吟游诗人在《死亡之舞》中对死神所说的话套用到利德盖特本人身上：

Any period of metrical uncertainty or transition will illustrate the native strength of the four-stress line. After the death of Chaucer and the change from middle to modern English, we find ourselves in the strange metrical world of Lydgate, in which we are strongly tempted to apply to Lydgate himself what the Minstrel says to Death in the Danse Macabre:

这支新舞对我来说太奇怪了

This newe daunce / is to me so straunge

Wonder dyverse / 和 passyngli 相反

Wonder dyverse / and passyngli contrarie

可怕的fotynge / 经常变化

The dredful fotynge / doth so ofte chaunge

而且测量结果/因此经常变化。

And the mesures / so ofte sithes varie.

但即便如此，其中仍然蕴含着一种舞蹈：让我们来看看前一节，死神对吟游诗人的讲话：

But there is a dance there all the same: let us look at the preceding stanza, Death’s speech to the Minstrel:

如果我们试图将这节诗分析成乔叟ABC诗节那样的五音步诗节，就会遇到麻烦：例如，最后一行根本不是五音步。如果把它当作连续的四音步诗行来读，就相当简单了；这样的读法会展现出韵律分析永远无法展现的东西——死神那怪诞的、骷髅跳跃般的轻快语调，最终以最后一行克制的讽刺结尾。我并不声称了解利德盖特的韵律细节，比如他可能更倾向于发音或省略哪些e，或者他可能对哪些外来词的重音处理不同。或许利德盖特本人和十五世纪的读者也并非完全清楚所有这些细节；但是，一行诗有四个主要重音，重音之间音节数可变，显然是解决这类问题的巧妙方法，因为很多细节都可以留给读者自行选择。总之，我并不是在指出这段文字应该如何阅读，而是在指出如何最容易地进行扫描：就像韵律分析一样，每个读者都会对模式进行自己的修改。

This stanza will give us a bad time if we try to analyze it as a pentameter stanza of Chaucer’s ABC type: the last line, for instance, is not a pentameter at all. Read as a continuous four-beat line, it is fairly simple; and such a reading will bring out what the prosodic analysis could never do, the grotesque, leaping-skeleton lilt of the voice of Death ending in the measured irony of the last line. I do not claim to know the details of Lydgate’s prosody, what e’s he might have preferred to pronounce or elide or what foreign words he might have accented differently. It is possible that neither Lydgate nor the fifteenth-century reader was entirely clear on all such points either; but a line with four main stresses and a variable number of syllables between the stresses is the obvious device for getting over such problems, as a good deal can be left to the individual reader’s choice. In any case I am not indicating how the passage is to be read so much as how it may most easily be scanned: as with metrical scansion, every reader will make his own modification of the pattern.

“骷髅”线通常也是四拍线：菲利普·斯帕罗的欢快前奏曲是一种快速进行曲节奏，休止符更多，重音节拍也更密集，这与我们在利德盖特发现的节奏不同：

The “Skeltonic” line is also usually a four-beat line: the spirited prelude to Philip Sparowe is a quick-march rhythm, with more rests and more accented beats coming close together than we found in Lydgate:

简而言之，柯勒律治创作《克里斯特贝尔》所依据的“新原则”与文学中通常的原则一样新颖。同样显而易见的是，《海华沙之歌》的芬兰灵感来源也并不比通常的此类灵感来源更具异域风情。《海华沙之歌》的韵律模式与英语的四音步模式非常契合，这或许可以解释为什么它是英语中最容易被戏仿的诗歌之一。梅瑞狄斯的《山谷之恋》也同样很容易被解读为四音步诗行，其节奏构成与利德盖特的诗歌非常相似：

In short, the “new principle” on which Coleridge constructed Christabel was about as new as principles usually are in literature. It is clear too that the Finnish inspiration of Hiawatha was no more fundamentally exotic than such inspirations usually are. Hiawatha fits the four-stress pattern of English very snugly, which explains perhaps why it is one of the easiest poems in the language to parody. Meredith’s Love in the Valley, also, is most easily scanned as a four-stress line very similar in its rhythmical make-up to Lydgate’s:

这些例子或许已经开始阐明“音乐性”（亚里士多德的“ melos ”）一词在现代文学批评中的真正含义。自利德盖特时代以来，与英国诗歌同时期的音乐几乎都带有重音，重音标记着节奏单位（小节），每个小节内允许出现数量不定的音符。当诗歌中存在一个主要的重音，且两个重音之间音节数量不定（通常每行四个重音，对应于音乐中的“四拍子”）时，我们就得到了音乐性诗歌，即结构与同时期音乐相似的诗歌。我们现在讨论的是史诗或采用连续韵律的长篇诗歌：与此类诗歌最接近的音乐形式是其更为宏大的器乐作品，其中的节奏更多地源自舞蹈而非歌曲。

These examples have, perhaps, begun to illustrate already something of what the word “musical,” Aristotle’s melos, really means as a term in modern literary criticism. In the music contemporary with English poetry since Lydgate’s time, we have had almost uniformly a stress accent, the stresses marking rhythmical units (measures) within which a variable number of notes is permitted. When in poetry we have a predominating stress accent and a variable number of syllables between two stresses (usually four stresses to a line, corresponding to “common time” in music), we have musical poetry, that is, poetry which resembles in its structure the music contemporary with it. We are speaking now of epos or extended poetry in a continuous metre: the music most closely analogous to such poetry is music in its more extended instrumental forms, in which the organizing rhythm has descended more directly from dance than from song.

“音乐性”一词的这种技术性用法，与那种只要诗歌听起来悦耳动听就称之为“音乐性”的感伤主义用法截然不同。实际上，技术性用法和感伤主义用法往往截然相反，例如，感伤主义的“音乐性”一词会用来形容丁尼生，而不会用来形容勃朗宁。然而，如果我们提出一个外部但相关的问题：这两位诗人中，谁更懂音乐，谁更容易受到音乐的影响？答案显然不是丁尼生。以下是丁尼生《俄诺涅》中的一段节选。

This technical use of the word musical is very different from the sentimental fashion of calling any poetry musical if it sounds nice. In practice the technical and the sentimental uses are often directly opposed, as the sentimental term would be applied to, for example, Tennyson, and withdrawn from, for example, Browning. Yet if we ask the external but relevant question: Which of these two poets knew more about music, and was a priori more likely to be influenced by it? the answer is certainly not Tennyson. Here is a passage from Tennyson’s Oenone·.

   哦，伊达母亲，拥有众多泉源的伊达，

   O mother Ida, many-fountain’d Ida,

亲爱的母亲艾达，在我临终前请听我说。

Dear mother Ida, harken ere I die.

我在晨曦初露的山丘下等待着，

I waited underneath the dawning hills,

山坡上的草坪在露水中泛着暗色，

Aloft the mountain lawn was dewy-dark,

山松之上，露水朦胧，一片幽暗：

And dewy dark aloft the mountain pine:

美丽的巴黎，邪恶的巴黎，

Beautiful Paris, evil-hearted Paris,

领头的是一只通体漆黑、白角白蹄的山羊，

Leading a jet-black goat white-horn’d, white-hooved,

他独自一人从芦苇丛生的西莫伊斯山上走下来。

Came up from reedy Simois all alone.

以下摘自勃朗宁的《公爵夫人的逃亡》：

And here is a passage from Browning’s The Flight of the Duchess:

我可以给你一些小小的恩惠

I could favour you with sundry touches

公爵夫人身上沾染的颜料污渍

Of the paint-smutches with which the Duchess

加深了她脸颊泛黄的柔和感

Heightened the mellowness of her cheek’s yellowness

（为了加快速度）直到最后她

(To get on faster) until at last her

脸颊逐渐成为一位大师级的石膏匠

Cheek grew to be one master-plaster

仅使用白垩粉即可产生粘液和墨角藻：

Of mucus and fucus from mere use of ceruse:

简而言之，她从头皮长到了乳房。

In short, she grew from scalp to udder

这东西简直让人不寒而栗。

Just the object to make you shudder.

在勃朗宁的段落中，速度是一个积极因素：它给人一种节拍器般的节奏感。丁尼生则试图弱化这种律动感；他的段落应该慢读，并着重体会元音的韵律。两段文字都明显地重复了某些音节，但丁尼生的重复是为了减缓思想的推进速度，迫使节奏回归自身，并细化其本质上的声音模式。在勃朗宁的诗歌中，韵脚强化了节奏的重音，并有助于构建一种累积的节奏。勃朗宁诗歌中的速度和鲜明的重音是其音乐特征，除了音乐提示（ più mosso的英文翻译）之外，很难看出括号中的文字还能作何解释。

In the Browning passage speed is a positive factor: one has the sense of a metronome beat. Tennyson has tried to minimize the sense of movement; his passage should be read slowly and with much dwelling on the vowels. Both passages repeat sounds obtrusively, but the repetitions in Tennyson are there to slow down the advance of ideas, to compel the rhythm to return on itself, and to elaborate what is essentially a pattern of sound. In Browning the rhymes sharpen the accentuation of the beat and help to build up a cumulative rhythm. The speed and the sharp accent in Browning’s poetry are musical features in it, and it is difficult to see what the words in parentheses can be except a musical direction, an English translation of più mosso.

诸如“流畅的音乐性”或“生硬不和谐的措辞”之类的短语属于“音乐性”一词的感伤用法，或许源于“和谐”一词在日常英语中，除了音乐之外，还指一种稳定而持久的关系。在这种比喻意义上，“和谐”一词并非一系列和谐音的序列，而是一系列不和谐音最终汇聚成和谐音的序列，音乐中唯一稳定持久的“和谐”是最终解决的主和弦。更有可能的是，那些生硬、粗犷、不和谐的诗歌（当然，前提是诗人具备一定的技巧）才能在诗歌中展现出音乐般的张力和强劲的冲击力。当我们发现元音和辅音的精心平衡以及梦幻般感性的音韵流动时，我们很可能是在面对一位缺乏音乐性的诗人。蒲柏、济慈和丁尼生都是缺乏音乐性的诗人。我几乎无需赘述，这个词并非贬义：《夺发记》缺乏音乐性，正如它是无韵诗的拙劣范例一样，因为它完全是另一种东西。当我们发现尖锐刺耳的重音、生硬晦涩的语言、大量的辅音以及冗长笨拙的多音节时，我们很可能是在面对一种“旋律诗”（ melos），或者说，一种与音乐有相似之处，甚至直接受到音乐影响的诗歌。

Such phrases as “smooth musical flow” or “harsh unmusical diction” belong to the sentimental use of the word musical, and are perhaps derived from the fact that the word “harmony” in ordinary English, apart from music, means a stable and permanent relationship. In this figurative sense of the word harmony, music is not a sequence of harmonies at all, but a sequence of discords ending in a harmony, the only stable and permanent “harmony” in music being the final resolving tonic chord. It is more likely to be the harsh, rugged, dissonant poem (assuming of course some technical competence in the poet) that will show in poetry the tension and the driving accented impetus of music.
