When we find a careful balancing of vowels and consonants and a dreamy sensuous flow of sound, we are probably dealing with an unmusical poet. Pope, Keats, and Tennyson are all unmusical. This term, I need hardly observe, is not pejorative: The Rape of the Lock is unmusical, just as it is a bad example of blank verse, because it is something else altogether. When we find sharp barking accents, crabbed and obscure language, mouthfuls of consonants, and long lumbering polysyllables, we are probably dealing with melos, or poetry which shows an analogy to music, if not an actual influence from it.

这种音乐语言更适合用来形容怪诞和恐怖的事物。或者用于谩骂和辱骂。它与所谓“形而上学”类型的古怪知识分子格格不入。它的韵律不规则（因为重音的切分音），大量运用跨行，并采用一种长而累积的节奏，将诗行向上推进，形成更大的节奏单元，例如段落。莎士比亚在其作品中越来越多地使用旋律诗体，这一事实是人们根据其作品内部证据来判断其创作年代的依据。当弥尔顿说押韵的英雄诗“没有真正的音乐性”，因为音乐诗必须“将意义从一节诗句巧妙地延伸到另一节诗句”时，他使用的是“音乐性”一词的字面含义。当塞缪尔·约翰逊谈到“将意义笨拙地从一节诗句延续到另一节诗句的旧方法”时，他是在表达他一贯的反音乐性观点。《异教徒的悲剧》是一首音乐诗；《提尔西斯》不是。《快乐的乞丐》是；《希腊古瓮颂》并非如此。蒲柏的《弥赛亚》不具音乐性，但斯马特的《大卫之歌》凭借其铿锵有力的主题词和尾声的强音爆发，堪称音乐上的杰作。克拉肖的赞美诗和考利的品达诗作具有音乐性，它们流畅多变、以四重音为主的诗行以及连贯的跨行；赫伯特的诗节和格雷的品达诗作则不具音乐性。斯凯尔顿、怀亚特和邓巴的作品具有音乐性；加文·道格拉斯和萨里的作品则不具音乐性。头韵诗通常具有重音和音乐性；而复杂的诗节形式通常不具备这些特点。当然，诗歌中运用旋律并不一定意味着诗人具备任何音乐方面的专业知识，但这种知识往往与之相伴而生。克拉肖的《音乐决斗》（一首巴洛克咏叹调，配有器乐伴奏）就是这样一首技术上非常注重音乐性的诗歌。

The musical diction is better fitted for the grotesque and horrible, or for invective and abuse. It is congenial to a gnarled intellectualism of the so-called “metaphysical” type. It is irregular in metre (because of the syncopation against stress), leans heavily on enjambement, and employs a long cumulative rhythm sweeping the lines up into larger rhythmical units such as the paragraph. The fact that Shakespeare shows an increasing use of melos as he goes on is the principle employed for dating his plays on internal evidence. When Milton says that rhymed heroic verse is “of no true musical delight,” because musical poetry must have “the sense variously drawn out from one verse into another,” he is using the word musical in its technical sense. When Samuel Johnson speaks of “the old manner of continuing the sense ungracefully from verse to verse,” he is speaking from his own consistently anti-musical point of view. The Heretic’s Tragedy is a musical poem; Thyrsis is not. The Jolly Beggars is; the Ode on a Grecian Urn is not. Pope’s Messiah is not musical, but Smart’s Song to David, with its pounding thematic words and the fortissimo explosion of its coda, is a musical tour de force. Crashaw’s hymns and Cowley’s Pindarics are musical, with their fluent, variable, prevailingly four-stress lines and their relentless pushing enjambement; Herbert’s stanzaic poems and Gray’s Pindarics are not. Skelton, Wyatt, and Dunbar are musical; Gavin Douglas and Surrey are not. Alliterative verse is usually accentual and musical; elaborate stanza forms usually are not. The use of melos in poetry does not, of course, necessarily imply any technical knowledge of music on the part of the poet, but it often goes with it. Such a technically musical poem as Crashaw’s Musicks Duell (a Baroque aria with instrumental accompaniment) is an example.

有时，至少可以设想，接触音乐可能会引导诗人倾向于在诗歌中运用旋律。例如，人们感觉骚塞从未完全阐明他在史诗节奏方面的卓越尝试：如果真是如此，那么将弥尔顿对诗歌音乐特质的精辟论述与《塔拉巴》序言中结结巴巴、含糊不清的文字并置，或许会有所启发： “我并不想要即兴曲调；——而是某种能够体现和谐感的东西，某种类似情感重音的东西——类似每位诗人赋予诗歌的必然音调。”旋律的概念或许也能更好地阐明华兹华斯在《彼得·贝尔》和《白痴男孩》中的创作意图。华兹华斯关于韵律是诗歌激情之源的论述尤其适用。强调的是舞蹈的律动，它本身就蕴含着舞蹈的脉动。韵律本身带来的愉悦，更多在于看到一个相对可预测的模式被那些必然优美的词句填满。蒲柏的“常人所想，却从未如此精妙地表达”便是一种韵律的体现：当我们聆听他的对句时，会感受到一种期待得到满足，这与显而易见截然相反。约翰·邓恩讽刺诗中意象的强烈冲击力，与更注重强调的节奏所带来的更充沛的能量相得益彰。

And occasionally it is at least conceivable that some exposure to music would have guided a tendency to melos in verse. One feels that Southey, for instance, never quite clarified his remarkable experiments in epos rhythm: if so, it may be instructive to set beside Milton’s incisive list of the musical qualities of poetry the stammer and mumble of the preface to Thalaba: “I do not wish the improvisatorè tune;—but something that denotes the sense of harmony, something like the accent of feeling,—like the tone which every poet necessarily gives to poetry.” The conception of melos, too, may throw more light on what Wordsworth was trying to do in Peter Bell and The Idiot Boy. Wordsworth’s remarks about metre as the source of excitement in verse apply more particularly to accent, in which the physical pulsation of the dance is present. What metre in itself gives is rather the pleasure of seeing a relatively predictable pattern filling up with the inevitably felicitous words. Pope’s “What oft was thought, but ne’er so well expressed” is a metrical conception: as we listen to his couplets, we have a sense of fulfilled expectation which is the opposite of obviousness. The greater violence in the imagery of Donne’s satires is appropriate to the greater energy of a more accentually-conceived rhythm.

如果我们转向与此形成鲜明对比的、我们称之为“非音乐性”的诗人群体，例如斯宾塞、蒲柏、济慈和丁尼生，我们会发现他们的节奏更慢、更有共鸣。《仙后》中四音步诗行远比《失乐园》中少见，而亚历山大体韵的反复出现则体现了相反的趋势。约翰逊在其反音乐性的格言中精辟地阐述了这群诗人的创作实践：“英国英雄诗行的音乐性如此微弱，以至于很容易被忽略，除非每行的所有音节都相互配合；而这种配合只能通过将每一节诗句都保持独立，作为一个独立的音响系统来实现。” 这意味着，由于约翰逊所考察的诗歌中唯一具有音乐性的元素——音高、重音和音长——随着音调的丧失而彻底消失，英国诗歌应该从音韵模式而非累积节奏的角度来思考。

If we turn to the contrasting group of what we have called the unmusical poets, Spenser, Pope, Keats, Tennyson, we find slower and more resonant rhythms. Four-stress lines are much rarer in The Faerie Queene than in Paradise Lost, and the opposite tendency is marked by the recurrent Alexandrine. The practice of this group of poets is finely expressed by Johnson in his anti-musical dictum: “The musick of the English heroic line strikes the ear so faintly that it is easily lost, unless all the syllables of every line co-operate together; this co-operation can be obtained only by the preservation of every verse unmingled with another, as a distinct system of sounds.” The implication is that as the only musical elements in poetry that Johnson is considering have been lost for good with the loss of pitch accent and quantity, English poetry should think in terms of sound-pattern rather than cumulative rhythm.

诗歌与视觉艺术之间的关系或许比诗歌与音乐之间的关系更为牵强。不擅长音乐的诗人往往在广义上具有“绘画性”：他们经常运用更具冥想性的节奏，一点一滴地构建出一幅静态的画面，例如《俄诺涅》中对裸体维纳斯的细致描写，或是《仙后》中如挂毯般精美的盛大场面。然而，真正与“opsis” （视觉意象）相似之处的，是被称为拟声或拟声的修辞手法，正如蒲柏在《论批评》中描述和举例的那样：

The relations between poetry and the visual arts are perhaps more far-fetched than those between poetry and music. Unmusical poets are often “pictorial” in a general sense: they frequently use their more meditative rhythms to build up, detail by detail, a static picture, as in the careful description of the nude Venus in Oenone or in the elaborate tapestry-like pageants in The Faerie Queene. Where we do have something really analogous to opsis, however, is in the rhetorical device known as imitative harmony or onomatopoeia, as described and exemplified by Pope in the Essay on Criticism:

仅仅严厉一点是不够的，否则会冒犯他人。

’Tis not enough no harshness gives offence,

这声音一定像是某种感觉的回响……

The sound must seem an echo to the sense …

当阿贾克斯努力投掷一块巨石时，

When Ajax strives some rock’s vast weight to throw,

台词也显得吃力，字迹缓慢；

The line too labours, and the words move slow;

但当迅捷的卡米拉搜寻平原时，情况就并非如此了。

Not so, when swift Camilla scours the plain,

飞过挺拔的玉米地，掠过主干道。

Flies o’er th’ unbending corn, and skims along the main.

这种手法很容易辨认，自亚里士多德在其修辞学著作中用荷马关于西西弗斯巨石的诗句来说明巨石从山上滚落的声音以来，就一直有人提及：

This device is easy to recognize, and has been remarked on ever since Aristotle, in his treatise on rhetoric, illustrated in Homer’s line about the stone of Sisyphus the sound of a large stone rolling downhill:

αὖτις ἔπειτα πέδουδε κυλίυδετο λᾶας ἀυαιδής

αὖτις ἔπειτα πέδουδε κυλίυδετο λᾶας ἀυαιδής

波普的译本将这句诗译为“雷声轰鸣而下，烟雾弥漫大地”，这难得地赢得了约翰逊的认可，要知道约翰逊通常对拟声诗持怀疑态度。他在《闲人》系列文章中借批评家迪克·米尼姆之口嘲讽了这句诗，指出“bubble”（气泡）和“trouble”（麻烦）这两个词会“让人屏住呼吸，脸颊瞬间鼓起，然后像吹泡泡一样用力吐气”。然而，这种嘲讽真正说明的是，拟声既是一种语言倾向，也是一种诗歌倾向，诗人会自然而然地利用语言所提供的一切。英语拥有许多绝妙的音效，尽管它也失去了一些：在古英语中，《漫游者》能够表达寒冷的天气，这是现代诗歌无法做到的。

Pope’s translation renders this line “Thunders impetuous down, and smoaks along the ground,” and won for once the approval of Johnson, Johnson being in general very doubtful about imitative harmony. He ridicules it in one of the Idler papers in the figure of Dick Minim the critic, who points out that the words bubble and trouble cause “a momentary inflation of the cheeks by the retention of the breath, which is afterwards forcibly emitted, as in the practice of blowing bubbles.” All that the ridicule really illustrates, however, is that onomatopoeia is a linguistic as well as a poetic tendency, and that the poet takes advantage of whatever his language offers as a matter of course. The English language has many excellent sound-effects, though it has lost a few: in Old English The Wanderer can express cold weather as a modern poem cannot:

Hreosan hrim ond snaw hagle gemenged

Hreosan hrim ond snaw   hagle gemenged

但由于这类修辞手法既是语言技巧又是文学手法，它们在口语中不断被重新运用。好的口语常常被形容为“生动形象”或“色彩鲜明”，这两个词本身就是形象化的比喻。例如， 《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》的叙事段落就具有模仿的灵活性，而《汤姆·索亚历险记》的叙事段落则很难达到这种程度。

But because such devices are linguistic as well as literary, they are continually being recreated in colloquial speech. Colloquial speech, when good, is frequently called “picturesque” or “colorful,” both words being pictorial metaphors. The narrative passages of Huckleberry Finn have an imitative flexibility about them that the narrative passages of Tom Sawyer, for instance, hardly attain to:

……然后传来一阵撕扯、撞击和砸碎的巨响，她倒了下去，人群的前排像波浪一样涌了过来。

… Then there was a racket of ripping and tearing and smashing, and down she goes, and the front wall of the crowd begins to roll in like a wave.

或许，英语中对语言表达方式最精妙、最持久的驾驭，要数《仙后》了。阅读这部作品，我们需要格外专注，具备通过声音捕捉画面的能力。因此，在

The most remarkably sustained mastery of verbal opsis in English, perhaps, is exhibited in The Faerie Queene, which we have to read with a special kind of attention, an ability to catch visualization through sound. Thus in

服从弯刀者意志的尤格

The Eugh obedient to the bender’s will,

这句诗中间有几个弱音节，使它呈弓形下垂。当乌娜迷失方向时，节奏也随之紊乱。

the line has a number of weak syllables in the middle that makes it sag out in a bow shape. When Una goes astray the rhythm goes astray with her:

而乌娜则在树林和森林里漫无目的地游荡……

And Una wandring farre in woods and forrests …

这句诗的部分效果是由于“forests”（森林）和“guests”（客人）押韵不准造成的。当主题是残骸时，同样的押韵不准也会破坏节奏：

Part of the effect of this line is due to the weak rhyme of “forrests” against “guests.” When the subject is wreckage, the rhythm is wrecked with the same kind of disappointment-rhyme:

否则，我这脆弱的船身会

   因你猛烈的撞击和无情的打击而疯狂、破碎，无法承受，它必须   在粗糙的岩石上或沙质浅滩上

   颠簸。

For else my feeble vessell crazd, and crackt

   Through thy strong buffets and outrageous blowes,

   Cannot endure, but needs it must be wrackt

   On the rough rocks, or on the sandy shallowes.

当弗洛里梅尔觉得她的叙述方式难以理解时，读者也会有同样的感受：

When Florimell finds her way difficult to scan, so does the reader:

透过高耸的树梢，她看到了……

Through the tops of the high trees she did descry …

当谈到音乐中的和声时，我们找到了一个与语言中为数不多的恰当词汇押韵的词语：

When the subject is harmony in music, we have an identical rhyme on one of the few appropriate words in the language:

乐器发出清晰的回应：

发出银色声音的乐器确实发出了回应……

To th’ instruments diuine respondence meet:

The siluer sounding instruments did meet …

当主题是“危险的桥梁”时，我们有：

When the subject is a “perillous Bridge,” we have:

通道笔直，如同犁过的山脊。

Streight was the passage like a ploughed ridge,

如果两个人相遇，其中一粒尘埃就会掉下悬崖。

That if two met, the one mote needes fall ouer the lidge.

文艺复兴时期的读者由于接受过修辞学的学校训练，对这类修辞手法早已有所警觉：例如，斯宾塞《一月》中一句看似无害的诗句，就被EK迅速地斥为“优美的复调……以及拙劣的谐音双关”。上面引用的蒲柏的段落出自维达的《诗艺》，其成书时间早于斯宾塞。在斯宾塞之后，对模仿和声表现出最持续兴趣的诗人是考利，他在《大卫》中如此频繁地运用这种手法，以至于约翰逊对此嗤之以鼻，认为他无法理解为什么亚历山大体诗行中的松树会比五音步诗行中的更高。然而，考利的一些修辞手法也颇为有趣，例如他对神谕般的半音步的运用。例如，在考利的诗中，五音步诗行的三个音步被用来表示静默的沉思：

Renaissance readers had been put on the alert for such effects by their school training in rhetoric: a harmless looking line from Spenser’s January, for instance, is promptly sandbagged by E. K. as “a prety Epanorthosis … and withall a Paronomasia.” The source of Pope’s passage quoted above is Vida’s Art of Poetry, which is earlier than Spenser. After Spenser the poet who showed the most consistent—or persistent—interest in imitative harmony was Cowley, who uses it so freely in Davideis as to draw a hoarse growl from Johnson that he saw no reason why a pine tree should be taller in Alexandrines than in pentameters. Some of Cowley’s effects however are interesting enough, such as his use of the oracular hemistich. Here, for instance, three feet of a pentameter line are assigned to silent contemplation:

谁能述说，谁能描述你的宝座，

伟大的三位一体神？

O who shall tell, who shall describe thy Throne,

Thou great Three-One?

引自蒲柏的段落第一句（“‘Tis soughness give offence’（这还不够，仅仅严厉是不够的）”暗示，写作中明显的刺耳不和谐或明显的失误往往可能被解读为模仿。礼仪。波普在同一首诗中也运用了这种刻意的冲突，他用这种冲突来举例说明他所不赞同的恶劣行径。艾迪生在《旁观者》杂志第253期中对这段文字的讨论表明，这种手法至今仍能激起人们浓厚的兴趣。例如，波普是这样描述“便秘的天才”的：

The first line in the passage quoted from Pope (“’Tis not enough no harshness gives offence”) implies that a sharp discord or apparent bungle in the writing may often be interpreted as imitative decorum. Pope uses such intentional discords in the same poem when he gives horrible examples of practices he disapproves of, and Addison’s discussion of the passage in Spectator 253 shows how lively an interest such devices still aroused. Here, for example, is the way that Pope describes constipated genius:

而菌株，来自坚硬的大脑，每年八行。

And strains, from hard-bound brains, eight lines a year.

斯宾塞自然而然地反复使用同样的修辞手法。对头韵的拙劣滥用，会使说话者（吹牛大王）显得虚伪做作：

Spenser, naturally, employs the same device constantly. A tasteless misuse of alliteration marks a speaker (Braggadocchio) as a liar and hypocrite:

但凡人的心思却很复杂，

而且很容易被大众的偏见所蒙蔽。

But minds of mortall men are muchell mard,

And mou’d amisse with massie mucks vnmeet regard.

当假杜埃萨引诱圣乔治时，其语法、节奏和韵律简直糟糕透顶：这位正直的骑士应该早就意识到事情不对劲了：

and when the false Duessa tempts St. George, the grammar, rhythm, and assonance could hardly be worse: the worthy knight’s ear should have warned him that all was not well:

然而，他却强迫我如此行，否​​则便死。

死亡是我的甘露；然而，

你却要拯救我这悲惨的境地……

Yet thus perforce he bids me do, or die.

Die is my dew; yet rew my wretched state

You …

某些模仿手法在每种语言中都趋于标准化，而英语中的大多数模仿手法都为人熟知，无需在此赘述：断句加快语速，扬抑格节奏暗示下落感，等等。英语词汇主要由单音节词构成，而单音节词总是需要单独的重音，无论多么细微。因此，如果巧妙运用，较长的拉丁语词汇可以起到节奏轻快的作用，与“十个低沉的词常常挤进一行沉闷的诗句”所造成的沉闷无韵形成鲜明对比。英语中后一种现象的副产品更有用：所谓的断句，即中间带有重读音节的诗行，自古英语时代（当时是西弗斯的C型诗行）以来，就一直被用作表达不祥和预兆的最有效方式。

Certain imitative devices become standardized in every language, and most of them in English are too familiar to need recapitulation here: beheaded lines increase speed, trochaic rhythms suggest falling movement, and so on. The native stock of English words consists largely of monosyllables, and a monosyllable always demands a separate accent, however slight. Hence long Latin words, if skilfully used, have the rhythmical function of lightening the metre, in contrast to the sodden unrhythmical roar that results “When ten low words oft creep in one dull line.” A by-product of this latter phenomenon in English is more useful: the so-called broken-backed line with a spondee in the middle has since Old English times (when it was Sievers’ type C) been most effective for suggesting the ominous and foreboding:

你的愿望因此不敢说出口。（怀亚特）

Thy wishes then dare not be told.   (Wyatt)

从高处俯瞰，景象惨不忍睹。（斯宾塞）

Depending from on high, dreadful to sight.   (Spenser)

尝过善恶知识的人。（弥尔顿）

Which tasted works knowledge of good and evil.   (Milton)

模仿和声当然可以偶尔用于任何形式的写作中，但作为一种持续的效果，它似乎更倾向于……在诗歌中，头韵最自然地出现在史诗中，它以变体的形式出现，与持续的常规模式形成对比。剧作家和散文作家则很少使用头韵：在莎士比亚的作品中，头韵的出现往往有其特定的原因，例如李尔王在荒野上呼唤风暴时，用风暴本身的音调来表达。在抒情诗中，头韵的引入往往具有炫技的效果，它吸引了大部分的注意力，使整首诗变成了警句。例如，十四世纪的杰作《铁匠》就运用了头韵来表现锤击的动作：

Imitative harmony may of course be employed occasionally in any form of writing, but as a continuous effect it seems to adhere most naturally to epos in verse, where it takes the form of variants from a sustained normal pattern. Dramatists and prose writers use it very sparingly: in Shakespeare it occurs only for some definite reason, as when Lear calls to the storm on the heath in the accents of the storm itself. In lyrics its introduction has the effect of a tour de force which absorbs most of the interest and turns the poem into an epigram. An example is the brilliant little fourteenth-century poem The Blacksmiths, which uses the alliterative line to represent hammering:

Swarte smekyd smethes smateryd wyth Smoke

让我彻底摆脱这里的巢穴……

Swarte smekyd smethes smateryd wyth smoke

Dryue me to deth wyth den of here dyntes …

在修辞学的历史上，关于声音与意义之间存在“自然”联系的理论屡见不鲜。这种自然联系不太可能存在，但语言中存在拟声元素，并被诗人加以发展和运用，这一点显而易见。更简单的理解方式是，将模仿和谐视为一种修辞特征的特殊应用，这种特征类似于古典的“数量”，但更准确地说是“质量”：即元音和辅音构成的谐音模式。区分具有连续“质量”或音韵模式的史诗，例如《海伯利安》，与那些主要为了表达意义而存在的史诗，例如《红棉睡帽之乡》 ，并不难，后者的音韵更接近散文。当同一首诗有两个同样令人满意的版本，但结构不同时，例如乔叟的《好女人传奇》序言，我们就可以看出并不存在一致的音韵模式。

Recurrently in the history of rhetoric some theory of a “natural” relation between sound and sense turns up. It is unlikely that there is any such natural relation, but that there is an onomatopoeic element in language which is developed and exploited by the poet is obvious enough. It is simpler to think rather of imitative harmony as a special application of a rhetorical feature which is analogous to Classical quantity, but would be better described as “quality”: the patterns of assonance made by vowels and consonants. It is not difficult to distinguish epos with a continuous “quality” or sound-pattern, such as Hyperion, from the epos of, say, Red Cotton Nightcap Country, where the sound exists primarily for the sake of the sense, and is consequently felt to be closer to prose. We have an indication that there is no consistent sound-pattern when there are two equally satisfactory versions of the same poem differing in texture, as in the Prologue to Chaucer’s Legend of Good Women.

文学批评中“音乐性”一词被混淆使用的主要原因是，批评家们在思考诗歌中的音乐性时，很少会想到与他们所讨论的诗歌同时代的实际音乐——那种音乐具有重音和舞曲节奏——而是想到古典音乐（当时人们大多不了解）的结构，而这种结构可能更接近歌曲和音高重音。我们强调模仿和声，是因为它阐明了一个原则：在古典诗歌中，声音模式或数量作为一种重复出现的元素，是诗​​歌旋律（melos）的一部分；而在我们的诗歌中，它则是诗歌结构（ opsis ）的一部分。

The main reason for the confused use of the term musical in literary criticism is that when critics think of music in poetry, they seldom think of the actual music contemporary with the poetry they are discussing, with its stress accent and dance rhythm, but of the (very largely unknown) structure of Classical music, which was presumably closer to song and to pitch accent. We have stressed imitative harmony because it illustrates the principle that while in Classical poetry sound-pattern or quantity, being an element of recurrence, is part of the melos of the poetry, it is part of the opsis in ours.

连续性的节奏：散文

THE RHYTHM OF CONTINUITY: PROSE

每首诗中我们至少可以听到两种截然不同的节奏。一种是反复出现的节奏，我们已经证明它是由重音、韵律和音韵模式构成的复杂组合。另一种是语义节奏，也就是通常所说的散文节奏。如果在朗诵诗歌时夸大前者，就会产生抑扬顿挫的语调；如果夸大后者，就会产生“极其浮夸的散文”，正如萧伯纳当年评价莎士比亚朗诵时所说的那样。当反复出现的节奏是主要的或组织性的节奏时，我们就有了诗体史诗；当语义节奏是主要的节奏时，我们就有了散文。文学散文源于文学作品中对论述性或陈述性写作形式的运用。然而，即使是“不诗意”的诗歌论著，也总是被归类为文学作品。

In every poem we can hear at least two distinct rhythms. One is the recurring rhythm, which we have shown to be a complex of accent, metre, and sound-pattern. The other is the semantic rhythm of sense, or what is usually felt to be the prose rhythm. Exaggerating the former, in speaking poetry aloud, will produce sing-song; exaggerating the latter will produce “insanely pompous prose,” to quote a remark of Bernard Shaw on the speaking of Shakespeare in his day. We have verse epos when the recurrent rhythm is the primary or organizing one, and prose when the semantic rhythm is primary. Literary prose results from the use within literature of the form used for discursive or assertive writing. Treatises in verse, however “unpoetical,” are invariably classified as literary.

十六世纪是一个实验时期，主要体现在诗体史诗或霍普金斯所说的“韵律诗”方面。旋律诗的影响催生了无韵诗；奥普西斯诗的影响则促成了斯宾塞诗节和德雷顿六音步诗的出现（《波利奥尔比翁》是一首描写诗，这或许可以解释德雷顿为何选择这种韵律）。如同所有实验时期一样，也出现了一些相对失败的尝试，例如家禽计量单位，它曾风靡一时，但随后便被弃用。散文史诗，即主要被视为演说散文的散文，反映了史诗在文化上的主导地位：它通常被认为是口语表达的一种辅助形式，而诗歌则是最高形式。它被归为低级或至多中级文体，例如弥尔顿“坐在这里，置身于散文的清凉之中”这样的比喻便很有代表性。因此，任何试图赋予散文文学尊严的尝试都可能使其带有诗歌的某些特征。

The sixteenth century was a period of experiment, mainly in verse epos or running rhythm, to use Hopkins’s term. The influence of melos developed blank verse; the influence of opsis the Spenserian stanza and Drayton’s hexameter (the fact that Polyolbion is a descriptive poem may account for Drayton’s choice of this metre). As in all experimental periods, there were some comparative failures, such as poulterer’s measure, which had a vogue and were then dropped. Prose epos, that is, prose which is conceived primarily as oratorical prose, reflects the cultural domination of epos: it is normally thought of as a subsidiary form of spoken expression, of which the highest form is verse. It is assigned to the low or at best the middle style, such metaphors as Milton’s “sitting here below in the cool element of prose” being typical. Hence any attempt to give literary dignity to prose is likely to give it some of the characteristics of verse.

据说杰里米·边沁曾以散文的每一行都延伸到页面末尾这一事实来区分散文和诗歌。如同许多看似简单的观察一样，这其中蕴含的真理往往被知识的短视所忽略。散文的节奏是连续的，而非循环的，这一点在印刷页面上机械地分割散文行时体现得淋漓尽致。当然，每位散文作家都知道，散文的写作远比印刷的过程复杂，印刷可能会破坏甚至破坏句子的节奏，例如将强调的词放在一行末尾而不是下一行的开头，或者用连字符连接重读的词等等。但散文作家很大程度上受制于运气，除非他愿意像马拉美的《骰子之战》中所描绘的那样，反抗运气。文艺复兴时期演说散文的特点，例如其节奏中诸多反复出现的特征，常常被印刷术的连续印刷所掩盖。字符集的对唱圣歌就是一个很好的例子。

Jeremy Bentham is reputed to have distinguished prose from verse by the fact that in prose all the lines run to the end of the page. Like many simple-minded observations, this has a truth that the myopia of knowledgeability is more apt to overlook. The rhythm of prose is continuous, not recurrent, and the fact is symbolized by the purely mechanical breaking of prose lines on a printed page. Of course every prose writer knows that the writing of prose is not as mechanical as the printing of it, and that it is possible for printing to injure or even spoil the rhythm of a sentence by putting an emphatic word at the end of a line instead of at the beginning of the next one, by hyphenating a strongly stressed word, and so on. But the prose writer is largely the prisoner of his luck, unless he is willing to make the kind of revolt against luck illustrated by Mallarmé’s Coup des Dés. The characteristics of Renaissance oratorical prose, with the many recurrent features in its rhythm, are often concealed by the continuous printing of typography. The antiphonal chant in which the character books are written is a good example.

他认为宗教是一件悲哀的事，并对此感到厌恶。

He distastes religion as a sad thing,

并且比同龄人年长六岁，因为他想到了天堂。

and is six years elder for a thought of heaven.

他鄙夷又恐惧，却又盼望着长寿。

He scorns and fears, and yet hopes for old age,

但我不敢想象它满是皱纹的样子……

but dare not imagine it with wrinkles …

他今天出于善意献出自己的鲜血，

He offers you his blood today in kindness,

明天就可以接受您的申请了。

and is ready to take yours tomorrow.

他很少做自己不想再做的事情。

He does seldom anything which he wishes not to do again,

只有经历过不幸之后才会变得明智……

and is only wise after a misfortune …

再次强调，华丽辞藻运用了修辞学著作中已知的所有修辞手法，包括押韵、韵律平衡和头韵，而这些通常被认为是诗歌的专属。西塞罗式的散文基于周期性的节奏和从句的平衡，这种平衡往往接近于一种准韵律平衡。在像布朗的《瓮葬》这样刻意练习修辞的散文作品中，我们可以辨认出反复出现的节奏单元，例如西塞罗的从句：“玻璃杯中精美的围护”、“罗马的复仇之争”都是抑扬格的例子。1611年版的《圣经》经常将每节经文单独成段印刷：这无疑主要是为了方便传道者，但与传统的印刷方式相比，它也更清晰地展现了其散文的节奏。如果将培根的一些散文，特别是早期那些更偏向格言式的文章，每个句子也单独成段，那么它们的节奏也会更加清晰地呈现出来。

Euphuism, again, employs every device known to the rhetoric books, including rhyme, metrical balance, and alliteration, which are usually thought of as the prerogative of verse. Ciceronian prose was based on a periodic rhythm and a balancing of clauses that was often a quasi-metrical balance. In prose works which are deliberate rhetorical exercises, such as Browne’s Urn Burial, one can pick out recurring units of rhythm like the clausulae of Cicero: “handsome enclosure in glasses,” “revengeful contentions of Rome,” are anapestic examples. The 1611 Bible is frequently printed with each verse a separate paragraph: this is doubtless done primarily for the convenience of preachers, but it also gives a clearer idea of its prose rhythm than conventionally printed prose would do. The rhythm of some of Bacon’s essays, especially the earlier and more aphoristic ones, would also emerge more clearly if each sentence were a separate paragraph.

到了十七世纪，诗歌韵律的实验时期已经结束，取而代之的是散文的实验时期。这始于“塞内卡式漫步”或阿提卡散文，它反抗西塞罗学派形式化的半韵律修辞，转而追求自然流畅的口语风格。在德莱顿的时代，散文摆脱了韵律的束缚，其独特的语义节奏得以解放，这已成为一项成就。因此，马修·阿诺德称德莱顿和蒲柏的时代为散文与理性的时代是正确的，这并非因为他们的诗歌平淡无奇。但正因为它的散文是完全成熟的散文。文学史上一个奇特的事实是，茹尔丹先生的著名发现实际上确实是一项发现，而且这种发现似乎通常是在文学发展到相当成熟的阶段才会出现的。

By the seventeenth century the period of experiment in running rhythm had run its course, and a period of experiment in prose succeeded. This begins with the “Senecan amble” or Attic prose, the revolt in the direction of a natural speaking style against the formal half-metrical rhetoric of the Ciceronians. In Dryden the emancipating of prose from the domination of metre and the liberating of the distinctive semantic rhythm of prose is an accomplished fact. Thus Matthew Arnold was right in calling the period of Dryden and Pope an age of prose and reason, not because its poetry is prosaic, but because its prose is fully realized prose. One of the curious facts of literary history is that M. Jourdain’s celebrated discovery in fact is a discovery, and one that a literature seems most often to make at a well advanced point in its development.

当然，我们说散文独特的节奏从德莱顿时代开始更加清晰地显现，并非意味着当时的散文更好，尽管读者或许无需再被提醒不要过早做出价值判断。但显而易见的是，散文本身是一种透明的媒介：当它最不引人注目，如同商店橱窗里的玻璃般清晰地呈现主题时，它便达到最纯粹的状态——也就是说，它最远离史诗和其他韵律的影响。毋庸置疑，这种中性的清晰绝非枯燥乏味，因为枯燥乏味总是晦涩难懂的。因此，虽然从文学角度来看，散文完全可以像作者希望的那样运用修辞手法，但当散文用于非文学目的时，修辞手法往往会成为一种劣势。有人说，用麦考利的风格无法表达真相，这便体现了这一点——当然，麦考利并非最适合用这句话来形容的作家。矫揉造作的散文不够灵活，无法胜任散文纯粹的描述性工作：它不断地过度简化和对称化其素材。即使是吉本，为了提出反义词，也难免会牺牲对事实的必要限定。文学本身也存在类似的原则：例如，在研究华丽辞藻的浪漫故事时，人们会意识到用华丽辞藻讲述故事是多么困难。华丽辞藻源于演说形式，并且仍然最适合长篇大论：华丽辞藻的作者会抓住一切机会，陷入独白式的叙述。

In saying that the distinctive rhythm of prose emerges more clearly from Dryden’s time on, we are not, of course, saying that better prose was then written, though perhaps the reader needs no further warnings against premature value-judgements. But it becomes obvious that prose by itself is a transparent medium: it is at its purest—that is, at its furthest from epos and other metrical influences—when it is least obtrusive and presents its subject-matter like plate glass in a shop window. It goes without saying that such neutral clarity is far from dullness, as dullness is invariably opaque. Hence, while there is no literary reason why prose should not be as rhetorical as the writer pleases, rhetorical prose often becomes a disadvantage when prose is used for non-literary purposes. Something of this is expressed by the remark that it is impossible to tell the truth in Macaulay’s style—not that Macaulay is the best writer to attach the remark to. A highly mannered prose is not sufficiently flexible to do the purely descriptive work of prose: it continually oversimplifies and over-symmetrizes its material. Even Gibbon is not above sacrificing a necessary qualification of a fact to an antithesis. Something of the same principle can be seen within literature itself: in studying the euphuist romances, for example, one becomes aware of how difficult it is to get a story told in euphuist prose. Euphuism grew out of oratorical forms, and remains best adapted to harangue: the euphuist writer seizes every chance for relapsing into monologue that he can get.

简而言之，修辞散文自然最适合修辞的两大目的：装饰和说服。但由于这两种目的在心理上截然相反，说服性散文的效果往往会被其本身所赋予的魅力装饰所抵消。杰里米·泰勒的宗教作品之美，正是其中一种不带任何私利的因素，使他的作品得以在文学的殿堂中永存，而非昙花一现的动感说服。这一原则绝非泰勒独有：即使在盎格鲁-撒克逊人聚集的伍尔夫斯坦教堂里，也必然有一些世俗的知识分子，他们关注的焦点并非自身的罪过，而是牧师对头韵韵律的驾驭能力。

Rhetorical prose, in short, is naturally best adapted to the two purposes of rhetoric, ornament and persuasion. But as these two purposes are a psychological contrast, persuasive prose is often neutralized in its effect by the very ornament that makes it delightfully persuasive. The beauty of Jeremy Taylor’s devotional writing is a disinterested factor in it which has kept him in the permanent confines of literature instead of in the transient stream of kinetic persuasion. The principle involved is by no means confined to Taylor: even in the Anglo-Saxon congregation of Wulfstan there must have been a few secular-minded highbrows who were thinking less of their sins than of the preacher’s mastery of alliterative rhythm:

她的 Syndan mannslagan 和 Maegslagan 和 Maesserbanan 和 Mynsterhatan，她的 Syndan Mansworan 和 morthorwyrhtan，她的 Syndan Myltestran 和 Bearnmyrthran 和 Fule Forlegene Horingas Manege，她的 Syndan Wiccan 和 waelcyrian，她的 Syndan ryperas 和 referas 等worolstrruderas、ond、hraedest 是 cwethenn、mana 和 Misdaeda ungerim alra。

Her syndan mannslagan ond maegslagan ond maesserbanan ond mynsterhatan, ond her syndan mansworan ond morthorwyrhtan, ond her syndan myltestran ond bearnmyrthran ond fule forlegene horingas manege, ond her syndan wiccan ond waelcyrian, ond her syndan ryperas ond reaferas ond worolstruderas, ond, hraedest is to cwethenne, mana ond misdaeda ungerim ealra.

本文主要探讨文学散文：非文学散文的节奏将在后文详述。散文的韵律特点包括：由短语和并列从句构成的长句、强调性的重复与流畅的线性节奏相结合、谩骂、详尽的罗列，以及表达思维过程或运动而非逻辑清晰的逻辑顺序。拉伯雷是散文韵律大师之一：在我看来，他第一卷第五章中那场精彩的饮酒聚会，在技巧上堪称音乐，仿佛是为文字谱写了一首《雅内金》。英语世界里也有伯顿，据说他曾到伊西斯号上去，听船夫们咒骂，以此为乐。或许他的来访是出于职业目的，因为他的风格本质上具备优秀脏话的特质：节奏感强，喜爱谩骂和罗列，词汇量丰富，思维习惯于使用简短的重音单位，并且对与脏话相关的两个主题——神学和个人卫生——有着百科全书般的了解。除了最后一点之外，其他所有特征都与音乐相关。

We are concerned here with literary prose: an account of non-literary prose rhythm will be given later in the essay. A tendency to long sentences made up of short phrases and coordinate clauses, to emphatic repetition combined with a driving linear rhythm, to invective, to exhaustive catalogues, and to expressing the process or movement of thought instead of the logical word-order of achieved thought, are among the signs of prose melos. Rabelais is one of the greatest masters of melos in prose: the wonderful drinking party in the fifth chapter of the first book seems to me to be technically musical, Jannequin set to words, so to speak. In English we have Burton, who is said to have amused himself by going down to the Isis and listening to the bargemen swear. Perhaps his visits were professional, for the qualities of his style are essentially the qualities of good swearing: a swinging sense of rhythm, a love of invective and of catalogue, an unlimited vocabulary, a tendency to think in short accentual units, and an encyclopaedic knowledge of the two subjects relevant to swearing, theology and personal hygiene. All of these except the last are musical characteristics.

弥尔顿的散文，如同他的诗歌，在其最佳状态下都充满了“真正的音乐之美”，当然，二者的美妙之处截然不同。其特点包括：篇幅巨大的周期性句子，句中短促有力的短语，句子内部语速的变化，情感饱满的形容词的修辞堆砌，以及贝多芬式的、气势磅礴的尾声。然而，在“意识流”技巧出现之前，斯特恩才是散文旋律的真正大师。意识流技巧将思想呈现为一个过程，并在我们这个时代复兴了这种风格。在普鲁斯特的作品中，这种技巧表现为瓦格纳式的主导动机交织。在格特鲁德·斯坦的作品中，语言的刻意冗长赋予了文字某种音乐般的重复性。当然，在旋律（melos）方面进行最精心实验的还是乔伊斯， 《尤利西斯》中的酒吧场景（在斯图亚特·吉尔伯特的评论中被称为“塞壬”）虽然有些杂技式的技巧，但仍然是很好的例证。刚才讨论的散文技巧与音乐之间存在着某种类比，这并非纯粹的臆想。例如，温德姆·刘易斯就接受了这种类比，他的《没有艺术的人》显然意在宣扬“奥普西斯” （opsis，一种修辞手法）。我们偶尔也能在一些通常不擅长音乐的作家身上发现“梅洛斯” （melos，一种修辞手法）的倾向。例如，在《衣裳哲学》（Sartor Resartus）的修辞中，我们读到这样一段话：“在这些混乱的颂词和挽歌中，疯狂的彼特拉克式和维特罗式的文风杂乱无章地散落在各种无关紧要的事物之间”，我们可以看出，一些华丽辞藻的技巧被用来强调线性结构，而不是像真正的华丽辞藻那样，用来达到平行结构的平衡。

The prose of Milton, like his verse, is at its best full of “true musical delight,” though of course of a very different kind. The enormous periodic sentences with their short barking phrases, the variations of speed within these sentences, the rhetorical accumulation of emotionally charged epithets, the roaring Beethovenish-coda perorations, are some of its features. Sterne, however, is the chief master of prose melos before the development of “stream of consciousness” techniques for presenting thought as a process revived it in our own day. In Proust this technique takes the form of a Wagnerian intertwining of leitmotifs. In Gertrude Stein a deliberate prolixity of language gives to the words something of the capacity for repetition that music has. But it is of course Joyce who has made the most elaborate experiments in melos, and the bar-room scene in Ulysses (the one called “Sirens” in the Stuart Gilbert commentary) is, if somewhat acrobatic, still good evidence that the prose techniques just discussed have an analogy to music which is not purely fanciful. The analogy is accepted in Wyndham Lewis, for example, whose Men Without Art is evidently intended as a manifesto in favor of opsis. Here and there we can discern a tendency to melos even in normally unmusical writers. When in the rhetoric of Sartor Resartus, for instance, we run across such a passage as “From amid these confused masses of Eulogy and Elegy, with their mad Petrarchan and Werterean ware lying madly scattered among all sorts of quite extraneous matter,” we can see that some of the devices of euphuism are being used for linear accentuation instead of for parallel balance, as they would be in actual euphuism.

散文和诗歌一样，那些常被称作“感伤音乐性”的作家，往往是那些与真正音乐相去甚远的作家。例如，德·昆西、佩特、罗斯金和莫里斯（仅举几例）的作品中，往往存在着一种“回文”倾向，这种倾向通常包含着对精细的画面描写和冗长的装饰性比喻的运用，但后一种倾向并不能定义前一种倾向：我们不能仅凭题材选择来评判文风的质量。真正的区别在于句子的构思。亨利·詹姆斯后期小说中的长句包含着多个句子：所有的限定语和插入语都符合某种模式，随着一个个要点的展开，呈现出的并非线性的思维过程，而是一种同步的理解。被解释的内容被反复推敲，从各个角度审视，但可以说，它从一开始就完整地存在着。在康拉德的作品中，叙事中的错位——正如他所说的“倒叙和正叙”——也是为了引导我们从聆听故事本身转移到关注核心情境。他那句“最重要的是让你看清”包含着一个视觉隐喻，并且保留了大部分原意。《项狄传》中叙事结构的错位则产生了相反的效果：它将我们的注意力从外部情境转移到聆听作者脑海中情境的形成过程。

In prose, as in verse, the writers most frequently called musical in the sentimental sense are usually the ones most remote from actual music. The tendency to opsis in De Quincey, Pater, Ruskin, and Morris, to name a few at random, often includes a tendency to elaborate pictorial description and long decorative similes, but the second tendency does not define the first: we cannot judge a quality of style by choice of subject-matter. The real difference is rather in the conception of the sentence. The long sentences in the later novels of Henry James are containing sentences: all the qualifications and parentheses are fitted in to a pattern, and as one point after another is made, there emerges not a linear process of thought but a simultaneous comprehension. What is explained is turned around and viewed from all aspects, but it is completely there, so to speak, from the beginning. In Conrad, too, the dislocations in the narrative—working backwards and forwards, as he put it—are designed to make us shift our attention from listening to the story to looking at the central situation. His phrase “above all to make you see” contains a visual metaphor with much of its original meaning left in it. The dislocations of narrative in Tristram Shandy have the opposite effect: they take our attention away from looking at the external situation to listening to the process of its coming into being in the author’s mind.

由于散文本身是一种透明的媒介，因此很少有散文作家会明显倾向于某一方面。一般来说，当我们最明显地意识到某种“风格”或语言结构的修辞特点时，我们最有可能接触到的是旋律（melos）或散文（opsis）。布朗和杰里米·泰勒倾向于散文，正如伯顿和弥尔顿倾向于旋律一样：欧·亨利小说中的一个人物对泰勒的评论是：“为什么没有人为它写歌词呢？”，这指的是类似的东西，不是音乐，而是丁尼生式的音韵模式。

As prose is by itself a transparent medium, relatively few prose writers show a pronounced leaning to one side or the other. In general, when we are most conscious of a marked “style,” or rhetorical idiosyncrasy of verbal structure, we are most likely to be in contact with either melos or opsis. Browne and Jeremy Taylor are as much inclined to opsis as Burton and Milton are to melos: the comment on Taylor made by a character in an O. Henry story, “Why doesn’t someone write words to it?”, refers to something analogous, not to music, but to a Tennysonian sound-pattern.

或许可以大胆概括，古典影响的主要体现在词序方面，因为屈折语比现代英语或法语在词序上拥有更大的自由度，因此人们倾向于认为句子的所有组成部分同时存在。即使在演说家西塞罗的作品中，我们也能强烈感受到“平衡”的重要性，而平衡意味着对线性运动的抑制。在后来的拉丁语中，一种新的线性推进方式开始显现，人们感觉与日耳曼文明的新兴文明更加接近，这种文明以其头韵和萌芽状态的重音韵律而著称。因此，在卡西奥多罗斯的著作中，主题词和头韵重音在冗长的句子中相互呼应、呼应：

One may perhaps risk the generalization that the main weight of Classical influence falls on the opsis side, for the reason that an inflected language permits greater freedom in word order than Modern English or French, and so one tends to think of the sentence as containing all its parts at once. Even in Cicero, who is an orator, we are intensely aware of “balance,” and balance implies a neutralizing of linear movement. In later Latin a new kind of linear propulsion begins to be perceptible, and one feels closer to the new Teutonic civilization with its alliterative line and its embryonic stress-accent music. Thus in Cassiodorus thematic words and alliterative accents echo and call and respond through the turgid sentences:

Hinc etiam appellatam aestimamus corda, quod facile corda moveat: ubi tenta vocum Collecta est sub diversitate concordia, ut vicina corda pulsata alteram faciat sponte contremiscere, quam nullam contigit attigisse.

Hinc etiam appellatam aestimamus chordam, quod facile corda moveat: ubi tenta vocum collecta est sub diversitate concordia, ut vicina chorda pulsata alteram faciat sponte contremiscere, quam nullam contigit attigisse.

礼仪的节奏：戏剧

THE RHYTHM OF DECORUM: DRAMA

在所有文学结构中，我们都能感受到一种特质，我们可以称之为语言个性或说话声音的特质——它不同于直接对话，但又与之相关。当这种特质被认为是作者自身的声音时，我们就称之为风格：“风格即人”是一条普遍接受的公理。风格的概念基于这样一个事实：每位作家都有其独特的节奏，如同其笔迹一般鲜明；他们也拥有独特的意象，从对某些元音和辅音的偏好到对两三种原型的执着，不一而足。风格当然存在于所有文学作品中，但在主题散文中体现得最为纯粹：事实上，它是通常被归类为非文学作品的散文作品的主要文学术语。风格在维多利亚时代晚期达到了鼎盛时期，当时写作与个性之间的主要联系是批评的基本原则。

In all literary structures we are aware of a quality that we may call the quality of a verbal personality or a speaking voice—something different from direct address, though related to it. When this quality is felt to be the voice of the author himself, we call it style: le style c’est l’homme is a generally accepted axiom. The conception of style is based on the fact that every writer has his own rhythm, as distinctive as his handwriting, and his own imagery, ranging from a preference for certain vowels and consonants to a preoccupation with two or three archetypes. Style exists in all literature, of course, but may be seen at its purest in thematic prose: in fact it is the chief literary term applied to works of prose generally classified as non-literary. Style had its great period in late Victorian times, when the primary connection between writing and personality was a fundamental principle of criticism.

在小说中，我们面临着一个更为复杂的问题：对话必须用人物自身的口吻，而非作者的口吻；有时对话和叙述的距离如此之远，以至于整本书仿佛被分割成了两种不同的语言。风格的契合至关重要。对内在人物或主题而言，风格与内容的契合被称为文雅或恰当。文雅通常体现为诗人伦理的声音，即诗人调整自身声音以适应人物的声音或主题或氛围所需的语调。正如散文的风格最为纯粹，文雅在戏剧中也最为纯粹，因为诗人并不亲自出场。从我们今天的角度来看，戏剧可以被描述为融入了文雅的史诗或虚构作品。

In a novel we are aware of a more complicated problem: dialogue has to speak with the voice of the internal characters, not the author, and sometimes dialogue and narrative are so far apart as to divide the book into two different languages. The suiting of style to an internal character or subject is known as decorum or appropriateness of style to content. Decorum is in general the poet’s ethical voice, the modification of his own voice to the voice of a character or to the vocal tone demanded by subject or mood. And as style is at its purest in discursive prose, so decorum is obviously at its purest in drama, where the poet does not appear in person. Drama might be described, from our present point of view, as epos or fiction absorbed by decorum.

戏剧是对对话或谈话的模仿，而谈话的修辞显然必须非常流畅。它可以从固定的演讲稿到以韵律为基础的“对答式”（stichomythia）式的针锋相对；它面临着双重挑战：既要表达说话者的性格和语调节奏，又要根据情境和其他说话者的情绪进行调整。在伊丽莎白时代的戏剧中，可以说其重心介于诗体史诗和散文之间，因此可以根据礼仪的要求轻松地在两者之间转换，而礼仪的要求主要取决于角色的社会地位和戏剧的类型。喜剧和地位较低的角色倾向于散文，而在后来的几个世纪里，随着史诗被小说取代，喜剧和散文展现出一种适应变化环境的能力，而悲剧和诗体史诗则明显缺乏这种能力。

Drama is a mimesis of dialogue or conversation, and the rhetoric of conversation obviously has to be a very fluid one. It may range from a set speech to the kind of thrust and parry which is called stichomythia when its basis is metrical; and it has the double difficulty of expressing the speaker’s character and speech rhythm and yet modifying them to the situation and the moods of other speakers. In Elizabethan drama the center of gravity, so to speak, is somewhere between verse epos and prose, so that it can move easily from one to the other depending on the requirements of decorum, which are chiefly the social rank of the character and the genre of the play. Comedy and lower ranks run to prose, and in later centuries, as epos gives way before fiction, comedy and prose exhibit a power of adaptation to the changed conditions that tragedy and verse epos conspicuously lack.

然而，即便在散文喜剧中，统治阶级人物所要求的那种高雅的修辞风格已基本消失，如何用散文来表达诗剧用诗歌来展现的特征——例如尊严、激情、诙谐的意象（或许是最重要的）以及悲悯之情——仍然是一个技术难题。散文喜剧通常通过发展一种矫揉造作的警句式散文风格来满足这些要求，这种风格中某种程度上重现了修辞散文的对立和重复结构。从康格里夫到奥凯西，几乎所有伟大的英国喜剧作家都是爱尔兰人，而修辞传统在爱尔兰也延续得更久。辛格的戏剧散文也属于文学矫饰主义的范畴，即便它确实再现了爱尔兰农民的语言节奏。相比之下，像19世纪勃朗宁或本世纪艾略特和弗莱那样的诗歌节奏，似乎毫不费力地就能跨越史诗和散文之间的鸿沟。人们不禁会想，萧伯纳关于用无韵诗写剧本实际上比用散文写剧本更容易的观点，是否真有几分道理。许多现代诗歌给人的感觉就是不自然和生硬。在这种情况下，戏剧性事件的产生是由于尝试了一种不恰当的修辞方式，这种方式与正常的对话节奏严重脱节，而伊丽莎白时代的戏剧，无论其风格多么精心设计，都很少出现这种情况。

Yet even in prose comedy, where the lofty style of rhetoric demanded by ruling-class figures has largely disappeared, there still remains the technical problem of representing in prose the features that a verse drama would express by verse: such features as dignity, passion, witty imagery (probably the most important), and pathos. Prose comedy often meets such requirements by developing a mannered epigrammatic prose style, in which something of the antithetical and repetitive structure of rhetorical prose reappears. Nearly all the great writers of English comedy from Congreve to O’Casey have been Irishmen, and the rhetorical tradition survived longer in Ireland. The dramatic prose of Synge also ranks as literary mannerism, even if it does reproduce the speech rhythms of Irish peasantry. By contrast a verse rhythm like that of Browning in the nineteenth century or that of Eliot and Fry in this one seems to straddle the gap between epos and prose with much less effort. One wonders if there is not something to be said for Shaw’s contention that it is actually easier to write a play in blank verse than in prose. The feeling of unnaturalness and strain in a good deal of modern verse drama would in that case be the result of attempting an inappropriate kind of rhetoric, one which is too far out of touch with normal conversational rhythms, in a way that Elizabethan drama, however elaborately stylized, very seldom is.

浪漫主义者和维多利亚时代的人们似乎对寻找适合对话节奏的诗歌形式并不感兴趣。英语学习者常常被浪漫主义者敦促尽可能多地使用本土短词，理由是这样能使词汇更加具体。然而，建立在简单本土词汇基础上的风格，反而可能是所有风格中最矫揉造作的。即使是塞缪尔·约翰逊最笨拙的作品，与威廉·莫里斯的浪漫小说相比，也依然显得口语化和对话化。如今，受过良好教育的标准英语口语充斥着冗长抽象的专业词汇，以及短词浓重的语调，构成了一种多音节的嘈杂语调，这种语调更容易被写成散文而非诗歌。布莱克的《预言书》是少数几个成功地用诗歌形式驾驭对话节奏的作品之一——其成功之处如此之大，以至于许多评论家至今仍在质疑它们是否称得上是“真正的诗歌”。布莱克认为，要用诗歌来表现受过良好教育的口语，需要比五音步更长的诗行。这种观点可以与克劳夫和布里奇斯在六音步诗中的尝试相比较，他们也试图捕捉同样的节奏。不过，至少在克劳夫的作品中，严格遵循韵律会使重音显得有些起伏不定。在《鸡尾酒会》的诗歌节奏中——这首诗或许最清晰地预示了现代口语中诗歌和散文之间新的节奏重心的发展——我们又回到了非常接近旧式四音步诗行的节奏。或许，这里正在形成的是一种较长的六七音步重音诗行，通过将其分成两部分，最终使其适用于口语对话。

The attempt to find verse forms for conversational rhythms did not interest very many of the Romantics or Victorians. Students of English are often urged, in Romantic fashion, to use as many short words of native origin as possible, on the ground that they make one’s vocabulary concrete, but a style founded on simple native words can be the most artificial of all styles. Samuel Johnson at his most bumbling is still colloquial and conversational compared to a William Morris romance. Standard educated English speech today, with its many long abstract and technical words and the heavy accent of its short ones, is a polysyllabic clatter which is much easier to fit to prose than to verse. Blake’s Prophetic Books represent one of the few successful efforts to tackle conversational rhythm in verse—so successful that many critics are still wondering if they are “real poetry.” Blake’s view that a longer line than the pentameter was needed to represent educated colloquial speech in verse may be compared with the experiments of Clough and Bridges in hexameters, which are also attempts to capture the same kind of rhythm, though at least in Clough one feels that a strict adherence to the metre gives a somewhat roller-coaster quality to the accent. In the verse rhythm of The Cocktail Party, which perhaps most clearly foreshadows the development of a new rhythmical center of gravity between verse and prose in modern speech, we go back to a rhythm very close to the old four-accent line. Perhaps what is taking shape here is a long six-or-seven-beat accentual line finally made practicable for spoken dialogue by being split in two.

戏剧中的melos和opsis的问题很容易解决：melos 指的是实际的音乐，opsis 指的是可见的布景和服装。

The question of melos and opsis in drama is easily dealt with: melos is actual music and opsis visible scenery and costume.

联想的节奏：抒情

THE RHYTHM OF ASSOCIATION: LYRIC

在历史的模式演进中，每一种体裁似乎都依次达到某种程度的主导地位。神话和浪漫故事主要以史诗的形式展现；在高级模仿艺术中，新的民族意识的兴起和世俗修辞的增多，使得传统剧院的戏剧性得以凸显。低级模仿艺术则带来了虚构作品和散文的日益普及，以及节奏的运用。最终，这种影响开始波及诗歌。华兹华斯认为，除了韵律之外，诗歌和散文的词汇完全相同，这是一种低级的模仿宣言。抒情诗这种体裁中，诗人如同反讽作家一样，背对着读者。它也是最清晰地展现文学、叙事和意义的假想核心的体裁，这些核心体现在其字面意义上，例如词序和词型。抒情诗似乎与反讽模式和字面意义有着某种特殊的密切联系。

In the historical sequence of modes, each genre in turn seems to rise to some degree of ascendancy. Myth and romance express themselves mainly in epos, and in the high mimetic the rise of a new national consciousness and an increase of secular rhetoric bring the drama of the settled theatre into the foreground. The low mimetic brings fiction and an increasing use of prose, the rhythm of which finally begins to influence verse. Wordsworth’s theory that apart from metre the lexis of poetry and of prose are identical is a low mimetic manifesto. The lyric is the genre in which the poet, like the ironic writer, turns his back on his audience. It is also the genre which most clearly shows the hypothetical core of literature, narrative and meaning in their literal aspects as word-order and word-pattern. It looks as though the lyric genre has some peculiarly close connection with the ironic mode and the literal level of meaning.

让我们随机选取一句诗，比如说《一报还一报》中克劳迪奥那段精彩演讲的开头：

Let us take a line of poetry at random, say the beginning of Claudio’s great speech in Measure for Measure:

是啊，但死亡，以及我们将去往何处，我们都不得而知：

Ay, but to die, and go we know not where:

我们当然能听出韵律节奏，抑扬格五音步，以四音步诗行的形式朗诵。我们能听出语义或散文节奏，也能听出我们称之为礼仪节奏的东西，即用语言描绘一个人面对死亡时的恐惧。但如果我们非常仔细地聆听这句诗，还能从中辨别出另一种节奏，一种预言般的、冥想式的、不规则的、不可预测的、本质上不连续的节奏，它源于音韵模式的巧合：

We can hear of course the metrical rhythm, an iambic pentameter spoken as a four-stress line. We can hear the semantic or prose rhythm, and we hear what we may call the rhythm of decorum, the verbal representation of the horror of a man facing death. But we can also, if we listen to the line very attentively, make out still another rhythm in it, an oracular, meditative, irregular, unpredictable, and essentially discontinuous rhythm, emerging from the coincidences of the sound-pattern:

艾：

Ay:

但死亡……

But to die …

然后走

and go

我们知道

we know

不是在……

not where …

正如语义节奏是散文的驱动力，韵律节奏是史诗的驱动力，这种预言般的节奏似乎也是抒情诗的主要驱动力。散文的驱动力通常重心在于意识层面：论述型作家写作时深思熟虑，文学散文作家则模仿深思熟虑的过程。在诗歌史诗中，韵律的选择决定了修辞组织的形式：诗人潜移默化地培养出一种运用这种韵律进行思考的习惯性技能，从而得以自由地去做其他事情，例如讲述故事、阐述思想，或根据礼仪要求进行各种修改。然而，这两者本身似乎都无法完全触及我们通常所认为的诗歌创作的本质，即一种联想性的修辞过程，其中大部分都处于意识的阈限之下，是一种混沌的状态。谐音双关、音韵关联、歧义意义关联以及记忆关联，都与梦境极为相似。由此，音韵与意义之间独具特色的抒情结合得以显现。如同梦境一般，语言联想也受到某种审查，我们可以称之为“合理性原则”，即必须将其塑造成诗人及其读者清醒意识所能接受的形式，并充分适应肯定性语言的符号意义，以便与这种意识进行沟通。但联想节奏似乎与梦境保持着某种联系，正如戏剧与仪式之间的联系。联想节奏与其他节奏一样，存在于所有文字之中：叶芝对《牛津现代诗集》开篇的《帕特》的排版重组，便展现了如何从散文中提取联想节奏。

Just as the semantic rhythm is the initiative of prose, and as the metrical rhythm is the initiative of epos, so this oracular rhythm seems to be the predominating initiative of lyric. The initiative of prose normally has its center of gravity in the conscious mind: the discursive writer writes deliberately, and the literary prose writer imitates a deliberative process. In verse epos the choice of a metre prescribes the form of rhetorical organization: the poet develops an unconscious habitual skill in thinking in this metre, and is thereby set free to do other things, such as tell stories, expound ideas, or make the various modifications demanded by decorum. Neither of these by itself seems quite to get down to what we think of as typically the poetic creation, which is an associative rhetorical process, most of it below the threshold of consciousness, a chaos of paronomasia, sound-links, ambiguous sense-links, and memory-links very like that of the dream. Out of this the distinctively lyrical union of sound and sense emerges. Like the dream, verbal association is subject to a censor, which (or whom) we may call the “plausibility-principle,” the necessity of shaping itself into a form acceptable to the poet’s and his reader’s waking consciousness, and of adapting itself to the sign-meanings of assertive language well enough to be communicable to that consciousness. But associative rhythm seems to retain a connection with dream corresponding to the drama’s connection with ritual. The associative rhythm, no less than the others, can be found in all writing: Yeats’s typographical rearrangement of Pater which begins The Oxford Book of Modern Verse illustrates how it may be extracted from prose.

抒情诗最自然的单位是诗节这种不连续的单位，早期的抒情诗大多采用相当规整的诗节结构，这反映了史诗的盛行。像中世纪传奇故事中那样的诗节式史诗，通常比线性史诗更接近梦境般的氛围。随着浪漫主义运动的兴起，人们开始逐渐意识到“情感的真实声音”是不可预测且节奏不规则的。爱伦·坡的诗歌原则认为，诗歌本质上是预言式的、不连续的，诗意即抒情，而诗体史诗实际上是由抒情段落与韵文散文拼接而成。这如同华兹华斯的序言是一篇低级的模仿之作，是反讽时代的宣言，它预示着英国文学第三次技术实验时期的到来，其目标是解放抒情诗独特的节奏。 “自由诗”的目的并非仅仅是反叛韵律和史诗的传统，而是要表达一种独立于韵律和散文之外的节奏。如果我们不承认这第三种节奏，就无法回应那种认为诗歌一旦失去规则韵律就变成散文的幼稚质疑。

The most natural unit of the lyric is the discontinuous unit of the stanza, and in earlier periods most lyrics tended to be fairly regular strophic patterns, reflecting the ascendancy of epos. Stanzaic epos, such as we find in medieval romance, is usually much closer to the atmosphere of a dream world than linear epos. With the Romantic movement a sense that the “true voice of feeling” was unpredictable and irregular in its rhythm began to increase. Poe’s Poetic Principle maintains that poetry is essentially oracular and discontinuous, that the poetic is the lyrical, and that verse epos consists really of lyrical passages stuck together with versified prose. This is a manifesto of the ironic age, as Wordsworth’s preface was a low mimetic one, and announces the arrival of a third period of technical experiment in English literature, in which the object is to liberate the distinctive rhythm of lyric. The aim of “free” verse is not simply revolt against metre and epos conventions, but the articulation of an independent rhythm equally distinct from metre and from prose. If we do not recognize this third rhythm, we shall have no answer for the naive objection that when poetry loses regular metre it becomes prose.

艾米莉·狄金森诗歌中韵律的松散和叶芝诗歌中诗节结构的松散，其目的并非使韵律模式更加不规则，而是为了使抒情节奏更加精准。霍普金斯的“跳跃节奏”一词，与抒情诗的关联，正如行进节奏与史诗的关联一样紧密。庞德的理论和技巧，从他早期的意象主义到《诗章》中不连续的拼贴（在此之前，法国和英国进行了长达半个世纪的史诗“碎片化”或抒情化的实验），都是以抒情诗为中心的理论。以及各种技巧。新批评中基于歧义的修辞分析是一种以抒情为中心的批评，它倾向于（通常是明确地）从所有体裁中提取抒情节奏。二十世纪最受推崇和最具前瞻性的诗人，主要是那些最充分掌握了解放的抒情节奏中那种难以捉摸、沉思冥想、回响悠长、向心性的语言魔力的人。在这一发展过程中，联想节奏变得更加灵活，并因此从其浪漫主义的风格基础转向了一种新的主​​观化的礼仪。

The loosening of rhyme in Emily Dickinson and of stanzaic structure in Yeats are intended, not to make the metrical pattern more irregular, but to make the lyric rhythm more precise. Hopkins’s term “sprung rhythm,” too, has as close an affinity with lyric as running rhythm has with epos. Pound’s theories and techniques, from his early imagism to the discontinuous pastiche of the Cantos (preceded by a half-century of French and English experiment in the “fragmentation” or lyricizing of epos), are lyric-centered theories and techniques. The rhetorical analysis founded on ambiguity in new criticism is a lyric-centered criticism which tends, often explicitly, to extract the lyrical rhythm from all the genres. The most admired and advanced poets of the twentieth century are chiefly those who have most fully mastered the elusive, meditative, resonant, centripetal word-magic of the emancipated lyrical rhythm. In the course of this development the associative rhythm has become more flexible, and has consequently moved from its Romantic basis in style to a new kind of subjectivized decorum.

抒情诗的传统关联主要在于音乐。古希腊人称抒情诗为“ta mele”，通常译为“可歌唱的诗”；文艺复兴时期，抒情诗与里拉琴和鲁特琴紧密相连；而前文提到的坡的文章也强调了音乐在诗歌中的重要性，音乐以其力量弥补了诗歌在精确性上的不足。然而，我们应该记住，当一首诗被“歌唱”时——至少在现代音乐意义上——它的节奏结构已被音乐所取代。“可歌唱的”抒情诗的歌词通常是中性且约定俗成的词语，现代歌曲具有音乐的重音，几乎完全失去了诗歌主导音乐的音高重音。因此，如果我们把“ ta mele ”译为“可吟诵的诗”，就能更清晰地理解抒情诗的含义，因为吟诵，或者叶芝所说的“吟唱”，强调的是词语本身。像叶芝这样希望自己的诗歌被吟诵的现代诗人，往往恰恰是对音乐配乐最持怀疑态度的人。

The traditional associations of lyric are chiefly with music. The Greeks spoke of lyrics as ta mele, usually translated as “poems to be sung”; in the Renaissance, lyric was constantly associated with the lyre and the lute, and Poe’s essay just referred to lays an emphasis on the importance of music in poetry which makes up in strength what it lacks in precision. We should remember, however, that when a poem is “sung,” at least in the modern musical sense, its rhythmical organization has been taken over by music. The words of a “singable” lyric are generally neutral and conventional words, and modern song has the stress accent of music, with little if anything left of the pitch accent that marks the domination of music by poetry. We should therefore get a clearer impression of the lyric if we translated ta mele as “poems to be chanted,” for chanting, or what Yeats called cantillation, is an emphasis on words as words. Modern poets who, like Yeats, want their poems chanted are often precisely those who are most suspicious of musical settings.

音乐史展现出一种反复出现的倾向，即发展出复杂的复调结构，在声乐作品中，这种结构几乎完全掩盖了歌词。同时，也存在着一种反复出现的倾向，即改革和简化音乐结构，以凸显歌词的重要性。这有时是宗教压力的结果，但文学的影响也发挥了作用。我们可以将牧歌视为诗歌对音乐屈从程度接近极限的一种体现。在牧歌中，随着歌词在声部间传递，诗歌的节奏消失了，歌词中的意象则通过通常被称为标题音乐的技巧来表达。我们可能会发现大段的段落充斥着无意义的词语，或者整部作品集都带有“适合人声或维奥尔琴”的副标题，表明歌词可以完全被舍弃。诗人对这种对歌词的粗略处理感到厌恶。他们的言论体现在他们对十七世纪将歌词置于单一旋律线上的风格的支持上，这种风格使得歌剧成为可能。这无疑使我们更接近诗歌，尽管音乐在节奏上仍然占据主导地位。但是，作曲家越是强调诗歌的语言节奏，就越接近吟唱，而吟唱才是抒情诗真正的节奏基础。亨利·劳斯在这方面进行了一些实验，赢得了弥尔顿的赞赏。许多象征主义者对瓦格纳的钦佩显然是基于这样一种观念（如果这种错误的观念可以被视为一种基础的话）：瓦格纳也在试图识别，或者至少将音乐的节奏与诗歌的节奏紧密联系起来。

The history of music shows a recurrent tendency to develop elaborate contrapuntal structures which, in vocal music, almost annihilate the words. There has also been a recurrent tendency to reform and simplify musical structures in order to give the words more prominence. This has sometimes been the result of religious pressure, but literary influences have been at work too. We may take the madrigal, perhaps, as representing something close to a limit of the subservience of poetry to music. In the madrigal the poetic rhythm disappears as the words are tossed from voice to voice, and the imagery in the words is expressed by the devices of what is usually called program music. We may find long passages filled up with nonsense words, or the whole collection may bear the subtitle “apt for voices or viols,” indicating that the words can be dispensed with altogether. The dislike of poets for this trituration of their words can be seen in the support they gave to the seventeenth-century style of isolating the words on a single melodic line, the style which made the opera possible. This certainly brings us closer to poetry, though music still predominates in the rhythm. But the closer the composer moves toward emphasizing the verbal rhythm of the poem, the closer he comes to the chanting which is the real rhythmical basis of lyric. Henry Lawes made some experiments in this direction which won the applause of Milton, and the admiration that so many symbolistes expressed for Wagner was evidently based on the notion (if so erroneous a notion can be said to be a base) that he was also trying to identify, or at least closely associate, the rhythm of music and the rhythm of poetry.

但现在，既然我们已经将音乐置于抒情诗的一侧，并将纯粹强调语言的吟诵置于中心，我们便可知，抒情诗与另一侧的绘画性也存在着同样重要的联系。这种联系体现在印刷页面上的歌词排版中，可以说，歌词既被“观看”，也被“聆听”。诗节和缩进的排列赋予了抒情诗一种清晰可见的模式，这与诗行长度大致相同的史诗截然不同，当然也与散文不同。无论如何，有成千上万的抒情诗如此专注于视觉意象，以至于我们可以说，它们被赋予了“图画”的意义。在纹章画中，一幅真实的图画赫然出现，而诗人兼画家布莱克（其雕刻的歌词也属于纹章画传统）在抒情诗领域扮演的角色，正如诗人兼作曲家坎皮恩和道兰在音乐领域所扮演的角色一样。意象主义运动非常重视抒情诗中的图像元素，许多意象诗几乎可以被描述为一系列对看不见的图像的说明文字。

But now that we have music on one boundary of lyric, and the purely verbal emphasis of cantillation in the center, we can see that lyric has a relation to the pictorial on the other side which is equally important. Something of this is present in the typographical appearance of a lyric on a printed page, where it is, so to speak, overseen as well as overheard. The arrangement of stanzas and indentations gives a visible pattern to a lyric which is quite distinct from epos, where the lines have approximately the same length, as well as of course from prose. In any case there are thousands of lyrics so intently focussed on visual imagery that they are, as we may say, set to pictures. In the emblem an actual picture appears, and the poet-painter Blake, whose engraved lyrics are in the emblem tradition, has a role in the lyric analogous to that of the poet-composers Campion and Dowland on the musical side. The movement called imagism made a great deal of the pictorial element in the lyric, and many imagistic poems could almost be described as a series of captions to invisible pictures.

在赫伯特的《祭坛》和《复活节之翼》等象征性作品中，诗歌的线条形状暗示了主题的图像形态，我们开始接近抒情诗的图像边界。图像对文字的吸收，正如牧歌对音乐的吸收，便是图画写作，这种写作形式我们最熟悉的便是连环画、带标题的漫画、海报和其他象征性形式。霍加斯的《浪子历程》以及类似的叙事性图画序列，东方的卷轴画，或偶尔出现的木刻小说，都代表了吸收的更高阶段。这些图画排列构成了文学可见基础的图像，而文学的基础是字母顺序的。文字的出现断断续续，零星散漫，从手抄本中的大写字母到拼贴画中的超现实主义实验，其文学意义并不突出。当然，如果我们的文字一直停留在象形文字阶段，它们的意义或许会更加重大，因为在象形文字中，书写和绘画几乎是同一门艺术。我们之前曾略微提及庞德将意象抒情诗与中国象形文字进行比较。

In such emblems as Herbert’s The Altar and Easter Wings, where the pictorial shape of the subject is suggested in the shape of the lines of the poem, we begin to approach the pictorial boundary of the lyric. The absorption of words by pictures, corresponding to the madrigal’s absorption of words by music, is picture-writing, of the kind most familiar to us in comic strips, captioned cartoons, posters, and other emblematic forms. A further stage of absorption is represented by Hogarth’s Rake’s Progress and similar narrative sequences of pictures, in the scroll pictures of the Orient, or in the novels in woodcuts that occasionally appear. Pictorial arrangements of the visible basis of literature, which is alphabetical writing, have had a more fitful and sporadic existence, ranging from capitals in illuminated manuscripts to surrealist experiments in collage, and have not had much specifically literary importance. They would have had more, of course, if our writing had remained in the hieroglyphic stage, as in hieroglyphics writing and drawing are much the same art. We have previously glanced at Pound’s comparison of the imagistic lyric to the Chinese ideogram.

我们应该预料到，上个世纪人们对诗歌与音乐以及与绘画的关系进行了大量的探讨。事实上，使文字尽可能接近音乐中重复而强调的节奏，或绘画中更为凝练的静止状态的尝试，构成了通常所说的实验性写作的主体。如果将这些发展视为对修辞学某一阶段的横向探索，而不是通过与科学的错误类比，将其视为预示着文学技巧在各个领域全面进步的“新方向”，那么思路会更加清晰。同样的进步谬误反过来，会让我们产生关于“颓废”的道德义愤。一个鲜少有人探讨的问题是，诗歌在多大程度上可以融入绘画或音乐，并以不同的节奏回归。例如，中世纪音乐中“散文”的出现就体现了这一点；而当一首歌成为多种不同歌词的节奏库时，这种现象则以另一种方式发生。

We should expect that during the last century there would have been a good deal said about the relation of poetry to music on the one hand, and to painting on the other. In fact the attempts to bring words as near as possible to the more repetitive and emphatic rhythm of music or the more concentrated stasis of painting make up the main body of what is usually called experimental writing. It would make for clearer thinking if these developments were regarded as lateral explorations of a single phase of rhetoric, not, through a false analogy with science, as “new directions” portending a general advance of literary technique on all fronts. The reverse movement of the same progressive fallacy gives us the moral indignation that talks about “decadence.” A question on which little has yet been said is the extent to which poetry may, so to speak, disappear into painting or music and come back with a different rhythm. This happened for example in the emergence of the “prosa” out of the sequence in medieval music, and it happens in a different way when a song becomes a kind of rhythmical reservoir for a number of different lyrics.

构成抒情旋律和韵律基础的潜意识联想的两个要素从未被赋予名称。如果觉得这些词语足够体面，我们可以称它们为胡言乱语和涂鸦。在胡言乱语中，韵律、谐音、头韵和双关语都源于声音联想。赋予这种联想以形态的，正是我们所说的节奏主动性，尽管在自由诗中，它更像是对节奏在一个逐渐被界定为包含形式的区域内的波动的感知。从诗人的修改中我们可以看出，节奏通常先于填充它的词语的选择，无论是在灵感上还是在重要性上，或者两者兼而有之。这种现象并非诗歌所独有：在贝多芬的笔记中，我们也经常看到，在他构思出任何到达某个小节的旋律序列之前，他就知道自己想要在该小节处使用终止式。类似的演变也可见于……孩子们从有节奏的咿呀学语开始，然后逐渐填入合适的词语。这种过程也体现在童谣、大学口号、劳动号子等等之中，其中的节奏是一种接近舞蹈的生理律动，并且常常充斥着无意义的词语。节奏明显优先于意义，这是流行诗歌的常见特征，而诗歌，就像音乐一样，如果节奏像火车车轮瘪了一样，就会被称作“轻快”。

The two elements of subconscious association which form the basis for lyrical melos and opsis respectively have never been given names. We may call them, if the terms are thought dignified enough, babble and doodle. In babble, rhyme, assonance, alliteration, and puns develop out of sound-associations. The thing that gives shape to the associating is what we have been calling the rhythmical initiative, though in a free verse poem it would be rather a sense of the oscillations of rhythm within an area which gradually becomes defined as the containing form. We can see from the revisions poets make that the rhythm is usually prior, either in inspiration or in importance or both, to the selection of words to fill it up. This phenomenon is not confined to poetry: in Beethoven’s notebooks, too, we often see how he knows that he wants a cadence at a certain bar before he has worked out any melodic sequence to reach it. One can see a similar evolution in children, who start with rhythmical babble and fill in the appropriate words as they go along. The process is also reflected in nursery rhymes, college yells, work songs, and the like, where rhythm is a physical pulsation close to the dance, and is often filled up with nonsense words. An obvious priority of rhythm to sense is a regular feature of popular poetry, and verse, like music, is called “light” whenever it has the rhythmical accentuation of a railway coach with a flat wheel.

当胡言乱语无法升华为意识时，它就停留在不受控制的联想层面。后者通常是文学作品中表现精神错乱的一种方式，而斯马特的《欢欣赞美》（Jubilate Agno） ——其中部分内容通常被认为是精神失常的——则展现了创作过程一个有趣的形成阶段：

When babble cannot rise into consciousness, it remains on the level of uncontrolled association. This latter is often a literary way of representing insanity, and Smart’s Jubilate Agno, parts of which are usually considered mentally unbalanced, shows the creative process in an interesting formative stage:

因为在每种语言中，某种动物的力量都占据主导地位。

For the power of some animal is predominant in every language.

猫的力量和精神蕴藏在希腊语中。

For the power and spirit of a CAT is in the Greek.

猫叫声在最有用的介词κατ᾽ εὐχεν …

For the sound of a cat is in the most useful preposition κατ᾽ εὐχεν …

因为老鼠（Mus）在拉丁语中占主导地位。

For the Mouse (Mus) prevails in the Latin.

对于 edi-mus、bibi-mus、vivi-mus——ore-mus ……

For edi-mus, bibi-mus, vivi-mus—ore-mus …

在英国，牛和狗是两种最主要的象征动物。

For two creatures the Bull & the Dog prevail in the English,

所有以ble结尾的单词都存在于这个生物中。

For all the words ending in ble are in the creature.

看不见的、不可理解的、不可言喻的、A-ble……

Invisi-ble, Incomprehensi-ble, ineffa-ble, A-ble …

因为在“公牛”这个词下有很多词……

For there are many words under Bull …

布鲁克在公牛手下。愿上帝怜悯博林布鲁克勋爵。

For Brook is under Bull. God be gracious to Lord Bolingbroke.

或许在所有诗意的思考中，都会出现类似的灵感火花。这段文字中的双关语既令人震惊又令人捧腹，这与弗洛伊德关于机智的观点相符，即机智是冲动挣脱审查机制控制的表现。在创作中，冲动本身就是创造的能量，而审查机制就是我们所说的“合理性原则”。谐音双关是语言创作的基本要素之一，但当一个双关语被引入对话时，它便背离了对话原有的意义，取而代之的是一种自成一体的语言音义模式。

It is possible that similar sputters and sparks of the fusing intellect take place in all poetic thinking. The puns in this passage impress the reader as both outrageous and humorous, which is consistent with Freud’s view of wit as the escape of impulse from the control of the censor. In creation the impulse is the creative energy itself, and the censor is what we have called the plausibility-principle. Paronomasia is one of the essential elements of verbal creation, but a pun introduced into a conversation turns its back on the sense of the conversation and sets up a self-contained verbal sound-sense pattern in its place.

在双关语中，语言的机智与催眠般的咒语之间存在着一种危险的平衡。在爱伦·坡的诗句“小提琴、紫罗兰和葡萄藤”中，我们看到了两种截然相反的特质的融合。机智让我们发笑，它面向的是觉醒的智慧；而咒语本身却缺乏幽默感，令人难以忘怀。机智使读者保持距离；神谕将他吞噬。在像亚瑟·本森的《凤凰》这样的梦境诗中，或者在旨在描绘梦境或昏昏欲睡状态的诗歌中，例如中世纪的《珍珠》以及斯宾塞和丁尼生的许多段落，我们都能注意到对催眠般反复出现的音韵模式的类似强调。如果我们嘲笑像爱伦·坡这样的诗句中的机智，就会破坏他诗歌的魔力，然而这句诗句本身就充满机智，正如《芬尼根守灵夜》是一本非常有趣的书，尽管它从未脱离梦境世界那种神谕般的庄严。当然，在后者中，弗洛伊德和荣格对梦境和机智机制的研究成果得到了广泛的借鉴。其中很可能隐藏着诸如“vinolent”（充满暴力感的）之类的词语，意在一次性表达爱伦·坡这句诗句中的所有含义。在小说中，联想过程通常主要体现在作者为笔下人物创造的名字上。因此，“小人国人”（Lilliputian）和“埃比尼泽·斯克鲁奇”（Ebenezer Scrooge）分别是侏儒和守财奴的联想词，因为前者暗示“小”和“弱小”，后者则暗示“吝啬”、“吝啬”，或许还有“老家伙”。斯宾塞说他笔下的一个人物名叫马尔方特（Malfont）：

There is a perilous balance in paronomasia between verbal wit and hypnotic incantation. In Poe’s line “the viol, the violet and the vine,” we have a fusion of two opposed qualities. Wit makes us laugh, and is addressed to the awakened intelligence; incantation by itself is humorlessly impressive. Wit detaches the reader; the oracle absorbs him. In dream-poems like Arthur Benson’s The Phoenix, or in poems intended to represent dreaming or drowsy states, like the medieval Pearl and many passages in Spenser and Tennyson, we notice a similar insistence on hypnotically recurrent sound-patterns. If we were to laugh at the wit in such a line as Poe’s, we should break the spell of his poem, yet the line is witty, just as Finnegans Wake is a very funny book, although it never leaves the oracular solemnity of the dream world. In the latter, of course, the researches of Freud and Jung into the mechanisms of both dream and wit have been extensively drawn upon. There may well be buried in it some such word as “vinolent,” intended to express everything in Poe’s line at once. In fiction the associative process ordinarily shows itself chiefly in the names the author invents for his characters. Thus “Lilliputian” and “Ebenezer Scrooge” are associative names for midgets and misers respectively, because one suggests “little” and “puny” and the other “squeeze,” “screw” and perhaps “geezer.” Spenser says that a character of his has been named Malfont:

无论是为了伤害，他都做到了。

Eyther for th’ euill, which he did therein,

或者他将其比作一个韦尔赫德人，

Or that he likened was to a welhed,

这意味着他名字的第二个音节既源自fons，也源自facere。我们可以把这种联想过程称为诗意词源学，稍后我们将对此进行更详细的讨论。

which implies that the second syllable of his name is to be derived both from fons and from facere. We may call this kind of associative process poetic etymology, and we shall say more about it later.

胡言乱语的特征在打油诗中再次出现，它也是一种因缺乏技巧或耐心而未完成的创作过程，尽管其心理状态与欢呼雀跃的诗歌截然相反。打油诗并非一定是愚蠢的诗歌；它是一种始于意识层面、从未经过联想过程的诗歌。它具有散文式的主动性，但试图通过意志行为使自身具有联想性，并揭示了伟大诗歌在潜意识层面所克服的相同难题。我们可以看到，在打油诗中，词语是如何因为押韵或韵律而被引入的，思想是如何因为押韵词的暗示而被引入的，等等。刻意创作的打油诗，例如我们在胡迪布拉斯或德国的克尼特尔弗斯中看到的，可以成为精彩的修辞讽刺的源泉，其中包含着对诗歌创作本身的一种戏仿，正如误用词是对诗歌词源学的戏仿一样。要使散文本身具备诗歌那种联想上的集中性，困难重重，而且并不多见。除了福楼拜和乔伊斯之外，散文作家们一直坚定地直面这些问题。

The characteristics of babble are again present in doggerel, which is also a creative process left unfinished through lack of skill or patience, though the psychological conditions are of the opposite kind from those of Jubilate Agno. Doggerel is not necessarily stupid poetry; it is poetry that begins in the conscious mind and has never gone through the associative process. It has a prose initiative, but tries to make itself associative by an act of will, and it reveals the same difficulties that great poetry has overcome at a subconscious level. We can see in doggerel how words are dragged in because they rhyme or scan, how ideas are dragged in because they are suggested by a rhyme-word, and so on. Deliberate doggerel, as we have it in Hudibras or German knittelvers, can be a source of brilliant rhetorical satire, and one which involves a kind of parody of poetic creation itself, just as malapropism is a parody of poetic etymology. The difficulties in the way of giving prose itself something of the associative concentration of poetry are enormous, and not many prose writers, apart from Flaubert and Joyce, have consistently and resolutely faced them.

创作过程中最初的语言构思（“涂鸦”）几乎与联想性的胡言乱语密不可分。一些词句被潦草地记在笔记本上，以备后用；第一节诗可能突然“涌现”，然后必须设计其他结构相同的诗节与之相配，弗洛伊德在梦境中描绘的所有创造力都必须运用到将词语编排成模式的过程中。传统诗歌形式的繁复——十四行诗及其不太灵活的同类诗体，如叙事诗、维拉内拉诗、六行诗等等，以及抒情诗人为自己创造的所有其他惯例——都表明，抒情创作的主动性与真正意义上的“心声”之间究竟有多么遥远。爱伦·坡关于他自己的《乌鸦》的文章，完全准确地描述了他在那首诗中所做的一切，无论他是否像文章所暗示的那样是在有意识的心理层面上进行的，而且这篇文章，就像《诗歌原理》一样，预示了一种新模式的批评技巧。

The first rough sketches of verbal design (“doodle”) in the creative process are hardly separable from associative babble. Phrases are scribbled in notebooks to be used later; a first stanza may suddenly “come” and then other stanzas of the same shape have to be designed to go with it, and all the ingenuity that Freud has traced in the dream has to be employed in putting words into patterns. The elaborateness of conventional forms—the sonnet and its less versatile congeners the ballade, villanelle, sestina, and the like, together with all the other conventions that the individual lyric poet invents for himself—indicates how far removed the lyrical initiative really is from whatever a cri de coeur is supposed to be. Poe’s essay on his own The Raven is a perfectly accurate account of what he did in that poem, whether he did it on the conscious mental level that the essay suggests or not, and this essay, like The Poetic Principle, anticipates the critical techniques of a new mode.

我们不妨注意到，虽然各个时代的歌词都是为了悦耳动听，但随着小说和印刷术的兴起，一种通过视觉来传递信息的趋势日益明显。E·E·卡明斯的视觉模式便是显而易见的例证，但这绝非孤例。玛丽安·摩尔的诗作《萨宾娜山茶花》采用八行诗节，押韵词分别位于第一行末尾、第八行末尾以及第七行的第三个音节。我怀疑即使是最细心的听众，仅凭朗读也未必能听出最后一个押韵：人们首先在纸面上看到它，然后将这种视觉结构模式转化为听觉体验。

We may note that although of course lyrics in all ages are addressed to the ear, the rise of fiction and the printing press develops an increasing tendency to address the ear through the eye. The visual patterns of E. E. Cummings are obvious examples, but do not by any means stand alone. A poem of Marianne Moore’s, Camellia Sabina, employs an eight-line stanza in which the rhyming words are at the end of the first line, at the end of the eighth line, and at the third syllable of the seventh line. I doubt if the most attentive listener could pick this last rhyme up merely from hearing the poem read aloud: one sees it first on the page, and then translates the visual structural pattern to the ear.

现在，我们可以找到更合适的词语来代替“babble”（胡言乱语）和“doodle”（涂鸦），它们分别是抒情词“melos” （旋律）和“opsis” （意为“行为”）的词根。 “melos”的词根是“charm”（魅力）：一种催眠般的咒语，它通过脉动的舞曲节奏，唤起人们不由自主的生理反应，因此与魔法或某种强大的力量的含义相近。值得注意的是，“charm”一词源于“carmen”（歌曲）。真正的咒语具有一种特质，这种特质在通俗文学中被各种劳动歌曲所模仿，尤其是摇篮曲，其中催眠般的重复清晰地展现了其潜在的预言或梦境模式。谩骂或争吵，即文学上对咒语的模仿，也使用了类似的表达方式。出于相反的原因而使用的咒语式装置，例如邓巴与肯尼迪的辩论：

We are now in a position to find more acceptable words for babble and doodle, the radicals of lyrical melos and opsis respectively. The radical of melos is charm: the hypnotic incantation that, through its pulsing dance rhythm, appeals to involuntary physical response, and is hence not far from the sense of magic, or physically compelling power. The etymological descent of charm from carmen, song, may be noted. Actual charms have a quality that is imitated in popular literature by work songs of various kinds, especially lullabies, where the drowsy sleep-inducing repetition shows the underlying oracular or dream pattern very clearly. Invective or flyting, the literary imitation of the spell-binding curse, uses similar incantatory devices for opposite reasons, as in Dunbar’s Flyting with Kennedy:

Mauch 羊肉，byt buttoun，peilit glotoun，空运到希卢斯；

Mauch mutton, byt buttoun, peilit gluttoun, air to Hilhous;

舰队中的乞丐、奥斯蒂尔·德雷加、福尔·弗莱格；

Rank beggar, ostir dregar, foule fleggar in the flet;

Chittirlilling, ruch rilling, like schilling in the milhous;

Chittirlilling, ruch rilling, like schilling in the milhous;

Baird rehator、theif of natour、fals tratour、feyindis gett ……

Baird rehator, theif of natour, fals tratour, feyindis gett …

从这里可以很容易地追溯到对声音和节奏的沉浸式体验，以及英语重音所带来的铿锵有力的节奏和碰撞声响。林赛的《刚果》和《斯威尼·阿戈尼斯特斯》是现代英语诗歌中拉格泰姆风格的代表作，这种风格可以追溯到爱伦·坡的《钟声》和德莱顿的《亚历山大的盛宴》，再到斯凯尔顿和邓巴的《圣母颂歌》。旋律的更精致之处在于，它将重音重复与速度变化相结合。例如怀亚特的十四行诗：

From here the line of descent is easy to the melos of physical absorption in sound and rhythm, the pounding movement and clashing noise which the heavy accentuation of English makes possible. Lindsay’s The Congo and Sweeney Agonistes are modern examples of a tendency to ragtime in English poetry that can be traced back through Poe’s Bells and Dryden’s Alexander’s Feast to Skelton and to Dunbar’s Ane Ballat of our Lady. A more refined aspect of melos is exhibited in lyrics which combine accentual repetition with variations in speed. Thus Wyatt’s sonnet:

我遵守，我遵守，我最好遵守。

I abide and abide and better abide,

而根据古老的谚语，快乐的日子：

And, after the olde proverbe, the happie daye:

我的夫人总是这样对我说：

And ever my ladye to me dothe saye,

“别管我，我会想办法的。”

“Let me alone and I will provyde.”

我遵守，遵守，停留于此

I abide and abide and tarrye the tyde

你们可以一路疾行：

And with abiding spede well ye maye:

我始终如此遵守，

Thus do I abide I wott allwaye,

既未获得也未否认。

Nother obtayning nor yet denied.

哎呀！这漫长的等待

Aye me! this long abidyng

对我来说，半神就像谁说的

Semithe to me as who sayethe

死亡的延长，

A prolonging of a dieng dethe,

或者拒绝想要的东西。

Or a refusing of a desyred thing.

Moche ware it bettre for to be playne,

Moche ware it bettre for to be playne,

然后说要遵守，却不能获得。

Then to saye abide and yet shall not obtayne.

这首优美的十四行诗构思精妙，极具音乐性：反复出现的“abide”铿锵有力，第五节中第一行的重复也颇具音乐性，尽管在诗意上十分大胆。随后，希望接踵而至，怀疑又带来希望，绝望又带来怀疑，轻快的节奏逐渐放缓，最终消散。另一方面，斯凯尔顿（Skelton）如同后来的斯卡拉蒂（Scarlatti）一样，在缓慢的节奏中显得焦躁不安，更倾向于加快速度。以下是《月桂花环》（The Garland of Laurell）中一段韵律优美的诗节的渐快（accelerando）示例：

This lovely sonnet is intensely musical in its conception: there is the repeated clang of “abide” and the musical, though poetically very audacious, sequential repetition of the first line in the fifth. Then as hope follows expectancy, doubt hope, and despair doubt, the lively rhythm gradually slows down and collapses. On the other hand, Skelton, like Scarlatti after him, gets fidgety in a slow rhythm and is more inclined to speed up. Here is an accelerando in a rhyme royal stanza from The Garland of Laurell:

那漫长的时光吹响了一声响亮的号角，

That long tyme blew a full tymorous blaste,

就像博里亚尔的风吹拂时一样，

Like to the Boriall wyndes, whan they blowe,

那些倒塌的塔楼、城镇和树木，

That towres and tounes and trees downe cast,

驱使云朵聚集在一起，如同干燥的雪层；

Drove clouds together like dryftes of snowe;

可怕的晚餐沿着一条路线排成一列行驶；

The dredful dinne drove all the route on a row;

索姆颤抖，索姆紧张，索姆喘息，索姆喘息，

Som trembled, som girned, som gasped, som gased,

就像那些半身像佩维什或被围攻的男人一样。

As people half pevissh or men that were mased.

同一首诗中与音乐有着奇特的巧合联系：献给玛格丽·温特沃斯、玛格丽特·赫西和格特鲁德·斯塔瑟姆的诗句是阿巴卡类型的微型音乐回旋曲。

In the same poem there is a curious coincidental link with music: the verses to Margery Wentworth, Margaret Hussey, and Gertrude Statham are miniature musical rondos of the abaca type.

我们曾多次注意到诗歌中视觉与概念之间的密切联系，而抒情诗中“opsis”一词的词根是“riddle”（谜语），它本质上是感官与反思的融合，即利用感官体验的对象来激发与之相关的思维活动。“riddle”一词最初与“read”（阅读）同源，并且似乎与将语言转化为可见形式的整个过程密切相关，这一过程贯穿于象形文字和表意文字等谜语的衍生形式之中。古英语的谜语诗中包含了一些最优秀的抒情诗，它们属于一个“精巧别致”这样的短语备受推崇的文化。正如咒语与某种魔法般的强制感相近一样，精巧别致的物品，无论是剑柄还是泥金装饰手抄本，都与某种魔力或魔法般的囚禁感相近。与古英语中的谜语非常相似的是一种称为肯宁格或隐晦描述的修辞手法，它将人体称为骨屋，将大海称为鲸鱼之路。

We have several times noticed the close relation between the visual and the conceptual in poetry, and the radical of opsis in the lyric is riddle, which is characteristically a fusion of sensation and reflection, the use of an object of sense experience to stimulate a mental activity in connection with it. Riddle was originally the cognate object of read, and the riddle seems intimately involved with the whole process of reducing language to visible form, a process which runs through such by-forms of riddle as hieroglyphic and ideogram. The actual riddle-poems of Old English include some of its finest lyrics, and belong to a culture in which such a phrase as “curiously inwrought” is a favorite aesthetic judgement. Just as the charm is not far from a sense of magical compulsion, so the curiously wrought object, whether sword-hilt or illuminated manuscript, is not far from a sense of enchantment or magical imprisonment. Closely parallel to the riddle in Old English is the figure of speech known as the kenning or oblique description which calls the body the bone-house and the sea the whale-road.

在诗歌的各个时代，具象与抽象、空间与概念层面的融合，一直是各种诗歌体裁中意象的核心特征，而隐喻（kenning）也传承了悠久的历史。十五世纪出现了“华丽辞藻”（aureate diction），即在诗歌中使用抽象词汇，当时被视为修辞的“色彩”。当这些词汇新颖且其所代表的思想令人兴奋时，华丽辞藻听起来肯定比我们现在听到的要生动得多，也更富有思想上的精确性，例如艾略特的“piaculative pence”（意为“令人愉悦的便士”）或奥登的“cerebrotonic Cato”（意为“脑力激荡的卡托”）。十七世纪则出现了比喻（conceit）或“玄学”诗歌的典型特征是其知识化的意象，巴洛克时期的诗歌往往能够表达一种奔放的设计感，同时又巧妙地、悖论式地展现出设计背后蕴含的张力和紧张感。十八世纪的诗歌语言体现了对抽象思维分类能力的尊重，例如，鱼被描绘成一个有鳍的族群。在模仿主义盛行的低潮期，人们对传统的抵触情绪日益增长，使得诗人对自身使用的陈规俗语不再那么在意，但诗歌意象的技术性问题并未因此消失，传统的修辞手法也依然存在。

In all ages of poetry the fusion of the concrete and the abstract, the spatial and the conceptual aspects of dianoia, has been a central feature of poetic imagery in every genre, and the kenning has had a long line of descent. In the fifteenth century we have “aureate diction,” the use of abstract terms in poetry, then thought of as “colors” of rhetoric. When such words were new and the ideas represented by them exciting, aureate diction must have sounded far less dull and bumbling than it generally does to us, and have had much more of the sense of intellectual precision that we feel in such phrases as Eliot’s “piaculative pence” or Auden’s “cerebrotonic Cato.” The seventeenth century gave us the conceit or intellectualized image of “metaphysical” poetry, typically Baroque in its ability to express an exuberant sense of design combined with a witty and paradoxical sense of the stress and tension underlying the design. The eighteenth century showed its respect for the categorizing power of abstract thought in its poetic diction, in which fish appear as the finny tribe. In the low mimetic period a growing prejudice against convention made poets less aware of the conventional phrases they used, but the technical problems of poetical imagery did not thereby disappear, nor did conventional figures of speech.

其中有两个例子与我们正在讨论的主题——具体与抽象的融合——相关，值得一提。抽象名词的所有格形式，后接形容词和具体名词（例如莎士比亚的“死亡无尽的夜晚”），是十九世纪常用的修辞手法。在J.R.洛厄尔1865年的《哈佛纪念颂》中，这种修辞手法出现了十九次，例如“人生最好的油”、“遗忘的微妙错误”和“命运变幻莫测的月亮”。到了二十世纪，另一种“名词的形容词名词”的修辞手法取而代之，其中第一个名词通常是具体名词，第二个名词是抽象名词。例如：“渴望的苍白黎明”、“沉默的断骨”、“时间的巨大眼睑”、“爱情的绯红之树”。这些是我自己编造的，任何诗人都可以免费使用，但在查阅一本二十世纪的抒情诗集时，我发现，算上所有变体，前五首诗中就有三十八个这样的短语。

Two of these connected with the matter under discussion, the fusion of the concrete with the abstract, may be noted. An abstract noun in the possessive case followed by an adjective and a concrete noun (“death’s dateless night” is a Shakespearean example) is a nineteenth-century favorite. In J. R. Lowell’s Harvard Commemoration Ode of 1865 this figure is employed nineteen times, “life’s best oil,” “Oblivion’s subtle wrong” and “Fortune’s fickle moon” being three examples. In the twentieth century it was succeeded in favor by another phrase of “the adjective noun of noun” type, in which the first noun is usually concrete and the second abstract. Thus: “the pale dawn of longing,” “the broken collar-bone of silence,” “the massive eyelids of time,” “the crimson tree of love.” I have made these up myself, and they are free to any poet who wants them, but on examining a volume of twentieth-century lyrics I find, counting all the variants, thirty-eight phrases of this type in the first five poems.

具体与抽象的融合是上个世纪技术发展使之受到批判性审视的一个普遍原则的特殊案例，尽管它非常重要。所有诗歌意象似乎都建立在隐喻之上，但在抒情诗中，联想过程最为强烈，而普通散文中现成的描述性短语则最为遥远，因此，被称为“误用”（catachresis）的出人意料或强烈的隐喻具有特殊的意义。与其他任何体裁相比，抒情诗更频繁地依赖于新鲜或令人惊讶的意象来达到其主要效果，这一事实常常造成一种错觉，即这种意象是全新的或非传统的。从纳什的《光芒从空中落下》到狄兰·托马斯的《悲伤之前》，抒情诗的情感核心总是反复地倾向于这种融合的隐喻所带来的“突如其来的荣耀”。

The fusion of the concrete and abstract is a special case, though a very important one, of a general principle that the technical development of the last century has exposed to critical view. All poetic imagery seems to be founded on metaphor, but in the lyric, where the associative process is strongest and the ready-made descriptive phrases of ordinary prose furthest away, the unexpected or violent metaphor that is called catachresis has a peculiar importance. Much more frequently than any other genre does the lyric depend for its main effect on the fresh or surprising image, a fact which often gives rise to the illusion that such imagery is radically new or unconventional. From Nashe’s “Brightness falls from the air” to Dylan Thomas’s “A grief ago,” the emotional crux of the lyric has over and over again tended to be this “sudden glory” of fused metaphor.

戏剧的具体形式

SPECIFIC FORMS OF DRAMA
