现在，我们必须考察这种视角拓展——它使我们能够考察词汇或语言模式与音乐和舞台效果之间的关系——是否能为传统的戏剧类型分类带来新的启示。例如，将戏剧分为悲剧和喜剧，这种概念完全基于语言戏剧，并未涵盖或解释歌剧或假面剧等其他戏剧类型，在这些类型中，音乐和布景扮演着更为重要的角色。然而，无论是悲剧还是喜剧，语言戏剧显然已经远远超越了戏剧的原始理念，即为社群呈现一个强烈的感官刺激。中世纪的圣经剧从这个意义上讲是原始的：它们向观众呈现一个对观众而言既熟悉又意义非凡的神话，其目的在于唤起观众对这一神话的共同认知。

We have now to see whether this expansion of perspective, which enables us to consider the relation of the lexis or verbal pattern to music and spectacle, gives us any new light on the traditional classifications within the genres. The division of dramas into tragedies and comedies, for instance, is a conception based entirely on verbal drama, and does not include or account for types of drama, such as the opera or masque, in which music and scenery have a more organic place. Yet verbal drama, whether tragic or comic, has clearly developed a long way from the primitive idea of drama, which is to present a powerful sensational focus for a community. The scriptural plays of the Middle Ages are primitive in this sense: they present to the audience a myth already familiar to and significant for that audience, and they are designed to remind the audience of their communal possession of this myth.

圣经剧是一种精彩绝伦的戏剧体裁，我们可以暂且称之为“神话剧”。它是一种略带消极和接受性的戏剧形式，并会吸收其所描绘的神话的情绪。汤利剧团的《耶稣受难剧》之所以是悲剧，是因为耶稣受难本身就是悲剧；但它并非像《奥赛罗》那样的悲剧。也就是说，它并没有刻意表达悲剧性的观点；它只是因为这个故事耳熟能详且意义重大而将其呈现出来。将诸如傲慢之类的悲剧概念应用于剧中基督的形象是荒谬的，尽管剧中确实唤起了怜悯和恐惧，但这些情绪始终萦绕在人物身上，并没有得到净化。神话剧的典型情绪和结局是沉思的，而在此语境下，沉思意味着持续的、想象力对故事的沉浸。神话剧戏剧性地强调了精神与肉体结合的象征意义。这些圣经剧本身就与圣体节相关，卡尔德隆的宗教剧明确地属于圣餐剧或圣体圣事剧。神话剧的吸引力在于其通俗性和神秘性的奇妙融合；它深受其特定受众的喜爱，但圈外人则需要有意识地去欣赏它。在充满争议的氛围中，它便会消失，因为除非它选择特定的受众，否则就无法处理争议性议题。鉴于“神话”一词的歧义，我们将把这种剧种称为“圣餐剧”。

The scriptural play is a form of a spectacular dramatic genre which we may provisionally call a “myth-play.” It is a somewhat negative and receptive form, and takes on the mood of the myth it represents. The crucifixion play in the Towneley cycle is tragic because the Crucifixion is; but it is not a tragedy in the sense that Othello is a tragedy. It does not, that is, make a tragic point; it simply presents the story because it is familiar and significant. It would be nonsense to apply such tragic conceptions as hybris to the figure of Christ in that play, and while pity and terror are raised, they remain attached to the subject, and there is no catharsis of them. The characteristic mood and resolution of the myth-play are pensive, and pensiveness, in this context, implies a continuing imaginative subjection to the story. The myth-play emphasizes dramatically the symbol of spiritual and corporeal communion. The scriptural plays themselves were associated with the festival of Corpus Christi, and Calderon’s religious plays are explicitly autos sacramentales or Eucharist plays. The appeal of the myth-play is a curious mixture of the popular and the esoteric; it is popular for its immediate audience, but those outside its circle have to make a conscious effort to appreciate it. In a controversial atmosphere it disappears, as it cannot deal with controversial issues unless it selects its audience. In view of the ambiguities attaching to the word myth, we shall speak of this genre as the auto.

当神与英雄之间没有明确界限时在一个社会的神话体系中，或者在贵族和祭司的理想之间，自传体戏剧（auto）可能呈现一个既世俗又神圣的传奇。日本的能剧就是一个例子，它融合了骑士精神和超凡脱俗的象征，以及梦幻般的非悲剧、非喜剧的氛围，深深吸引了叶芝。有趣的是，叶芝在其“世界灵魂”（anima mundi）理论以及他力求使戏剧与观众尽可能贴近的愿望中，都回归了古老的肉体交流观念。在希腊戏剧中，神圣与英雄的主角之间也没有明确的界限。但在基督教社会中，我们可以看到世俗自传体戏剧的雏形，这是一种浪漫主义戏剧，展现英雄的功绩，与悲剧密切相关——英雄的功绩最终以死亡告终——但它本身既非悲剧也非喜剧，其主要特点是壮观的场面。

When there is no clear-cut distinction between gods and heroes in a society’s mythology, or between the ideals of the nobility and the priesthood, the auto may present a legend which is secular and sacred at once. An example is the No drama of Japan, which with its unification of chivalric and otherworldly symbols and its dreamy un-tragic, un-comic mood so strongly attracted Yeats. It is interesting to see how Yeats, both in his theory of the anima mundi and in his desire to get his play as physically close to the audience as possible, reverts to the archaic idea of corporeal communion. In Greek drama, too, there is no sharp boundary line between the divine and the heroic protagonist. But in Christian societies we can see glimpses of a secular auto, a romantic drama presenting the exploits of a hero, which is closely related to tragedy, the end of a hero’s exploit being eventually his death, but which in itself is neither tragic nor comic, being primarily spectacular.

《帖木儿》就是这样一部剧：剧中主人公的傲慢与他的死亡之间的关系与其说是因果关系，不如说是偶然关系。这种戏剧体裁的命运各不相同：例如，在西班牙比在法国更为成功，在法国，悲剧的确立是知识革命的一部分。法国曾两次尝试将悲剧回归英雄传奇，分别是《熙德》和《埃尔纳尼》，但每次都引发了巨大的争议。另一方面，在德国，歌德和席勒的许多剧作显然属于英雄传奇的范畴，尽管它们深受悲剧声望的影响。在瓦格纳的作品中，他将英雄剧的形式扩展到了神圣的神剧领域，而“圣餐”的象征再次占据了显著的位置，在《特里斯坦与伊索尔德》中是负面的，在《帕西法尔》中则是正面的。戏剧越接近悲剧，越远离神圣的自传体戏剧，就越倾向于减少音乐的使用。如果我们看看埃斯库罗斯现存最早的戏剧《请愿者》，就会发现紧随其后的是一种以音乐为主的结构，其现代对应物通常是清唱剧——或许可以将瓦格纳的歌剧描述为发酵的清唱剧。

Tamburlaine is such a play: there the relation between the hero’s hybris and his death is more casual than causal. This genre has had varying luck: more in Spain, for instance, than in France, where the establishing of tragedy was part of an intellectual revolution. The two attempts in France to move tragedy back towards heroic romance, Le Cid and Hernani, each precipitated a big row. In Germany, on the other hand, it is clear that the actual genre of many plays by Goethe and Schiller is the heroic romance, however much affected they have been by the prestige of tragedy. In Wagner, who expands the heroic form all the way back to a sacramental drama of gods, the symbol of communion again occupies a conspicuous place, negatively in Tristan, positively in Parsifal. In proportion as it moves closer to tragedy and further from the sacred auto, drama tends to make less use of music. If we look at the earliest extant play of Aeschylus, The Suppliants, we can see that close behind it is a predominantly musical structure of which the modern counterpart would normally be the oratorio—it is perhaps possible to describe Wagner’s operas as fermented oratorios.

在文艺复兴时期的英国，观众的阶层过于中产阶级化，骑士剧难以站稳脚跟，伊丽莎白时代的世俗戏剧最终演变成了历史剧。历史剧使戏剧形式从视觉奇观转向了更为纯粹的语言表达，象征社会凝聚力的符号也大大减弱，尽管它们依然存在。伊丽莎白时代历史剧的核心主题是国家的统一，以及将观众融入神话之中，使他们成为这种统一的继承者，并与灾难进行对比。内战和软弱的领导。人们甚至可以从红白玫瑰中辨认出世俗的圣餐象征，正如人们可以从那些以指向伊丽莎白女王结尾的戏剧中辨认出的那样，例如皮尔的《巴黎的审判》，它是圣母神秘剧的世俗版本。但历史剧的重点和典型结局在于延续性，以及对悲剧灾难和（如福斯塔夫的例子）喜剧庆典的收尾。人们可以将其与萧伯纳的“编年史剧”《圣女贞德》进行比较，该剧以悲剧结尾，随后的尾声中，贞德的遭遇如同福斯塔夫的遭遇一样，具有历史意义，暗示着延续性而非圆满的结局。

In Renaissance England the audience was too bourgeois for a chivalric drama to get firmly established, and the Elizabethan secular auto eventually became the history-play. With the history-play we move from spectacle to a more purely verbal drama, and the symbols of communion become much attenuated, although they are still there. The central theme of Elizabethan history is the unifying of the nation and the binding of the audience into the myth as the inheritors of that unity, set over against the disasters of civil war and weak leadership. One may even recognize a secular Eucharist symbol in the red and white rose, just as one may recognize in the plays that end by pointing to Elizabeth, like Peele’s Arraignment of Paris, a secular counterpart of a mystery play of the Virgin. But the emphasis and characteristic resolution of the history play are in terms of continuity and the closing up both of tragic catastrophe and (as in the case of Falstaff) of the comic festival. One may compare Shaw’s “chronicle play” of Saint Joan, where the end of the play is a tragedy, followed by an epilogue in which the rejection of Joan is, like the rejection of Falstaff, historical, suggesting continuity rather than a rounded finish.

历史逐渐演变为悲剧，以至于我们常常无法确定何时是情感的交流转变为情感的宣泄。理查二世和理查三世之所以是悲剧，是因为它们最终都以战败的国王为结局；它们之所以是历史剧，是因为它们最终都以博林布鲁克和里士满为结局；我们最多只能说它们更偏向历史。哈姆雷特和麦克白则更偏向悲剧，但福丁布拉斯和马尔科姆这两个贯穿全剧的人物，却在悲剧的结局中体现了历史的元素。历史与喜剧之间的联系似乎远没有那么直接：历史剧中的喜剧场景，可以说具有颠覆性。亨利五世以胜利和婚姻告终，但其中导致福斯塔夫死亡、巴多夫被绞死、皮斯托尔身败名裂的情节，与喜剧的关联远不及理查二世与悲剧的关联。

The history merges so gradually into tragedy that we often cannot be sure when communion has turned into catharsis. Richard II and Richard III are tragedies insofar as they resolve on those defeated kings; they are histories insofar as they resolve on Bolingbroke and Richmond, and the most one can say is that they lean toward history. Hamlet and Macbeth lean toward tragedy, but Fortinbras and Malcolm, the continuing characters, indicate the historical element in the tragic resolution. There seems to be a far less direct connection between history and comedy: the comic scenes in the histories are, so to speak, subversive. Henry V ends in triumph and marriage, but an action that kills Falstaff, hangs Bardolph and debases Pistol is not related to comedy in the way that Richard II is related to tragedy.

我们在此仅探讨悲剧作为一种戏剧形式。悲剧的核心英雄人物源于“自创”（auto），但英雄主义与陨落的关联则源于讽刺的并存。悲剧越接近“自创”，英雄就越与神性紧密相连；越接近讽刺，英雄就越有人性，而灾难也越像是社会事件而非宇宙事件。伊丽莎白时代的悲剧展现了从马洛到韦伯斯特的历史发展：马洛笔下的英雄或多或少如同游走于社会虚空中的半神，而韦伯斯特的悲剧则几乎是对病态社会的临床分析。希腊悲剧从未完全摆脱“自创” ，因此也从未发展出社会悲剧的形式，尽管欧里庇得斯的作品中存在这种倾向。但无论英雄主义和讽刺的比例如何，悲剧本质上都是对事件或神话至高无上的一种诠释。面对悲剧，人们的反应往往是“这一定是这样”，或者说，或许更准确地说，“这种情况确实会发生”：事件本身是首要的，而对事件的解释是次要的，并且是可变的。

We are here concerned only with tragedy as a species of drama. Tragic drama derives from the auto its central heroic figure, but the association of heroism with downfall is due to the simultaneous presence of irony. The nearer the tragedy is to auto, the more closely associated the hero is with divinity; the nearer to irony, the more human the hero is, and the more the catastrophe appears to be a social rather than a cosmological event. Elizabethan tragedy shows a historical development from Marlowe, who presents his heroes more or less as demigods moving in a kind of social ether, to Webster, whose tragedies are almost clinical analyses of a sick society. Greek tragedy never broke completely from the auto, and so never developed a social form, though there are tendencies to it in Euripides. But whatever the proportions of heroism and irony, tragedy shows itself to be primarily a vision of the supremacy of the event or mythos. The response to tragedy is “this must be,” or, perhaps more accurately, “this does happen”: the event is primary, the explanation of it secondary and variable.

随着悲剧向反讽转变，事件不可避免的感觉开始消退，灾难的根源逐渐显现。在反讽中，灾难要么是任意的、毫无意义的，要么是无意识的（或者，在拟人谬误中，是恶意的）世界对有意识的人的影响，要么是或多或少可定义的社会和心理力量的结果。悲剧的“必然如此”变成了反讽的“至少如此”，它强调的是前景事实，摒弃了神话般的上层建筑。因此，反讽戏剧展现的是神学中所谓的堕落世界，是简单的人性，是作为自然之人与人性和非人性冲突的景象。在十九世纪戏剧中，悲剧视角往往与讽刺视角一致，因此，十九世纪的悲剧要么是探讨命运无常的讽刺剧，要么（显然更值得称道的形式）研究人类活动在外部反动社会和内心混乱灵魂的双重压力下所受到的挫败和窒息。这种讽刺在戏剧中难以维持，因为它容易导致行动停滞。在契诃夫的某些段落，尤其是在《三姐妹》的最后一幕中，当人物一个个退缩到各自的主观牢笼中时，我们几乎看到了舞台上所能达到的纯粹讽刺的极致。

As tragedy moves over towards irony, the sense of inevitable event begins to fade out, and the sources of catastrophe come into view. In irony catastrophe is either arbitrary and meaningless, the impact of an unconscious (or, in the pathetic fallacy, malignant) world on conscious man, or the result of more or less definable social and psychological forces. Tragedy’s “this must be” becomes irony’s “this at least is,” a concentration on foreground facts and a rejection of mythical superstructures. Thus the ironic drama is a vision of what in theology is called the fallen world, of simple humanity, man as natural man and in conflict with both human and non-human nature. In nineteenth-century drama the tragic vision is often identical with the ironic one, hence nineteenth-century tragedies tend to be either Schicksal dramas dealing with the arbitrary ironies of fate, or (clearly the more rewarding form) studies of the frustrating and smothering of human activity by the combined pressure of a reactionary society without and a disorganized soul within. Such irony is difficult to sustain in the theatre because it tends toward a stasis of action. In those parts of Chekhov, notably the last act of The Three Sisters, where the characters one by one withdraw from each other into their subjective prison-cells, we are coming about as close to pure irony as the stage can get.

讽刺剧穿过完全现实主义的死胡同，以纯粹的哑剧形式呈现人类生活，不加任何评论，也不强加任何超出简单表演所需之外的戏剧形式。这种偶像崇拜式的模仿形式虽然罕见，但其传统的脉络可以追溯到古典哑剧作家如希罗达斯，直至近代的“生活片段”（tranche-de-vie）后继者。哑剧作为一种个人表演形式较为常见，而在剧院之外，勃朗宁的独角戏则是讽刺冲突中孤立和独白倾向的合乎逻辑的发展。在剧院里，我们通常发现“过于人性化”的生活景象要么令人压抑，要么荒诞可笑，而且往往在两者之间直接转换。因此，讽刺在远离悲剧的同时，开始向喜剧融合。

The ironic play passes through a dead center of complete realism, a pure mime representing human life without comment and without imposing any sort of dramatic form beyond what is required for simple exhibition. This idolatrous form of mimesis is rare, but the thin line of its tradition can be traced from Classical mime-writers like Herodas to their tranche-de-vie descendants in recent times. The mime is somewhat commoner as an individual performance, and, outside the theatre, the Browning monodrama is a logical development of the isolating and soliloquizing tendencies of ironic conflict. In the theatre we usually find that the spectacle of “all too human” life is either oppressive or ridiculous, and that it tends to pass directly from one to the other. Irony, then, as it moves away from tragedy, begins to merge into comedy.

讽刺喜剧当然向我们展现了“世事无常”，但一旦我们在喜剧中发现令人同情甚至中立的角色，我们就进入了更熟悉的喜剧领域，在那里，一群幽默者被另一群幽默者智胜。正如悲剧一样戏剧是一种对神话或已完成之事至高无上的愿景，正如反讽是对人格（或称伦理）的愿景，即人物在环境中的个体化，喜剧则是一种对和谐（或称意义）的愿景，其意义最终指向社会意义，即建立一个理想的社会。作为对生活的模仿，戏剧从神话的角度来看是冲突；从人格的角度来看是代表性的形象；从和谐的角度来看是揭示叙事运动基调的最终和声，它代表着社群。喜剧越是远离反讽，就越接近我们这里所说的理想喜剧，它展现的不是世俗的运行方式，而是你所希望的，你所向往的生活。莎士比亚的主要兴趣在于摆脱反讽喜剧中父子冲突的模式，转向对宁静社群的描绘，这种描绘在《暴风雨》中最为突出。在《暴风雨》中，剧情围绕着一位年轻男子和一位年长男子和谐共处展开，他们既是恋人又是仁慈的老师。

Ironic comedy presents us of course with “the way of the world,” but as soon as we find sympathetic or even neutral characters in a comedy, we move into the more familiar comic area where we have a group of humors outwitted by the opposing group. Just as tragedy is a vision of the supremacy of mythos or thing done, and just as irony is a vision of ethos, or character individualized against environment, so comedy is a vision of dianoia, a significance which is ultimately social significance, the establishing of a desirable society. As an imitation of life, drama is, in terms of mythos, conflict; in terms of ethos, a representative image; in terms of dianoia, the final harmonic chord revealing the tonality under the narrative movement, it is community. The further comedy moves from irony, the more it becomes what we here call ideal comedy, the vision not of the way of the world, but of what you will, life as you like it. Shakespeare’s main interest is in getting away from the son-father conflict of ironic comedy towards a vision of a serene community, a vision most prominent in The Tempest. Here the action is polarized around a younger and an older man working in harmony together, a lover and a benevolent teacher.

下一步，我们将目光转向社会喜剧的极致——会饮。正如我们所料，会饮的结构在柏拉图的著作中最为清晰。柏拉图笔下的苏格拉底既是老师又是爱人，他的愿景是将社会整合到会饮本身的形式中，即辩证的盛宴。正如《法律篇》开篇所解释的，这种盛宴正是维系社会团结的根本力量。不难看出，柏拉图的对话形式具有戏剧性，与喜剧和哑剧有相似之处；尽管柏拉图的思想中有很多内容与我们概述的喜剧精神相悖，但值得注意的是，他直接地反驳了喜剧精神，或者说，他试图“劫持”喜剧精神。似乎有一条不成文的规律：他越是这样做，就越是走向纯粹的阐述或独白式的独白，而远离戏剧。他最具戏剧性的对话，例如《欧绪德谟篇》，往往也是他在哲学“立场”上最犹豫不决的。

The next step brings us to the extreme limit of social comedy, the symposium, the structure of which is, as we should expect, clearest in Plato, whose Socrates is both teacher and lover, and whose vision moves toward an integration of society in a form like that of the symposium itself, the dialectic festivity which, as is explained in the opening of the Laws, is the controlling force that holds society together. It is easy to see that Plato’s dialogue form is dramatic and has affinities with comedy and mime; and while there is much in Plato’s thought that contradicts the spirit of comedy as we have outlined it, it is significant that he contradicts it directly, tries to kidnap it, so to speak. It seems almost a rule that the more he does this, the further he moves into pure exposition or dictatorial monologue and away from drama. The most dramatic of his dialogues, such as Euthydemus, are regularly the most indecisive in philosophical “position.”

在当今时代，萧伯纳一直努力在戏剧中保留会谈的形式。他早期的宣言《易卜生主义的精髓》指出，戏剧应当是对严肃问题的理性探讨；在《结婚》的序言中，他赞赏该剧遵循了时间和空间的统一性。因为萧伯纳类型的喜剧倾向于会谈的形式，其演出时长与观众观看时长相同。然而，萧伯纳在实践中发现，从戏剧会谈中产生的并非一种迫使人们采取某种行动或思考的辩证法，而是一种……这种喜剧摆脱了既定的行为准则。在《好国王查理的黄金时代》这首妙趣横生的小品中，这种喜剧的雏形展现得淋漓尽致：即使是最高尚的人格类型，如圣洁的福克斯和哲思高尚的牛顿，也仅仅因为其他类型人物的存在，就显得滑稽可笑。然而，在《人与超人》中，那位喋喋不休的情人这一核心人物形象却显得格外引人注目；甚至在《回到玛土撒拉》的结尾，主人公放弃了对数学的热爱，也与这种宴饮精神相符。

In our own day Bernard Shaw has tried hard to keep the symposium in the theatre. His early manifesto, The Quintessence of Ibsenism, states that a play should be an intelligent discussion of a serious problem, and in his preface to Getting Married he remarks approvingly on the fact that it observes the unities of time and place. For comedy of Shaw’s type tends to a symposium form which occupies the same amount of time in its action that the audience consumes in watching it. However, Shaw discovered in practice that what emerges from the theatrical symposium is not a dialectic that compels to a course of action or thought, but one that emancipates from formulated principles of conduct. The shape of such a comedy is very clear in the bright little sketch In Good King Charles’s Golden Days, where even the most highly developed human types, the saintly Fox and the philosophical Newton, are shown to be comic humors by the mere presence of other types of people. Yet the central symposium figure of the haranguing lover bulks formidably in Man and Superman, and even the renunciation of love for mathematics at the end of Back to Methusaleh is consistent with the symposium spirit.

那种认为诗歌介于历史与哲学之间，其意象融合了历史的时间事件与哲学的永恒理念的观点，似乎仍然与这种对戏剧形式的阐述息息相关。我们现在可以看到，模仿或语言戏剧从历史剧延伸到哲学剧（即幕剧和场景剧），而哑剧，这种纯粹的意象，则介于两者之间。这三种是专门的形式，是戏剧的基点，而非通用领域。但整个模仿领域只是所有戏剧的一部分，或者说，只是一个半圆。在另一个半圆——壮观戏剧——的迷雾和未知领域中，我们已经确定了一个象限，我们称之为“自体”（auto），现在我们必须描绘出位于自体和喜剧之间的第四个象限，并确定它与自体再次相交的第四个基点。当我们想到属于这个领域的各种繁杂形式时，我们很想把这第四个领域称为“杂项”，然后就此作罢；但正是在这里，我们需要新的普遍性批评。

The view of poetry which sees it as intermediate between history and philosophy, its images combining the temporal events of the one with the timeless ideas of the other, seems to be still involved in this exposition of dramatic forms. We can now see a mimetic or verbal drama stretching from the history-play to the philosophy-play (the act-play and the scene-play), with the mime, the pure image, halfway between. These three are specialized forms, cardinal points of drama rather than generic areas. But the whole mimetic area is only a part, a semicircle, let us say, of all drama. In the misty and unexplored region of the other semicircle of spectacular drama we have identified a quadrant that we have called the auto, and we have now to chart the fourth quadrant that lies between the auto and comedy, and establish the fourth cardinal point where it meets the auto again. When we think of the clutter of forms that belong here, we are strongly tempted to call our fourth area “miscellaneous” and let it go; but it is precisely here that new generic criticism is needed.

喜剧越是远离讽刺，越是歌颂其欢乐社会的自由流动，就越容易融入音乐和舞蹈。随着音乐和布景的重要性日益提升，理想的喜剧便跨越了戏剧的界限，演变为假面剧。在莎士比亚的理想喜剧中，尤其是在《仲夏夜之梦》和《暴风雨》中，与假面剧的密切联系显而易见。假面剧——或者至少是最接近喜剧的那种假面剧，我们在此称之为理想假面剧——仍然属于“dianoia”（赞美）的范畴：它通常是对观众，或其中一位重要成员的赞美，并最终将观众所代表的社会理想化。其情节和人物都相当程式化，因为它们的存在仅仅是为了契合特定场合的意义。

The further comedy moves from irony, and the more it rejoices in the free movement of its happy society, the more readily it takes to music and dancing. As music and scenery increase in importance, the ideal comedy crosses the boundary line of spectacular drama and becomes the masque. In Shakespeare’s ideal comedies, especially A Midsummer Night’s Dream and The Tempest, the close affinity with the masque is not hard to see. The masque—or at least the kind of masque that is nearest to comedy, and which we shall here call the ideal masque—is still in the area of dianoia: it is usually a compliment to the audience, or an important member of it, and leads up to an idealization of the society represented by that audience. Its plots and characters are fairly stock, as they exist only in relation to the significance of the occasion.

因此，它与喜剧的不同之处在于它对事物更亲密的态度。观众：这类戏剧更强调观众与舞台上社群之间的联系。假面剧的演员通常是伪装的观众，当演员摘下面具加入观众的舞蹈时，便象征着一种最终的臣服。理想的假面剧实际上是一种神话剧，类似于自演剧，它与自演剧的关系如同喜剧与悲剧的关系。它旨在强调的并非通过纪律或信仰所能达到的理想，而是人们渴望拥有或认为已经拥有的理想。其场景很少远离魔法和仙境，远离阿卡迪亚和人间天堂的景象。它像自演剧一样自由地运用神祇，但带有占有欲，缺乏想象力的臣服。在西方戏剧中，从文艺复兴到十八世纪末，假面剧和理想喜剧大量运用古典神话，而观众并无义务接受这些神话的“真实性”。

It thus differs from comedy in its more intimate attitude to the audience: there is more insistence on the connection between the audience and the community on the stage. The members of a masque are ordinarily disguised members of the audience, and there is a final gesture of surrender when the actors unmask and join the audience in a dance. The ideal masque is in fact a myth-play like the auto, to which it is related much as comedy is to tragedy. It is designed to emphasize, not the ideals to be achieved by discipline or faith, but ideals which are desired or considered to be already possessed. Its settings are seldom remote from magic and fairyland, from Arcadias and visions of earthly Paradise. It uses gods freely, like the auto, but possessively, and without imaginative subjection. In Western drama, from the Renaissance to the end of the eighteenth century, masque and ideal comedy make great use of Classical mythology, which the audience is not obliged to accept as “true.”

规模相对有限的假面剧为我们理解其两个更为重要且用途广泛的邻居——歌剧和舞台剧——的结构和特征提供了一些启示。假面剧的一侧是音乐编排的戏剧，即我们称之为歌剧的戏剧；另一侧则是舞台剧，如今已融入电影之中。木偶戏和宏大的中国爱情剧（如同电影一样，观众可以随时进出）都是摄影机出现之前的舞台假面剧的例证。歌剧和电影都像假面剧一样，以奢华的展示而闻名。电影之所以如此，部分原因在于许多电影实际上是资产阶级的神话剧，正如几年前六位评论家几乎同时发现的那样。许多影迷对演员私生活的过度关注，或许与假面剧中演员刻意伪装的形象有着某种相似之处。

The rather limited masque throws some light on the structure and characteristics of its two far more important and versatile neighbors. For the masque is flanked on one side by the musically organized drama which we call opera, and on the other by a scenically organized drama, which has now settled in the movie. Puppet-plays and the vast Chinese romances where, as in the movie, the audience enters and leaves unpredictably, are examples of pre-camera scenic masques. Both opera and movie are, like the masque, proverbial for lavish display, and part of the reason for it in the movie is that many movies are actually bourgeois myth-plays, as half a dozen critics suddenly and almost simultaneously discovered a few years ago. The predominance of the private life of the actor in the imaginations of many moviegoers may perhaps have some analogy with the consciously assumed disguise of the masque.

与假面剧不同，歌剧和电影拥有制作精彩绝伦的模仿戏剧作品的能力。歌剧只有简化其音乐结构才能做到这一点，否则，高度重复的音乐结构必然会导致表演变形，从而模糊其戏剧结构。电影也同样必须简化其视觉效果。随着电影遵循其天然的舞台布景倾向，它与其他舞台假面剧形式的相似之处也日益凸显：例如卓别林等人的木偶戏，近期意大利电影中的即兴喜剧，以及音乐喜剧中的芭蕾舞和哑剧。当电影成功模仿一部模仿戏剧时，两者之间的区别便不复存在。这两种形式本身并无必要区分，但它们之间的本质区别却体现在其他方面。模仿剧旨在通过与开端逻辑相连来阐明最终结果：因此，典型的五幕模仿剧结构呈抛物线形，戏剧的目的论特质也体现在“发现”一词中。另一方面，奇观剧本质上是游行式的，倾向于片段式和零散式的发现，正如我们在各种纯粹的奇观形式中看到的那样，从马戏游行到歌舞杂耍。在与奇观剧相对的汽车中，同样的游行式结构也出现在莎士比亚历史剧和圣经故事的长篇叙事中。在电影的轮播放映和随意观看，以及歌剧中通过宣叙调与戏剧结构紧密相连的咏叹调序列中，我们可以看到奇观剧形式中强烈的线性运动倾向。在莎士比亚的第一部实验性浪漫剧《佩里克利斯》中，向列队式结构（即“分散在不同国家”的一系列场景）的转变非常明显。

Opera and movie possess, unlike the masque, the power of producing spectacular imitations of mimetic drama. The opera can only do this by simplifying its musical organization, otherwise its dramatic structure will be blurred by the distortion of acting which the highly repetitive structure of music makes necessary. The movie similarly must simplify its spectacle. In proportion as it follows its natural bent for scenic organization, the movie reveals its affinities with other forms of scenic masque: with the puppet-play in Chaplin and others, with the commedia dell’ arte in recent Italian films, with the ballet and pantomime in musical comedies. When the movie succeeds in imitating a mimetic drama, the distinction between the two forms is not worth making, but the generic difference shows itself in other ways. Mimetic drama works towards an end which illuminates, by being logically connected with, the beginning: hence the parabola shape of the typical five-act mimetic structure, and hence the teleological quality in drama expressed by the term discovery. Spectacular drama, on the other hand, is by nature processional, and tends to episodic and piecemeal discovery, as we can see in all forms of pure spectacle, from the circus parade to the revue. In the auto too, on the other side of spectacular drama, the same processional structure appears in the long continued stories of Shakespearean history and scriptural pageant. In the rotating performance and casual attendance of the movie, and the sequence of arias forcibly linked to dramatic structure by recitative in the opera, one can see the strong native tendency to linear movement in spectacular forms. In Shakespeare’s first experimental romance, Pericles, the movement toward processional structure, a sequence of scenes “dispersedly in various countries,” is very clear.

理想假面剧的精髓在于提升观众的体验，观众是其表演的目标。在自演剧中，戏剧最为客观；观众的任务是接受故事而不加评判。在悲剧中，评判是存在的，但悲剧的根源却在舞台的另一侧；无论它是什么，它都比观众更强大。在讽刺剧中，观众与戏剧直接对峙；在喜剧中，发现的根源则转移到了观众自身。理想的假面剧将观众置于一种凌驾于发现之上的地位。《费加罗的婚礼》中的语言行为是喜剧性的，《唐璜》中的语言行为是悲剧性的；但在这两种情况下，观众都被音乐提升到超越悲剧和喜剧的范畴，尽管他们依然深受感动，但却不会在情感上参与到情节或人物的发现之中。它将唐璜的陨落视为一场精彩绝伦的娱乐，正如众神看待埃阿斯或大流士的陨落一样。这种透过壮观的兴奋感来观看戏剧性模仿的视角，在电影中也至关重要，而这一点在电影的主要灵感来源——木偶戏中则更为明显。我们通过《会饮篇》从讽刺喜剧过渡到理想喜剧，并注意到柏拉图在《会饮篇》结尾预言，同一位诗人应该能够创作悲剧和喜剧，尽管那些最成功地做到这一点的诗人是……那些像莎士比亚和莫扎特一样，对壮观的艺术形式有着浓厚兴趣的人。

The essential feature of the ideal masque is the exaltation of the audience, who form the goal of its procession. In the auto, drama is at its most objective; the audience’s part is to accept the story without judgement. In tragedy there is judgement, but the source of the tragic discovery is on the other side of the stage; and whatever it is, it is stronger than the audience. In the ironic play, audience and drama confront each other directly; in the comedy the source of the discovery has moved across to the audience itself. The ideal masque places the audience in a position of superiority to discovery. The verbal action of Figaro is comic and that of Don Giovanni tragic; but in both cases the audience is exalted by the music above the reach of tragedy and comedy, and, though as profoundly moved as ever, is not emotionally involved with the discovery of plot or characters. It looks at the downfall of Don Juan as spectacular entertainment, much as the gods are supposed to look at the downfall of Ajax or Darius. The same sense of viewing the dramatic mimesis through a haze of spectacular exhilaration is also of central importance in the movie, as it is even more obviously in the puppet-play from which the movie is chiefly descended. We move from ironic to ideal comedy through the symposium, and we note that at the conclusion of Plato’s Symposium the prophecy is made that the same poet should be able to write both tragedy and comedy, though the ones who have done so most successfully are those who, like Shakespeare and Mozart, have had a strong interest in spectacular forms.

接下来，我们必须回到假面剧本身。喜剧越是远离讽刺，体液所拥有的社会权力就越少。在假面剧中，理想社会仍然占据主导地位，体液逐渐堕落为琼森式反假面剧中粗俗的人物，据说这些人物源自一种比假面剧其他部分更为古老的戏剧形式。闹剧作为一种非模仿性的喜剧形式，在假面剧中自然而然地占有一席之地，尽管在理想的假面剧中，它更像是一个严格控制的插曲。在《暴风雨》这部深刻到似乎将整个假面剧都纳入其中的喜剧中，斯蒂法诺和特林库洛是喜剧体液的代表，而卡利班则是反假面剧的人物，这群人物清晰地展现了这种转变。假面剧的主题涉及神祇、仙女和美德的化身；因此，反假面剧中的人物往往变得妖魔化，戏剧人物塑造也开始分裂为善与恶、神与魔、仙女与怪物的对立。这种对立之间的张力在一定程度上解释了假面剧中魔法主题的重要性。在喜剧的结尾，这种魔法掌握在善良的一方手中，例如《暴风雨》；但随着剧情逐渐远离喜剧，冲突变得愈发严肃，反假面剧中的人物也变得不再滑稽可笑，反而更加阴险狡诈，他们自身也拥有了魔法的力量。《科莫斯》正是展现了这一阶段，它与道德剧中善恶的公开冲突非常接近。道德剧让我们进入了假面剧的另一个领域，我们称之为原型假面剧，它是二十世纪大多数高雅戏剧（至少在欧洲大陆）以及许多实验歌剧和不受欢迎的电影的主流形式。

For our next step we must return to the masque proper. The further comedy moves from irony, the less social power is allowed to the humors. In the masque, where the ideal society is still more in the ascendant, the humors become degraded into the uncouth figures of the Jonsonian antimasque, who are said to be descended from a dramatic form far older than the rest of the masque. Farce, being a non-mimetic form of comedy, has a natural place in the masque, though in the ideal masque its natural place is that of a rigorously controlled interlude. In The Tempest, a comedy so profound that it seems to draw the whole masque into itself, Stephano and Trinculo are comic humors and Caliban an antimasque figure, and the group shows the transition very clearly. The main theme of the masque involves gods, fairies, and personifications of virtues; the figures of the antimasque thus tend to become demonic, and dramatic characterization begins to split into an antithesis of virtue and vice, god and devil, fairy and monster. The tension between them partly accounts for the importance of the theme of magic in the masque. At the comic end this magic is held by the benevolent side, as in The Tempest; but as we move further away from comedy, the conflict becomes increasingly serious, and the antimasque figures less ridiculous and more sinister, possessed in their turn of powers of enchantment. This is the stage represented by Comus, which is very close to the open conflict of good and evil in the morality play. With the morality play we pass into another area of masque which we shall here call the archetypal masque, the prevailing form of most twentieth-century highbrow drama, at least in continental Europe, as well as of many experimental operas and unpopular movies.

理想的假面剧倾向于通过指向观众的核心人物来赋予他们个体性：即使是坐在黑暗中、以小组（通常是两人一组）形式观看电影的观众，也是一种相对个体化的群体。随着我们逐渐远离喜剧，一种日益增长的孤独感也愈发明显。典型的假面剧，如同所有形式的戏剧一样，倾向于将场景从时间和空间中剥离出来，但我们并非置身于理想假面剧的田园牧歌式世界，而是常常发现自己身处一种阴森的虚无之中，如同《人人》中死亡的门槛、梅特林克封闭的地下墓穴，或是表现主义戏剧中对未来的噩梦。随着我们越来越接近……的逻辑从形式上看，一体性交流的自我象征再次出现，但这次是以一种心理的、主观的形式，且不涉及神祇。原型假面剧的行动发生在一个由各种人性构成的世界中，而这个世界在其最集中之处便成为人类心灵的内在世界。这一点在《曼金德》和《坚忍城堡》等古老的道德剧中已是显而易见的，至少在梅特林克、皮兰德娄、安德烈耶夫和斯特林堡的许多作品中也隐含其中。

The ideal masque tends to individualize its audience by pointing to the central member of it: even the movie audience, sitting in the dark in small units (usually of two), is a relatively individualized one. A growing sense of loneliness is noticeable as we move away from comedy. The archetypal masque, like all forms of spectacular drama, tends to detach its settings from time and space, but instead of the Arcadias of the ideal masque, we find ourselves frequently in a sinister limbo, like the threshold of death in Everyman, the sealed underworld crypts of Maeterlinck, or the nightmares of the future in expressionist plays. As we get nearer the rationale of the form, we see that the auto symbol of communion in one body is reappearing, but in a psychological and subjective form, and without gods. The action of the archetypal masque takes place in a world of human types, which at its most concentrated becomes the interior of the human mind. This is explicit even in the old moralities, like Mankynd and The Castell of Perseveraunce, and at least implicit in a good deal of Maeterlinck, Pirandello, Andreyev, and Strindberg.

在这种背景下，人物塑造自然必须分解为各种元素和人格碎片。因此，我将这种形式称为原型面具剧，这里的“原型”一词沿用了荣格对人格中能够进行戏剧性投射的方面的定义。荣格的人格面具、阿尼玛、咨询师和阴影等概念，极大地启发了现代寓言剧、心理剧和表现主义戏剧的人物塑造，这些戏剧中充斥着马戏团的叫卖者、幽灵般的女性、深不可测的智者和执迷不悟的恶魔。道德剧中的抽象实体和即兴喜剧（后者代表了该剧种的原始根源之一）中的典型人物，都是类似的建构。

Naturally, with such a setting, characterization has to break down into elements and fragments of personality. This is why I call the form the archetypal masque, the word archetype being in this context used in Jung’s sense of an aspect of the personality capable of dramatic projection. Jung’s persona and anima and counsellor and shadow throw a great deal of light on the characterization of modern allegorical, psychic, and expressionist dramas, with their circus barkers and wraith-like females and inscrutable sages and obsessed demons. The abstract entities of the morality play and the stock types of the commedia dell’ arte (this latter representing one of the primitive roots of the genre) are similar constructions.

孤独感伴随着困惑和恐惧：梅特林克的早期剧作几乎都围绕着恐惧展开，幻觉与现实之间界限的不断模糊——精神投射化为物质实体，反之亦然——将剧情撕裂成万花筒般纷乱的镜像。德国表现主义戏剧中的暴民场景和恰佩克兄弟的机械幻想，都展现了社会背景下同样的瓦解现象。从类型学的角度来看，安德烈耶夫的力作《黑面具》是最引人入胜的原型剧作之一。剧中，作者不仅反映了个人高贵城堡的崩塌（这是其明确的主题），更折射出整个现代俄罗斯的社会崩溃。该剧区分了人格中两类分离的元素，一类与自我谴责相关，另一类与死亡愿望相关，并将人类灵魂描绘成一座被恶魔军团占据的城堡。显而易见，原型假面剧越是偏离理想假面剧，就越清晰地展现出其解放后的反假面剧本质——一群失控的萨提尔的狂欢。复杂戏剧的发展似乎正朝着一种顿悟或对所有戏剧形式中最原始形式的认知迈进。

A sense of confusion and fear accompanies the sense of loneliness: Maeterlinck’s early plays are almost dedicated to fear, and the constant undermining of the distinction between illusion and reality, as mental projections become physical bodies and vice versa, splits the action up into a kaleidoscopic chaos of reflecting mirrors. The mob scenes of German expressionist plays and the mechanical fantasies of the Capeks show the same disintegration at work in a social context. From the generic point of view, one of the most interesting archetypal plays is Andreyev’s powerful The Black Maskers, in which its author saw reflected not only the destruction of an individual’s nobile castello, which is its explicit theme, but the whole social collapse of modern Russia. This play distinguishes two groups of dissociative elements of personality, one group connected with self-accusation and the other with the death-wish, and it exhibits the human soul as a castle possessed by a legion of demons. It is evident that the further the archetypal masque gets from the ideal masque, the more clearly it reveals itself as the emancipated antimasque, a revel of satyrs who have got out of control. The progress of sophisticated drama appears to be towards an anagnorisis or recognition of the most primitive of all dramatic forms.

在原型假面剧的尽头，当它与自演剧（auto）交汇时，我们便抵达了尼采所指出的悲剧诞生之点。在那里，萨提尔的狂欢与威严神祇的显现交织，狄俄尼索斯与阿波罗融为一体。我们可以将戏剧的这第四个关键点称为顿悟，即神圣与魔鬼的戏剧性启示或分离，它与呈现纯粹人性混合的哑剧截然相反。这一点是顿悟点的戏剧形式，最广为人知的例子是《约伯记》在描述了从悲剧到宴饮的完整循环之后，最终在此结束。在这里，巨兽贝希摩斯和利维坦取代了更为常见的恶魔动物。

At the far end of the archetypal masque, where it joins the auto, we reach the point indicated by Nietzsche as the point of the birth of tragedy, where the revel of satyrs impinges on the appearance of a commanding god, and Dionysos is brought into line with Apollo. We may call this fourth cardinal point of drama the epiphany, the dramatic apocalypse or separation of the divine and the demonic, a point directly opposite the mime, which presents the simply human mixture. This point is the dramatic form of the point of epiphany, most familiar as the point at which the Book of Job, after describing a complete circuit from tragedy through symposium, finally ends. Here the two monsters behemoth and leviathan replace the more frequent demonic animals.

从亚里士多德到贺拉斯，古典批评家们都困惑于为何像萨提尔剧这样杂乱无章、粗俗滑稽的闹剧竟会成为悲剧的源泉，尽管他们清楚地知道事实的确如此。在中世纪戏剧中，从神圣英雄的自传体戏剧到悲剧的演进过程远没有那么曲折，其发展也更为清晰。圣经戏剧中最具顿悟意义的形式是《地狱之旅》，它描绘了神圣的救赎者战胜恶魔抵抗的场景。该剧中的魔鬼形象与希腊萨提尔非常相似，而与萨提尔在类型上极为接近的戏剧群体，几乎总是出现在所有直接描写基督的圣经戏剧中，无论是像《牧羊人第二部》中那样温顺敬畏的基督，还是像《耶稣受难记》和《希律王》中那样得意洋洋的邪恶反派。正如希腊悲剧保留并发展了萨提尔剧一样，伊丽莎白时代的悲剧也在其小丑场景和《浮士德》及许多后世悲剧的滑稽情节中保留了萨提尔式的对位。同样的元素也造就了《麦克白》中守门人、 《哈姆雷特》中掘墓人以及《安东尼与克莉奥佩特拉》中持蛇人的精彩片段，这些片段令那些遗忘了萨提尔剧的古典主义评论家们百思不得其解。如果我们能将《泰特斯·安德洛尼克斯》视为一个未经蹂躏的地狱，一个由淫秽而胡言乱语的恶魔组成的萨提尔剧，或许就能更好地理解它的戏剧性。

The Classical critics, from Aristotle to Horace, were puzzled to understand why a disorganized ribald farce like the satyr-play should be the source of tragedy, though they were clear that it was. In medieval drama, where the progression through sacred and heroic auto to tragedy is so much less foreshortened, the development is plainer. The most clearly epiphanic form of scriptural drama is the Harrowing of Hell play, which depicts the triumph of a divine redeemer over demonic resistance. The devils of that play are the Christian forms of figures very like the Greek satyrs, and dramatic groups generically very close to the satyrs are never far from any scriptural play that deals directly with Christ, whether tamed and awed as in the Secunda Pastorum, or triumphantly villainous, as in the crucifixion and Herod plays. And just as Greek tragedy retained and developed the satyr-play, so Elizabethan tragedy retains a satyric counterpoint in its clown scenes and the farcical underplots of Faustus and many later tragedies. The same element provides those superb episodes of the porter in Macbeth, the grave-diggers in Hamlet, and the serpent-bearer in Antony and Cleopatra, which so baffled Classically-minded critics who had forgotten about the satyr-play. Perhaps we could make more dramatic sense out of Titus Andronicus if we could see it as an unharrowed hell, a satyr-play of obscene and gibbering demons.

这部圣经剧的两个节点是圣诞节和复活节：后者展现了凯旋的神，前者则展现了静谧的圣母玛利亚，她聚集了国王和牧羊人的游行假面剧。这个人物与理想假面剧中旁观的女王或贵族截然相反，而贤良却瘫痪的科莫斯圣母则介于两者之间。在《浮士德》和《培尔·金特》这两部宏大的全景式假面剧的结尾，一个象征着某种和解的统一与秩序的女性形象若隐若现，前者中的“永恒女性”形象与此有着一些传统渊源。现代作品中也出现了类似的顿悟形式，从克洛岱尔的《天使报喜》到叶芝的《凯瑟琳伯爵夫人》，不一而足。在《凯瑟琳伯爵夫人》中，女主人公实际上是一位女性的爱尔兰耶稣，她为自己的人民牺牲自己，并凭借其纯洁的本性战胜了魔鬼，这与安瑟伦之前的赎罪论颇为相似。正如叶芝在一则注释中所说，这个故事堪称世间至高无上的寓言之一。

The two nodes of the scriptural play are Christmas and Easter: the latter presents the triumphant god, the former the quiet virgin mother who gathers to herself the processional masque of the kings and shepherds. This figure is at the opposite end of the masque from the watching queen or peeress of an ideal masque, with the virtuous but paralyzed Lady of Comus halfway between. A female figure symbolizing some kind of reconciling unity and order appears dimly at the end of the great panoramic masques of Faust and Peer Gynt, the “eternal feminine” of the former having some of its traditional links. Modern examples of the same epiphanic form range from Claudel’s Annunciation play to Yeats’s Countess Cathleen, where the heroine is really a female and Irish Jesus, sacrificing herself for her people and then cheating the devils by the purity of her nature, very much as in the pre-Anselm theory of the atonement. As Yeats remarks in a note, the story represents one of the supreme parables of the world.

特定主题形式

（抒情诗和史诗）

SPECIFIC THEMATIC FORMS

(LYRIC AND EPOS)

我们曾说过，戏剧是对声音和意象的外在模仿，而抒情诗则是对声音和意象的内在模仿，这两种体裁都避免了直接对话的模仿。同样，根据我们第一篇文章的论述，戏剧倾向于虚构，而抒情诗倾向于主题。我们发现，将戏剧的具体形式视为一系列虚构作品进行考察最为便捷，这也为我们提供了一个粗略但或许有用的戏剧类型分类。现在，我们计划考察一个相应的主题循环，并将此考察应用于抒情诗，以及那些主题足够鲜明或与抒情诗较为接近的史诗形式，包括演说散文。纯粹的叙事诗，作为虚构作品，如果是片段式的，则对应于戏剧类型；如果是连续式的，则对应于我们将在后文探讨的散文小说类型。

We said that the drama was an external and the lyric an internal mimesis of sound and imagery, both genres avoiding the mimesis of direct address. Again, in the terms of our first essay, drama tends to be a fictional and lyric a thematic mode. We found it most convenient to survey the specific forms of drama as a cycle of fictions, and this gave us a rough but possibly useful classification of the species of drama as well. We propose now to make a survey of a corresponding cycle of themes, and apply the survey to the lyric, along with such epos forms, including oratorical prose, as are sufficiently thematic or close to the lyric to belong here. Purely narrative poems, being fictions, will, if episodic, correspond to the species of drama; if continuous, to the species of prose fiction to be examined later.

然而，抒情诗显然可以题材不限，形式不限。它不像戏剧那样受受众的程式化影响，也不像戏剧那样受制于固定的表演形式。因此，本文不会，也无意对抒情诗的具体形式进行分类：它试图阐述的是抒情诗和史诗的主要传统主题。再次强调，本文的目的并非将诗歌“套入”既定的类别，而是通过实证研究来展示传统原型如何在传统体裁中得以体现。

The lyric, however, can obviously be on any subject and of any shape. It is not conventionalized by its audience, like the drama, or by a fixed radical of presentation, such as the drama has in the theatre. Consequently this survey will not give, and is not intended to give, a classification of specific forms of lyric: what it attempts to give is an account of the chief conventional themes of lyric and epos. Once more, the object is not to “fit” poems into categories, but to show empirically how conventional archetypes get embodied in conventional genres.

让我们从我们之前提到的、被认为是抒情诗创作源泉之一的预言式联想过程开始，它与我们在戏剧中所说的顿悟相对应。这一过程最直接的产物之一，便是以音韵集中和意义模糊为特征的宗教诗歌，其中最广为人知的便是……现代的例子是霍普金斯的诗歌。在诸如《珍珠》和赫伯特的许多诗作等具有复杂诗节结构的宗教诗歌中，我们意识到，寻找韵脚和将词语排列成精巧的模式的严谨性，与这种形式所蕴含的克己智慧——一种智力上的牺牲——相契合。这种精巧的语言模式可以追溯到英国诗歌之初阿尔德赫姆的藏头诗，乃至希伯来诗篇本身。

Let us start with the oracular associative process that we identified as one of the initiatives of lyric, and which corresponds to what we called the epiphany in drama. One of the most direct products of this is a type of religious poetry marked by a concentration of sound and ambiguity of sense, of which the most familiar modem example is the poetry of Hopkins. In religious poetry with elaborate stanzaic patterns, such as the Pearl and many poems of Herbert, we realize that the discipline of finding rhymes and arranging words in intricate patterns is appropriate to the sense of chastened wit, a type of sacrificium intellectus, that goes with the form. Such intricate verbal patterns go back through the acrostics of Aldhelm at the very beginning of poetry in England to the Hebrew psalms themselves.

我们注意到，许多宗教文献的写作风格充满了双关语和语言上的回响，诗句和散文之间的节奏界限往往难以清晰区分。圣经的英文译本，尤其是1611年的译本，出色地保留了这种神谕式的散文韵律；当然，希伯来语中的双关语则另当别论。古兰经中奇特的吟诵式圣歌是神谕风格的一个非常纯粹的例子，古典神谕的诗歌歧义也遵循同样的惯例。这些特征在宗教诗歌中以残余的形式保留了下来：在英语中，从盎格鲁-撒克逊时代一直延续到《圣灰星期三》第五部分开头。由此可见，神谕也是一种雄辩散文韵律的萌芽或发展点。这种韵律最明显的体现就是祈祷，而祈祷似乎需要一种并列句式的修辞，即将短句以接近自由诗的节奏串联起来。

We notice that a good deal of sacred literature is written in a style full of puns and verbal echoes, in which the distinction in rhythm between verse and prose is often hard to feel consistently. The English translations of the Bible, especially the 1611, preserve this oracular prose-verse rhythm admirably; the Hebrew puns of course are another matter. The curious sing-song chant of the Koran is a very pure example of oracular style, and the poetic ambiguities of the Classical oracles are in the same convention. Such features survive vestigially throughout religious poetry: in English from Anglo-Saxon times to the opening of the fifth section of Ash Wednesday. From what has been said it is clear that the oracle is the germ or growing point of an oratorical prose rhythm as well. The most obvious result of this is prayer, and prayer seems to require a rhetoric of parataxis, short phrases strung together in a rhythm close to free verse.

在以阿波罗颂歌、希伯来诗篇、基督教圣歌或印度教吠陀经为代表的更为公开的宗教抒情诗中，节奏变得更加庄严、简洁和肃穆，“我”指的是一个可见的信徒群体，句法和用词也更加清晰明确。这类诗歌通常强调神的客观性和至高无上的地位，其抒情诗也体现了一种外部的社会规范感。

In the more public type of religious lyric represented by the Apollonian paean, the Hebrew psalm, the Christian hymn, or the Hindu Vedas, the rhythms become more stately, simple, and dignified, the “I” of the poem is one of a visible community of worshippers, and the syntax and diction become less ambiguous. Here the emphasis is usually thrown on the objectivity and ascendancy of the god, and the lyric reflects the sense of an external and social discipline.

与诗篇或赞美诗相对应的叙事史诗形式，对神祇的描述更为连贯。这种神话包含两个主要部分：传说，讲述神祇的生平或其与子民的过往交往；以及对神祇所需祭祀仪式的描述。通常，前者引出后者，并为其提供解释。荷马史诗主要关注传说；吠陀史诗则倾向于将过去的传说置于当下的祭祀仪式之下。我们可以将《圣经》开篇的创世叙事“P”与吠陀史诗进行比较，后者以诗节体的形式呈现。七日创世记具有许多赞美诗的特征：其中，安息日的设立是创世故事的高潮。与我们稍后将要讨论的更具狂想曲或酒神颂歌风格的形式不同，颂歌或诗篇中敬拜者的愿望与其说是与神合而为一，不如说是与神的敬拜者合而为一。

The narrative epos form corresponding to the psalm or hymn presents a more connected account of the god. This myth has two main parts: legend, recounting the god’s biography or his former dealings with his people; and the description of the ritual he requires. Often the first leads up to, and provides an explanation for, the second. The Homeric hymns are largely concerned with legend; the Vedic hymns tend to subordinate the past legend to the present ritual. One may compare the “P” narrative of creation with which the Bible opens, and which, in the strophic form given it by the seven days of creation, has many of the characteristics of a hymn: here the account of creation has the establishing of the Sabbath as its climax. In contrast to the more rhapsodic or dithyrambic forms that we shall deal with later, the desire of the worshipper in the paean or psalm is not so much to be identified with his god as to be identified as his worshipper.

与赞美诗密切相关的是颂歌，颂扬神祇的人间化身，无论是英雄还是君王。在一些希伯来诗篇中，尤其是第45首，君王是弥赛亚——大卫之子，他为子民承受了极致的荣耀与苦难——的中间人。在希腊文学中，品达的颂歌聚焦于凯旋的运动员，尽管他们是凡人，但颂歌中融入的神话传说赋予了他们与神祇的仪式性联系。在罗马时代，对皇帝和国家的颂扬成为神话颂歌的另一个焦点，这种颂歌形式在维吉尔的第四首田园诗、卡尔普尼乌斯的第一首田园诗以及贺拉斯的《世纪颂歌》中得以延续。后来，颂歌的主要形式演变为赞美宫廷情妇的诗歌。颂词也是一种修辞散文形式，当其主题是人时，其文学成就并不突出，但在更客观的方向上则具有一定的灵活性。赞美美德或文化（尤其是诗歌）的散文颂词不时出现，通常出现在辩护或辩解等准法律语境中。诗歌本身也有诸如圣塞西莉亚颂歌、音乐颂词之类的形式。婚礼颂歌、凯旋诗以及类似的庆典或游行诗歌也属于颂词的范畴。由于颂词本身是一种公共习俗，因此其篇幅通常较长，兼具抒情诗和史诗的特点。

Closely related to the hymn is the panegyrical ode to a human representative of deity, whether hero or king. In some of the Hebrew psalms, notably the 45th, the king is the intermediary figure out of which the Messiah, the son of David who reaches the extreme both of exaltation and of suffering for his people, develops. In Greek literature, the Pindaric ode focusses on the victorious athlete who, though a human figure, has the ritual link with deity brought out by the mythology and legend incorporated into the ode. In Roman times the honors paid to the Emperor and the state provided another focus for mythological panegyric, which continues in the fourth eclogue of Virgil, the first of Calpurnius, and the Carmen Saeculare of Horace. Later the chief form of panegyric becomes the poem in praise of the Courtly Love mistress. The panegyric is also one of the rhetorical prose forms, not one with a very impressive literary record when its subject is a human being, but capable of some flexibility in more impersonal directions. Prose panegyrics of virtues or aspects of culture, notably poetry, appear from time to time, often in the quasi-legal aspect of the apology or defence. In poetry itself we have such forms as the St. Cecilia ode, the panegyric of music. The epithalamium, the triumph, and similar poems of festivity or procession are also species of panegyric. As it is naturally a public convention, the panegyric is often in an extended form which combines both lyric and epos characteristics.

在颂歌中，诗人邀请读者与他一同凝视别处。如果这别处并非显而易见，那么我们便能读到社群之诗，例如各种爱国诗歌。社群之诗将我们引向抒情诗的下一个关键点，即之前所定义的对某种生理或准生理冲动的魅力或回应——或许“推动”一词更为贴切。人们对这种魅力的领悟始于童谣，在童谣中，婴儿随着节奏被摇晃或弹跳，或者主题包含某种对孩子的爱抚。这种魅力贯穿于大学校园的呐喊、歌唱以及其他类似的参与式神秘体验。国歌……诗歌是另一种体现其与社群诗歌密切关系的文体。在早期社会中，我们发现和平时期的劳动歌和战争时期的战斗歌，二者都具有相同的特征。在史诗的发展中，最著名的当属民谣，其诸多特征，例如渐进式的重复以及通常以吸引注意力开头的特点，都与社群诗歌极为相似，以至于一些学者认为其起源于社群创作。与咒语相对应的演说散文的核心是诫命或劝诫，而在以劝诫为基础的较长散文体中，西方文学中最发达的是布道。其他文体将在后文提及。

In the panegyric the poet invites his reader to gaze with him at something else. If this something else is not visibly present, we have the poem of community, such as we get in patriotic verse of all kinds. The poem of community brings us to the next cardinal point of the lyric, defined earlier as the charm or response to some kind of physical or quasi-physical compulsion—perhaps propulsion is the word. One’s education in this type of charm begins with nursery rhymes, where the infant is swung or bounced to the rhythm, or where the theme includes some form of affectionate assault on the child. It continues through college yells, sing-songs, and similar forms of participation mystique. The national anthem is another form which illustrates the close relationship to the poem of community. In earlier societies we find work songs in peace and battle songs in war, both with the same characteristics. Of epos developments, the best known is the ballad, many features of which, such as incremental repetition and the demand for attention with which it often begins, are so close to the poem of community as to have led some scholars to believe that its origin was in communal composition. The cardinal point of oratorical prose corresponding to the charm is the commandment or exhortation, and of the longer prose forms founded on the exhortation the most highly developed in Western literature is the sermon. Other forms will be mentioned later.

参与的神秘感本质上是间歇性的：在原始社群中，它可能通过舞蹈持续数小时；在颓废的社群中，它可能通过演说来维持；但在文明社会中，它则退居幕后。对于文学而言，颂词的可见性消失通常意味着死亡的不可见性出现。颂词式的葬礼颂歌标志着我们从戏剧自传的惯例转向悲剧的惯例。在这里，我们首先遇到的是悼念英雄、朋友、领袖或爱人的挽歌或哀歌。哀歌也表现出强烈的神话扩张倾向：主题不仅被理想化，而且常常被提升为自然精灵或垂死的神祇。田园挽歌传统上将主题与阿多尼斯联系起来，构成了哀歌的传统核心。华兹华斯的一些露西诗表明，即使是非常简短朴素的挽歌也能容纳这样的意象。与之对应的散文体是悼词（oraison funèbre），这种形式在一些现代讣告中得以保留：正如散文体裁的自然特性，神话式的扩展在这里并不明显，往往被教义或概念的扩展所取代。悲剧颂歌（tragic panegyric）是一种罕见且晦涩的史诗体裁，它将英雄既描绘成征服者的英雄，也描绘成悲剧人物。马维尔的《克伦威尔颂》及其原型——贺拉斯的《雷古勒斯颂》便是这种颂歌的代表。

Participation mystique is essentially spasmodic: in primitive communities it may be sustained for hours by dance, and in decadent ones by oratory, but in a state of culture it falls into the background. For literature, the disappearance of the visible presence of panegyric usually means the invisible presence of death. With the panegyrical funeral ode we move from the conventions corresponding to the dramatic auto to those corresponding to tragedy. Here we meet first of all the elegy or threnody on the death of a hero, friend, leader or mistress. Threnodies also show a strong tendency to mythological expansion: the subject is not only idealized but often exalted into a nature-spirit or dying god. The pastoral elegy, which traditionally identifies its subject with Adonis, forms the conventional center of the threnody. Some of Wordsworth’s Lucy poems indicate the capacity of even a very brief and simple elegy to absorb such imagery. The corresponding form in oratorical prose is the oraison funèbre, which survives in some forms of modern obituary: here, as is natural for a prose medium, mythological expansion is less marked, and is often replaced by doctrinal or conceptual expansion. A rare and difficult epos form, the tragic panegyric, in which a hero is presented as a tragic figure as well as a conquering hero, is represented by Marvell’s ode on Cromwell and by its prototype, the Regulus ode of Horace.

在墓志铭的惯例中，我们看到了一种更为独立的挽歌形式，其中往往描绘了逝者一生的完整轮廓。墓志铭的语气可能从颂扬到诙谐不等，但即使在希腊诗选集中，它们仍然保留着作为路标的原始功能，一种引人注目、促使路人驻足阅读的醒目之物。史诗体裁是历史性的墓志铭，是对逝去往昔的沉思，它与废墟的关系，正如个人墓志铭与墓碑的关系。散文体裁中，则有修辞性的挽歌式沉思，以布朗的《瓮葬》为代表。

We come to a more isolated form of elegy in the convention of the epitaph, in which the whole shape of a life is frequently indicated. Epitaphs may vary in tone from the panegyrical to the ribald, but even in the Greek Anthology they retain something of their original function as markers, as something visibly set up to arrest the passer-by and compel him to read. The corresponding epos form is the historical epitaph, the meditation over a vanished past which has the same relation to the ruin that the individual epitaph has to the gravestone. In prose there is the rhetorical elegiac meditation represented in English by Browne’s Urn Burial.

更接近讽刺意味的是哀歌，即流放、忽视或对残酷的抗议之诗。在这里，发出呼唤的个体，与墓志铭中的尸体不同，能够为自己发声，当然，通常被描绘成诗人本人。这一主题占据了宫廷爱情诗的大部分篇幅，其核心原型是轻蔑而无情的情妇。这样的形象是对田园挽歌原始形式的一种讽刺性颠覆。最合乎逻辑地哀悼阿多尼斯之死的人是维纳斯，尽管除非以该神话为主题，否则她在文学作品中很少这样做；但在大多数宫廷爱情诗中，情妇要为恋人的所有苦难，包括他的死亡负责。我们将在本文后面部分讨论这个矛盾的女性形象。哀歌很容易扩展到史诗形式，包括叙事悲剧，在这些悲剧中，情感的焦点不是灾难本身，而是灾难之后的哀悼，例如莎士比亚的两首叙事诗。

Still closer to irony is the complaint, the poem of exile, neglect or protest at cruelty. Here the individual demanding attention, unlike the corpse in the epitaph, is able to speak for himself, and is of course usually represented as the poet himself. This theme takes up most of the Courtly Love convention, where the central archetype is the scornful and unrelenting mistress. Such a figure is an ironic reversal of the original form of pastoral elegy. The most logical person to lament the death of Adonis is Venus, though she seldom does so in literature unless that specific myth is the theme; but in most Courtly Love poetry the mistress is responsible for all the lover’s sufferings, including his death. We shall meet this ambivalent female figure later in the essay. The complaint is easily extended into epos forms, including narrative tragedies in which the emotional focus is not the catastrophe but the lament following the catastrophe, as in the two narrative poems of Shakespeare.

悲剧性讽刺的阶段以忧郁诗的形式呈现，其极端表现形式为厌世或倦怠，诗中人物极度孤立，仿佛活着如同行尸走肉。在波德莱尔的《巨人》中，轻蔑的情妇形象更显阴险，死亡主题被简化为简单的肉体消亡：“尘归尘，土归土”，正如一首中世纪诗歌所言。这一阶段的恰当史诗形式是死亡之舞，即垂死社群的诗歌。

The phase of tragic irony is represented by the poem of melancholy in its extreme form of accidia or ennui, where the individual is so isolated as to feel his existence a living death. In Baudelaire’s géante the scornful mistress takes on a more deeply sinister tone, and the theme of death is presented in terms of simple physical dissolution: “earth upon earth,” as a medieval poem has it. The appropriate epos form of this phase is the danse macabre, the poem of the dying community.

我们下一个关键点很难命名：我们或许可以戏仿霍普金斯的说法，称之为“外景诗”。它是戏剧中“哑剧”的抒情对应物，是悲剧和喜剧中常见的讽刺的核心。这是一种纯粹投射式的超脱，诗人将所有的想象力倾注于观察某个意象、情境或情绪，并将之抛向外部，远离自身。广义上的警句一词可以概括其部分特征，但通常意义上的警句更倾向于喜剧和讽刺。中国和日本的抒情诗似乎很大程度上基于这种惯例，这与西方诗歌形成鲜明对比，西方诗歌中的警句则更倾向于与……相连。表达情感或进行修辞论证。莎士比亚的一些十四行诗，例如《精神的代价是羞耻的浪费》，是例外。

Our next cardinal point is difficult to name: we might almost parody Hopkins’s term and call it the poem of “outscape.” It is the lyrical counterpart of what in drama we call the mime, the center of the irony which is common to tragedy and comedy. It is a convention of pure projected detachment, in which an image, a situation, or a mood is observed with all the imaginative energy thrown outward to it and away from the poet. The word epigram in its broadest sense defines some of its characteristics, except that epigram as ordinarily used leans strongly in the direction of comedy and satire. The lyrical poetry of China and Japan appears to be based very largely on this convention, in striking contrast to Western poetry, where epigram shows much more of a tendency to attach emotions or make out a rhetorical case. Some of Shakespeare’s sonnets, such as “The expense of spirit in a waste of shame,” are exceptions.

散文中与之对应的基本要素是谚语或格言，它是《圣经》智慧文学等文体的雏形。这里我们接近于审慎劝诫式的讽刺，而与神谕截然相反。谚语是一种世俗的或纯粹人性的神谕：它通常具有与神谕相同的修辞特征，如头韵、谐音和排比，但它面向的是超脱的意识和批判性的智慧。它的权威性源于经验：对它而言，智慧是经过实践检验的道路；只有愚人才会追求新奇，而真正的美德是审慎和节制。布莱克的《天堂与地狱的婚姻》中的谚语是戏仿谚语，是从神谕或顿悟的角度写成的。

The corresponding cardinal point of prose is the proverb or aphorism, the germ of such forms as the wisdom literature of the Bible. Here we are close to the counsel-of-prudence type of satire, and at the opposite pole from the oracle. The proverb is a secular or purely human oracle: it usually has the same rhetorical features, alliteration, assonance, parallelism, that we find in the oracle, but it is addressed to the detached consciousness and the critical wit. Its authority comes from experience: for it, wisdom is the tried and tested way; only folly seeks what is new, and the essential virtues are prudence and moderation. The proverbs in Blake’s Marriage of Heaven and Hell are parody-proverbs, written from the oracular or epiphanic point of view.

当我们进入讽刺诗的创作领域，无论是哈代和豪斯曼的抒情诗形式，还是德莱顿和蒲柏的史诗形式，警句和谚语的特征依然存在。这类诗人追求的是精妙和清晰，而非神秘或魔幻，他们的技巧在于意义的集中。这其中有两个关键要素：一是严谨的韵律框架，词语按照清晰的顺序排列；二是明确地表达我们可以期待的音韵模式，例如完整的押韵对句。额外的或意料之外的音韵模式，例如诗行内的头韵或元音韵，都被控制在最低限度。除了韵律之外，诗歌的本质遵循华兹华斯的原则，其用词与非修辞散文非常相似。这一阶段的史诗和散文形式，例如书信体和正式讽刺诗，自然非常接近。

As we move into the conventions of satire, either in the lyric forms of Hardy and Housman or the epos form of Dryden and Pope, the features of epigram and proverb persist. Such poets produce brilliance and clarity rather than mystery or magic, and their technique is concerned with concentration of sense. Two things are essential to this: one is a tight metrical framework of words stepping along in a sharply outlined order; the other is a clear statement of what sound-patterns we may expect, such as the full ring of the rhyming couplet. Additional or unexpected sound-patterns, such as alliteration or assonance within the line, are kept to a minimum, and the poetry follows Wordsworth’s precept in being, except for the metre, very like non-rhetorical prose in its diction. The epos and prose forms of this phase, such as the epistle and the formal satire, are naturally very close together.

在讽刺作品中，观察仍然是首要的，但随着观察的现象从阴森诡谲走向怪诞怪诞，它们也变得越来越虚幻和不真实。我们注意到，在史诗体裁中，有一种与死亡之舞相对应的喜剧形式，即“遗嘱诗”，其中最著名的英文例子是斯威夫特的自传体诗歌。与遗嘱诗形式密切相关的还有约翰·邓恩的《周年纪念》，其中一位少女的死亡被扩展成一部普遍的讽刺作品或“剖析”——这个术语我们稍后还会用到。

In satire observation is still primary, but as the observed phenomena move from the sinister to the grotesque, they grow more illusory and unsubstantial. We note among epos forms a comic counterpart of the danse macabre: the “testament” poem, of which the best known English example is Swift’s poem on his death. Closely related to the testament convention are Donne’s Anniversaries, where the death of a girl expands into a general satire or “anatomy”—this term will also meet us later.

我们现在进入了喜剧领域，仍然处于经验的范畴之内。标志着与讽刺略有区别的惯例是悖论诗，即……的诗歌。某种形式的悖论是其主题，而不仅仅是技巧上的偶然特征。我们自然会在“玄学”诗歌中发现许多此类悖论，这类诗歌经常使用刻意为之、因而带有幽默感的比喻。约翰·邓恩、约翰·赫伯特以及艾米莉·狄金森的作品都提供了例证。悖论往往也是一种情感上的悖论，以至于我们有时会犹豫该认真对待还是以幽默的态度看待这首诗。悖论诗属于经验喜剧的范畴，接近讽刺，因为诗歌中的悖论通常是对堂吉诃德式的爱情或宗教的一种反讽式处理，例如邓恩评论的程式化的彼特拉克式信条“愿不育的天使也如此相爱”，或者赫伯特某些诗歌中自负的美德最终屈辱地沦为人性的一部分。另一种对宫廷爱情传统的悖论式处理是田园诗，或者说是陷入僵局的爱情对话。与史诗密切相关的一种形式是辩论，它让人联想到喜剧与法庭的联系。在辩论中，正反双方就某个问题进行详尽的辩论，然后提交给仲裁人，仲裁人通常会推迟或延后做出裁决。例如《猫头鹰与夜莺》、乔叟的《百鸟议会》和斯宾塞的《变幻诗篇》。

We are now in the area corresponding to comedy, and still within the vision of experience. The convention that marks a slight removal from satire is the poem of paradox, i.e., the poem in which some form of paradox is the theme and not simply an incidental feature of the technique. Naturally we find many of this type in the “metaphysical” poetry which makes a regular use of a deliberately forced and consequently humorous conceit. Donne and Herbert provide examples, and so does Emily Dickinson. The paradox is among other things often a paradox of feeling as well, so that we are sometimes in doubt whether to “take” the poem seriously or humorously. The paradox poem belongs in the comedy of experience, near satire, because paradox in poetry is usually an ironic treatment of quixotic love or religion, like the stylized Petrarchan code of which Donne remarks “May barren angels love so,” or the vaunting virtue that ignominiously collapses into human nature in some poems of Herbert. Another paradoxical treatment of the Courtly Love convention is the pastourelle, or deadlocked love dialogue. A closely related epos form, recalling the association of comedy with law courts, is the debate, in which two sides of a question are argued at length and then submitted to an umpire, who often postpones or puts off the decision. Examples include The Owl and the Nightingale, Chaucer’s Parliament of Fowls, and Spenser’s Mutability Cantos.

一种不那么含糊的抒情喜剧形式是“及时行乐”诗，它基于体验中某个愉悦的瞬间。这类诗歌的基调是超脱的，既有主观的，也有客观的。诗人通常即便在醉酒状态下，也保持着完全的清醒，而愉悦的瞬间本身也脱离了时间。大多数纯粹的欢乐诗都与某种天真的愿景联系在一起，例如布莱克的作品：伟大的伊壁鸠鲁派诗人，从贺拉斯到赫里克，都接受了体验中快乐的局限性，以及它在“无尽黑夜”深渊中的短暂性。即使在赫里克的作品中，也有许多特征，例如对民间传说的热爱以及对服饰、珠宝和香水的意象，表明他更接近假面剧而非喜剧。抒情喜剧中普通体验的极限，体现在宁静心灵的诗歌中，体现在凯旋的“低调满足”（eiron）或“安定的低调满足”中，体现在一种适应体验并摒弃情感幻想的宁静之中。与大多数浪漫主义诗人不同，华兹华斯宁静回忆的模式标志着他倾向于沉浸于体验之中。这种宁静的史诗表达方式通常是描写性的诗歌，诗人攀登山巅，俯瞰山下景色，以此模仿顿悟的时刻。平静的心灵，如果它有一个不值得推荐的主题，就会试图向读者传达一种私人的、秘密的感受，这就引出了下一个关键点，谜语。

A less ambiguous form of lyrical comedy is represented by the carpe diem poem based on a moment of pleasure in experience. The mood of such a poem is one of detachment, both subjective and objective. The poet is usually, even when drunk, in full conscious control, and the moment of pleasure itself is detached from time. Most unqualified poems of joy are associated with some kind of innocent vision, as in Blake: the great Epicurean poets, from Horace to Herrick, accept the limitations of joy in experience, its transience in an abyss of “endless night.” Even in Herrick there are many features, such as the love of folklore and the imagery of clothes, jewels and perfumes, which indicate an affinity with masque rather than comedy. The limits of ordinary experience in lyrical comedy are reached by the poem of the quiet mind, the triumphant eiron or “settled low content,” the serenity which adjusts itself to experience and renounces the emotionally quixotic. Wordsworth’s formula of tranquil recollection marks his tendency to remain within the state of experience, in contrast to most Romantics. The epos expression of serenity is frequently the descriptive poem, where the poet climbs a hill and surveys a landscape below, an imitation in experience of the point of epiphany. The poem of the quiet mind, if it has a subject beyond recommending itself, attempts to communicate to the reader a private and secret possession, which brings us to the next cardinal point, the riddle.

谜语的精髓在于描述性的包围：主题并非被直接描述，而是被限定，如同用文字将其圈起来。在简单的谜语中，中心主题是一个意象，读者会不由自主地去猜测，也就是将诗歌与该意象的名称或符号联系起来。谜语的一种稍为复杂的形式是象征性视觉，它可能是人类最古老的交流方式之一，在这种情况下，举例比描述更为简洁：

The idea of the riddle is descriptive containment: the subject is not described but circumscribed, a circle of words drawn around it. In simple riddles, the central subject is an image, and the reader feels impelled to guess, that is, to equate the poem to the name or sign-symbol of its image. A slightly more complicated form of riddle is the emblematic vision, probably one of the oldest forms of human communication, where an example will be briefer than description:

耶和华对我说：“阿摩司，你看见了什么？”我说：“我看见了铅垂线。”耶和华说：“我必在我民以色列中间设立铅垂线。”

And the Lord said unto me, Amos, what seest thou? And I said, A plumbline. Then said the Lord, Behold, I will set a plumbline in the midst of my people Israel.

其他先知也被描绘成随身携带象征性器物，例如第欧根尼的灯笼，这种修辞手法一直沿用至伯克的匕首。文学发展中也出现了相同形式的象征符号本身，布莱克的《老虎与向日葵》和《病玫瑰》等都属于这一传统，还有赫伯特的《滑轮》等图画式的奇想诗。象征性意象与现代小说中的纹章意象之间的联系显而易见。在象征主义中，我们看到了第三种谜语形式，其中通常包含的是一种情绪而非具体的物体。同样，正如在复杂的发展中经常发生的那样，同一传统中更简单的元素也以残余的形式保留了下来，例如马拉美的谜语“ptyx”。

Other prophets are represented as carrying symbolic apparatus around with them, like Diogenes’ lantern, a rhetorical device surviving as late as Burke’s dagger. Literary developments of the same form include the emblem itself, to the tradition of which Blake’s tiger and sunflower and sick rose belong, and such pictorial conceit-poems as Herbert’s Pulley. The connection of the emblematic vision with the heraldic image of modern fiction is easy to see. In symbolisme we have a third form of riddle where it is normally a mood rather than an object that is contained. Here, too, as usually happens in sophisticated developments, simpler elements in the same tradition survive vestigially, like the riddling “ptyx” in Mallarmé.

谜语和象征性意象与散文中相应的基本要素——寓言或寓言——密切相关，而寓言和寓言当然也都是史诗的形式。寓言是这两种形式中较为简单的一种，更接近于简单的谜语，寓言中蕴含的道德教训与猜谜相对应。寓言则是一种更为复杂的形式，更倾向于蕴含自身的道德教训。在寓言中，神话式的修辞手法（例如会说话的动物）是叙事中常见的特征；而在寓言中，这种修辞手法则不那么明显。在耶稣的寓言中，只有绵羊和山羊的寓言（它带有启示录的意味）大量运用了超出现实可信范围的素材。

The riddle and emblematic vision are closely related to the corresponding cardinal point of prose, which is the parable or fable, both of which are of course epos forms as well. The fable is the simpler of the two forms, and nearer the simple riddle, the providing of the moral in the fable being the counterpart of guessing the riddle. The parable is a more highly developed form with a greater tendency to contain its own moral. In the fable, mythical stylizing (talking animals and the like) is a regular feature of the narrative; in the parable the stylizing is less obvious. Of the parables of Jesus, only the parable of the sheep and goats, which is an apocalypse, makes much use of material outside the realistic range of credibility.

在赫里克的诗作中，我们仍然非常……它与寓言和象征诗的传统十分接近：如此接近，以至于从报春花中“解读一段讲道”并不显得突兀。然而，与华兹华斯不同，赫里克的黄水仙直接面对着某种事物，而这种面对的意象很容易被拟人化。这里我们进入了戏剧中假面剧的领域，纯真的愿景和万物有灵论浪漫主义的仙境再次出现。这种想象性的对抗诗，通过拟人化意象来表达诗人情绪与意象之间的紧密联系，正是济慈颂歌的体裁，《希腊古瓮》则最接近象征诗。下一步将我们带入田园诗的领域，在那里我们回到了第一篇文章中提到的浪漫主义模式，怜悯和恐惧成为愉悦的模式，通常分别代表着美和崇高。人们通常认为这两种情绪是对比，就像弥尔顿那美妙的田园诗和沉思诗的二联画一样，但有时，就像马维尔的一些“绿色”诗歌一样，我们会看到一种完全沉浸其中的诗歌，以至于这两种情绪似乎融合为一体。

In Herrick’s poems on primroses and daffodils we are still very close to the fable and emblem tradition: so close that there is no incongruity in “reading a lecture” from the primroses. Nevertheless Herrick’s daffodils, unlike Wordsworth’s, are directly confronted, and the confronted image readily becomes personified. Here we are in the area corresponding to the masque in drama, and the innocent vision and the fairyland of animistic romance return. The poem of imaginative confrontation, where a close connection between the poet’s mood and the imagery is expressed by the personifying of the imagery, is the genre of the Keats ode, the Grecian Urn being the nearest to the emblem poem. The next step takes us into the pastoral, where we come back to the mode of romance mentioned in the first essay, pity and terror becoming modes of pleasure, usually the beautiful and the sublime respectively. These are generally thought of as a contrast, as they are in Milton’s wonderful diptych of idyllic and pensive moods, but occasionally, as in some of the “green” poems of Marvell, we have a poetry of absorption so complete that the two moods seem blended into one.

但当纯真愿景趋于统一时，与之形成对比的经验愿景往往会再次出现，这种惯例我们可以称之为意识扩展的诗歌。在这种诗歌中，诗人将经验观带来的净化感与精神的、不可见的或想象的世界带来的狂喜感相平衡。在此，如同在相应的戏剧形式中一样，我们看到的并非对生活的直接模仿，而是对生活的奇观式模仿，这种模仿能够俯视经验，正是因为同时存在着另一种愿景。在戏剧中，这种奇观式模仿是借助音乐和视觉效果实现的。音乐和绘画无法表达悲剧或喜剧，因为它们仅仅是语言概念：它们表达的是情绪，如果我们事先准备好某种文学纲领，就可以将这些情绪赋予悲剧或喜剧的内涵。在我们这个时代，意识扩展诗歌最令人印象深刻的例子是艾略特的四重奏和里尔克的杜伊诺挽歌，前者的音乐典故和后者的绘画意象表达了这种体裁与那些比诗歌更明显地不说话的艺术的密切联系。

But when the vision of innocence becomes unified, the contrasting vision of experience often reappears, in a convention that we might call the poem of expanded consciousness, where the poet balances the catharsis of his view of experience with the ecstasis of his view of a spiritual, invisible, or imaginative world. Here, as in the corresponding forms of drama, we have not a direct mimesis of life but a spectacular mimesis of it, able to look down on experience because of the simultaneous presence of another kind of vision. In drama this spectacular mimesis is attained by the help of music as well as spectacle. Music and painting cannot express the tragic or comic, which are verbal conceptions only: they express moods which we may fit to tragedy or comedy if we have some literary program ready for them. In our day the most impressive examples of the poem of expanded consciousness are the Eliot quartets and the Duino elegies of Rilke, and the musical references of the one and the pictorial images of the other express the close affinity of the genre with arts which, much more obviously than poetry, do not speak.

下一个惯例我们可以称之为“认知诗”，这种诗歌颠倒了梦境与清醒的通常关联，使得经验似乎成了噩梦，而幻象似乎成了现实。这种惯例的史诗形式包括中世纪的爱情幻象，其中我们再次看到了奇观。 这种情感源于身处一个非凡的世界，从而建立起一种直接的个人关系。就抒情诗体而言，一个非常纯粹的现代例子，就其体裁而言，是艾略特的《玛丽娜》，它与相应的戏剧形式十分接近。里尔克的许多《俄耳甫斯》十四行诗也属于此类；它也是沃恩和特拉赫恩的核心创作手法。这种主题在散文的节奏中较为罕见且难以驾驭，但在《沉思录》中却有所体现，尤其是著名的“庄稼是东方不朽的小麦”这一段落。

The next convention we might call the recognition poem, the poem which reverses the usual associations of dream and waking, so that it is experience that seems to be the nightmare and the vision that seems to be reality. The epos form of this convention includes the medieval love vision, where we have again a spectacle of a direct personal relation, attained by being placed in an extraordinary world. Of lyrical forms, a very pure modern example, generically speaking, is Eliot’s Marina, which is close to the corresponding dramatic forms. Many of Rilke’s Orpheus sonnets belong to it; it is also the central convention of Vaughan and Traherne. This theme is rare and difficult to handle in the rhythm of prose, but we have it in the Centuries of Meditation, especially the famous “The corn was orient and immortal wheat” passage.

自我认知诗是一类非常重要的诗歌类型，诗人自身参与其中，从经验中觉醒，进入一种充满灵性的现实。例如柯林斯的《论诗歌性格》、柯勒律治的《忽必烈汗》以及叶芝的《塔》和《驶向拜占庭》。这一体裁接近我们接下来要讨论的最后一类主题的边界，而这类主题又将我们带回了神谕。这些诗歌形式是酒神颂或狂想曲，诗人在诗中感受到某种内在的、近乎个人的力量占据了自身。与自我认知诗最接近的是象征回应诗，例如克拉肖的一些颂歌；在浪漫主义时期，一种更为主观的酒神颂诗形式变得非常流行。雪莱的《西风颂》、斯温伯恩的大量作品、维克多·雨果、尼采（他曾奇特地声称自己发明了酒神颂）、布莱克的预言，尤其是《四佐阿斯》的第九夜，以及斯马特的两首伟大诗篇，都是例证。这些作品大多是史诗形式：酒神颂本身就适合采用重复的韵律。在抒情诗形式方面，我们可以注意到疯歌的惯例，这种形式出现在《李尔王》中埃德加的歌谣、叶芝的《疯癫的简》诗篇，以及包括斯科特在内的其他一些诗人的零星作品中。由于疯歌的演唱者通常是流浪汉，他暗示着自己与神秘的存在和力量（例如自然精灵）之间比常人更为密切的联系。在更复杂的层面上，当诗人暗示将独立的幻象融入自己的思想时，我们可以提及兰波的启示诗。

A very important group of recognition poems are the poems of self-recognition, where the poet himself is involved in the awakening from experience into a visionary reality. Examples include Collins’s Ode on the Poetical Character, Coleridge’s Kubla Khan, and Yeats’s Tower and Sailing to Byzantium. This genre is near the boundary line of our next and last group of themes, which bring us back to the oracle again. These are the dithyrambic or rhapsodic forms, where the poet feels taken possession of by some internal and quasi-personal force. Nearest the poem of recognition is the poem of iconic response, such as we have in some of the odes of Crashaw; in Romantic times a more subjective and dithyrambic form became very popular. Shelley’s Ode to the West Wind, a good deal of Swinburne, of Victor Hugo, of Nietzsche (who makes the curious statement that he invented the dithyramb), of Blake’s prophecies, especially the ninth night of The Four Zoas, and the two great poems of Smart, are examples. Most of these are epos forms: the dithyrambic lends itself readily to recurring metre. Of lyric forms, we may note the convention of the mad song, which we have in Edgar’s songs in King Lear, in Yeats’s Crazy Jane poems, and sporadically in a few other poets, including Scott. As the singer of a mad song is usually a vagrant, he suggests a closer rapport with mysterious beings and forces, such as nature-spirits, than normal people have. On a more sophisticated level, where the poet suggests the breaking of autonomous visions into his own mind, the illuminations of Rimbaud may be mentioned.

随着我们逐渐接近最初那种充满预言性的节奏，诗歌和散文的节奏开始再次融合。例如，我们注意到惠特曼的诗歌中，每行结尾都有一个明显的停顿——这很自然，因为在节奏不规则的地方，连续的诗行毫无意义。这种节奏正趋向于一种形式，在这种形式中，抒情的联想节奏、史诗般的诗行和散文的句子几乎成为同一个整体，这是一种趋势。我们可以观察到，无论是像奥西恩的诗歌那样天真质朴的酒神颂，还是像《地狱之季》之后法国现代酒神颂那样精妙复杂的作品，都体现了这一点。

As we come nearer to the oracular rhythm with which we began, the rhythms of verse and prose begin to merge once more. We notice in Whitman, for example, that there is a strong pause at the end of every line—naturally enough, for where the rhythm is irregular there is no point in a run-on line. The rhythm is approaching a form in which the lyrical associative rhythm, the epos line and the prose sentence are becoming much the same unit, a tendency that we can observe in dithyrambic poetry as naive as Ossian’s or as sophisticated as the modern French developments of it that follow the Saison en Enfer.

特定连续体形式

（散文小说）

SPECIFIC CONTINUOUS FORMS

(PROSE FICTION)

将“虚构”一词用于以散文为主的文字体裁时，我们便会与“虚构的真正含义是虚假或不真实”的观点相冲突。因此，如果图书管理员相信作者，那么图书馆收到的自传就会被归类为非虚构作品；如果她认为作者在撒谎，则会被归类为虚构作品。很难看出这种区分对文学批评家有何用处。既然“虚构”一词，如同诗歌一样，其词源学含义是“为自身而创作”，那么它完全可以用于批评任何形式的、具有连续性的文学作品，而这几乎总是指散文作品。或者，即便这要求过高，至少也可以对将“虚构”等同于我们所知的唯一真正虚构形式——小说——的草率做法提出抗议。

In assigning the term fiction to the genre of the written word, in which prose tends to become the predominating rhythm, we collide with the view that the real meaning of fiction is falsehood or unreality. Thus an autobiography coming into a library would be classified as non-fiction if the librarian believed the author, and as fiction if she thought he was lying. It is difficult to see what use such a distinction can be to a literary critic. Surely the word fiction, which, like poetry, means etymologically something made for its own sake, could be applied in criticism to any work of literary art in a radically continuous form, which almost always means a work of art in prose. Or, if that is too much to ask, at least some protest can be entered against the sloppy habit of identifying fiction with the one genuine form of fiction which we know as the novel.

让我们来看看几本介于“非虚构”和“文学”之间的未分类书籍。《项狄传》是小说吗？几乎所有人都会说是，尽管它对“故事价值”毫不在意。 《格列佛游记》是小说吗？大多数人会对此表示异议，包括杜威十进制分类法，它将其归类为“讽刺与幽默”。但想必大家都会称其为虚构作品，如果它是虚构作品，那么虚构作品作为一个类别和小说作为该类别的一个种之间就存在区别。那么，如果将讨论范围扩大到虚构作品，《衣裳哲学》是虚构作品吗？如果不是，为什么？如果它是，《忧郁的解剖》是虚构作品吗？它是一种文学形式，还是仅仅是一部文笔优美的“非虚构”作品？《拉文格罗》是虚构作品吗？《人人文库》认为是；《世界经典》则将其归类为“旅行与地形学”。

Let us look at a few of the unclassified books lying on the boundary of “non-fiction” and “literature.” Is Tristram Shandy a novel? Nearly everyone would say yes, in spite of its easygoing disregard of “story values.” Is Gulliver’s Travels a novel? Here most would demur, including the Dewey decimal system, which puts it under “Satire and Humor.” But surely everyone would call it fiction, and if it is fiction, a distinction appears between fiction as a genus and the novel as a species of that genus. Shifting the ground to fiction, then, is Sartor Resartus fiction? If not, why not? If it is, is The Anatomy of Melancholy fiction? Is it a literary form or only a work of “non-fiction” written with “style”? Is Borrow’s Lavengro fiction? Everyman’s Library says yes; the World’s Classics puts it under “Travel and Topography.”

这位将虚构作品等同于小说的文学史家，对世界在没有小说的情况下运转如此之久感到十分尴尬。直到他读到笛福的作品才获得解脱，他的视野才得以真正开阔起来。他被迫将都铎时期的虚构作品简化为一系列尝试性的小说形式的散文，这种做法对德洛尼的作品尚可接受，但却使西德尼的作品显得荒谬可笑。他假定十七世纪存在一个巨大的虚构作品空白期，而这一空白期恰好涵盖了修辞学的黄金时代。散文。他最终发现，“小说”一词——直到1900年左右，它还指代一种或多或少可辨识的文学形式——如今已演变成一个包罗万象的术语，几乎可以用来指代任何不以“主题”为核心的散文作品。显然，这种以小说为中心的散文小说观是一种托勒密式的视角，如今已过于复杂而不再适用，必须用一种更为相对、更为“哥白尼式”的视角取而代之。

The literary historian who identifies fiction with the novel is greatly embarrassed by the length of time that the world managed to get along without the novel, and until he reaches his great deliverance in Defoe, his perspective is intolerably cramped. He is compelled to reduce Tudor fiction to a series of tentative essays in the novel form, which works well enough for Deloney but makes nonsense of Sidney. He postulates a great fictional gap in the seventeenth century which exactly covers the golden age of rhetorical prose. He finally discovers that the word novel, which up to about 1900 was still the name of a more or less recognizable form, has since expanded into a catchall term which can be applied to practically any prose book that is not “on” something. Clearly, this novel-centered view of prose fiction is a Ptolemaic perspective which is now too complicated to be any longer workable, and some more relative and Copernican view must take its place.

当我们开始认真思考小说，不是将其视为虚构作品，而是将其视为一种虚构形式时，我们会发现，无论小说的特征是什么，都使得笛福、菲尔丁、奥斯汀和詹姆斯等人在其传统中占据核心地位，而博罗、皮科克、梅尔维尔和艾米莉·勃朗特等人则显得有些边缘化。这并非是对优劣的评判：我们或许认为《白鲸》比《利己主义者》 “更伟大” ，但同时又觉得梅瑞狄斯的作品更接近于一部典型的小说。菲尔丁将小说视为散文体喜剧史诗的构想，似乎是他为之做出巨大贡献的这一传统的根本所在。在我们认为的典型小说中，例如简·奥斯汀的作品，情节和对话都与风俗喜剧的惯例紧密相连。《呼啸山庄》的惯例则更多地与故事和民谣联系在一起。她们似乎更倾向于悲剧，而那些在简·奥斯汀的作品中会破坏整体基调平衡的激情与愤怒等悲剧性情感，在这里却能得到妥善的容纳。超自然元素，或者说对超自然元素的暗示，也同样可以融入其中，这在小说中是很难实现的。情节结构也截然不同：艾米莉·勃朗特并没有像简·奥斯汀那样围绕中心事件展开叙事，而是以线性叙事的方式讲述故事，而且她似乎需要一位叙述者的帮助，这在简·奥斯汀的作品中会显得格格不入。如此迥异的惯例使我们有理由将《呼啸山庄》视为一种不同于小说的散文体裁，我们不妨称之为“浪漫小说”。这里我们又一次在不同的语境中使用了同一个词，但总的来说，“浪漫小说”似乎比“故事”更贴切，“故事”似乎更适合篇幅较短的作品形式。

When we start to think seriously about the novel, not as fiction, but as a form of fiction, we feel that its characteristics, whatever they are, are such as make, say, Defoe, Fielding, Austen, and James central in its tradition, and Borrow, Peacock, Melville, and Emily Bronte somehow peripheral. This is not an estimate of merit: we may think Moby Dick “greater” than The Egoist and yet feel that Meredith’s book is closer to being a typical novel. Fielding’s conception of the novel as a comic epic in prose seems fundamental to the tradition he did so much to establish. In novels that we think of as typical, like those of Jane Austen, plot and dialogue are closely linked to the conventions of the comedy of manners. The conventions of Wuthering Heights are linked rather with the tale and the ballad. They seem to have more affinity with tragedy, and the tragic emotions of passion and fury, which would shatter the balance of tone in Jane Austen, can be safely accommodated here. So can the supernatural, or the suggestion of it, which is difficult to get into a novel. The shape of the plot is different: instead of manoeuvering around a central situation, as Jane Austen does, Emily Bronte tells her story with linear accents, and she seems to need the help of a narrator, who would be absurdly out of place in Jane Austen. Conventions so different justify us in regarding Wuthering Heights as a different form of prose fiction from the novel, a form which we shall here call the romance. Here again we have to use the same word in several different contexts, but romance seems on the whole better than tale, which appears to fit a somewhat shorter form.

小说与言情小说的本质区别在于人物塑造的理念。言情小说作家并不试图塑造“真实的人”，而是塑造风格化的形象，这些形象逐渐演变为心理原型。在言情小说中，我们分别在男主角、女主角和反派身上看到了荣格的力比多、阿尼玛和阴影的体现。正因如此，言情小说常常散发出小说所缺乏的主观强烈感，也正因如此，其边缘总是隐隐透着寓言的意味。某些元素浪漫小说中人物性格的释放，使其自然而然地成为比小说更具革命性的形式。小说家关注的是人物的个性，是人物戴着各自的面具或社会面具。他需要一个稳定的社会框架，而我们许多最优秀的小说家都过于墨守成规，甚至到了吹毛求疵的地步。浪漫小说家关注的是个性，是处于幻想理想化状态的人物，无论他多么保守，某种虚无主义和难以驯服的东西都可能不断地从他的文字中迸发出来。

The essential difference between novel and romance lies in the conception of characterization. The romancer does not attempt to create “real people” so much as stylized figures which expand into psychological archetypes. It is in the romance that we find Jung’s libido, anima, and shadow reflected in the hero, heroine, and villain respectively. That is why the romance so often radiates a glow of subjective intensity that the novel lacks, and why a suggestion of allegory is constantly creeping in around its fringes. Certain elements of character are released in the romance which make it naturally a more revolutionary form than the novel. The novelist deals with personality, with characters wearing their personae or social masks. He needs the framework of a stable society, and many of our best novelists have been conventional to the verge of fussiness. The romancer deals with individuality, with characters in vacuo idealized by revery, and, however conservative he may be, something nihilistic and untamable is likely to keep breaking out of his pages.

因此，散文爱情小说是一种独立的虚构形式，它有别于长篇小说，并从如今被统称为“长篇小说”的杂糅的散文作品中脱颖而出。即使在被称为短篇小说的另一类作品中，我们也能将爱伦·坡的短篇小说形式单独挑出来，它与完整的爱情小说之间的关系，正如契诃夫或凯瑟琳·曼斯菲尔德的短篇小说与长篇小说之间的关系一样。“纯粹”的爱情小说或短篇小说形式都不存在；几乎所有现代爱情小说都可以被视为长篇小说，反之亦然。散文小说的形式是混合的，就像人类的种族血统一样，不像性别那样泾渭分明。事实上，大众对小说的需求总是混合的，既要浪漫到足以让读者将自己的欲望投射到男主角身上，将自己的灵魂投射到女主角身上，又要足够新颖，使这些投射保持在一个熟悉的世界中。因此，人们可能会问，做出上述区分有何用处？尤其是在批评界尚未充分发展，但这种区分并非无人意识到的情况下。听说特罗洛普写过小说和威廉·莫里斯的爱情故事，这并不令人惊讶。

The prose romance, then, is an independent form of fiction to be distinguished from the novel and extracted from the miscellaneous heap of prose works now covered by that term. Even in the other heap known as short stories one can isolate the tale form used by Poe, which bears the same relation to the full romance that the stories of Chekhov or Katherine Mansfield do to the novel. “Pure” examples of either form are never found; there is hardly any modern romance that could not be made out to be a novel, and vice versa. The forms of prose fiction are mixed, like racial strains in human beings, not separable like the sexes. In fact the popular demand in fiction is always for a mixed form, a romantic novel just romantic enough for the reader to project his libido on the hero and his anima on the heroine, and just novel enough to keep these projections in a familiar world. It may be asked, therefore, what is the use of making the above distinction, especially when, though undeveloped in criticism, it is by no means unrealized. It is no surprise to hear that Trollope wrote novels and William Morris romances.

原因在于，一位伟大的浪漫小说家应当从他所选择的文学传统角度进行考察。威廉·莫里斯不应仅仅因为批评家尚未学会认真对待浪漫小说这一文体就被排除在散文小说之外。此外，鉴于前文对浪漫小说革命性的论述，也不应将他选择这一文体视为对其社会态度的“逃避”。如果斯科特有资格被称为浪漫小说家，那么仅仅关注他作为小说家的缺陷就不是好的批评。同样， 《天路历程》的浪漫特质、其原型化的人物塑造以及其对宗教体验的革命性诠释，使其成为一种文学形式的典范：它并非仅仅是英国文学为了补充宗教内容而吞噬的一本书。最后，当霍桑在《霍桑之家》的序言中写道…… 《七个尖角阁》的作者坚持认为他的故事应该被当作浪漫故事而不是小说来读，他可能确实是这么想的，尽管他表示，竞争形式的声望促使这位浪漫故事作者为没有采用这种形式而道歉。

The reason is that a great romancer should be examined in terms of the conventions he chose. William Morris should not be left on the side lines of prose fiction merely because the critic has not learned to take the romance form seriously. Nor, in view of what has been said about the revolutionary nature of the romance, should his choice of that form be regarded as an “escape” from his social attitude. If Scott has any claims to be a romancer, it is not good criticism to deal only with his defects as a novelist. The romantic qualities of The Pilgrim’s Progress, too, its archetypal characterization and its revolutionary approach to religious experience, make it a well-rounded example of a literary form: it is not merely a book swallowed by English literature to get some religious bulk in its diet. Finally, when Hawthorne, in the preface to The House of the Seven Gables, insists that his story should be read as romance and not as novel, it is possible that he meant what he said, even though he indicates that the prestige of the rival form has induced the romancer to apologize for not using it.
