浪漫小说比小说更古老，这一事实造成了一种历史错觉，认为浪漫小说是一种需要被淘汰的、不成熟且不成熟的文体。浪漫小说的社会属性，以及其对英雄主义和纯洁的严肃理想化，与贵族阶层密切相关（关于这一点与前文提及的该文体革命性本质的明显矛盾，请​​参阅前文对浪漫小说神话的引言）。在被称为浪漫主义的时期，浪漫小说复兴，成为浪漫主义倾向的一部分，这种倾向体现了对古老封建主义和英雄崇拜，或对理想化性欲的崇敬。在英国，斯科特的浪漫小说，以及程度稍逊的勃朗特姐妹的浪漫小说，是神秘的诺森伯兰文艺复兴的一部分，是浪漫主义对中部地区新兴工业化的反动，而这场工业化也催生了华兹华斯和伯恩斯的诗歌以及卡莱尔的哲学思想。因此，在更偏向资产阶级的小说中，对浪漫小说及其理想的戏仿成为重要主题也就不足为奇了。《堂吉诃德》开创的传统在一种以独特视角审视爱情故事的小说类型中得以延续，这种小说将两种形式的惯例融合在一起，形成一种讽刺性的复合体，而非感伤的混合体。此类小说的例子包括《诺桑觉寺》、《包法利夫人》和《吉姆爷》。

Romance is older than the novel, a fact which has developed the historical illusion that it is something to be outgrown, a juvenile and undeveloped form. The social affinities of the romance, with its grave idealizing of heroism and purity, are with the aristocracy (for the apparent inconsistency of this with the revolutionary nature of the form just mentioned, see the introductory comment on the mythos of romance in the previous essay). It revived in the period we call Romantic as part of the Romantic tendency to archaic feudalism and a cult of the hero, or idealized libido. In England the romances of Scott and, in less degree, the Brontes, are part of a mysterious Northumbrian renaissance, a Romantic reaction against the new industrialism in the Midlands, which also produced the poetry of Wordsworth and Burns and the philosophy of Carlyle. It is not surprising, therefore, that an important theme in the more bourgeois novel should be the parody of the romance and its ideals. The tradition established by Don Quixote continues in a type of novel which looks at a romantic situation from its own point of view, so that the conventions of the two forms make up an ironic compound instead of a sentimental mixture. Examples range from Northanger Abbey to Madame Bovary and Lord Jim.

浪漫小说中的寓言倾向可能是自觉的，如《天路历程》；也可能是无意识的，如威廉·莫里斯作品中显而易见的性神话。浪漫小说以英雄为主角，介于以人为主角的小说和以神为主角的神话之间。散文浪漫小说最早出现于古典神话的后期发展阶段，冰岛的散文萨迦紧随神话埃达之后。小说则倾向于以虚构的方式呈现历史。菲尔丁将《汤姆·琼斯》称为历史小说的直觉是正确的，这得到了普遍规律的印证：小说的格局越大，其历史性质就越明显。然而，由于小说是创造性的历史，小说家通常更倾向于使用具有可塑性或大致当代性的素材，并感到受限于固定的历史模式。《威弗利》的创作时间距今约六十年，《小多丽》则距今约四十年，但浪漫小说的历史模式是固定的，而《小多丽》的历史模式是可塑的。小说暗示了一个普遍原则，即大多数“历史小说”本质上都是浪漫小说。同样，当小说所反映的生活逝去后，其浪漫魅力也会随之增强：因此，在二战期间，特罗洛普的小说主要被当作浪漫小说来解读。或许正是与历史的联系以及对时代背景的感知，使得小说与世界范围内流行的浪漫小说形成鲜明对比，将小说局限于时间与西方人的结合之中。

The tendency to allegory in the romance may be conscious, as in The Pilgrim’s Progress, or unconscious, as in the very obvious sexual mythopoeia in William Morris. The romance, which deals with heroes, is intermediate between the novel, which deals with men, and the myth, which deals with gods. Prose romance first appears as a late development of Classical mythology, and the prose Sagas of Iceland follow close on the mythical Eddas. The novel tends rather to expand into a fictional approach to history. The soundness of Fielding’s instinct in calling Tom Jones a history is confirmed by the general rule that the larger the scheme of a novel becomes, the more obviously its historical nature appears. As it is creative history, however, the novelist usually prefers his material in a plastic, or roughly contemporary state, and feels cramped by a fixed historical pattern. Waverley is dated about sixty years back from the time of writing and Little Dorrit about forty years, but the historical pattern is fixed in the romance and plastic in the novel, suggesting the general principle that most “historical novels” are romances. Similarly a novel becomes more romantic in its appeal when the life it reflects has passed away: thus the novels of Trollope were read primarily as romances during the Second World War. It is perhaps the link with history and a sense of temporal context that has confined the novel, in striking contrast to the worldwide romance, to the alliance of time and Western man.

自传是另一种与小说通过一系列不易察觉的渐进式融合而融合的文体。大多数自传都源于一种创作冲动，这种冲动带有虚构的成分，即只选取作者生活中那些能够构建完整模式的事件和经历。这种模式可能超越作者自身，成为他认同的对象；也可能仅仅是他性格和态度的内在一致性。我们可以将这种非常重要的散文小说形式称为“忏悔体”，这一名称源于圣奥古斯丁（他似乎是这种文体的创始人）和卢梭（他确立了现代忏悔体的类型）。早期的传统为英国文学贡献了《医者之信》、《恩典满溢》和纽曼的《辩护词》，此外还有神秘主义者所推崇的那种相关但又略有不同的忏悔体。

Autobiography is another form which merges with the novel by a series of insensible gradations. Most autobiographies are inspired by a creative, and therefore fictional, impulse to select only those events and experiences in the writer’s life that go to build up an integrated pattern. This pattern may be something larger than himself with which he has come to identify himself, or simply the coherence of his character and attitudes. We may call this very important form of prose fiction the confession form, following St. Augustine, who appears to have invented it, and Rousseau, who established a modern type of it. The earlier tradition gave Religio Medici, Grace Abounding, and Newman’s Apologia to English literature, besides the related but subtly different type of confession favored by the mystics.

同样，正如浪漫小说一样，承认自白作品中存在一种独特的散文形式也具有一定的价值。这使得我们一些最优秀的散文作品在虚构作品中找到了一个明确的定位，而不是让它们处于一种模糊的境地——它们既不完全属于文学，因为它们是“思想”；也不完全属于宗教或哲学，因为它们只是散文风格的范例。自白作品也像小说和浪漫小说一样，拥有其自身的短篇形式，即我们熟悉的随笔。蒙田的《好愚行之书》就是一部由随笔组成的自白作品，它唯一缺少的是长篇作品中那种连续的叙事结构。蒙田的这种结构之于自白作品，正如由短篇小说组成的虚构作品，例如乔伊斯的《都柏林人》或薄伽丘的《十日谈》，之于小说或浪漫小说。

Here again, as with the romance, there is some value in recognizing a distinct prose form in the confession. It gives several of our best prose works a definable place in fiction instead of keeping them in a vague limbo of books which are not quite literature because they are “thought,” and not quite religion or philosophy because they are Examples of Prose Style. The confession, too, like the novel and the romance, has its own short form, the familiar essay, and Montaigne’s livre de bonne foy is a confession made up of essays in which only the continuous narrative of the longer form is missing. Montaigne’s scheme is to the confession what a work of fiction made up of short stories, such as Joyce’s Dubliners or Boccaccio’s Decameron, is to the novel or romance.

卢梭之后——实际上正是在卢梭的作品中——忏悔融入了小说，这种融合催生了虚构自传、艺术家小说以及其他类似类型。忏悔的主题并非必须是作者本人，戏剧性的忏悔至少从《莫尔·弗兰德斯》开始就已出现在小说中。“意识流”技巧使得这两种形式的融合更加集中，但……即使在这里，忏悔录特有的特征也清晰可见。几乎总是，对宗教、政治或艺术的某种理论和知识兴趣在忏悔录中扮演着主导角色。正是忏悔录作者成功地将自己的思想整合于这些主题之上，才使他觉得自己的人生值得书写。然而，这种对思想和理论陈述的兴趣与小说的真正精髓格格不入，小说的技术难点在于将所有理论融入到人际关系之中。以简·奥斯汀为例，教会、国家和文化从未被单独审视，而只是作为社会数据来探讨；亨利·詹姆斯则被誉为拥有如此精妙的头脑，任何思想都无法撼动它。那些离不开思想，或者没有耐心像詹姆斯那样消化思想的小说家，会本能地诉诸于密尔所说的单一人物的“精神史”。当我们发现对美学理论的技术性探讨构成了乔伊斯《青年艺术家画像》的高潮时，我们意识到，使这一切成为可能的，是这部小说中存在着另一种散文小说的传统。

After Rousseau—in fact in Rousseau—the confession flows into the novel, and the mixture produces the fictional autobiography, the Künstler-roman, and kindred types. There is no literary reason why the subject of a confession should always be the author himself, and dramatic confessions have been used in the novel at least since Moll Flanders. The “stream of consciousness” technique permits of a much more concentrated fusion of the two forms, but even here the characteristics peculiar to the confession form show up clearly. Nearly always some theoretical and intellectual interest in religion, politics, or art plays a leading role in the confession. It is his success in integrating his mind on such subjects that makes the author of a confession feel that his life is worth writing about. But this interest in ideas and theoretical statements is alien to the genius of the novel proper, where the technical problem is to dissolve all theory into personal relationships. In Jane Austen, to take a familiar instance, church, state, and culture are never examined except as social data, and Henry James has been described as having a mind so fine that no idea could violate it. The novelist who cannot get along without ideas, or has not the patience to digest them in the way that James did, instinctively resorts to what Mill calls a “mental history” of a single character. And when we find that a technical discussion of a theory of aesthetics forms the climax of Joyce’s Portrait, we realize that what makes this possible is the presence in that novel of another tradition of prose fiction.

小说往往是外向且个人化的；它主要关注的是人性在社会中的展现。爱情小说则往往是内向且个人化的：它也描写人物，但方式更为主观。（这里的主观指的是处理方式，而非题材。爱情小说中的人物往往是英雄式的，因此难以捉摸；小说家因为更加客观，所以能够更自由地进入人物的内心世界。）自白也属于内向型，但其内容更具理性化。显然，我们下一步要探索的是第四种小说形式，即外向且理性的小说。

The novel tends to be extroverted and personal; its chief interest is in human character as it manifests itself in society. The romance tends to be introverted and personal: it also deals with characters, but in a more subjective way. (Subjective here refers to treatment, not subject-matter. The characters of romance are heroic and therefore inscrutable; the novelist is freer to enter his characters’ minds because he is more objective.) The confession is also introverted, but intellectualized in content. Our next step is evidently to discover a fourth form of fiction which is extroverted and intellectual.

我们之前提到过，大多数人会把《格列佛游记》称为虚构作品，但不会称之为长篇小说。那么它必然是另一种虚构形式，因为它确实有其形式。当我们从卢梭的《爱弥儿》转向伏尔泰的《老实人》 ，或者从巴特勒的《众生之路》转向《埃瑞璜》系列，或者从赫胥黎的《对位论》转向《美丽新世界》时，我们感觉自己正从长篇小说转向这种形式，无论它是什么。因此，这种形式有其自身的传统，并且，正如巴特勒和赫胥黎的例子所示，即使在长篇小说盛行的时代，它也保留了一定的完整性。它的存在很容易证明，没有人会质疑《格列佛游记》和《老实人》的文学渊源可以追溯到拉伯雷、伊拉斯谟和卢奇安。但是，尽管人们对拉伯雷、斯威夫特和……的风格和思想已经进行了很多讨论，伏尔泰的作品很少被人们视为在特定媒介中创作的匠人，而这一点对于任何一位小说家来说都是不容忽视的。另一位同属这一传统的伟大作家，赫胥黎的老师皮科克，境遇更糟。由于他的写作风格不被理解，人们普遍认为他在散文小说发展史上的地位只是一个粗制滥造的怪才。事实上，他在自己的领域里是一位技艺精湛、精准无比的艺术家，正如简·奥斯汀在她的领域里一样。

We remarked earlier that most people would call Gulliver’s Travels fiction but not a novel. It must then be another form of fiction, as it certainly has a form, and we feel that we are turning from the novel to this form, whatever it is, when we turn from Rousseau’s Emile to Voltaire’s Candide, or from Butler’s The Way of All Flesh to the Erewhon books, or from Huxley’s Point Counterpoint to Brave New World. The form thus has its own traditions, and, as the examples of Butler and Huxley show, has preserved some integrity even under the ascendancy of the novel. Its existence is easy enough to demonstrate, and no one will challenge the statement that the literary ancestry of Gulliver’s Travels and Candide runs through Rabelais and Erasmus to Lucian. But while much has been said about the style and thought of Rabelais, Swift, and Voltaire, very little has been made of them as craftsmen working in a specific medium, a point no one dealing with a novelist would ignore. Another great writer in this tradition, Huxley’s master Peacock, has fared even worse, for, his form not being understood, a general impression has grown up that his status in the development of prose fiction is that of a slapdash eccentric. Actually, he is as exquisite and precise an artist in his medium as Jane Austen is in hers.

这些作者采用的讽刺形式是梅尼普斯讽刺诗，也称瓦罗讽刺诗（但这种形式较为少见），据说是由一位名叫梅尼普斯的希腊犬儒学家所创。他的作品已佚失，但他有两位杰出的弟子：希腊的卢奇安和罗马的瓦罗。瓦罗本人也仅存残篇，他的讽刺传统由佩特罗尼乌斯和阿普列乌斯继承。梅尼普斯讽刺诗似乎是在诗歌讽刺诗的基础上，通过穿插散文段落而发展起来的，但我们目前所知的梅尼普斯讽刺诗只有散文形式，尽管其反复出现的特征之一（如《孔雀》所示）是穿插诗句。

The form used by these authors is the Menippean satire, also more rarely called the Varronian satire, allegedly invented by a Greek cynic named Menippus. His works are lost, but he had two great disciples, the Greek Lucian and the Roman Varro, and the tradition of Varro, who has not survived either except in fragments, was carried on by Petronius and Apuleius. The Menippean satire appears to have developed out of verse satire through the practice of adding prose interludes, but we know it only as a prose form, though one of its recurrent features (seen in Peacock) is the use of incidental verse.

梅尼普式讽刺与其说是关注人物本身，不如说是关注人物的心理态度。迂腐之人、偏执狂、怪人、暴发户、艺术大师、狂热分子、贪婪无能的各色专业人士，都被置于其职业生活态度而非社会行为的语境中进行刻画。因此，梅尼普式讽刺与忏悔录在处理抽象概念和理论方面颇为相似，而与小说则在人物塑造上有所不同——前者风格化而非自然主义，将人物描绘成其所代表思想的代言人。此处并无泾渭分明的界限，也不应如此划分，但如果我们比较简·奥斯汀笔下的人物和皮科克笔下的类似人物，便能立刻感受到两种形式之间的差异。韦斯特恩乡绅属于小说范畴，而斯瓦克姆和斯奎尔则带有梅尼普式讽刺的血统。这一传统中一个永恒的主题是对“光荣哲学家”（philosophus gloriosus）的嘲讽，这一点前文已有所论述。小说家将邪恶和愚蠢视为社会疾病，但梅尼普讽刺作家则将它们视为智力疾病，一种疯狂的学究气，而光荣的哲学家既象征又定义了这种学究气。

The Menippean satire deals less with people as such than with mental attitudes. Pedants, bigots, cranks, parvenus, virtuosi, enthusiasts, rapacious and incompetent professional men of all kinds, are handled in terms of their occupational approach to life as distinct from their social behavior. The Menippean satire thus resembles the confession in its ability to handle abstract ideas and theories, and differs from the novel in its characterization, which is stylized rather than naturalistic, and presents people as mouthpieces of the ideas they represent. Here again no sharp boundary lines can or should be drawn, but if we compare a character in Jane Austen with a similar character in Peacock we can immediately feel the difference between the two forms. Squire Western belongs to the novel, but Thwackum and Square have Menippean blood in them. A constant theme in the tradition is the ridicule of the philosophus gloriosus, already discussed. The novelist sees evil and folly as social diseases, but the Menippean satirist sees them as diseases of the intellect, as a kind of maddened pedantry which the philosophus gloriosus at once symbolizes and defines.

佩特罗尼乌斯、阿普列乌斯、拉伯雷、斯威夫特和伏尔泰都采用了一种结构松散的叙事形式，这种形式常被误认为是浪漫传奇。然而，它与浪漫传奇有所不同（尽管拉伯雷的作品中也大量融入了浪漫传奇的元素），因为它主要关注的并非冒险经历。它并非以英雄为主角，而是依赖于自由的智力想象和那种能产生讽刺意味的幽默观察。它也不同于流浪汉小说，后者关注的是社会的实际结构。梅尼普式的讽刺作品在其最精炼的层面，向我们展现了一种基于单一智力模式的世界观。故事构建的智力结构对传统的叙事逻辑造成了剧烈的冲击，尽管由此产生的看似漫不经心的表象，实际上反映的只是读者的漫不经心，或是他们倾向于以小说本身为中心的观念来评判虚构作品。

Petronius, Apuleius, Rabelais, Swift, and Voltaire all use a loose-jointed narrative form often confused with the romance. It differs from the romance, however (though there is a strong admixture of romance in Rabelais), as it is not primarily concerned with the exploits of heroes, but relies on the free play of intellectual fancy and the kind of humorous observation that produces caricature. It differs also from the picaresque form, which has the novel’s interest in the actual structure of society. At its most concentrated the Menippean satire presents us with a vision of the world in terms of a single intellectual pattern. The intellectual structure built up from the story makes for violent dislocations in the customary logic of narrative, though the appearance of carelessness that results reflects only the carelessness of the reader or his tendency to judge by a novel-centered conception of fiction.

在罗马和文艺复兴时期，“讽刺”一词指的是两种特定的文学形式，一种是散文（本文所指），另一种是诗歌。如今，它指的是一种结构原则或态度，我们称之为“神话” （mythos ）。在我们讨论过的梅尼普式讽刺作品中，这种形式的名称也适用于这种态度。作为一种态度，讽刺正如我们所见，是幻想与道德的结合。但作为一种形式的名称，“讽刺”一词虽然局限于文学领域（因为作为一种神话，它可以出现在任何艺术形式中，例如漫画），却更加灵活，它可以是完全虚构的，也可以是完全道德的。因此，梅尼普式的冒险故事可能纯粹是幻想，就像文学童话一样。《爱丽丝梦游仙境》系列是完美的梅尼普式讽刺作品，受拉伯雷影响的《水孩子》也是如此。纯粹的道德类型是对社会作为单一知识模式的严肃构想，换句话说，是一种乌托邦。

The word “satire,” in Roman and Renaissance times, meant either of two specific literary forms of that name, one (this one) prose and the other verse. Now it means a structural principle or attitude, what we have called a mythos. In the Menippean satires we have been discussing, the name of the form also applies to the attitude. As the name of an attitude, satire is, we have seen, a combination of fantasy and morality. But as the name of a form, the term satire, though confined to literature (for as a mythos it may appear in any art, a cartoon, for example), is more flexible, and can be either entirely fantastic or entirely moral. The Menippean adventure story may thus be pure fantasy, as it is in the literary fairy tale. The Alice books are perfect Menippean satires, and so is The Water-Babies, which has been influenced by Rabelais. The purely moral type is a serious vision of society as a single intellectual pattern, in other words a Utopia.

梅尼普斯式讽刺的短篇形式通常是对话或会谈，其戏剧性在于思想的冲突而非人物的冲突。这是伊拉斯谟最喜爱的形式，在伏尔泰的作品中也很常见。这种形式并非总是带有讽刺意味，而是会逐渐转向更纯粹的幻想或道德探讨，例如《兰多尔的虚构对话》或《死者的对话》。有时，这种形式会扩展成完整的篇幅，并采用两个以上的对话者：此时的背景通常是晚宴或宴饮，例如佩特罗尼乌斯作品中占据重要地位的宴会。柏拉图虽然比梅尼普斯早得多涉足这一领域，但他对这种类型的影响却十分显著，这种类型以不间断的传统延续至今，体现在卡斯蒂廖内笔下那些优雅悠闲的对话中，这些对话塑造了理想的朝臣形象，也体现在沃尔顿对垂钓的理论和纪律的阐述中。现代发展则体现在皮科克、赫胥黎及其模仿者笔下的乡村别墅周末场景中。所表达的观点、想法和文化兴趣与性爱本身同样重要。

The short form of the Menippean satire is usually a dialogue or colloquy, in which the dramatic interest is in a conflict of ideas rather than of character. This is the favorite form of Erasmus, and is common in Voltaire. Here again the form is not invariably satiric in attitude, but shades off into more purely fanciful or moral discussions, like the Imaginary Conversations of Landor or the “dialogue of the dead.” Sometimes this form expands to full length, and more than two speakers are used: the setting then is usually a cena or symposium, like the one that looms so large in Petronius. Plato, though much earlier in the field than Menippus, is a strong influence on this type, which stretches in an unbroken tradition down through those urbane and leisurely conversations which define the ideal courtier in Castiglione or the doctrine and discipline of angling in Walton. A modern development produces the country-house weekends in Peacock, Huxley, and their imitators in which the opinions and ideas and cultural interests expressed are as important as the love-making.

小说家展现其热情的方式有两种：一是像亨利·詹姆斯那样，通过对人际关系的详尽分析；二是像托尔斯泰那样，通过对社会现象的深入剖析。梅尼普式的讽刺作家则以知识分子的方式展现其热情，他们探讨主题和态度，要么堆砌大量关于主题的博学知识，要么用滔滔不绝的术语淹没那些迂腐的讽刺对象。这种形式的一个分支，或者更确切地说，一个亚分支，是阿特纳奥斯的《宴饮智者》和马可比乌斯的《农神节》所代表的那种百科全书式的杂糅，在这些作品中，人们围坐在宴会上，就谈话中可能涉及的每一个话题，滔滔不绝地倾泻出大量的学识。这种博学的炫耀很可能是由瓦罗与梅尼普传统联系起来的，瓦罗本人博学多才，即使昆体良没有目瞪口呆、惊叹不已，至少也会称他为“罗马最博学之士”。拉伯雷的作品中明显体现出一种将内容扩展成百科全书式杂糅的倾向，尤其体现在他那篇篇幅浩繁的火炬图谱、护裆的别称以及占卜方法的汇编中。伊拉斯谟和伏尔泰在履行职责时所创作的百科全书式汇编表明，他们收集事实的本能与他们作为艺术家的卓越才能并非毫无关联。如果我们将其解释为福楼拜在《布瓦尔与佩库谢》中采用的百科全书式结构体现了他对梅尼普传统的认同，那么这种结构就很容易理解了。

The novelist shows his exuberance either by an exhaustive analysis of human relationships, as in Henry James, or of social phenomena, as in Tolstoy. The Menippean satirist, dealing with intellectual themes and attitudes, shows his exuberance in intellectual ways, by piling up an enormous mass of erudition about his theme or in overwhelming his pedantic targets with an avalanche of their own jargon. A species, or rather sub-species, of the form is the kind of encyclopaedic farrago represented by Athenaeus’ Deipnosophists and Macrobius’ Saturnalia, where people sit at a banquet and pour out a vast mass of erudition on every subject that might conceivably come up in a conversation. The display of erudition had probably been associated with the Menippean tradition by Varro, who was enough of a polymath to make Quintilian, if not stare and gasp, at any rate call him vir Romanorum eruditissimus. The tendency to expand into an encyclopaedic farrago is clearly marked in Rabelais, notably in the great catalogues of torcheculs and epithets of codpieces and methods of divination. The encyclopaedic compilations produced in the line of duty by Erasmus and Voltaire suggest that a magpie instinct to collect facts is not unrelated to the type of ability that has made them famous as artists. Flaubert’s encyclopaedic approach to the construction of Bouvard et Pecuchet is quite comprehensible if we explain it as marking an affinity with the Menippean tradition.

这种对渊博学识的创造性运用，是斯威夫特之前英语世界最伟大的梅尼普式讽刺作品——伯顿的《忧郁的解剖》——的组织原则。在这部作品中，人类社会以忧郁症概念所提供的知识模式为框架进行研究，书籍的会谈取代了对话，其结果是自乔叟（伯顿最喜爱的作家之一）以来，英国文学中对人类生活最全面的单部著作。我们不妨顺便提一下他在引言中对乌托邦的设想以及他的“离题之谈”，这些离题之谈经分析，实则是对梅尼普式形式的精炼提炼：关于空气的离题之谈，即奇妙的旅程；关于精神的离题之谈，即对博学的讽刺性运用；关于学者苦难的离题之谈，即对“光荣哲学家”的讽刺。伯顿书名中的“解剖”一词意为剖析或分析，非常准确地表达了他作品形式的理性化方法。我们不妨将其采纳为一种为了取代冗长且在现代容易产生误导的“梅尼普讽刺剧”，我们采用了一个方便的名称。

This creative treatment of exhaustive erudition is the organizing principle of the greatest Menippean satire in English before Swift, Burton’s Anatomy of Melancholy. Here human society is studied in terms of the intellectual pattern provided by the conception of melancholy, a symposium of books replaces dialogue, and the result is the most comprehensive survey of human life in one book that English literature had seen since Chaucer, one of Burton’s favorite authors. We may note in passing the Utopia in his introduction and his “digressions,” which when examined turn out to be scholarly distillations of Menippean forms: the digression of air, of the marvellous journey; the digression of spirits, of the ironic use of erudition; the digression of the miseries of scholars, of the satire on the philosophus gloriosus. The word “anatomy” in Burton’s title means a dissection or analysis, and expresses very accurately the intellectualized approach of his form. We may as well adopt it as a convenient name to replace the cumbersome and in modern times rather misleading “Menippean satire.”

当然，解剖学最终会与小说融合，产生各种混合体，包括人物小说和以人物象征社会或其他理念的小说，例如本世纪三十年代的无产阶级小说。然而，将二者结合得最为成功的，是伯顿和拉伯雷的门徒斯特恩。《项狄传》或许如前所述是一部小说，但其中离题的叙事、目录式的描写、以“幽默”为主题的人物风格化、大鼻子的奇妙旅程、研讨会式的讨论，以及对哲学家和迂腐评论家的不断嘲讽，所有这些都属于解剖学的范畴。

The anatomy, of course, eventually begins to merge with the novel, producing various hybrids including the roman à these and novels in which the characters are symbols of social or other ideas, like the proletarian novels of the thirties in this century. It was Sterne, however, the disciple of Burton and Rabelais, who combined them with greatest success. Tristram Shandy may be, as was said at the beginning, a novel, but the digressing narrative, the catalogues, the stylizing of character along “humor” lines, the marvellous journey of the great nose, the symposium discussions, and the constant ridicule of philosophers and pedantic critics are all features that belong to the anatomy.

对文学解剖学的形式和传统有更清晰的理解，将有助于我们更好地理解文学史上的许多要素。波伊提乌斯的《哲学的慰藉》采用对话形式，穿插诗歌段落，并贯穿着沉思式的反讽，堪称一部纯粹的文学解剖学作品，这对于理解其深远的影响至关重要。《垂钓者全书》也是一部文学解剖学作品，因为它融合了散文和诗歌，以乡村晚宴为背景，采用对话形式，对食物抱有沉思冥想的兴趣，并以温和的梅尼普式讽刺，嘲讽一个认为一切都比钓鱼更重要，却又鲜少发现其他更好消遣的社会。几乎在每个文学时期，都有许多传奇故事、忏悔录和文学解剖学作品被忽视，仅仅是因为它们所属的类别未被识别。例如，在斯特恩和皮科克之间的时期，我们有传奇故事《漫游者梅尔莫斯》；在忏悔录中，有霍格的《一个正义罪人的忏悔录》；在解剖学著作中，有骚塞的《医生》、阿莫里的《约翰·邦克尔》和《安布罗西亚之夜》。

A clearer understanding of the form and traditions of the anatomy would make a good many elements in the history of literature come into focus. Boethius’ Consolation of Philosophy, with its dialogue form, its verse interludes and its pervading tone of contemplative irony, is a pure anatomy, a fact of considerable importance for the understanding of its vast influence. The Compleat Angler is an anatomy because of its mixture of prose and verse, its rural cena setting, its dialogue form, its deipnosophistical interest in food, and its gentle Menippean raillery of a society which considers everything more important than fishing and yet has discovered very few better things to do. In nearly every period of literature there are many romances, confessions, and anatomies that are neglected only because the categories to which they belong are unrecognized. In the period between Sterne and Peacock, for example, we have, among romances, Melmoth the Wanderer; among confessions, Hogg’s Confessions of a Justified Sinner; among anatomies, Southey’s Doctor, Amory’s John Buncle, and the Noctes Ambrosianae.

综上所述：当我们从形式的角度审视小说时，可以看到四条主要线索将其串联起来：小说、自白、解剖学和浪漫小说。这六种形式都存在，我们已经展示了小说是如何与其他三种形式结合的。完全专注于一种形式的小说很少见：例如，乔治·艾略特的早期小说受到浪漫小说的影响，而后期的小说则受到解剖学的影响。浪漫小说与自白的混合体自然可以在自传中找到。这种浪漫情怀在英语文学中以性格外向的乔治·博罗和性格内向的德·昆西为代表。我们在拉伯雷的作品中已经注意到浪漫与解剖相结合的风格；后来的例子是《白鲸》，其中浪漫的狩猎主题扩展到对鲸鱼的百科全书式解剖。忏悔与解剖在《衣裳哲学》以及克尔凯郭尔一些极具原创性的散文小说实验作品中得以融合，例如《非此即彼》。更全面的小说结构通常至少运用三种形式：我们可以在《帕梅拉》中看到小说、浪漫和忏悔的元素，在《堂吉诃德》中看到小说、浪漫和解剖的元素，在普鲁斯特的作品中看到小说、忏悔和解剖的元素，在阿普列乌斯的作品中也看到浪漫、忏悔和解剖的元素。

To sum up then: when we examine fiction from the point of view of form, we can see four chief strands binding it together, novel, confession, anatomy, and romance. The six possible combinations of these forms all exist, and we have shown how the novel has combined with each of the other three. Exclusive concentration on one form is rare: the early novels of George Eliot, for instance, are influenced by the romance, and the later ones by the anatomy. The romance-confession hybrid is found, naturally, in the autobiography of a romantic temperament, and is represented in English by the extroverted George Borrow and the introverted De Quincey. The romance-anatomy one we have noticed in Rabelais; a later example is Moby Dick, where the romantic theme of the wild hunt expands into an encyclopaedic anatomy of the whale. Confession and anatomy are united in Sartor Resartus and in some of Kierkegaard’s strikingly original experiments in prose fiction form, including Either/Or. More comprehensive fictional schemes usually employ at least three forms: we can see strains of novel, romance, and confession in Pamela, of novel, romance, and anatomy in Don Quixote, of novel, confession, and anatomy in Proust, and of romance, confession, and anatomy in Apuleius.

我特意将这个结构图绘制得如此清晰，是为了说明对《白鲸》或《项狄传》这类作品的形式进行简单而合乎逻辑的解释的优势所在。通常，评论家们对这类作品形式的解读，就像布罗卜丁奈格的医生们一样，经过一番激烈的争论后，最终宣布《格列佛游记》是“自然界的怪胎”。尤其令评论家们困惑的是作品的结构，几乎所有深受其影响的小说家都被指责行为怪异。读者或许会想起乔伊斯，因为用“怪诞”来形容乔伊斯的作品似乎成了一种习惯。我发现一些优秀的评论家会用“魔王”、“巨兽”和“白象”这样的词语来形容作品；而那些水平不高的评论家或许会用得更夸张。乔伊斯在《尤利西斯》和《芬尼根守灵夜》的结构安排上近乎痴迷，但由于它们并非按照散文小说的传统原则来组织，因此给人一种结构松散的印象。让我们用我们现有的公式来分析他的作品吧。

I deliberately make this sound schematic in order to suggest the advantage of having a simple and logical explanation for the form of, say, Moby Dick or Tristram Shandy. The usual critical approach to the form of such works resembles that of the doctors in Brobdingnag, who after great wrangling finally pronounced Gulliver a lusus naturae. It is the anatomy in particular that has baffled critics, and there is hardly any fiction writer deeply influenced by it who has not been accused of disorderly conduct. The reader may be reminded here of Joyce, for describing Joyce’s books as monstrous has become a nervous tic. I find “demogorgon,” “behemoth,” and “white elephant” in good critics; the bad ones could probably do much better. The care that Joyce took to organize Ulysses and Finnegans Wake amounted nearly to obsession, but as they are not organized on familiar principles of prose fiction, the impression of shapelessness remains. Let us try our formulas on him.

如果让读者列出《尤利西斯》中最令他印象深刻的几点，答案可能大致如下。首先，都柏林的景象、声音和气味跃然纸上，人物刻画生动饱满，对话自然流畅。其次，故事和人物巧妙地与典型的英雄模式（尤其是《奥德赛》中的英雄模式）进行对比，从而达到戏仿的效果。第三，意识流技巧的运用，使人物和事件的刻画更加深入人心。第四，无论在技巧还是主题上，作者都力求做到百科全书式的全面和详尽，并以高度理性化的视角来审视两者。现在我们应该不难看出，这四点描述的正是书中与……相关的要素。《尤利西斯》分别融合了小说、爱情故事、自白和解剖学四种体裁。因此， 《尤利西斯》是一部完整的散文史诗，它运用了这四种体裁，而且这四种体裁几乎同等重要，彼此之间又不可或缺，使得整部作品浑然一体，而非简单的拼凑。

If a reader were asked to set down a list of the things that had most impressed him about Ulysses, it might reasonably be somewhat as follows. First, the clarity with which the sights and sounds and smells of Dublin come to life, the rotundity of the characterdrawing, and the naturalness of the dialogue. Second, the elaborate way that the story and characters are parodied by being set against archetypal heroic patterns, notably the one provided by the Odyssey. Third, the revelation of character and incident through the searching use of the stream-of-consciousness technique. Fourth, the constant tendency to be encyclopaedic and exhaustive both in technique and in subject matter, and to see both in highly intellectualized terms. It should not be too hard for us by now to see that these four points describe elements in the book which relate to the novel, romance, confession, and anatomy respectively. Ulysses, then, is a complete prose epic with all four forms employed in it, all of practically equal importance, and all essential to one another, so that the book is a unity and not an aggregate.

这种统一性建立在错综复杂的平行对比之上。哈姆雷特和尤利西斯的浪漫原型如同文学天堂中遥远的星辰，带着疑惑俯视着都柏林那些卑微的生灵，他们顺从地交织在自身影响所设定的模式之中。尤其是在“独眼巨人”和“喀耳刻”这两个章节中，浪漫主义模式对现实主义模式的持续戏仿，令人想起《包法利夫人》 ，尽管讽刺的方向截然相反。小说和自白式写作技巧的关系也类似：作者跃入人物的内心世界，追寻他们的意识流，然后再跳出来，从外部描述他们。在“伊萨卡”这一章节中，小说与解剖学的结合也体现了这一点，场景中个人层面与理性层面之间潜藏的对抗感，构成了其大部分的悲情所在。同样的平行对比原则也适用于其他三种组合：《瑙西卡》和《佩内洛普》中的爱情与忏悔，《普罗透斯》和《食莲者》中的忏悔与解剖，《塞壬》和《喀耳刻》的部分内容中的爱情与解剖（一种罕见且断断续续的组合）。

This unity is built up from an intricate scheme of parallel contrasts. The romantic archetypes of Hamlet and Ulysses are like remote stars in a literary heaven looking down quizzically on the shabby creatures of Dublin obediently intertwining themselves in the patterns set by their influences. In the “Cyclops” and “Circe” episodes particularly there is a continuous parody of realistic patterns by romantic ones which reminds us, though the irony leans in the opposite direction, of Madame Bovary. The relation of novel and confession techniques is similar; the author jumps into his characters’ minds to follow their stream of consciousness, and out again to describe them externally. In the novel-anatomy combination, too, found in the “Ithaca” chapter, the sense of lurking antagonism between the personal and intellectual aspects of the scene accounts for much of its pathos. The same principle of parallel contrast holds good for the other three combinations: of romance and confession in “Nausicaa” and “Penelope,” of confession and anatomy in “Proteus” and “The Lotos-Eaters,” of romance and anatomy (a rare and fitful combination) in “Sirens” and parts of “Circe.”

在《芬尼根守灵夜》中，设计的统一性远不止于此。醉醺醺的HCE和他被掐住脖子的妻子的凄凉故事，并没有与特里斯特拉姆和神圣国王的原型形成对比：HCE本身就是特里斯特拉姆和神圣国王。由于故事的背景设定在梦境中，忏悔与小说、意识流与外部世界的显现之间，都不存在对比。小说的体验世界也与解剖学的可理解世界截然不同。我们在小说中一直分离出来的那些形式，以及那些依赖于日常意识中常识二元对立而存在的形式，在《芬尼根守灵夜》中消失，融入到第五种也是最本质的形式之中。这种形式传统上与经文和圣书联系在一起，它以人类灵魂的堕落与觉醒以及自然的创造与毁灭来处理生命。《圣经》就是这种形式的权威例证； 《埃及亡灵书》和《冰岛散文埃达》也属于这一范畴，这两部作品都对《芬尼根守灵夜》产生了深远的影响。

In Finnegans Wake the unity of design goes far beyond this. The dingy story of the sodden HCE and his pinched wife is not contrasted with the archetypes of Tristram and the divine king: HCE is himself Tristram and the divine king. As the setting is a dream, no contrast is possible between confession and novel, between a stream of consciousness inside the mind and the appearances of other people outside it. Nor is the experiential world of the novel to be separated from the intelligible world of the anatomy. The forms we have been isolating in fiction, and which depend for their existence on the commonsense dichotomies of the daylight consciousness, vanish in Finnegans Wake into a fifth and quintessential form. This form is the one traditionally associated with scriptures and sacred books, and treats life in terms of the fall and awakening of the human soul and the creation and apocalypse of nature. The Bible is the definitive example of it; the Egyptian Book of the Dead and the Icelandic Prose Edda, both of which have left deep imprints on Finnegans Wake, also belong to it.

特定百科全书形式

SPECIFIC ENCYCLOPAEDIC FORMS

我们在第一篇文章中探讨了一个原则：在每个文学时代，往往都存在某种核心的百科全书式作品，通常是神话模式下的经文或圣书，以及我们称之为其他模式下的某种“启示类比”。在我们的文化中，核心的圣书是基督教的《圣经》，它也可能是世界上结构最严谨的圣书。说《圣经》“不仅仅是”一部文学作品，仅仅意味着还有其他解读它的方法。任何书籍若不具备文学特质，就不可能对文学产生影响；只要接受文学批评家的审视，《圣经》就是一部文学作品。

We met in the first essay the principle that in every age of literature there tends to be some kind of central encyclopaedic form, which is normally a scripture or sacred book in the mythical mode, and some “analogy of revelation,” as we called it, in the other modes. In our culture the central sacred book is the Christian Bible, which is also probably the most systematically constructed sacred book in the world. To say that the Bible is “more” than a work of literature is merely to say that other methods of approaching it are possible. No book could have had its influence on literature without itself having literary qualities, and the Bible is a work of literature as long as it is being examined by a literary critic.

在近代（直到最近），真正意义上的圣经文学批评的缺失，导致我们对圣经文学象征主义的整体认知存在巨大的空白，而所有新近获得的知识都无法填补这一空白。我认为，历史学术研究无一例外都属于“低级”或分析性批评，而“高级”批评则截然不同。后者在我看来是一种纯粹的文学批评，它不会将圣经视为分析性批评所揭示的讹误、注释、删改、插入、混淆、错置和误解的剪贴簿，而是将其视为所有这些因素最初旨在构建的象征性统一体。任何止步于将圣经视为某种具有专家集邮式文学形式的批评，都无法解释圣经巨大的文化影响力。因此，对圣经进行真正的高等批判，将是一个综合性的过程，其出发点是圣经是一个最终的神话，一个从创世到启示录的单一原型结构。其启发式原则是圣奥古斯丁的公理：旧约在新约中显明，新约隐藏在旧约中；也就是说，新旧约与其说是彼此的寓言，不如说是彼此的隐喻性对应。我们甚至无法追溯圣经的历史，找到一个其素材尚未被塑造成类型学统一体的时期。如果圣经在任何意义上——无论是神圣的还是世俗的——被视为受圣灵启示的，那么它的编辑和编纂过程也必须被视为受圣灵启示的。

The absence of any genuinely literary criticism of the Bible in modern times (until very recently) has left an enormous gap in our knowledge of literary symbolism as a whole, a gap which all the new knowledge brought to bear on it is quite incompetent to fill. I feel that historical scholarship is without exception “lower” or analytic criticism, and that “higher” criticism would be a quite different activity. The latter seems to me to be a purely literary criticism which would see the Bible, not as the scrapbook of corruptions, glosses, redactions, insertions, conflations, misplacings, and misunderstandings revealed by the analytic critic, but as the typological unity which all these things were originally intended to help construct. The tremendous cultural influence of the Bible is inexplicable by any criticism of it which stops where it begins to look like something with the literary form of a specialist’s stamp collection. A genuine higher criticism of the Bible, therefore, would be a synthetizing process which would start with the assumption that the Bible is a definitive myth, a single archetypal structure extending from creation to apocalypse. Its heuristic principle would be St. Augustine’s axiom that the Old Testament is revealed in the New and the New concealed in the Old: that the two testaments are not so much allegories of one another as metaphorical identifications of one another. We cannot trace the Bible back, even historically, to a time when its materials were not being shaped into a typological unity, and if the Bible is to be regarded as inspired in any sense, sacred or secular, its editorial and redacting processes must be regarded as inspired too.

这是我们对待圣经的唯一方式。它对文学象征主义的主要影响，实际上正是如此。这种方法是一种保守的批评，它基于其象征意义的统一性假设，恢复并重建了传统的类型学。例如，《雅歌》的历史批评家主要关注生育崇拜和乡村节日；而文化批评家则主要关注但丁、克莱尔沃的伯纳德以及其他神秘主义者和诗人对其象征意义的发展，在他们看来，《雅歌》象征着基督对教会的爱。后者并非生硬地强加于诗歌之上的寓言，而是诗歌所融入的更大的原型或文化阐释语境。我们无需在两种批评类型之间做出选择；无需将这部作品的文学历程视为一种迂腐的扭曲或过度想象的错误；也无需将它视为一部充满感官享受的东方故事的观点视为一种现代的、带有讽刺意味的发现。

This is the only way in which we can deal with the Bible as the major informing influence on literary symbolism which it actually has been. Such an approach would be a conservative criticism recovering and re-establishing the traditional typologies based on the assumption of its figurative unity. The historical critic of the Song of Songs, for instance, is largely concerned with fertility cults and village festivals: the cultural criticism of it would concern itself mainly with the developments of its symbolism in Dante, Bernard of Clairvaux and other mystics and poets, for whom it represented the love of Christ for his Church. This latter is not an allegory inappropriately stuck on to the poem, but the larger archetypal or cultural context of interpretation into which it has been fitted. There is no need to choose between the two types of criticism; no need to regard the book’s literary career as the result of a prudish distortion or over-imaginative mistake; no need to treat the view of it as a voluptuous orientale as a modern and an ironic discovery.

一旦我们对《圣经》的理解变得清晰明了，从《十字架之梦》到《小吉丁》，大量的文学象征便开始显现其意义。我们目前关注的是被称为弥赛亚的中心人物的英雄之旅。在旧约中，弥赛亚与多位王室成员相关联，而在新约中，他则被视为基督。这一旅程的各个阶段及其象征意义，此前已在浪漫神话的框架下有所阐述。神秘的诞生之后，是顿悟或认出他是上帝之子；随后是屈辱、背叛和殉道的象征，即所谓的“受苦仆人情结”；而这些象征又被弥赛亚作为新郎、战胜怪物的勇士以及带领他的子民回归故土的领袖等象征所取代。原始先知的预言似乎主要（如果不是完全）是谴责性的，但它们被赋予了“后流放”的续篇，这有助于将整部圣经注入完整的循环神话的节奏，在这个神话中，灾难之后是复兴，屈辱之后是繁荣，我们在约伯和浪子的故事中找到了这种神话的缩影。

Once our view of the Bible comes into proper focus, a great mass of literary symbols from The Dream of the Rood to Little Gidding begins to take on meaning. We are concerned at present with the heroic quest of the central figure called the Messiah, who is associated with various royal figures in the Old Testament and identified with Christ in the New. The stages and symbols of this quest have been dealt with under the mythos of romance. A mysterious birth is followed by an epiphany or recognition as God’s son; symbols of humiliation, betrayal, and martyrdom, the so-called suffering servant complex, follow, and in their turn are succeeded by symbols of the Messiah as bridegroom, as conqueror of a monster, and as the leader of his people into their rightful home. The oracles of the original prophets appear to have been mainly if not entirely denunciatory, but they have been furnished with “post-exilic” sequels which help to infuse the whole Bible with the rhythm of the total cyclical mythos in which disaster is followed by restoration, humiliation by prosperity, and which we find in epitome in the stories of Job and the prodigal son.

因此，整部《圣经》呈现出一个从创世到末世的巨大循环，其中包含了弥赛亚从道成肉身到神化的英勇历程。在这个循环中，又包含着三个其他的循环运动，或明示或暗示：个人层面的循环，从出生到救赎；性层面的循环，从亚当和夏娃到末世婚礼；社会层面的循环，从律法的颁布到建立的秩序。律法的国度、旧约中重建的锡安以及新约的千禧年，这些都是完整的或辩证的循环，其运动轨迹先是下降，然后上升到一个永久救赎的世界。此外，还有一种讽刺的或“过于人性化”的循环，即没有救赎帮助的人类生命循环，它反复经历着布莱克所说的“同样的枯燥轮回”，从出生到死亡。在这里，最终的结局是奴役、流放、持续的战争，或是被火（所多玛、巴比伦）或水（洪水）毁灭。这两种循环运动形式为我们提供了两种史诗框架：回归史诗和愤怒史诗。生、死、重生的循环在象征意义上与弥赛亚的先存、死中生、复活的循环密切相关，这为我们提供了第三种类比史诗。第四种类型是对比史诗，其中一极是充满讽刺意味的人类处境，另一极是神圣社会的起源或延续。

The Bible as a whole, therefore, presents a gigantic cycle from creation to apocalypse, within which is the heroic quest of the Messiah from incarnation to apotheosis. Within this again are three other cyclical movements, expressed or implied: individual from birth to salvation; sexual from Adam and Eve to the apocalyptic wedding; social from the giving of the law to the established kingdom of the law, the rebuilt Zion of the Old Testament and the millennium of the New. These are all completed or dialectic cycles, where the movement is first down and then up to a permanently redeemed world. In addition there is the ironic or “all too human” cycle, the mere cycle of human life without redemptive assistance, which goes recurrently through the “same dull round,” in Blake’s phrase, from birth to death. Here the final cadence is one of bondage, exile, continuing war, or destruction by fire (Sodom, Babylon) or water (the flood). These two forms of cyclical movement supply us with two epic frameworks: the epic of return and the epic of wrath. The fact that the cycle of life and death and rebirth is closely analogous in its symbolism to the Messianic cycle of pre-existence, life-in-death and resurrection gives us a third type of analogical epic. A fourth type is the contrast-epic, where one pole is the ironic human situation and the other the origin or continuation of a divine society.

即使在神话中，完整的末世论节奏也十分罕见，尽管它出现在北欧神话、《埃达》和《穆斯皮利》中，《摩诃婆罗多》的最后一卷也描绘了进入天堂的场景。神话中既有关于神化的，例如赫拉克勒斯的传说，也有关于救赎的，例如《亡灵书》中奥西里斯的象征意义，但大多数圣书的主要目的是制定法律，尤其是礼仪法。由此形成了一种对比史诗的雏形：一端是解释法律起源的神话，包括创世神话；另一端是法律下的人类社会。《吉尔伽美什史诗》表明了对比史诗的古老性，其中英雄对永生的追求最终只让他听到了自然循环的终结，正如《圣经》中一样，自然循环的终结以洪水为象征。赫西俄德和奥维德的神话集都基于相同的结构：诗人本人，作为不公正或流放的受害者，在人物关系中占据着显著的位置。这种结构在波伊提乌斯的作品中得以延续，其两极分别是逝去的黄金时代和被诬陷入狱的诗人，并一直延续到中世纪。

Even in myth the full apocalyptic cadence is rare, though it occurs in Northern mythology, in the Eddas and the Muspilli, and the last book of the Mahabharata is an entry into heaven. There are myths of apotheosis, as in the legend of Hercules, and of salvation, as in the Osiris symbolism of the Book of the Dead, but the main concern of most sacred books is to lay down the law, chiefly of course the ceremonial law. The resulting shape is an embryonic form of contrast-epic: myths accounting for the origin of law, including creation myths, are at one pole and human society under the law is at the other. The antiquity of the contrast-epic is indicated by the epic of Gilgamesh, where the hero’s search for immortality leads him only to hear about the end of the natural cycle, symbolized here, as in the Bible, by a flood. The collections of myth made by Hesiod and Ovid are based on the same form: here the poet himself, a victim of injustice or exile, has a prominent place at the human pole. The same structure is carried on through Boethius, where the two poles are the lost golden age and the poet in prison falsely accused, into medieval times.

浪漫主义百科全书式的作品运用了对弥赛亚神话的人性化或圣礼式模仿，例如但丁在《神曲》中的探寻之旅、斯宾塞笔下圣乔治的冒险以及圣杯骑士的故事。《神曲》颠覆了对比史诗的通常结构，它以充满讽刺意味的人性处境开篇，最终以神圣的启示告终。但丁探寻之旅的人性本质是……他无法战胜甚至直面开篇遇到的怪物，这便奠定了他的故事基调：他的冒险之旅由此开始，他背离了传统的游侠骑士角色。在兰格伦的这部杰作中，我们看到了英国文学中对对比史诗的首次重要诠释。一端是复活的基督和皮尔斯的救赎；另一端则是对人类生活的阴郁描绘，最终呈现出一种反基督的胜利景象。《仙后》原本应该以一首婚礼颂歌结尾，其中很可能充满了圣经中新郎的意象，但如今我们看到的版本却是，诽谤的恶兽依然逍遥法外，而诗人本人也成为了它的受害者。

Romantic encyclopaedic forms use human or sacramental imitations of the Messianic myth, like the quest of Dante in the Commedia, of St. George in Spenser, and of the knights of the Holy Grail. The Commedia reverses the usual structure of the contrast-epic, as it starts with the ironic human situation and ends with divine vision. The human nature of Dante’s quest is established by the fact that he is unable to overcome or even to face the monsters who confront him at the beginning: his quest thus begins in a retreat from the conventional knight-errant role. In Langland’s great vision we have the first major English treatment of the contrast-epic. At one pole is the risen Christ and the salvation of Piers: at the other is the somber vision of human life which presents at the end of the poem something very like a triumph of Antichrist. The Faerie Queene was to have ended with an epithalamium, which would probably have been filled with Biblical bridegroom imagery, but as we have it the poem ends with the Blatant Beast of calumny still at large and the poet a victim of it.

在高度模仿的诗歌形式中，我们达到了通常意义上的史诗结构，荷马、维吉尔和弥尔顿的作品便是这种形式的代表。史诗与叙事诗的区别在于其百科全书式的主题广博，涵盖从天堂到冥界，以及浩瀚的传统知识。叙事诗人，例如骚塞或利德盖特，可以创作无数叙事作品，但史诗诗人通常只完成一部史诗，而他决定创作主题的那一刻，往往是他人生中的关键时刻。

In the high mimetic we reach the structure that we think of as typically epic, the form represented by Homer, Virgil, and Milton. The epic differs from the narrative in the encyclopaedic range of its theme, from heaven to the underworld, and over an enormous mass of traditional knowledge. A narrative poet, a Southey or a Lydgate, may write any number of narratives, but an epic poet normally completes only one epic structure, the moment when he decides on his theme being the crisis of his life.

古典史诗的循环形式源于自然循环，其核心是一个位于无垠（apeiron）之中、介于上位神与下位神之间的已知世界——地中海世界。这一循环包含两大节奏：个体的生与死，以及更为缓慢的社会节奏。后者在岁月的流逝中（荷马史诗中为periplomenon eniauton，维吉尔史诗中为volvibus或labentibus annis），引领着城邦和帝国的兴衰更替。唯有神祇才能洞察后一种运动的动态。开篇即进入正题的惯例，可谓在时间上打了个结。 《伊利亚特》的整体故事背景从希腊城邦出发，途经特洛伊长达十年的围城战，最终又回到希腊；《奥德赛》则是同一主题的一个特殊例证，其故事从伊萨卡岛展开，最终又回到伊萨卡岛。《埃涅阿斯纪》则跟随普里阿摩斯的家神，从特洛伊城迁徙到新特洛伊城。

The cyclical form of the Classical epic is based on the natural cycle, a mediterranean known world in the middle of a boundlessness (apeiron) and between the upper and the lower gods. The cycle has two main rhythms: the life and death of the individual, and the slower social rhythm which, in the course of years (periplomenon eniauton in Homer, volvibus or labentibus annis in Virgil), brings cities and empires to their rise and fall. The steady vision of the latter movement is possible only to gods. The convention of beginning the action in medias res ties a knot in time, so to speak. The total action in the background of the Iliad moves from the cities of Greece through the ten-year siege of Troy back to Greece again; the total action of the Odyssey is a specialized example of the same thing, moving from Ithaca back to Ithaca. The Aeneid moves with the household gods of Priam, from Troy to New Troy.

前景故事的开端在《奥德赛》中被描述为“某处” （hamothen）：实际上，它的选择更为精妙。这三部史诗都始于整个循环故事的某种低谷：《伊利亚特》始于希腊军营的绝望时刻；《奥德赛》始于奥德修斯和佩涅洛佩彼此疏远，两人都受到纠缠不休的求婚者的追求；《埃涅阿斯纪》始于主人公遭遇海难。故事发生在迦太基海岸，那是朱诺的城堡，也是罗马的敌人。从那里开始，情节向前向后推进，足以展现历史循环的大致轮廓。史诗般的行动的发现在于，它让人感受到整个行动的结束如同开始一般，从而感受到贯穿始终的秩序与平衡。这种秩序并非神意或宿命论的因果关系，而是神明掌控的自然界的稳定，如果人类接受它，这种稳定也会延伸到人类身上。这种稳定感本身未必是悲剧性的，但它却是悲剧得以发生的根源。

The foreground action begins at a point described in the Odyssey as hamothen, “somewhere”: actually, it is far more carefully chosen. All three epics begin at a kind of nadir of the total cyclical action: the Iliad, at a moment of despair in the Greek camp; the Odyssey, with Odysseus and Penelope furthest from one another, both wooed by importunate suitors; the Aeneid, with its hero shipwrecked on the shores of Carthage, citadel of Juno and enemy of Rome. From there, the action moves both backward and forward far enough to indicate the general shape of the historical cycle. The discovery of the epic action is the sense of the end of the total action as like the beginning, and hence of a consistent order and balance running through the whole. This consistent order is not a divine fiat or fatalistic causation, but a stability in nature controlled by the gods, and extended to human beings if they accept it. The sense of this stability is not necessarily tragic, but it is the kind of sense that makes tragedy possible.

例如，《伊利亚特》就体现了这一点。赞美《伊利亚特》的理由不胜枚举，足以写成一本比本书厚得多的书，但对我们而言，相关的理由在于它的主题是“愤怒之歌”（menis ）。 《伊利亚特》向西方文学表明，敌人的陨落，与朋友或领袖的陨落一样，都是悲剧而非喜剧，这一点的重要性怎么强调都不为过。《伊利亚特》的出现，使诗人对人生的理解中，终于融入了一种客观、不带偏见的元素。如果没有这一元素，诗歌就仅仅是服务于各种社会目的的工具，用于宣传、娱乐、宗教仪式和教化；而有了这一元素，诗歌便获得了自《伊利亚特》以来从未失去的权威，这种权威如同科学的权威一样，建立在将自然视为一种非人格化的秩序之上。

It does so in the Iliad, for example. The number of valid reasons for praising the Iliad would fill a bigger book than this, but the relevant reason for us here is the fact that its theme is menis, a song of wrath. It is hardly possible to overestimate the importance for Western literature of the Iliad’s demonstration that the fall of an enemy, no less than of a friend or leader, is tragic and not comic. With the Iliad, once for all, an objective and disinterested element enters into the poet’s vision of human life. Without this element, poetry is merely instrumental to various social aims, to propaganda, to amusement, to devotion, to instruction: with it, it acquires the authority that since the Iliad it has never lost, an authority based, like the authority of science, on the vision of nature as an impersonal order.

《奥德赛》开启了另一种回归史诗的传统。故事讲述的是一位英雄从重重险境中脱险，及时赶回迎娶新娘并击败恶人的浪漫故事。但我们从中感受到的核心，是一种更为审慎的认知，这种认知根植于我们对自然、社会和法律的普遍接受，即一位合格的主人最终会回到自己的家园。《埃涅阿斯纪》将回归的主题发展为重生，新特洛伊的结局是英雄征程中焕然一新、重获新生的起点。基督教史诗将同样的主题融入更广阔的原型语境中。从诗歌的角度来看，《圣经》的叙事包含了三大史诗的主题：《伊利亚特》中城市的毁灭和沦陷，《奥德赛》中回归故土的主题，以及《埃涅阿斯纪》中重建新城的主题。亚当和奥德修斯一样，都是愤怒之人，因行事鲁莽、超越常人极限而触怒上帝，被逐出家园。在这两个故事中，这种挑衅行为都以食用预留的食物为象征。对于神而言，正如奥德修斯一样，亚当能否回归故土取决于神明的智慧能否平息神的怒火（荷马史诗中，宙斯的意志使波塞冬与雅典娜和解；基督教的赎罪中，天父与人和解）。以色列人将约柜从埃及运往应许之地，正如埃涅阿斯将家当从陷落的特洛伊城运往永恒的圣城一样。

The Odyssey begins the other tradition of the epic of return. The story is a romance of a hero escaping safely from incredible perils and arriving in the nick of time to claim his bride and baffle the villains, but our central feeling about it is a much more prudent sense, rooted in all our acceptance of nature, society, and law, of the proper master of the house coming to reclaim his own. The Aeneid develops the theme of return into one of rebirth, the end in New Troy being the starting-point renewed and transformed by the hero’s quest. The Christian epic carries the same themes into a wider archetypal context. The action of the Bible, from the poetic point of view, includes the themes of the three great epics: the theme of the destruction and captivity of the city in the Iliad, the theme of the nostos or return home in the Odyssey, and the theme of the building of the new city in the Aeneid. Adam is, like Odysseus, a man of wrath, exiled from home because he angered God by going hyper moron, beyond his limit as a man. In both stories the provoking act is symbolized by the eating of food reserved for deity. As with Odysseus, Adam’s return home is contingent on the appeasing of divine wrath by divine wisdom (Poseidon and Athene reconciled by the will of Zeus in Homer; the Father reconciled with man in the Christian atonement). Israel carries its ark from Egypt to the Promised Land just as Aeneas carries his household goods from the fallen Troy to the eternally established one.

因此，从古典史诗到基督教史诗，其主题的完整性（而非价值）有所提升，正如弥尔顿在“超越埃俄尼亚山”等词句中所暗示的那样。在弥尔顿的作品中，史诗的前景行动再次指向整个循环行动的最低点——撒旦和亚当的堕落。从那里开始，行动通过拉斐尔的言语倒叙，再通过米迦勒的言语向前推进，直至整个行动的开始和结束。开始是上帝在圣子显现之前与天使同在；结束发生在启示录之后，上帝再次成为“万物之主”，但开始和结束是同一点，即上帝的临在，因基督的英雄之旅而更新和转化。作为一名基督徒，弥尔顿必须重新思考史诗中英雄行动的主题，以确定在基督教语境下，英雄和行动的意义是什么。在他看来，英雄主义在于服从、忠诚和在嘲讽或迫害中坚韧不拔，忠诚的天使阿布迪尔便是其典范。行动对他而言意味着积极的或创造性的行为，基督创造世界和重塑人类便是例证。因此，撒旦继承了传统武士英雄的特质：他是愤怒的阿喀琉斯，是狡猾的尤利西斯，是完成混沌险阻的游侠骑士；但在上帝看来，他不过是个伪英雄，是堕落的人类自然而然地崇拜的对象，是王国、权力和荣耀的偶像化象征。

Hence there is, as we go from the Classical to the Christian epic, a progress in completeness of theme (not in any kind of value), as Milton indicates in such phrases as “Beyond the Aonian mount.” In Milton the foreground action of the epic is again the nadir of the total cyclical action, the fall of Satan and Adam. From there the action works backward through the speech of Raphael, and forward through the speech of Michael, to the beginning and end of the total action. The beginning is God’s presence among the angels before the Son is manifested to them; the end comes after the apocalypse when God again is “all in all,” but the beginning and end are the same point, the presence of God, renewed and transformed by the heroic quest of Christ. As a Christian, Milton has to reconsider the epic theme of heroic action, to decide what in Christian terms a hero is and what an act is. Heroism for him consists in obedience, fidelity and perseverance through ridicule or persecution, and is exemplified by Abdiel, the faithful angel. Action for him means positive or creative act, exemplified by Christ in the creation of the world and the recreation of man. Satan thus takes over the traditional qualities of martial heroism: he is the wrathful Achilles, the cunning Ulysses, the knight-errant who achieves the perilous quest of chaos; but he is from God’s point of view a mock-hero, what man in his fallen state naturally turns to with admiration as the idolatrous form of the kingdom, the power, and the glory.

在低模仿时期，百科全书式的结构往往趋向于主观和神话化，或客观和历史化。前者通常以史诗的形式呈现，后者则以散文小说的形式展现。令人颇感意外的是，将二者结合起来的主要尝试出现在法国，其范围从谢尼埃留下的残篇一直延续到维克多·雨果的《世纪传说》。在这里，英雄行动的主题，按照低模仿时期的惯例，从领袖转移到了整个人类。因此，该行动的实现主要被视为对未来社会的改善。

In the low mimetic period the encyclopaedic structure tends to become either subjective and mythological, or objective and historical. The former is usually expressed in epos and the latter in prose fiction. The main attempts to combine the two were made, somewhat unexpectedly, in France, and extend from the fragments left by Chenier to Victor Hugo’s Légendes des Siècles. Here the theme of heroic action is transferred, consistently with low mimetic conventions, from the leader to humanity as a whole. Hence the fulfilment of the action is conceived mainly as social improvement in the future.

在传统史诗中，诸神从持续的当下影响着故事的进程：雅典娜和维纳斯会在特定的场合以显灵的方式出现，为英雄带来启迪或鼓励。为了获得关于未来，或者说在较低层次的生命循环中“即将到来”的信息，通常需要下到死者的下界，正如《奥德赛》第十一卷和《埃涅阿斯纪》第六卷中出现的下行通道（nekyia 或 katabasis）那样。同样，在但丁的作品中，受诅咒者知晓未来却不知晓当下；而在弥尔顿的作品中，那“将死亡带入世界”的禁忌知识则以米迦勒对未来的预言的形式得以实现。因此，我们并不惊讶地发现，在对未来充满希望的低级模仿时期，弥赛亚力量的观念显著增强，这种力量被认为来自“底层”或通过秘传和隐秘的传统而来。《解放了的普罗米修斯》是英语世界最广为人知的例子：在《浮士德》第二部分中插入下行（katabasis）的尝试——先是作为前往“众神”的旅程，后又作为古典瓦尔普吉斯之夜——显然是该作品中最令人费解的结构问题之一。然而，有时下行（katabasis）会与更传统的顿悟点相结合，并与之相辅相成。济慈的《恩底弥翁》中，恩底弥翁“下行”是为了寻求真理，“上行”是为了寻求美，最终发现，不出所料，真理与美是同一的。在《海伯利安》中，狄俄尼索斯式的“下行”与阿波罗式的“上行”之间的某种契合显然是创作意图之一。艾略特的《烧焦的诺顿》建立在“上行之路与下行之路相同”的原则之上，这用基督教的术语解决了这种二元对立。这个世界的时间是一条水平线，而上帝永恒的存在则是一条垂直线，与它垂直相交，交点便是道成肉身。玫瑰园和地铁的片段勾勒出自然循环的两个半圆，上方的半圆代表浪漫的、充满神话色彩的纯真世界，下方的半圆则代表经验的世界。但如果我们向上超越玫瑰园，向下超越地铁，最终会到达同一个点。

In the traditional epic the gods affect the action from a continuous present: Athene and Venus appear epiphanically, on definite occasions, to illuminate or cheer the hero at that moment. To gain information about the future, or what is “ahead” in terms of the lower cycle of life, it is normally necessary to descend to a lower world of the dead, as is done in the nekyia, or katabasis, in the eleventh book of the Odyssey and the sixth of the Aeneid. Similarly in Dante the damned know the future but not the present, and in Milton the forbidden knowledge which “brought death into the world” is actualized in the form of Michael’s prophecy of the future. We are thus not surprised to find a great increase, in the low mimetic period of future hopes, of a sense of Messianic powers as coming from “underneath” or through esoteric and hermetic traditions. Prometheus Unbound is the most familiar English example: the attempt to insert a katabasis into the second part of Faust, first as the descent to the “mothers” and then as the Classical Walpurgis Night, was evidently one of the most baffling structural problems in that work. Sometimes, however, the katabasis is combined with and complemented by the more traditional point of epiphany. Keats’s Endymion goes “down” in search of truth and “up” in search of beauty, discovering, not surprisingly for Keats, that truth and beauty are the same. In Hyperion some alignment between a Dionysian “below” and an Apollonian “above” was clearly on the agenda. Eliot’s Burnt Norton is founded on the principle that “the way up and the way down are the same,” which resolves this dichotomy in Christian terms. Time in this world is a horizontal line, and God’s timeless presence is a vertical one crossing it at right angles, the crossing point being the Incarnation. The rose garden and subway episodes outline the two semi-circles of the cycle of nature, the upper one the romantic mythopoeic fantasy world of innocence and the lower the world of experience. But if we go further up than the rose garden and further down than the subway we reach the same point.

喜剧和反讽为我们提供了戏仿象征，例如《小人国》中被缚的格列佛与普罗米修斯的关系、《芬尼根守灵夜》中步履蹒跚的搬运工与亚当的关系、普鲁斯特笔下玛德琳蛋糕与圣餐的关系，这些都是不同程度严肃性的例证。原型结构的运用也属于此类。在《押沙龙与亚希多弗》中，故事与旧约原型之间的相似之处被处理成一系列机智的巧合。百科全书式的戏仿主题在讽刺作品中十分常见，而在散文小说中，则主要体现在阿普列乌斯、拉伯雷和斯威夫特等人的风格和传统中。讽刺作品与小说之间的关系，类似于史诗与叙事作品之间的关系：小说家创作的小说越多，就越成功，但拉伯雷、伯顿和斯特恩的创作生涯却围绕着一部杰作展开。因此，我们应该在讽刺和反讽中寻找百科全书式传统的延续，并且应该期待反讽或讽刺史诗的容纳形式是纯粹的循环，其中每一次探索，无论多么成功或英勇，迟早都要再次进行。

Comedy and irony supply us with parody-symbolism, of which the relation of the bound Gulliver in Lilliput to Prometheus, of the staggering hod-carrier in Finnegans Wake to Adam, of the madeleine cake in Proust to the Eucharist, are examples on varying levels of seriousness. Here too belongs the kind of use of archetypal structure made in Absalom and Achitophel, where the resemblance between the story and its Old Testament model is treated as a series of witty coincidences. The theme of encyclopaedic parody is endemic in satire, and in prose fiction is chiefly to be found in the anatomy, the tradition of Apuleius and Rabelais and Swift. Satires and novels show a relation corresponding to that of epics and narratives: the more novels a novelist writes the more successful he is, but Rabelais, Burton, and Sterne build their creative lives around one supreme effort. Hence it is in satire and irony that we should look for the continuing encyclopaedic tradition, and we should expect that the containing form of the ironic or satiric epic would be the pure cycle, in which every quest, however successful or heroic, has sooner or later to be made over again.

在布莱克的诗作《精神旅人》中，我们看到了人类生命从出生到死亡再到重生的循环。诗中的两个人物是一男一女，他们的生命轨迹截然相反：一人衰老，另一人青春永驻，反之亦然。他们之间的循环关系贯穿四个基本阶段：母子阶段、夫妻阶段、父女阶段，以及布莱克称之为“幽灵”和“流溢”的第四个阶段，这两个术语大致对应于雪莱的“阿拉斯托”和“埃庇普西克”。然而，这些阶段都不完全准确：母亲只是乳母，妻子只是为了取悦男性而被“束缚”，女儿是易位的，而“流溢”并非“流溢”，而是始终难以捉摸。男性形象代表着人类，因此也包括女性——布莱克笔下的“女性意志”只有在女性戏剧化或模仿上述人类关系时才会与女性联系起来，正如她们在宫廷爱情传统中所做的那样。女性形象象征着自然环境，人类只能部分征服自然环境，而永远无法完全征服自然环境。正如诗歌的四个阶段所暗示的那样，这首诗的核心象征意义是月亮。

In Blake’s poem The Mental Traveller we have a vision of the cycle of human life, from birth to death to rebirth. The two characters of the poem are a male and a female figure, moving in opposite directions, one growing old as the other grows young, and vice versa. The cyclical relation between them runs through four cardinal points: a son-mother phase, a husband-wife phase, a father-daughter phase, and a fourth phase of what Blake calls spectre and emanation, terms corresponding roughly to Shelley’s alastor and epipsyche. None of these phases is quite true: the mother is only a nurse, the wife merely “bound down” for the male’s delight, the daughter a changeling, and the emanation does not “emanate,” but remains elusive. The male figure represents humanity, and therefore includes women—the “female will” in Blake becomes associated with women only when women dramatize or mimic the above relation in human life, as they do in the Courtly Love convention. The female figure represents the natural environment which man partially but never wholly subdues. The controlling symbolism of the poem, as the four phases suggest, is lunar.

百科全书式的著作关注人类生命周期，因此其中出现了一个矛盾的女性原型，时而仁慈，时而阴险，但通常主导并确认着这一循环往复的运动。她的一端由伊西斯女神、佩涅洛佩或索尔维格等形象代表，她们是故事的终点。经常开启和结束循环的女神与此密切相关。这位女神在《奥德赛》中是雅典娜，在《埃涅阿斯纪》中是维纳斯；在伊丽莎白时代的文学中，出于政治原因，通常是狄安娜的某种变体，例如……斯宾塞笔下的仙后，卢克莱修笔下那贯穿始终的、象征生命平衡于自然秩序的维纳斯，则是另一种版本。但丁笔下的贝阿特丽切并非掌管一个循环，而是引领人走向神性的圣礼螺旋，浮士德笔下的永恒女神也以一种远不那么具体的方式扮演着类似的角色。与之相对的是一些人物——荷马笔下的卡吕普索或喀耳刻、维吉尔笔下的狄多、莎士比亚笔下的克利奥帕特拉、斯宾塞笔下的杜埃萨（有时是“可怕的母亲”，但通常也受到同情的对待）——她们代表着与英雄之旅截然相反的方向。弥尔顿笔下的夏娃，引领人类堕落，正是与贝阿特丽切形成鲜明对比的人物。

To the extent that the encyclopaedic form concerns itself with the cycle of human life, an ambivalent female archetype appears in it, sometimes benevolent, sometimes sinister, but usually presiding over and confirming the cyclical movement. One pole of her is represented by an Isis figure, a Penelope or Solveig who is the fixed point on which the action ends. The goddess who frequently begins and ends the cyclical action is closely related. This figure is Athene in the Odyssey and Venus in the Aeneid; in Elizabethan literature, for political reasons, usually some variant of Diana, like the Faerie Queen in Spenser. The alma Venus who suffuses Lucretius’ great vision of life balanced in the order of nature is another version. Beatrice in Dante presides over not a cycle but a sacramental spiral leading up to deity, as does, in a far less concrete way, the Ewig-Weibliche of Faust. At the opposite pole is a figure—Calypso or Circe in Homer, Dido in Virgil, Cleopatra in Shakespeare, Duessa in Spenser, sometimes a “terrible mother” but often sympathetically treated—who represents the opposite direction from the heroic quest. Eve in Milton, who spirals man downward into the Fall, is the contrasting figure to Beatrice.

在充满讽刺意味的时代，自然涌现出许多关于人生轮回的意象，这些意象通常由一位兼具月亮和蛇蝎美人特质的女性形象主导。叶芝的《幻象》 （叶芝将其与《精神旅行者》联系起来，这一点他完全正确）正是基于这种象征意义。而罗伯特·格雷夫斯先生的《白女神》则以更为渊博的学识和精妙的构思对此进行了更深入的阐释。在艾略特的《荒原》中，背景中的人物与其说是“情境的掌控者”，不如说是雌雄同体的忒瑞西阿斯。尽管诗中既有关于火的布道，也有关于雷霆的布道（两者都带有末世的意味），但水的自然循环——泰晤士河流入大海，又在春雨中以水的滋润重返人间——才是整首诗的核心主题。在乔伊斯的《尤利西斯》中，女性形象既是母亲，又是妻子，又是轻浮之人，佩内洛普拥抱了所有追求者，在睡梦中与昏昏欲睡的旋转大地融为一体，不断地肯定却从未形成，并将整本书都带走了。

In the ironic age there are naturally a good many visions of a cycle of experience, often presided over by a female figure with lunar and femme fatale affiliations. Yeats’s Vision, which Yeats was quite right in associating with The Mental Traveller, is based on this symbolism, and more recently Mr. Robert Graves’ The White Goddess has expounded it with even greater learning and ingenuity. In Eliot’s Waste Land the figure in the background is less “the lady of situations” than the androgynous Teiresias, and although there is a fire sermon and a thunder sermon, both with apocalyptic overtones, the natural cycle of water, the Thames flowing into the sea and returning through death by water in the spring rains, is the containing form of the poem. In Joyce’s Ulysses a female figure at once maternal, marital, and meretricious, a Penelope who embraces all her suitors, merges in her sleep with the drowsy spinning earth, constantly affirming but never forming, and taking the whole book with her.

但《芬尼根守灵夜》才是我们这个时代最具讽刺意味的史诗。这部作品的结构同样是循环往复的，结尾又将我们带回开头。芬尼根从未真正醒来，因为亨利·柯南·道尔未能建立起他梦境与现实世界之间的任何连续性。故事的核心人物是艾尔·帕特里夏，但我们注意到，艾尔·帕特里夏身上几乎没有贝阿特丽斯或圣母玛利亚的影子，更没有蛇蝎美人的气质。她是一位忙碌却又无比耐心体贴的妻子和母亲：她按部就班地经历着人生的轮回，自己并未完成任何使命，但她显然是那种能够促成使命的人。那么，在《芬尼根守灵夜》中，谁才是最终完成永恒使命的英雄呢？书中似乎没有哪个角色是合适的人选；然而，我们却能感受到，这本书带给我们的远不止是循环往复这种不负责任的讽刺。最终……我们渐渐明白，是读者完成了这项探索，是读者掌握了《双重旋转之书》的精髓，从而能够俯视它的旋转，并将其形式视为比旋转更伟大的东西。

But it is Finnegans Wake which is the chief ironic epic of our time. Here again the containing structure is cyclical, as the end of the book swings us around to the beginning again. Finnegan never really wakes up, because HCE fails to establish any continuity between his dreaming and waking worlds. The central figure is ALP, but we notice that ALP, although she has very little of the Beatrice or Virgin Mary about her, has even less of the femme fatale. She is a harried but endlessly patient and solicitous wife and mother: she runs through her natural cycle and achieves no quest herself, but she is clearly the kind of being who makes a quest possible. Who then is the hero who achieves the permanent quest in Finnegans Wake? No character in the book itself seems a likely candidate; yet one feels that this book gives us something more than the merely irresponsible irony of a turning cycle. Eventually it dawns on us that it is the reader who achieves the quest, the reader who, to the extent that he masters the book of Doublends Jined, is able to look down on its rotation, and see its form as something more than rotation.

在百科全书式的文学形式中，例如史诗及其同类作品，我们可以看到，围绕抒情诗展开的传统主题，是如何以篇幅更长的故事片段的形式反复出现的。例如，颂歌出现在英雄竞赛中，描写社群行动的诗歌出现在竞技会的场景中，挽歌出现在英雄的死亡中，等等。相反的发展则发生在围绕传统主题的抒情诗达到一定程度，从而扩展成一部微型史诗时：即便不是历史上的“小史诗”或小故事集，也是在类型上与之非常相似的某种作品。例如，《利西达斯》就是一部微型圣经史诗，其内容涵盖了《失乐园》的全部主题——人类的死亡以及基督的救赎。斯宾塞的《婚歌》可能也以微型的形式包含了与他未完成的史诗结尾部分同样丰富的象征意义。在现代，微型史诗成为一种非常常见的形式：艾略特的后期诗歌、伊迪丝·西特韦尔的诗歌以及庞德的许多诗章都属于这种形式。

In encyclopaedic forms, such as the epic and its congeners, we see how the conventional themes, around which lyrics cluster, reappear as episodes of a longer story. Thus the panegyric reappears in the klea andron or heroic contests, the poem of community action in the convention of the games, the elegy in heroic death, and so on. The reverse development occurs when a lyric on a conventional theme achieves a concentration that expands it into a miniature epic: if not the historical “little epic” or epyllion, something very like it generically. Thus Lycidas is a miniature scriptural epic extending over the whole range covered by Paradise Lost, the death of man and his redemption by Christ. Spenser’s Epithalamion also probably contains in miniature as much symbolic range as the unwritten conclusion to his epic would have had. In modern times the miniature epic becomes a very common form: the later poems of Eliot, of Edith Sitwell, and many cantos of Pound belong to it.

此外，为了阐明我们的一般原则，微型史诗往往实际上是大型史诗的一部分。《失乐园》中米迦勒的预言将整本圣经呈现为一部微型对比史诗，一极是世界末日，另一极是洪水。圣经本身包含《约伯记》，它是整部圣经主题的缩影，弥尔顿曾将其视为“简短”史诗的典范。

Often too, in illustration of our general principle, a miniature epic actually forms part of a bigger one. The prophecy of Michael in Paradise Lost presents the whole Bible as a miniature contrast-epic, with one pole at the apocalypse and the other at the flood. The Bible itself contains the Book of Job, which is a kind of microcosm of its total theme, and is cited by Milton as the model for the “brief” epic.

同样，演说散文发展成为更为连贯的散文小说形式，同样，散文的成长点——我们称之为诫命、寓言、格言和神谕——也以经文形式的雏形再次出现。在许多类型的散文浪漫诗中，诗歌或诗歌的特征都十分突出：古爱尔兰史诗、伊丽莎白时代浪漫小说中的华丽辞藻、《一千零一夜》的押韵散文、日本《源氏物语》中运用诗歌进行文雅对话，这些例子都表明了这种趋势的普遍性。但随着史诗的发展，它的韵律逐渐规范化和统一，而散文则以不同的形式发展出自己的道路。在模仿主义低潮时期，主观的神话史诗和客观的历史史诗之间存在着鸿沟。前者似乎因其文体而更接近诗歌，后者则更接近散文，这更凸显了二者之间的差异。然而，在散文讽刺作品中，我们注意到散文有强烈的吸收诗歌的倾向。我们曾提及解剖学传统中诗歌插曲的频繁出现，而在拉伯雷、斯特恩和乔伊斯的讽刺诗中，这种倾向则更为显著。在圣经体裁中，我们已经看到散文与诗歌之间的界限非常模糊，有时甚至几乎不存在。

Similarly, oratorical prose develops into the more continuous forms of prose fiction, and similarly too the growing points of prose, so to speak, which we called the commandment, parable, aphorism, and oracle, reappear as the kernels of scriptural forms. In many types of prose romance verse or characteristics of verse are prominent: the old Irish epics, euphuism in Elizabethan romance, the rhyming prose of the Arabian Nights, the use of poems for cultivated dialogue in the Japanese Tale of Genji, are random examples showing how universal the tendency is. But as epos grows into epic, it conventionalizes and unifies its metre, while prose goes its own way in separate forms. In the low mimetic period the gap between the subjective mythological epic and the objective historical one is increased by the fact that the former seems to belong by its decorum to verse and the latter to prose. In prose satire, however, we notice a strong tendency on the part of prose to reabsorb verse. We have mentioned the frequency of the verse interlude in the anatomy tradition, and in the melos of Rabelais, Sterne and Joyce the tendency is carried much farther. In scriptural forms, we have seen, the gap between prose and verse is very narrow, and sometimes hardly exists at all.

那么，我们又回到了本节的起点——《圣经》。它是唯一一种将但丁的宏伟结构与拉伯雷的支离破碎融为一体的文学体裁。从某种角度来看，《圣经》展现了无与伦比的史诗般的宏大结构，其范围之广、逻辑之严密、完整性之高，无人能及；而从另一个角度来看，它又呈现出一种支离破碎、杂乱无章的面貌，相比之下，《木桶的故事》、《项狄传》和《衣裳哲学家》都显得如同晴空万里般和谐统一。其中蕴藏着某种奥秘，或许值得文学批评家们深入探究。

We come back to where we started this section, then, to the Bible, the only form which unites the architectonics of Dante with the disintegration of Rabelais. From one point of view, the Bible presents an epic structure of unsurpassed range, consistency and completeness; from another, it presents a seamy side of bits and pieces which makes the Tale of a Tub, Tristram Shandy, and Sartor Resartus look as homogeneous as a cloudless sky. Some mystery is here which literary criticism might find it instructive to look into.

当我们深入探究时，会发现圣经作为一部虚构作品，其所具有的统一连续性，正是其作为一部跨越时空、涵盖可见与不可见现实秩序的权威神话的精髓所在。它拥有寓言式的戏剧结构，其五幕分别为：创造、堕落、流放、救赎和复兴。我们越深入研究这个神话，其描述性或象征性的一面似乎就越发显得次要。对大多数读者而言，圣经中的神话、传说、历史回忆和真实历史密不可分；即使是历史事实，其存在也并非因为其“真实”，而是因为它具有神话意义。《历代志》中的家谱或许是真实的历史；《约伯记》显然是一部充满想象的戏剧，但它更为重要，也更接近基督通过寓言启示真理的实践。神话优先于事实，这既是宗教层面的，也是文学层面的。在这两种语境下，洪水故事的意义在于它作为一种原型所具有的想象性地位，而这种地位绝非苏美尔地表上覆盖的一层淤泥所能解释。当我们把这一原则应用于福音书时，考虑到它们叙事上的种种差异，其描述性特征也随之消解。它们的形式基础并非传记，正如出埃及记故事的基础并非历史一样。

When we do look into it, we find that the sense of unified continuity is what the Bible has as a work of fiction, as a definitive myth extending over time and space, over invisible and visible orders of reality, and with a parabolic dramatic structure of which the five acts are creation, fall, exile, redemption, and restoration. The more we study this myth, the more its descriptive or sigmatic aspect seems to fall into the background. For most readers, myth, legend, historical reminiscence, and actual history are inseparable in the Bible; and even what is historical fact is not there because it is “true” but because it is mythically significant. The begats in Chronicles may be authentic history; the Book of Job is clearly an imaginative drama, but the Book of Job is more important, and closer to Christ’s practice of revelation through parable. The priority of myth to fact is religious as well as literary; in both contexts the significance of the flood story is in its imaginative status as an archetype, a status which no layer of mud on top of Sumeria will ever account for. When we apply this principle to the gospels, with all the variations in their narratives, the descriptive aspect of them too dissolves. The basis of their form is something other than biography, just as the basis of the Exodus story is something other than history.

此时，对圣经的分析视角开始逐渐清晰，其主题层面也随之显现。随着圣经主题的不断深入，这种分析视角也愈发凸显。随着文本被分解成越来越小的碎片，虚构的神话开始显得虚幻，它呈现出一系列顿悟的形态，一系列虽不连续却秩序井然的重要领悟或洞见时刻。因此，我们可以从美学或亚里士多德的视角来审视《圣经》，将其视为一个单一的形式，一个故事，其中怜悯和恐惧——在此语境下，它们分别代表着对善恶的认知——被唤起和驱散。或者，我们也可以从朗吉尼的视角来审视它，将其视为一系列狂喜的时刻或领悟不断扩展的点——事实上，这种方法正是所有布道文本选择的基础。在这里，我们拥有一个可以运用到文学领域的批评原则，它可以适用于任何我们感兴趣的事物，一个能够调和柯勒律治所谓的“整体论”与爱伦·坡、休姆和庞德的非连续性理论的原则。然而，《圣经》远不止是一部文学作品，因此，或许这一原则的适用范围甚至超越了文学本身。无论如何，我们在文学领域已经探讨到此为止，本书的其余部分将着重探讨通常被称为非文学性的语言结构的文学层面。

At this point the analytic view of the Bible begins to come into focus as the thematic aspect of it. In proportion as the continuous fictional myth begins to look illusory, as the text breaks down into smaller and smaller fragments, it takes on the appearance of a sequence of epiphanies, a discontinuous but rightly ordered series of significant moments of apprehension or vision. The Bible may thus be examined from an aesthetic or Aristotelian point of view as a single form, as a story in which pity and terror, which in this context are the knowledge of good and evil, are raised and cast out. Or it may be examined from a Longinian point of view as a series of ecstatic moments or points of expanding apprehension—this approach is in fact the assumption on which every selection of a text for a sermon is based. Here we have a critical principle which we can take back to literature and apply to anything we like, a principle in which the “holism,” as it has been called, of Coleridge and the discontinuous theories of Poe, Hulme, and Pound are reconciled. Yet the Bible is “more” than a work of literature, so perhaps the principle has a wider range of extension even than literature. In any case we have gone as far as we can within literature, and the remainder of this book will be concerned with the literary aspect of verbal structures generally called non-literary.

非文学散文的修辞

THE RHETORIC OF NON-LITERARY PROSE

与诗歌不同，散文也用于非文学目的：它不仅延伸至文学的“旋律”（melos）和“论述”（opsis）范畴，更触及“实践”（praxis）和“理论”（theoria）的外部世界，涵盖社会行动和个人思想本身。文艺复兴时期的评论家们常常争论诗歌的最高形式是什么，是史诗还是悲剧。这个问题或许没有标准答案，但通过讨论，我们可以深入了解文学形式。如今，如果我们提出这样一个问题：散文的最高形式是什么？这个问题或许也没有答案，但当我们提出这个问题时，大量的作品，例如《圣经》、柏拉图的对话录、帕斯卡的沉思录——事实上，所有通常被排除在文学之外的“伟大著作”——都跃然纸上，获得了新的文学意义。因此，我们有必要思考，在那些并非以文学或假设意图为主要目的的语言结构中，究竟蕴含着哪些文学要素。

Prose is, unlike verse, used also for non-literary purposes: it extends not only to the literary boundaries of melos and opsis, but to the outer worlds of praxis and theoria, social action and individual thought themselves. Renaissance critics used to argue about what the greatest form for poetry was, and whether it was epic or tragedy. There is probably no answer to such a question, but one can learn a good deal about literary form by discussing it. Now if we ask the question: What is the greatest possible prose form? there is probably no answer to that question either, but the moment we ask it, a great number of works, the Bible, the dialogues of Plato, the meditations of Pascal—in fact, all “great books” usually placed outside literature—leap into a new literary significance. It is thus necessary for us at this point to consider what literary elements are involved in the verbal structures in which the literary or hypothetical intention is not the primary one.

我们仍然认为文学一方面面向社会行动的世界，另一方面面向个人思想的世界，因此非文学散文的修辞往往会强调情感。前者侧重于通过听觉诉诸行动，后者侧重于通过视觉隐喻诉诸理性和沉思。让我们先从散文中那个关注社会或演说说服技巧的广阔分支入手。

We are still thinking of literature as facing the world of social action on one side, and of individual thought on the other, so that the rhetoric of non-literary prose would tend to emphasize emotion and the appeal to action through the ear in the former area, and intellect and the appeal to contemplation based predominantly on visual metaphors in the latter. Let us begin with that extensive suburb of prose that is concerned with the technique of social or oratorical persuasion.

最集中的例子见于那些捕捉历史节奏、抓住关键事件或行动阶段、对其进行诠释、阐明与之相关的情感，或以某种方式运用语言结构来把握和引导历史潮流的小册子或演讲中。例如， 《论出版自由》（Areopagitica）、约翰逊致切斯特菲尔德的信、拉蒂默与英联邦时期的一些布道、伯克的一些演讲、林肯的葛底斯堡演说、范泽蒂的临终演说、丘吉尔1940年的演讲等等，都是我们很容易想到的例子。这些作品最初并非出于文学目的而创作，如​​果真是如此，它们就无法达到最初的目的，但如今它们都具有文学价值，也为评论家提供了素材。几乎所有这些作品都带有修辞散文特有的强调性重复和反复的修辞手法。

The most concentrated examples of this are to be found in the pamphlet or speech that catches the rhythm of history, that seizes on a crucial event or phase of action, interprets it, articulates the emotions concerned with it, or in some means employs a verbal structure to insulate and conduct the current of history. Areopagitica, Johnson’s letter to Chesterfield, some sermons in the period between Latimer and the Commonwealth, some of Burke’s speeches, Lincoln’s Gettysburg address, Vanzetti’s death speech, Churchill’s 1940 speeches, are a few examples that come readily to mind. None of these were designed with a primarily literary intention, and would have failed of their original purpose if they had been, but they are literary now, and data for the critic. Nearly all of them are marked by the emphatic patterns of repetition and anaphora characteristic of rhetorical prose.

这些历史预言的沉稳节奏体现了一种策略性的行动回避：它们梳理并审视那些耳熟能详却根深蒂固的观念。而当我们从文学走向社会生活，散文的下一个阶段便是以劝说行动为核心的修辞，其节奏则显著加快。此时的重复具有催眠般的魔力，旨在打破人们习以为常的观念联想和习惯性反应，并排除任何其他可能的行动方案。这种修辞最纯粹的形式体现在一个男孩与狗说话的语调中，目的是劝说狗坐起来、握手或做出其他超出其正常活动范围的动作。当面向人类听众时，这种修辞必须遵循修辞辩证法：它必须包含一个凝聚点或一个攻击点，或者两者兼备。攻击或谩骂的修辞手法在讲坛上对罪恶的批判以及法庭上检察官的总结陈词中均有体现。后者衍生出了檄文，即对社会敌人的控诉。颂词的修辞手法，也就是古典世界所谓的颂扬修辞，在当今最明显地体现在广告和宣传中，尽管它也以“华丽辞藻”之类的文体呈现出更为纯粹的文学形式。“段落”散文，通常以描述性内容为主，试图传达某种无言的情感。

The measured cadences of these historical oracles represent a kind of strategic withdrawal from action: they marshal and review the ranks of familiar but deeply-held ideas. The rhetoric of persuasion to action itself, which is the next stage of prose as we proceed from literature outwards into social life, is considerably stepped up in its rhythm. Here the repetitions are hypnotic and incantatory, aimed at breaking down customary associations of ideas and habitual responses, and at excluding any alternative line of action. Such a rhetoric may be heard in its purest form in the speech rhythms of a boy talking to a dog, with the object of persuading him to sit up or shake hands or otherwise move out of the normal line of canine endeavor. When addressed to a human audience, such rhetoric must follow the dialectic of rhetoric: it must have either a rallying point or a point of attack, or both. The rhetoric of attack or invective is exemplified in the pulpit’s crusade against sin and in the prosecutor’s summing-up in the courtroom. The latter has produced the by-form of the philippic, the indictment of a social enemy. The rhetoric of eulogy, the so-called epideictic rhetoric of the Classical world, is in our day most clearly seen in advertising and publicity, although it has a more genuinely literary form in the type of “purple passage” prose, usually with a descriptive content, that attempts to communicate some kind of wordless emotion.

正如这些例子所示，我们正迅速地从文学转向直接用语言表达情感。我们越是朝着这个方向发展，作者就越有可能（或者假装）与他的主题产生情感上的联系，以至于他劝诫我们接受或避免的东西，在某种程度上是他自身情感生活的投射。随着这种倾向的加剧，某种自动化的表达方式开始渗透到写作中：以孩童般的仇恨、恐惧、爱恋和崇拜对象为中心，进行语言上的直接表达。当斯温伯恩谈到“那些在当今社会可耻而荒谬的放纵下，肆意横行、横冲直撞的野蛮人”时，我们或许不知道他指的是什么，但只要瞥一眼他那行文的结构，看看其中自动出现的头韵和形容词的重复使用，就会明白，无论他指的是什么，我们都无需认真对待。这种写作风格是一种常见且易于辨认的现象：它是情绪化的散文，是维多利亚时代大量批评作品、卡莱尔和罗斯金的大量著作、神职人员对异端邪说或世俗娱乐的谴责、极权主义宣传的惯用手法，事实上，几乎所有我们感觉作者笔锋失控、为想象力的迸发而机械式表达的修辞手法，都属于此类。“陶醉”的隐喻常被用来形容这种修辞控制的崩溃。

As these examples show, we are moving rapidly away from literature towards the direct verbal expression of kinetic emotion. The further we go in this direction, the more likely the author is to be, or to pretend to be, emotionally involved with his subject, so that what he exhorts us to embrace or avoid is in part a projection from his own emotional life. As this increases, a certain automatism comes into the writing: the verbal expression of infantile-centered hatreds, fears, loves, and objects of adoration. When Swinburne speaks of “the yelling Yahoos whom the scandalous and senseless license of our own day allows to run and roar about the country unmuzzled and unwhipped,” we may not know what he is referring to, but a glance at the prose structure, with its automatic alliteration and doubling of adjectives, makes it clear that whatever it is we hardly need to take it seriously. Such writing is a familiar and easily recognized phenomenon: it is tantrum prose, the prose of so much Victorian criticism, of several acres of Carlyle and Ruskin, of clerical denunciations of heresies or secular amusements, of totalitarian propaganda, and in fact of nearly all rhetoric in which we feel that the author’s pen is running away from him, setting up a mechanical for an imaginative impetus. The metaphor of “intoxication” is often employed for the breakdown of rhetorical control.

这种修辞越是语无伦次，就越能清晰地展现出它试图脱离理性或缺乏理性地表达情感的本质。此时，我们便进入了情感术语的领域，其主要表现为对固定句式的执着重复。与之相近的，是那种粗俗无礼的表达方式，它用一个词（通常是无法印刷的词）来表达句子的全部修辞，包括形容词、副词、修饰语和标点符号。最终，词语彻底消失，我们又回到了由尖叫、手势和叹息构成的原始语言。当然，文学作品中也存在着对这一过程的模仿，莎士比亚的作品中就包含了从亨利五世在哈弗勒尔城墙前的演说到奥赛罗的“山羊和猴子”独白等诸多例子。在文学散文中对情感修辞的模仿，正是后者产生“旋律” （melos ）这一特征的原因之一。同样，在文学领域，我们偶尔也会遇到一些作家，他们运用这类修辞手法，却无法吸收或理解：其结果是病态的，一种文学上的缺陷。糖尿病，阿曼达·罗斯的小说中也有相关描写。

The more incoherent this kind of rhetoric becomes, the more clearly it shows itself to be an attempt to express emotion apart from or without intellect. At this point we enter the area of emotional jargon, which consists largely in an obsessive repetition of verbal formulas. Not far removed is the kind of vulgar inarticulateness that uses one word, generally unprintable, for the whole rhetorical ornament of the sentence, including adjectives, adverbs, epithets, and punctuation. Finally, words disappear altogether, and we are back to a primitive language of screams and gestures and sighs. The whole sequence can of course be imitated within literature, Shakespeare giving us everything from Henry V’s address before the walls of Harfleur to Othello’s “goats and monkeys” speech. The imitation of emotional rhetoric in literary prose is a feature making for melos in the latter. Similarly in literature we occasionally run across a writer who uses such rhetorical material without being able to absorb or assimilate it: the result is pathological, a kind of literary diabetes, and may be studied in the novels of Amanda Ros.

散文中概念性思维的表达展现出一系列与之平行的现象，但方向相反。哲学是断言式或命题式的写作，我们在哲学史上注意到，人们一直在努力提炼命题的节奏。哲学始于谚语和公理，并在不同时期产生了柏拉图的辩证对话和《奥义书》、与其密切相关的圣托马斯·阿奎那的问答模式、斯宾诺莎的准数学式思想体系、培根的格言（培根认为格言是哲学活力的标志），以及我们今天的维特根斯坦《逻辑哲学论》中的编号命题。所有这些显然至少在某种程度上都是为了净化语言交流中修辞的情感内容；然而，在文学批评家看来，它们本身也是修辞手法。

The expression of conceptual thought in prose exhibits a parallel sequence of phenomena, moving in the opposite direction. Philosophy is assertive or propositional writing, and we notice in the history of philosophy a persistent attempt to isolate the rhythm of the proposition. Philosophy begins in proverbs and axioms, and at various times it has produced the dialectic dialogue of Plato and the Upanishads, the closely related question-objection-answer scheme of St. Thomas, the quasi-mathematical arrangements of ideas in Spinoza, the aphorisms of Bacon (who remarks that aphorisms are a sign of vitality in philosophy), and, in our day, the numbered propositions of Wittgenstein’s Tractatus. All of these are clearly at least in part endeavors to purify verbal communication of the emotional content of rhetoric; all of them, however, impress the literary critic as being themselves rhetorical devices.

这意味着存在一种概念修辞，其目的与说服性修辞类似，都是为了将​​情感与理智分离，但却试图摒弃情感的成分。它寻求的是书籍和个体读者，正如其寻求的是听众一样；它的目标是理解，正如说服的目标是行动或情感反应。教学策略很大程度上是一种修辞策略，精心选择词语和意象，以引发这样的反应：“我以前从未这样想过”，或者“你这么一说，我明白了”。区分格言警句乃至深刻内涵与陈词滥调的关键，往往在于修辞的机智。事实上，除非我们欣赏某个思想表达的机智，否则我们是否真的会称其深刻，这一点值得怀疑。教学和说服一样，都运用了一种分离性修辞，旨在打破习惯性的反应：东方经文冗长繁复正是由此而来，新约圣经中也有一些段落几乎和格特鲁德·斯坦一样具有分离性：

The implication is that there is a conceptual rhetoric aimed, like persuasive rhetoric, at separating emotion and intellect, but attempting to throw away the emotional half. It seeks the book and the individual reader as its fellow seeks the audience; its goal is understanding as the goal of persuasion is action or emotional response. A good deal of the strategy of teaching is rhetorical strategy, choosing words and images with great care in order to evoke the response: “I never thought of it that way before,” or “Now that you put it that way, I can see it.” What distinguishes, not simply the epigram, but profundity itself from platitude is very frequently rhetorical wit. In fact it may be doubted whether we ever really call an idea profound unless we are pleased with the wit of its expression. Teaching, like persuasion, employs a dissociative rhetoric aimed at breaking down habitual response: the maddening prolixity of Oriental sutras results from this, and there are passages in the New Testament almost as dissociative as Gertrude Stein:

从起初就有的生命之道，就是我们所听见、所看见、亲眼看过、亲手摸过的；（这生命已经显现出来，我们也看见了，现在又作见证，将这原与父同在、且显现与我们、永生的生命传给你们。）我们所看见、所听见的，现在传给你们……

That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life; (For the life was manifested, and we have seen it, and bear witness, and shew unto you that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us;) That which we have seen and heard declare we unto you …

我们并非想暗示只有优秀的作家才能成为优秀的哲学家，但我们仍然可以观察到，哲学文风中的许多难点源于修辞手法，其根源在于一种将理智与情感分离的观念。詹姆斯·密尔的《政府论》中的一句话便可说明我的意思：

Without trying to suggest that only good writers can be good philosophers, we may still observe that much of the difficulty in a philosophical style is rhetorical in origin, resulting from a feeling that it is necessary to detach and isolate the intellect from the emotions.
