A sentence from James Mill’s Essay on Government will illustrate what I mean:

首先，我们必须谨记一点：所有那些掌握政府权力却与社会利益不一致的人，所有那些分享滥用权力所得利益的人，以及所有受前两者榜样和言论影响的人，都必然会将社会或与社会利益一致的群体描绘成完全无法维护自身利益的人；显然，如果希望那些与社会利益一致的人能够以任何可以容忍的方式维护自身利益，那么那些与社会利益不一致的人就不应该再掌握政府权力。

One caution, first of all, we should take along with us, and it is this: that all those persons who hold the powers of government without having an identity of interests with the community, and all those persons who share in the profits which are made by the abuse of those powers, and all those persons whom the example and representations of the two first classes influence, will be sure to represent the community, or a part having an identity of interest with the community, as incapable in the highest degree of acting according to their own interest; it being clear that they who have not an identity of interest with the community ought to hold the power of government no longer, if those who have that identity of interest could be expected to act in any tolerable conformity with their interest.

最终，经过一番如同解谜般的推敲，人们发现，这其实意味着那些在某种政体中拥有既得利益的人，很可能会抵制另一种政体的引入。批评家苦苦思索，如果詹姆斯·密尔的本意如此，为何他却无法直白地表达出来，最终才意识到，这种文风源于一种反常的、略显尖锐的知识分子式的诚实。他不会屈尊使用任何花哨的劝说技巧、粉饰太平的例证或煽情的言辞；他只会诉诸理性本身的冷酷逻辑——当然，这种逻辑也受到一种独特的维多利亚时代观念的强化，即文风越晦涩难懂，人们在与之搏斗的过程中，就越能培养出坚韧的道德和智力。

This is finally discovered to mean, after one has worked it all out like a crossword puzzle, that those who have a stake in one form of government are likely to resist the introduction of another. The critic, searching for the reasons why, if James Mill meant that, he could not have said it, eventually realizes that the style is motivated by a perverse, bristly intellectual honesty. He will not condescend to employ any of the pretty arts of persuasion, sugar-coated illustrations or emotionally-loaded terms; he will appeal only to the cold logic of reason itself—reinforced, to be sure, by a peculiarly Victorian sense that the more difficult the style, the tougher the moral and intellectual fibre one develops in wrestling with it.

我们注意到，詹姆斯·密尔的修辞基础是对法律文风的模仿，其特点是谨慎的限定性包容性。前文提及的亨利·詹姆斯后期作品中冗长的包含句，也体现了类似修辞手法的文学运用。经过一些中间阶段，在追求非情感化修辞的过程中，我们最终会达到概念术语的境界，也就是所谓的晦涩难懂的文字或官话。这体现了密尔想要用理性本身而非个性的声音说话的愿望，只不过这种愿望被天真地强化了。政府报告、内部备忘录以及……的术语，都体现了这一点。军事指令的动机在于尽可能做到客观冷静，用语言来代表体制或某种匿名的、处于“正常”状态的赛博神灵。当然，它实际表达的却是孤独人群的声音，是那些向外寻求认同的顺从者的焦虑。借用医学术语，这种行话或许可以称之为良性行话：它无疑是一种语言疾病，但还不是像煽动家的演说那样具有致病性的疾病。它存在于新闻报道的各个方面，也是大量专业写作（包括人文主义者的写作）的标配。1984 年的小说暗示了它可能变得有害，小说中将其进一步发展成“新语”，一种伪逻辑的语言简化，其目标与情感化的行话一样，是完全的自动化。我们并不惊讶地发现，我们越是远离文学，或者说越是远离用语言来表达我们称之为想象力的那种完全整合的情感意识状态，就越是接近于将语言作为反射性表达的方式。无论我们走向情感方向还是理性方向，最终都会到达一个大致相同的点，一个与文学截然相反的点——在文学中，语言就像松鼠的啁啾声一样，是对无意识的持续评论。

We note that the basis of James Mill’s rhetoric is the imitation of legal style, with its careful qualifying inclusiveness. The long containing sentences of the later Henry James already mentioned illustrate the literary use of similar devices. Passing over some intermediate stages, we eventually arrive, in this pursuit of non-emotional rhetoric, at conceptual jargon, otherwise known as gobble-dygook or officialese. This is a naive intensification of Mill’s desire to speak with the voice, not of personality, but of Reason itself. The jargon of government reports, inter-office memoranda, and military instructions is motivated by a wish to be as impersonal as possible, to represent verbally the Institution or some anonymous cybernetic deity functioning in a state of “normalcy.” What it actually utters, of course, is the voice of the lonely crowd, the anxiety of the outward-directed conformist. Such jargon may be called, borrowing a term from medicine, benign jargon: it is unmistakably a disease of language, but not—yet—a cancerous disease like a demagogue’s oratory. It is found in most aspects of journalism and is the dress uniform of a large amount of professional writing, including that of humanists. That it could become malignant is indicated in 1984, where a further stage of it is caricatured as “Newspeak,” a pseudo-logical simplification of language which has, like emotional jargon, complete automatism as its goal. We are not surprised to find that the further we depart from literature, or the use of language to express the completely integrated state of emotional consciousness we call imagination, the nearer we come to the use of language as the expression of reflex. Whether we go in the emotional or in the intellectual direction, we arrive at much the same point, a point antipodal to literature in which language is a running commentary on the unconscious, like a squirrel’s chatter.

如果真存在概念修辞这种东西（而且随着论述者试图避免它，概念修辞反而可能日益增多），那么我们在本文开头提出的语法与逻辑的直接结合——这或许是非文学语言结构的特征——从长远来看似乎并不存在。任何对词语进行功能性运用的事物，都必然会卷入所有与词语相关的技术问题，包括修辞问题。因此，从语法到逻辑的唯一路径，必须经过修辞这一中间领域。

If there is such a thing as conceptual rhetoric, which is likely to increase in proportion as the discursive writer tries to avoid it, it seems as though the direct union of grammar and logic, which we suggested at the beginning of this essay might be the characteristic of the non-literary verbal structure, does not, in the long run, exist. Anything which makes a functional use of words will always be involved in all the technical problems of words, including rhetorical problems. The only road from grammar to logic, then, runs through the intermediate territory of rhetoric.

首先我们注意到，试图将语法还原为逻辑，或将逻辑还原为语法的尝试，并未取得应有的成功——如果存在一个庞大而重要的非修辞性共同因素，非文学写作便可依此构建的话。长期以来，话语理性的威望助长了这样一种观念：逻辑是语言的形式成因，基于逻辑原则的普遍语法是可能的，并且语言表达的全部资源都可以被归类。如今，我们更倾向于将推理视为人类运用语言的众多活动之一，是语言的一种特殊功能。没有任何证据表明，这个人学习说话主要是因为他想逻辑清晰地表达自己的想法。

We notice in the first place that attempts to reduce grammar to logic, or logic to grammar, have not had the success they should have had if there were a large and important non-rhetorical common factor on which non-literary writing could be built. For a long time the prestige of the discursive reason fostered the notion that logic was the formal cause of language, that universal grammars on logical principles were possible, and that the entire resources of linguistic expression could be categorized. We are now more accustomed to think of reasoning as one of many things that man does with words, a specialized function of language. There seems to be no evidence whatever that man learned to speak primarily because he wanted to speak logically.

将逻辑简化为语法的尝试出现较晚，但并未取得多大成功。逻辑源于语法，即语言中固有的无意识或潜在逻辑。我们常常发现，概念思维的构成形式也源于语法，最典型的例子就是亚里士多德逻辑中的主语和谓语。人类学家经常提及的那些流动性强的原始语言概念，例如波利尼西亚语的“ mana”或易洛魁语的“orenda”，都是分词或动名词形式：它们属于一个能量和物质尚未被清晰区分的世界，无论是在思想层面，还是在我们自身较为僵化的语言结构中的动词和名词层面。由于在核物理学中能量和物质也尚未被清晰区分，我们或许可以考虑回归到这些“原始”的词汇。例如，“原子”和“光”这两个词作为名词，可能过于物质化和静态，不足以作为它们现在含义的充分符号，当它们从物理学家的方程式进入当代社会意识的语言体系时，翻译中的语法困难就显露无疑了。

The attempts to reduce logic to grammar are more recent, but not much more successful. Logic grows out of grammar, the unconscious or potential logic inherent in language, and we often find that the containing forms of conceptual thought are of grammatical origin, the stock example being the subject and predicate of Aristotelian logic. The fluid primitive linguistic conceptions often mentioned by anthropologists, such as the Polynesian mana or the Iroquois orenda, are participial or gerundive conceptions: they belong in a world where energy and matter have not been clearly separated, either in thought or into the verbs and nouns of our own less flexible language-structure. As energy and matter are not clearly separated in nuclear physics either, we might do worse than to return to such “primitive” words ourselves. The words atom and light, for example, being nouns, may be too material and static to be adequate symbols for what they now mean, and when they pass from the equations of a physicist into the linguistic apparatus of contemporary social consciousness, the grammatical difficulties in the translation show up clearly.

然而，将逻辑简化为语法的论证中仍然存在一个学者们的共同谬误：即认为我们通过解释某事物的起源就解释了它的本质。逻辑或许源于语法，但从某种事物中发展而来，在某种程度上意味着超越它。因为语法也可能成为逻辑发展的阻碍，以及逻辑混乱和伪问题的主要来源。这些混乱的范围甚至远超谐音双关所衍生的大量谬误——谐音双关如同我们生活中的许多其他现象一样，既是文学中的结构原则，也是论述性写作中的障碍。例如，许多冗长的论证可能因为语法结构上的改变而瓦解，例如从定冠词和同一性陈述改为不定冠词和主动语态。说“理性是心灵的功能”不太可能引发争论；而说“理性是心灵的功能”则会陷入一场毫无意义的争夺，试图独占某种本质。说“艺术具有交流功能”就好比满足于显而易见的多种功能；说“艺术就是交流”则迫使我们围绕一个被当作断言的比喻进行循环论证。因此，许多逻辑学家倾向于将语法视为某种逻辑疾病也就不足为奇了。他们中有些人甚至坚持认为，数学才是逻辑一致性的真正来源。对此我无可奉告，只想重申一点：任何对文字进行功能性运用的事物，都必然会卷入所有与文字相关的问题之中。

But there is still the scholar’s mate in the argument for reducing logic to grammar: the fallacy of thinking that we have explained the nature of something by accounting for its origin in something else. Logic may have grown out of grammar, but to grow out of something is in part to outgrow it. For grammar may also be a hampering force in the development of logic, and a major source of logical confusions and pseudo-problems. These confusions extend much further than even the enormous brood of fallacies spawned by paronomasia, which is, like so many of our phenomena, a structural principle in literature and an obstacle in discursive writing. For instance, many long arguments may be annihilated by a grammatical change from definite articles and statements of identity to indefinite articles and active verbs. To say “reason is a function of the mind” is unlikely to lead to dispute; to say “reason is the function of the mind” involves one in a pointless struggle for the exclusive possession of an essence. To say “art communicates” is similarly to be content with an obvious plurality of functions: to say “art is communication” forces us into circular wrangling around a metaphor taken as an assertion. It is no wonder, then, that many logicians tend to think of grammar as something of a logical disease, some of them even maintaining that mathematics is the real source of coherence in logic. I have no opinion on this, except to repeat that anything which makes a functional use of words will always be involved in all the problems of words.

语法和逻辑似乎都是在内部冲突中发展起来的。人文主义传统一直以来都强调语言冲突在训练思维中的重要性，而且这种强调是正确的：如果我们不懂另一种语言，我们就错失了将我们的思想从其母语语法的束缚中解脱出来的最佳且最简单的机会。同样，逻辑也离不开辩证法——思想中的对立原则。当说不同语言的人们接触时，在沟通的努力中便会构建出一种表意符号结构。数字5就是一个表意符号，因为它对那些称它为“五”、cinq、cinque、fünf以及其他十几种不同发音的人来说，都代表着同一个数字。同样，英语“time”和法语“temps”的纯粹语言联想虽然不同，但将普鲁斯特或柏格森关于时间的论述翻译成英语却完全可行，不会造成严重的误解。当两种语言处于不同的文化轨道上时，例如英语和祖鲁语，构建表意结构就更加困难，但似乎总有一定可能。所有英语词汇和概念在法语中都有对应的表达，但显然我们无法走进波利尼西亚或易洛魁人的社会，然后问：“你们用什么词来指代上帝、灵魂、现实和知识？”他们可能没有这些词汇或概念，我们也无法用英语中的“mana” （神力）和“orenda” （神圣的）来表达他们的想法。然而，显而易见的是，通过耐心和同理心的研究，我们最终能够了解波利尼西亚人或易洛魁人的思维方式。说同一种语言的两个人之间的沟通问题在某些方面可能更大，因为更难察觉，但即使是这些问题最终也能被克服。正是基于这种表意结构的内在联系——无论是两种语言之间语言上的交流，还是说同一种语言的两个人之间心理上的交流——才能发展出将语言融入理性思维的能力。

Grammar and logic both seem to develop through internal conflict. The humanist tradition has always, and rightly, stressed the importance of linguistic conflict in training the mind: if we do not know another language, we have missed the best and simplest opportunity of getting our ideas disentangled from the swaddling clothes of their native syntax. Similarly logic cannot develop properly without dialectic, the principle of opposition in thought. Now when people speaking different languages come into contact, an ideogrammatic structure is built up out of the efforts at communication. The figure 5 is an ideogram, because it means the same number to people who call it five, cinq, cinque, fünf, and a dozen other things. Similarly, the purely linguistic associations of English “time” and French “temps” are different, but it is quite practicable to translate Proust or Bergson on time into English without serious risk of misunderstanding the meaning. When two languages are in different cultural orbits, like English and Zulu, the ideogrammatic structure is more difficult to build up, but it always seems to be more or less possible. There are French equivalents for all English words and ideas, but obviously one cannot walk into a Polynesian or Iroquois society and ask: “What are your words for God, the soul, reality, knowledge?” They may have no such words or concepts, nor can we give them our equivalents for mana and orenda. Yet it seems clear that we can eventually, with patient and sympathetic study, find out what is going on in a Polynesian or Iroquois mind. The problems of communication between two people speaking the same language may in some respects be even greater, because more difficult to become aware of, but even they can be ultimately surmounted. It is out of such ideogrammatic inner structures, whether produced linguistically between two languages, or psychologically between two people speaking the same language, that the capacity to assimilate language to rational thought develops.

这种介于两种语言之间，或者介于同一种语言中两种不同意义结构之间的表意符号中间地带，本身必然是一种符号结构，而不仅仅是一部双语词典。因此，表意符号既非纯粹的语法结构，也非纯粹的逻辑结构。它既是符号，又是修辞符号，因为如同修辞一样，它能唤起受众，并用联想的语言强化意识的语言。简而言之，象形文字是一种隐喻，它将两个各自保留自身形式的事物联系起来，使人意识到你在此语境中用X指代的正是我用Y指代的。这样的象形文字或许与诗歌中纯粹假设的隐喻有所不同，但它同样体现了从简单的“这表示那”的符号出发，进行隐喻式思维的飞跃。

This ideogrammatic middle ground between two languages, or between two personal structures of meaning in the same language, must itself be a symbolic structure, not simply a bilingual dictionary. Hence the ideogram is neither purely grammatical nor purely logical: it is both at once, and rhetorical as well, for, like rhetoric, it brings an audience into being, and reinforces the language of consciousness with that of association. The ideogram, in short, is a metaphor, the identification of two things of which each retains its own form, the realization that what you mean by X in this context is what I mean by Y. Ṡuch an ideogram may differ from the purely hypothetical metaphor of the poem, but the mental leap of metaphor away from the simple “this means that” sign is present in it.

无论读者是否同意以上所有观点，他至少可能愿意承认语法与修辞之间、修辞与逻辑之间可能存在联系，而这些联系虽然被忽视，却至关重要。我们先来看语法与修辞之间的联系。

Whether the reader agrees with all this or not, he may at any rate be willing to admit the possibility of links between grammar and rhetoric, and between rhetoric and logic, that have a neglected but crucial importance. Let us take the link of grammar and rhetoric first.

我们记得，许多语言创作都始于联想式的胡言乱语，其中声音和意义同样重要。其结果便是诗歌的歧义性，正如前文所述，诗人并不定义词语，而是通过将其置于各种各样的语境中来确立其力量。因此，诗歌词源学，即联想发音或意义相近的词语，就显得尤为重要。几个世纪以来，这种倾向一直被当作真正的词源学来对待，学生们被教导要从词语联想的角度思考问题。他们学会了从词源学和物理意义上都认为雪源于云（nix a nubes），而黑暗的树林则源于阳光（这种反义词衍生出了著名的lucus a non lucendo）。当真正的词源学发展起来后，这种联想过程被斥为胡言乱语，从某种角度来看的确如此，但它在批评中仍然是一个至关重要的因素。这里我们再次遇到这样的原则：即使放弃“A是B的来源”这种观点，A和B（在本例中是两个词）之间的类比仍然可能很重要。无论从词源学角度来看，将普罗米修斯与远见卓识联系起来，或将奥德修斯与愤怒联系起来是否合理，诗人都接受了这种联系，而这些联系也为批评家提供了素材。无论“新”批评家在阐释早期诗歌的内涵时是否会犯错或出现时代错置，其中涉及的原则在历史和心理学上都是站得住脚的。

We remember that a good deal of verbal creation begins in associative babble, in which sound and sense are equally involved. The result of this is poetic ambiguity, the fact that, as remarked earlier, the poet does not define his words but establishes their powers by placing them in a great variety of contexts. Hence the importance of poetic etymology, or the tendency to associate words similar in sound or sense. For many centuries this tendency passed itself off as genuine etymology, and the student was taught to think in terms of verbal association. He learned to think of snow as coming etymologically as well as physically from clouds (nix a nubes), and of dark groves as derived from sunlight (the derivation by opposites which produced the famous lucus a non lucendo). When real etymology developed, this associative process was discarded as mumbo-jumbo, which it is from one point of view, but it remains a factor of great importance in criticism. Here again we meet the principle that an analogy between A and B (in this case two words) may still be important even if the view that A is the source of B is dropped. Whether or not one is etymologically justified in associating Prometheus with forethought or Odysseus with wrath, the poets have accepted such associations and they are data for the critic. Whether or not “new” critics make mistakes or anachronisms in explicating the texture of earlier poetry, the principle involved is defensible historically as well as psychologically.

此外，我们很快就会意识到，即使在理性思维中，语言联想仍然是一个重要的因素。例如，翻译中最有效的传达意义的方法之一，就是故意不翻译某个关键词，让读者自行选择。他从自己的语言出发，追溯其在原文中的语境关联。同样，在试图理解一位哲学家的思想时，人们常常从考察一个词入手，比如亚里士多德的“自然”、斯宾诺莎的“实体”或柏格森的“时间”，考察其全部内涵。人们常常觉得，对这类词的全面理解将是理解整个体系的关键。如果真是如此，那也只是一把隐喻的钥匙，因为它代表了思想家与该词之间的一系列关联。试图将这些带有内涵的术语视为必然谬误的做法并不能让我们走得很远。学生们毕业时常常只会抱怨人们不愿定义术语、不愿清晰地推理、不愿抛开情感因素去讨论自由或秩序。或许，将我们的注意力从语言交流的“非本质”转移到“本质”上更为有效，而语言交流所传达的通常是一些含糊不清且充满情感的复杂概念。总之，认为可以将语言简化为手语，使一个词永远只有一个含义，这是一种错觉。在消除动词和名词的联想歧义之后，接下来是形容词和副词的问题，它们本质上就是普遍词；最后是介词和连词，它们作为纯粹的连接词，总是会展现出令人不安的语义多样性。只需浏览一下《美国国家英语词典》中关于“to”、“for”和“in”的词条，就能让最鲁莽的词语原子化者打消念头。

We soon become aware, moreover, that verbal association is still a factor of importance even in rational thought. One of the most effective methods of conveying meaning in translation, for instance, is to leave a key word untranslated, so that the reader has to pick up its contextual associations in the original language from his own. Again, in trying to understand the thought of a philosopher, one often starts by considering a single word, say nature in Aristotle, substance in Spinoza, or time in Bergson, in the total range of its connotations. One often feels that a full understanding of such a word would be a key to the understanding of the whole system. If so, it would be a metaphorical key, as it would be a set of identifications made by the thinker with the word. The attempt to regard such connotative terms as invariably fallacious does not get us very far. Students are often graduated from college armed only with complaints that people will not define their terms, reason clearly, or argue about freedom or order without emotional attachments to those words. It is perhaps more useful to shift our attention from what verbal communication is not to what it is, and what is communicated is usually some ambiguous and emotionally charged complex. In any case the notion that it is possible to reduce language to sign-language, to make one word invariably mean one thing, is an illusion. After one has removed associative ambiguity from verbs and nouns, one has then the problem of adjectives and adverbs, which are universals by their very nature, and finally prepositions and conjunctions, which, being pure connectives, will always display a disconcerting semantic versatility. A glance at the N.E.D. entries for “to,” “for,” and “in” should discourage the brashest of verbal atomizers.

修辞与逻辑之间的联系在于“涂鸦”或联想图，即通过空间来表达概念。大量的介词都是空间隐喻，其中大多数源于人体方位。“上”、“下”、“此外”、“另一方面”、“在……之下”等词语的每一次使用，无论论证的内容是什么，都暗示着论证中潜意识里存在着某种图式。如果一位作者写道：“但另一方面，还有一点需要考虑，以支持反方论点”，他或许是在用正常的（尽管略显冗长）英语写作，但他所做的，恰恰与纸上谈兵的战略家在桌布上涂鸦作战计划时所做的一样。很多时候，一种“结构”或“系统”的思想都可以简化为一种图式模式——事实上，这两个词在某种程度上都是“图式”的同义词。当一位哲学家意识到这种图式的存在并将其提取出来时，他对读者来说就大有裨益，正如柏拉图在讨论分裂问题时所做的那样。线。任何论证，若不意识到其中蕴含某种图形公式，我们都无法深入探讨。所有的划分和分类、章节的使用、以“现在让我们转向”或“回到前面提到的要点”为标志的指向性（如果我的理解正确的话）、论证中“契合”的判断、以及某个要点是“中心”而另一个要点是“边缘”的感觉，都具有某种几何基础。

The link between rhetoric and logic is “doodle” or associative diagram, the expression of the conceptual by the spatial. A great number of prepositions are spatial metaphors, most of them derived from the orientation of the human body. Every use of “up,” “down,” “besides,” “on the other hand,” “under” implies a subconscious diagram in the argument, whatever it is. If a writer says “But on the other hand there is a further consideration to be brought forward in support of the opposing argument,” he may be writing normal (if wordy) English, but he is also doing precisely what an armchair strategist does when he scrawls plans of battle on a tablecloth. Very often a “structure” or “system” of thought can be reduced to a diagrammatic pattern—in fact both words are to some extent synonyms of diagram. A philosopher is of great assistance to his reader when he realizes the presence of such a diagram and extracts it, as Plato does in his discussion of the divided line. We cannot go far in any argument without realizing that there is some kind of graphic formula involved. All division and categorization, the use of chapters, the topotropism (if I have constructed this correctly) signalled by “let us now turn to” or “reverting to the point made earlier,” the sense of what “fits” the argument, the feeling that one point is “central” and another peripheral, has some kind of geometrical basis.

过去人们常说，所有抽象词最初都是具体的隐喻，因此，在词语的整个语义历史中，都会始终带有某种具体隐喻的痕迹。这种观点如今已被否定，但其中仍蕴含着许多真理：我质疑，是否真的有可能使B依赖于A而不使其在某种程度上依附于A，或者使B与A相关而不使其在某种程度上被包裹。我认为，这种观点唯一的谬误在于，它假定所依附的隐喻必然是词源中隐含的隐喻。当然，作者可以赋予一个词一个与其词源毫无关联的含义。但抽象的词语和概念似乎都是从某种潜在的具体表述中借用而来，而这种表述并非存在于词语的使用历史中，而是存在于词语所融入的论证结构中。

It used to be said that, as all abstract words were originally concrete metaphors, something of the latter will always adhere to the word through all its semantic history. This view is discredited now, but it still has much truth in it: I question whether it is really possible to make B depend on A without in some measure hanging it on, or involve B with A without in some measure wrapping them up. The only fallacy in it, I think, is the assumption that the attached metaphor must necessarily be the one implied in the etymology of the word. Of course a writer may give a word a meaning which has no recognizable connection with its origin. But it looks as though abstract words and ideas were on loan, so to speak, from a latent concrete formulation which is to be found, not in the history of the word used, but in the structure of the argument into which the word is fitted.

一旦开始思考联想和图表在论证中的作用，就会意识到它们无处不在。我曾听一位牧师鼓吹宗教，理由是科学过于冷漠枯燥，无法指导人生，而革命热情的火焰却让人渴望更多。他举的图表看似寻常，但显然，古老的物质四要素图表——冷、热、干、湿——正是他论证的图形化表达，而宗教对他而言意味着某种湿润之物，一种滋养的水分，能够温暖科学家，冷却激进分子。同样的图形化表达原则也体现在以下假设中：理智冷静理智，情感热情奔放；实践感行走，想象力跳跃；事实坚实（“顽固”），假设流动（“覆盖”事实），理论如气体；心灵“内部”的一切昏暗无光，心灵“外部”的一切清晰明了，等等。价值假设中也存在这样的假设：具体优于抽象，主动优于被动，动态优于静态，统一优于多元，简单优于复杂。宗教人们认为天堂是“上方”的；心理学家认为潜意识是意识的“下方”，这两个词显然都是空间隐喻。

As soon as one starts to think of the role of association and diagram in argument, one begins to realize how extraordinarily pervasive they are. I once heard a preacher advocate religion on the ground that science was too cold and dry to serve as a guide to life, while the heat of revolutionary zeal still left one thirsting for something more. The figures seemed commonplace, yet it was clear that the ancient diagram of the four principles of substance, hot, cold, moist, and dry, was the graphic formula of his argument, and that religion meant something wet to him, a fertilizing moisture that would warm the scientists and cool the radicals. The same principle of a graphic formula is found in such assumptions as: that the intellect is cool and sober and the emotions warm and drunk; that the practical sense walks and the imaginative one leaps; that facts are solid (“stubborn”), hypotheses liquid (“covering” facts), and theories gaseous; that whatever is “inside” the mind is dimly lit and whatever is “outside” it clear, and so on. Also in value-assumptions: that the concrete is better than the abstract, the active better than the passive, the dynamic better than the static, the unified better than the multiple, the simple better than the complex. Religious people think of heaven as “up”; psychologists think of the subconscious as “underneath” the consciousness, both words being obviously spatial metaphors.

我们可以继续讨论很久，但现在显然，与其试图根除隐喻，不如意识到隐喻的存在更为明智。仅仅为了驳斥某个论点或断言它“不过”是隐喻而进行的隐喻分析是不值得提倡的。我们应该提倡的是分析本身，我认为，正如本书结论部分将要阐述的那样，这种分析对于文学批评家而言具有相当重要的意义，而且其重要性还在不断提升。

We could go on for a long time, but by now it is surely clear that it is wiser simply to become aware of metaphor than to try to eradicate it. Attempts to analyze metaphor solely to debunk an argument or suggest that it is “nothing but” a metaphor are not to be encouraged. What is to be encouraged is the analysis itself, in which there is, I think, an activity of considerable and increasing importance for literary critics, as the conclusion of this book will suggest.

在西方文化中，论述理性历来享有至高无上的地位。在宗教领域，除圣经之外的任何诗歌都不能与神学家的命题相提并论；在哲学领域，理性是现实的最高祭司（除非该哲学体系具有赋予艺术特殊重要性的特征，例如谢林的哲学）；在科学领域，同样的层级结构则更为清晰。因此，艺术历来被视为一种“调和”形式，其功能在于建立理性与假定体系中“低于”理性的事物之间的联系，例如情感或感官。因此，在旨在唤起情感或进行某种形式的动感劝说的语言结构中发现“调和”现象也就不足为奇了。这种调和现象已被人们认识数个世纪，因为它与修辞学传统上从属于辩证法的观念相一致。概念修辞学的概念提出了新的问题，因为它表明，任何由文字构成的事物都不能超越文字的性质和条件，并且，就理性而言，理性的性质和条件包含在言辞之中。

The discursive reason has traditionally been given the place of honor in Western culture. In religion, no poetry outside Scripture is given the authority of the theologian’s propositions; in philosophy, the reason is the high priest of reality (unless there are special features in the philosophy giving a peculiar importance to the arts, as there are in Schelling’s); in science the same hierarchical diagram is even clearer. Hence the arts have been traditionally regarded as forms of “accommodation,” their function being to establish a link between reason and whatever is put “below” it on the assumed diagram, such as the emotions or the senses. It is thus no surprise to find “accommodation” in verbal structures aimed at rousing emotion or at some form of kinetic persuasion. Such accommodation has been recognized for centuries, as it is consistent with the traditional subordinating of rhetoric to dialectic. The notion of a conceptual rhetoric raises new problems, as it suggests that nothing built out of words can transcend the nature and conditions of words, and that the nature and conditions of ratio, so far as ratio is verbal, are contained by oratio.

初步结论

TENTATIVE CONCLUSION

初步结论

Tentative Conclusion

本书探讨了多种批评技巧和方法，其中大部分已被当代学术界所采用。我们试图阐明，在全面的批评观中，原型或神话批评家、审美形式批评家、历史批评家、中世纪四层次批评家以及文本与质感批评家应处于何种位置。无论这种全面的批评观是否正确，我希望本书能够阐明，试图将任何批评群体排除在外都是愚蠢的。正如开篇所述，本书并非旨在为批评家们提出一套新的方案，而是为他们现有的方案提供一种新的视角，而这些方案本身已足够有效。本书并不攻击任何批评方法本身（一旦“方法”一词被界定），而是攻击各种方法之间的壁垒。这些壁垒往往使批评家局限于单一的批评方法，而这并非必要；它们也往往使批评家们的主要关注点并非其他批评家，而是批评之外的领域。因此，神话批评中出现了大量（虽然不多，但也太多）读起来像糟糕的比较宗教学的文章，修辞批评中出现了大量（读起来像糟糕的语义学的文章），美学批评中出现了大量（读起来像糟糕的形而上学的文章），等等。

THE PRESENT BOOK has dealt with a variety of critical techniques and approaches, most of them already used in contemporary scholarship. We have tried to show where the archetypal or mythical critic, the aesthetic form critic, the historical critic, the medieval four-level critic, the text-and-texture critic, belong in a comprehensive view of criticism. Whether the comprehensive view is right or not, I hope some sense has been communicated of what folly it would be to try to exclude any of these groups from criticism. As was said at the beginning, the present book is not designed to suggest a new program for critics, but a new perspective on their existing programs, which in themselves are valid enough. The book attacks no methods of criticism, once that subject has been defined: what it attacks are the barriers between the methods. These barriers tend to make a critic confine himself to a single method of criticism, which is unnecessary, and they tend to make him establish his primary contacts, not with other critics, but with subjects outside criticism. Hence the number of essays, not large but too large, in mythical criticism that read like bad comparative religion, in rhetorical criticism that read like bad semantics, in aesthetic criticism that read like bad metaphysics, and so on.

在打破壁垒的过程中，我认为原型批评扮演着核心角色，我也赋予了它重要的地位。我们文化传统中有一个元素通常被视为荒谬绝伦，那就是对神话的寓言式解释。这种解释在中世纪和文艺复兴时期的批评中占据了举足轻重的地位，并且断断续续地延续至今（例如，罗斯金的《空中女王》）。神话寓言化的障碍在于，它假定解释“就是”神话“所指”。然而，神话作为一种向心式的意义结构，可以被赋予无数种含义，因此，研究神话实际被赋予的意义更为有意义。

In this process of breaking down barriers I think archetypal criticism has a central role, and I have given it a prominent place. One element in our cultural tradition which is usually regarded as fantastic nonsense is the allegorical explanations of myths which bulk so large in medieval and Renaissance criticism and continue sporadically (e.g., Ruskin’s Queen of the Air) to our own time. The allegorization of myth is hampered by the assumption that the explanation “is” what the myth “means.” A myth being a centripetal structure of meaning, it can be made to mean an indefinite number of things, and it is more fruitful to study what in fact myths have been made to mean.

“神话”一词在不同领域可能具有，而且显然确实具有不同的含义。从长远来看，这些含义无疑是可以调和的，但调和它们的任务尚待未来。在文学批评中，“神话”最终指的是“神话体系”（mythos），即文学形式的结构性组织原则。我们记得，评注是一种寓言化，任何伟大的文学作品都可能……评论浩如烟海，无穷无尽。这一事实常常令评论家感到沮丧，让他们觉得关于《哈姆雷特》的一切，例如，恐怕早已被反复提及。A和B两位博学睿智的学者在解读《哈姆雷特》时已有的见解，再加上C、D、E等人的见解，最终，出于自我保护的本能，大部分评论要么无人问津，要么（在文化层面上也大同小异）被转交给专家来解读。因此，那些缺乏对文学整体原型结构的理解的评论，延续了寓言神话的传统，并继承了其精妙绝伦、匠心独运和徒劳无功的特质。

The term myth may have, and obviously does have, different meanings in different subjects. These meanings are doubtless reconcilable in the long run, but the task of reconciling them lies in the future. In literary criticism myth means ultimately mythos, a structural organizing principle of literary form. Commentary, we remember, is allegorization, and any great work of literature may carry an infinite amount of commentary. This fact often depresses the critic and makes him feel that everything to be said about Hamlet, for instance, must already have been said many times. To what has occurred to the learned and astute minds of A and B in reading Hamlet is added what occurs to the learned and astute minds of C, D, E, and so on, until out of sheer self-preservation most of it is left unread, or (much the same thing culturally) is assigned to specialists. Commentary which has no sense of the archetypal shape of literature as a whole, then, continues the tradition of allegorized myth, and inherits its characteristics of brilliance, ingenuity, and futility.

解决这一困境的唯一办法，就是将寓言批评与原型批评相结合。一旦人们哪怕隐约意识到，批评的终点在于文学整体的结构，起点在于所研究的文本，那么情况就会好转许多。仅仅将文本当作注释的检验工具，如同系在风筝上的线，是远远不够的。因为人们可以围绕显而易见的意义展开第一层注释，然后围绕潜意识的意义展开第二层注释，再围绕诗歌的惯例和外部关系展开第三层注释，如此循环往复，永无止境。这种做法并非现代批评家所独有，因为对维吉尔《第四牧歌》的弥赛亚预言解读，也同样假定维吉尔“无意识地”预言了弥赛亚的到来。但诗人无意中指的是他所有可能的评注，因此更简单的说法是，维吉尔和以赛亚在描写英雄诞生的神话时都使用了同一种意象，正因为这种相似性，例如，《圣诞颂》才能同时运用这两种意象。这种方法有助于分散评注，避免每首诗都成为孤立的学术中心。

The only cure for this situation is the supplementing of allegorical with archetypal criticism. Things become more hopeful as soon as there is a feeling, however dim, that criticism has an end in the structure of literature as a total form, as well as a beginning in the text studied. It is not sufficient to use the text as a check on commentary, like a string tied to a kite, for one may develop a primary body of commentary around the obvious meaning, then a secondary body about the unconscious meaning, then a third body around the conventions and external relations of the poem, and so on indefinitely. This practice is not confined to modern critics, for the interpretation of Virgil’s Fourth Eclogue as Messianic also assumed that Virgil was “unconsciously” prophesying the Messiah. But the poet unconsciously meant the whole corpus of his possible commentary, and it is simpler merely to say that Virgil and Isaiah use the same type of imagery dealing with the myth of the hero’s birth, and that because of this similarity the Nativity Ode, for instance, is able to use both. This procedure helps to distribute the commentary, and prevents each poem from becoming a separate center of isolated scholarship.

根据我们的原则，批评理论涵盖了“人文学科”的教育层面，因为直接教授和学习的是批评而非文学。因此，对批评理论的困惑很容易被解读为对人文学科“命运”或“困境”的担忧。因此，打破批评内部的壁垒，从长远来看，将使批评家们更加意识到批评整体与其他学科之间的外部联系。关于最后一个问题，我仅作几句最后的补充说明，因为在我看来，过多的谨慎反而显得多余。完全回避这里讨论的更重大的问题，这实在称不上诚实。

The theory of criticism embraces the “humanities,” in their educational aspect, according to our principle that it is criticism and not literature which is directly taught and learned. Hence a sense of bewilderment about the theory of criticism is readily projected as a concern over the “fate” or “plight” of the humanities. The breaking down of barriers within criticism would therefore have the long-run effect of making critics more aware of the external relations of criticism as a whole with other disciplines. This last subject is one on which I make a few final comments only because it seems to me that it would be an excess of prudence, in fact hardly honest, to shrink altogether from the larger issues of the questions here discussed.

艺术的创作通常以有机生命的“创造性”隐喻来描述。人类生活有一种奇特的倾向，即模仿“低等”存在形式的某些方面，例如模仿植物生命与四季更迭微妙节奏同步的仪式。人类文化无意识地采用有机体的节奏本身并非不合理。艺术家倾向于以一种更为精妙的方式模仿前人，从而形成一种文化老化的传统，这种传统会持续下去，直到某些重大变革中断这一过程并重新开始。因此，历史批评的内在形式很可能就是某种准有机的文化老化节奏，正如我们这个时代的大多数哲学史学家所提出的，其中斯宾格勒的观点最为明确。如今，人们普遍认为我们所处的时代是“西方”文化的“晚期”阶段，而中世纪则是其青年时期；同时，我们这个时代也类似于早期古典文化的罗马时期。这种观点似乎已成为当代世界观中不可避免的范畴之一。第一篇文章中探讨的各种模式的演变似乎与这种文化史观存在某种相似之处。

The production of art is usually described in the “creative” metaphors of organic life. There is a curious tendency in human life to imitate some of the aspects of “lower” forms of existence, like the rituals which imitate the subtle synchronizations with the rhythms of the turning year that vegetable life makes. It is not in itself unreasonable that human culture would unconsciously assume the rhythms of an organism. Artists tend to imitate their predecessors in a slightly more sophisticated way, thus producing a tradition of cultural aging which goes on until some large change interrupts the process and starts it over again. Hence the containing form of historical criticism may well be some quasi-organic rhythm of cultural aging, such as is postulated in one form or another by most of the philosophical historians of our time, most explicitly by Spengler. The conception of our own time as a “late” phase of a “Western” culture of which the Middle Ages was the youth, and as a phase resembling the Roman phase of an earlier Classical culture, is in practice taken for granted by everyone today, and seems to be one of the inevitable categories of the contemporary outlook. The progression of modes traced in the first essay seems to have some analogy to this view of cultural history.

任何此类观点，如果被采纳，都可以用形而上学的论调加以修饰，以迎合持有者；但没有任何理由认为它一定是“宿命论”的，除非认为人每年都会变老也算是宿命论；也没有理由认为它应该包含任何关于历史必然循环或预定未来的理论。当然，它不应该被扭曲成修辞价值判断的基础。例如，在对中世纪文化的感伤主义观点中，我们就能看到这种观点，这种观点认为中世纪文化是一个庞大的综合体，随后逐渐瓦解，不断细分和专业化，最终将我们所有人带到了今天这个“美好通道”（Pretty Pass）。自十八世纪中叶以来，几乎每一代人都以某种形式呼吁恢复中世纪文化的某种统一性，或者恢复其中的某些特质。同样的观点的衍生形式也存在于那些无法欣赏莫扎特之后任何音乐的人身上，或者无论他们选择哪个流派。在那些谈论资本主义文化颓废的马克思主义者身上；在那些谈论回归的危言耸听者身上。进入新的黑暗时代，等等。所有这些都以某种或多或少混乱的准有机历史理论为基础。

Any such view, if adopted, could be decorated metaphysically to suit the tenant: but there is no reason why it should be “fatalistic,” unless it is fatalism to say that one gets older every year, nor why it should include any theory of inevitable cycles in history or a pre-ordained future. Certainly it should not be perverted into a basis for rhetorical value-judgements. We get these, for instance, in the sentimental view of medieval culture which sees it as a gigantic synthesis followed by a progressive disintegration which has subdivided and specialized until it has finally landed us all in the Pretty Pass which we are in today. A movement which will restore something of the unity of medieval culture to the modern world, or some other qualities of it, has been hailed in one form or other in nearly every generation since the middle of the eighteenth century. Subsidiary forms of the same view are present in the people who cannot listen with pleasure to any music later than Mozart, or whatever terminal they choose; in the Marxists who speak of the decadence of capitalist culture; in the alarmists who speak of a return to a new Dark Ages, and so on. All these have a more or less muddled version of some quasi-organic theory of history as their basis.

批评界常说艺术不会进化或进步，它只会制造经典或范式。我们仍然可以买到讲述绘画“发展史”的书籍，从石器时代到毕加索，但这些书籍展现的并非发展，而仅仅是一系列技艺的变异，毕加索的水平与他的马格德林先祖几乎不相上下。我们偶尔会在艺术中体验到一种醍醐灌顶般的顿悟。听完帕莱斯特里纳的经文歌或莫扎特的嬉游曲后，我们或许会感受到音乐本身的声音：这正是音乐存在的意义所在。这种简洁让我们意识到，简洁与平庸截然相反，它让我们感受到艺术表达的极限已被永远触及。这种感受源于直接体验，而非批评，但它暗示着一个重要的批评原则：艺术中最深刻的体验就蕴藏在已完成的艺术作品之中。

It is a commonplace of criticism that art does not evolve or improve: it produces the classic or model. One can still buy books narrating the “development” of painting from the Stone Age to Picasso, but they show no development, only a series of mutations in skill, Picasso being on much the same level as his Magdalenian ancestors. Every once in a while we experience in the arts a feeling of definitive revelation. This, we may feel after a Palestrina motet or a Mozart divertimento, is the voice of music itself: this is the kind of thing that music was invented to say. Here is a simplicity which makes us realize that the simple is the opposite of the commonplace, a feeling that the boundaries of possible expression in the art have been reached for all time. This feeling belongs to direct experience, not to criticism, but it suggests the critical principle that the profoundest experiences possible to obtain in the arts are available in the art already produced.

艺术的进步在于人们对艺术的理解，以及由此带来的社会提升。文化的受益者是消费者而非生产者，是消费者变得更加人性化、更具博学。伟大的诗人未必一定要是智者、善人，甚至不必是品行端正的人，但他的读者却完全有理由在阅读他的作品后提升自身的人性。因此，文化的生产或许如同仪式一般，是对有机节奏或过程的一种半自发的模仿；而对文化的回应，则如同神话一般，是一种革命性的意识行为。当代艺术研究技术能力的提升，例如绘画复制、音乐录制和现代图书馆的建立，构成了一场文化革命的一部分，这场革命使得人文学科与自然科学一样，都孕育着新的发展。因为这场革命不仅仅体现在技术层面，更体现在精神生产力的提升。人文主义传统以其现代形式出现，伴随着印刷机的发明，其直接影响与其说是刺激了新文化，不如说是编纂了过去的遗产。

What does improve in the arts is the comprehension of them, and the refining of society which results from it. It is the consumer, not the producer, who benefits by culture, the consumer who becomes humanized and liberally educated. There is no reason why a great poet should be a wise and good man, or even a tolerable human being, but there is every reason why his reader should be improved in his humanity as a result of reading him. Hence while the production of culture may be, like ritual, a half-involuntary imitation of organic rhythms or processes, the response to culture is, like myth, a revolutionary act of consciousness. The contemporary development of the technical ability to study the arts, represented by reproductions of painting, the recording of music, and modem libraries, forms part of a cultural revolution which makes the humanities quite as pregnant with new developments as the sciences. For the revolution is not simply in technology, but in spiritual productive power. The humanistic tradition itself arose, in its modern form, with the invention of the printing press, the immediate effect of which was not to stimulate new culture so much as to codify the heritage of the past.

过去几乎每一件艺术作品在其所处的时代都具有社会功能，而这种功能往往并非主要出于审美目的。“艺术作品”作为一种分类的整个概念所有绘画、雕塑、诗歌和音乐作品的艺术性都相对而言是近代才出现的。我们可以在秘鲁纺织品、旧石器时代的绘画、斯基泰人的马饰或夸夸卡瓦克族的面具中看到审美冲动的体现，但这样做会形成一种复杂的抽象概念，而这种概念很可能超出了创作者的思维习惯。因此，判断一件事物是否“是”艺术品，不能仅仅诉诸于事物本身的性质。决定其归属的是习俗、社会认可以及广义上的批评。它最初可能是为了实用而非娱乐而创作的，因此可能不符合亚里士多德对艺术的普遍定义，但如果它现在是为了取悦我们而存在，那么它就是我们所说的艺术。

Nearly every work of art in the past had a social function in its own time, a function which was often not primarily an aesthetic function at all. The whole conception of “works of art” as a classification for all pictures, statues, poems, and musical compositions is a relatively modern one. We can see an aesthetic impulse at work in Peruvian textiles, palaeolithic drawings, Scythian horse ornaments, or Kwakiutl masks, but in doing so we make a sophisticated abstraction which may well have been outside the mental habits of the people who produced them. Thus the question of whether a thing “is” a work of art or not is one which cannot be settled by appealing to something in the nature of the thing itself. It is convention, social acceptance, and the work of criticism in the broadest sense that determines where it belongs. It may have been originally made for use rather than pleasure, and so fall outside the general Aristotelian conception of art, but if it now exists for our pleasure it is what we call art.

当任何事物被如此重新归类时，它便会失去大部分原有功能。即使是最狂热的历史批评家也必然会认为，我们之所以钦佩莎士比亚和荷马，是因为他们自身以及他们所处的社会背景在很大程度上是无法理解的。然而，我们绝不能满足于仅仅剥离艺术作品原有功能的研究方法。批评的任务之一在于恢复其功能，当然，这并非是要还原其原始功能（这是不可能的），而是要在新的语境中重新创造其功能。

When anything is reclassified in this way, it loses much of its original function. Even the most fanatical historical critic is bound to see Shakespeare and Homer as writers whom we admire for reasons that would have been largely unintelligible to them, to say nothing of their societies. But we can hardly be satisfied with an approach to works of art which simply strips from them their original function. One of the tasks of criticism is that of the recovery of function, not of course the restoration of an original function, which is out of the question, but the recreation of function in a new context.

克尔凯郭尔写了一本引人入胜的小书，名为《重复》，书中他提议用“重复”一词来取代柏拉图更传统的术语“追忆”（anamnesis）或“回忆”。他显然指的是，并非简单地重复某种经验，而是对其进行重塑，使其焕发新生，最终达到他所说的末世预言：“看哪，我将一切都更新了。” 人文学科对过去的执着有时会被一些人诟病，这些人忘记了我们面对的正是过去：它或许模糊不清，但它却是我们存在的全部。柏拉图描绘了一幅阴郁的景象：人凝视着客观世界墙壁上由我们身后如同太阳的火焰所投射出的闪烁光影。但当这些阴影代表过去时，这种类比便不再成立，因为我们唯一能够看到它们的光芒，是我们内心深处那普罗米修斯般的火焰。这些阴影的实质只能存在于我们自身之中，而历史批判的目标，正如我们经常用比喻来表达的那样，是一种自我复活，一种将枯骨之谷的景象转化为我们自身景象的血肉之躯的景象。过去的文化不仅是人类的记忆，也是我们自身埋藏的生命。对它的研究会引向一个认知的场景，一种发现：我们看到的并非过去的生命，而是当下生活的完整文化形态。不仅诗人，他的读者也负有“赋予其新意”的义务。

Kierkegaard has written a fascinating little book called Repetition, in which he proposes to use this term to replace the more traditional Platonic term anamnesis or recollection. By it he apparently means, not the simple repeating of an experience, but the recreating of it which redeems or awakens it to life, the end of the process, he says, being the apocalyptic promise: “Behold, I make all things new.” The preoccupation of the humanities with the past is sometimes made a reproach against them by those who forget that we face the past: it may be shadowy, but it is all that is there. Plato draws a gloomy picture of man staring at the flickering shapes made on the wall of the objective world by a fire behind us like the sun. But the analogy breaks down when the shadows are those of the past, for the only light we can see them by is the Promethean fire within us. The substance of these shadows can only be in ourselves, and the goal of historical criticism, as our metaphors about it often indicate, is a kind of self-resurrection, the vision of a valley of dry bones that takes on the flesh and blood of our own vision. The culture of the past is not only the memory of mankind, but our own buried life, and study of it leads to a recognition scene, a discovery in which we see, not our past lives, but the total cultural form of our present life. It is not only the poet but his reader who is subject to the obligation to “make it new.”

如果缺乏这种“重复”意识，历史批评往往会将文化产物从我们的关注范围中剥离出去。正如所有真正的历史批评家所做的那样，历史批评必须与对过去艺术当代意义的感知相平衡。但这种当代意义的感知自然常常局限于当下的特定议题；它不应被视为拓展当下生活的视角，而应被视为支持当下的某种事业或论点。

Without this sense of “repetition,” historical criticism tends to remove the products of culture from our own sphere of interest. It must be counterpoised, as it is in all genuine historical critics, by a sense of the contemporary relevance of past art. But it is natural that this sense of contemporary relevance should often be confined to a specific issue in the present; that it should be thought of, not as expanding the perspective of present life, but as supporting a cause or thesis in the present.

如果我们从历史的任何一点切入，包括我们自身的历史，并研究其横截面，就会发现阶级结构的存在。文化可能被某个社会或知识阶层用来提升其声望；一般来说，道德审查者、伟大传统的甄选者、宗教或政治事业的辩护者、唯美主义者、激进分子、经典著作的编纂者等等，都是这种阶级张力的体现。在研究他们的言论时，我们很快就会意识到，真正连贯一致的此类道德批判，唯有那些与全面革命的社会哲学相契合的批判才算得上是此类批判，例如马克思主义、尼采，以及十九世纪英国和二十世纪美国对寡头价值观的某些合理化解释。在所有这些论述中，文化都被视为一种人类生产力，它过去像其他生产力一样，被其他统治阶级所剥削，而现在则需要根据构建更美好社会的标准来重新评估其价值。但由于这种理想社会只存在于未来，因此目前对文化的价值评价是基于其暂时的革命性效果。

If we cut through history at any point, including our own, and study a cross-section of it, we get a class structure. Culture may be employed by a social or intellectual class to increase its prestige; and in general, moral censors, selectors of great traditions, apologists of religious or political causes, aesthetes, radicals, codifiers of great books, and the like, are expressions of such class tensions. We soon realize, in studying their pronouncements, that the only really consistent moral criticism of this type would be the kind which is harnessed to an all-round revolutionary philosophy of society, such as we find not only in Marxism but in Nietzsche and in some of the rationalizations of oligarchic values in nineteenth-century Britain and twentieth-century America. In all these culture is treated as a human productive power which in the past has been, like other productive powers, exploited by other ruling classes and is now to be revalued in terms of a better society. But as this ideal society exists only in the future, the present valuation of culture is in terms of its interim revolutionary effectiveness.

这种革命性的文化观也与柏拉图一样古老，其所选择的传统总是《理想国》中关于诗人的论证的某种形式。一旦我们将文化视为未来乃至或许可以实现的社会的明确图景，我们便开始对传统进行甄别和清洗，所有不符合这一标准的艺术家（随着这一过程的进行，人数会越来越多）都必须被淘汰。因此，正如未经修正的历史批判将文化仅仅与过去联系起来一样，未经修正的伦理批判也将文化仅仅与未来联系起来，与理想社会联系起来——如果我们足够重视对青年的教育，这个理想社会最终或许就能实现。对于所有这些……各种思想最终都会导致对下一代的灌输，就像维多利亚时代进步主义的道德版本导致了 Podsnap 和年轻人的脸红一样。

This revolutionary way of looking at culture is also as old as Plato, the selected tradition being always some version of the argument about poets in the Republic. As soon as we make culture a definite image of a future and perhaps attainable society, we start selecting and purging a tradition, and all the artists who don’t fit (an increasing number as the process goes on) have to be thrown out. So, just as historical criticism uncorrected relates culture only to the past, ethical criticism uncorrected relates culture only to the future, to the ideal society which may eventually come if we take sufficient pains to guard the educating of our youth. For all such lines of thought end in indoctrinating the next generation, just as the moral version of Victorian progressivism led to Podsnap and the blushing cheeks of the young person.

社会或文明中的一切活动既维护又削弱着该社会的阶级结构。维系阶级结构的社会能量催生出三种主要形式的堕落文化：纯粹的上层阶级文化（或炫耀文化）、纯粹的中产阶级文化（或庸俗文化）以及纯粹的下层阶级文化（或肮脏文化）。马修·阿诺德将这三个阶级分别称为野蛮人、庸俗人和平民。任何形式的革命行动都会导致一个阶级的专政，历史的记录似乎清楚地表明，没有比这更快捷的方式来摧毁文化的益处。如果我们把文化的理念与统治者的道德观念联系起来，我们得到的就是野蛮人的文化；如果我们把它与无产阶级的观念联系起来，我们得到的就是平民的文化；如果我们把它与任何形式的资产阶级乌托邦联系起来，我们得到的就是庸俗的文化。

The body of work done in society, or civilization, both maintains and undermines the class structure of that society. The social energy which maintains the class structure produces perverted culture in its three chief forms: mere upper-class culture, or ostentation, mere middle-class culture, or vulgarity, and mere lower-class culture, or squalor. These three classes are called by Matthew Arnold respectively, in so far as they are classes, the barbarians, the philistines, and the populace. Revolutionary action, of whatever kind, leads to the dictatorship of one class, and the record of history seems clear that there is no quicker way of destroying the benefits of culture. If we attach our vision of culture to the conception of ruler-morality, we get the culture of barbarians; if we attach it to the conception of a proletariat, we get the culture of the populace; if we attach it to any kind of bourgeois Utopia, we get the culture of philistinism.

无论人们如何看待辩证唯物主义哲学，不可否认的是，当人们的行为或假装行为像物质实体时，他们的行为确实具有辩证性。如果英国与法国开战，英国的所有弱点和法国的所有优点在英国都会被忽略；叛徒不仅被视为罪大恶极的罪犯，而且还会被愤慨地否认任何叛徒的动机是正当的。在战争中，物质或偶像崇拜取代了精神的真正辩证法，人们只能依靠半真半假的真理生活。同样的原则也适用于由“观点”引发的言语战争或模仿战争，而这些“观点”通常是某种社会冲突的幽灵。

Whatever one thinks of dialectic materialism as a philosophy, it is certainly true that when men behave or pretend to behave like material bodies they do behave dialectically. If England goes to war with France, all the weaknesses in the English case and all the virtues in the French case are ignored in England; not only is the traitor the lowest of criminals, but it is indignantly denied that any traitor can be honestly motivated. In war, the physical or idolatrous substitute for the real dialectic of the spirit, one lives by half-truths. The same principle applies to the verbal or mimic wars made out of “points of view,” which are usually the ghosts of some kind of social conflict.

似乎最好是努力摆脱所有这些冲突，并遵循阿诺德的另一条公理：“文化力求消除阶级”。博雅教育的伦理目的是解放，这只能意味着使人能够设想一个自由、无阶级且文明的社会。这样的社会并不存在，这也是博雅教育必须高度重视想象力作品的原因之一。艺术作品中的想象力元素，再次使它们摆脱了历史的束缚。任何从完整的批评经验中涌现出来，并成为博雅教育一部分的事物，无论其最初的指涉对象是什么，都因此成为解放的、人道的文化共同体的一部分。因此，博雅教育解放了文化作品本身。以及它们所培养的心灵。人类艺术赖以建立的腐败将永远存在于艺术之中，但艺术的想象力使其在腐败中得以保存，如同圣人的遗体一般。任何关于美的讨论都不能局限于孤立的艺术作品的形式关系；它还必须考虑艺术作品在社会努力目标愿景——即完全无阶级文明的理念——中所扮演的角色。这种完全文明的理念也是伦理批判始终指向的隐含道德标准，它与任何道德体系都截然不同。

It seems better to try to get clear of all such conflicts, attaching ourselves to Arnold’s other axiom that “culture seeks to do away with classes.” The ethical purpose of a liberal education is to liberate, which can only mean to make one capable of conceiving society as free, classless, and urbane. No such society exists, which is one reason why a liberal education must be deeply concerned with works of imagination. The imaginative element in works of art, again, lifts them clear of the bondage of history. Anything that emerges from the total experience of criticism to form part of a liberal education becomes, by virtue of that fact, part of the emancipated and humane community of culture, whatever its original reference. Thus liberal education liberates the works of culture themselves as well as the mind they educate. The corruption out of which human art has been constructed will always remain in the art, but the imaginative quality of the art preserves it in its corruption, like the corpse of a saint. No discussion of beauty can confine itself to the formal relations of the isolated work of art; it must consider, too, the participation of the work of art in the vision of the goal of social effort, the idea of complete and classless civilization. This idea of complete civilization is also the implicit moral standard to which ethical criticism always refers, something very different from any system of morals.

文化中蕴含的自由社会理念永远无法被具体化，更遑论建立成一个社会。文化是一种当下的社会理想，我们通过努力追求它来教育和解放自己，却永远无法真正达到。它如同书本般耐心地教导我们，每次翻开都呈现相同的文字，但我们无法拥有它，因为文字所承载的经验和意义总是新的。任何社会都无法规划自身的文化，除非它将文化产出限制在社会可预测的标准之内。伦理批判的目标是价值重估，即能够以一种超脱的视角审视当代社会价值观，并将它们与文化所呈现的无限可能性进行某种程度的比较。拥有这种价值重估能力的人处于一种思想自由的状态。而缺乏这种能力的人则沦为社会价值观的奴隶，受制于先入为主的观念、教条和偏见。当前那种坚持认为人不能成为自己人生的旁观者的倾向，在我看来，是一种致命的半真半假的说法，它源于某种社会弊病。大多数伦理行为都是一种机械的习惯性反应：要想在其中融入任何自由原则，我们就需要某种行动理论，这里的“理论”指的是一种超脱的、抽离的视角，它审视行动的手段和目的，这种视角不会使行动瘫痪，而是通过阐明行动的目标，使行动变得有意义。

The idea of the free society implied in culture can never be formulated, much less established as a society. Culture is a present social ideal which we educate and free ourselves by trying to attain, and never do attain. It teaches, with the endless patience of the book which always presents the same words whenever we open it, but it is not possessed, for the experiences and meanings attached to the words are always new. No society can plan for its own culture unless it restricts the output of culture to socially predictable standards. The goal of ethical criticism is transvaluation, the ability to look at contemporary social values with the detachment of one who is able to compare them in some degree with the infinite vision of possibilities presented by culture. One who possesses such a standard of transvaluation is in a state of intellectual freedom. One who does not possess it is a creature of whatever social values get to him first: he has only the compulsions of habit, indoctrination, and prejudice. The current tendency to insist that man cannot be a spectator of his own life seems to me to be one of those lethal half-truths that arise in response to some kind of social malaise. Most ethical action is a mechanical reflex of habit: to get any principle of freedom in it we need some kind of theory of action, theory in the sense of theoria, a withdrawn or detached vision of the means and end of action which does not paralyze action, but makes it purposeful by enlightening its aims.

现代世界自由理论的两大经典之作——弥尔顿的《论出版自由》和密尔的《论自由》 ——当然是在不同的语境下探讨自由。对弥尔顿而言，文化是一种潜在的预言，它与审查制度所代表的那种社会认可的错误形成鲜明对比；而对密尔而言，文化则是一种社会批判。但即便如此，两篇文章都坚持认为，自由只能始于一种直接而现实的保障。关于文化自主性。在密尔看来，思想和讨论的无限自由不仅是发展行动自由的最佳途径，也是控制行动自由的最佳途径，因为它是防止冲动或盲目行动的唯一手段。在弥尔顿看来，良心自由并非听从童年时期习得的、构成我们通常所说的良心大部分的那些冲动，而是听从上帝圣言的自由。上帝圣言是无限的心灵向有限的心灵传递的信息，因此后者永远无法完全理解它。

The two great classics of the theory of liberty in the modern world, Areopagitica and Mill’s Essay on Liberty, deal of course with liberty in different contexts. For Milton culture is potential prophecy, set in judgement over against the kind of social acceptance of sanctioned error represented by the censor, whereas for Mill culture is a social critique. But allowing for this, both essays insist that liberty can begin only with an immediate and present guarantee of the autonomy of culture. In Mill unlimited liberty of thought and discussion is not only the best way of developing liberty of action, but the best way of controlling it, because it is the only means of preventing impulsive or stampeded action. In Milton liberty of conscience is not the freedom to listen to the compulsions acquired in childhood which make up the greater part of what we ordinarily call conscience, but the freedom to listen to the Word of God, which, as it is a message from an infinite mind to a finite one, can never be definitively understood by the latter.

至此，批评理论似乎已准备好静静地融入更宏大的人文主义原则，即人的自由与他对自身文化遗产的接受密不可分。作者当然相信这一点，而且很可能大多数读者也会认同；但批评中寄生谬误的残余或许仍然存在，我们所有的论证或许尚未完全消除。这种残余感觉是，由于批评建立在文化产品之上，批评家越是声称自己的作品重要，就越倾向于将一个有教养的人在艺术中获得的正常愉悦放大成某种可怕而又不祥的东西，用审美迷信取代文化，用歌谣崇拜取代文学，无论这种崇拜多么高明。

At this point the theory of criticism seems ready to settle quietly into the larger humanistic principle that the freedom of man is inseparably bound up with his acceptance of his cultural heritage. The writer believes this, of course, and so probably do most of those who will read his book; but there may still be a residue from the parasite fallacy of criticism, which all our arguments may not yet have dispelled. This is the feeling that as criticism is based on cultural products, the more important the critic claims his work to be, the more he tends to magnify the normal pleasure that a cultivated person finds in the arts into something awful and portentous, replacing culture with aesthetic superstition, literature with bardolatry, of however sophisticated a kind.

如果艺术的审美或沉思层面确实是艺术或批评的最终归宿，那么上述观点或许成立。然而，原型批评再次为我们提供了帮助。我们在第二篇文章中试图论证，当我们从单个艺术作品转向对艺术整体形式的感知时，艺术便不再是审美沉思的对象，而成为参与文明进程的伦理工具。在这种向伦理层面的转变中，批评和诗歌都参与其中，尽管它们参与的某些方式通常不被认为是批评的范畴。例如，显而易见，社会秩序的一个重要来源是既定的语言模式。在宗教中，这可以是经文、礼拜仪式或信条；在政治中，这可以是成文宪法或一系列意识形态指导方针，例如列宁在当今俄罗斯的小册子。这种语言模式可能会保持几个世纪不变：在此期间，赋予它们的含义会发生翻天覆地的变化，但语言结构必须保持不变的感觉，以及由此产生的重新解释它以适应历史变化的必要性，使得批评活动成为社会的中心。

This would be true if in fact the aesthetic or contemplative aspect of art were the final resting place for either art or criticism. Here again it is archetypal criticism that comes to our aid. We tried to show in the second essay that the moment we go from the individual work of art to the sense of the total form of the art, the art becomes no longer an object of aesthetic contemplation but an ethical instrument, participating in the work of civilization. In this shift to the ethical, criticism as well as poetry is involved, though some of the ways in which it is involved are not commonly recognized as aspects of criticism. It is obvious, for instance, that one major source of order in society is an established pattern of words. In religion this may be a scripture, a liturgy, or a creed; in politics it may be a written constitution or a set of ideological directives like the pamphlets of Lenin in present-day Russia. Such verbal patterns may remain fixed for centuries: the meanings attached to them will change out of all recognition in that time, but the feeling that the verbal structure must remain unchanged, and the consequent necessity of reinterpreting it to suit the changes of history, bring the operations of criticism into the center of society.

但我们随后不得不通过剔除文学中所有外部目标来完成论证，从而假定存在一个自洽的文学宇宙。或许这样做，我们只是在规模上恢复了审美观，用“诗歌”取代了大量的诗歌，用审美神秘主义取代了审美经验主义。然而，我们上一篇文章的论证得出了一个原则：所有文字结构都部分具有修辞性，因此也具有文学性；而认为存在一种不包含修辞元素的科学或哲学语言结构的想法，则是一种错觉。如果真是如此，那么我们的文学宇宙就扩展成了一个语言宇宙，任何自洽的审美原则都将不再适用。

But we then had to complete our argument by removing all external goals from literature, thus postulating a self-contained literary universe. Perhaps in doing so we merely restored the aesthetic view on a gigantic scale, substituting Poetry for a mass of poems, aesthetic mysticism for aesthetic empiricism. The argument of our last essay, however, led to the principle that all structures in words are partly rhetorical, and hence literary, and that the notion of a scientific or philosophical verbal structure free of rhetorical elements is an illusion. If so, then our literary universe has expanded into a verbal universe, and no aesthetic principle of self-containment will work.

我并非完全不了解，论证的每一步都涉及极其复杂的哲学问题，而我自身能力有限，无法直接解答。然而，我也意识到其他一些因素。这些因素指的是当今围绕着诸如“交流”、“符号学”、“语义学”、“语言学”、“元语言学”、“语用学”、“控制论”等词汇，以及卡西尔、科日布斯基等数十位学者在史前史、数学、逻辑学、工程学、社会学和物理学等看似遥远的领域（直到最近看来）所提出的思想而展开的一系列纷繁复杂的新兴学术活动。许多此类运动的兴起，源于一种将现代人的思想从情感修辞的桎梏中解放出来的愿望，摆脱了那些试图通过滥用反讽将思想扭曲成条件反射的广告和宣传。其中许多运动也朝着概念修辞的方向发展，将许多论证的内容简化为模糊不清或图解式的结构。我对大多数涉及这一新材料的书籍的了解，就像摩西在山上对上帝的了解一样，主要局限于浏览它们的书脊，但我很清楚，文学批评在所有这些活动中都占据着核心地位，从文学批评的角度来看，我提出一个诚然非常推测性的建议。

I am not wholly unaware that at every step of this argument there are extremely complicated philosophical problems which I am incompetent to solve as such. I am aware also, however, of something else. That something else is the confused swirl of new intellectual activities today associated with such words as communication, symbolism, semantics, linguistics, metalinguistics, pragmatics, cybernetics, and the ideas generated by and around Cassirer, Korzybsky, and dozens of others in fields as remote (as they seemed until recently) as prehistory and mathematics, logic and engineering, sociology and physics. Many of these movements were instigated by a desire to free the modern mind from the tyranny of emotional rhetoric, from the advertising and propaganda that try to pervert thought by a misuse of irony into conditioned reflex. Many of them have also moved in the direction of conceptual rhetoric, reducing the content of many arguments to their ambiguous or diagrammatic structures. My knowledge of most of the books dealing with this new material is largely confined, like Moses’ knowledge of God in the mount, to gazing at their spines, but it is clear to me that literary criticism has a central place in all this activity, and from the point of view of literary criticism I offer an admittedly very speculative suggestion.

我们曾多次暗示文学与数学之间存在相似之处。数学似乎起源于对物体的计数和测量，是对外部世界的一种数值描述。但数学家并不这样看待他的学科：对他而言，数学是一种独立的语言，并且存在一个临界点，在这个临界点上，它成为一种独立于我们称之为客观世界、自然、存在或现实（取决于我们的情绪）的共同经验领域的度量。数学的许多术语，例如……作为无理数，它们与日常经验领域没有直接联系，其意义完全取决于数学主体自身的相互关系。数学中的无理数可以比作语言中的介词，我们已经注意到介词的向心性。当我们区分纯粹数学和应用数学时，我们指的是前者是一种对数值关系的客观理解，它越来越关注数值关系的内在完整性，而越来越少地关注其与外部标准的关联。

We have several times hinted at an analogy between literature and mathematics. Mathematics appears to begin in the counting and measuring of objects, as a numerical commentary on the outside world. But the mathematician does not think of his subject so: for him it is an autonomous language, and there is a point at which it becomes in a measure independent of that common field of experience which we call the objective world, or nature, or existence, or reality, according to our mood. Many of its terms, such as irrational numbers, have no direct connection with the common field of experience, but depend for their meaning solely on the interrelations of the subject itself. Irrational numbers in mathematics may be compared to prepositions in verbal languages, the centripetal character of which we have noted. When we distinguish pure from applied mathematics, we are thinking of the former as a disinterested conception of numerical relationships, concerned more and more with its inner integrity, and less and less with its reference to external criteria.

我们最初也常常把文学视为对外部“生活”或“现实”的评论。但正如在数学中，我们必须从三个苹果推导出三个，从正方形的田地推导出正方形一样，在阅读小说时，我们也必须从文学作为生活的反映推导出文学作为独立语言的本质。文学也通过假设的可能性来发展，而且尽管文学和数学一样，具有持续的实用性——“实用性”一词意味着与共同的经验领域保持着持续的联系——但纯粹的文学，就像纯粹的数学一样，蕴含着自身的意义。

We think also of literature at first as a commentary on an external “life” or “reality.” But just as in mathematics we have to go from three apples to three, and from a square field to a square, so in reading a novel we have to go from literature as reflection of life to literature as autonomous language. Literature also proceeds by hypothetical possibilities, and though literature, like mathematics, is constantly useful—a word which means having a continuing relationship to the common field of experience—pure literature, like pure mathematics, contains its own meaning.

文学和数学都源于公理而非事实；两者都可以应用于外部现实，同时又以“纯粹”或自洽的形式存在。此外，两者都在存在与非存在这一对立面之间制造了隔阂，而这对于论述性思维至关重要。符号既非它所展现的现实，也非它所不是的现实。一个初学几何的孩子面对一个点，首先被告知这是一个点，其次又被告知它不是一个点。他必须同时接受这两种说法才能继续学习。一个不是数字的东西也可以是一个数字，这很荒谬，但接受这种荒谬的结果就是零的发现。文学中也存在类似的假设，哈姆雷特和福斯塔夫既非存在也非不存在，而虚无缥缈的存在也被自信地定位和命名。我们注意到，修辞与逻辑的显著区别在于，它总是赋予否定性陈述某种肯定的性质。逻辑会计算陈述句中的否定词数量，如果数量为偶数则称之为肯定句，但在交流史上，没有人会把“我没钱”理解为说话者其实有钱。文学中也是如此：伊阿古告诫奥赛罗要提防嫉妒，其目的就是要在奥赛罗心中种下嫉妒的种子；《杰龙提翁》开头的否定词，从逻辑上讲意味着杰龙提翁并非英雄，但从修辞上讲，它们却构建了一幅与之形成鲜明对比的牺牲与奉献的画面。忍耐。如果诗人从不肯定，他也从不否定；在这方面，亚里士多德关于修辞学的开篇论述——即修辞学是辩证法的对立合唱或回应合唱——就站不住脚了。

Both literature and mathematics proceed from postulates, not facts; both can be applied to external reality and yet exist also in a “pure” or self-contained form. Both, furthermore, drive a wedge between the antithesis of being and non-being that is so important for discursive thought. The symbol neither is nor is not the reality which it manifests. The child beginning geometry is presented with a dot and is told, first, that that is a point, and second, that it is not a point. He cannot advance until he accepts both statements at once. It is absurd that that which is no number can also be a number, but the result of accepting the absurdity was the discovery of zero. The same kind of hypothesis exists in literature, where Hamlet and Falstaff neither exist nor do not exist, and where an airy nothing is confidently located and named. We notice that rhetoric differs sharply from logic in that it invariably gives some positive quality to a negative statement. Logic counts the negatives in a statement and calls it affirmative if there is an even number, but no one in the history of communication ever took “I hain’t got no money” to mean that the speaker did have money. Similarly in literature: Iago’s urging Othello to beware of jealousy is designed to plant jealousy in Othello’s mind; the negatives at the beginning of Gerontion mean logically that Gerontion is not a hero, but rhetorically they build up a contrasting picture of sacrifice and endurance. If the poet never affirmeth, he never denies either; and in this respect Aristotle’s opening statement about rhetoric, that it is the antistrophos or answering chorus of dialectic, breaks down.

在詹姆斯·金斯爵士的《神秘的宇宙》一书的最后一章中，作者谈到十九世纪物理宇宙学未能将宇宙最终视为机械的本质，并提出数学方法或许能带来更好的结果。宇宙不可能是一台机器，但它可能是一套相互关联的数学公式。这意味着，纯粹数学存在于一个数学宇宙之中，这个宇宙不再是对外部世界的评述，而是将外部世界本身包含在其中。数学最初是一种理解客观世界的方式，并将客观世界视为其内容；但最终，它将内容本身视为数学形式；当数学宇宙的概念形成时，形式与内容便合二为一。因此，数学与共同经验领域间接地联系在一起，并非为了回避它，而是为了最终将其吞噬。它似乎是自然科学中的一种指导或建构原则：它不断地赋予自然科学以形态和连贯性，而它本身并不依赖于外部的证明或证据；然而最终，物理或定量的宇宙似乎都被数学所涵盖。吉恩斯这一章中那种神秘莫测的语调，尽管表达了一个至少自毕达哥拉斯以来就一直困扰着数学家的梦想，却可以与我们一旦达到对文学或语言宇宙的相应概念时，就不得不使用的宗教术语相比较。

In the final chapter of Sir James Jeans’ The Mysterious Universe, the author speaks of the failure of physical cosmology in the nineteenth century to conceive of the universe as ultimately mechanical, and suggests that a mathematical approach to it may have better luck. The universe cannot be a machine, but it may be an interlocking set of mathematical formulas. What this means is surely that pure mathematics exists in a mathematical universe which is no longer a commentary on an outside world, but contains that world within itself. Mathematics is at first a form of understanding an objective world regarded as its content, but in the end it conceives of the content as being itself mathematical in form, and when a conception of a mathematical universe is reached, form and content become the same thing. Mathematics relates itself indirectly to the common field of experience, then, not to avoid it, but with the ultimate design of swallowing it. It appears to be a kind of informing or constructive principle in the natural sciences: it continually gives shape and coherence to them without being itself dependent on external proof or evidence, and yet finally the physical or quantitative universe appears to be contained by mathematics. The occult or mystical sound of Jeans’ chapter, which nevertheless expresses a dream that has haunted mathematicians at least since Pythagoras, may be compared with the religious terminology we found ourselves compelled to use as soon as we reached the corresponding conception of a literary or verbal universe.

这个类比中还有其他一些值得注意的地方：例如，文学和数学的基本单位——隐喻和方程式——在形式上有着奇特的相似性。在许多逻辑学家所使用的广义术语中，两者都属于同义反复。但如果这个类比成立，那么问题自然就出现了：文学是否像数学一样具有实质上的实用性，而不仅仅是偶然的实用性？也就是说，心理学、人类学、神学、历史学、法学以及其他所有由文字构建的学科的语言结构，是否也像文学中那些最初以假设形式出现的神话和隐喻一样，受到它们的启发或建构？

Other points in this analogy strike one: the curious similarity in form, for instance, between the units of literature and of mathematics, the metaphor and the equation. Both of these are, in the expanded sense of the term employed by many logicians, tautologies. But if the analogy is to hold, the question of course arises: is literature like mathematics in being substantially useful, and not just incidentally so? That is, is it true that the verbal structures of psychology, anthropology, theology, history, law, and everything else built out of words have been informed or constructed by the same kind of myths and metaphors that we find, in their original hypothetical form, in literature?

在我看来，目前的讨论暗示了一种可能性，即话语性语言结构有两个方面：一种是描述性的，另一种是建构性的；一种是内容，一种是形式。描述性的是符号性的：也就是说，它建立了一种外部现象的语言复制，其语言符号应被理解为一组代表性符号。但任何语言结构中的建构性内容，在我看来，总是某种隐喻或假设性的等同，无论它是通过同一词语的不同含义建立的，还是通过图表的使用而建立的。这些假定的隐喻反过来又成为论证的神话或建构原则的单元。当我们阅读时，我们意识到一系列隐喻性的等同；当我们读完时，我们意识到一个组织性的结构模式或概念化的神话。

The possibility that seems to me suggested by the present discussion is as follows. Discursive verbal structures have two aspects, one descriptive, the other constructive, a content and a form. What is descriptive is sigmatic: that is, it establishes a verbal replica of external phenomena, and its verbal symbolism is to be understood as a set of representative signs. But whatever is constructive in any verbal structure seems to me to be invariably some kind of metaphor or hypothetical identification, whether it is established among different meanings of the same word or by the use of a diagram. The assumed metaphors in their turn become the units of the myth or constructive principle of the argument. While we read, we are aware of a sequence of metaphorical identifications; when we have finished, we are aware of an organizing structural pattern or conceptualized myth.

现在看来，弗洛伊德对俄狄浦斯情结的看法似乎是一种心理学概念，它为文学批评提供了一些启示。或许我们最终会发现，我们之前的理解是错误的：俄狄浦斯神话在当时为某些心理学研究提供了理论基础和结构。如果真是如此，弗洛伊德的独特之处仅仅在于他博览群书，能够发现神话的来源。现在看来，对意识“之下”的预言性心灵的心理学发现，恰好为贯穿文学作品的诗歌原型提供了一种恰当的寓言式解释，这种原型从特洛福尼奥斯的洞穴一直延续到我们今天。或许正是这个原型启发了我们的发现：毕竟它的历史更为久远，用这种方式解释它，我们就不会陷入时代错置的困境。诗歌神话，或者类似于诗歌神话的联想和图式，对形而上学和神学建构的影响，则更为显而易见。

It looks now as though Freud’s view of the Oedipus complex were a psychological conception that throws some light on literary criticism. Perhaps we shall eventually decide that we have got it the wrong way round: that what happened was that the myth of Oedipus informed and gave structure to some psychological investigations at this point. Freud would in that case be exceptional only in having been well read enough to spot the source of the myth. It looks now as though the psychological discovery of an oracular mind “underneath” the conscious one forms an appropriate allegorical explanation of a poetic archetype that has run through literature from the cave of Trophonius to our own day. Perhaps it was the archetype that informed the discovery: it is after all considerably older, and to explain it in this way would involve us in less anachronism. The informing of metaphysical and theological constructs by poetic myths, or by associations and diagrams analogous to poetic myths, is even more obvious.

这种方法不必扭曲成诗意的决定论，因为正如前文所述，用简化论证来证明神学、形而上学、法学、社会科学，或者我们碰巧不喜欢的其中任何一个或每一类学科，都“仅仅”建立在隐喻或神话之上，是愚蠢的。如果我们是对的，任何这样的证明本身也具有同样的根基。因此，对真理或充分性的批判，主要针对的是内容，而非形式。卢梭认为，自然与理性的原始社会已被文明的腐败所覆盖，而足够勇敢的革命行动可以重建它。指出这一论点受到睡美人神话的影响，既不赞成也不反对它。但我们既不能赞同也不反对卢梭的观点。直到我们完全理解他所说的话，当然，即使不剥离神话，我们也能很好地理解他，但如果神话确实如我们在此所暗示的那样，是他论证连贯性的来源，那么剥离神话将大有裨益。这种关于神话与论证关系的观点，使我们非常接近柏拉图，在他看来，最终的理解行为要么是数学的，要么是神话的。

Such an approach need not be distorted into a poetic determinism, for, as has been said, it would be silly to use a reductive rhetoric to try to prove that theology, metaphysics, law, the social sciences, or whichever one or group of these we happen to dislike, are based on “nothing but” metaphors or myths. Any such proof, if we are right, would have the same kind of basis itself. Criticisms of truth or adequacy, then, are mainly criticism of content, not form. Rousseau says that the original society of nature and reason has been overlaid by the corruptions of civilization, and that a sufficiently courageous revolutionary act could reestablish it. It is nothing either for or against this argument to say that it is informed by the myth of the sleeping beauty. But we cannot agree or disagree with Rousseau until we fully understand what he does say, and while of course we can understand him well enough without extracting the myth, there is much to be gained by extracting the myth if the myth is in fact, as we are suggesting here, the source of the coherence of his argument. Such a view of the relation of myth to argument would take us very close to Plato, for whom the ultimate acts of apprehension were either mathematical or mythical.

文学如同数学，是一种语言，而语言本身并不代表真理，尽管它可以提供表达各种真理的手段。但诗人与评论家始终相信某种想象的真理，或许这种信念的依据在于语言能够容纳它所能表达的内容。数学世界和语言世界无疑是构想同一宇宙的不同方式。客观世界提供了一种暂时的统一经验的手段，人们自然会由此推断出一种更高的统一性，一种对常识的某种神圣化。然而，要找到一种能够表达这种更高层次的理性宇宙统一性的语言并非易事。形而上学、神学、历史、法律都曾被尝试过，但它们都只是语言建构，我们越深入研究，它们隐喻和神话的轮廓就越发清晰地显露出来。每当我们构建一个将天地合一的思想体系时，巴别塔的故事就会重演：我们发现，最终我们还是无法完全实现这个目标，而我们目前所拥有的只是多种语言。

Literature, like mathematics, is a language, and a language in itself represents no truth, though it may provide the means for expressing any number of them. But poets and critics alike have always believed in some kind of imaginative truth, and perhaps the justification for the belief is in the containment by the language of what it can express. The mathematical and the verbal universes are doubtless different ways of conceiving the same universe. The objective world affords a provisional means of unifying experience, and it is natural to infer a higher unity, a sort of beatification of common sense. But it is not easy to find any language capable of expressing the unity of this higher intellectual universe. Metaphysics, theology, history, law, have all been used, but all are verbal constructs, and the further we take them, the more clearly their metaphorical and mythical outlines show through. Whenever we construct a system of thought to unite earth with heaven, the story of the Tower of Babel recurs: we discover that after all we can’t quite make it, and that what we have in the meantime is a plurality of languages.

如果我对《芬尼根守灵夜》最后一章的理解没错，那么故事讲述的是，做梦者在与大量的隐喻性联想交流了一夜之后，醒来后便像尼布甲尼撒一样，忘记了梦境，忙于日常事务，未能运用，甚至没有意识到自己能够运用“梦境之钥”。因此，他未能做到的事情，就留给了读者，也就是乔伊斯所说的“患有理想失眠症的理想读者”，换句话说，就是批评家。我设想，批评的某种意义就在于此，即重建创造与知识、艺术与科学、神话与概念之间断裂的联系。再次强调，我并非在谈论批评方向或活动的改变：我的意思是，如果批评家们继续从事他们的工作，那么这将会越来越明显地成为他们劳动的社会和实践成果。

If I have read the last chapter of Finnegans Wake correctly, what happens there is that the dreamer, after spending the night in communion with a vast body of metaphorical identifications, wakens and goes about his business forgetting his dream, like Nebuchadnezzar, failing to use, or even to realize that he can use, the “keys to dreamland.” What he fails to do is therefore left for the reader to do, the “ideal reader suffering from an ideal insomnia,” as Joyce calls him, in other words the critic. Some such activity as this of reforging the broken links between creation and knowledge, art and science, myth and concept, is what I envisage for criticism. Once more, I am not speaking of a change of direction or activity in criticism: I mean only that if critics go on with their own business, this will appear to be, with increasing obviousness, the social and practical result of their labors.

第15页，第7行

p.   15, line  7

“无论它现在是什么。”这句话表达的并非对美学的蔑视，而是认为美学应该像心理学那样，从哲学中独立出来。大多数哲学家仅仅将美学问题视为与其逻辑和形而上学观点相类比，因此，如果不陷入康德或黑格尔式的“立场”，就很难在艺术领域运用康德或黑格尔的理论。据我所知，亚里士多德是唯一一位不仅在意识到更宏大的美学问题时专门探讨诗学，而且还假定诗学将成为一门独立学科的工具的哲学家。因此，批评家可以运用《诗学》而不陷入亚里士多德主义（尽管我知道一些亚里士多德主义批评家并不这么认为）。

“whatever it is now.” This phrase expresses, not a contempt for aesthetics, but a conviction that it is time for aesthetics to get out from under philosophy, as psychology has already done. Most philosophers deal with aesthetic questions only as a set of analogies to their logical and metaphysical views, hence it is difficult to use, say, Kant or Hegel on the arts without getting into a Kantian or Hegelian “position.” Aristotle is the only philosopher known to me who not only talks specifically about poetics when he is aware of larger aesthetic problems, but who assumes that such poetics would be the organon of an independent discipline. Consequently a critic can use the Poetics without involving himself in Aristotelianism (though I know that some Aristotelian critics do not think so).

“lack of a technical vocabulary.” The revival of the technical language of rhetoric would not only provide us with useful terms, but in many cases would revive the conceptions themselves which have been forgotten along with their names. It may be true that, as Samuel Butler said:

除了列举他的工具之外，什么也教不了。

 … all a rhetorician’s rules

Teach nothing but to name his tools

 

 

但如果一位评论家连他使用的工具都说不清楚，世人就很难认可他的技艺。我们不应该把车交给一个只知道摆设和各种小玩意儿的修车工。

but if a critic cannot name his tools, the world is unlikely to concede much authority to his craft. We should not entrust our cars to a mechanic who lived entirely in a world of gadgets and doohickeys.

One wonders if there is anything more than doubtful puns connecting the anagogic perspective in literature with Kant’s conception of “transcendental aesthetic” as the a priori consciousness of space and time.

“柯勒律治。” 《柯勒律治杂评》，TM Raysor 编辑（1936 年），第 343 页。

“可信的事实。”我略过了弟弟被哥哥的牛警告有危险这一点。

“credible facts.” I pass over the point that the younger brother is warned of his danger by the elder brother’s cow.

“英雄降临”。虽然哈姆雷特下葬的说法可以省略，但他在这一幕前后情绪的对比表明他经历了一种过渡仪式。

“hero descending.” The statement that Hamlet descends into the grave is expendable, but the contrast in his mood before and after the scene indicates some kind of rite de passage.

第141页，第21行

p. 141, line 21

“末世意象的语法”。关于圣经类型学，奥斯汀·法勒的《意象的重生》（1949）是一本很有用的书。另见艾伦·W·沃茨的《基督教中的神话与仪式》（1954）。

“grammar of apocalyptic imagery.” For Biblical typology a useful book is Austin Farrer, A Rebirth of Images (1949). See also Alan W. Watts, Myth and Ritual in Christianity (1954).
