p. 142, line  5

“ ‘figura’。 ”参见埃里希·奥尔巴赫，《模仿》，威拉德·特拉斯克译（1953 年），第 73 页。

“‘figura.’” See Erich Auerbach, Mimesis, tr. Willard Trask (1953), 73.

第144页，第1行

p. 144, line  1

“论鸟类。”华莱士·史蒂文斯的多首诗作，包括《腹中的鸽子》，都运用了这种象征手法。其他受青睐的动物还包括鱼类和海豚，它们在传统基督教中象征着利维坦；昆虫中则有蜜蜂，维吉尔对蜜蜂情有独钟，蜜蜂的甜美和轻盈与吞噬一切的蜘蛛形成鲜明对比。参见伊迪丝·西特韦尔夫人的诗作《蜜蜂神谕》。古代关于各界“灵长类动物”的理论与这种典型代表的象征性运用密切相关。

“Of birds.” Several poems by Wallace Stevens, including “The Dove in the Belly,” employ this symbolism. Other favored members of the animal kingdom include the fish and the dolphin, traditionally Christian in contrast to the leviathan, and among insects the bee, so beloved of Virgil, whose sweetness and light are a contrast to the devouring spider. Cf. Dame Edith Sitwell’s poem, “The Bee Oracles.” The old theory of “primates” in the various kingdoms is connected with this symbolic use of typical representatives.

第145页，第37行

p. 145, line 37

“燃烧的人。”参见D.H.劳伦斯在《伊特鲁里亚地方》中关于朱砂颜料的评论，第1章。

“burning man.” Cf. D. H. Lawrence’s remarks on vermilion paint in Etruscan Places, Ch. in.

第146页，第4行

p. 146, line  4

“在炼金术中。”关于炼金术的象征意义，参见赫伯特·西尔伯勒的《神秘主义及其象征意义问题》（史密斯·伊利·杰利夫译，1917年）和荣格的《心理学与炼金术》（R.F.C.赫尔译，1953年）。寓言炼金术、玫瑰十字会、卡巴拉、共济会和塔罗牌都是基于与此处所述范式相似的类型学建构。对于文学批评家而言，它们仅仅是参考表格：一种关于神谕的傲慢态度。它们在某些形式的原型批评中反复出现，但并没有什么实际意义。

“In alchemy.” For alchemical symbolism see Herbert Silberer, Problems of Mysticism and its Symbolism, tr. Smith Ely Jelliffe (1917), and C. G. Jung, Psychology and Alchemy, tr. R. F. C. Hull (1953). Allegorical alchemy, Rosicrucianism, Cabbalism, Freemasonry, and the Tarot pack are all typological constructs based on paradigms similar to those given here. For the literary critic they are simply reference tables: the atmosphere of oracular harrumph about them, which recurs in some forms of archetypal criticism, is not much to the point.

第159-160页

pp. 159-160

“动物的生命永存。”因此，动物象征与生命周期阶段的关系，取决于动物的选择，而非其年龄。我们会在浪漫故事中看到鹿，在《荒原》中看到老鼠。

“Animal lives.” Hence the relation of animal symbolism to the phase of the cycle is characterized by the choice of animal rather than by its age. We expect to find deer in romances and rats in The Waste Land.

第165页，第28行

p. 165, line 28

“仔细标记。” Volpone，V，ii，12-14。

“carefully marked.” Volpone, V, ii, 12-14.

第166页，第14行

p. 166, line 14

“ Tractatus Coislinianus。”参见 Lane Cooper，《亚里士多德喜剧理论》（1922 年）。

“Tractatus Coislinianus.” See Lane Cooper, An Aristotelian Theory of Comedy (1922).

第168页，第39行

p. 168, line 39

“ E·M·福斯特先生。” 《小说面面观》（1927），第一章。或许最好将虚构的重复（例如米考伯太太的套路）与主题的重复（例如马修·阿诺德故意反复重复对手使用的愚蠢短语）进行对比。关于此类主题重复在福斯特作品中的作用，参见E·K·布朗的《小说中的节奏》（1950）。

“Mr. E. M. Forster.” Aspects of the Novel (1927), Ch. 1. It would perhaps be better to draw the contrast between a fictional repetition like Mrs. Micawber’s formula, and a thematic repetition, like Matthew Arnold’s deliberate echoing ad nauseam of fatuous phrases used by his opponents. For the role of such thematic repetitions in Forster’s own work, see E. K. Brown, Rhythm in the Novel (1950).

第171页，第28行

p. 171, line 28

“占据中间行动。”因此，喜剧中阻碍角色的原型是“中间人”或副统治者：参见西奥多·H·加斯特，《忒斯庇斯》（1950），34。《一报还一报》中的安杰洛是最明显的例子。

“occupies the middle action.” Hence the archetype of the blocking character in comedy is the “interrex” or deputy ruler: see Theodor H. Gaster, Thespis (1950), 34. Angelo in Measure for Measure is the clearest example.

第173页，第28行

p. 173, line 28

“现代小说中的业余侦探”。这是他天真的化身；在更成熟的喜剧中，一种流行的滑稽人物是花花公子，他是一个超脱尘世的人物，他的警句大多是陈词滥调的反转，他对感伤主义的态度是滑稽的蔑视（如第48页所述），他通常是保守派，反对那些自认为进步的幽默群体，因为他们都朝着同一个方向前进。王尔德的《理想丈夫》很好地展现了这一形象。在20世纪20年代，花花公子这一形象在小说和主题上都得到了复兴，出现在菲尔班克、赫胥黎、沃、 《纽约客》中的尼克博克人物以及其他作品中。

“amateur detective of modern fiction.” This is his naive incarnation; in more sophisticated comedy a popular form of gracioso is the dandy, a disengaged figure whose epigrams are largely inverted clichés, whose attitude is that of comic scorn for sentimentality as described on p. 48, and who is normally a conservative, opposed to a group of humors who feel that they are progressive because they all face in the same direction. He is well exhibited in Wilde’s An Ideal Husband. In the twenties the dandy revived, both fictionally and thematically, in Firbank, Huxley, Waugh, the Knickerbocker figure of The New Yorker, and elsewhere.

第178页，第34行

p. 178, line 34

“然后剧情反转。”讽刺或“现实主义”的驱动力在于得出一个仍停留在经验状态之内的结论；喜剧的驱动力则在于将这种状态提升到一个新的层次。作者选择哪种结论往往只用一两句话就能决定，就像一首小调乐曲，结尾可能落在平行大调和弦上，也可能不落在。除了《乞丐歌剧》之外，狄更斯的《远大前程》和夏洛蒂·勃朗特的《维莱特》也提供了不同的结局，一个是传统的喜剧结局，另一个则更加模棱两可。

“and then reverses the action.” The impetus of irony or “realism” is toward a conclusion which remains within the state of experience; the impetus of comedy is toward a lift out of that state. Which conclusion the author chooses is often a matter of a sentence or two, like a piece of music in a minor key which may or may not end on the parallel major chord. Besides The Beggar’s Opera, Dickens’s Great Expectations and Charlotte Bronte’s Villette go to the length of providing alternative endings, one conventionally comic, the other more equivocal.

第183页，第30行

p. 183, line 30

“ ‘陷入困境’。 ”我忘了是在哪里看到的，但或许读者会原谅我引用这句话。

“‘behind the eight-ball.’ ” I forget where I read this, but perhaps the reader will excuse the reference.

第186页，第32行

p. 186, line 32

“无尽的形式”。这种无尽的形式在文学中有很多表现形式：例如，基于同一模式的一系列故事，如乔叟的《僧侣的故事》及其在利德盖特和《官镜》中略显逊色的后继作品；又如，在特定情境下任意决定要讲述的故事数量，如舍赫拉扎德为了保命而讲述的一千零一个故事；再如，紫式部《源氏物语》中那略显沉寂的结尾，尽管……即使结论合乎逻辑，也几乎不会阻止作者重新开始。关于它在戏剧中的运用，请参见第289页的注释。这种使结尾与开头相呼应的发现原则，赋予了对称情节以典型的抛物线形状。

“endless form.” This endless form has many literary manifestations: in the sequence of stories based on the same formula, like The Monk’s Tale in Chaucer and its slower-witted descendants in Lydgate and The Mirror for Magistrates; in the arbitrarily determined number of stories to be told in a given situation, like the thousand and one that Scheherezade tells for dear life; in the curiously muted conclusion of Lady Murasaki’s Tale of Genji, which, though a logical enough conclusion, would hardly have precluded the author from starting again. For its appearance in drama, see the note to p. 289. The principle of discovery, which brings the end into line with the beginning, gives to the symmetrical plot its characteristic parabola shape.

第187页，第10行

p. 187, line 10

“使用希腊语术语。”也就是说，使用吉尔伯特·默里爵士在简·哈里森所著《忒弥斯》第二版（1927 年）第 341 页及后续章节的注释中使用的术语。

“using Greek terms.” That is, using the terms employed by Sir Gilbert Murray in his Excursus in Jane Harrison, Themis, 2nd ed. (1927), 341 ff.

第188页，第18行

p. 188, line 18

“ ‘潜意识’因素”。然而，也应该指出的是，原型批评除了抽象化、类型化和简化为惯例之外别无他用，因此在直接的文学体验中，它只扮演着“潜意识”的角色，因为在文学体验中，独特性至关重要。在直接体验中，我们隐约意识到一些熟悉的惯例，但通常只有在感到厌倦或失望，觉得作品毫无新意时，我们才会意识到它们的存在。因此，人们常常将直接体验与批评混淆，这很可能导致人们认为原型批评根本就是糟糕的批评，正如温德姆·刘易斯先生的一些言论所言。

“‘subconscious’ factor.” It should also be said, however, that archetypal criticism, which can do nothing but abstract and typify and reduce to convention, has only a “subconscious” role in the direct experience of literature, where uniqueness is everything. In direct experience we are dimly aware of familiar conventions, but as a rule we are consciously aware of them only when we are bored or disap pointed, and feel that there is nothing new here. Hence the usual confusion between direct experience and criticism may well lead to the feeling that archetypal criticism is simply bad criticism, as in some pronouncements of Mr. Wyndham Lewis.

p. 191, line 17

“Paradise Regained.” See “The Typology of Paradise Regained,” Modern Philology (1956), 227 ff.

p. 192, line 26

“核心统一神话”。参见约瑟夫·坎贝尔，《千面英雄》（1949）；拉格伦勋爵，《英雄》（1936）；荣格，《力比多的转变与象征》（即将由博林根出版社重新翻译为《转变的象征》），以及简·哈里森在《忒弥斯》中对“eniautos-daimon”的描述。或许我还可以补充我在《恐惧的对称》（1947）第七章中对布莱克矿石象征意义的阐述。

“studied in some detail.” See Otto Rank, The Myth of the Birth of the Hero (1910); also C. G. Jung and C. Kerenyi, Essays toward a Science of Mythology, tr. R. F. C. Hull (1949).

第201页，第13行

p. 201, line 13

“第一本书的自然续篇。”其原型是为神或英雄凯旋后建造居所：参见西奥多·H·加斯特，《忒斯庇斯》，163页。“美貌与金钱”一词出自《仙后》，第二卷，第十一章。关于节制与自律以及自然界两个层次之间的区别，参见A·S·P·伍德豪斯，《仙后中的自然与恩典》，ELH（1949），194页及以下；以及《弥尔顿<科莫斯>的论证》，多伦多大学季刊（1941），46页及以下。

The phrase “Beauty and money” is from Faerie Queene, II, xi. For the distinctions between temperance and continence and the two levels of nature, see A. S. P. Woodhouse, “Nature and Grace in The Faerie Queene,” ELH (1949), 194 ff. and “The Argument of Milton’s Comus,” University of Toronto Quarterly (1941), 46 ff.

“与圣经中堕落故事类似的事件。”参见阿波罗多洛斯，《书库》，弗雷泽编辑（勒布古典丛书，1921 年）；James Frazer 爵士，《旧约中的民间传说》，第一卷（1918 年）；Leo Frobenius，《人类的童年》，AH Keane 译（1909 年）。

第204页，第2行

p. 204, line  2

“爱伦·坡故事中的‘金甲虫’。”这个例子或许会让那些故作姿态的批评家们不悦，但之所以提及，是因为它阐明了一个原则：在通俗故事中，逻辑结构的关键在于原型之间的关联。从无关紧要的合理性角度来看，用金甲虫来发现宝藏是多余的，对话中给出的理由也十分牵强。

“ ‘gold bug’ in Poe’s story.” This example will not please the oh-come-now school of criticism, but is added because it illustrates the principle that logical construction, in a popular tale, is a matter of the linking of archetypes. The use of the gold bug to discover the treasure is, from the irrelevant point of view of plausibility, unnecessary, and only the lamest excuse is given for it in the dialogue.

第208页，第23行

p. 208, line 23

“爱奥尼亚科学和文艺复兴科学的兴起。”参见 A.N.怀特海，《科学与现代世界》（1925 年），第一章。

“rise of Ionian and of Renaissance science.” Cf. A. N. Whitehead, Science and the Modern World (1925), Ch. I.

第214页，第20行

p. 214, line 20

“对悲剧幻象的处理”。另见《查拉图斯特拉如是说》第三卷第五十八章。查拉图斯特拉正处于顿悟的时刻，循环往复的世界在他脚下；由于他的幻象主要源于悲剧英雄的视角，他自然而然地向下进入循环之中。如同弥尔顿笔下父亲的演讲（两者之间存在着富有启发性的相似之处），这一论证本身或许缺乏说服力，但其存在的理由却十分清晰。艾略特的《圣灰星期三》和叶芝的《自我与灵魂的对话》从截然相反的角度探讨了同一原型，它们的结构则清晰得多。

“treatment of the tragic vision.” See Also Sprach Zarathustra, III, lvii. Zarathustra is at the point of epiphany, with the cyclical world below him; as his vision is primarily that of the tragic hero, his natural movement is downward into the cycle. Like the Father’s speech in Milton, to which it affords an instructive parallel, the argument itself may be unconvincing, but the reason for its being there is plain enough. Eliot’s Ash Wednesday and Yeats’s Dialogue of Self and Soul, which deal with the same archetype from directly opposed points of view, are much clearer in structure.

“does not need a great person.” Chaucer’s pardoner is a perhaps better example.

p. 261, line 26

“ ‘十个低级词语。’ ” 《论批评》，347；当然，这句诗的问题不在于单音节词太多，而在于重音符号太多。

“ ‘ten low words.’ ” Essay on Criticism, 347; what is wrong with the line, of course, is not too many monosyllables, but too many stressed accents.

第264页，第32行

p. 264, line 32

“ ‘塞内卡漫步’。 ”参见乔治·威廉姆森 (George Williamson) 1951 年出版的同名书籍。

“ ‘Senecan amble.’ ” See the book of that title by George Williamson (1951).

第265页，第37行

p. 265, line 37

“ Wulfstan 。” 《Sermo Lupi ad Anglos》的另一文本在所给出的引文中又增加了两对头韵，表明这种修辞具有某种随意性。

“Wulfstan.” Another text of the Sermo Lupi ad Anglos adds two more alliterative pairs to the quotation given, indicating a certain ad libitum quality in such rhetoric.

第268页，第13行

p. 268, line 13

“卡西奥多鲁斯。”引自 WP Ker，《黑暗时代》（1911 年），第 119 页。

“Cassiodorus.” Quoted from W. P. Ker, The Dark Ages (1911), 119.

第269页，第33行

p. 269, line 33

“文学风格主义。”参见 T.S. 艾略特，《诗歌与戏剧》（1951 年）。

“literary mannerism.” Cf. T. S. Eliot, Poetry and Drama (1951).

第272页，第19行

p. 272, line 19

“ ‘真情流露’。 ”请参阅赫伯特·里德爵士 (Sir Herbert Read) 1953 年出版的同名著作。

“ ‘true voice of feeling.’ ” See the book of that title by Sir Herbert Read (1953).

第275页，第20行

p. 275, line 20

“目前还没有什么可说的。” 但请参阅弗雷德里克·W·斯特恩菲尔德 (Frederick W. Sternfeld) 的《歌德与音乐》 (1954)中关于“戏仿”的概念。

“little has yet been said.” See however the conception of “parody” in Frederick W. Sternfeld, Goethe and Music (1954).

第278页，第23行

p. 278, line 23

“山茶花萨宾娜。”参见玛丽安·摩尔的《诗选》（1935 年）；该诗的结构在后来的版本中有所改变。

“Camellia Sabina.” See Marianne Moore, Selected Poems (1935); the scheme of the poem is altered in later editions.

第281页，第25行

p. 281, line 25

“三十八个短语。”所分析的书籍是奥斯卡·威廉姆斯的《向你走来的人》（1940 年）；该统计得出的唯一结论是，现代语言的措辞与其他任何语言一样，都是约定俗成的。

“thirty-eight phrases.” The book examined was Oscar Williams, The Man Coming Toward You (1940); the only point made by the count is that modern diction is as conventionalized as any other diction.

第284页，第1行

p. 284, line  1

“世俗圣餐的象征。”我们不妨顺便看一下《理查三世》（第五幕第四场，31-32行）的结尾：

“secular Eucharist symbol.” We may glance in passing at the conclusion of Richard III (V, iv, 31-32):

 

 

然后，既然我们已经领受了圣餐，

我们将把白玫瑰和红玫瑰结合在一起。

And then, as we have ta’en the sacrament,

We will unite the white rose and the red.

第286页，第34行

p. 286, line 34

“《结婚指南》的前言”。更准确地说，是在与前言分开的一篇序言中。

“preface to Getting Married.” More exactly, in a prefatory note separated from the preface.

第289页，第14行

p. 289, line 14

“倾向于线性运动”。关于这种亚里士多德非常厌恶的行进式结构，请参阅第186页的注释。莎士比亚在《伯里克利》中可能使用了合作者的假设并不影响我对这部作品的论述。

“tendency to linear movement.” For this processional structure, so much disliked by Aristotle, cf. the note to p. 186. The hypothesis that Shakespeare may have used a collaborator in Pericles does not affect my statements about it.

第290页，第7行

p. 290, line  7

“据说是后裔。”参见伊妮德·韦尔斯福德，《宫廷假面舞会》（1927）。

“said to be descended.” See Enid Welsford, The Court Masque (1927).

第293页，第21行

p. 293, line 21

“以及此类史诗形式。”抒情诗和史诗之间过渡体裁阶段的问题极其复杂，因此不得不从本次讨论中省略。

“along with such epos forms.” An extremely complicated problem, the problem of the intervening generic stages between lyric and epos, has had to be omitted from this discussion.

第317页，第10行

p. 317, line 10

“两种史诗框架”。在G.R. Levy的《岩石中的剑》（1954）中，史诗结构被分为三种类型：神话史诗、探险史诗和冲突史诗。就史诗素材而言，这些大致对应于我们所知的神话、浪漫和高度模仿的百科全书式叙事形式。

“two epic frameworks.” In G. R. Levy, The Sword from the Rock (1954), three types of epic structure are recognized: mythical epics, quest-epics, and conflict-epics. As far as the epic material used is concerned, these correspond roughly to our mythical, romantic and high mimetic encyclopaedic forms.

第320页，第36行

p. 320, line 36

“在法国。”参见 HJ Hunt，《十九世纪法国的史诗》（1941 年）。

“in France.” See H. J. Hunt, The Epic in Nineteenth-Century France (1941).

第326页，第8行

p. 326, line  8

“朗吉尼的观点。”这种将亚里士多德的审美净化和朗吉尼的心理狂喜视为彼此互补的观念（参见第 66 页）在《走向感性时代的定义》一文中得到了更连贯的解释，该文与十八世纪英国文学有关。

“a Longinian point of view.” This conception of Aristotelian aesthetic catharsis and Longinian psychological ecstasis as complementary to one another (cf. p. 66) is explained perhaps more coherently in “Towards Defining an Age of Sensibility,” ELH (1956), l44ff., in connection with eighteenth-century English literature.

第328页，第10行

p. 328, line 10

“斯温伯恩。”如果这很重要的话，这段文字出自他为哈夫洛克·艾利斯编辑的《米德尔顿》美人鱼系列版所作的序言（1887 年）。

“Swinburne.” The passage, if it matters, comes from his introduction to the Mermaid Series edition of Middleton, ed. Havelock Ellis (1887).

第334页，第10行

p. 334, line 10

“联系的可能性。”有关对这里提出的一些观点的批评，请参阅唐纳德·戴维的《清晰的能量》（1955 年），第 130 页及后续页。

“possibility of links.” For a criticism of some of the views here advanced, see Donald Davie, Articulate Energy (1955), 130 ff.

第341页，第24行

p. 341, line 24

“神话的寓言解释。”参见 Jean Seznec，《异教诸神的存续》，Barbara Sessions 译（1953 年），第二卷。

“allegorical explanations of myths.” See Jean Seznec, The Survival of the Pagan Gods, tr. Barbara Sessions (1953), Bk. II.

第349页，第40行

p. 349, line 40

“社会中心”。参见埃兹拉·庞德的“稳固枢纽”概念。

“center of society.” Cf. Ezra Pound’s conception of the “unwobbling pivot.”

第353页，第5行

p. 353, line  5

“某种隐喻。”批评家当然需要区分显性隐喻和隐喻性的语言结构。“X 对 Y 耿耿于怀”是一个显性隐喻；“X 脑子里一直想着 Y”则是同一个隐喻的语言结构，但在通常情况下，它只是一个简单的描述性陈述。

“some kind of metaphor.” The critic would of course need to distinguish an explicit metaphor from a metaphorical verbal construct. “X has a bee in his bonnet about Y” is an explicit metaphor; “X has got the notion Y into his head” is the verbal frame of the same metaphor, but for ordinary purposes it would pass as a simply descriptive statement.

第354页，第7行

p. 354, line  7

“要么是数学的，要么是神话的。”如果不承认数学中的创造性元素，美学理论很难取得更大的进展。如果将艺术视为一个圆环，从音乐延伸到文学、绘画和雕塑，最终到达建筑，而数学——这缺失的艺术——则填补了建筑和音乐之间的空白，那么我们或许能够更清晰地理解艺术。之所以认为数学属于科学而非艺术，很大程度上是因为数学本身就是一种我们懂得如何运用的艺术。当批评理论发展到其恰当的语言运用理论形式时，数学与文学在这方面的差异将会大大缩小。

“either mathematical or mythical.” It is difficult to see how aesthetic theory can get much further without recognizing the creative element in mathematics. The arts might be more clearly understood if they were thought of as forming a circle, stretching from music through literature, painting and sculpture to architecture, with mathematics, the missing art, occupying the vacant place between architecture and music. The feeling that mathematics belongs to science rather than art is largely due to the fact that mathematics is an art that we know how to use. The difference between mathematics and literature on this point will be greatly reduced when criticism achieves its proper form of the theory of the use of words.

词汇表

GLOSSARY

（本词汇表省略了本书中也经常使用的亚里士多德术语、修辞学术语和批评学术语。）

(This glossary omits the regular Aristotelian, rhetorical, and critical terms which are also employed in this book.)

拉宗（LAZON）：虚构作品中指自欺欺人或自欺欺人的角色，通常在喜剧或讽刺作品中是嘲笑的对象，但在悲剧中往往是英雄。在喜剧中，他最常以自负之人或学究的形象出现。

ALAZON: A deceiving or self-deceived character in fiction, normally an object of ridicule in comedy or satire, but often the hero of a tragedy. In comedy he most frequently takes the form of a miles gloriosus or a pedant.

NAGOGIC ：将文学视为词语的整体秩序。

ANAGOGIC: Relating to literature as a total order of words.

《解剖学》：一种散文小说形式，传统上被称为梅尼普式或瓦龙式讽刺小说，以伯顿的《忧郁的解剖》为代表，其特点是题材广泛，且对思想抱有浓厚的兴趣。篇幅较短的《解剖学》通常以晚宴或会谈为背景，并穿插诗歌体裁。

ANATOMY: A form of prose fiction, traditionally known as the Menippean or Varronian satire and represented by Burton’s Anatomy of Melancholy, characterized by a great variety of subject-matter and a strong interest in ideas. In shorter forms it often has a cena or symposium setting and verse interludes.

末世论：与虚构文学中的“神话”相对应的主题术语：隐喻，即纯粹的、潜在的完全认同，而不考虑合理性或普通经验。

APOCALYPTIC: The thematic term corresponding to “myth” in fictional literature: metaphor as pure and potentially total identification, without regard to plausibility or ordinary experience.

原型：一种符号，通常是一个意象，在文学作品中反复出现，以至于可以被识别为一个人整体文学体验中的一个元素。

ARCHETYPE: A symbol, usually an image, which recurs often enough in literature to be recognizable as an element of one’s literary experience as a whole.

UTO ：一种戏剧形式，其主要题材是神圣或神圣的传说，例如奇迹剧，形式庄严肃穆，但并非严格意义上的悲剧。名称取自卡尔德隆的《圣事剧》（Autos Sacramentales）。

AUTO: A form of drama in which the main subject is sacred or sacrosanct legend, such as miracle plays, solemn and processional in form but not strictly tragic. Name taken from Calderon’s Autos Sacramentales.

忏悔：自传被视为一种散文小说形式，或者以自传形式写成的散文小说。

CONFESSION: Autobiography regarded as a form of prose fiction, or prose fiction cast in the form of autobiography.

意义：文学作品的意义，可以是其符号的整体模式（字面意义），它与外部命题或事实的关联（描述意义），它的主题，或作为一种意象形式与潜在评论的关系（形式意义），它作为文学惯例或体裁的意义（原型意义），或它与整体文学体验的关系（寓意意义）。

DIANOIA: The meaning of a work of literature, which may be the total pattern of its symbols (literal meaning), its correlation with an external body of propositions or facts (descriptive meaning), its theme, or relation as a form of imagery to a potential commentary (formal meaning), its significance as a literary convention or genre (archetypal meaning), or its relation to total literary experience (anagogic meaning).

置换：将神话和隐喻适应道德或合理性的准则。

DISPLACEMENT: The adaptation of myth and metaphor to canons of morality or plausibility.

E IRON：小说中一个自嘲或不引人注目的角色，通常是喜剧中幸福结局的推动者，以及悲剧中灾难的推动者。

EIRON: A self-deprecating or unobtrusively treated character in fiction, usually an agent of the happy ending in comedy and of the catastrophe in tragedy.

百科全书式：一种以寓意象征形式呈现的作品体裁，例如圣经，或其他形式的类似作品。该术语涵盖《圣经》、但丁的《神曲》、伟大的史诗以及乔伊斯和普鲁斯特的作品。

ENCYCLOPAEDIC FORM: A genre presenting an anagogic form of symbolism, such as a sacred scripture, or its analogues in other modes. The term includes the Bible, Dante’s Commedia, the great epics, and the works of Joyce and Proust.

E POS：一种文学体裁，其表现形式是作者或吟游诗人作为口头朗诵者，面前有听众。

EPOS: The literary genre in which the radical of presentation is the author or minstrel as oral reciter, with a listening audience in front of him.

伦理：文学作品的内部社会背景，包括虚构文学的人物塑造和背景设定，以及主题文学中作者与其读者或受众的关系。

ETHOS: The internal social context of a work of literature, comprising the characterization and setting of fictional literature and the relation of the author to his reader or audience in thematic literature.

小说：以印刷或书写文字为表现形式的文学作品，例如小说和散文。

FICTION: Literature in which the radical of presentation is the printed or written word, such as novels and essays.

虚构的：指文学作品中除了作者和读者之外，还有内部人物；与主题性相对。（注：遗憾的是，本术语的使用与前文所述不一致，详见第248页。）

FICTIONAL: Relating to literature in which there are internal characters, apart from the author and his audience; opposed to thematic. (N.B. The use of this term is regrettably inconsistent with the preceding one, as noted on p. 248.)

高度模仿：一种文学模式，如同大多数史诗和悲剧一样，中心人物超越了我们自身的权力和权威水平，尽管在自然秩序之内，并受到社会批判。

HIGH MIMETIC: A mode of literature in which, as in most epics and tragedies, the central characters are above our own level of power and authority, though within the order of nature and subject to social criticism.

图像：从形式上看，它是一个具有自然内容的艺术单元，象征着某种符号。

IMAGE: A symbol in its aspect as a formal unit of art with a natural content.

主动性：指导创作过程的主要考虑因素，例如为诗歌选择的韵律；出自柯勒律治。

INITIATIVE: A primary consideration governing the process of composition, such as the metre selected for a poem; taken from Coleridge.

反讽：一种文学模式，其中人物所表现出的行动能力低于读者或观众所认为的正常水平，或者诗人的态度是超然的客观性。

IRONIC: A mode of literature in which the characters exhibit a power of action inferior to the one assumed to be normal in the reader or audience, or in which the poet’s attitude is one of detached objectivity.

反讽：指主要关注“现实”层面体验的文学作品中的神话（含义2），通常以戏仿或与浪漫故事形成对比的形式出现。这种反讽的主要侧重点可能是悲剧性的，也可能是喜剧性的；当它是喜剧性的时，通常与讽刺的通常含义相同。

IRONY: The mythos (sense 2) of the literature concerned primarily with a “realistic” level of experience, usually taking the form of a parody or contrasting analogue to romance. Such irony may be tragic or comic in its main emphasis; when comic it is normally identical with the usual meaning of satire.

L EXIS：文学作品的语言“质感”或修辞方面，包括“措辞”和“意象”等术语的通常含义。

LEXIS: The verbal “texture” or rhetorical aspect of a work of literature, including the usual meanings of the terms “diction” and “imagery.”

低模仿：一种文学模式，其中人物所展现的行动能力大致与我们自身的水平相当，例如大多数喜剧和现实主义小说。

LOW MIMETIC: A mode of literature in which the characters exhibit a power of action which is roughly on our own level, as in most comedy and realistic fiction.

抒情诗：一种文学体裁，其特点是假定读者对诗人不知情，并且以联想节奏为主，这种节奏既不同于反复出现的韵律，也不同于语义或散文节奏。

LYRIC: A literary genre characterized by the assumed concealment of the audience from the poet and by the predominance of an associational rhythm distinguishable both from recurrent metre and from semantic or prose rhythm.

马斯奎：一种戏剧类型，其中音乐和奇观扮演着重要的角色，角色往往是或成为人类性格的某些方面，而不是独立的角色。

MASQUE: A species of drama in which music and spectacle play an important role and in which the characters tend to be or become aspects of human personality rather than independent characters.

韵律（M ELOS）：词语的节奏、韵律和声音；文学中与音乐相似，且往往与音乐存在某种实际联系的方面。源自亚里士多德的“melopoiia”（韵律学）。

MELOS: The rhythm, movement, and sound of words; the aspect of literature which is analogous to music, and often shows some actual relation to it. From Aristotle’s melopoiia.

隐喻：两个符号之间的关系，可以是简单的并置（字面隐喻），相似或相近的修辞性陈述（描述性隐喻），四个术语之间的比例类比（形式隐喻），个人与其类别的同一性（具体普遍或原型隐喻），或假设身份的陈述（寓意隐喻）。

METAPHOR: A relation between two symbols, which may be simple juxtaposition (literal metaphor), a rhetorical statement of likeness or similarity (descriptive metaphor), an analogy of proportion among four terms (formal metaphor), an identity of an individual with its class (concrete universal or archetypal metaphor), or statement of hypothetical identity (anagogic metaphor).

模式：虚构文学中主要人物所具有的约定俗成的行动能力，或主题文学中诗人对读者所持的相应态度。这些模式往往在历史进程中依次出现。

MODE: A conventional power of action assumed about the chief characters in fictional literature, or the corresponding attitude assumed by the poet toward his audience in thematic literature. Such modes tend to succeed one another in a historical sequence.

一元论：象征着一个人的全部文学体验的中心；与霍普金斯的术语“内在景观”和乔伊斯的术语“顿悟”相关。

MONAD: A symbol in its aspect as a center of one’s total literary experience; related to Hopkins’s term “inscape” and to Joyce’s term “epiphany.”

主题：文学作品中作为语言单位的象征意义。

MOTIF: A symbol in its aspect as a verbal unit in a work of literary art.

神话：一种叙事，其中某些角色是超人，他们做的事情“只发生在故事里”；因此，这是一种程式化的或风格化的叙事，并不完全符合合理性或“现实主义”。

MYTH: A narrative in which some characters are superhuman beings who do things that “happen only in stories”; hence, a conventionalized or stylized narrative not fully adapted to plausibility or “realism.”

神话：（1）文学作品的叙事，被视为语法或词语顺序（字面叙事）、情节或“论点”（描述性叙事）、对动作的二次模仿（形式叙事）、模仿（1） 指一般性的、反复出现的行为或仪式（原型叙事），或模仿全能的神或人类社会所有可想象的行为（寓言叙事）。（2）四种原型叙事之一，分为喜剧、浪漫、悲剧和讽刺四种。

MYTHOS: (1) The narrative of a work of literature, considered as the grammar or order of words (literal narrative), plot or “argument” (descriptive narrative), secondary imitation of action (formal narrative), imitation of generic and recurrent action or ritual (archetypal narrative), or imitation of the total conceivable action of an omnipotent god or human society (anagogic narrative). (2) One of the four archetypal narratives, classified as comic, romantic, tragic, and ironic.

天真：原始的或流行的，从这些术语的意义上讲，它比其他类型的文学更容易在时间和空间上进行交流。

NAIVE: Primitive or popular, in the sense given those terms of an ability to communicate in time and space more readily than other types of literature.

O PSIS：戏剧中壮观或可见的方面；其他文学作品中理想的可见或具象的方面。

OPSIS: The spectacular or visible aspect of drama; the ideally visible or pictorial aspect of other literature.

P HARMAKOS：讽刺小说中扮演替罪羊或任意选择的受害者的角色。

PHARMAKOS: The character in an ironic fiction who has the role of a scapegoat or arbitrarily chosen victim.

阶段：（1）文学作品的叙事和意义可以从五个层面来考察，这五个层面分别是字面层面、描述层面、形式层面、原型层面和寓意层面。（2）神话的六个可区分阶段之一（含义2）。

PHASE: (1) One of the five contexts in which the narrative and meaning of a work of literature may be considered, classified as literal, descriptive, formal, archetypal, and anagogic. (2) One of six distinguishable stages of a mythos (sense 2).

顿悟点：一种原型，同时展现了末世景象和自然循环秩序，有时也仅展现后者。其常用象征物包括梯子、山脉、灯塔、岛屿和塔楼。

POINT OF EPIPHANY: An archetype presenting simultaneously an apocalyptic world and a cyclical order of nature, or sometimes the latter alone. Its usual symbols are ladders, mountains, lighthouses, islands, and towers.

浪漫小说：（1）主要关注理想化世界的文学神话。（2）斯科特、霍桑、威廉·莫里斯等人创作的一种散文小说形式，与长篇小说有所区别。

ROMANCE: (1) The mythos of literature concerned primarily with an idealized world. (2) A form of prose fiction practised by Scott, Hawthorne, William Morris, etc., distinguishable from the novel.

浪漫主义：（1）一种虚构模式，其主要人物生活在一个充满奇迹的世界中（天真浪漫主义），或者其氛围哀婉或田园牧歌式，因此比模仿模式较少受到社会批判。（2）一种普遍倾向，即以理想化的人类形象来呈现神话和隐喻，介于纯粹的神话和“现实主义”之间。

ROMANTIC: (1) A fictional mode in which the chief characters live in a world of marvels (naive romance), or in which the mood is elegiac or idyllic and hence less subject to social criticism than in the mimetic modes. (2) The general tendency to present myth and metaphor in an idealized human form, midway between undisplaced myth and “realism.”

S IGN：符号，指自然物体或概念的语言代表。

SIGN: A symbol in its aspect as a verbal representative of a natural object or concept.

符号：文学作品中任何可以单独提取出来进行批判性分析的单元。通常指较小的单元，例如词语、短语、图像等。

SYMBOL: Any unit of any work of literature which can be isolated for critical attention. In general usage restricted to the smaller units, such as words, phrases, images, etc.

主题性的：指除了作者和读者之外没有其他人物的文学作品，如大多数抒情诗和散文；或者指内部人物服从于作者所坚持的论点的文学作品，如寓言和比喻；与虚构的相对。

THEMATIC: Relating to works of literature in which no characters are involved except the author and his audience, as in most lyrics and essays, or to works of literature in which internal characters are subordinated to an argument maintained by the author, as in allegories and parables; opposed to fictional.
